source.title: Geometrization of the local Langlands correspondence
readSections: The whole of arXiv:2102.13459v4 (27 November 2024; 356 pp., SHA-256 1f8040751d3424f59ae56651d990d7b2d5030e6b7cae58bc2fc683358dfc2027, fetched 29 September 2026): Chapters I–X and the bibliography, every page, with quoted formulas checked on page images. The published version (Astérisque 466, 2026, 674 pp.) is paywalled and was not consulted, so locators and findings refer to arXiv v4.

sourceVersions.citation: Astérisque 466 (2026), doi:10.24033/ast.1270 — paywalled (SMF), not read; findings are scoped to arXiv v4

summary: Fargues and Scholze develop the geometric Langlands program on the Fargues–Fontaine curve and use it to attach L-parameters to smooth irreducible representations of G(E) for any reductive group G over a local field E. The paper has four layers. The first is the curve and its vector bundles (Chapter II: relative curves, Div¹, the classification of bundles, Banach–Colmez spaces). The second is the stack Bun_G of G-bundles, with |Bun_G| ≅ B(G), Beauville–Laszlo uniformization, the semistable locus and the strata (Chapter III). The third is a six-functor sheaf theory on Artin v-stacks (Chapters IV, V and VII: universally locally acyclic sheaves, the Jacobian criterion, hyperbolic localization, Drinfeld's lemma, D_ét(Bun_G) with compact generation and Bernstein–Zelevinsky and Verdier duality, solid and lisse sheaves D_■ and D_lis). The fourth is geometric Satake over the curve, identifying the Tannakian group with the Langlands dual group with its Weil action (Chapter VI). Building on these, it constructs the stack of L-parameters and its coarse moduli, excursion operators, and integral generation results (Chapter VIII). The Hecke action and excursion operators give the L-parameter φ_π, with its properties and compatibility with known cases (Chapter IX), and the spectral action of Perf(Par_Ĝ) on D_lis(Bun_G) (Chapter X). The categorical local Langlands conjecture is stated but not proved. The atlas's campaign roadmaps were built for this paper, and they plan 661 of its 834 items: DiamondsAndVStacks, RelativeFarguesFontaine, VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals, BunGAndNewtonStrata, VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories, GeometricSatakeAndFusion, HeckeStacksAndLocalShtukas, LanglandsParameterStacks and ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction. Two items are in Mathlib: the Proj construction, and the open point of a finite T0 space. After review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21) the extraction has 847 items: 733 planned, 2 library and 112 missing. The review found many items the extraction had marked missing that are planned node by node in the accepted decompositions (VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals, RelativeFarguesFontaine, VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories, GeometricSatakeAndFusion, LanglandsParameterStacks); items planned only by draft, unpromoted packets stay missing and are routed to the layers those packets name. The 112 missing items go as sources of: RelativeFarguesFontaine (9), VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals (10), BunGAndNewtonStrata (32), VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories (22), GeometricSatakeAndFusion (3), LanglandsParameterStacks (15), ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction (15), EnhancedDerivedSheaves (1), DiamondEtaleCohomology (1), SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups (1); and two Part IIs proposed by other papers and accepted, which they join: ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralActionStableCenter (Haines' conjecture, 1) and LubinTateFormalModulesAndQuasiCanonicalLifts (the Lubin–Tate formal group, 2). No new roadmap is needed. 129 mistakes are recorded (70 by the extraction, all confirmed; 59 found in review), almost all misprints; the substantive ones are a sign error in Lemmas IV.4.25–IV.4.26 (φ − π^{−d} for φ − π^{d}), a false identification HH²(B/A) = Ext¹(L_{B/A}, B) in §VIII.2, and gaps or failing steps in the proofs of Theorem II.2.6, Proposition II.3.1, Theorem VIII.5.15 and Proposition IX.6.3, none of which changes a main theorem.

items.name: Weil group W_E (nonarchimedean case)
items.statement: E nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p > 0 with residue field F_q. W_E is the dense subgroup of Gal(Ē|E) given by the preimage of ℤ ⊂ Gal(F̄_q|F_q) ≅ Ẑ, the subgroup generated by the Frobenius x ↦ x^q. An L-parameter is (conjecturally attached to π) a homomorphism φ_π : W_E → Ĝ(ℂ), Ĝ the Langlands dual group (split reductive over ℤ with dual root datum).
items.note: Background definition fixing W_E ⊂ Gal(Ē|E) with inertia I_E and wild inertia P_E (§I.13, p. 44). Used throughout (π_1(Div¹) = W_E, Hecke W_E-equivariance, Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)). Owner: the Tau Ceti roadmap Class field theory, Layer 9 ('localWeilGroup K ≤ G_K, the preimage of ℤ ⊆ Ẑ', the Weil topology, 1 → I_K → W_K → ℤ → 1); wild inertia P_K = Gal(K^s/K^t) is Local fields and ramification, Layer 4. LanglandsParameterStacks:LP0 only consumes it ('Use the local-field Weil-group carrier, inertia and wild inertia with their topologies'). Neither pinned library has a Weil group. The dual group Ĝ is item c6b-dual-group-with-twisted-Weil-action.

items.name: Dieudonné–Manin classification of Isoc_E (cited)
items.statement: Isoc_E, the category of Ĕ-vector spaces V with a φ-linear automorphism σ (Ĕ the completion of the maximal unramified extension of E), is semisimple, with one simple object V_λ for each λ ∈ ℚ; End(V_λ) is the central simple E-algebra D_λ of Brauer invariant λ̄ ∈ ℚ/ℤ, so Isoc_E ≅ ⊕_{λ∈ℚ} Vect_{D_λ} ⊗ V_λ. If λ = s/r with coprime integers s, r, r > 0, then V_λ ≅ Ĕ^r of rank r with σ given by the matrix with 1's on the superdiagonal and π^s in the lower-left corner (π ∈ E a uniformizer).
items.note: Classical input (Dieudonné–Manin), not proved in the paper; used in II.2 (e.g. proof of Proposition II.3.7) and to define O(λ). VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0 plans: "Prove the Dieudonné–Manin classification after the stipulated algebraically closed residue base, including simple objects of rational slope, multiplicities, Hom and endomorphism division algebras" and pins "the standard rank-r block with Frobenius r-th power pi^s sigma^r". Locator: Isoc_E is introduced at the foot of p. 8 and the classification continues on p. 9. Convention caution (checked by computation, not a recorded mistake): with σ the arithmetic Frobenius and V_λ = (Ĕ^r, σ given by the printed matrix), End(V_λ) = E_r⟨Π⟩ with Π the E-linear map of the same matrix, Π^r = π^s and ΠaΠ⁻¹ = σ⁻¹(a) for a ∈ E_r; this cyclic algebra has invariant −λ̄ under the normalization inv(E_r/E, σ, π) = 1/r and λ̄ under the geometric-Frobenius normalization. The paper does not state its normalization; FF18 Déf. 8.2.7/Prop. 8.2.8 (End(O(λ)) = D_λ with Π^h = π^d, ΠxΠ⁻¹ = σ(x), and O(λ) = E(V_{−λ})) follow the first. VB0's obligation to 'record any sign reversal explicitly' should pin this.

items.name: G-isocrystals, Kottwitz set B(E,G), basic elements, G_b
items.statement: A G-isocrystal is a G-torsor in Isoc_E (exact ⊗-functor Rep_E G → Isoc_E); B(E,G) = B(G) is the set of G-isocrystals up to isomorphism, E_b the G-isocrystal attached to b. There is an injection H¹_ét(Spec E, G) ↪ B(E,G) with image in B(E,G)_basic. For b ∈ B(E,G), G_b = Aut(E_b), an inner form of a Levi subgroup of G (an inner form of G, i.e. an extended pure inner form, when b is basic). For G = GL_n, E_b is basic iff it has a single slope. The groupoid of G-torsors in Isoc_E is G-Isoc ≅ ⊔_{[b]∈B(E,G)} [∗/G_b(E)].
items.note: Body: Definition III.2.1 (p. 89), identified with σ-conjugacy classes in G(Ĕ). BunGAndNewtonStrata:BG0 plans: "Define B(G) as sigma-conjugacy classes in G(E-breve) ... and compare with isomorphism classes of G-isocrystals. Construct J_b as its algebraic sigma-centralizer and prove representability and its inner-Levi description."

items.name: The stack G-𝓘soc of families of G-isocrystals
items.statement: On perfect F̄_q-algebras R: G-𝓘soc(R) = {G-torsors on Spec R((t))/φ^ℤ} in equal characteristic, resp. G-𝓘soc(R) = {G-torsors on Spec(W_{O_E}(R)[1/π])/φ^ℤ} in mixed characteristic, where W_{O_E}(R) = W(R) ⊗_{W(F_q)} O_E is the unique π-adically complete flat O_E-algebra with reduction R. Equivalently (v-locally on R every G-torsor over R((t)), resp. W_{O_E}(R)[1/π], is trivial by [Ans22]), G-𝓘soc = LG/_{Ad,σ}LG as v-stacks, with LG(R) = G(R((t))) (resp. G(W_{O_E}(R)[1/π])), the quotient of the loop group by σ-conjugation.
items.note: Motivational object: 'We will not use the stack G-𝓘soc in this paper.' No atlas stage plans G-𝓘soc (grep of the campaign stages finds only Isoc_E in VB0/RF3).

items.name: Theorem I.2.1 (structure of G-𝓘soc)
items.statement: The prestack G-𝓘soc is a stack for the v-topology on perfect F̄_q-algebras. It admits a stratification into locally closed substacks G-𝓘soc^b ⊂ G-𝓘soc for b ∈ B(E,G), consisting of the locus where at each geometric point the G-isocrystal is isomorphic to E_b. Moreover each stratum G-𝓘soc^b ≅ [∗/G_b(E)] is a classifying stack for the locally profinite group G_b(E).
items.note: Not proved in the paper (footnote 3: 'well-known to experts'): v-(arc-)descent [Iva23, Lemma 5.9]; stratification essentially [RR96]; local constancy of the Kottwitz map proved in Corollary III.2.8; identification of strata [CS17, Prop. 4.3.13], in general [HK22, Theorem 1.4]. Only motivational; contrast with Theorem I.2.7 (closure relations reversed, Remark I.2.8). No stage plans it.

items.name: Definition I.2.2 (relative Fargues–Fontaine curve X_S)
items.statement: For S = Spa(R,R⁺) ∈ Perf = Perf_{F̄_q} (R a perfectoid Tate F̄_q-algebra with pseudouniformizer ϖ, R⁺ ⊂ R an open integrally closed subring of powerbounded elements), X_S = X_{S,E} = (Spa(R,R⁺) ×_{Spa F_q} Spa F_q((t)))/φ^ℤ in equal characteristic, resp. X_S = (Spa(R,R⁺) ×̇_{Spa F_q} Spa E)/φ^ℤ, where Y_S := Spa(R,R⁺) ×̇_{Spa F_q} Spa E ⊂ Spa W_{O_E}(R⁺) is the open locus where π and [ϖ] are invertible (independent of ϖ); φ acts via the Frobenius of (R,R⁺). It is an adic space over E.
items.note: Body: Definition II.1.15 (p. 54) with Proposition II.1.1, II.1.3. The ×̇ is purely symbolic. RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF1 plans: "Glue Y_S over perfectoid affinoid covers; establish q-Frobenius action, wandering annuli and the adic quotient X_S = Y_S/phi^Z." (RF0 builds Y_S.)

items.name: φ acts freely and totally discontinuously on Y_S (radius function)
items.statement: On Y_S the map rad = log(|[ϖ]|)/log(|π|) : |Y_S| → (0,∞) is well-defined and continuous, and Frobenius multiplies rad by q; hence the action of φ^ℤ on Y_S is free and totally discontinuous and X_S = Y_S/φ^ℤ is a well-defined adic space. In equal characteristic Y_S = D*_S is a punctured open unit disc over S and X_S is locally, but not globally, of finite type over S.
items.note: Body: Proposition II.1.16 (p. 54). RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF1 plans the "q-Frobenius action, wandering annuli and the adic quotient".

items.name: Proposition I.2.3 (classical points of X_C, mixed characteristic)
items.statement: If E is of mixed characteristic and S = Spa C is a geometric point, the classical points of X_C are in bijection with untilts C♯|E of C, up to the action of Frobenius.
items.note: Body: Definition/Proposition II.1.22 (with Propositions II.1.18, II.1.8). Restated in Theorem I.3.1. Planned: the accepted VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals decomposition node VB2:classification/classical-points-and-principal-ideal-domains ('FS II.1.11–II.1.12 and II.1.22 … the classical points of X_C are |Y_C|^cl/φ^ℤ and are in bijection with Div¹(C)'), with RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2:untilts supplying Div¹(C) = untilts of C over E modulo Frobenius (RF0 packet node div1-moduli-and-properness: 'Verify Div^1(C) = untilts of C over E modulo Frobenius, matching Def./Prop. II.1.22'). FarguesFontaineDiamonds:F4 disclaims the classification, but it is not the owner. The accepted FF18 extraction cites the same VB node (items 298, 333).

items.name: Diamond Z^♢ and the mirror curve Div¹
items.statement: For an adic space Z over W(F̄_q), Z^♢ : Perf → Sets, S ↦ {(S♯, f : S♯ → Z)} (S♯ an untilt of S); if Z is analytic, Z^♢ is a diamond (quotient of a perfectoid space by a pro-étale equivalence relation). Div¹ := (Spa Ĕ)^♢/φ^ℤ = Spd Ĕ/φ^ℤ (φ acting as geometric Frobenius on the diamond); for S ∈ Perf, maps S → Div¹ are in bijection with degree 1 Cartier divisors D_S ⊂ X_S (locally an untilt S♯ ⊂ X_S over E); the classical points of X_C are the C-points of Div¹; π_1(Div¹) = W_E.
items.note: Body: [SW20] for Z^♢; Proposition II.1.17–II.1.18, Definition II.1.19 (degree 1 Cartier divisors), Proposition II.1.21 (Div¹ → ∗ proper, representable in spatial diamonds, cohomologically smooth). 'π_1(Div¹) = W_E' is heuristic: Chapter IV intro says 'we know no definition of π_1 making this true', replaced by Drinfeld's lemma (IV.7). Planned: DiamondsAndVStacks:D6 ("Glue these affine objects to define X^♢ for analytic adic spaces over ℤ_p"); RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2:untilts ("Define Div^1 using the unramified coefficient base Spd(E-breve)/phi^Z over Perf_Fq").

items.name: Perfectoid spaces over F̄_q (Perf), perfectoid Tate algebras and tilting
items.statement: Perf = Perf_{F̄_q} is the category of perfectoid spaces over F̄_q; locally S = Spa(R,R⁺) with R a perfectoid Tate F̄_q-algebra, i.e. a perfect topological F̄_q-algebra with a topologically nilpotent unit ϖ (pseudouniformizer) making it a Banach algebra over F̄_q((ϖ)), and R⁺ ⊂ R an open integrally closed subring of powerbounded elements (Spa R := Spa(R,R°)); the geometric rank-1 points of S are Spa C, C complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean. For a perfectoid Tate ring R (e.g. a complete algebraically closed C′|E) the tilt is R♭ = lim_{x↦x^p} R, with addition defined through R^{♭+} = lim_{x↦x^p} R⁺ ≅ lim_{x↦x^p} R⁺/π; R♭ is a perfectoid Tate algebra of characteristic p, and Spa(R,R⁺) ↦ Spa(R♭,R^{♭+}) defines a tilting functor T ↦ T♭ on perfectoid spaces preserving the underlying topological space and the étale site.
items.note: The test category of the whole paper; the tilt is used to classify classical points (Proposition I.2.3) and in Z^♢. Planned: PerfectoidSpaces:P1 ('Construct the multiplicative inverse limit defining R♭, the limiting addition, the topology … Prove classification of marked untilts'), P2 ('Prove the tilting homeomorphism of valuation spectra … Define perfectoid spaces … Glue tilting and prove the slice-category equivalence of ECD 3.20'), P3 ('Almost purity and étale tilting'). Mathlib has only the ring-level PreTilt (Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfection.lean), not perfectoid spaces or the tilting equivalence. Added in review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21).

items.name: Definition I.2.4 (Bun_G)
items.statement: Bun_G : Perf → {groupoids}, S ↦ {G-torsors on X_S}, the moduli stack of G-torsors on the Fargues–Fontaine curve.
items.note: Body: Definition III.0.1/III.1.2 (on Perf_k, k = F̄_q), G-torsors via Definition/Proposition III.1.1. Remark I.2.5: 'the Fargues–Fontaine curve' is not well-defined but Bun_G is. BunGAndNewtonStrata:BG2:uniformization plans: "Define the groupoid-valued functor S ↦ G-bundles on X_S. Prove v-descent, smallness with cutoffs".

items.name: Theorem I.2.6 (Fargues, Anschütz: G-bundles at a geometric point)
items.statement: If S = Spa C is a geometric point, the map B(G) → Bun_G(S)/≅ (pullback of G-isocrystals along X_S → Spa Ĕ/φ^ℤ) is a bijection. In particular, any vector bundle on X_S is a direct sum of the vector bundles O_{X_S}(λ), λ ∈ ℚ, where O_{X_S}(λ) is the bundle associated with the simple isocrystal V_{−λ} of slope −λ (printed 'associated to D_{−λ}'; PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E2). Under this bijection, b ∈ B(G) is basic iff the G-torsor E_b on X_S is semistable in the sense of Atiyah–Bott.
items.note: Body: Theorem III.2.2 ([Far20a], [Ans19]; sketch of Anschütz's proof given), vector-bundle case Theorem II.2.14. (PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E2). BunGAndNewtonStrata:BG2:uniformization plans "Prove the bijection |Bun_G| → B(G), geometric-base independence"; the GL_n case is VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:classification.

items.name: Theorem I.2.7 (Bun_G is a v-stack with Harder–Narasimhan strata)
items.statement: The prestack Bun_G is a v-stack. It admits a stratification into locally closed substacks i^b : Bun_G^b ⊂ Bun_G for b ∈ B(G), consisting of the locus where at each geometric point the G-torsor is isomorphic to E_b. Each stratum Bun_G^b ≅ [∗/G̃_b] is a classifying space for a group G̃_b that is an extension of the locally profinite group G_b(E) by a 'unipotent group diamond'. The semistable locus Bun_G^ss ⊂ Bun_G is an open substack and Bun_G^ss = ⊔_{b∈B(G)_basic} [∗/G_b(E)].
items.note: Refined in Theorem I.4.1 (i),(iv),(v) = Theorem III.0.2; see those items. Remark I.2.8: basic strata are open (closure relations reversed relative to G-𝓘soc). Planned in BunGAndNewtonStrata:BG2:uniformization and BG3 ("prove that the union of basic strata is open", "Bun_G^b = [*/Gtilde_b]").

items.name: Global/local Hecke stacks, Schubert cells and Hecke operators (one leg)
items.statement: Hck_G parametrizes (E, E′) G-bundles on X_S, a map S → Div¹ with divisor D_S ⊂ X_S, and an isomorphism f : E|_{X_S∖D_S} ≅ E′|_{X_S∖D_S} meromorphic along D_S; it gives Bun_G ←h₁– Hck_G –h₂→ Bun_G × Div¹. The local Hecke stack 𝓗ck_G (pairs of G-torsors on the completion of X_S along D_S with an isomorphism off D_S) receives Hck_G → 𝓗ck_G and has a Schubert stratification by conjugacy classes of cocharacters µ : G_m → G, with closed Schubert cells 𝓗ck_{G,≤µ}; pulling back gives Bun_G ←h_{1,≤µ}– Hck_{G,≤µ} –h_{2,≤µ}→ Bun_G × Div¹ with h_{1,≤µ}, h_{2,≤µ} proper, and Hecke operators Rh_{2,≤µ,∗}h*_{1,≤µ} : D(Bun_G, Λ) → D(Bun_G × Div¹, Λ).
items.note: Body: §VI.1 (local Hecke stack, Definition VI.1.6), §VI.2 (Schubert varieties), §IX.2 (Hecke operators via Satake kernels). HeckeStacksAndLocalShtukas:HS0 plans: "define the stack of two G-bundles and an isomorphism away from the selected divisors. Construct its source, target and leg maps ... and bounded substacks for tuples of dominant cocharacters"; HS1 defines T_V "by the actual pull-tensor-push construction".

items.name: Theorem I.2.11 (sheaves on Bun_G × Div¹ are W_E-equivariant sheaves)
items.statement: Pullback along the map Div¹ → [∗/W_E] induces an equivalence D(Bun_G × Div¹, Q̄_ℓ) ≅ D(Bun_G × [∗/W_E], Q̄_ℓ) ≅ D(Bun_G, Q̄_ℓ)^{BW_E}. (Stated 'somewhat cavalier[ly]' regarding D(−, Q̄_ℓ) and W_E-equivariance; fine print in the main text.) Hence Hecke operators produce W_E-equivariant objects of D(Bun_G, Q̄_ℓ).
items.note: Body: Proposition IV.7.1, Corollary IV.7.2, Proposition IV.7.3 (torsion coefficients; equivalence only on locally constant objects in general), Corollary VII.2.7–VII.2.8 (solid: fully faithful; an equivalence when D(X) → D(X × Spd Ĕ) is one, which holds for X = Bun_G by Proposition VII.7.3), Proposition IX.1.1 and Corollary IX.2.3 (Hecke operators land in the W_E^I-equivariant part). As literally stated for all of D(Bun_G × Div¹) the equivalence is stronger than the body's fully-faithful statements; the intro flags its imprecision. VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories:VS1 plans: "Establish Drinfeld's lemma IV.7 for the divisor/Weil-action applications".

items.name: Theorem I.2.12 (monoidal functor from Rep Ĝ to sheaves on the local Hecke stack)
items.statement: There is a natural monoidal functor from Rep Ĝ to D(𝓗ck_G, Q̄_ℓ).
items.note: First approximation of Theorem I.6.3 (body Theorem VI.0.2 = VI.11.1). Remark I.2.13: proof follows Mirković–Vilonen with fusion. Remark I.2.15: the D(−, Q̄_ℓ) implicit here differs from that of Bun_G; no issue with torsion coefficients. GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS4:integral-dual-group plans reconstruction and identification "with the pinned dual".

items.name: Remark I.2.14 (new proof of Zhu's Witt-vector geometric Satake, and Yu's integral version)
items.statement: Using a degeneration of the local Hecke stack (essentially the B_dR⁺-affine Grassmannian of [SW20]) to the Witt vector affine Grassmannian, Theorem I.2.12 gives a new proof of Zhu's geometric Satake equivalence for the Witt vector affine Grassmannian [Zhu17]; the version with ℤ_ℓ-coefficients recovers the result of Yu [Yu22].
items.note: Body: Chapter VI introduction (p. 188: Satake categories over Spd F̄_q, Spd O_C, Spd C are equivalent via base change), §§VI.6–VI.7 and §VI.11. GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS1 plans: "Construct the one-leg special/generic-fibre comparison on the ULA, flat-perverse categories over Spd(O_C), Spd(C) and Spd(k̄)"; combined with GS4:integral-dual-group.

items.name: Hecke operators T_V commute and compose tensorially
items.statement: For any representation V of Ĝ one gets T_V : D(Bun_G, Q̄_ℓ) → D(Bun_G, Q̄_ℓ)^{BW_E}; the Hecke operators commute and T_{V⊗W} ≅ T_V ∘ T_W|_{Δ(W_E)}, where T_V ∘ T_W takes values in W_E × W_E-equivariant objects and the restriction is to the diagonal Δ(W_E) ⊂ W_E × W_E.
items.note: Body: Theorem IX.0.1 (ii)–(iii), Corollary IX.2.4 (monoidal functor Rep_Λ(Ĝ⋊Q)^I → End_Λ(D_lis(Bun_G,Λ)^ω)^{BW_E^I} functorial in I). HeckeStacksAndLocalShtukas:HS1 plans "T_unit = identity, tensor/convolution composition and fusion across arbitrary finite sets".

items.name: Theorem I.3.1 (local structure and classical points of X_C)
items.statement: Let C|F_q be complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean. The adic space X_C is locally Spa(B,B⁺) with B a principal ideal domain; the classical points of Spa(B,B⁺) ⊂ X_C are in bijection with the maximal ideals of B. For each classical point x ∈ X_C, the residue field of x is an untilt C♯ of C over E, and this induces a bijection of the classical points of X_C with untilts C♯ of C over E, taken up to the action of Frobenius.
items.note: Body: Theorem II.0.1 (stated for 𝒴_C) = Proposition II.1.11, Corollary II.1.12, Definition/Proposition II.1.22 (B Dedekind; PID via the Picard group computation, footnote 2 p. 56 and Proposition II.2.10). Proof uses tilting and 'Zariski closed implies strongly Zariski closed' [BS22] (Proposition II.0.2). Planned by the accepted VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals decomposition node VB2:classification/classical-points-and-principal-ideal-domains: 'Spm(B) → |U| is a bijection onto |U|^cl … if U is connected then B is a principal ideal domain … the classical points of X_C are |Y_C|^cl/φ^ℤ and are in bijection with Div¹(C); for U = Spa(B,B⁺) an affinoid open of X_C with U connected, B is a Dedekind domain (in fact a PID, by the Picard computation)', with acceptance 'Verify the footnote's upgrade from Dedekind to PID via Pic(X_C) = Z'. Div¹(C) = untilts modulo Frobenius and the residue fields at untilts are RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2:untilts ('At a geometric untilt identify the complete discrete valuation ring and its residue field').

items.name: Theorem I.3.2 (classification of vector bundles on X_C)
items.statement: The functor from Isoc_E to vector bundles on X_C induces a bijection on isomorphism classes. In particular, there is a unique stable vector bundle O_{X_C}(λ) of any slope λ ∈ ℚ, and any vector bundle E can be written as a direct sum of stable bundles.
items.note: Body: Theorem II.0.3 = Theorem II.2.14 (new proof via v-descent and Banach–Colmez geometry; key Lemma II.2.15 uses non-representability of BC(O(−1)[1])). VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:classification plans: "Prove that every bundle at a geometric point is a direct sum of the stable O(lambda) ... The isocrystal functor induces the source's bijection on isomorphism classes".

items.name: Theorem I.3.3 (ampleness and algebraic curve X_S^alg)
items.statement: Assume S ∈ Perf is affinoid. For any vector bundle E on X_S, the twist E(n) is globally generated and has no higher cohomology for all n ≫ 0. With P = ⊕_{n≥0} H⁰(X_S, O_{X_S}(n)) and X_S^alg = Proj P, there is a natural map of locally ringed spaces X_S → X_S^alg, pullback along which defines an equivalence of categories of vector bundles, preserving cohomology. If S = Spa C (C complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean), X_C^alg is a regular noetherian scheme of Krull dimension 1, locally the spectrum of a principal ideal domain, and its closed points are in bijection with the classical points of X_C.
items.note: Body: Theorem II.0.4 = Theorem II.2.6, Proposition II.2.7, Proposition II.2.9; cf. [KL15, Proposition 6.2.4]. Planned: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:ampleness ("For affinoid perfectoid S prove that sufficiently positive twists of a bundle are globally generated with higher cohomology zero. Compare bundles and cohomology on X_S and the Proj curve built in RF3"), RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF3 (graded algebra, Proj and the map).

items.name: Theorem I.3.4 (families of vector bundles: HN semicontinuity, local splitting, local systems)
items.statement: Let S ∈ Perf and E a vector bundle on X_S. The function s ↦ Harder–Narasimhan polygon of E|_{X_s} is semicontinuous on S. If it is constant, E admits a global Harder–Narasimhan stratification, and pro-étale locally on S E is isomorphic to a direct sum of O_{X_S}(λ)'s. In particular, if E is everywhere semistable of slope 0, then E is pro-étale locally trivial, and the category of such E is equivalent to the category of pro-étale E-local systems on S.
items.note: Body: Theorem II.0.5 = Theorem II.2.19 (upper semicontinuous; [KL15]) and Corollary II.2.20. Key input: properness of projectivized Banach–Colmez spaces (Proposition II.2.16). VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB4 plans: "Construct the geometric HN polygon of E_s, prove its semicontinuity ... existence of the relative HN filtration ... equivalence between everywhere slope-zero bundles and pro-étale E-local systems".

items.name: Definition I.3.5 (Banach–Colmez spaces)
items.statement: Let E be a vector bundle on X_S. BC(E) is the locally spatial diamond over S with BC(E)(T) = H⁰(X_T, E|_{X_T}) for T ∈ Perf_S. If E has everywhere only negative Harder–Narasimhan slopes, the negative Banach–Colmez space BC(E[1]) is the locally spatial diamond over S with BC(E[1])(T) = H¹(X_T, E|_{X_T}).
items.note: Body: Definition II.0.6; representability Proposition II.2.5 (O(λ)), Proposition II.2.16 (general E, partially proper), Proposition II.3.5 (negative/complexes). Planned: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:positive-basic-examples ("Construct the sheaf of sections T ↦ H^0(X_T,E_T) ... Negative H^1 spaces have their separate construction") and VB3:general-BC.

items.name: BC(O(λ)) is a perfectoid open unit disc for small positive λ; BC(O(1)) and Lubin–Tate
items.statement: If E = O_{X_S}(λ) with 0 < λ ≤ [E : ℚ_p] (resp. all λ > 0 if E has equal characteristic), BC(E) is representable by a perfectoid open unit disc of dimension the numerator of λ (body: BC(O(λ)) ≅ Spd k[[x_1^{1/p^∞}, …, x_r^{1/p^∞}]], λ = r/s). In particular BC(O_{X_S}(1)) is identified with the universal cover of a Lubin–Tate formal group law; e.g. BC(O(1)) ≅ Spd F̄_q[[t^{1/p^∞}]].
items.note: Body: Proposition II.2.5 (iv); Lubin–Tate calculation §II.2.1. Planned: the accepted VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals decomposition node VB1/cohomology-of-twists states II.2.5(iv) with the [E:Q_p] bound ('If 0 < lambda <= [E:Q_p] (resp. all positive lambda in equal characteristic) then BC(O(lambda)) = Spd k[[x_1^{1/p^infty},...,x_r^{1/p^infty}]]'); VB3:positive-basic-examples/lubin-tate-universal-cover gives BC(O(1)) as the universal cover of the Lubin–Tate group (II.2.2); VB3:general-BC 'State the slope bounds in perfectoid-open-ball identifications'.

items.name: Negative Banach–Colmez space BC(O_{X_C}(−1)[1]) and its non-representability
items.statement: BC(O_{X_C}(−1)[1]) ≅ (A¹_{C♯})^♢/E, the quotient of the affine line by the translation action of E ⊂ A¹_{C♯}; it is not representable by a perfectoid space (known for E p-adic; in the function field case the paper supplies a small extra argument circumventing the issue). The proof of Theorem I.3.2 ultimately relies on this non-representability.
items.note: Body: Proposition II.2.5(i) and the proof of Lemma II.2.15 (pp. 71–72, footnote 5), used for Theorem II.2.14. Planned in the accepted VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals decomposition: VB1/cohomology-of-twists derives the presentation from '0 -> E -> (A^1_{S^sharp})^diamond -> BC(O(-1)[1]) -> 0'; VB2:classification/key-extension-lemma carries the non-representability step ('Then BC(O(-1)[1]) would be a perfectoid space. In the p-adic case this is absurd since (A^1_{C^sharp})^diamond would be pro-etale over a perfectoid space') and the equal-characteristic workaround (hypothesis: 'in equal characteristic Fargues-Scholze … could not settle whether BC(O(-1)[1]) is perfectoid, and argue differently'). The Chapter II item c2a-fact-BC-O-minus-1-quotient (the same presentation) is already planned.

items.name: Projectivized Banach–Colmez spaces are proper
items.statement: For a vector bundle E on X_S, the projectivized Banach–Colmez space (BC(E) ∖ {0})/E^× is proper over S; hence its image in S is closed, and if the image is all of S one finds a nowhere vanishing section of E after a v-cover.
items.note: Body: Proposition II.2.16 (with Lemma II.2.17); used in Theorem II.2.19. VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:projectivized-properness plans: "Prove II.2.16's properness of (BC(E)\{0})/E× using II.2.6 ampleness and II.2.5(iii)".

items.name: Newton point ν, Kottwitz invariant κ and the partial order on B(G)
items.statement: For G reductive over E with universal Cartan T and Γ = Gal(Ē|E): the Newton point ν : B(G) → (X_*(T)^+_ℚ)^Γ (conjugacy class of the slope morphism D → G_Ĕ, D the diagonalizable group with character group ℚ) and the Kottwitz invariant κ : B(G) → π_1(G_Ē)_Γ (defined via tori, simply connected derived group and z-extensions). b ≤ b′ iff κ(b) = κ(b′) and ν_b ≤ ν_{b′} in the dominance order. Up to sign, ν and κ are the HN polygon and first Chern class of a G-bundle.
items.note: Body: §III.2 (Theorem III.2.3, III.2.7 use them); inputs from [Kot85], [Kot97]. BunGAndNewtonStrata:BG1 plans: "Construct pi_1(G), its Galois coinvariants, the Kottwitz map kappa and rational dominant Newton cocharacter nu ... Define the partial order with equal kappa and the dominance comparison of Newton points". The statement uses the corrected 'character group ℚ'; p. 20 prints 'the diagonalizable group with cocharacter group ℚ' (new misprint reported by this review; the body, proof of Proposition III.5.2, p. 105, has 'the pro-torus with character group ℚ').

items.name: Kottwitz: (ν,κ) injective and κ : B(G)_basic ≅ π_1(G_Ē)_Γ (cited)
items.statement: (ν, κ) : B(G) → (X_*(T)^+_ℚ)^Γ × π_1(G_Ē)_Γ is injective. Moreover κ induces a bijection between B(G)_basic and π_1(G_Ē)_Γ. The non-basic elements can be described in terms of Levi subgroups.
items.note: Cited from Kottwitz [Kot85], [Kot97]; used in Corollary IV.1.23 and throughout III. BunGAndNewtonStrata:BG1 plans: "Prove the classification/uniqueness assertions for B(G) used in FS III, including basic classes, the centralizer Levi".

items.name: Theorem I.4.1(i) (Bun_G is a v-stack)
items.statement: The prestack Bun_G is a stack for the v-topology.
items.note: Body: Theorem III.0.2(i) (small v-stack): Proposition II.2.1 (v-descent for vector bundles; essentially [SW20]) and Proposition III.1.3 (smallness). BunGAndNewtonStrata:BG2:uniformization: "Prove v-descent, smallness with cutoffs, and the diagonal's representability".

items.name: Theorem I.4.1(ii) (points of Bun_G)
items.statement: The points |Bun_G| are naturally in bijection with Kottwitz' set B(G) of G-isocrystals.
items.note: Body: Theorem III.0.2(ii), from Theorem III.2.2 (Fargues, Anschütz = Theorem I.2.6). BunGAndNewtonStrata:BG2:uniformization: "Prove the bijection |Bun_G| → B(G), geometric-base independence".

items.name: Theorem I.4.1(iii) (ν semicontinuous, κ locally constant)
items.statement: The map ν : |Bun_G| → B(G) → (X_*(T)^+_ℚ)^Γ is semicontinuous, and κ : |Bun_G| → B(G) → π_1(G_Ē)_Γ is locally constant. Equivalently, |Bun_G| → B(G) is continuous when B(G) carries the order topology.
items.note: Body: Theorem III.2.3 ([SW20, Cor. 22.5.1]; upper semicontinuity of ν, reducing to GL_n / Theorem I.3.4 via [RR96]) and Theorem III.2.7 (κ locally constant; via z-extensions and Beauville–Laszlo uniformization §III.3, or Borovoi's abelianized set). Corollary III.2.8 recovers [RR96, Cor. 3.11]. BunGAndNewtonStrata:BG2:uniformization: "Prove kappa locally constant using the source z-extension route ... prove nu semicontinuous by faithful-representation HN theory"; BG1 fixes the order topology.

items.name: Theorem I.4.1(iv) (strata Bun_G^b ≅ [∗/G̃_b])
items.statement: For any b ∈ B(G), the subfunctor i^b : Bun_G^b = Bun_G ×_{|Bun_G|} {b} ⊂ Bun_G is locally closed and isomorphic to [∗/G̃_b], where G̃_b is a v-sheaf of groups such that G̃_b → ∗ is representable in locally spatial diamonds with π_0 G̃_b = G_b(E). The connected component G̃_b° ⊂ G̃_b of the identity is cohomologically smooth of dimension ⟨2ρ, ν_b⟩.
items.note: Body: Theorem III.0.2(v), Proposition III.5.1–III.5.3 (G̃_b° a successive extension of positive Banach–Colmez spaces); stratum dimension Proposition IV.1.22 (ℓ-dimension −⟨2ρ,ν_b⟩). BunGAndNewtonStrata:BG3 plans: "construct the full automorphism v-group Gtilde_b, its map to J_b(E), connected kernel and quotient description Bun_G^b = [*/Gtilde_b] ... prove its ell-cohomological smoothness and dimension pairing <2rho,nu_b>".

items.name: Theorem I.4.1(v) (semistable locus)
items.statement: The semistable locus Bun_G^ss ⊂ Bun_G is open, and Bun_G^ss ≅ ⊔_{b∈B(G)_basic} [∗/G_b(E)] (G_b(E) viewed as the v-sheaf of continuous maps into it). E.g. Pic := Bun_{GL_1} ≅ ⊔_ℤ [∗/E^×].
items.note: Body: Theorem III.0.2(iv) = Theorem III.4.5 (with Proposition III.4.2, Corollary III.4.3, Theorem III.2.4 for b = 1). BunGAndNewtonStrata:BG3: "For basic b prove the classifying-stack description by J_b(E), and prove that the union of basic strata is open".

items.name: Theorem I.4.1(vi) (local charts π_b : M_b → Bun_G)
items.statement: For any b ∈ B(G) there is a map π_b : M_b → Bun_G that is representable in locally spatial diamonds, partially proper and cohomologically smooth, where M_b parametrizes G-bundles E with an increasing ℚ-filtration whose associated graded is, at all geometric points, isomorphic to E_b with its slope grading. The v-stack M_b is representable in locally spatial diamonds, partially proper and cohomologically smooth over [∗/G_b(E)].
items.note: Body: Theorem V.0.1(o) = Theorem V.3.7 and Proposition V.3.5–V.3.6; cohomological smoothness via the Jacobian criterion (Theorem I.4.2 = IV.4.2), M_b open in M_Z^sm for Z the flag variety of ℚ-filtrations. Example GL_2 (p. 22): M̃_b = BC(O(−1)[1]) for the degeneration O(1/2) ⇝ O ⊕ O(1). BunGAndNewtonStrata:BG4 plans: "Construct the filtered-bundle chart M_b ... Prove representability, partial properness and cohomological smoothness over [*/J_b(E)] and for M_b → Bun_G in FS V.3's precise sense".

items.name: Theorem I.4.1(vii) (Bun_G is a smooth Artin stack of dimension 0)
items.statement: The v-stack Bun_G is a cohomologically smooth Artin stack of dimension 0.
items.note: Body: Theorem IV.1.19 (ℓ-cohomologically smooth Artin v-stack of ℓ-dimension 0, via the Beauville–Laszlo cover ⊔_µ̄ [G(E)∖Gr_{G,µ̄}] → Bun_G); Artin v-stacks: Definition IV.1.1. Also formally from (vi). BunGAndNewtonStrata:BG2:smooth-Artin: "Prove FS IV.1.19: Bun_G is an ℓ-cohomologically smooth Artin v-stack of ℓ-dimension zero".

items.name: Connected components of Bun_G
items.statement: Bun_G = ⊔_{α∈π_1(G)_Γ} Bun_G^α (decomposition by κ), and each connected component Bun_G^α admits a unique semistable point. E.g. Bun_{GL_2} = ⊔_{α∈½ℤ} Bun^α_{GL_2}, G_b(E) = GL_2(E) for b ∈ ℤ and D^× (D|E the quaternion algebra) for b ∈ ½ℤ ∖ ℤ.
items.note: Body: Corollary IV.1.23 (κ : π_0(Bun_G) ≅ π_1(G)_Γ, proved using the ℓ-dimension of strata) with Theorem I.4.1(iii),(v). Planned: the BunGAndNewtonStrata packet node BG2:smooth-Artin/connected-components ('FS IV.1.23: the Kottwitz map is a bijection on connected components … The Kottwitz map induces a BIJECTION kappa : pi_0(Bun_G) -> pi_1(G)_Gamma'); the unique semistable point per component is κ : B(G)_basic ≅ π_1(G)_Γ, planned in BG1 ('Prove the classification/uniqueness assertions for B(G) … including basic classes'; packet node BG1/partial-order-on-B-of-G cites the proof of IV.1.23). The GL_2 example is illustrative. Review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21): a node of the draft BunGAndNewtonStrata packet states this (layer BunGAndNewtonStrata:BG2:smooth-Artin, BunGAndNewtonStrata:BG1), but that packet has not been reviewed or promoted, and the stage description alone does not name the statement. Packets count as planning only once promoted (PROTOCOL §6), so the item stays missing and is routed as a source to that layer.

items.name: Viehmann: |Bun_G| → B(G) is a homeomorphism (cited)
items.statement: The map |Bun_G| → B(G) is a homeomorphism (B(G) with the order topology). Previously proved for G = GL_n by Hansen [Han17] based on [BFH+22], extended to some classical groups by Hamann (unpublished).
items.note: Cited result [Vie21]; stated as Conjecture III.2.15 in the body (p. 97). Not used in the proofs. BunGAndNewtonStrata:BG1 explicitly excludes it: "not an unstated stronger closure equality or topological homeomorphism".

items.name: Theorem I.4.2 (Jacobian criterion for cohomological smoothness)
items.statement: Let S be a perfectoid space and Z → X_S a smooth map of (sousperfectoid) adic spaces (locally étale over a finite-dimensional ball over X_S); M_Z → S the v-sheaf of sections (S′-points: maps s : X_{S′} → Z lifting X_{S′} → X_S), and M_Z^sm ⊂ M_Z the open subspace where s*T_{Z/X_S} has everywhere positive Harder–Narasimhan slopes. Assume that Z → X_S can, locally on S, be embedded as a Zariski closed subset of an open subset of (the adic space) ℙⁿ_{X_S}. Then M_Z → S is representable in locally spatial diamonds, compactifiable, and of locally finite dim. trg. Moreover, M_Z^sm ⊂ M_Z is cohomologically smooth over S.
items.note: Body: Theorem IV.4.2 (p. 134; also gives ℓ-dimension = deg s*T_{Z/X_S}), Definition IV.4.1. Proof: formal smoothness (§IV.3, akin to absolute neighborhood retracts), [BS22] Zariski closed ⇒ strongly Zariski closed, ULA theory (§IV.2), deformation to the normal cone comparing with BC(s*T_{Z/X_S}). VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories:VS1 plans: "Construct formal smoothness and the Jacobian criterion of IV.3–IV.4 for the specified relative section functors on Fargues–Fontaine curves".

items.name: D(Bun_G, Λ) := D_lis(Bun_G, Λ) ⊂ D_■(Bun_G, Λ)
items.statement: For a ℤ_ℓ-algebra Λ, D(Bun_G, Λ) is defined as a certain full subcategory D_lis(Bun_G, Λ) ⊂ D_■(Bun_G, Λ) of the category of solid complexes of Λ-modules on the v-site of Bun_G. In the solid formalism every pullback f* has a left adjoint f_♮ satisfying base change and a projection formula (while Rf_! fails to exist in general).
items.note: Body: Chapter VII (solid sheaves VII.1, four functors VII.2, relative homology f_♮ VII.3, lisse-étale sheaves VII.6, D_lis(Bun_G) VII.7). Planned: VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories:VS2 ("Construct D_solid(X,Lambda) ... four operations and relative homology f-sharp in the FS VII.2–VII.3 range") and VS3 ("Define D_lis of an Artin v-stack as the stable subcategory closed under sums generated by f-sharp Lambda").

items.name: Theorem I.5.1(i) (semiorthogonal decomposition)
items.statement: Let Λ be any ℤ_ℓ-algebra. Via excision triangles, there is an infinite semiorthogonal decomposition of D(Bun_G, Λ) into the various D(Bun_G^b, Λ) for b ∈ B(G).
items.note: Body: Proposition VII.7.3 (D_lis; on quasicompact opens) and Theorem V.0.1(i) (torsion Λ, D_ét). Planned in VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories:VS4: "Prove localization triangles and the infinite semiorthogonal decomposition along the HN strata".

items.name: Theorem I.5.1(ii) (strata are smooth representations)
items.statement: Let Λ be any ℤ_ℓ-algebra. For each b ∈ B(G), pullback along Bun_G^b ≅ [∗/G̃_b] → [∗/G_b(E)] gives an equivalence D([∗/G_b(E)], Λ) ≅ D(Bun_G^b, Λ), and D([∗/G_b(E)], Λ) ≅ D(G_b(E), Λ) is equivalent to the derived category of the category of smooth representations of G_b(E) on Λ-modules.
items.note: Body: Proposition VII.7.1 (D_lis); torsion case Theorem V.1.1 and Proposition V.2.2 (Theorem V.0.1(ii)). Planned in VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories:VS4: "Identify D_et([*/H],Lambda) with the enhanced derived category of smooth H-representations ... prove the connected-kernel invariance giving the category for nonbasic Bun_G^b. Extend to D_lis in the precise coefficient range of VII.7".

items.name: Theorem I.5.1(iii) (compact generation)
items.statement: Let Λ be any ℤ_ℓ-algebra. D(Bun_G, Λ) is compactly generated, and A ∈ D(Bun_G, Λ) is compact iff for all b ∈ B(G) the restriction i^{b*}A ∈ D(Bun_G^b, Λ) ≅ D(G_b(E), Λ) is compact, and zero for almost all b. Compactness in D(G_b(E), Λ) is equivalent to lying in the thick triangulated subcategory generated by c-Ind_K^{G_b(E)} Λ as K runs over open pro-p subgroups of G_b(E).
items.note: Body: Proposition VII.7.2 (i^{b*} has left adjoint π_{b♮}q_b^*, via 'strict locality' RΓ(M_b, A) ≅ RΓ([∗/G_b(E)], A)), Proposition VII.7.4; torsion case Theorem V.4.1, Corollary V.4.4. Planned in VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories:VS4: "Characterize compact objects by compact restrictions with finite stratum support, and by the thick closure of compact induction from pro-p open subgroups".

items.name: Theorem I.5.1(iv) (Bernstein–Zelevinsky duality)
items.statement: Let Λ be any ℤ_ℓ-algebra. On D(Bun_G, Λ)^ω there is a Bernstein–Zelevinsky duality functor 𝔻_BZ : (D(Bun_G, Λ)^ω)^op → D(Bun_G, Λ)^ω with a functorial identification R Hom(A, B) ≅ π_♮(𝔻_BZ(A) ⊗^𝕃_Λ B) for B ∈ D(Bun_G, Λ), π : Bun_G → ∗. 𝔻_BZ is an equivalence and 𝔻_BZ² ≅ id. It is compatible with usual Bernstein–Zelevinsky duality on D(G_b(E), Λ) for basic b.
items.note: Body: Proposition VII.7.6 (D_lis); torsion case Theorem V.5.1. Planned in VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories:VS5: "Construct Bernstein–Zelevinsky duality on compact Bun_G objects using the partial-support functor; prove biduality and its basic-stratum comparison".

items.name: Theorem I.5.1(v) (ULA objects are admissible)
items.statement: Let Λ be any ℤ_ℓ-algebra. A ∈ D(Bun_G, Λ) is universally locally acyclic (with respect to Bun_G → ∗) iff for all b ∈ B(G) the restriction i^{b*}A ∈ D(G_b(E), Λ) is admissible, i.e. (i^{b*}A)^K is perfect for all pro-p open subgroups K ⊂ G_b(E). ULA complexes are preserved by Verdier duality and satisfy Verdier biduality.
items.note: Body: Definition VII.7.8 and Proposition VII.7.9 (D_lis; ULA defined via the Künneth-type map), Proposition VII.7.7; torsion case Theorem V.7.1, Theorems V.6.1–V.6.2. Planned in VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories:VS5: "Separately construct Verdier duality on ULA objects and prove that ULA is equivalent to perfection of K-invariants on every stratum for every appropriate pro-p open K".

items.name: Theorem I.5.2 (vanishing of cohomology compactly supported at one end)
items.statement: Let X be a spatial diamond such that f : X → ∗ is partially proper and of finite dim. trg. Then for any affinoid perfectoid space S, the base change X_S = X × S naturally admits two ends. Taking compactly supported cohomology with respect to one end (but no support condition at the other end), RΓ_{∂-c}(X_S, A) = 0 for all A ∈ D⁺_■(X, ℤ_ℓ) (resp. all A ∈ D_■(X, ℤ_ℓ) if f is ℓ-cohomologically smooth). Example: X = Spa F̄_q((t)), X_S = D*_S, RΓ_{∂-c}(D*_S, ℤ_ℓ) = 0, so Spa F̄_q[[t]] is 'strictly local'.
items.note: Body: Theorem IV.5.3 (D_ét, torsion Λ; Definition IV.5.2 of Rβ_{!±}; Lemma IV.5.1 for the disc) and Theorem VII.2.10 (solid version, stated for X → ∗ proper with X spatial, which for spatial X is the same as partially proper). Key input for Theorem I.5.1(iii) (applied to M̃_b ∖ ∗). The D_ét theorem is already planned: accepted VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories decomposition node VS0/partial-compactly-supported-vanishing ('FS IV.5: partially compactly supported cohomology towards one end vanishes', with the base case on the punctured disc). What remains missing is the solid ℤ_ℓ-version VII.2.10 in which Theorem I.5.2 is stated (D_■^+(X,ℤ_ℓ), or all of D_■ for X → ∗ ℓ-cohomologically smooth); VS2 plans solid sheaves 'in the FS VII.2–VII.3 range' but names no such node.

items.name: Local Hecke stack Hck^I_G and Beilinson–Drinfeld Grassmannian Gr^I_G over (Div¹)^I
items.statement: For a finite set I, (Div¹)^I parametrizes degree 1 Cartier divisors D_i ⊂ X_S; B⁺ is the completion of O_{X_S} along ∪D_i and B its localization inverting the D_i; L⁺G = L⁺_{(Div¹)^I}G, LG with values G(B⁺), G(B). Hck^I_G = [L⁺G∖LG/L⁺G] → (Div¹)^I (already defined over Div^d = (Div¹)^d/Σ_d, d = |I|), Gr^I_G = LG/L⁺G → (Div¹)^I, Hck^I_G = L⁺G∖Gr^I_G. Gr^I_G is a small v-sheaf, an increasing union of closed subsheaves proper and representable in spatial diamonds (bounded relative position, [SW20]); L⁺G is an inverse limit of cohomologically smooth truncated positive loop groups representable in locally spatial diamonds, acting on bounded subsets through a finite-dimensional quotient.
items.note: Body: §VI.1 (Definitions VI.1.1, VI.1.5–VI.1.8, Propositions VI.1.7–VI.1.12), §VI.2 (Schubert varieties). GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS0:loop-geometry plans: "Construct L+G, LG, the étale quotient LG/L+G and double quotient local Hecke stack ... For a finite set I construct ordered leg divisors on Div^1 ... Prove properness of bounded Schubert diamonds, dimension <2rho,mu>".

items.name: Convolution on D_ét(Hck^I_G, Λ)^bd and the relative perverse t-structure
items.statement: For Λ killed by a power of ℓ, D_ét(Hck^I_G, Λ)^bd (objects with quasicompact support over (Div¹)^I) is monoidal under A ⋆ B = Rm_*(p_1^*A ⊗^𝕃_Λ p_2^*B), via Hck^I_G ×_{(Div¹)^I} Hck^I_G ←(p_1,p_2)– L⁺G∖LG ×^{L⁺G} LG/L⁺G –m→ Hck^I_G (m ind-proper with fibres Gr^I_G; associativity by proper base change). There is a relative perverse t-structure (perverse iff perverse on every geometric fibre of (Div¹)^I, Schubert cells of dimension Σ_i⟨2ρ, µ_i⟩), for which ⋆ is left t-exact (t-exactness failing only through non-flatness over Λ); ULA-ness over (Div¹)^I is preserved by ⋆.
items.note: Body: §VI.7 (perverse sheaves), §VI.8 (convolution, Proposition VI.8.1–VI.8.2), using hyperbolic localization and degeneration to the Witt vector affine Grassmannian [Zhu17], [BS17]. Remark I.6.1 notes a scheme analogue [HS23]. Planned: GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS2:correspondences ("Construct convolution diagrams, the convolution map and operation"), GS1 ("Construct the relative perverse t-structure on bounded constructible complexes"), GS2:Satake-closure ("prove perversity, flatness and ULA preservation").

items.name: Definition I.6.2 (Satake category Sat^I_G(Λ))
items.statement: Sat^I_G(Λ) ⊂ D_ét(Hck^I_G, Λ)^bd is the category of all A ∈ D_ét(Hck^I_G, Λ)^bd that are perverse, flat over Λ (i.e. A ⊗^𝕃_Λ M is perverse for all Λ-modules M), and universally locally acyclic over (Div¹)^I. It is monoidal under convolution and covariantly functorial in I.
items.note: Body: Definition VI.0.1, Definition VI.9.1. GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS2:correspondences plans: "Define Satake objects by the equivariance, relative perversity, ULA and coefficient flatness conditions of FS VI.6–VI.8".

items.name: Fusion product: symmetric monoidal structure on Sat^I_G(Λ)
items.statement: For I = I_1 ⊔ … ⊔ I_k, Hck^I_G ×_{(Div¹)^I} (Div¹)^{I;I_1,…,I_k} ≅ Π_j Hck^{I_j}_G ×_{(Div¹)^I} (Div¹)^{I;I_1,…,I_k} over the open locus where x_i ≠ x_{i′} for i, i′ in different I_j; the restriction Sat^I_G(Λ) → Sat^{I;I_1,…,I_k}_G(Λ) is fully faithful and contains the essential image of ⊠_j, giving ∗_{j=1}^k : Π_j Sat^{I_j}_G(Λ) → Sat^I_G(Λ) independent of ordering, hence (via Sat^{I⊔I} → Sat^I) a symmetric monoidal structure ∗ on Sat^I_G(Λ) commuting with ⋆ and therefore refining ⋆ (with sign-modified commutativity constraint depending on parity of supports).
items.note: Body: §VI.9 (Proposition VI.9.3–VI.9.6). GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS3:fusion plans: "Over disjoint-leg loci prove factorization into products of single-leg Grassmannians. Construct fusion by the source's ULA extension along collision diagonals ... Verify the Koszul/sign ... normalization".

items.name: Fibre functor F^I : Sat^I_G(Λ) → Rep_{W_E^I}(Λ) and Tannakian group Ǧ
items.statement: Restricting A ∈ Sat^I_G(Λ) to Gr^I_G and pushing forward to (Div¹)^I gives local systems of Λ-modules on (Div¹)^I, which by a version of Drinfeld's lemma are representations of W_E^I; this defines a symmetric monoidal fibre functor F^I : Sat^I_G(Λ) → Rep_{W_E^I}(Λ) (continuous representations on finite projective Λ-modules). Tannaka duality gives a Hopf algebra in Ind Rep_{W_E^I}(Λ) with Sat^I_G(Λ) its representations; it is the I-fold tensor power of the one for I = {∗}, given by an affine group scheme Ǧ over Λ with W_E-action.
items.note: Body: Proposition VI.9.2 (local systems on (Div¹)^I vs W_E^I-representations), §VI.10 (Tannakian reconstruction, Propositions VI.10.1–VI.10.3). Planned: GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS4:integral-dual-group ("Construct the total cohomology fibre functor, prove exactness, faithfulness, tensor compatibility and duals in the precise integral category, and reconstruct its affine group scheme"); Drinfeld's lemma in VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories:VS1.

items.name: Theorem I.6.3 (geometric Satake: Ǧ ≅ Ĝ_Λ)
items.statement: There is a canonical isomorphism Ǧ ≅ Ĝ_Λ with the Langlands dual group, under which the action of W_E on Ǧ agrees with the usual action of W_E on Ĝ up to an explicit cyclotomic twist. If √q ∈ Λ, the cyclotomic twist can be trivialized, and Sat^I_G(Λ) is naturally equivalent to the category of (Ĝ ⋊ W_E)^I-representations on finite projective Λ-modules.
items.note: Body: Theorem VI.0.2 = Theorem VI.11.1 (Λ killed by a power of ℓ, then limit to ℤ_ℓ). Proof: generic fibre reductive by geometric semisimplicity (Witt degeneration + decomposition theorem), tori and rank 1 (PGL_2, minuscule cell), hyperbolic localization to Levis, Bruhat–Tits maximal compactness of Ĝ(ℤ_ℓ); explicit (cyclotomic) pinning; purely local proof, valid for any Λ. Planned: GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS4:integral-dual-group ("identify the group with the pinned dual. ... distinguish the geometric Weil action from the standard pinned action, with the normalization isomorphism involving rho and the chosen sqrt(q)"), GS4:rational-reductivity.

items.name: Proposition I.6.4 (sw* is the Chevalley involution twisted by ρ̂(−1))
items.statement: Let sw be the involution of 𝓗ck_G reversing the roles of the two G-torsors (inversion on LG). The action of sw* on Sat_G induces the automorphism of Ĝ that is the Chevalley involution of the split group Ĝ, conjugated by ρ̂(−1).
items.note: Body: Proposition VI.0.3 = Proposition VI.12.1 (p. 239; notes a sign ρ̂(−1) overlooked in earlier literature). Used in Theorem I.7.2 / IX.2.2 and Proposition IX.5.3. GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS4:integral-dual-group plans: "Construct the Chevalley involution and prove its compatibility with Verdier duality, inversion of modifications and representation duals".

items.name: Hyperbolic localization on Gr^I_G (constant term functors)
items.statement: For opposite parabolics P⁺, P⁻ ⊂ G with common Levi M and the diagram Gr^I_G ←q^±– Gr^I_{P^±} –p^±→ Gr^I_M, set CT⁺ = R(p⁺)_!(q⁺)^*, CT⁻ = R(p⁻)_*R(q⁻)^! : D_ét(Gr^I_G, Λ)^bd → D_ét(Gr^I_M, Λ)^bd. There is a natural transformation CT⁻ → CT⁺, and it is an equivalence when restricted to L⁺G-equivariant objects; consequently hyperbolic localization commutes with all colimits and limits, preserves relative perversity and universal local acyclicity, and commutes with any base change.
items.note: Body: §VI.3 (Proposition VI.3.1, Corollary VI.3.5), a special case of Theorem I.6.5 = IV.6.5. CT⁺ classically is the Satake transform (integration along U⁺-orbits). GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS1 plans "Construct positive-loop equivariance, orbit stratifications, semi-infinite orbits ... finiteness needed for compact-support cohomology and hyperbolic-localization comparisons".

items.name: Theorem I.6.5 (Braden's hyperbolic localization for diamonds)
items.statement: Let S be a small v-stack, f : X → S proper and representable in spatial diamonds with dim. trg f < ∞, with a G_m-action on X/S (G_m(R,R⁺) = R^×), fixed points X⁰ ⊂ X (a closed substack), and attractor/repeller loci X⁺, X⁻ ⊂ X (disjoint unions of locally closed subspaces on which t → 0, resp. t → ∞, has a limit), giving X ←q^±– X^± –p^±→ X⁰. With L⁺ = R(p⁺)_!(q⁺)^*, L⁻ = R(p⁻)_*R(q⁻)^! : D_ét(X, Λ) → D_ét(X⁰, Λ), the natural transformation L⁻ → L⁺ is an equivalence when restricted to the essential image of D_ét(X/G_m, Λ) → D_ét(X, Λ).
items.note: Body: Theorem IV.6.5 under Hypothesis IV.6.1 (precise form of the attractor/repeller assumption), Proposition IV.6.2, Lemma IV.6.3; cf. [Bra03], [Ric19]. VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories:VS1 plans: "Construct attractor/repeller correspondences, hyperbolic localization and the comparison map of FS IV.6, including equivariance and boundedness hypotheses".

items.name: Vanishing of partially compactly supported cohomology for G_m-equivariant sheaves
items.statement: If Y → S is partially proper with a G_m-action such that Y/G_m is qcqs over S, then Y admits two ends, and the partially compactly supported cohomology of Y with coefficients in any A ∈ D_ét(Y/G_m, Λ) vanishes identically.
items.note: Principle used to prove Theorem I.6.5. Body: Proposition IV.6.6 (affinoid perfectoid base, partially proper Y → S of locally spatial diamonds, Y/G_m qcqs: the partially supported cohomology lim_n Rf_*(j_{n!}A|_{V_n}) vanishes), applied in the proof of Theorem IV.6.5 with Lemma IV.6.8. Planned only as part of VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories:VS1's "hyperbolic localization and the comparison map of FS IV.6"; the principle is not named separately.

items.name: Hecke operators T_V for V ∈ Sat^I_G(Λ) with W_E^I-equivariance
items.statement: Using Bun_G ←h₁– Hck^I_G –h₂→ Bun_G × (Div¹)^I and q : Hck^I_G → 𝓗ck^I_G, T_V = Rh_{2*}(h_1^* ⊗^𝕃_Λ q^*S_V) : D(Bun_G, Λ) → D(Bun_G × (Div¹)^I, Λ) for V ∈ Sat^I_G(Λ) (Λ killed by a power of ℓ), extended to all ℤ_ℓ-algebras Λ; its image lies in the objects locally constant along (Div¹)^I, giving T_V : D(Bun_G, Λ) → D(Bun_G, Λ)^{BW_E^I}, using that D(Bun_G, Λ) → D(Bun_G × Spd Ĕ̂, Λ) (Ĕ̂ the completed algebraic closure) is an equivalence. D(Bun_G, Λ)^{BW_E^I} requires upgrading D(Bun_G, Λ) to a condensed ∞-category (Remark I.7.1).
items.note: Body: Chapter IX introduction, Theorem IX.0.1, §IX.1 (condensed ∞-categories, Proposition IX.1.1–IX.1.2), Proposition IX.2.1, Corollary IX.2.3–IX.2.4, Proposition VII.7.3 (base-change equivalence). HeckeStacksAndLocalShtukas:HS1 plans: "define T_V by the actual pull-tensor-push construction ... Construct the continuous W_E^I action through Drinfeld's lemma and the condensed enriched functor category".

items.name: Theorem I.7.2 (Hecke operators preserve compact and ULA objects; duality)
items.statement: The functor T_V : D(Bun_G, Λ) → D(Bun_G, Λ) (forgetting W_E^I-equivariance) preserves compact objects and universally locally acyclic objects. It commutes with Bernstein–Zelevinsky and Verdier duality: 𝔻_BZ(T_V(A)) ≅ T_{sw*V^∨}(𝔻_BZ(A)) and R𝓗om(T_V(A), Λ) ≅ T_{(sw*V)^∨} R𝓗om(A, Λ), sw* the involution of Sat^I_G of Proposition I.6.4. (T_V ∘ T_W ≅ T_{V⊗W}, so T_V is left and right adjoint to T_{V*}.)
items.note: Body: Theorem IX.2.2 (= IX.0.1(i); also commutes with all limits and colimits). HeckeStacksAndLocalShtukas:HS1 plans: "Prove preservation of D_lis, compact objects and ULA objects in the source's range"; duality uses VS5 and GS4's sw.

items.name: Corollary I.7.3 (finiteness of cohomology of moduli of local shtukas)
items.statement: Let Λ be killed by ℓⁿ. For conjugacy classes {µ_i}_{i∈I} of cocharacters with fields of definition E_i/E and b ∈ B(G), let f_K : (Sht_{(G,b,µ•),K})_{K⊂G(E)} → Π_{i∈I} Spd Ĕ_i be the tower of moduli spaces of local shtukas [SW20, Lecture XXIII] with étale period maps π_K : Sht_{(G,b,µ•),K} → Gr^tw_{G,Π Spd Ĕ_i,≤µ•}, W = ⊠_{i∈I} V_{µ_i}, S_W the corresponding sheaf. Then Rf_{K!}S_W ∈ D([∗/G_b(E)] × Π_i Spd Ĕ_i, Λ) is equipped with partial Frobenii, hence descends to D([∗/G_b(E)] × Π_i Spd Ĕ_i/φ_i^ℤ, Λ); it lies in D(G_b(E), Λ)^{BΠ_i W_{E_i}} and its restriction to D(G_b(E), Λ) is compact. For any admissible G_b(E)-representation ρ, R Hom_{G_b(E)}(Rf_{K!}S_W, ρ) ∈ D(Λ)^{BΠW_{E_i}} is a representation of Π_i W_{E_i} on a perfect complex of Λ-modules; lim_{→K} R Hom_{G_b(E)}(Rf_{K!}S_W, ρ) is a complex of admissible G(E)-representations with Π_i W_{E_i}-action. If ρ is compact, so is lim_{→K} R Hom_{G_b(E)}(Rf_{K!}S_W, ρ) as a complex of G(E)-representations.
items.note: Body: §IX.3 (Theorem IX.3.1 for local Shimura varieties; Proposition IX.3.2 for the general statement, proved by 'the same arguments'). For I = {∗}, µ minuscule, proves [RV14, Proposition 6.1] unconditionally and [RV14, Remark 6.2 (iii)] (finite length for Q̄_ℓ, ρ of finite length). HeckeStacksAndLocalShtukas:HS3 plans: "Prove the source's finiteness, compactness and admissibility statements using compact Hecke kernels and the pro-p compact-induction generators"; moduli in HS2.

items.name: Theorem I.8.1 (the scheme of L-parameters Z¹(W_E, Ĝ))
items.statement: There is a scheme Z¹(W_E, Ĝ) over ℤ_ℓ whose Λ-valued points, for a ℤ_ℓ-algebra Λ, are the condensed 1-cocycles φ : W_E → Ĝ(Λ) (Λ regarded as a relatively discrete condensed ℤ_ℓ-algebra, M ↦ M_disc ⊗_{ℤ_ℓ,disc} ℤ_ℓ; Ĝ with its usual W_E-action factoring through a finite quotient Q). Z¹(W_E, Ĝ) is a union of open and closed affine subschemes Z¹(W_E/P, Ĝ) as P runs through open subgroups of the wild inertia subgroup of W_E, and each Z¹(W_E/P, Ĝ) is a flat local complete intersection over ℤ_ℓ of dimension dim G.
items.note: Body: Theorem VIII.0.1 = Theorem VIII.1.3 (Definition VIII.1.1; following [DHKM20], [Zhu20]: restriction Z¹(W_E/P, Ĝ) → Z¹(W, Ĝ) to a discretization W is an isomorphism). LanglandsParameterStacks:LP1 plans: "Construct the affine scheme Z^1(W_E/P,dual G) over Z_ell ... glue the open-and-closed pieces over P to Z^1(W_E,dual G). Prove flatness and local complete-intersection structure, including the dimension dim G"; LP0 the discretization.

items.name: Theorem I.8.2 (invariant theory of Z¹(W_E/P, Ĝ); excursion presentation)
items.statement: Assume ℓ does not divide the order of π_0 Z(G) (equivalently, of π_1(Ĝ)_tor). Then H^i(Ĝ, O(Z¹(W_E/P, Ĝ))) = 0 for i > 0 and the formation of the invariants O(Z¹(W_E/P, Ĝ))^Ĝ commutes with any base change. O(Z¹(W_E/P, Ĝ))^Ĝ = colim_{(n, F_n → W)} O(Z¹(F_n, Ĝ))^Ĝ, the colimit over all maps from a free group F_n to W ⊂ W_E/P, with Z¹(F_n, Ĝ) ≅ Ĝⁿ under simultaneous twisted Ĝ-conjugation.
items.locator: Chapter I, §I.8, Theorem I.8.2 (first part), p. 33
items.note: Body: Theorem VIII.0.2 = Theorem VIII.5.1 (reduced to Theorem VIII.5.2 over F̄_ℓ), Theorem VIII.3.6, Definition VIII.3.4 (Exc(W, Ĝ)). Proof via modular representation theory (good filtrations, Theorem I.8.3). Planned: LanglandsParameterStacks:LP2:integral-invariants ("Prove the presentation of the invariant algebra by all finite free-group cocycle spaces mapping to W ... impose ell not dividing the torsion order of pi_1(dual G)"), LP3 ("vanishing of higher group cohomology of the cocycle coordinate algebra and base change of invariants").

items.name: Theorem I.8.2 (Perf of the parameter stack generated by Rep Ĝ)
items.statement: Assume ℓ does not divide the order of π_0 Z(G). The ∞-category Perf(Z¹(W_E/P, Ĝ)/Ĝ) is generated under cones and retracts by the image of Rep(Ĝ) → Perf(Z¹(W_E/P, Ĝ)/Ĝ), and Ind Perf(Z¹(W_E/P, Ĝ)/Ĝ) (printed: Ind Perf(Z¹(W_E/P, Ĝ))) is equivalent to the ∞-category of modules over O(Z¹(W_E/P, Ĝ)) in Ind Perf(∗/Ĝ). All results of Theorem I.8.2 also hold with Q_ℓ-coefficients, without the assumption on ℓ.
items.locator: Chapter I, §I.8, Theorem I.8.2 (second part), p. 33
items.note: Body: Theorem VIII.5.1 (second half), Theorem VIII.5.2; this is the key input to Theorem I.10.1 (X.3). The printed 'Ind Perf(Z¹(W_E/P, Ĝ))' omits the quotient by Ĝ, which Theorem VIII.5.1 (p. 293) has; Theorem VIII.0.2 (p. 278) repeats the same slip (PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E3, E57). The statement here uses the body's Ind Perf(Z¹(W_E/P, Ĝ)/Ĝ). LanglandsParameterStacks:LP4 plans: "Prove generation by representation bundles under cones, shifts and retracts, and the comparison of Ind-Perf with module objects over the cocycle algebra in Ind-Perf(B dual G)".

items.name: Theorem I.8.3 (fixed points of prime-to-ℓ solvable actions; good filtrations)
items.statement: Let G be a reductive group over an algebraically closed field L of characteristic ℓ, and P a finite solvable group of order prime to ℓ acting on G. The fixed point group H = G^P is a smooth linear algebraic group with H° reductive and π_0 H of order prime to ℓ. For any representation V of G admitting a good G-filtration, V|_{H°} admits a good H°-filtration. Moreover, the image of Perf(∗/G) → Perf(∗/H) generates the whole category under cones and retracts.
items.note: Body: Theorem VIII.0.3 (§VIII.5.3), Theorem VIII.5.15 (Donkin subgroup), Proposition VIII.5.17–VIII.5.21 (generation, uniform proof). Recovers the Levi case (classical) and Brundan's conjecture P = ℤ/2ℤ ([Bru98], [vdK01]). LanglandsParameterStacks:LP3 plans: "For a finite group P of order prime to ell acting on a reductive group in characteristic ell, construct the fixed-point subgroup, prove smoothness/reductivity of its identity component and the prime-to-ell component-group order. Under the source's solvability hypothesis prove the Donkin subgroup property and generation of perfect complexes by restriction".

items.name: Excursion operators on Schur-irreducible A ∈ D(Bun_G, Q̄_ℓ)
items.statement: Let Λ = Q̄_ℓ with fixed √q ∈ Q̄_ℓ and A ∈ D(Bun_G, Q̄_ℓ) Schur-irreducible (End(A) = Q̄_ℓ), e.g. the extension by zero of an irreducible smooth G(E)-representation along [∗/G(E)] ↪ Bun_G. For a finite set I, a representation V of (Ĝ ⋊ W_E)^I over Q̄_ℓ, maps α : Q̄_ℓ → V|_Ĝ, β : V|_Ĝ → Q̄_ℓ (restriction to the diagonal Ĝ ⊂ (Ĝ ⋊ W_E)^I) and γ_i ∈ W_E (i ∈ I), the excursion operator is the endomorphism A –T_α→ T_V(A) –(γ_i)_{i∈I}→ T_V(A) –T_β→ A, an element of Q̄_ℓ.
items.note: Following V. Lafforgue [Laf18]. Body: §VIII.4 (Theorem VIII.4.1, Definition VIII.4.2 'excursion datum'), §IX.4–IX.5. ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction:ES0 plans: "Construct excursion operators from a finite leg set, a matrix coefficient/invariant function, creation by a coevaluation map, the prescribed tuple of Weil elements and annihilation by evaluation".

items.name: Proposition I.9.1 (existence and uniqueness of φ_A)
items.statement: For A ∈ D(Bun_G, Q̄_ℓ) Schur-irreducible, there is a unique continuous semisimple L-parameter φ_A : W_E → Ĝ(Q̄_ℓ) such that for all (I, V, α, β, (γ_i)_{i∈I}), the excursion operator A –T_α→ T_V(A) –(γ_i)→ T_V(A) –T_β→ A is multiplication by the scalar Q̄_ℓ –α→ V –(φ_A(γ_i))_{i∈I}→ V –β→ Q̄_ℓ.
items.note: Essentially [Laf18, Proposition 11.7]. Body: Definition/Proposition IX.0.4 (= IX.4.1): for any algebraically closed L over ℤ_ℓ[√q], End(A) = L as condensed algebras, φ_A : W_E → Ĝ(L) ⋊ Q, unique up to Ĝ-conjugacy; uses Proposition VIII.3.8. Planned: ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction:ES5 ("construct FS Definition/Proposition IX.4.1's continuous semisimple parameter ... Prove the defining identity for every excursion datum"), LanglandsParameterStacks:LP2:semisimple-characters ("Prove FS VIII.3.8").

items.name: Definition I.9.2(i) (Bernstein center of G(E))
items.statement: Z(G(E), Λ) = π_0 End(id_{D(G(E),Λ)}) = lim_{←K⊂G(E)} Z(Λ[K∖G(E)/K]), where K runs over open pro-p subgroups of G(E) and Λ[K∖G(E)/K] = End_{G(E)}(c-Ind_K^{G(E)} Λ) is the Hecke algebra of level K.
items.note: Body: Definition IX.0.2(i). ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction:ES0 plans: "Define the algebra of natural endomorphisms of the identity ... Compare the degree-zero center with the ordinary smooth-representation Bernstein center"; Hecke algebras in SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.1.

items.name: Definition I.9.2(ii) (geometric Bernstein center and its Hecke-commuting part)
items.statement: Z^geom(G, Λ) = π_0 End(id_{D_lis(Bun_G,Λ)}); Z^geom_Hecke(G, Λ) ⊂ Z^geom(G, Λ) is the subring of endomorphisms f : id → id commuting with Hecke operators: T_V(f(A)) = f(T_V(A)) ∈ End(T_V(A)) for all V ∈ Rep(Ĝ^I) and A ∈ D_lis(Bun_G, Λ). The inclusion D(G(E), Λ) ↪ D_lis(Bun_G, Λ) induces an algebra map Z^geom(G, Λ) → Z(G(E), Λ).
items.note: Body: Definition IX.0.2(ii). ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction:ES0: "Define the algebra of natural endomorphisms of the identity, its centrality and scalar structure on the chosen enhanced category".

items.name: Definition I.9.2(iii) (spectral Bernstein center)
items.statement: Z^spec(G, Λ) = O(Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)_Λ)^Ĝ, the ring of global functions on the quotient stack Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)_Λ/Ĝ.
items.note: Body: Definition IX.0.2(iii). Invariant algebra planned in LanglandsParameterStacks:LP2:integral-invariants ("Construct the invariant algebra and the affine coarse quotient on each finite-wild piece").

items.name: Proposition I.9.3 (map from the spectral to the (Hecke-)geometric Bernstein center)
items.statement: Let Λ be a ℤ_ℓ[√q]-algebra in which the order of π_0 Z(G) is invertible. There is a canonical map Z^spec(G, Λ) → Z^geom_Hecke(G, Λ) ⊂ Z^geom(G, Λ), and in particular a map Ψ_G : Z^spec(G, Λ) → Z(G(E), Λ).
items.note: Body: Corollary IX.0.3 = Theorem IX.5.2 (via Theorem VIII.4.1, Proposition IX.5.1 finite ramification, Theorem VIII.3.6). For G = GL_n the integral map is due to Helm–Moss [HM18]; Remark I.9.4: function-field analogue [GL17], agreement [LH23]. ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction:ES1:spectral-center plans: "When |π₀Z(G)| is invertible in Λ, use LP2:integral-invariants to construct the map from functions on the parameter stack to the categorical center, then to the relevant Bernstein center ... (FS IX.5.2)".

items.name: Conjecture I.9.5 (independence of ℓ) (statement)
items.statement: There is a natural ℚ-algebra Z^spec(G, ℚ) (global functions on the stack of L-parameters continuous for the discrete topology, i.e. trivial on an open subgroup of W_E) with Z^spec(G, ℚ) ⊗ ℚ_ℓ = Z^spec(G, ℚ_ℓ) for all ℓ ≠ p. Conjecture: there is a (necessarily unique) map Z^spec(G, ℚ(√q)) → Z(G(E), ℚ(√q)) that after base extension to any ℚ_ℓ, ℓ ≠ p, recovers the composite Z^spec(G, ℚ_ℓ(√q)) → Z^geom(G, ℚ_ℓ(√q)) → Z(G(E), ℚ_ℓ(√q)).
items.note: Open conjecture; not addressed in the body. Would give ℓ-independence of the constructed L-parameters. No stage plans it (ES4 excludes conjectural statements).

items.name: Haines' conjecture on Ψ_G and the stable Bernstein center (cited, statement)
items.statement: Conjectured (Haines [Hai14]; see [BKV15], [SS13, §6]): for G quasisplit, Ψ_G : Z^spec(G, Λ) → Z(G(E), Λ) is injective, and its image is the set of elements of the Bernstein center of G(E) whose corresponding distribution is invariant under stable conjugation.
items.note: Attributed conjecture, not used or proved in the paper; recorded for completeness. Owner: the accepted Part II ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralActionStableCenter ("Excursion operators and the spectral action, Part II: stability of the Fargues–Scholze Bernstein center", PAPER-HANSEN-26 route 1). Its review says that no ES stage mentions "the stable-center conjectures of Haines and Scholze–Shin", which is why that Part II was accepted. Hansen's Theorem 1.1 (Z^FS(G) ⊆ Z^vst(G)) proves part of the image assertion. Recorded as a statement, not a target.

items.name: Excursion operators via cohomology of local shtukas agree with the Bun_G construction
items.statement: For Λ a ℤ/ℓⁿ-algebra, I and V as above, let Sht_{(G,1,V),K} (b = 1, bound by the support of V) with period map π_K to Gr^tw_{G,Π_{i=1}^n Spd Ĕ} and perverse sheaf S_V; over the geometric diagonal x̄ : Spd Ĕ̂ → Π Spd Ĕ it becomes the one-leg space f_K^Δ : Sht_{(G,1,V|_Ĝ)} → Spd Ĕ̂ with S_{V|_Ĝ}, and α, β give maps from/to i_*Λ, i : G(E)/K = Sht_{(G,1,1),K} ↪ Sht_{(G,1,V|_Ĝ),K}. The resulting endomorphism c-Ind_K^{G(E)} Λ –α→ Rf^Δ_{K!}S_{V|_Ĝ} = (Rf_{K!}S_V)_{x̄} –(γ_i)→ (Rf_{K!}S_V)_{x̄} –β→ c-Ind_K^{G(E)} Λ (the (γ_i)-action from Corollary I.7.3) is precisely the Bun_G excursion operator applied to c-Ind_K^{G(E)} Λ; these endomorphisms are central in Λ[K∖G(E)/K] and their inverse limit over K gives the elements of the Bernstein center.
items.note: 'It follows from the definitions'; not separately proved in the body (uses §IX.3 and Corollary I.7.3). Footnote 5: the local-system property of local shtuka cohomology on (Div¹)^I seems inaccessible purely from the shtuka spaces (global analogue [Xue20]). ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction:ES4 plans: "For local shtuka cohomology recover the resulting commuting excursion operators and their compatibility with the two smooth group actions through the Hecke comparison". The statement writes Sht_{(G,1,1),K} for the no-leg space; p. 36 prints 'i : G(E)/K = Sht_{(G,1,Q̄_ℓ),K}' although Λ is a ℤ/ℓⁿ-algebra here (new misprint reported by this review). The index n in Π_{i=1}^n is printed as such, clashing with the n of ℤ/ℓⁿ; it means |I|.

items.name: Theorem I.9.6(i) (tori)
items.statement: If G = T is a torus, then π ↦ φ_π is the usual Langlands correspondence.
items.note: Body: Theorem IX.0.5 (Sections IX.6, IX.7); §IX.6 (torus case, reduction to induced tori and G_m). Planned in ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction:ES6:functoriality: "For a torus, resolve by induced tori and reduce to G_m ... φ_χ equals local class field theory".

items.name: Theorem I.9.6(ii) (twisting)
items.statement: The correspondence π ↦ φ_π is compatible with twisting.
items.note: Body: Theorem IX.0.5 (Sections IX.6, IX.7); §IX.6 (via G → G × (G/G_der)). Planned in ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction:ES6:functoriality: "Derive twisting through G→G×(G/G_der)".

items.name: Theorem I.9.6(iii) (central characters)
items.statement: The correspondence π ↦ φ_π is compatible with central characters (cf. [Bor79, 10.1]).
items.note: Body: Theorem IX.0.5 (Sections IX.6, IX.7); §IX.6 (via Z × G → G, z-embeddings). Planned in ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction:ES6:functoriality: "central-character compatibility through Z×G→G".

items.name: Theorem I.9.6(iv) (contragredients)
items.statement: The correspondence π ↦ φ_π is compatible with passage to contragredients (printed 'congradients'; cf. [AV16]).
items.note: Body: Theorem IX.0.5 (Sections IX.6, IX.7); Proposition IX.5.3 (Bernstein–Zelevinsky and smooth duals, via Proposition VI.12.1). Planned in ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction:ES6:duality: "Use VS5 and GS4's Chevalley/sw comparison to prove IX.5.3 for the Bernstein–Zelevinsky dual and hence parameters of supercuspidal smooth duals".

items.name: Theorem I.9.6(v) (isogenies)
items.statement: If G′ → G is a map of reductive groups inducing an isomorphism of adjoint groups, π is an irreducible smooth representation of G(E) and π′ is an irreducible constituent of π|_{G′(E)}, then φ_{π′} is the image of φ_π under the induced map Ĝ → Ĝ′.
items.note: Body: Theorem IX.0.5 (Sections IX.6, IX.7); Theorem IX.6.1. Planned in ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction:ES6:functoriality: "For G'→G inducing an adjoint-group isomorphism, parameters of Schur-irreducible constituents of pullback are composed with dual G→dual G'".

items.name: Theorem I.9.6(vi) (products)
items.statement: If G = G_1 × G_2 and π is an irreducible smooth representation of G(E), then π = π_1 ⊠ π_2 for irreducible smooth representations π_i of G_i(E), and φ_π = φ_{π_1} × φ_{π_2} under Ĝ = Ĝ_1 × Ĝ_2.
items.note: Body: Theorem IX.0.5 (Sections IX.6, IX.7); Proposition IX.6.2 (and Proposition VII.7.10 / V.7.2 for exterior products). Planned in ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction:ES6:functoriality: "Product groups give product parameters for Schur-irreducible constituents of exterior products".

items.name: Theorem I.9.6(vii) (weil restriction)
items.statement: If G = Res_{E′|E} G′ for a reductive group G′ over a finite separable extension E′|E, so that G(E) = G′(E′), then L-parameters for G|E agree with L-parameters for G′|E′.
items.note: Body: Theorem IX.0.5 (Sections IX.6, IX.7); Proposition IX.6.3 (and IX.6.4–IX.6.5). Planned in ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction:ES6:functoriality: "For finite separable E'/E and G=Res_(E'/E)G', construct nonabelian Shapiro equivalence ... Prove Weil-restriction compatibility".

items.name: Theorem I.9.6(viii) (parabolic induction)
items.statement: The correspondence π ↦ φ_π is compatible with parabolic induction.
items.note: Body: Theorem IX.0.5 (Sections IX.6, IX.7); Theorem IX.7.2, Corollary IX.7.3 (unnormalized induction with a twisted Levi embedding of parameters). Planned in ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction:ES7:parabolic: "Deduce IX.7.3 for unnormalized parabolic induction and every irreducible subquotient".

items.name: Theorem I.9.6(ix) (GLn)
items.statement: For G = GL_n and supercuspidal π, the correspondence π ↦ φ_π agrees with the usual local Langlands correspondence [LRS93], [HT01], [Hen00]. With (viii), for GL_n and general π, φ_π is the semisimple L-parameter.
items.note: Body: Theorem IX.0.5 (Sections IX.6, IX.7); Theorem IX.7.4 (all irreducible π, Q̄_ℓ-coefficients). Planned in ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction:ES7:GLn-comparison: "Use semisimple trace determination and ES5 uniqueness to obtain φ_π=ρ_π^ss. Extend to all irreducible smooth Qbar_ell-representations by ES7:parabolic".

items.name: Theorem I.10.1 (spectral action)
items.statement: Let Λ be the ring of integers in a finite extension of ℚ_ℓ(√q), Q a finite quotient of W_E through which it acts on Ĝ. Assume ℓ does not divide the order of π_0 Z(G). Let C be a small idempotent-complete Λ-linear stable ∞-category (the introduction omits 'idempotent-complete', which Theorem X.0.1 has; PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E5). Then giving, functorially in the finite set I, an exact Rep_Λ(Q^I)-linear monoidal functor Rep(Ĝ ⋊ Q)^I → End_Λ(C)^{BW_E^I} is equivalent to giving a compactly supported Λ-linear action of Perf(Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)_Λ/Ĝ) (compactly supported: for each X ∈ C, Perf(Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)/Ĝ) → C factors over some Perf(Z¹(W_E/P, Ĝ)/Ĝ)). Given such an action, the functor is obtained by composing the exact Rep_Λ(Q^I)-linear symmetric monoidal functor Rep(Ĝ ⋊ Q)^I → Perf(Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)_Λ/Ĝ)^{BW_E^I} (tensor products of the one from the universal Ĝ ⋊ Q-torsor with universal W_E-equivariance) with the action. The same holds with Λ a field over ℚ_ℓ, for any prime ℓ. In particular Perf(Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)_Λ/Ĝ) acts on D_lis(Bun_G, Λ), compatibly with the Hecke action.
items.note: Body: Theorem X.0.1 (hypothesis ℓ ∤ |π_1(Ĝ)_tor|, and C idempotent-complete: (PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E5)), reduced to Theorem X.0.2 (discretization W); rational case Theorem X.1.1, Corollary X.1.3; integral case §X.3 (Propositions X.3.1–X.3.4) using Theorem I.8.2's generation statement. Earlier versions: Nadler–Yun [NY19], GKRV [GKRV22]. Planned: ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction:ES2 ("For characteristic-zero coefficients prove the universal theorem of FS X.1") and ES3 ("Construct the integral Perf action and its equivalence with coherent Hecke data in FS X.0.1–X.0.2/X.3").

items.name: Conjecture I.10.2 (categorical local Langlands) (statement)
items.statement: Assume G quasisplit; choose Whittaker data: a Borel B ⊂ G and a generic character ψ : U(E) → O_L^× of the unipotent radical U ⊂ B, L/ℚ_ℓ algebraic; fix √q ∈ O_L. Let n = |π_0 Z(G)|, Λ = O_L[1/n], W_ψ ∈ D_lis(Bun_G, Λ) the Whittaker sheaf (concentrated on Bun_G^1, corresponding to c-Ind_{U(E)}^{G(E)} ψ), and Ind Perf^qc(Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)_Λ/Ĝ) → D_lis(Bun_G, Λ), M ↦ Act_M(W_ψ), the colimit-preserving extension of the spectral action on W_ψ. Conjecture: the corresponding right adjoint functor is fully faithful when restricted to compact objects, and induces an equivalence of (Perf(Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)_Λ/Ĝ)-linear small stable) ∞-categories D(Bun_G, Λ)^ω ≅ D^{b,qc}_{coh,Nilp}(Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)_Λ/Ĝ) (bounded complexes with quasicompact support, coherent cohomology and nilpotent singular support [AG15]).
items.note: Body: Conjecture X.3.5 (and variants Conjecture X.1.4, X.2.2), which the extraction marks planned in ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions:ML.5 ("formalize statements and conditional implications for general global/local and categorical Langlands"); this introduction statement follows them. Recorded as a statement, not a target. Footnote 6: the functor, if it exists, is unique as a right adjoint (Hansen [Han24]). With characteristic 0 or banal ℓ, nilpotent singular support is automatic. Review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21): kept missing. ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions:ML.5 names categorical Langlands only as an area, has no Bun_G or spectral-action inputs, and its packet says 'Not started'; the body forms of these conjectures (X.1.4, X.3.5) are missing too, and all go to route 7.

items.name: Problem I.11.1 (dimension of Zariski closed subsets of perfectoid balls) (statement)
items.statement: Let X ⊂ B̃ⁿ_C be Zariski closed, where B̃ⁿ_C is a perfectoid ball. Show that X has a well-behaved dimension (e.g. that Krull dimension, dim. trg and cohomological dimension of [Sch17a] agree).
items.note: Open foundational problem ('may well be the most important foundational open problem in the theory'); the Jacobian criterion is proved circumventing it via ULA sheaves. Not addressed in the body. Owner: DiamondEtaleCohomology:C8 ("Dimension and cohomological bounds", which implements dim.trg and the cohomological dimension of [Sch17a, §21] and already records ECD's open Question 21.4 as a question rather than a theorem). Zariski closed subsets of perfectoid spaces are PerfectoidSpaces:P4. It has nothing to do with LanglandsParameterStacks. Recorded as an open problem, not a target.

items.name: Zariski closed implies strongly Zariski closed (Bhatt–Scholze, cited)
items.statement: For an affinoid perfectoid space S = Spa(R,R⁺) with tilt S♭, a closed subspace Z ⊂ |S| is the vanishing locus of an ideal I ⊂ R iff Z ⊂ |S| ≅ |S♭| is the vanishing locus of an ideal J ⊂ R♭; then there is a universal perfectoid S_Z = Spa(T,T⁺) → S with |S_Z| ≅ Z, R → T surjective, R⁺ → T⁺ almost surjective, T⁺ the integral closure of R⁺ in T (Zariski closed immersions are strongly Zariski closed, contrary to a claim in [Sch15]).
items.note: Cited input [BS22, Remark 7.5], [Sch15, §II.2], [Sch17a, Def. 5.7, Thm. 5.8]; stated in the body as Proposition II.0.2 and used for Theorem I.3.1 and the Jacobian criterion. PerfectoidQuotients:Q4 plans: "Prove BS22 Theorem 7.4 ... This yields ECD Theorem 5.8" (PerfectoidSpaces:P4 defers to it).

items.name: Notation: underline X and C^{BG}
items.statement: For a topological space X, X̲ denotes the sheaf S ↦ C⁰(|S|, X) (continuous maps) on the relevant test category (usually perfectoid spaces). For an (∞-)category C with an action of a group G (a functor BG → Cat_∞), C^{BG} denotes the (∞-)category of G-equivariant objects, the limit of this diagram. Classifying stacks are written ∗/G. Anima = ∞-groupoids; animated A-algebras are obtained from simplicial A-algebras by inverting weak equivalences.
items.note: Conventions used throughout (e.g. [∗/G_b(E)] with underline, D(Bun_G,Λ)^{BW_E^I}); reductive groups are always connected.
