Planned: X̲ is the DiamondsAndVStacks packet node D3/locally-profinite-torsors ('For a topological space T let T underline be the v-sheaf sending X to the continuous maps from |X| to T'; D3 'Construct locally profinite group torsors'); anima and animated A-algebras are EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation ('Construct animated commutative algebras from simplicial commutative rings, polynomial resolutions, sifted left Kan extensions'); C^{BG} as used here (condensed W_E^I-equivariant objects) is the accepted HeckeStacksAndLocalShtukas decomposition node HS1/condensed-enrichment ('FS IX.1: the condensed infinity-category structure and the identification of W_E^I-equivariant objects'); the ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction ES0 packet requests the same ('equivariant objects C^{S} for an anima S').

items.name: Theorem II.0.1(a): 𝒴_C is locally Spa of a PID; classical points ↔ maximal ideals
items.statement: Standing notation of Chapter II: E is a nonarchimedean local field with residue field 𝔽_q of characteristic p, 𝒪_E its ring of integers, π a uniformizer; Perf = Perf_{𝔽_q}. Let C|𝔽_q be a complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean field. The adic space 𝒴_C is locally the adic spectrum Spa(B, B⁺) where B is a principal ideal domain; the classical points of Spa(B, B⁺) ⊂ 𝒴_C are in bijection with the maximal ideals of B. A similar result holds true for Y_C ⊂ 𝒴_C, and the quotient X_C = Y_C/φ^ℤ.
items.locator: Chapter II, introduction, Theorem II.0.1, p. 45
items.note: Summary theorem; restated and proved as Proposition II.1.11, Corollary II.1.12 and Definition/Proposition II.1.22. Planned by the node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:classification/classical-points-and-principal-ideal-domains, whose statement reads 'Let U = Spa(B,B^+) be an affinoid subset of Y_C. Then for any maximal ideal m of B the quotient B/m is a nonarchimedean field, and Spm(B) -> |U| is a bijection onto |U|^cl ... if U is connected then B is a principal ideal domain. Correspondingly, the classical points of X_C are |Y_C|^cl/phi^Z ...'. The node states the result for affinoids of the generic curve Y_C only, while FS state it for affinoids of the integral curve 𝒴_C (which also contains the characteristic-p classical point π = 0); the node must be widened to 𝒴_C. The RelativeFarguesFontaine packet (RF0 gap 'Classical points of Y_C and X_C are not covered by any RF stage text') leaves this block to that VB node. Fargues–Fontaine's more general principality theorem (FF18 Théorèmes 2.5.1, 3.5.1, for any perfect F) is owned by the accepted FF18 route 2 Part II, which must cite this special case.

items.name: Theorem II.0.1(b): classical points of 𝒴_C ↔ untilts of C over 𝒪_E
items.statement: Standing notation of Chapter II: E is a nonarchimedean local field with residue field 𝔽_q of characteristic p, 𝒪_E its ring of integers, π a uniformizer; Perf = Perf_{𝔽_q}. For each classical point x ∈ 𝒴_C, the residue field of x is an untilt C^♯ of C over 𝒪_E, and this induces a bijection of the classical points of 𝒴_C with untilts C^♯ of C over 𝒪_E. A similar result holds true for Y_C ⊂ 𝒴_C (untilts over E), and the quotient X_C = Y_C/φ^ℤ (untilts over E up to Frobenius).
items.locator: Chapter II, introduction, Theorem II.0.1, p. 45
items.note: Summary of Definition/Proposition II.1.7 (injectivity; classical points are by definition the image) and II.1.22 for X_C. The X_C part (bijection of |X_C|^cl with Div¹(C)) is planned by VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:classification/classical-points-and-principal-ideal-domains ('the classical points of X_C are |Y_C|^cl/phi^Z and are in bijection with Div^1(C)'); the 𝒴_C and Y_C parts (residue field of a classical point is an untilt; bijection with untilts over 𝒪_E, resp. E) are not stated by any node. They are inputs of that node and belong with it (route to VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB2:classification, not RelativeFarguesFontaine: the RF0 packet records that classical points 'correspond to no stage text in the RelativeFarguesFontaine roadmap' and are 'decomposed in the VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals packet').

items.name: Proposition II.0.2(a): Zariski closed subsets are invariant under tilting
items.statement: Let S = Spa(R, R⁺) be an affinoid perfectoid space with tilt S^♭ = Spa(R^♭, R^{♭+}). Then a closed subspace Z ⊂ |S| is the vanishing locus of an ideal I ⊂ R if and only if Z ⊂ |S| ≅ |S^♭| is the vanishing locus of an ideal J ⊂ R^♭.
items.locator: Chapter II, introduction, Proposition II.0.2, p. 45
items.note: Cited from [Sch15, §II.2], [BS22, Remark 7.5], [Sch17a, Definition 5.7, Theorem 5.8] ('Zariski closed implies strongly Zariski closed', cf. Remark II.1.13). PerfectoidQuotients:Q4: 'Apply Remark 7.5 to a perfectoid Tate ring R with plus ring R⁺ and an ideal defining a Zariski closed subset ... This yields ECD Theorem 5.8'; PerfectoidSpaces:P4 imports it ('The stronger assertion “Zariski closed implies strongly Zariski closed”, ECD Theorem 5.8, is supplied by Q4'). Used in the proof of Proposition II.1.11 to reduce to the perfectoid open disc.

items.name: Proposition II.0.2(b): universal perfectoid space over a Zariski closed subset
items.statement: Let S = Spa(R, R⁺) be an affinoid perfectoid space and Z ⊂ |S| the vanishing locus of an ideal I ⊂ R (equivalently of an ideal of R^♭). Then there is a universal perfectoid space S_Z → S such that |S_Z| → |S| factors over Z, and S_Z = Spa(T, T⁺) is affinoid perfectoid with |S_Z| → Z a homeomorphism, R → T surjective, R⁺ → T⁺ almost surjective, and T⁺ is the integral closure of R⁺ in T.
items.locator: Chapter II, introduction, Proposition II.0.2, p. 45
items.note: Cited ([Sch17a, Theorem 5.8], [BS22, Remark 7.5]). PerfectoidQuotients:Q4: 'Prove the universal property, surjectivity from R, identification of the plus ring as the appropriate integral closure, and almost surjectivity on integral rings. Prove that the resulting spectrum is the desired Zariski closed subset.'

items.name: Theorem II.0.3: classification of vector bundles on X_C (summary)
items.statement: Standing notation of Chapter II: E is a nonarchimedean local field with residue field 𝔽_q of characteristic p, 𝒪_E its ring of integers, π a uniformizer; Perf = Perf_{𝔽_q}. Let C be a complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean field over k. The functor from Isoc_E (isocrystals over Ĕ) to vector bundles on X_C induces a bijection on isomorphism classes. In particular, there is a unique stable vector bundle 𝒪_{X_C}(λ) of any slope λ ∈ ℚ, and any vector bundle ℰ can be written as a direct sum of stable bundles.
items.locator: Chapter II, introduction, Theorem II.0.3, p. 46
items.note: Summary of Theorem II.2.14 (+ Example II.2.11 and Dieudonné–Manin). VB2:classification: 'The isocrystal functor induces the source's bijection on isomorphism classes; it is not asserted fully faithful onto all bundle morphisms.' The uniqueness of the stable bundle of slope λ follows from Theorem II.2.14 (a stable bundle is semistable, hence ≅ 𝒪(λ)^m, and stability forces m = 1). New proof via v-descent and Banach–Colmez geometry (Lemma II.2.15).

items.name: Theorem II.0.4(a): ampleness and algebraization of X_S (summary)
items.statement: Assume that S ∈ Perf is affinoid. For any vector bundle ℰ on X_S, the twist ℰ(n) is globally generated and has no higher cohomology for all n ≫ 0. Defining the graded ring P = ⊕_{n≥0} H⁰(X_S, 𝒪_{X_S}(n)) and the scheme X_S^alg = Proj P, there is a natural map of locally ringed spaces X_S → X_S^alg, pullback along which defines an equivalence of categories of vector bundles, preserving cohomology.
items.locator: Chapter II, introduction, Theorem II.0.4, p. 46
items.note: Summary of Theorem II.2.6, Proposition II.2.7 and the definition of X_S^alg (p. 67). VB2:ampleness: 'For affinoid perfectoid S prove that sufficiently positive twists of a bundle are globally generated with higher cohomology zero. Compare bundles and cohomology on X_S and the Proj curve built in RF3.' Cf. [KL15, Proposition 6.2.4].

items.name: Theorem II.0.4(b): X_C^alg is a regular noetherian curve (summary)
items.statement: If S = Spa C for some complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean field C, then X_C^alg is a regular noetherian scheme of Krull dimension 1, locally the spectrum of a principal ideal domain, and its closed points are in bijection with the classical points of X_C.
items.locator: Chapter II, introduction, Theorem II.0.4, p. 46
items.note: Summary of Proposition II.2.9. VB2:ampleness: 'For S a geometric perfectoid point, prove regular noetherian dimension-one structure of the schematic curve, its local principal-ideal properties and the closed-point description'.

items.name: Theorem II.0.5: families of vector bundles (summary)
items.statement: Let S ∈ Perf and let ℰ be a vector bundle on X_S. Then the function taking a point s ∈ S to the Harder–Narasimhan polygon of ℰ|_{X_s} defines a semicontinuous function on S. If it is constant, then ℰ admits a global Harder–Narasimhan stratification, and pro-étale locally on S one can find an isomorphism with a direct sum of 𝒪_{X_S}(λ)'s. In particular, if ℰ is everywhere semistable of slope 0, then ℰ is pro-étale locally trivial, and the category of such ℰ is equivalent to the category of pro-étale E-local systems on S.
items.locator: Chapter II, introduction, Theorem II.0.5, p. 46
items.note: Summary of Theorem II.2.19 and Corollary II.2.20 (originally Kedlaya–Liu [KL15]). VB4: 'Construct the geometric HN polygon of E_s, prove its semicontinuity ... prove existence of the relative HN filtration on constant-polygon loci ... Prove the equivalence between everywhere slope-zero bundles and pro-étale E-local systems'.

items.name: Definition II.0.6: Banach–Colmez spaces BC(ℰ) and BC(ℰ[1])
items.statement: Let ℰ be a vector bundle on X_S. The Banach–Colmez space BC(ℰ) associated with ℰ is the locally spatial diamond over S whose T-valued points, for T ∈ Perf_S, are given by BC(ℰ)(T) = H⁰(X_T, ℰ|_{X_T}). Similarly, if ℰ is everywhere of only negative Harder–Narasimhan slopes, the negative Banach–Colmez space BC(ℰ[1]) is the locally spatial diamond over S whose T-valued points are BC(ℰ[1])(T) = H¹(X_T, ℰ|_{X_T}).
items.locator: Chapter II, introduction, Definition II.0.6, pp. 46–47
items.note: The definition presupposes representability, proved for BC(ℰ) in Proposition II.2.16 and for O(λ) in Proposition II.2.5; the general negative case BC(ℰ[1]) is Proposition II.3.5 (two-term complexes). VB3:positive-basic-examples: 'Construct the sheaf of sections T ↦ H^0(X_T,E_T) ... Negative H^1 spaces have their separate construction'; node VB3:positive-basic-examples/banach-colmez-space-definition.

items.name: BC(𝒪(−1)[1]) ≅ (𝔸¹_{C♯})^♢/E
items.statement: For a complete algebraically closed C with an untilt C^♯ over E, the negative Banach–Colmez space is BC(𝒪_{X_C}(−1)[1]) ≅ (𝔸¹_{C^♯})^♢/E, the quotient of the affine line by the translation action of E ⊂ 𝔸¹_{C^♯}. More generally, for S ∈ Perf with untilt S^♯ over E (as in the proof of Proposition II.2.5(i)) there is an exact sequence 0 → E̲ → (𝔸¹_{S^♯})^♢ → BC(𝒪(−1)[1])|_S → 0.
items.locator: Chapter II, introduction, p. 47 (displayed formula); proved in the proof of Proposition II.2.5(i), p. 64
items.note: Unnumbered key example; used in Lemma II.2.15. Follows from the sequence 0 → 𝒪(−1) → 𝒪 → 𝒪_{S♯} → 0 and Proposition II.2.5(ii). VB3:positive-basic-examples: 'Negative H^1 spaces have their separate construction.'

items.name: Ramified Witt vectors W_{𝒪_E}(R) and Teichmüller lift
items.statement: Standing notation of Chapter II: E is a nonarchimedean local field with residue field 𝔽_q of characteristic p, 𝒪_E its ring of integers, π a uniformizer; Perf = Perf_{𝔽_q}. For any perfect 𝔽_q-algebra R, there is a unique π-adically complete flat 𝒪_E-algebra R̃ such that R̃/π = R. There is a unique multiplicative lift [·] : R → R̃ of the identity R → R, called the Teichmüller lift. Explicitly, one can take R̃ = W_{𝒪_E}(R) = W(R) ⊗̂_{W(𝔽_q)} 𝒪_E (π-adic completion); if E = 𝔽_q((π)) is of equal characteristic, this becomes R[[π]].
items.note: RF0: 'For a perfect F_q-algebra R construct W_OE(R), its Teichmüller representatives, Frobenius and the pi-adically complete flat O_E universal property. In mixed characteristic compare with the completed scalar extension of p-typical Witt vectors over W(F_q); in equal characteristic identify it with R[[pi]].' Mathlib has only p-typical WittVector and its Teichmüller map (Mathlib/RingTheory/WittVector/Teichmuller.lean), not the ramified version.

items.name: The integral curve 𝒴_S and its Frobenius
items.statement: If S = Spa(R, R⁺) is an affinoid perfectoid space over 𝔽_q, and ϖ ∈ R⁺ is a pseudouniformizer, let 𝒴_S = Spa W_{𝒪_E}(R⁺) ∖ V([ϖ]), where W_{𝒪_E}(R⁺) has the (π, [ϖ])-adic topology. This does not depend on the choice of ϖ (for ϖ, ϖ′ one has ϖ | ϖ′ⁿ, ϖ′ | ϖⁿ for some n > 0). The q-th power Frobenius of R⁺ induces an automorphism φ of 𝒴_S.
items.note: RF0:integral-Y: 'equip W_OE(R+) with the (pi,[varpi])-adic topology and construct 𝒴_S = Spa(W_OE(R+)) \ V([varpi]) over Spa(O_E).' Glued for general S via Proposition II.1.3.

items.name: Proposition II.1.1: 𝒴_S is an analytic adic space, preperfectoid with tilt the perfectoid open disc
items.statement: The above defines an analytic adic space 𝒴_S over 𝒪_E. Letting E_∞ be the completion of E(π^{1/p^∞}), the base change 𝒴_S ×_{Spa 𝒪_E} Spa 𝒪_{E_∞} is a perfectoid space, with tilt given by S ×_{𝔽_q} Spa 𝔽_q[[t^{1/p^∞}]] = 𝔻_{S,perf}, a perfectoid open unit disc over S.
items.note: Proof covers 𝒴_S by rational subsets 𝒴_{S,[0,n]} = {|π|ⁿ ≤ |[ϖ]| ≠ 0} = Spa(B_{S,[0,n]}, B⁺_{S,[0,n]}) with B_{S,[0,n]} = W_{𝒪_E}(R⁺)⟨πⁿ/[ϖ]⟩[1/[ϖ]], shows B_{S,[0,1]} ⊗̂ 𝒪_{E∞} is perfectoid via [BMS18, Lemmas 3.10, 3.21], and deduces sheafiness by the split-direct-summand (sousperfectoid) argument [HK20], [SW20, §6.3]. RF0:integral-Y: 'prove FS II.1.1: after the specified completed extension O_E→O_(E∞) ... these charts are perfectoid and their tilt glues to the perfected open unit disc over S. Derive sheafiness by the topological direct-summand argument'.

items.name: Proposition II.1.2: 𝒴_S^♢ ≅ Spd 𝒪_E × S
items.statement: For any perfectoid space T over 𝔽_q, giving an untilt T^♯ of T together with a map T^♯ → 𝒴_S of analytic adic spaces is equivalent to giving an untilt T^♯ together with a map T^♯ → Spa 𝒪_E, and a map T → S. In other words, there is a natural isomorphism 𝒴_S^♢ ≅ Spd 𝒪_E × S. In particular there is a natural map |𝒴_S| ≅ |𝒴_S^♢| ≅ |Spd 𝒪_E × S| → |S|.
items.note: Proof: maps W_{𝒪_E}(R⁺) → A⁺ with [ϖ] invertible ↔ maps R⁺ → (A⁺)^♭ with ϖ invertible (universal property of Witt vectors of a perfect ring). RF0:integral-Y: 'Prove II.1.2's untilt functor 𝒴_S^diamond ≅ S × Spd(O_E).' Fixed-field Q_p analogue for Y: FarguesFontaineDiamonds:F1.

items.name: Proposition II.1.3: 𝒴_{S′} → 𝒴_S is an open immersion over affinoid S′ ⊂ S
items.statement: If S′ ⊂ S is an affinoid subset (of an affinoid perfectoid S), then 𝒴_{S′} → 𝒴_S is an open immersion, with the square |𝒴_{S′}| → |𝒴_S| over |S′| → |S| cartesian. Consequently, for any perfectoid space S over 𝔽_q there is an analytic adic space 𝒴_S equipped with an isomorphism 𝒴_S^♢ ≅ Spd 𝒪_E × S (and a map |𝒴_S| → |S|) such that for U = Spa(R, R⁺) ⊂ S affinoid the pullback of 𝒴_S is 𝒴_U.
items.note: Proof checks the map to the open Z = |𝒴_S| ×_{|S|} |S′| after base change to 𝒪_{E∞} (split injective structure maps), then on diamonds via II.1.2. Planned by the node RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0:integral-Y/gluing-for-general-base ('FS II.1.3: open immersion and cartesian square for affinoid subsets of the base ... Consequently Y-curly_S can be defined for an arbitrary perfectoid space S by gluing'). The accepted restructuring RS-20 keeps 'gluing and integral product' of 𝒴 in RF0:integral-Y and narrows RF1 to 'Gluing of the relative generic Y and X', so RF1 does not own the integral gluing.

items.name: Proposition II.1.4(a): sections of 𝒴_S^♢ → S ↔ maps S → Spd 𝒪_E ↔ untilts over 𝒪_E
items.statement: Let S be a perfectoid space over 𝔽_q. The following objects are in natural bijection: (i) sections of 𝒴_S^♢ → S; (ii) morphisms S → Spd 𝒪_E; (iii) untilts S^♯ over 𝒪_E of S.
items.note: Cited from [SW20, Proposition 11.3.1]; immediate from II.1.2. F4 (fixed field, over ℚ_p): 'identify sections of Y_F^♢ → S with maps S → Spd ℚ_p, equivalently marked untilts'. RF2:integral-divisors plans the integral 𝒴_S divisor theory (Div^d_𝒴 = (Spd O_E)^d/Σ_d).

items.name: Proposition II.1.4(b): an untilt over 𝒪_E is a closed Cartier divisor in 𝒴_S
items.statement: Given an untilt S^♯ over 𝒪_E of S, there is a natural closed immersion of adic spaces S^♯ ↪ 𝒴_S that presents S^♯ as a closed Cartier divisor in 𝒴_S, i.e. 0 → 𝒪_{𝒴_S} →^ξ 𝒪_{𝒴_S} → i_*𝒪_{S^♯} → 0 is exact, where locally R^{♯+} = W_{𝒪_E}(R⁺)/ξ with ξ a nonzerodivisor of the form π − a[ϖ].
items.note: Proof: on U = {|ξ| ≤ |[ϖ]|ⁿ} with spectral norm normalized by |[ϖ]| = 1/q one shows |ξa| ≥ q^{−n}|a| via the Shilov boundary (reduced to the tilt, an affinoid in 𝔻_{S,perf}). RF2:integral-divisors: 'prove FS VI.1.1–VI.1.4: its map into relative degree-d closed Cartier divisors on 𝒴_S'; F4 (fixed field over ℚ_p): 'The auxiliary analytic argument is the fixed-field case of FS II.1.4 ... use the maximum/annulus boundary estimate to obtain the lower bound for multiplication by the primitive generator.'

items.name: Remark II.1.5: the untilt divisor is a relative Cartier divisor
items.statement: The Cartier divisor S^♯ ⊂ 𝒴_S of Proposition II.1.4 satisfies the stronger property of being a “relative Cartier divisor” in the sense that for all s ∈ S its pullback to 𝒴_{Spa(K(s),K(s)⁺)} is a Cartier divisor.
items.note: Asserted without separate proof (follows from II.1.4 applied to each Spa(K(s),K(s)⁺)). RF2:integral-divisors: 'its map into relative degree-d closed Cartier divisors on 𝒴_S'.

items.name: Example II.1.6: 𝒴_C = 𝔻_C in equal characteristic; classical points
items.statement: Assume that E = 𝔽_q((t)) is of equal characteristic. Then 𝒴_C = 𝔻_C is an open unit disc over C, with coordinate t. Inside |𝒴_C| the subset of classical points is |𝒴_C|^cl = {x ∈ C | |x| < 1}, and these are in bijection with maps 𝒪_E → C over 𝔽_q, i.e. with “untilts of C over 𝒪_E”.
items.note: Model case motivating Definition II.1.7. Missing. Its consumer is VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:classification/classical-points-and-principal-ideal-domains (FS II.1.11–II.1.12, II.1.22), so it belongs in route 2 with stage VB2:classification; RelativeFarguesFontaine's packet explicitly leaves the classical-point block to that VB node (RF0 gap 'Classical points of Y_C and X_C are not covered by any RF stage text').

items.name: Definition/Proposition II.1.7: classical points of 𝒴_C
items.statement: Let C|𝔽_q be complete algebraically closed. Any untilt C^♯ of C over 𝒪_E defines a closed Cartier divisor Spa C^♯ ↪ 𝒴_C, and in particular a closed point of |𝒴_C|. This induces an injection from the set of such untilts to |𝒴_C|. The set of classical points |𝒴_C|^cl ⊂ |𝒴_C| is defined to be the set of such points.
items.note: Defines the classical points |𝒴_C|^cl that the VB2:classification node uses without defining them. Missing. Its consumer is VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:classification/classical-points-and-principal-ideal-domains (FS II.1.11–II.1.12, II.1.22), so it belongs in route 2 with stage VB2:classification; RelativeFarguesFontaine's packet explicitly leaves the classical-point block to that VB node (RF0 gap 'Classical points of Y_C and X_C are not covered by any RF stage text').

items.name: The tilting map |𝔻_C| → |𝒴_C|
items.statement: 𝒴_C is preperfectoid: 𝒴_C ×_{𝒪_E} 𝒪_{E∞} is perfectoid with tilt Spa C × Spa 𝒪^♭_{E∞} ≅ Spa C × Spa 𝔽_q[[t^{1/p^∞}]]. This gives a map |𝔻_C| = |Spa C × Spa 𝔽_q[[t]]| ≅ |Spa C × Spa 𝔽_q[[t^{1/p^∞}]]| ≅ |𝒴_C ×_{𝒪_E} 𝒪_{E∞}| → |𝒴_C|. On classical points it sends x ∈ C with |x| < 1 to the closed point defined by the ideal (π − [x]).
items.note: Unnumbered; the tilt itself is Proposition II.1.1 at S = Spa C (planned, RF0:integral-Y/chart-cover-perfectoidness-and-sheafiness); the map on classical points x ↦ (π − [x]) is not stated anywhere. Missing. Its consumer is VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:classification/classical-points-and-principal-ideal-domains (FS II.1.11–II.1.12, II.1.22), so it belongs in route 2 with stage VB2:classification; RelativeFarguesFontaine's packet explicitly leaves the classical-point block to that VB node (RF0 gap 'Classical points of Y_C and X_C are not covered by any RF stage text').

items.name: Proposition II.1.8: classical points of 𝔻_C are the preimage of classical points of 𝒴_C
items.statement: Under the map |𝔻_C| → |𝒴_C|, the classical points |𝔻_C|^cl = {x ∈ C | |x| < 1} ⊂ |𝔻_C| are exactly the preimage of the classical points |𝒴_C|^cl ⊂ |𝒴_C|. In particular, any classical point of 𝒴_C is the closed point defined by (π − [x]) for some x ∈ C with |x| < 1.
items.note: Used in the proofs of II.1.9 and II.1.11. Missing. Its consumer is VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:classification/classical-points-and-principal-ideal-domains (FS II.1.11–II.1.12, II.1.22), so it belongs in route 2 with stage VB2:classification; RelativeFarguesFontaine's packet explicitly leaves the classical-point block to that VB node (RF0 gap 'Classical points of Y_C and X_C are not covered by any RF stage text').

items.name: Proposition II.1.9: classical points are stable under base change; non-classical rank-1 points thicken
items.statement: Let C′|C be an extension of complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean fields over 𝔽_q, inducing the map 𝒴_{C′} → 𝒴_C. A point x ∈ |𝒴_C| is classical if and only if its preimage in |𝒴_{C′}| is a classical point. Moreover, if x ∈ |𝒴_C| is a rank-1-point that is not classical, then there is some C′|C such that the preimage of x contains a nonempty open subset of |𝒴_{C′}|.
items.note: Named only in an acceptance test of the VB2:classification node ('exhibiting a nonclassical rank-1 point whose preimage in some |Y_{C'}| contains an open set (Prop. II.1.9, Lemma II.1.10)'), and used as a proof step there; not stated. Missing. Its consumer is VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:classification/classical-points-and-principal-ideal-domains (FS II.1.11–II.1.12, II.1.22), so it belongs in route 2 with stage VB2:classification; RelativeFarguesFontaine's packet explicitly leaves the classical-point block to that VB node (RF0 gap 'Classical points of Y_C and X_C are not covered by any RF stage text').

items.name: Lemma II.1.10: preimage of a Gauss point contains an open disc
items.statement: Let x ∈ 𝔻_C(C), ρ ∈ (0, 1), and x_ρ ∈ |𝔻_C| be the Gauss norm with radius ρ centered at x. The preimage of x_ρ in |𝔻_{C(x_ρ)}| contains the open disk with radius ρ centered at x_ρ ∈ 𝔻_{C(x_ρ)}(C(x_ρ)).
items.note: Printed with ρ ∈ (0, 1]; for ρ = 1 the Gauss point of radius 1 is not a point of the open unit disc 𝔻_C (see newIssues), and the application in Proposition II.1.9 only uses discs B(x, r_0) ⊂ 𝔻_C. Elementary estimate |Σ a_n uⁿ| = |Σ a_n tⁿ| for |u − t| < ρ = |t|. Here C(x_ρ) denotes (a completed algebraic closure of) the residue field at x_ρ. Missing; named only in an acceptance test of VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:classification/classical-points-and-principal-ideal-domains; route 2 (VB2:classification).

items.name: Proposition II.1.11: maximal ideals of affinoid algebras on 𝒴_C are classical points
items.statement: Let U = Spa(B, B⁺) ⊂ 𝒴_C be an affinoid subset. Then for any maximal ideal 𝔪 ⊂ B, the quotient B/𝔪 is a nonarchimedean field, inducing an injection Spm(B) ↪ |U|. This gives a bijection between Spm(B) and |U|^cl := |U| ∩ |𝒴_C|^cl ⊂ |𝒴_C|.
items.note: Proposition II.1.11 is planned by the node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:classification/classical-points-and-principal-ideal-domains (title 'FS II.1.11-II.1.12 and II.1.22 ...'; statement 'for any maximal ideal m of B the quotient B/m is a nonarchimedean field, and Spm(B) -> |U| is a bijection onto |U|^cl ... U has finitely many connected components, and if U is connected then B is a principal ideal domain'; its proof steps reproduce FS's argument via Proposition II.0.2 and the Shilov boundary). The node writes 'an affinoid subset of Y_C' where FS have 𝒴_C; it must be widened to 𝒴_C. The general-F version (FF18 Théorèmes 2.5.1, 3.5.1) is owned by the accepted FF18 route 2 Part II, which must prove compatibility with this node.

items.name: Corollary II.1.12: affinoids in 𝒴_C have finitely many components; connected ones are PIDs
items.statement: Let U = Spa(B, B⁺) ⊂ 𝒴_C be an affinoid subset. Then U has finitely many connected components. Assuming that U is connected, the ring B is a principal ideal domain.
items.note: Corollary II.1.12 is planned by the node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:classification/classical-points-and-principal-ideal-domains (title 'FS II.1.11-II.1.12 and II.1.22 ...'; statement 'for any maximal ideal m of B the quotient B/m is a nonarchimedean field, and Spm(B) -> |U| is a bijection onto |U|^cl ... U has finitely many connected components, and if U is connected then B is a principal ideal domain'; its proof steps reproduce FS's argument via Proposition II.0.2 and the Shilov boundary). The node writes 'an affinoid subset of Y_C' where FS have 𝒴_C; it must be widened to 𝒴_C. The general-F version (FF18 Théorèmes 2.5.1, 3.5.1) is owned by the accepted FF18 route 2 Part II, which must prove compatibility with this node.

items.name: Lemma II.1.14: a point of Y_C whose residue field sees all of inertia
items.statement: There is a point x ∈ |Y_C| (Y_C = 𝒴_C ×_{Spa 𝒪_E} Spa E), with completed residue field K(x), such that the induced map Gal(K̄(x)|K(x)) → I_E is surjective, where I_E is the inertia subgroup of the absolute Galois group of E. (The image of Gal(K̄(x)|K(x)) → Gal(Ē|E) lies in I_E as K(x) contains Ĕ.) Explicitly, the image in |Y_C| of any Gauß point of the punctured disc 𝔻*_C (radius r, 0 < r < 1) works.
items.note: Used only in Proposition IV.7.3 (drinfeldlemmalocallyconstant), which the extraction plans at VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories:VS1. Proof: the Gauss-point locus lifts uniquely to |Y_C ×_{Spa Ĕ} Spa E′| for every finite E′|Ĕ. Missing; no stage or node states it (the RF0 packet says the classical-point block including 'Lemma II.1.14's inertia-surjectivity point used later in IV.7.3' corresponds to no RF stage text). Route with its consumer: route 4 (VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories, stage VS1), not route 1.

items.name: Definition II.1.15: the relative Fargues–Fontaine curve X_S
items.statement: For any perfectoid space S over 𝔽_q, the relative Fargues–Fontaine curve is X_S = Y_S/φ^ℤ where Y_S = 𝒴_S ×_{Spa 𝒪_E} Spa E = 𝒴_S ∖ V(π), which for affinoid S = Spa(R, R⁺) with pseudouniformizer ϖ is given by Y_S = Spa W_{𝒪_E}(R⁺) ∖ V(π[ϖ]).
items.note: Well-formed by Proposition II.1.16. RF0:annuli: 'construct Y_S = 𝒴_S \ V(pi), the open where pi[varpi] is nonzero'; RF1: 'establish q-Frobenius action, wandering annuli and the adic quotient X_S = Y_S/phi^Z'. Fixed-field (E = ℚ_p, S = Spa F) version already specified upstream (FarguesFontaineDiamonds:F0 'Reuse the actual adic objects', TauCeti AdicSpaces Layer 6).

items.name: The radius function rad and the annuli Y_{S,I}
items.statement: If S = Spa(R, R⁺) is affinoid and ϖ ∈ R is a pseudouniformizer, define rad : |Y_S| → (0, ∞) taking any point x ∈ Y_S with rank-1-generalization x̃ to log|[ϖ](x̃)| / log|π(x̃)|. For any interval I = [a, b] ⊂ (0, ∞) with rational ends (possibly a = b), let Y_{S,I} = {|π|^b ≤ |[ϖ]| ≤ |π|^a} ⊂ rad^{−1}(I) ⊂ Y_S, a rational open subset of Spa W_{𝒪_E}(R⁺), Y_{S,I} = Spa(B_{S,I}, B⁺_{S,I}). The end 0 corresponds to the boundary divisor (π) and ∞ to the boundary divisor ([ϖ]).
items.note: RF0:annuli: 'construct ... the annulus rings with their explicit plus subrings. Prove complete separated sheafiness, restriction, completed base change and independence of varpi'; RF1 'wandering annuli'.

items.name: Proposition II.1.16: φ acts freely and totally discontinuously; X_S as a glued quotient
items.statement: The action of φ on Y_S is free and totally discontinuous. In fact, for affinoid S = Spa(R, R⁺) with pseudouniformizer ϖ, the function rad : |Y_S| → (0, ∞) factorizes through the Berkovich space quotient of |Y_S| and satisfies rad ∘ φ = q · rad; each Y_{S,I} is a rational open subset of Spa W_{𝒪_E}(R⁺) and thus affinoid; and one can form X_S as the quotient of Y_{S,[1,q]} via the identification φ : Y_{S,[1,1]} ≅ Y_{S,[q,q]}. In particular, X_S is qcqs in case S is affinoid.
items.note: Cf. [SW20, Lecture 12]; proof 'follows directly from the definitions'. RF1: 'establish q-Frobenius action, wandering annuli and the adic quotient X_S = Y_S/phi^Z'. FarguesFontaineDiamonds:F2 warns to check the generator convention (rad ∘ φ = q·rad here).

items.name: |X_S| sits over |S| via a qcqs map
items.statement: Although X_S does not sit over S, the absolute Frobenius φ × φ of S × Spd(E) acts trivially on the topological space and one has |X_S| ≅ |X_S^♢| ≅ |S × Spd(E)/φ^ℤ × id| ≅ |S × Spd(E)/id × φ^ℤ| → |S|. Thus |X_S| sits over |S|, and for all S the map |X_S| → |S| is qcqs. For each s ∈ S, functoriality gives X_{K(s),K(s)⁺} → X_S, so X_S is a “family of curves” (X_{K(s),K(s)⁺})_{s∈S}.
items.note: Unnumbered; uses Proposition II.1.17. Planned by the node RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF1/diamond-formula-and-map-to-base: 'Although X_S carries no structural morphism of adic spaces to S, the absolute Frobenius phi x phi of S x Spd(E) acts trivially on the underlying topological space, giving |X_S| = ... -> |S|, and this map is qcqs for every S.'

items.name: Proposition II.1.17: Y_S^♢ ≅ S × Spd(E) and X_S^♢ ≅ (S × Spd E)/φ^ℤ × id
items.statement: There is a natural isomorphism Y_S^♢ ≅ S × Spd(E), descending to an isomorphism X_S^♢ ≅ (S × Spd(E))/φ^ℤ × id.
items.note: Immediate from II.1.2. RF1: 'Construct the diamond formulas over Perf_Fq with the chosen coefficient-field embedding, and compare the Q_p, fixed-field specialization with FarguesFontaineDiamonds F1–F3.' F1 ('α_F : Y_F^♢ ≅ S × Spd(Q_p)') and F2 ('β_F : X_F^♢ ≅ (S × Spd(Q_p))/(φ_S^ℤ × id)') do the fixed-field case.

items.name: Proposition II.1.18(a): sections of Y_S^♢ → S ↔ maps S → Spd E ↔ untilts over E
items.statement: The following objects are naturally in bijection: (i) sections of Y_S^♢ → S; (ii) maps S → Spd(E); (iii) untilts S^♯ over E of S.
items.note: Immediate from II.1.4. RF2:untilts: 'Construct marked untilts over E, the primitive kernel of theta, and its divisor on Y_S and X_S.'

items.name: Proposition II.1.18(b): untilts over E give closed Cartier divisors on Y_S and X_S; Spd(E)/φ^ℤ injects into divisors
items.statement: Given an untilt S^♯ over E of S, there is a natural closed immersion S^♯ ↪ Y_S presenting S^♯ as a closed Cartier divisor in Y_S. The composite map S^♯ → Y_S → X_S is still a closed Cartier divisor, and depends only on the composite S → Spd(E) → Spd(E)/φ^ℤ. In this way, any map S → Spd(E)/φ^ℤ defines a closed Cartier divisor D ⊂ X_S; this gives an injection of Spd(E)/φ^ℤ into the space of closed Cartier divisors on X_S.
items.note: RF2:untilts: 'Prove injectivity and closed image of multiplication by a local generator on appropriate annular neighborhoods, identify the complete quotient, and descend the Cartier divisor.' F4 fixed-field: 'Use the Frobenius translates and local quotient charts to descend the divisor to X_F.'

items.name: Definition II.1.19: closed Cartier divisors of degree 1; Div¹ = Spd(E)/φ^ℤ
items.statement: A closed Cartier divisor of degree 1 on X_S is a closed Cartier divisor D ⊂ X_S that arises from a map S → Spd(E)/φ^ℤ. Equivalently, it arises locally on S from an untilt S^♯ over E of S. The moduli space of degree 1 closed Cartier divisors is Div¹ = Spd(E)/φ^ℤ (quotient in v-sheaves). In the introduction, over Perf_k this is written Div¹ = Spd Ĕ/φ^ℤ.
items.locator: Chapter II, §II.1.2, Definition II.1.19, p. 56 (and introduction, p. 46)
items.note: RF2:untilts: 'Define Div^1 using the unramified coefficient base Spd(E-breve)/phi^Z over Perf_Fq. Keep this moduli object distinct from the diamond of one fixed curve.' Note the paper uses Spd(E) over Perf_{𝔽_q} in §II.1 and Spd Ĕ over Perf_k in the introduction and §II.2.1; these agree after base change to k. Remark II.1.20 cites [Far20b, Définition 2.6] for an equivalent definition.

items.name: The v-quotient Spd(E)/φ^ℤ agrees with the quotient for open covers
items.statement: The quotient Spd(E)/φ^ℤ, formed in the category of v-sheaves, agrees with the quotient computed in the category of sheaves on Perf_{𝔽_q} for the topology of open covers. In particular, “locally on S” in Definition II.1.19 can be taken to mean v-locally, or on open subsets of |S|.
items.note: Unnumbered remark. Planned by the node RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2:untilts/div1-moduli-and-properness: 'Div^1 = Spd(E)/phi^Z, where the quotient may be computed either as a v-sheaf quotient or for the topology of open covers, so that "locally on S" may be read v-locally or on open subsets of |S|.'

items.name: Remark II.1.20: equivalence with Fargues' relative Cartier divisors of degree 1
items.statement: In [Far20b, Définition 2.6] Fargues gives a definition of a Cartier divisor of degree 1 on X_S equivalent to the one in Definition II.1.19, similar to the definition of a relative Cartier divisor in classical algebraic geometry.
items.note: Cited equivalence, not proved in FS. It is the case d = 1 on X_S of Remark VI.1.3, which the node RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2:integral-divisors/relative-degree-criterion plans: 'Div^d_{Y-curly}(S) is exactly the set of relative Cartier divisors of degree d ... The same holds for Div^d_Y and Div^d_X.' The RF0 packet records [Far20b] (Fargues, Simple connexité ..., Définition 2.6) as an unread source for this equivalence (gap 'Fargues' [Far20b] is absent from the supplied library'); the arXiv preprint 1705.01526 is freely available.

items.name: Proposition II.1.21: Div¹ → ∗ is proper, representable in spatial diamonds and cohomologically smooth
items.statement: Write ∗ = Spd(𝔽_q) for the v-sheaf taking any S ∈ Perf_{𝔽_q} to a point. The map Div¹ → ∗ is proper, representable in spatial diamonds, and cohomologically smooth.
items.note: Proof: Spd(E) → ∗ is representable in locally spatial diamonds and cohomologically smooth by [Sch17a, Proposition 24.5]; φ^ℤ acts totally discontinuously with qcqs quotient |X_S| → |S|; properness by the valuative criterion [Sch17a, Proposition 18.3]. Planned by the node RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2:untilts/div1-moduli-and-properness ('The map Div^1 -> * is proper, representable in spatial diamonds, and cohomologically smooth'); RS-20 keeps 'source-qualified Div^1 properness/smoothness obligations' in RF2:untilts.

items.name: |X_S| → |S| is open and closed
items.statement: The map |X_S| = |Div¹ × S| → |S| is open and closed; thus X_S may be pictured as “a proper and smooth family over S”.
items.note: Unnumbered consequence of Proposition II.1.21 (proper and cohomologically smooth maps are closed and open). Not planned.

items.name: Definition/Proposition II.1.22: classical points of X_C and affinoids in X_C
items.statement: Let C be complete algebraically closed over 𝔽_q. The classical points of X_C are |X_C|^cl := |Y_C|^cl/φ^ℤ ⊂ |X_C| = |Y_C|/φ^ℤ. They are in bijection with (Spd(E)/φ^ℤ)(C) = Div¹(C), i.e. are given by untilts of C over E up to Frobenius, or by degree 1 closed Cartier divisors on X_C. For any affinoid open subset U = Spa(B, B⁺) ⊂ X_C, the maximal ideals of B are in bijection with |U|^cl = |U| ∩ |X_C|^cl. Any such U has only finitely many connected components, and if U is connected, then B is a Dedekind domain.
items.note: Definition/Proposition II.1.22 is planned by the node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:classification/classical-points-and-principal-ideal-domains: 'Correspondingly, the classical points of X_C are |Y_C|^cl/phi^Z and are in bijection with Div^1(C); for U = Spa(B,B^+) an affinoid open of X_C with U connected, B is a Dedekind domain (in fact a PID, by the Picard computation).' Its sources quote FS p. 56 including the footnote, and its acceptance tests 'the footnote's upgrade from Dedekind to PID via Pic(X_C) = Z'.

items.name: Footnote to II.1.22: connected affinoids of X_C have PID coordinate rings
items.statement: For connected affinoid U = Spa(B, B⁺) ⊂ X_C, B is in fact a principal ideal domain: the map Pic(X_C) → Pic(B) is surjective, the source is ℤ and generated by any classical point outside of U, so the map is zero and hence Pic(B) = 0.
items.locator: Chapter II, §II.1.2, footnote 2 to Definition/Proposition II.1.22, p. 56
items.note: the footnote to II.1.22 is planned by the node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:classification/classical-points-and-principal-ideal-domains: 'Correspondingly, the classical points of X_C are |Y_C|^cl/phi^Z and are in bijection with Div^1(C); for U = Spa(B,B^+) an affinoid open of X_C with U connected, B is a Dedekind domain (in fact a PID, by the Picard computation).' Its sources quote FS p. 56 including the footnote, and its acceptance tests 'the footnote's upgrade from Dedekind to PID via Pic(X_C) = Z'.

items.name: Vector bundles on Y_S have no higher cohomology; RΓ(X_S, ℰ) as Frobenius fixed points
items.statement: Suppose S = Spa(R, R⁺) is affinoid perfectoid. Then Y_S = ⋃_{I⊂(0,∞)} Y_{(R,R⁺),I} with (i) I a compact interval with rational ends, (ii) Y_{(R,R⁺),I} affinoid sous-perfectoid, (iii) for I₁ ⊂ I₂ the restriction O(Y_{(R,R⁺),I₂}) → O(Y_{(R,R⁺),I₁}) has dense image. Hence for any vector bundle ℱ on Y_S, Hⁱ(Y_{S,I}, ℱ) = 0 and R¹lim_I Γ(Y_{(R,R⁺),I}, ℱ) = 0, so Hⁱ(Y_S, ℱ) = 0 for i > 0. Thus for a vector bundle ℰ on X_S, RΓ(X_S, ℰ) = [H⁰(Y_S, ℰ|_{Y_S}) →^{φ−1} H⁰(Y_S, ℰ|_{Y_S})]; in particular it vanishes in degree > 1.
items.note: Uses [Gro61, 0.13.2.4] for the R¹lim vanishing. VB1: 'Construct H^0 and H^1 and prove higher vanishing for bundles in the stipulated affinoid-relative setting ... establish them from annular descent.'

items.name: Proposition II.2.1(a): T ↦ RΓ(X_T, ℰ|_{X_T}) is a v-sheaf of complexes
items.statement: Let S be a perfectoid space over 𝔽_q and ℰ a vector bundle on X_S. The functor taking any T ∈ Perf_S to RΓ(X_T, ℰ|_{X_T}) is a v-sheaf of complexes. In fact, the functor taking any T ∈ Perf_S to H⁰(Y_T, ℰ|_{Y_T}) is a v-sheaf, whose cohomology vanishes in case T is affinoid.
items.note: Proof: reduce to 𝒪 on Y_{T,I}; exactness of the Čech complex of E-Banach spaces after ⊗̂ E_∞ by [Sch17a, Theorem 8.7, Proposition 8.8]. VB1: 'Prove rational/pro-étale/v descent in the exact source scope'.

items.name: Proposition II.2.1(b): vector bundles on X_S form a v-stack
items.statement: Sending S ∈ Perf_{𝔽_q} to the groupoid of vector bundles on X_S defines a v-stack.
items.note: Proof cites [SW20, Lemma 17.1.8, Proposition 19.5.3]. VB1: 'Prove rational/pro-étale/v descent in the exact source scope, effective gluing and preservation of tensor, Hom and duals.' Basis of Bun_G in Chapter III.

items.name: Banach–Colmez space of a two-term complex
items.statement: If [ℰ₁ → ℰ₀] is a complex of vector bundles on X_S sitting in homological degrees [0, 1], such that H⁰(X_T, ℰ₁|_{X_T}) = 0 for all T ∈ Perf_S, let BC([ℰ₁ → ℰ₀]) : T ↦ ℍ⁰(X_T, [ℰ₁ → ℰ₀]|_{X_T}) (hypercohomology) be the corresponding v-sheaf on Perf_S, the Banach–Colmez space associated with [ℰ₁ → ℰ₀]. (Usually applied only when ℰ₁ or ℰ₀ is zero.)
items.note: Unnumbered definition generalizing Definition II.0.6; v-sheaf property from Proposition II.2.1. Planned explicitly by the node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:positive-basic-examples/banach-colmez-space-definition ('if [E_1 -> E_0] is a complex of vector bundles on X_S in homological degrees [0,1] such that H^0(X_T, E_1|_{X_T}) = 0 for all T in Perf_S, then BC([E_1 -> E_0]) : T -> H^0(X_T, [E_1 -> E_0]|_{X_T}) is the Banach-Colmez space of the complex').

items.name: The functor ℰ : Isoc_k → Bun(X_S) and the bundles 𝒪_{X_S}(λ)
items.statement: Fix an algebraically closed field k|𝔽_q and Ĕ = W_{𝒪_E}(k)[1/π] with Frobenius σ. Functorially in S ∈ Perf_k, there is a natural exact ⊗-functor Isoc_k → Bun(X_S), (D, φ) ↦ ℰ(D, φ), from isocrystals (finite-dimensional Ĕ-vector spaces D with σ-linear automorphism φ) to vector bundles on X_S, defined by descending D ⊗_Ĕ 𝒪_{Y_S} to X_S via φ ⊗ φ. 𝒪_{X_S}(n) denotes the image of (Ĕ, π^{−n}σ) (the functor ℰ reverses slopes); more generally, if (D_λ, φ_λ) is the simple isocrystal of slope λ ∈ ℚ in the Dieudonné–Manin classification, 𝒪_{X_S}(−λ) = ℰ(D_λ, φ_λ).
items.note: VB1: 'Construct the isocrystal-to-bundle functor and natural comparison under S-base change.' VB0: 'Pin the convention by the standard rank-r block ... Compute the slope of its associated bundle and record any sign reversal explicitly.' RF3: 'Define O(1) by Frobenius descent with the chosen pi-normalization'. Mathlib's WittVector.Isocrystal (Mathlib/RingTheory/WittVector/Isocrystal.lean) covers only p-typical isocrystals over FractionRing (WittVector p k) and the rank-1 classification, not ramified Ĕ nor the functor to bundles.

items.name: The Lubin–Tate formal group G and its normalization
items.statement: Up to isomorphism, there is a unique 1-dimensional formal group G over 𝒪_Ĕ with action by 𝒪_E such that the two induced actions on Lie G coincide and [π]_G is an isogeny of 𝒪_E-height 1 (i.e. G is a π-divisible formal 𝒪_E-module of height one; “the” Lubin–Tate formal group G = G_LT of E). Any Lubin–Tate formal group law over 𝒪_E is the unique (up to unique isomorphism) lift of a 1-dimensional formal 𝒪_E-module of height one over k whose Lie algebra has the correct 𝒪_E-action. For E p-adic, G_k is classified by a finite projective W_{𝒪_E}(k)-module M with σ-linear isomorphism F : M[1/π] ≅ M[1/π] such that M ⊂ F(M) ⊂ (1/π)M; one takes M = W_{𝒪_E}(k) with F = (1/π)σ. Under this normalization G is already defined over 𝒪_E, and one can choose a coordinate G ≅ Spf 𝒪_E[[X]] with log_G(X) = X + (1/π)X^q + (1/π²)X^{q²} + … + (1/πⁿ)X^{qⁿ} + ….
items.note: Dieudonné theory renormalized as in [SW20, p. 99] (footnote 3). The printed uniqueness omits the height-one (π-divisibility) condition; see newIssues. Lubin–Tate formal 𝒪_E-modules, their logarithm and torsion are owned by the accepted Part II 'Finite flat group schemes and integral p-adic Hodge theory, Part II: Lubin–Tate formal modules and quasi-canonical lifts' (LubinTateFormalModulesAndQuasiCanonicalLifts; PAPER-BURUNGALE-KOBAYASHI-OTA-21 route 2 and PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18 route 8, both accepted), whose brief says 'VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:positive-basic-examples owns the diamond universal-cover calculation. Supply their common formal-module foundation'. VB3:positive-basic-examples plans only the universal-cover calculation, so this item is missing and goes to that Part II, whose brief must be extended to E of equal characteristic (it is stated for finite E/ℚ_p). Mathlib has FormalGroup (Mathlib/RingTheory/FormalGroup/Basic.lean) but no Lubin–Tate formal groups.

items.name: Logarithm exact sequence for the Lubin–Tate group
items.statement: log_G defines a map of rigid-analytic varieties log_G : G^ad_E ≅ 𝔻_E → 𝔾^ad_{a,E} from the open unit disc G^ad_E = Spa 𝒪_E[[X]] ×_{Spa 𝒪_E} Spa E, and there is an exact sequence 0 → G^ad_E[π^∞] → G^ad_E → 𝔾^ad_{a,E} → 0 on the big étale site of adic spaces over Spa E, where G^ad_E[π^∞] = ⋃_n Spa A_n[1/π] = ⊔_n Spa E_n, with G[πⁿ] = Spa A_n finite of degree qⁿ over 𝒪_E and E_n|E totally ramified.
items.note: Unnumbered. The logarithm and torsion of the Lubin–Tate formal module are formal-module foundations owned by the accepted Part II LubinTateFormalModulesAndQuasiCanonicalLifts (PAPER-BURUNGALE-KOBAYASHI-OTA-21 route 2: 'add the formal O-action, logarithm, torsion, coordinate change and complete local-field point APIs'), stated there for finite E/ℚ_p; VB3:positive-basic-examples plans only the universal-cover calculation. Missing; route to that Part II with the extension to equal characteristic. EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison:ET.6a constructs Lubin–Tate towers from formal-module owners but not this sequence.

items.name: The universal cover G̃ ≅ Spf 𝒪_E[[X̃^{1/p^∞}]] and its points
items.statement: The universal cover G̃ = lim_{←,×π} G is isomorphic to Spf 𝒪_E[[X̃^{1/p^∞}]], with X̃ = lim_{n→∞} X_n^{qⁿ} (X̃ ≡ X_n^{qⁿ} mod πⁿ). The logarithm log_G : G̃_E → G_E → 𝔾_{a,E} is given by Σ_{i∈ℤ} π^i X̃^{q^{−i}} = lim_{n→∞} πⁿ log_G(X_n) = lim_{n→∞} log_G([πⁿ]_G(X_n)). For any π-adically complete 𝒪_E-algebra A, G̃(A) ≅ G̃(A/π) = Hom_{𝒪_E}(E/𝒪_E, G(A/π))[1/π], and G̃(A) = lim_{←, x↦x^p} A°° = A^{♭,°°} ⊂ A^♭, the topologically nilpotent elements of the tilt.
items.note: Unnumbered. VB3:positive-basic-examples: 'Lubin–Tate universal-cover calculations'.

items.name: Proposition II.2.2: H⁰(X_S, 𝒪(1)) ≅ G̃(R^{♯+}) with evaluation = logarithm
items.statement: Let S = Spa(R, R⁺) be an affinoid perfectoid space over 𝔽_q and let S^♯ = Spa(R^♯, R^{♯+}) be an untilt of S over E, giving rise to the closed immersion S^♯ ↪ X_S. Let 𝒪_{X_S}(1) be the line bundle on X_S corresponding to the isocrystal (E, π^{−1}). Then the map G̃(R^{♯+}) ≅ R°° → H⁰(Y_S, 𝒪_{Y_S}) : X ↦ Σ_{i∈ℤ} π^i [X^{q^{−i}}] defines a natural isomorphism G̃(R^{♯+}) ≅ H⁰(X_S, 𝒪_{X_S}(1)) = H⁰(Y_S, 𝒪_{Y_S})^{φ=π}. Under this isomorphism, the map H⁰(X_S, 𝒪_{X_S}(1)) → H⁰(S^♯, 𝒪_{S^♯}) = R^♯ of evaluation at S^♯ is given by the logarithm map log_G : G̃(R^{♯+}) → G(R^{♯+}) → R^♯.
items.note: Equal characteristic: explicit power series with r_i = r_{i+1}^q. p-adic: H⁰ = B_{R,[1,∞]}^{φ=π}, replaced by B⁺_crys of R^{♯+}/π, then [SW13, Theorem A, Lemma 3.5.1]. VB3:positive-basic-examples: 'Use FS II.2.1's Lubin–Tate calculation ... as the positive/basic input to VB2:classification'.

items.name: E_∞ is perfectoid and embeds in G̃
items.statement: The field E_∞, the completion of the union of all E_n, is perfectoid: there is a closed immersion Spf 𝒪_{E∞} ↪ G̃ = Spf 𝒪_E[[X̃^{1/p^∞}]], which induces an isomorphism Spf 𝒪^♭_{E∞} ≅ Spf 𝔽_q[[X^{1/p^∞}]]. Over E_∞ there is an isomorphism 𝒪_E ≅ (T_πG)(𝒪_{E∞}) ⊂ G̃(𝒪_{E∞}); hence if S^♯ lives over E_∞, one gets a nonzero section of 𝒪_{X_S}(1) vanishing at S^♯ ⊂ X_S.
items.note: Unnumbered ('Recall'); here E_∞ is the Lubin–Tate extension (not E(π^{1/p^∞}) of §II.1 — same notation). VB3:positive-basic-examples: 'Lubin–Tate universal-cover calculations'.

items.name: Proposition II.2.3: 0 → 𝒪_{X_S} → 𝒪_{X_S}(1) → 𝒪_{S♯} → 0
items.statement: For any perfectoid space S with untilt S^♯ over E_∞ (the Lubin–Tate extension), the above construction defines an exact sequence 0 → 𝒪_{X_S} → 𝒪_{X_S}(1) → 𝒪_{S^♯} → 0 of 𝒪_{X_S}-modules.
items.note: Proof: reduces to geometric points; the section Σ π^i [X̃^{q^{−i}}] is the pullback of the logarithm on G̃^ad_E ∖ {0}, whose zero locus is ⊔_n Spa E_∞ with simple zeros. RF3: 'construct O(n), tensor and dual comparisons, divisor sections and transition functions'; VB3:positive-basic-examples 'positive line-bundle ... calculations'.

items.name: Corollary II.2.4: (BC(𝒪(1)) ∖ {0})/E^× ≅ Div¹
items.statement: There is a well-defined map BC(𝒪(1)) ∖ {0} → Div¹ sending a nonzero section f ∈ H⁰(X_S, 𝒪_{X_S}(1)) to the closed Cartier divisor given by V(f). This descends to an isomorphism (BC(𝒪(1)) ∖ {0})/E^× ≅ Div¹. Moreover BC(𝒪(1)) ≅ Spd 𝔽_q[[X^{1/p^∞}]], BC(𝒪(1)) ∖ {0} ≅ Spa 𝔽_q((X^{1/p^∞})) ≅ Spd E_∞, and the map to Div¹ is Spd E_∞ → Spd E → Spd E/φ^ℤ, the first map being a quotient by 𝒪_E^× and the second the quotient by π^ℤ (φ = π on BC(𝒪(1))).
items.note: Cited from [Far20b, Proposition 2.12]. Planned by the node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:positive-basic-examples/fundamental-exact-sequence ('FS II.2.3 and II.2.4 ... there is a well-defined map BC(O(1)) minus {0} -> Div^1 sending a nonzero section f to V(f), and it descends to an isomorphism (BC(O(1)) minus {0})/E^times = Div^1'), whose hypotheses include BC(O(1)) ∖ {0} = Spd E_∞ and the two-step quotient by 𝒪_E^× and π^ℤ.

items.name: Div¹ over Perf_k and local class field theory
items.statement: Working on Perf_k, Div¹ = Spd Ĕ/φ^ℤ, whose π₁^ét is given by the absolute Galois group of E (Weil group version). Corollary II.2.4 gives a canonical E^×-torsor over Div¹, hence a natural map from the absolute Galois group of E to the profinite completion of E^×; by comparison with Lubin–Tate theory, this is the usual Artin reciprocity map.
items.note: Unnumbered remark; details in [Far20b, §2.3]. Planned by the node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:positive-basic-examples/fundamental-exact-sequence: its last proof step says 'the induced map from the absolute Galois group of E to the profinite completion of E^times is the Artin reciprocity map', and its acceptance test is 'Verify the Artin reciprocity identification against local class field theory'. The node should also state it. The Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory roadmap routes local class field theory 'never through Lubin–Tate theory', so this is a comparison with that Artin map, not a new construction of it.

items.name: Proposition II.2.5(i): negative slopes — H⁰ = 0 and BC(𝒪(λ)[1]) is smooth
items.statement: Let λ ∈ ℚ, λ < 0. Then H⁰(X_S, 𝒪_{X_S}(λ)) = 0 for all S ∈ Perf_{𝔽_q}. Moreover, the projection from BC(𝒪(λ)[1]) : S ↦ H¹(X_S, 𝒪_{X_S}(λ)) to the point ∗ is relatively representable in locally spatial diamonds, partially proper, and cohomologically smooth.
items.note: Proof: n = −1 via 0 → E̲ → (𝔸¹_{S♯})^♢ → BC(𝒪(−1)[1]) → 0 and [Sch17a, Proposition 24.2]; induction via [Sch17a, Proposition 23.13] (the printed induction sequence has a sign misprint, (PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E11)). VB3:positive-basic-examples: 'Negative H^1 spaces have their separate construction'; cohomological smoothness needs DiamondSixOperations.

items.name: Proposition II.2.5(ii): BC(𝒪) = E̲ and RΓ_proét(S, E̲) ≅ RΓ(X_S, 𝒪)
items.statement: For λ = 0, the map E̲ → BC(𝒪) is an isomorphism of pro-étale sheaves, and the pro-étale sheafification of S ↦ H¹(X_S, 𝒪_{X_S}) vanishes. In particular, for all S one gets an isomorphism RΓ_proét(S, E̲) → RΓ(X_S, 𝒪_{X_S}).
items.note: Proof: the sequence 0 → H⁰(X_S,𝒪) → H⁰(X_S,𝒪(1)) → R^♯ → H¹(X_S,𝒪) → 0 with the middle map the Lubin–Tate logarithm, pro-étale locally surjective with kernel E. Used for Ext¹(𝒪(λ),𝒪(λ)) = 0 in Theorem II.2.14 and in Corollary II.2.20. VB3:general-BC: 'for degree-zero pieces identify the locally profinite E-vector-space behavior'; VB1: 'Compute O(n) sections and first cohomology'.

items.name: Proposition II.2.5(iii): positive slopes — H¹ = 0 on affinoids and BC(𝒪(λ)) is smooth
items.statement: For λ > 0, one has H¹(X_S, 𝒪_{X_S}(λ)) = 0 for all affinoid S ∈ Perf_{𝔽_q}, and the projection from BC(𝒪(λ)) : S ↦ H⁰(X_S, 𝒪_{X_S}(λ)) to the point ∗ is relatively representable in locally spatial diamonds, partially proper, and cohomologically smooth.
items.note: Proof: reduce to λ = n ∈ ℤ by unramified extension of degree s; surjectivity of φ − πⁿ : B_{R,[1,q]} → B_{R,[1,1]} by explicit geometric series; smoothness by induction from 0 → BC(𝒪(n)) → BC(𝒪(n+1)) → (𝔸¹_{S♯})^♢ → 0 and [Sch17a, Proposition 23.13]. VB3:general-BC: 'For the positive-slope range prove dimension and cohomological smoothness'; VB1 for the H¹ vanishing.

items.name: Proposition II.2.5(iv): BC(𝒪(λ)) is a perfectoid open ball for small λ
items.statement: If 0 < λ ≤ [E : ℚ_p] (resp. for all positive λ if E is of equal characteristic), there is an isomorphism BC(𝒪(λ)) ≅ Spd k[[x₁^{1/p^∞}, …, x_r^{1/p^∞}]] where λ = r/s with coprime integers r, s > 0.
items.note: Proof: equal characteristic by explicit power series; p-adic by pushforward to E = ℚ_p and [SW13, Theorem A, Proposition 3.1.3(iii)] (the printed coefficient relation has the shift reversed, PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E9, and the printed eigen-equation has r and s swapped, PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E10). Stated in the node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/cohomology-of-twists ('(iv) If 0 < lambda <= [E:Q_p] ... BC(O(lambda)) = Spd k[[x_1^{1/p^infty},...,x_r^{1/p^infty}]]'); VB3:general-BC: 'State the slope bounds in perfectoid-open-ball identifications'.

items.name: Unramified change of coefficients: pullback multiplies slopes, pushforward of 𝒪(s) is 𝒪(s/r)
items.statement: Let E′|E be the unramified extension of degree r and f : X_{S,E′} = X_{S,E} ⊗_E E′ = Y_S/φ^{rℤ} → X_{S,E} = X_S the induced finite étale cover. Then f^*𝒪_{X_S}(1) ≅ 𝒪_{X_{S,E′}}(r), so f^* multiplies Harder–Narasimhan slopes by r; f_*𝒪_{X_{S,E′}}(s) ≅ 𝒪_{X_S}(s/r) for s ∈ ℤ; and every vector bundle ℰ on X_S is a direct summand of f_*f^*ℰ = ℰ ⊗_E E′.
items.locator: Chapter II, used in the proofs of Proposition II.2.5 (p. 62), Proposition II.2.13 (p. 69), Theorem II.2.14 (p. 70), Proposition II.3.2 (p. 77) and Corollary II.3.3 (p. 79)
items.note: FS use it without a separate statement: 'we can reduce to the case λ = n ∈ ℤ by replacing E by its unramified extension of degree s' (II.2.5), 'the pullback of 𝒪_{X_{C,E}}(1) is 𝒪_{X_{C,E′}}(r)' (II.2.13), '𝒪_{X_C}(λ) = f_*𝒪_{X_{C,E′}}(s)' (II.2.14), 'this pullback multiplies slopes by [E′:E] ... ℰ′ is a direct factor of f_*f^*ℰ′ = ℰ′ ⊗_E E′' (II.3.2), 'π_{2r*}' (II.3.3). Planned by the node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0/scalar-extension-adjunction ('Under E(-) these correspond to pi_{E'|E}^* and pi_{E'|E *} along pi_{E'|E} : X_{E'} -> X_E'), with VB0's standard block computing the slopes. Added in review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21).

items.name: Cohomology of 𝒪(n) via B_{R,[1,∞]}
items.statement: For S = Spa(R, R⁺) affinoid with pseudouniformizer ϖ and n ∈ ℤ, the map [B_{R,[1,∞]} →^{φ−πⁿ} B_{R,[1,∞]}] → [B_{R,[1,q]} →^{φ−πⁿ} B_{R,[1,1]}] is a quasi-isomorphism, where B_{R,[1,∞]} = O(Y_{S,[1,∞]}), Y_{S,[1,∞]} = {|[ϖ]| ≤ |π| ≠ 0} ⊂ Spa W_{𝒪_E}(R⁺). In particular H⁰(X_S, 𝒪_{X_S}(n)) = B_{R,[1,∞]}^{φ=πⁿ}. The proof uses the exact sequences 0 → W_{𝒪_E}(R⁺)[1/π] → B_{R,[1,∞]} ⊕ B_{R,[0,q]}[1/π] → B_{R,[1,q]} → 0 (and the analogue with [0,1], [1,1]) and invertibility of φ − πⁿ on B_{R,[0,q]}[1/π] → B_{R,[0,1]}[1/π] and on W_{𝒪_E}(R⁺)[1/π].
items.locator: Chapter II, §II.2.2, proof of Proposition II.2.5, p. 63
items.note: Unnumbered but used in Proposition II.2.2 (p-adic case) and in II.2.5(iv). VB1: 'Compute O(n) sections and first cohomology with actual Frobenius maps and signs ... establish them from annular descent.'

items.name: Fibrewise nonzero sections and 0 → 𝒪(n) → 𝒪(n+1) → 𝒪_{S♯} → 0
items.statement: For affinoid S one can choose a fibrewise nonzero map 𝒪_{X_S} → 𝒪_{X_S}(1), by taking a map S → BC(𝒪(1)) ≅ Spd 𝔽_q[[x^{1/p^∞}]] sending x to a pseudouniformizer. For the corresponding untilt S^♯ and any n ∈ ℤ one gets an exact sequence 0 → 𝒪_{X_S}(n) → 𝒪_{X_S}(n+1) → 𝒪_{S^♯} → 0, and for n > 0 an exact sequence of v-sheaves 0 → BC(𝒪(n))|_S → BC(𝒪(n+1))|_S → (𝔸¹_{S^♯})^♢ → 0.
items.locator: Chapter II, §II.2.2, proof of Proposition II.2.5, p. 63
items.note: Unnumbered; from Proposition II.2.3. Used repeatedly (II.2.5, II.2.9, II.3.1). RF3: 'divisor sections and transition functions'; VB3:positive-basic-examples 'exact-sequence behavior'.

items.name: Theorem II.2.6: ampleness of 𝒪(1) on X_S
items.statement: Let S = Spa(R, R⁺) be an affinoid perfectoid space over 𝔽_q and let ℰ be any vector bundle on X_S. Then there is an integer n₀ such that for all n ≥ n₀, the vector bundle ℰ(n) is globally generated, i.e. there is a surjective map 𝒪_{X_S}^m → ℰ(n) for some m ≥ 0, and moreover H¹(X_S, ℰ(n)) = 0.
items.note: Cited from [KL15, Proposition 6.2.4]; the theorem stands. FS's proof reduces to free M_{[1,q]} via K₀ (cf. [KL15, Corollary 1.5.3]), writes φ_M = A^{−1}φ with A ∈ GL_m(B_{R,[1,q]}), and claims the quantitative surjectivity (II.2.1). As printed, (II.2.1) is false and the norm computations use the reciprocal radius convention, and the containment of φ(A^{−1}w₂) drops a factor π^{−N} (see newIssues); the blueprint must follow [KL15, Proposition 6.2.4] or a corrected estimate. VB2:ampleness: 'For affinoid perfectoid S prove that sufficiently positive twists of a bundle are globally generated with higher cohomology zero'; node VB2:ampleness/quantitative-global-generation.

items.name: Proposition II.2.7: abstract GAGA
items.statement: Let (X, 𝒪_X) be a locally ringed spectral space equipped with a line bundle 𝒪_X(1) such that for any vector bundle ℰ on X, there is some n₀ such that for all n ≥ n₀, the bundle ℰ(n) is globally generated. Moreover, assume that for i > 0, the cohomology group Hⁱ(X, ℰ(n)) = 0 vanishes for all sufficiently large n. Let P = ⊕_{n≥0} H⁰(X, 𝒪_X(n)) be the graded ring and X^alg = Proj(P). There is a natural map (X, 𝒪_X) → X^alg of locally ringed topological spaces, and pullback along this map induces an equivalence of categories between vector bundles on X^alg and vector bundles on (X, 𝒪_X). Moreover, for any vector bundle ℰ^alg on X^alg with pullback ℰ to X, the map Hⁱ(X^alg, ℰ^alg) → Hⁱ(X, ℰ) is an isomorphism for all i ≥ 0.
items.note: Axiomatization of [KL15, Theorem 6.3.9]. The map is built from P[g^{−1}]₀ → O(D(g)) for g ∈ P_n; FS call this construction 'formal (and does not rely on any assumptions)', but the D(g) cover X only because O_X(n) is globally generated for large n (see newIssues; the accepted restructuring RS-20 made the same point and moved the global morphism, the tautological twists and the pullback of O(1) to VB2:ampleness). The inverse functor is ℰ ↦ (⊕ H⁰(X, ℰ(n)))~. A spectral space is quasicompact, as the proof uses. VB2:ampleness: 'Compare bundles and cohomology on X_S and the Proj curve built in RF3'; node VB2:ampleness/gaga-equivalence.

items.name: Proj of a graded ring and its tautological ample line bundle
items.statement: For any graded ring P = ⊕_{n≥0} P_n, one can define a separated scheme Proj(P) by gluing Spec P[f^{−1}]₀ for all f ∈ P_n, n > 0, where P[f^{−1}]₀ = lim_{→i} f^{−i}P_{in} is the degree 0 part of P[f^{−1}].
items.note: In Mathlib: AlgebraicGeometry.Proj (Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/ProjectiveSpectrum/Scheme.lean) for a graded algebra 𝒜 : ℕ → Submodule, with the open immersions Proj.awayι : Spec (A_f)₀ ⟶ Proj 𝒜 (Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/ProjectiveSpectrum/Basic.lean:186, with the instance IsOpenImmersion at line 193) and separatedness Proj.isSeparated : IsSeparated (toSpecZero 𝒜) (Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/ProjectiveSpectrum/Proper.lean:82). The rest of FS's paragraph (quasicompactness, the tautological line bundles O_{Proj(P)}(n) for large n and O(1), ampleness and pullback to O_X(1)) is not in Mathlib and is a separate item (see missingItems), owned by VB2:ampleness after RS-20.

items.name: Tautological twists on Proj(P) and the pullback of 𝒪(1) (situation of Proposition II.2.7)
items.statement: In the situation of Proposition II.2.7 ((X, 𝒪_X) a locally ringed spectral space with a line bundle 𝒪_X(1) all of whose sufficiently positive twists are globally generated), if n is large enough that 𝒪_X(n) is globally generated then Proj(P) is covered by Spec P[f^{−1}]₀ for finitely many f ∈ P_n (X is quasicompact), so Proj(P) is quasicompact; the loci D(f) ⊂ X, f ∈ P_n, cover X, so the chart maps D(f) → D₊(f) glue to a morphism of locally ringed spaces X → Proj(P); there is a tautological line bundle 𝒪_{Proj(P)}(n) for all sufficiently large n, compatible with tensor products, hence 𝒪_{Proj(P)}(1), which is ample, and its pullback to X is 𝒪_X(1).
items.locator: Chapter II, §II.2.3, paragraph after Proposition II.2.7 and first paragraph of its proof, pp. 66–67
items.note: Split off c2a-constr-Proj-graded-ring, whose first sentence is in Mathlib. The accepted restructuring RS-20 (research/blueprint/restructure/RS-20.result.json) makes VB2:ampleness the owner of 'The global morphism (X_S, O_{X_S}) -> X_S^alg = Proj(P) on all of X_S, the tautological twists O_Proj(P)(m) (m >= n0) and O_Proj(P)(1), and the pullback identification', formerly RF3; RF3 keeps P, Proj(P) and the chart maps on the D(g). Added in review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21).

items.name: Remark II.2.8: X^alg is independent of the choice of 𝒪_X(1)
items.statement: X^alg is, up to canonical isomorphism, independent of the choice of a line bundle 𝒪_X(1) satisfying the hypotheses of Proposition II.2.7.
items.note: Stated without proof ('One can check'). Planned by the node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:ampleness/gaga-equivalence, whose statement ends 'X^alg is independent of the chosen O_X(1) up to canonical isomorphism.'

items.name: The algebraic curve X_S^alg
items.statement: For any affinoid perfectoid space S over 𝔽_q, define the algebraic curve X_S^alg = Proj ⊕_{n≥0} H⁰(X_S, 𝒪_{X_S}(n)). There is a well-defined map X_S → X_S^alg of locally ringed spectral spaces, pullback along which defines an equivalence of categories of vector bundles, and is compatible with cohomology.
items.note: Consequence of Theorem II.2.6 and Proposition II.2.7 (X_S qcqs for affinoid S by II.1.16). Connects to the original [FF18] definition for S = Spa(F, 𝒪_F). RF3: 'Form the graded algebra of global sections for affinoid S and construct Proj and the analytic-to-schematic map'; VB2:ampleness for the equivalence.

items.name: Proposition II.2.9: X_C^alg is a connected regular noetherian curve
items.statement: Let C be a complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean field over 𝔽_q. Then X_C^alg is a connected regular noetherian scheme of Krull dimension 1, and the map |X_C| → |X_C^alg| induces a bijection between |X_C|^cl and the closed points of |X_C^alg|. Moreover, for any classical point x ∈ |X_C|, the complement X_C^alg ∖ {x} is the spectrum of a principal ideal domain.
items.note: Proof: for a classical point x, 0 → 𝒪 → 𝒪(1) → 𝒪_{C♯} → 0 gives f_x ∈ H⁰(𝒪(1)) with V(f_x) = Spec C^♯; every g ∈ H⁰(𝒪(n)) factors as ∏ f_{x_i}^{n_i}·h with h ∈ E^×, so P[f^{−1}]₀ is a PID. VB2:ampleness: 'For S a geometric perfectoid point, prove regular noetherian dimension-one structure of the schematic curve, its local principal-ideal properties and the closed-point description under the source's hypotheses.'

items.name: Proposition II.2.10: Pic(X_C) ≅ ℤ
items.statement: The map ℤ → Pic(X_C), n ↦ 𝒪_{X_C}(n), is an isomorphism.
items.note: Proof: by II.2.9 any line bundle is trivial off one closed point, so ≅ 𝒪(n[x]); and 𝒪([x]) ≅ 𝒪(1) (cited as II.2.2; the exact sequence is II.2.3/II.2.9). Planned by the node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/degree-rank-slope-and-HN-formalism ('Pic(X_C) = Z via n -> O_{X_C}(n), so deg(E) := deg(det E) is well defined'), whose first proof step is FS's proof.

items.name: Degree, rank, slope; semistable and stable bundles on X_C
items.statement: For a vector bundle ℰ on X_C define deg(ℰ) = deg(det(ℰ)) ∈ ℤ via deg : Pic(X_C) ≅ ℤ of Proposition II.2.10, the rank rk(ℰ), and for nonzero ℰ the slope μ(ℰ) = deg(ℰ)/rk(ℰ) ∈ ℚ. ℰ is semistable if for all proper nonzero ℱ ⊂ ℰ one has μ(ℱ) ≤ μ(ℰ), and stable if μ(ℱ) < μ(ℰ) for all such ℱ.
items.note: VB1: 'Build degree, rank, slope, saturated subbundles and semistability, including exact-sequence degree additivity'.

items.name: (rk, deg) on X_C satisfy the Harder–Narasimhan axiomatics
items.statement: Rank and degree of vector bundles on X_C satisfy the Harder–Narasimhan axiomatics of [FF18, 5.5.1]; for example, rank and degree are additive in short exact sequences.
items.note: Unnumbered ('It is easy to see'). VB1: 'including exact-sequence degree additivity and the behavior of torsion quotients'.

items.name: Example II.2.11: 𝒪_{X_C}(λ) is stable of slope λ
items.statement: For any λ ∈ ℚ, the bundle 𝒪_{X_C}(λ) is stable of slope λ.
items.note: Proof via r-th wedge powers: det(ℱ) ≅ 𝒪(s) ↪ 𝒪(rλ)^m, using that ∧^r 𝒪(λ) is a direct sum of copies of 𝒪(rλ); so s ≤ rλ, with equality only if r ≥ denominator of λ = rk 𝒪(λ). VB2:classification: 'these stable bundles have the ranks and degrees prescribed by reduced rational slopes'.

items.name: Proposition II.2.12: existence and uniqueness of the Harder–Narasimhan filtration
items.statement: Any vector bundle ℰ on X_C admits a unique exhaustive separating ℚ-indexed filtration by saturated subbundles ℰ^{≥λ} ⊂ ℰ, called the Harder–Narasimhan filtration, such that ℰ^λ := ℰ^{≥λ}/ℰ^{>λ}, where ℰ^{>λ} = ⋃_{λ′>λ} ℰ^{≥λ′}, is semistable of slope λ. The formation of the Harder–Narasimhan filtration is functorial in ℰ.
items.note: Stated with □ and no proof (general HN formalism, [FF18, 5.5]). Planned by the node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/degree-rank-slope-and-HN-formalism ('Every E on X_C admits a unique exhaustive separating Q-indexed HN filtration by saturated subbundles, functorial in E'). The abstract HN formalism of [FF18, §5.5] is owned by the accepted FF18 route 3 Part II; this item is its instance on X_C.

items.name: Proposition II.2.13(a): HN filtration commutes with extension of C
items.statement: Let ℰ be a vector bundle on X_C, and let C′|C be an extension of complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean fields, with pullback ℰ′ of ℰ to X_{C′}. Then (ℰ′)^{≥λ} is the pullback of ℰ^{≥λ}.
items.note: Planned by the node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:classification/HN-filtration-base-change ('FS II.2.13: the Harder-Narasimhan filtration commutes with extension of C and rescales under extension of E': '(E')^{>= lambda} is the pullback of E^{>= lambda}' and, for E'|E finite separable of degree r, 'the pullback of E^{>= lambda/r}'). Proof: pullbacks of semistable bundles stay semistable; the first HN piece descends by Proposition II.2.1; Galois descent for E′|E, the slope rescaling coming from the pullback of 𝒪(1) being 𝒪(r).

items.name: Proposition II.2.13(b): HN filtration under finite separable extension of E
items.statement: If E′|E is a finite separable extension of degree r, and ℰ′ is the pullback of ℰ along X_{C,E′} = X_{C,E} ⊗_E E′ → X_{C,E} = X_C, then (ℰ′)^{≥λ} is the pullback of ℰ^{≥λ/r}.
items.note: Planned by the node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:classification/HN-filtration-base-change ('FS II.2.13: the Harder-Narasimhan filtration commutes with extension of C and rescales under extension of E': '(E')^{>= lambda} is the pullback of E^{>= lambda}' and, for E'|E finite separable of degree r, 'the pullback of E^{>= lambda/r}'). Proof: pullbacks of semistable bundles stay semistable; the first HN piece descends by Proposition II.2.1; Galois descent for E′|E, the slope rescaling coming from the pullback of 𝒪(1) being 𝒪(r).

items.name: Theorem II.2.14(a): every vector bundle on X_C is ⊕ 𝒪(λ_i)
items.statement: Any vector bundle ℰ on X_C is isomorphic to a direct sum of vector bundles of the form 𝒪_{X_C}(λ) with λ ∈ ℚ.
items.note: Proof (after Hartl–Pink [HP04]) by induction on rank: non-semistable case splits by H¹(𝒪(λ)) = 0 for λ > 0; semistable case reduces (via unramified extension, twisting, extension of C using GL_n(E)-torsors and [Sch17a, Lemma 10.13]) to Lemma II.2.15. Footnote 4 surveys earlier proofs ([HP04], [Ked04], [FF18], [Col02]). VB2:classification: 'Prove that every bundle at a geometric point is a direct sum of the stable O(lambda)'.

items.name: Theorem II.2.14(b): semistable of slope λ ⇒ 𝒪(λ)^m
items.statement: If a vector bundle ℰ on X_C is semistable of slope λ, then ℰ ≅ 𝒪_{X_C}(λ)^m for some m ≥ 0.
items.note: Uses Ext¹_{X_C}(𝒪(λ), 𝒪(λ)) = 0 from Proposition II.2.5(ii). VB2:classification (same quote as part (a)).

items.name: Semistable bundles of fixed slope form an abelian category with stable simple objects
items.statement: The category of semistable vector bundles of slope λ on X_C is abelian with simple objects the stable vector bundles of slope λ; in particular a nonzero map 𝒪_{X_C}(λ) → ℰ with ℰ semistable of slope λ is injective with semistable cokernel of slope λ.
items.locator: Chapter II, §II.2.4, proof of Theorem II.2.14, p. 70
items.note: Unnumbered parenthetical fact from the HN formalism, used in the induction of Theorem II.2.14. Planned by the node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/degree-rank-slope-and-HN-formalism: 'C_lambda^ss is abelian and stable under extensions, its objects have finite length and its simple objects are the stable objects of slope lambda'.

items.name: Lemma II.2.15: key lemma — extensions of 𝒪(1/n) by 𝒪(−1) acquire sections
items.statement: Let 0 → 𝒪_{X_C}(−1) → ℰ → 𝒪_{X_C}(1/n) → 0 be an extension of vector bundles on X_C, for some n ≥ 1. Then there is some extension C′|C of complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean fields such that H⁰(X_{C′}, ℰ|_{X_{C′}}) ≠ 0.
items.note: New proof: otherwise BC(𝒪(1/n)) ↪ BC(𝒪(−1)[1]) = (𝔸¹_{C♯})^♢/E; non-classical points (II.1.9) and the contracting E^×-action force an isomorphism, contradicted by classifying E-linear endomorphisms of (𝔸¹_{C♯})^♢ (in the p-adic case also since 𝔸¹ is not perfectoid; footnote 5: equal-characteristic non-perfectoidness left open). VB3:positive-basic-examples: 'Use ... II.2.15's endomorphism analysis as the positive/basic input to VB2:classification'.

items.name: E-linear endomorphisms of (𝔸¹_{C♯})^♢ are scalars
items.statement: Every E-linear map (𝔸¹_{C^♯})^♢ → (𝔸¹_{C^♯})^♢ is of the form X ↦ cX for some c ∈ C^♯; hence it is either an isomorphism or zero. (Such maps are maps 𝔸¹_{C♯} → 𝔸¹_{C♯} if E is p-adic by [SW20, Proposition 10.2.3], resp. 𝔸¹_{C,perf} → 𝔸¹_{C,perf} in equal characteristic, i.e. additive convergent power series g with g(aX) = a g(X) for a ∈ E; g(πX) = πg(X) forces g linear.)
items.locator: Chapter II, §II.2.4, proof of Lemma II.2.15, pp. 71–72
items.note: Unnumbered. VB3:positive-basic-examples: 'II.2.15's endomorphism analysis'.

items.name: Proposition II.2.16(a): BC(ℰ) is a locally spatial diamond, partially proper over S
items.statement: Let S be a perfectoid space over 𝔽_q and ℰ a vector bundle on X_S. Then the Banach–Colmez space BC(ℰ) : T ↦ H⁰(X_T, ℰ|_{X_T}) is a locally spatial diamond, partially proper over S.
items.note: Proof: by Theorem II.2.6, 0 → ℰ → 𝒪(n)^m → 𝒪(n′)^{m′}, so BC(ℰ) is closed in BC(𝒪(n))^m; conclude by II.2.5(iii). VB3:general-BC ('Construct projectivization with scalar action and prove the properness ...') and VB3:positive-basic-examples ('Prove diamond representability, local spatiality and exact-sequence behavior').

items.name: Proposition II.2.16(b): the projectivized Banach–Colmez space (BC(ℰ) ∖ {0})/E^× is proper over S
items.statement: Let S be a perfectoid space over 𝔽_q and ℰ a vector bundle on X_S. The projectivized Banach–Colmez space (BC(ℰ) ∖ {0})/E^× is a locally spatial diamond, proper over S.
items.note: Proof: reduce to (BC(ℰ) ∖ {0})/π^ℤ (𝒪_E^× acts freely, [Sch17a, Proposition 11.24]) and apply Lemma II.2.17 with Remark II.2.18. VB3:projectivized-properness: 'Prove II.2.16's properness of (BC(E)\{0})/E× using II.2.6 ampleness and II.2.5(iii)'.

items.name: Lemma II.2.17: quotients by contracting automorphisms are spectral
items.statement: Let X be a taut locally spectral space such that for any x ∈ X, the set X_x ⊂ X of generalizations of x is a totally ordered chain under specialization. Let γ : X ≅ X be an automorphism of X such that the subset X₀ ⊂ X of fixed points is a spectral space. Moreover, assume that (i) for all x ∈ X, the sequence γⁿ(x) for n → ∞ converges towards X₀, i.e. for all open neighborhoods U of X₀, one has γⁿ(x) ∈ U for all sufficiently positive n; (ii) for all x ∈ X ∖ X₀, the sequence γⁿ(x) for n → −∞ diverges, i.e. for all quasicompact open subspaces U ⊂ X, one has γⁿ(x) ∉ U for all sufficiently negative n. Then X₀ ⊂ X is a closed subspace, the action of γ on X ∖ X₀ is free and totally discontinuous (i.e. the action map (X ∖ X₀) × ℤ → (X ∖ X₀) × (X ∖ X₀) is a closed immersion), and the quotient (X ∖ X₀)/γ^ℤ is a spectral space.
items.note: Pure point-set topology of locally spectral spaces; the key input to II.2.16(b). Planned by the node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:projectivized-properness/contracting-action-lemma ('FS II.2.17: quotients by contracting automorphisms of taut locally spectral spaces'), which states the lemma with FS's hypotheses and proof.

items.name: Remark II.2.18(i): generalizations in a locally spatial diamond form a chain
items.statement: If X is any locally spatial diamond, then |X| is a locally spectral space such that for all x ∈ |X|, the set of generalizations of x in |X| is a totally ordered chain under specialization.
items.note: Cited from [Sch17a, Proposition 11.19] and the analogous property for analytic adic spaces. DiamondsAndVStacks:D5: 'Prove the structural and permanence results of 11.17–11.31'.

items.name: Remark II.2.18(ii): partially proper over spatial implies taut
items.statement: If X is a locally spatial diamond that is partially proper over a spatial diamond, then |X| is taut.
items.note: Cited from [Sch17a, Proposition 18.10]. DiamondEtaleCohomology:C4 'Build[s] ECD §18 on D5's small-v-stack geometry ... Distinguish universal closedness, separatedness, properness and partial properness. Prove the tautness comparison in its stated locally spatial scope.' The VB3 contracting-action node records it as a hypothesis ('tautness holds if X is partially proper over a spatial diamond by ECD Prop. 18.10').

items.name: Theorem II.2.19(i): upper semicontinuity of the HN polygon
items.statement: Let S be a perfectoid space over 𝔽_q and let ℰ be a vector bundle over X_S of constant rank n. The function taking a geometric point Spa C → S of S to the Harder–Narasimhan polygon of ℰ|_{X_C} is upper semicontinuous.
items.note: Cited from [KL15, Theorem 7.4.5, 7.4.9, 7.3.7, Proposition 7.3.6]. Proof: the locus where H⁰(X_C, ℱ|_{X_C}) ≠ 0 is the image of the proper map (BC(ℱ) ∖ {0})/E^× → S (II.2.16), hence closed; applied to (∧^iℰ)(−d); endpoint locally constant via det(ℰ)^∨. VB4: 'Construct the geometric HN polygon of E_s, prove its semicontinuity with the source's dominance convention'.

items.name: The HN polygon as convex hull of (i, d_i)
items.statement: For a vector bundle ℰ of rank n on X_C, the Harder–Narasimhan polygon is the convex hull of the points (i, d_i) for i = 0, …, n, where d_i is the maximal integer such that H⁰(X_C, (∧^iℰ)(−d_i)|_{X_C}) ≠ 0.
items.locator: Chapter II, §II.2.5, proof of Theorem II.2.19, p. 74
items.note: Unnumbered; follows from Theorem II.2.14 and II.2.5(i) (H⁰(𝒪(λ)) ≠ 0 iff λ ≥ 0). 'Convex hull' means the upper boundary (the concave HN polygon). Planned in the node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB4/semicontinuity-of-HN-polygon: hypothesis 'the polygon is described as the convex hull of the points (i,d_i), i = 0..n, where d_i is the maximal integer with H^0(X_C, (wedge^i E)(-d_i)|_{X_C}) nonzero', first proof step, and acceptance test 'Verify the convex-hull description of the polygon on a rank-2 example'.

items.name: Theorem II.2.19(ii): constant HN polygon ⇒ global HN filtration, pro-étale locally split
items.statement: Let S be a perfectoid space over 𝔽_q and ℰ a vector bundle over X_S of constant rank n. Assume that the Harder–Narasimhan polygon of ℰ is constant. Then there exists a global (separated exhaustive decreasing) Harder–Narasimhan filtration ℰ^{≥λ} ⊂ ℰ specializing to the Harder–Narasimhan filtration at each point. Moreover, after replacing S by a pro-étale cover, the Harder–Narasimhan filtration can be split, and there are isomorphisms ℰ^λ ≅ 𝒪_{X_S}(λ)^{n_λ} for some integers n_λ ≥ 0.
items.locator: Chapter II, §II.2.5, Theorem II.2.19(ii), p. 74 (proof continues p. 75)
items.note: Proof: v-locally find a fibrewise nonzero 𝒪(λ) → ℰ for the maximal slope λ using that (BC(ℱ) ∖ {0})/E^× → S is a proper surjective v-cover ([Sch17a, Lemma 12.11]); induct; trivialize pieces pro-étale locally via [Sch17a, Lemma 10.13]; split via II.2.5(ii)–(iii) (printed '(i)–(ii)', see newIssues). VB4: 'prove existence of the relative HN filtration on constant-polygon loci. Show that constant-slope pieces become sums of O(lambda) pro-étale locally under the precise source assumptions.'; node VB4/relative-HN-filtration-and-proetale-splitting.

items.name: Corollary II.2.20: pro-étale E-local systems ≃ slope-0 bundles
items.statement: Let S be a perfectoid space. The category of pro-étale E-local systems 𝕃 is equivalent to the category of vector bundles on X_S whose Harder–Narasimhan polygon is constant 0, via 𝕃 ↦ 𝕃 ⊗_E 𝒪_{X_S}.
items.note: Cited from [KL15, Theorem 8.5.12]. Full faithfulness by pro-étale descent and II.2.5; essential surjectivity from Theorem II.2.19. Stated on p. 75 (end of §II.2), included for completeness of §II.2; the assembler should dedupe with the neighbouring range. VB4: 'Prove the equivalence between everywhere slope-zero bundles and pro-étale E-local systems'.

items.name: Presentation 0→O^m→F→E→0 with F semistable of slope 1/r
items.statement: Let S be a perfectoid space over F_q, and let ℰ be a vector bundle on X_S such that all Harder–Narasimhan slopes of ℰ at all geometric points are ≥ 1/r, for some r ≥ 1. Then locally (in the analytic topology) on S, there is an exact sequence 0 → 𝒪_{X_S}^m → ℱ → ℰ → 0 where ℱ is semistable of slope 1/r at all geometric points (printed 'of degree 1/r', PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E12).
items.note: Small strengthening of [KL15, Lemma 8.8.13]. Proof: with rank n, degree d, m = dr − n; choose m pairwise disjoint untilts S_i^♯ (maps S → BC(O(1))∖{0}), pull back 0→O^m→O(1)^m→⊕O_{S_i^♯}→0 (Prop. II.2.3) along rank-one quotients of the fibres, inductively keeping HN slopes ≥ 1/r, first over a perfectoid field then spreading out by Theorem II.2.19 (openness of HN-polygon loci). Used for II.3.2, II.3.3, II.3.4(ii). No atlas stage names this presentation (VB3:general-BC/VB4 do not mention it). Planned by the node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:general-BC/positive-slope-resolution ('FS II.3.1 and Cor. II.3.3: resolving a positive-slope bundle by semistable bundles of small slope'; statement: 'locally in the analytic topology on S there is an exact sequence 0 -> O_{X_S}^m -> F -> E -> 0 ... Corollary II.3.3 gives the variants used later, in particular (iii) an etale-local exact sequence 0 -> G -> O_{X_S}(1/r)^m -> E -> 0'). The node carries FS's slip 'semistable of degree 1/r' (E12) and must say slope.

items.name: Étale-local presentation 0→G→O(1/r)^m→E→0 with G slope 0
items.statement: Let S be a perfectoid space over F_q and let ℰ be a vector bundle on X_S such that at all geometric points of S, all Harder–Narasimhan slopes of ℰ are > 1/r, for some r ≥ 1. Then étale locally on S, there is a short exact sequence 0 → 𝒢 → 𝒪_{X_S}(1/r)^m → ℰ → 0 where 𝒢 is semistable of slope 0 at all geometric points.
items.note: Proof: the locus U ⊂ BC(ℰ′), ℰ′ = Hom(O(1/r)^m, ℰ), of surjections with semistable slope-0 kernel is open (Theorem II.2.19) with nonempty geometric fibres (Prop. II.3.1); a section over a geometric point T = lim S_i is approximated by sections over étale S_i using a uniform bound M for surjectivity of φ − D : B^r_{R,[1,q]} → B^r_{R,[1,1]} (Prop. II.2.5; bound proved by a product-of-rings argument). The proof's 'm = dr' is a misprint for m = d (PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E13). Planned by the node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:general-BC/positive-slope-resolution ('FS II.3.1 and Cor. II.3.3: resolving a positive-slope bundle by semistable bundles of small slope'; statement: 'locally in the analytic topology on S there is an exact sequence 0 -> O_{X_S}^m -> F -> E -> 0 ... Corollary II.3.3 gives the variants used later, in particular (iii) an etale-local exact sequence 0 -> G -> O_{X_S}(1/r)^m -> E -> 0'). II.3.2 is restated as Corollary II.3.3(iii), which the node names; its statement says 'when all slopes are positive' where FS assume slopes > 1/r.

items.name: Corollary II.3.3(i)
items.statement: Let S be a perfectoid space over F_q and let ℰ be a vector bundle on X_S. Assume that all Harder–Narasimhan slopes of ℰ are ≥ 1/r. Then locally on S, for some m ≥ 0 there is a short exact sequence 0 → 𝒪_{X_S}^m → ℱ → ℰ → 0, where ℱ is fibrewise semistable of slope 1/r.
items.note: Restatement of Proposition II.3.1. Planned by the node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:general-BC/positive-slope-resolution ('FS II.3.1 and Cor.
