II.3.3: resolving a positive-slope bundle by semistable bundles of small slope'; statement: 'locally in the analytic topology on S there is an exact sequence 0 -> O_{X_S}^m -> F -> E -> 0 ... Corollary II.3.3 gives the variants used later, in particular (iii) an etale-local exact sequence 0 -> G -> O_{X_S}(1/r)^m -> E -> 0').

items.name: Corollary II.3.3(ii)
items.statement: Let S be a perfectoid space over F_q and let ℰ be a vector bundle on X_S. Assume that all Harder–Narasimhan slopes of ℰ are ≥ 1/r. Then locally on S, for some m ≥ 0 there is a short exact sequence 0 → 𝒪_{X_S}(1/(2r))^m → ℱ → ℰ′ → 0, where ℱ is fibrewise semistable of slope 1/r, and ℰ is a direct summand of ℰ′.
items.note: Proof (p. 79): apply Prop. II.3.1 to (π_{2r}^*ℰ)(−1) on X_{S,E_{2r}} (E_{2r} unramified of degree 2r), twist and push forward along π_{2r}; ℰ is a summand of π_{2r*}π_{2r}^*ℰ = ℰ ⊗_E E_{2r}. Authors remark passing to ℰ′ is probably unnecessary. Planned by the node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:general-BC/positive-slope-resolution ('FS II.3.1 and Cor. II.3.3: resolving a positive-slope bundle by semistable bundles of small slope'; statement: 'locally in the analytic topology on S there is an exact sequence 0 -> O_{X_S}^m -> F -> E -> 0 ... Corollary II.3.3 gives the variants used later, in particular (iii) an etale-local exact sequence 0 -> G -> O_{X_S}(1/r)^m -> E -> 0'). The node's proof steps include FS's proof of (ii) via π_{2r}.

items.name: Corollary II.3.3(iii)
items.statement: Let S be a perfectoid space over F_q and let ℰ be a vector bundle on X_S. Assume that all Harder–Narasimhan slopes of ℰ are > 1/r. Then étale locally on S, for some m ≥ 0 there is a short exact sequence 0 → 𝒢 → 𝒪_{X_S}(1/r)^m → ℰ → 0, where 𝒢 is fibrewise semistable of slope 0.
items.note: Restatement of Proposition II.3.2. Planned by the node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:general-BC/positive-slope-resolution ('FS II.3.1 and Cor. II.3.3: resolving a positive-slope bundle by semistable bundles of small slope'; statement: 'locally in the analytic topology on S there is an exact sequence 0 -> O_{X_S}^m -> F -> E -> 0 ... Corollary II.3.3 gives the variants used later, in particular (iii) an etale-local exact sequence 0 -> G -> O_{X_S}(1/r)^m -> E -> 0').

items.name: Corollary II.3.3(iv)
items.statement: Let S be a perfectoid space over F_q and let ℰ be a vector bundle on X_S. Assume that all Harder–Narasimhan slopes of ℰ are > 1/r. Then étale locally on S, for some m ≥ 0 there is a short exact sequence 0 → 𝒢 → 𝒪_{X_S}(1/r)^m → ℰ′ → 0, where 𝒢 is fibrewise semistable of slope 1/(2r), and ℰ is a direct summand of ℰ′.
items.note: 'One argues similarly' via π_{2r} and Prop. II.3.2. Used in Prop. II.3.5(i),(iii). Planned by the node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:general-BC/positive-slope-resolution ('FS II.3.1 and Cor. II.3.3: resolving a positive-slope bundle by semistable bundles of small slope'; statement: 'locally in the analytic topology on S there is an exact sequence 0 -> O_{X_S}^m -> F -> E -> 0 ... Corollary II.3.3 gives the variants used later, in particular (iii) an etale-local exact sequence 0 -> G -> O_{X_S}(1/r)^m -> E -> 0').

items.name: H^0 vanishing for negative slopes in families
items.statement: Let S ∈ Perf_{F_q}, and let ℰ be a vector bundle on X_S. If at all geometric points of S, all slopes of ℰ are negative, then H^0(X_S, ℰ) = 0.
items.note: Checked on geometric points via Theorem II.2.14 and Prop. II.2.5(i). VB1 plans H^0/H^1 for bundles but not this family statement explicitly. No Banach–Colmez spaces, relative Fargues–Fontaine curve or HN theory for families in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (declarations.tsv and source grep: no Fargues/BanachColmez/isocrystal-with-G-structure declarations; data/library-coverage.json records B(G), G-isocrystals and the Kottwitz set as absent; Mathlib's WittVector.isocrystal_classification is only the rank-one Dieudonné–Manin case over W(k)). Overlap: PAPER-KEDLAYA-LIU-15 item 228 ("If M over R̃_R has everywhere negative slopes, then H^0_{φ^a}(M) = 0 ..."), accepted in VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB4 (route 19), is the same vanishing in φ-module language. II.3.5 (node VB3:general-BC/families-of-banach-colmez-spaces) consumes II.3.4(i), and VB3:general-BC lies upstream of VB4, so the statement must be owned in VB3:general-BC (or earlier), and VB4 should import it.

items.name: Pro-étale local H^1 vanishing for nonnegative slopes
items.statement: Let S ∈ Perf_{F_q}, and let ℰ be a vector bundle on X_S. If at all geometric points of S, all slopes of ℰ are nonnegative, then there is a pro-étale cover S̃ → S such that H^1(X_{S̃}, ℰ|_{X_{S̃}}) = 0.
items.note: Proof: Prop. II.3.1 applied to ℰ(1) gives 0 → O(−1)^d → ℰ′ → ℰ → 0 with ℰ′ semistable of degree 0; trivialize ℰ′ pro-étale locally (Theorem II.2.19); H^1(X_S,O) = H^1_proét(S,E) (Prop. II.2.5(ii)) vanishes on strictly totally disconnected S (Lemma III.2.6). No Banach–Colmez spaces, relative Fargues–Fontaine curve or HN theory for families in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (declarations.tsv and source grep: no Fargues/BanachColmez/isocrystal-with-G-structure declarations; data/library-coverage.json records B(G), G-isocrystals and the Kottwitz set as absent; Mathlib's WittVector.isocrystal_classification is only the rank-one Dieudonné–Manin case over W(k)).

items.name: Étale local universal H^1 vanishing for positive slopes
items.statement: Let S ∈ Perf_{F_q}, and let ℰ be a vector bundle on X_S. If at all geometric points of S, all slopes of ℰ are positive, then there is an étale cover S′ → S such that for any affinoid perfectoid T over S′, one has H^1(X_T, ℰ|_{X_T}) = 0.
items.note: From Cor. II.3.3(iii) and Prop. II.2.5(iii). No Banach–Colmez spaces, relative Fargues–Fontaine curve or HN theory for families in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (declarations.tsv and source grep: no Fargues/BanachColmez/isocrystal-with-G-structure declarations; data/library-coverage.json records B(G), G-isocrystals and the Kottwitz set as absent; Mathlib's WittVector.isocrystal_classification is only the rank-one Dieudonné–Manin case over W(k)).

items.name: Banach–Colmez space of a two-term complex is a locally spatial diamond
items.statement: Let S be a perfectoid space over F_q. Let [ℰ_1 → ℰ_0] be a map of vector bundles on X_S such that at all geometric points of S, the bundle ℰ_1 has only negative Harder–Narasimhan slopes. Then the Banach–Colmez space 𝓑𝓒([ℰ_1 → ℰ_0]) : T ↦ H^0(X_T, [ℰ_1 → ℰ_0]|_{X_T}) is a locally spatial diamond, partially proper over S.
items.note: Strengthening of Prop. II.2.16. Proof reduces via Theorem II.2.6 to [ℰ₁′ → 𝒪(−d)^m], then via Cor. II.3.3(iv) applied to ℰ₁′^∨ to a closed subfunctor of BC(𝒪(−1/r)^m[1]) (the printed third term should be BC(𝒢^∨[1]), PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E14). Planned by the node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:general-BC/families-of-banach-colmez-spaces ('FS II.3.5: ... (i) BC([E_1 -> E_0]) is a locally spatial diamond, partially proper over S; (ii) ... proper over S; (iii) ... cohomologically smooth').

items.name: Projectivized Banach–Colmez space of a complex is proper
items.statement: In the situation of Proposition II.3.5, the projectivized Banach–Colmez space (𝓑𝓒([ℰ_1 → ℰ_0]) ∖ {0})/E^× is a locally spatial diamond, proper over S.
items.note: VB3:general-BC: 'Construct projectivization with scalar action and prove the properness and v-cover properties used to produce nowhere-zero sections' (stated there for BC(ℰ); the complex case here is an extension). Proof reduces to BC(O(−1)^m[1]) = (A^1_{S♯})^♢/E and Lemma II.2.17.

items.name: Cohomological smoothness of BC([ℰ_1 → ℰ_0]) for positive ℰ_0
items.statement: In the situation of Proposition II.3.5, assume that all Harder–Narasimhan slopes of ℰ_0 at all geometric points are positive. Then 𝓑𝓒([ℰ_1 → ℰ_0]) → S is cohomologically smooth.
items.note: VB3:general-BC: 'For the positive-slope range prove dimension and cohomological smoothness'. Proof uses 0 → BC(ℰ_0) → BC([ℰ_1→ℰ_0]) → BC(ℰ_1[1]) → 0, [Sch17a, Proposition 23.13] (DiamondSixOperations:S4 '23.13'), Cor. II.3.3(iv) and a surjection O(−d)^m → ℰ_1^∨. Key input to the Jacobian criterion / smoothness of Bun_G charts (Ch. IV–V).

items.name: Punctured absolute BC(O(d)) is a qcqs perfectoid space
items.statement: In the situation of Proposition II.2.5 (iv), one has 𝓑𝓒(𝒪(d)) ≅ Spd(k[[x_1^{1/p^∞}, …, x_d^{1/p^∞}]]), which is not a diamond (it contains the non-analytic point Spd k), while 𝓑𝓒(𝒪(d)) ∖ {0} ≅ Spa(k[[x_1^{1/p^∞}, …, x_d^{1/p^∞}]])^{an} = Spa(k[[x_1^{1/p^∞}, …, x_d^{1/p^∞}]]) ∖ V(x_1, …, x_d) is a qcqs perfectoid space, simply connected when d > 1; after base change to Spa(C) it is a punctured open ball, not quasicompact and not simply connected.
items.note: Recalled/observed facts. FS's two thresholds on p. 81 are consistent with [Far20b, Théorème 5.4]: 'Pour d > 1, resp. d > 2 si E|ℚ_p, le diamant B^{φ=π^d}_{𝔽_q} ∖ {0} est simplement connexe' ('simply connected when d > 2' is Fargues' bound for general d in mixed characteristic); in the situation of Proposition II.2.5(iv) the space is a punctured perfectoid ball and the equal-characteristic purity argument gives d > 1. [Far20b, Remarque 6.2] is the non-simple-connectedness after base change to C. No proof of simple connectivity in FS. Not stated by the node VB3:general-BC/absolute-BC-spatiality; missing, route 2 (VB3:general-BC).

items.name: Div = ⊔_d Div^d, Div^d ≅ (BC(O(d))∖{0})/E^×
items.statement: A closed relative Cartier divisor D ⊂ X_S is a line bundle ℐ on X_S with an injection ℐ ↪ 𝒪_{X_S} with closed image that stays injective after base change to any geometric point. The v-sheaf Div of closed relative Cartier divisors satisfies Div = ⊔_{d≥0} Div^d, Div^d ≅ (𝓑𝓒(𝒪(d)) ∖ {0})/E^×; this agrees with the earlier definition of Div^1 by Corollary II.2.4. Sums of Cartier divisors are defined by tensoring ideal sheaves.
items.note: Via Theorem II.2.19: after an open-closed cover ℐ has degree −d and Isom(ℐ, O(−d)) is an E^×-torsor. RF2:untilts: 'For d ≥ 0, construct effective Cartier divisors of degree d, addition, disjoint-divisor loci and the finite symmetric-power comparison in the source's range'.

items.name: Div^d = (Div^1)^d/Σ_d
items.statement: For any d ≥ 1, the sum map (Div^1)^d → Div^d : (D_1, …, D_d) ↦ D_1 + … + D_d is a quasi-pro-étale cover, identifying Div^d = (Div^1)^d/Σ_d, where Σ_d is the symmetric group. In particular, Div^d is a diamond.
items.note: Proof: all spaces are proper over ∗ (printed 'By Proposition II.2.16 (ii)'; II.2.16 has no part (ii) — its second statement, or Proposition II.3.5(ii), is meant, see newIssues), surjectivity on geometric points (Prop. II.2.9: every element of P_d is a product of elements of P_1), [Sch17a, Lemma 7.19, Def. 10.1(i), Props. 11.4, 11.6]; Div^1 = Spd E/φ^ℤ. RF2:untilts: 'the finite symmetric-power comparison in the source's range, retaining multiplicities'; also stated by the node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:general-BC/absolute-BC-spatiality. Used for Hecke operators with several legs (GS/HS roadmaps).

items.name: Decent bases of isocrystals
items.statement: Let D be an isocrystal over Ĕ (k algebraically closed). There is a basis of D in which φ is E-rational (φ = A·σ with A ∈ GL_n(E)) and U := φ^N is a diagonal matrix with entries powers of π for some N > 0 (D is decent in the sense of [RZ96, Definition 1.8]). In particular BC(D) and BC(D[1]) are defined on Perf_{𝔽_q}, U commutes with φ, and U acts on them as Frob^N.
items.locator: Chapter II, §II.3.3, proof of Proposition II.3.7(i), p. 82
items.note: Consequence of the Dieudonné–Manin classification: the standard block of slope d/h has φ^h = π^{−d}σ^h in its E-rational basis. VB0 plans the classification and the node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0/isocrystal-category-and-standard-block the standard block ('phi(e_h) = pi^{-d} e_1, so phi^h = pi^{-d} sigma^h'); the node VB3:general-BC/absolute-BC-spatiality lists decency as a hypothesis ('D is DECENT in the sense of Rapoport-Zink Definition 1.8'). The VB0 packet records that Dieudonné–Manin itself was not read in a source that proves it (gap 'Dieudonne-Manin is quoted, never proved, in anything read'). Added in review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21).

items.name: Punctured absolute Banach–Colmez spaces are spatial diamonds
items.statement: Let D be an isocrystal with only negative slopes (resp. with only positive slopes), and work on Perf_k. The punctured Banach–Colmez space 𝓑𝓒(D) ∖ {0} (resp. 𝓑𝓒(D[1]) ∖ {0}) is a spatial diamond. (Here 𝓑𝓒(D) = 𝓑𝓒(ℰ(D)).)
items.note: Proof: spatial v-sheaf via Lemma II.3.8(i) using a decent basis (U = φ^N diagonal, [RZ96, Def. 1.8]) and Lemma II.2.17 on BC(D)∖{0} ×_{F_q} Spa F_q((t^{1/p^∞}))/φ^N; diamond via Prop. II.3.6 (positive case) and, in the negative case D = (E, π^n φ), via the HN stratification of extensions 0→O(−n)→ℰ→O→0 and Lemma II.3.8(ii). Planned by the node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:general-BC/absolute-BC-spatiality ('FS II.3.6-II.3.7 ... For an isocrystal D with only negative slopes (resp. only positive slopes), working on Perf_k: (i) BC(D) minus {0} (resp. BC(D[1]) minus {0}) is a spatial diamond; (ii) the quotient by E^times is proper, representable in spatial diamonds and cohomologically smooth').

items.name: Projectivized absolute BC spaces are proper and cohomologically smooth over ∗
items.statement: Let D be an isocrystal with only negative slopes (resp. with only positive slopes), and work on Perf_k. The quotient (𝓑𝓒(D) ∖ {0})/E^× → ∗ (resp. (𝓑𝓒(D[1]) ∖ {0})/E^× → ∗) is proper, representable in spatial diamonds, and cohomologically smooth.
items.note: From Prop. II.3.5 and [Sch17a, Proposition 24.2] (DiamondSixOperations:S5 '24.2' for the quotient by E^×). Planned by the node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:general-BC/absolute-BC-spatiality ('FS II.3.6-II.3.7 ... For an isocrystal D with only negative slopes (resp. only positive slopes), working on Perf_k: (i) BC(D) minus {0} (resp. BC(D[1]) minus {0}) is a spatial diamond; (ii) the quotient by E^times is proper, representable in spatial diamonds and cohomologically smooth').

items.name: Spatiality criterion via smooth cover
items.statement: Let ℱ be a small v-sheaf. Suppose there exists a surjective qcqs cohomologically smooth morphism D → ℱ where D is a spatial diamond. Then ℱ is a spatial v-sheaf.
items.note: Proof: cohomologically smooth ⇒ universally open; apply [Sch17a, Lemma 2.10]. The ingredients are in DiamondsAndVStacks:D5 / DiamondSixOperations:S4 but the lemma itself is not named in a stage.

items.name: Spatial diamond criterion via generalizing strata
items.statement: Let ℱ be a small v-sheaf as in Lemma II.3.8 (i) (so ℱ is a spatial v-sheaf). Suppose moreover there is a family of locally closed generalizing subsets (X_α)_α, X_α ⊂ |ℱ|, covering |ℱ| (|ℱ| = ⋃_α X_α), such that for each α the associated subsheaf of ℱ is a diamond. Then ℱ is a spatial diamond.
items.note: Proof: [Sch17a, Theorem 12.18] ('Let Y be a spatial v-sheaf such that there exists a perfectoid space X with a quasi-pro-étale map f : X -> Y for which |f| is surjective. Then Y is a spatial diamond', as quoted in the DiamondsAndVStacks packet) and [Sch17a, Lemma 7.6] (the subsheaves are quasi-pro-étale). The surjectivity of |f| requires the X_α to cover |ℱ|, which the printed statement omits (see newIssues); the application (Harder–Narasimhan strata of BC(D[1]) ∖ {0}) covers. Named in a proof step of VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:general-BC/absolute-BC-spatiality ('then apply Lemma II.3.8') but not stated; missing, route 2 (VB3:general-BC).

items.name: (BC(O(d))∖{0})/π^ℤ is not quasiseparated
items.statement: Although the absolute 𝓑𝓒(𝒪(d)) ∖ {0} is a spatial diamond, (𝓑𝓒(𝒪(d)) ∖ {0})/π^ℤ is not spatial since not quasiseparated [Far20b, Remarque 2.15]; the morphism (𝓑𝓒(𝒪(d)) ∖ {0})/π^ℤ → ∗ is representable in spatial diamonds.
items.note: Cited from [Far20b]; cautionary remark. No Banach–Colmez spaces, relative Fargues–Fontaine curve or HN theory for families in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (declarations.tsv and source grep: no Fargues/BanachColmez/isocrystal-with-G-structure declarations; data/library-coverage.json records B(G), G-isocrystals and the Kottwitz set as absent; Mathlib's WittVector.isocrystal_classification is only the rank-one Dieudonné–Manin case over W(k)).

items.name: Equal characteristic: punctured positive absolute BC spaces are perfectoid
items.statement: In the equal characteristic case E = F_q((π)), punctured positive absolute Banach–Colmez spaces are perfectoid spaces, while punctured negative ones are only spatial diamonds; 𝓑𝓒(𝒪(−1)[1]) is stratified into an open part, a quotient of Spd k((t)) by a profinite group, and a point Spd k, the degeneration happening as |t| → 1.
items.note: Descriptive remark without proof; footnote 6 explains why non-analytic test objects are not admitted. No Banach–Colmez spaces, relative Fargues–Fontaine curve or HN theory for families in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (declarations.tsv and source grep: no Fargues/BanachColmez/isocrystal-with-G-structure declarations; data/library-coverage.json records B(G), G-isocrystals and the Kottwitz set as absent; Mathlib's WittVector.isocrystal_classification is only the rank-one Dieudonné–Manin case over W(k)).

items.name: BC(O(−1)[1])∖{0} via the quaternion algebra and Drinfeld's upper half plane
items.statement: The absolute 𝓑𝓒(𝒪(−1)[1]) ∖ {0} classifies extensions 0 → 𝒪_{X_S}(−1) → ℰ → 𝒪_{X_S} → 0 that are non-split fiberwise on S; each such ℰ is geometrically isomorphic to 𝒪_{X_S}(−1/2), and 𝓑𝓒(𝒪(−1)[1]) ∖ {0} ≃ (𝓑𝓒(𝒪(1/2)) ∖ {0})/SL_1(D) with 𝓑𝓒(𝒪(1/2)) ∖ {0} ≃ Spa(k((x^{1/p^∞}))), D the quaternion algebra over E. After base change to Spa(C) with an untilt C^♯: 𝓑𝓒(𝒪(−1)[1]) ×_k Spa(C) ≅ (𝔸^1_{C^♯})^♢/E and 𝓑𝓒(𝒪(−1)[1]) ∖ {0} ×_k Spa(C) ≅ (Ω_{C^♯})^♢/E, Ω = 𝔸^1_E ∖ E Drinfeld's upper half plane; hence ((𝓑𝓒(𝒪(1/2)) ∖ {0}) ×_k Spa(C))/SL_1(D) ≅ (Ω_{C^♯})^♢/E, compatible with LT_∞^♭/(1 E; 0 E^×) ≅ (𝓑𝓒(𝒪(1/2)) ∖ {0}) ×_k Spa(C).
items.note: Uses Theorem II.2.19 and the Lubin–Tate/Drinfeld tower isomorphism at infinite level [SW13]. VB3:positive-basic-examples plans the Lubin–Tate universal cover calculation of BC(O(1/2))-type spaces but not this example. No Banach–Colmez spaces, relative Fargues–Fontaine curve or HN theory for families in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (declarations.tsv and source grep: no Fargues/BanachColmez/isocrystal-with-G-structure declarations; data/library-coverage.json records B(G), G-isocrystals and the Kottwitz set as absent; Mathlib's WittVector.isocrystal_classification is only the rank-one Dieudonné–Manin case over W(k)).

items.name: BC(O(−2)[1])∖{0} = U/SL_2(E)
items.statement: The absolute 𝓑𝓒(𝒪(−2)[1]) ∖ {0} classifies extensions 0 → 𝒪_{X_S}(−1) → ℰ → 𝒪_{X_S}(1) → 0 non-split fiberwise on S; geometrically fiberwise ℰ is trivial. The moduli of surjections 𝒪_{X_S}^2 ↠ 𝒪_{X_S}(1) is the open U = (𝓑𝓒(𝒪(1)) ∖ {0})^2 ∖ (E^× × 1).Δ ⊂ (𝓑𝓒(𝒪(1)) ∖ {0}) ×_k (𝓑𝓒(𝒪(1)) ∖ {0}) (pairs of fibrewise nonzero, E-linearly independent sections of H^0(X_S, 𝒪(1))), and 𝓑𝓒(𝒪(−2)[1]) ∖ {0} = U/SL_2(E).
items.note: Kernel of O^2 ↠ O(1) is canonically O(−1) by determinants, whence SL_2 rather than GL_2. No Banach–Colmez spaces, relative Fargues–Fontaine curve or HN theory for families in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (declarations.tsv and source grep: no Fargues/BanachColmez/isocrystal-with-G-structure declarations; data/library-coverage.json records B(G), G-isocrystals and the Kottwitz set as absent; Mathlib's WittVector.isocrystal_classification is only the rank-one Dieudonné–Manin case over W(k)).

items.name: Bun_G
items.statement: Fix a reductive group G over the nonarchimedean local field E and an algebraic closure k of F_q; Perf_k is the category of perfectoid spaces over Spd k. Bun_G is the prestack (v-stack by Prop. II.2.1) taking a perfectoid space S ∈ Perf_k to the groupoid of G-bundles on X_S.
items.locator: Chapter III, Definition III.0.1, p. 87; Definition III.1.2, p. 88
items.note: BG2:uniformization: 'Define the groupoid-valued functor S ↦ G-bundles on X_S. Prove v-descent'. By GAGA one may replace X_S by X_S^alg for S affinoid.

items.name: Bun_G is a small v-stack
items.statement: The prestack Bun_G is a small v-stack.
items.locator: Chapter III, Theorem III.0.2 (i), p. 87 (= Proposition III.1.3)
items.note: Summary; see c3-prop-III.1.3. BG2:uniformization: 'Prove v-descent, smallness with cutoffs'.

items.name: |Bun_G| ≅ B(G)
items.statement: The points |Bun_G| are naturally in bijection with Kottwitz' set B(G) of isomorphism classes of G-isocrystals.
items.locator: Chapter III, Theorem III.0.2 (ii), p. 87 (= Theorem III.2.2)
items.note: BG2:uniformization: 'Prove the bijection |Bun_G| → B(G), geometric-base independence'.

items.name: ν semicontinuous, κ locally constant
items.statement: The map ν : |Bun_G| → B(G) → (X_*(T)^+_ℚ)^Γ is semicontinuous, and κ : |Bun_G| → B(G) → π_1(G_{Ē})_Γ is locally constant. Equivalently, the map |Bun_G| → B(G) is continuous when B(G) is equipped with the order topology.
items.locator: Chapter III, Theorem III.0.2 (iii), p. 87 (= Theorems III.2.3, III.2.7)
items.note: BG2:uniformization: 'Prove kappa locally constant using the source z-extension route and its v-surjectivity lemma; prove nu semicontinuous'; BG1: 'this roadmap requires continuity of the map from Bun_G points with the stated order topology'.

items.name: Semistable locus open, disjoint union of [∗/G_b(E)]
items.statement: The semistable locus Bun_G^{ss} ⊂ Bun_G is open, and given by Bun_G^{ss} ≅ ⊔_{b ∈ B(G)_basic} [∗/G_b(E)].
items.locator: Chapter III, Theorem III.0.2 (iv), p. 87 (= Theorem III.4.5)
items.note: BG3: 'For basic b prove the classifying-stack description by J_b(E), and prove that the union of basic strata is open.'

items.name: HN strata Bun_G^b = [∗/G̃_b]
items.statement: For any b ∈ B(G), the corresponding subfunctor i^b : Bun_G^b = Bun_G ×_{|Bun_G|} {b} ⊂ Bun_G is locally closed, and isomorphic to [∗/G̃_b], where G̃_b is a v-sheaf of groups such that G̃_b → ∗ is representable in locally spatial diamonds with π_0 G̃_b = G_b(E). The connected component G̃_b^◦ ⊂ G̃_b of the identity is cohomologically smooth of dimension ⟨2ρ, ν_b⟩.
items.locator: Chapter III, Theorem III.0.2 (v), p. 87 (= Proposition III.5.3, Proposition III.5.1)
items.note: BG3: 'Construct Bun_G^b as the locally closed substack for each b ... construct the full automorphism v-group Gtilde_b, its map to J_b(E), connected kernel and quotient description Bun_G^b = [*/Gtilde_b] ... prove its ell-cohomological smoothness and dimension pairing <2rho,nu_b>'. Local closedness follows from III.2.3 + III.2.7.

items.name: Three descriptions of G-torsors on sousperfectoid spaces
items.statement: Let X be a sousperfectoid space over E. The following categories are naturally equivalent: (i) adic spaces T → X with a G-action such that étale locally on X, there is a G-equivariant isomorphism T ≅ G × X; (ii) étale sheaves Q on X equipped with an action of G such that étale locally, Q ≅ G; (iii) exact ⊗-functors Rep_E G → Bun(X) to the category of vector bundles on X. A G-bundle on X is an exact ⊗-functor Rep_E G → Bun(X). In particular G-torsors up to isomorphism are classified by H^1_ét(X, G).
items.note: From [SW20, Proposition 19.5.1] (stated for ℤ_p, extends verbatim to O_E). BG0: 'prove the comparison between geometric étale torsors, étale sheaf torsors, and exact tensor functors Rep_E(G) → vector bundles'. Mathlib/Tau Ceti have no adic-space G-torsors.

items.name: Bun_G is small
items.statement: The v-stack Bun_G is small, i.e. there are perfectoid spaces S, R with a v-surjection S → Bun_G and a v-surjection R → S ×_{Bun_G} S.
items.note: Proof: for an ω_1-cofiltered system of affinoid perfectoids S_i with limit S, Bun_G(S) = lim→ Bun_G(S_i) (since R = lim→ R_i, likewise B_{R,I}, hence Bun(X_S) = lim→ Bun(X_{S_i})); then sections factor through topologically countably generated R′, a set's worth. BG2:uniformization: 'smallness with cutoffs'.

items.name: G-isocrystals and B(G)
items.statement: A G-isocrystal is an exact ⊗-functor Rep_E G → Isoc_E. The set of isomorphism classes of G-isocrystals is denoted B(G). By Steinberg's theorem, B(G) identifies with the quotient of G(Ĕ) under σ-conjugation. Composing with Isoc_E → Bun(X_S) : D ↦ ℰ(D), any b ∈ B(G) gives a G-bundle ℰ_b on X_S for any S ∈ Perf_k.
items.note: Kottwitz [Kot85]. BG0: 'Define B(G) as sigma-conjugacy classes in G(E-breve), with relation b' = g b sigma(g)^(-1), and compare with isomorphism classes of G-isocrystals.' Not in Mathlib/Tau Ceti (library-coverage.json: 'no σ-conjugacy set B(G)').

items.name: Classification of G-bundles on X_C
items.statement: For any complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean field C over k, the construction b ↦ ℰ_b defines a bijection B(G) → Bun_G(C)/≅. In particular (using [Sch17a, Proposition 12.7]) the map B(G) → |Bun_G| is a bijection.
items.locator: Chapter III, §III.2.1, Theorem III.2.2, p. 89 (and p. 90)
items.note: [Far20a], [Ans19]. Sketch of Anschütz's proof: HN filtration gives an exact ⊗-functor to ℚ-filtered bundles (exactness automatic for p-adic E by semisimplicity of Rep_E G; equal characteristic needs [Ans19, Thm 3.11]); the associated graded lands in semistable-graded bundles ≃ Isoc_E (Thm II.2.14, Prop II.2.5(ii)); splittings form a torsor under a unipotent group filtered by positive-slope bundles, H^1 = 0. BG2:uniformization: 'Prove the bijection |Bun_G| → B(G), geometric-base independence'.

items.name: Newton point ν : B(G) → (X_*(T)^+_ℚ)^Γ
items.statement: Let Ē be a separable closure of E, T ⊂ B ⊂ G_Ē a maximal torus in a Borel; X_*(T)^+ (independent of choices, = Hom(𝔾_{m,Ē}, G_Ē)/G(Ē)-conjugacy) carries an action of Γ = Gal(Ē|E). The Newton point is a map ν : B(G) → (X_*(T)^+_ℚ)^Γ, b ↦ ν_b; for G = GL_n it records the (nonincreasing) slopes of the Newton polygon of the isocrystal.
items.note: Kottwitz [Kot97]. BG1: 'Construct ... rational dominant Newton cocharacter nu'.

items.name: Kottwitz point κ : B(G) → π_1(G)_Γ
items.statement: The Kottwitz point is a map κ : B(G) → π_1(G)_Γ, b ↦ κ(b), where π_1(G) := π_1(G_Ē) = X_*(T)/(coroot lattice) is the Borovoi fundamental group. For GL_n, π_1(G)_Γ ≅ ℤ and κ(b) is the endpoint of the Newton polygon. The images of κ(b) and ν_b in π_1(G)^Γ_ℚ agree. κ is defined first for tori (where it is a bijection), then for G with simply connected derived group via G/G_der, and in general via a z-extension G̃ → G with B(G̃) → B(G) surjective.
items.note: Kottwitz [Kot97]. BG1: 'Construct pi_1(G), its Galois coinvariants, the Kottwitz map kappa ... behavior under ... central quotients and z-extensions'.

items.name: (ν, κ) is injective on B(G)
items.statement: The map (ν, κ) : B(G) → (X_*(T)^+_ℚ)^Γ × π_1(G)_Γ is injective.
items.note: Recalled from Kottwitz [Kot97] (printed with X^*(T), a misprint for X_*(T): (PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E16)). BG1: 'Prove the classification/uniqueness assertions for B(G) used in FS III'.

items.name: HN polygon and first Chern class of ℰ_b
items.statement: Let v ↦ v^* = w_0(−v) be the involution of the positive Weyl chamber X_*(T)^+_ℚ, w_0 the longest Weyl element. The Harder–Narasimhan polygon of ℰ_b is ν_b^*, and its first Chern class is −κ(b) (a theorem for GL_n; the definition for general G).
items.note: Sign reversal from D ↦ ℰ(D) reversing slopes. BG1/BG2: 'the kappa/nu formulas'.

items.name: Newton map is upper semicontinuous
items.statement: The map ν^* : |Bun_G| ≅ B(G) → (X_*(T)^+_ℚ)^Γ is upper semicontinuous.
items.note: [SW20, Corollary 22.5.1]; follows from Theorem II.2.19 and [RR96, Lemma 2.2]. BG2:uniformization: 'prove nu semicontinuous by faithful-representation HN theory'.

items.name: Bun_G^1 ⊂ Bun_G is open and equals [∗/G(E)]
items.statement: Let [∗/G(E)] be the classifying stack of pro-étale G(E)-torsors and Bun_G^1 ⊂ Bun_G the substack of geometrically fiberwise trivial G-bundles (G(E) = automorphisms of the trivial G-bundle, as H^0(X_S, 𝒪_{X_S}) = E(S)). The substack Bun_G^1 ⊂ Bun_G is open, and the map [∗/G(E)] → Bun_G^1 is an isomorphism.
items.note: Proof on strictly totally disconnected S: the locus where the Newton point vanishes is open (III.2.3); via Corollary II.2.20 one gets a fibre functor to C^0(π_0(S), E)-modules, i.e. a G-torsor over Spec C^0(π_0(S), E), whose local rings are henselian; so ∗ → Bun_G^1 is a pro-étale cover with ∗ ×_{Bun_G^1} ∗ = G(E). [SW20, Lemma 12.5] cannot be used as qcqs-ness is unclear. Owner: BunGAndNewtonStrata packet node BG2:uniformization/geometrically-trivial-locus, which states this theorem together with Lemma III.2.6. It is an input of Proposition III.3.1 in the same stage; BG3 ('for basic b prove the classifying-stack description by J_b(E)', b = 1) consumes it.

items.name: Pro-étale G(E)-torsors over perfectoids are perfectoid
items.statement: If S is a perfectoid space, and T → S is a pro-étale G(E)-torsor then T is representable by a perfectoid space: T = lim← K∖T over compact open subgroups K ⊂ G(E), each K∖T a separated étale perfectoid space over S (by [Sch17a, Proposition 9.7]), with finite étale transition maps.
items.note: [Sch17a, Lemma 10.13], quoted in the remark. Planned by DiamondsAndVStacks:D3 ('Construct locally profinite group torsors and their representability/pro-étale presentation over perfectoid bases; include finite quotient towers and universal openness') and by its packet node D3/locally-profinite-torsors, which states Lemma 10.13 for v-locally trivial G-torsors (a class containing the pro-étale ones): X̃ is a perfectoid space, each X̃_K is separated étale over X, the transition maps are finite étale and X̃ = lim X̃_K.

items.name: Pro-étale torsors under first-countable locally profinite groups are trivial on strictly totally disconnected spaces
items.statement: Let S be a strictly totally disconnected perfectoid space, and let H be a first-countable locally profinite group. Then any pro-étale H-torsor on S is trivial.
items.note: Proof: reduce to a K-torsor for a compact open K (K∖T → S is an étale cover, so it has a section), then split the tower of finite étale covers K_{n+1}∖T → K_n∖T inductively. Used in II.3.4(ii), III.2.4, III.3.1, III.4.7. Planned in the BunGAndNewtonStrata packet node BG2:uniformization/geometrically-trivial-locus (statement and last proof step). Review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21): a node of the draft BunGAndNewtonStrata packet states this (layer BunGAndNewtonStrata:BG2:uniformization), but that packet has not been reviewed or promoted, and the stage description alone does not name the statement. Packets count as planning only once promoted (PROTOCOL §6), so the item stays missing and is routed as a source to that layer.

items.name: Kottwitz map is locally constant on |Bun_G|
items.statement: The map κ : |Bun_G| ≅ B(G) → π_1(G)_Γ is locally constant.
items.note: Two proofs: (1) z-extension G̃ → G + Lemma III.2.10 reduces to induced tori where π_1(G)_Γ is torsion-free and κ is determined by ν (III.2.3); (2) for p-adic E, via B_ab(G) and Prop. III.2.13. A third via III.3.6 + III.3.1. BG2:uniformization: 'Prove kappa locally constant using the source z-extension route and its v-surjectivity lemma ... This explicitly includes the non-simply-connected derived-group case.'

items.name: Local constancy of κ for G-isocrystals over F_q-schemes
items.statement: Let S be an F_q-scheme and ℰ a G-isocrystal on S. The map |S| → π_1(G)_Γ that sends a geometric point s̄ → S to κ(ℰ_{s̄}) is locally constant.
items.note: [RR96, Corollary 3.11], new proof without the finite-type hypothesis. Proof: Spd(R,R) → Bun_G for S = Spec R over k; open-closed subsets of Spd(R,R) ↔ those of Spec R ([SW20, Prop. 18.3.1]); Remark III.2.9 warns that the natural maps |Spd(R,R)| → |Spec R| do not commute with κ, but |Spec R| → |Spd(R,R)| does. Planned in the BunGAndNewtonStrata packet node BG2:uniformization/semicontinuity-and-local-constancy (statement and last proof step). Review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21): a node of the draft BunGAndNewtonStrata packet states this (layer BunGAndNewtonStrata:BG2:uniformization), but that packet has not been reviewed or promoted, and the stage description alone does not name the statement. Packets count as planning only once promoted (PROTOCOL §6), so the item stays missing and is routed as a source to that layer.

items.name: Bun_{G̃} → Bun_G is surjective for central torus extensions
items.statement: Let G̃ → G be a central extension with kernel a torus. Then Bun_{G̃} → Bun_G is a surjective map of v-stacks.
items.locator: Chapter III, §III.2.4.1, Lemma III.2.10, p. 93 (proved p. 99 via Prop. III.3.1 and Lemma III.3.5)
items.note: Bun_Z (Z the kernel) is a Picard stack acting on Bun_{G̃} with Bun_G the quotient (quasi-torsor; the lemma gives surjectivity). BG2:uniformization: 'Prove kappa locally constant using the source z-extension route and its v-surjectivity lemma'.

items.name: Abelianized Kottwitz set B_ab(G)
items.statement: Assume E is p-adic (standing assumption of the second proof, §III.2.4.2), and let Ĕ̄ be an algebraic closure of Ĕ. B_ab(G) = H^1(W_E, [G_sc(Ĕ̄) → G(Ĕ̄)]) (cohomology with coefficients in a crossed module), with abelianization map B(G) → B_ab(G) induced by [1 → G] → [G_sc → G]. For T a maximal torus with preimage T_sc in G_sc, [T_sc → T] → [G_sc → G] is a homotopy equivalence, and likewise [Z_sc → Z] → [G_sc → G] for the centres.
items.note: [Bor98], [Lab99, Appendix B]. Planned in the BunGAndNewtonStrata packet node BG1/abelianization-identification ('FS III.2.11-III.2.13: B^ab(G) = pi_1(G)_Gamma and the cohomological description of kappa'), whose first proof step computes B^ab(G) through [T_sc → T]. No crossed-module Galois cohomology in the pinned libraries. Review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21): a node of the draft BunGAndNewtonStrata packet states this (layer BunGAndNewtonStrata:BG1), but that packet has not been reviewed or promoted, and the stage description alone does not name the statement. Packets count as planning only once promoted (PROTOCOL §6), so the item stays missing and is routed as a source to that layer.

items.name: B_ab(G) = π_1(G)_Γ compatibly with κ
items.statement: There is an identification B_ab(G) = π_1(G)_Γ through which the Kottwitz map κ is identified with the abelianization map B(G) → B_ab(G).
items.note: Proof: B_ab(G) = H^1(W_E,[T_sc(Ĕ̄)→T(Ĕ̄)]) = coker(B(T_sc) → B(T)) using H^2(W_E, T_sc(Ĕ̄)) = 0 ([Ser94]) and B(T) = X_*(T)_Γ. Planned in the BunGAndNewtonStrata packet node BG1/abelianization-identification, whose statement opens with this identification. Review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21): a node of the draft BunGAndNewtonStrata packet states this (layer BunGAndNewtonStrata:BG1), but that packet has not been reviewed or promoted, and the stage description alone does not name the statement. Packets count as planning only once promoted (PROTOCOL §6), so the item stays missing and is routed as a source to that layer.

items.name: Morphism of sites τ : (X_S)_ét → S_ét
items.statement: For S ∈ Perf_k there is a morphism of sites τ : (X_S)_ét → S_ét deduced from (X_S)_ét = (X_S^♢)_ét = (Div^1_S)_ét and the projection Div^1_S = Div^1 × S → S; equivalently τ^* takes étale T → S to X_T → X_S.
items.note: Planned in the BunGAndNewtonStrata packet node BG1/abelianization-identification, which records it as a hypothesis: 'pi : (X_S)_et -> S_et is the morphism of sites deduced from (X_S)_et = (X_S^diamond)_et = (Div^1_S)_et and the projection Div^1_S -> S'. FarguesFontaineDiamonds:F3 plans (X_F)_ét ≃ (X_F^♢)_ét only for a fixed field. Review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21): a node of the draft BunGAndNewtonStrata packet states this (layer BunGAndNewtonStrata:BG1), but that packet has not been reviewed or promoted, and the stage description alone does not name the statement. Packets count as planning only once promoted (PROTOCOL §6), so the item stays missing and is routed as a source to that layer.

items.name: Rτ_* of constant torsion sheaves
items.statement: Assume E is p-adic (standing assumption of the second proof, §III.2.4.2). Let S ∈ Perf_k and let F be a locally constant sheaf of finite abelian groups on Spa(E)_ét. One has Rτ_* F|_{X_S} = RΓ_ét(Spa(E), F) as a constant complex on S_ét.
items.note: Proof: proper base change [Sch17a, Cor. 16.10(ii)] reduces to X_{C,C+}; Galois descent and the comparison with the equal-characteristic curve (tilting \widehat{\overline E}); Kummer theory for n ≠ p (punctured disc 𝔻*) and Artin–Schreier for n = p. Generalizes [Far20a, Thm 3.7]. Planned in the BunGAndNewtonStrata packet node BG1/abelianization-identification (second sentence of its statement). Review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21): a node of the draft BunGAndNewtonStrata packet states this (layer BunGAndNewtonStrata:BG1), but that packet has not been reviewed or promoted, and the stage description alone does not name the statement. Packets count as planning only once promoted (PROTOCOL §6), so the item stays missing and is routed as a source to that layer.

items.name: H^1 of diagonalizable groups on the curve is constant
items.statement: Assume E is p-adic (standing assumption of §III.2.4.2). Let S ∈ Perf_k and let D be a diagonalizable algebraic group over E. The pro-étale sheaf associated to T/S ↦ H^1_ét(X_T, D) is the constant sheaf with value H^1(W_E, D(Ĕ̄)), where Ĕ̄ is an algebraic closure of Ĕ.
items.note: The proof uses that D^0 is a torus 'as E is of characteristic 0'. Torus case: the coarse moduli of Bun_D, from Theorem III.2.4 by translation; general case via 1 → D^0 → D → π_0(D) → 1 and (i). The comparison map comes from the morphism of sites (X_S)_ét → {discrete W_E-sets} (p. 96). Planned in the BunGAndNewtonStrata packet node BG1/abelianization-identification (third clause of its statement). Review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21): a node of the draft BunGAndNewtonStrata packet states this (layer BunGAndNewtonStrata:BG1), but that packet has not been reviewed or promoted, and the stage description alone does not name the statement. Packets count as planning only once promoted (PROTOCOL §6), so the item stays missing and is routed as a source to that layer.

items.name: Comparison morphism from W_E-cohomology to étale cohomology of X_S
items.statement: Assume E is p-adic (standing assumption of the second proof, §III.2.4.2), let S ∈ Perf_k and let Ĕ̄ be an algebraic closure of Ĕ. There is a natural continuous morphism of sites (X_S)_ét → {discrete W_E-sets}. It induces the natural maps H^1(W_E, D(Ĕ̄)) → H^1_ét(X_S, D) for D diagonalizable over E, used in Proposition III.2.12 (ii), and the natural morphism of groups B_ab(G) = H^1(W_E, [G_sc(Ĕ̄) → G(Ĕ̄)]) → H^1_ét(X_S, [G_sc → G]) used in Proposition III.2.13; for S = Spa C the same maps appear in Remark III.2.14.
items.locator: Chapter III, §III.2.4.2, p. 96, paragraph between Proposition III.2.12 and Proposition III.2.13 (announced in the proof of Proposition III.2.12 (ii), p. 95: 'see just after the proof of this proposition')
items.note: The paper only names the morphism of sites and does not construct it. The BunGAndNewtonStrata packet node BG1/abelianization-identification states the constancy results III.2.12–III.2.13 whose comparison maps come from it, but does not name the morphism. Nothing in the pinned libraries. Added in review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21).

items.name: H^1_ét(X_T, [G_sc → G]) is locally constant with value B_ab(G)
items.statement: For S ∈ Perf_k (E p-adic), the pro-étale sheaf on S associated with T/S ↦ H^1_ét(X_T, [G_sc → G]) is the constant sheaf with value B_ab(G).
items.note: Via [Z_sc → Z] ≃ [G_sc → G], Proposition III.2.12 and diagram chasing; the natural map B_ab(G) → H^1_ét(X_S,[G_sc→G]) comes from (X_S)_ét → {discrete W_E-sets}. Gives the second proof of Theorem III.2.7 through the abelianization H^1_ét(X_S,G) → H^1_ét(X_S,[G_sc→G]). Planned in the BunGAndNewtonStrata packet node BG1/abelianization-identification (last clause of its statement, third and fourth proof steps). Review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21): a node of the draft BunGAndNewtonStrata packet states this (layer BunGAndNewtonStrata:BG1), but that packet has not been reviewed or promoted, and the stage description alone does not name the statement. Packets count as planning only once promoted (PROTOCOL §6), so the item stays missing and is routed as a source to that layer.

items.name: H^i(W_E, D(Ĕ̄)) ≅ H^i_ét(X_C, D) for diagonalizable D
items.statement: Let X_C^alg be the schematical curve for C|F_q algebraically closed, and Ĕ̄ an algebraic closure of Ĕ. If D is a diagonalizable group over E then H^i(W_E, D(Ĕ̄)) → H^i_ét(X_C, D) is an isomorphism for 0 ≤ i ≤ 2; Theorem III.2.2 can be restated as H^1(W_E, G(Ĕ̄)) ≅ H^1_ét(X_C, G) for reductive G.
items.note: Repackages [Far20a, Theorems 3.7, 2.7]; no proof given.

items.name: Conjecture: |Bun_G| → B(G) is a homeomorphism
items.statement: Theorems III.2.3 and III.2.7 imply |Bun_G| → B(G) is continuous for the topology induced by the order on (X_*(T)^+_ℚ)^Γ and the discrete topology on π_1(G)_Γ. Conjecture III.2.15: the map |Bun_G| → B(G) is a homeomorphism; i.e. whenever b > b′ in B(G) there is a specialization from b to b′ in |Bun_G|.
items.note: Conjecture in the paper (known for GL_n by Hansen [Han17] using [BFH+22]; proved in general by Viehmann [Vie21]). BG1 explicitly excludes it: 'not an unstated stronger closure equality or topological homeomorphism'. Weak form (connected components) in Corollary IV.1.23.

items.name: B_dR^+-affine Grassmannian Gr_G over Spd E
items.statement: Gr_G is the functor over Spd E sending an affinoid perfectoid S = Spa(R, R^+) over Spd E to G-torsors over Spec(B_dR^+(R^♯)) with a trivialization over B_dR(R^♯), R^♯ the untilt given by S → Spd E; equivalently the étale sheafification of (R, R^+) ↦ G(B_dR(R^♯))/G(B_dR^+(R^♯)). By Beauville–Laszlo gluing Gr_G/φ^ℤ → Div^1 is the moduli of D ∈ Div^1(S), ℰ ∈ Bun_G(X_S) and a modification between the trivial G-bundle and ℰ at D (an isomorphism off D, meromorphic along D: for every representation F|_{X_S∖D} ≅ F′|_{X_S∖D} extends to F → F′(kD) for k ≫ 0), giving the Beauville–Laszlo morphism Gr_G → Bun_G.
items.note: [SW20, Lecture XIX, Proposition 19.1.2], here 'absolute' over Spd E. GS0:loop-geometry: 'construct ... the relative Grassmannian of a G-bundle with trivialization off those divisors. Prove that the torsor-modification and loop-quotient descriptions agree by Beauville–Laszlo gluing'; RF4:G-torsors for gluing.

items.name: Beauville–Laszlo uniformization is surjective
items.statement: The Beauville–Laszlo morphism Gr_G → Bun_G is a surjective map of v-stacks; in fact, of pro-étale stacks.
items.note: Proof on strictly totally disconnected S: at each connected component Spa(C,C^+), Gr_G(C) → Bun_G(C) is surjective ([Far20a, Théorème 7.1] quasisplit, [Ans19, Theorem 6.5] general); lift via Lemma III.3.2, then Theorem III.2.4 and Lemma III.2.6. Remark III.3.3: classically true only for semisimple G; here because Pic^0(X_{C,C+}) is trivial. BG2:uniformization: 'Construct the Hecke modification uniformization around an untilt divisor through RF4 patching, including v-surjectivity in the exact source range.'

items.name: Gr_G(R) → Gr_G(K(s)) surjective on strictly totally disconnected S
items.statement: For S = Spa(R, R^+) a strictly totally disconnected perfectoid space over Spa(E), and s ∈ S, the map Gr_G(R) → Gr_G(K(s)) is surjective.
items.note: Proof: R → C = K(s) surjective; splitting field E′ embeds in R; Cartan decomposition G(B_dR(C)) = ⊔_{μ} G(B_dR^+(C)) μ(ξ) G(B_dR^+(C)) (printed index X^*(T)^+, misprint for X_*(T)^+: PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E17); G(R) → G(C) surjective by smoothness and henselian O_{S,s}; approximation over B_dR^+/Fil^n. Planned in the BunGAndNewtonStrata packet node BG2:uniformization/beauville-laszlo-surjectivity, which states Lemma III.3.2 and gives its proof as a proof step. Review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21): a node of the draft BunGAndNewtonStrata packet states this (layer BunGAndNewtonStrata:BG2:uniformization), but that packet has not been reviewed or promoted, and the stage description alone does not name the statement. items.name: Gr_G = colim Gr_{G,≤μ} for split G
items.statement: If G is split then Gr_G = lim→_{μ ∈ X_*(T)^+} Gr_{G,≤μ} as a v-sheaf, where the index set is partially ordered by the dominance order (μ ≤ μ′ if μ′ − μ is a nonnegative integral sum of positive coroots).
items.note: Proof via an embedding G ↪ GL_n, finiteness of fibres of X_*(T)^+ → ℤ^n/𝔖_n, closedness of Gr_{G,≤μ} ([SW20, Prop. 19.2.3]). Planned in the BunGAndNewtonStrata packet node BG2:uniformization/beauville-laszlo-surjectivity, which states Lemma III.3.4 and gives its proof as a proof step. items.name: Gr_{G̃} → Gr_G surjective for central torus extensions
items.statement: Suppose G̃ → G is a central extension with kernel a torus. Then Gr_{G̃} → Gr_G is a surjective map of v-sheaves.
items.note: Proof: reduce to split, use Lemma III.3.4; surjective on points as H^1_ét(Spec B_dR(C), D) = 0 for the torus kernel D; Gr_{G̃,≤μ̃} → Gr_{G,≤μ} quasicompact hence v-cover ([Sch17a, Lemma 12.11]). With Prop. III.3.1 this proves Lemma III.2.10 (BG2:uniformization's 'v-surjectivity lemma'). Planned in the BunGAndNewtonStrata packet node BG2:uniformization/beauville-laszlo-surjectivity, which states Lemma III.3.5 and gives its proof as a proof step. items.name: Decomposition Gr_G = ⊔_{α∈π_1(G)} Gr_G^α (split G)
items.statement: Suppose G is split. There is a locally constant map |Gr_G| → π_1(G) inducing a decomposition in open/closed subsheaves Gr_G = ⊔_{α ∈ π_1(G)} Gr_G^α characterized by Gr_{G,μ} ⊂ Gr_G^{μ^♯}, where μ^♯ ∈ π_1(G) is the image of μ ∈ X_*(T)^+.
items.note: Reduced to simply connected G_der by Lemma III.3.5 and a z-extension. items.statement: Suppose G is split. The composite |Gr_G| → |Bun_G| → π_1(G) (Beauville–Laszlo, then κ) is the opposite of the map of Proposition III.3.6 (i).
items.note: Reduced via z-extensions, G/G_der, induced tori to 𝔾_m, then Prop. II.2.3. items.name: Gr_G^α as filtered colimit
items.statement: Suppose G is split. For each α ∈ π_1(G), Gr_G^α = lim→_{μ ∈ X_*(T)^+, μ^♯ = α} Gr_{G,≤μ}^α as a filtered colimit of v-sheaves.
items.note: {μ : μ^♯ = α} is filtered since differences lie in the coroot lattice. items.name: Non-split Gr_G decomposition and κ
items.statement: For general G, choosing E′|E Galois of finite degree splitting G and using Gr_G ×_{Spd(E)} Spd(E′) = Gr_{G_{E′}}: (i) there is a decomposition Gr_G = ⊔_{ᾱ ∈ Γ∖π_1(G)} Gr_G^{ᾱ} and a formula Gr_G = lim→_{μ̄ ∈ Γ∖X_*(T)^+} Gr_{G,≤μ̄} such that Gr_{G,≤μ̄} ⊂ Gr_G^{μ̄^♯}; (ii) the composite |Gr_G| → |Bun_G| → π_1(G)_Γ is induced by the opposite of Γ∖π_1(G) → π_1(G)_Γ and this decomposition. Together with Prop. III.3.1 this gives another proof of Theorem III.2.7.
items.note: Printed index set Γ∖X^*(T)^+ is a misprint for Γ∖X_*(T)^+ (PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E18).

items.name: Pure inner twisting in a topos
items.statement: Let X be a topos, H a group in X and T an H-torsor. Let H^T = Aut(T) as a group in X. Then: (i) H^T is the 'pure inner twisting' of H by T, H^T = H ∧^H T where H acts by conjugation on H; in particular [H^T] ∈ H^1(X, H_ad) is the image of [T] via H^1(X, H) → H^1(X, H_ad). (ii) The morphism of stacks on X, [∗/H] → [∗/H^T], that sends an H-torsor S to Isom(S, T), is an equivalence.
items.note: Serre's 'torsion au moyen d'un cocycle' [Ser94, I.5.3]. BG0: 'Include ... inner twisting'. Neither Mathlib nor Tau Ceti has torsors in a general topos with twisting (searched declarations.tsv for Torsor/InnerTwist: only AddTorsor).

items.name: The group G_b (Kottwitz's J_b)
items.statement: For b ∈ B(G), the automorphism group of the corresponding G-isocrystal defines a reductive group G_b over E via G_b(R) = {g ∈ G(R ⊗_E Ĕ) | g b = b σ(g)}. G_b is an inner form of a Levi subgroup of the quasisplit inner form of G (of a Levi of G if G is quasisplit); it is an inner form of G precisely when b is basic, i.e. the Newton point is central. A G-bundle over X_{C,C+} is semistable iff it corresponds to a basic b.
items.note: [Kot97, 3.3] (J there); semistability criterion from [Far20a], may be taken as definition. BG0: 'Construct J_b as its algebraic sigma-centralizer and prove representability and its inner-Levi description.'

items.name: G_b × X_S is the pure inner twist of G × X_S by ℰ_b (b basic)
items.statement: Let S ∈ Perf_k, b ∈ B(G) basic and ℰ_b → X_S the associated étale G-torsor. Then the étale sheaf of groups G_b ×_{Spa(E)} X_S over X_S is the pure inner twisting of G ×_{Spa(E)} X_S by ℰ_b.
items.note: Proof: ℰ_b = (G_Ĕ ×_{Spa Ĕ} Y_S)/((bσ) × φ)^ℤ; G_b × X_S → Aut(ℰ_b) is, on Y_S, the map G_b(R) → G(R), an isomorphism since G_b ×_E Ĕ → G ×_E Ĕ is an isomorphism for basic b ([RZ96, Corollary 1.14]). 'Extended pure inner forms (Kottwitz) become pure inner forms (Vogan) on the curve.' Planned in the BunGAndNewtonStrata packet node BG0/pure-inner-twisting, which states Proposition III.4.2 and gives its proof steps. Input for BG3. Review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21): a node of the draft BunGAndNewtonStrata packet states this (layer BunGAndNewtonStrata:BG0), but that packet has not been reviewed or promoted, and the stage description alone does not name the statement. Packets count as planning only once promoted (PROTOCOL §6), so the item stays missing and is routed as a source to that layer.

items.name: Bun_G ≃ Bun_{G_b} for basic b
items.statement: For b basic there is an isomorphism of v-stacks Bun_G ≃ Bun_{G_b} that induces an isomorphism Bun_G^b ≃ Bun_{G_b}^1.
items.note: From Propositions III.4.1(ii) and III.4.2; only for basic b. Planned in the BunGAndNewtonStrata packet node BG0/pure-inner-twisting ('whence Bun_G = Bun_{G_b} and Bun^b_G = Bun^1_{G_b} (Corollary III.4.3)'); used in BG3's node for Theorem III.4.5. Review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21): a node of the draft BunGAndNewtonStrata packet states this (layer BunGAndNewtonStrata:BG0), but that packet has not been reviewed or promoted, and the stage description alone does not name the statement. Packets count as planning only once promoted (PROTOCOL §6), so the item stays missing and is routed as a source to that layer.

items.name: Morita equivalence Bun_{GL_n} ≅ Bun_{B^×}
items.statement: Take G = GL_n and (D, φ) an isoclinic isocrystal of height n, B = End(D, φ) the associated simple E-algebra. Then B ⊗_E 𝒪_{X_S} ≅ End(ℰ(D, φ)) for any S ∈ Perf_k, Bun_{B^×} is the stack S ↦ {rank 1 locally free B ⊗_E 𝒪_{X_S}-modules}, and ℰ ↦ Hom_{𝒪_{X_S}}(ℰ, ℰ(D, φ)) is an isomorphism Bun_{GL_n} ≅ Bun_{B^×}.
items.note: Concrete instance of Cor. III.4.3.

items.name: Description of the semistable locus
items.statement: A family of G-bundles is semistable if all of its geometric fibres are (Newton point central). The semistable locus Bun_G^{ss} ⊂ Bun_G is open, and there is a canonical decomposition as open/closed substacks Bun_G^{ss} = ⊔_{b ∈ B(G)_basic} Bun_G^b. For b basic there is an isomorphism [∗/G_b(E)] ≅ Bun_G^b.
items.note: Proof: openness from III.2.3 (centrality of the Newton point is a minimality condition — printed 'μ is central', misprint for ν); basic elements map bijectively to π_1(G)_Γ ([Kot97, 4.9, (4.4.1)]) so III.2.7 gives the decomposition; then III.4.2 and III.2.4. BG3: 'For basic b prove the classifying-stack description by J_b(E), and prove that the union of basic strata is open.'

items.name: Bun_T for a torus
items.statement: For a torus T, Bun_T = Bun_T^{ss} and there is an exact sequence of Picard stacks 0 → [∗/T(E)] → Bun_T → X_*(T)_Γ → 0, where X_*(T)_Γ = B(T). The fibre of Bun_T → B(T) over β is a gerbe banded by T(E) over ∗ (via the action of Bun_T^1), neutralized after choosing b with [b] = β. If T(Ĕ) ↠ B(T) has a section (e.g. B(T) torsion free), then Bun_T ≃ [∗/T(E)] × X_*(T)_Γ as a Picard stack.
items.note: Special case of Theorem III.4.5.

items.name: Moduli of G-bundles with split HN filtration
items.statement: Consider the functor Bun_G^{HN-split} taking each S ∈ Perf_k to the groupoid of exact ⊗-functors from Rep_E G to the category of ℚ-graded vector bundles ℰ = ⊕_λ ℰ^λ on X_S such that ℰ^λ is everywhere semistable of slope λ for all λ ∈ ℚ. For any b ∈ B(G), ℰ_b refines to a ℚ-graded bundle ℰ_b^{gr}, and for S affinoid the natural map G_b ×_E X_S^{alg} → Aut(ℰ_b^{gr}) of group schemes over X_S^{alg} is an isomorphism. In particular there is a natural map ⊔_{b ∈ B(G)} [∗/G_b(E)] → Bun_G^{HN-split}, and this is an isomorphism.
items.note: G_b ×_E Ĕ is the centralizer of the slope homomorphism ν_b ([RZ96, Cor. 1.14]); surjectivity via Theorem III.2.4 and Lemma III.2.6 for Bun_{G_b}. Used to split G̃_b = G̃_b^{>0} ⋊ G_b(E), and for the charts of §V.3 (BG4). Planned in the BunGAndNewtonStrata packet node BG3/semistable-locus-and-basic-strata, whose statement ends with this proposition and whose last proof step is its proof. Review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21): a node of the draft BunGAndNewtonStrata packet states this (layer BunGAndNewtonStrata:BG3), but that packet has not been reviewed or promoted, and the stage description alone does not name the statement. Packets count as planning only once promoted (PROTOCOL §6), so the item stays missing and is routed as a source to that layer.

items.name: Automorphism v-group G̃_b and its filtration G̃_b^{≥λ}
items.statement: For b ∈ B(G), G̃_b = Aut(ℰ_b) : (S ∈ Perf_k) ↦ Aut_{X_S}(ℰ_b|_{X_S}), which preserves the HN filtrations (ρ_*ℰ_b)^{≥λ} for every ρ ∈ Rep_E(G). For λ > 0, G̃_b^{≥λ} ⊂ G̃_b is the subgroup of automorphisms γ with (γ − 1)(ρ_*ℰ_b)^{≥λ′} ⊂ (ρ_*ℰ_b)^{≥λ′+λ} for all λ′ and all ρ; G̃_b^{>λ} = ∪_{λ′>λ} G̃_b^{≥λ′} (eventually constant). For G = GL_2 and ℰ_b = O ⊕ O(1): G̃_b = (E^× BC(O(1)); 0 E^×).
items.note: If G is quasisplit with Borel B the HN filtration is a reduction of ℰ_b to a parabolic P ⊃ B. BG3: 'For general b construct the full automorphism v-group Gtilde_b, its map to J_b(E), connected kernel'.

items.name: Structure of G̃_b
items.statement: One has G̃_b = G̃_b^{>0} ⋊ G_b(E), and for any λ > 0, there is a natural isomorphism G̃_b^{≥λ}/G̃_b^{>λ} ≅ 𝓑𝓒((ad ℰ_b)^{≥λ}/(ad ℰ_b)^{>λ}), the Banach–Colmez space associated to the slope −λ isoclinic part of (Lie(G) ⊗_E Ĕ, Ad(b)σ). In particular, G̃_b is an extension of G_b(E) by a successive extension of positive Banach–Colmez spaces, and thus G̃_b → ∗ is representable in locally spatial diamonds, of dimension ⟨2ρ, ν_b⟩ (ρ the half-sum of the positive roots).
items.note: Proof via GAGA and Prop. III.5.2 on X_R^alg: filtration H^{≥λ} of the inner twist H with H^{≥0}/H^{>0} ≅ G_b ×_E X_R^alg (Prop. III.4.7), H^{≥λ}/H^{>λ} = (ad ℰ_b)^{≥λ}/(ad ℰ_b)^{>λ}, H^1(X_R^alg, H^{≥μ}) = 0 for μ > 0; dimension Σ_{λ>0} λ·dim((ad ℰ_b)^{≥λ}/(ad ℰ_b)^{>λ}) = ⟨2ρ, ν_b⟩. BG3: 'Use the positive Banach–Colmez filtration to identify the kernel and prove its ell-cohomological smoothness and dimension pairing <2rho,nu_b>'.

items.name: Filtration of the automorphism group scheme of a filtered G-bundle
items.statement: Let G be a reductive group over a field K, and let X be a scheme over K. Let ℰ be a G-bundle on X with automorphism group scheme H/X (an inner form of G ×_K X, cf. Proposition III.4.1). Consider a ℚ-filtration on the fibre functor Rep_K(G) → {Vector bundles on X} associated with ℰ. Defining groups H^{≥λ} ⊂ H for λ ≥ 0 as before, they are smooth group schemes, H^{≥0} is a parabolic subgroup with unipotent radical H^{>0}, the Lie algebra of H^{≥λ} is (ad ℰ)^{≥λ} ⊂ Lie ad ℰ = Lie H, and for λ > 0 the quotient H^{≥λ}/H^{>λ} is a vector group, thus H^{≥λ}/H^{>λ} ≅ (ad ℰ)^{≥λ}/(ad ℰ)^{>λ}.
items.note: Proof: étale locally the filtration splits ([Zie15, Theorem 1.3]) and ℰ is trivial, so the filtration comes from ν : 𝔻/X → G ×_K X (𝔻 the pro-torus with character group ℚ); then [SR72]. Planned in the BunGAndNewtonStrata packet node BG3/full-automorphism-v-group ('The algebraic input is Proposition III.5.2: ...', stated in full). Tau Ceti has the dynamic subgroup functors TauCeti.Cocharacter.parabolic, .levi and .unipotent (TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Dynamic/Parabolic.lean) for a cocharacter of an affine group scheme over a ring, with the Levi decomposition on points; representability, smoothness, Lie algebras, the ℚ-indexed filtration and the vector-group graded pieces are not there. Review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21): a node of the draft BunGAndNewtonStrata packet states this (layer BunGAndNewtonStrata:BG3), but that packet has not been reviewed or promoted, and the stage description alone does not name the statement. Packets count as planning only once promoted (PROTOCOL §6), so the item stays missing and is routed as a source to that layer.

items.name: G̃_b in the quasi-split case via the opposite parabolic
items.statement: Suppose G is quasi-split, A ⊂ T ⊂ B with A maximal split. Up to σ-conjugating b, ν_b : 𝔻 → A with ν_b ∈ X_*(A)^+_ℚ; let M_b be the centralizer of ν_b, P_b^+ the standard parabolic (weights of ν_b on Lie P_b^+ ≥ 0) with Levi M_b, P_b^− the opposite parabolic, b = b_M ∈ M_b(Ĕ). With Q = ℰ_{b_M} ×^{M_b} P_b^− and R_uQ = ℰ_{b_M} ×^{M_b} R_uP_b^− as X_R^alg-group schemes, G̃_b(R, R^+) = Q(X_R^alg) and G̃_b^{>0}(R, R^+) = R_uQ(X_R^alg).
items.note: For GL_2 and O ⊕ O(1), Q is the upper triangular subgroup of GL(O ⊕ O(1)). Used later for parabolic induction (ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction:ES7:parabolic consumes BG3).

items.name: Bun_G^b ≅ [∗/G̃_b]
items.statement: Let b ∈ B(G) be any element given by some G-isocrystal. The induced map x_b : ∗ → Bun_G^b is a surjective map of v-stacks, and ∗ ×_{Bun_G^b} ∗ ≅ G̃_b, so that Bun_G^b ≅ [∗/G̃_b] is the classifying stack of G̃_b-torsors. In particular, the map G̃_b → π_0 G̃_b ≅ G_b(E) induces a map Bun_G^b → [∗/G_b(E)] that admits a splitting.
items.note: Proof on strictly totally disconnected S: relative HN filtration (Thm II.2.19) gives a ℚ-filtered fibre functor of the same type as ℰ_b; T = Isom^{filtered}(ℰ_b, ℰ) is an H^{≥0}-torsor whose graded part is locally trivial (Prop. III.4.7) and H^1(X_R^alg, H^{>0}) = 0. BG3: 'quotient description Bun_G^b = [*/Gtilde_b]. Retain the connected kernel for nonbasic b; the stack is not in general [*/J_b(E)].'

items.name: G̃_b-torsors over affinoid perfectoids
items.statement: From the vanishing of H^1_v(S, G̃_b^{>0}) for S affinoid perfectoid, for such S any G̃_b-torsor is of the form T × G̃_b^{>0} where T → S is a G_b(E)-torsor; here g_1 ⋉ g_2 ∈ G_b(E) ⋉ G̃_b^{>0} acts on T × G̃_b^{>0} by (x, y) ↦ (g_1·x, g_1 g_2 y g_1^{−1}). In particular any G̃_b-torsor is representable in locally spatial diamonds.
items.note: Follow-up to Remark III.2.5. Planned in the BunGAndNewtonStrata packet node BG3/stratum-is-classifying-stack ('Moreover (Remark III.5.4) for S affinoid perfectoid the vanishing of H^1_v(S, G-tilde^{>0}_b) shows that every G-tilde_b-torsor is of the form T x G-tilde^{>0}_b for a G_b(E)-torsor T, so in particular every G-tilde_b-torsor is representable in locally spatial diamonds'). Review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21): a node of the draft BunGAndNewtonStrata packet states this (layer BunGAndNewtonStrata:BG3), but that packet has not been reviewed or promoted, and the stage description alone does not name the statement. Packets count as planning only once promoted (PROTOCOL §6), so the item stays missing and is routed as a source to that layer.

items.name: Artin v-stack
items.statement: An Artin v-stack is a small v-stack X such that the diagonal ∆_X : X → X × X is representable in locally spatial diamonds, and there is some surjective map f : U → X from a locally spatial diamond U such that f is separated and cohomologically smooth.
items.note: VS0 plans: "Define Artin v-stacks by representable diagonals and the cohomologically smooth atlas condition of FS IV.1; prove atlas independence and stability under fibre products." Separatedness of the chart is imposed because cohomological smoothness is only defined for separated maps (Remark IV.1.2). Basic notion for Bun_G, [∗/G], Hecke stacks throughout the paper.

items.name: Diagonal of an Artin v-stack is quasiseparated
items.statement: For any Artin v-stack X, the diagonal ∆_X : X → X × X is quasiseparated.
items.locator: Chapter IV, §IV.1.1.1, Remark IV.1.2 (and first sentence of Remark IV.1.4), pp. 107–108
items.note: Proof: take a chart U → X with U a disjoint union of spatial diamonds; U ×_X U → U is separated so U ×_X U is quasiseparated, and it is the pullback of ∆_X along the surjection U × U → X × X. Remark IV.1.3 notes Bun_G and even [∗/G(E)] are not quasiseparated. Planned in node VS0/artin-v-stack-definition of the VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories decomposition (accepted review, 2026-09-16; the same node is in its packet) ('Separatedness of f forces Delta_X to be quasiseparated'), with this proof as its first proof step.

items.name: Criterion for being an Artin v-stack
items.statement: Let X be a small v-stack with a surjective separated map U → X from a small v-sheaf. (i) If U is quasiseparated, then ∆_X is quasiseparated. (ii) If U is a locally spatial diamond and U → X is representable in locally spatial diamonds, then ∆_X is quasiseparated, and ∆_X is representable in locally spatial diamonds as soon as it is representable in diamonds. (iii) In the situation of (ii), whether ∆_X is representable in diamonds can be checked after pullback along a map V → X × X that is surjective as a map of pro-étale stacks. In particular, if there is a map f : U → X from a locally spatial diamond U that is separated, cohomologically smooth, representable in locally spatial diamonds and surjective as a map of pro-étale stacks, then X is an Artin v-stack.
items.note: Uses [Sch17a, Proposition 13.4 (v)] and [Sch17a, Proposition 13.2 (iii)]. Used in the proofs of Proposition IV.1.8 (ii),(iii). Planned in node VS0/artin-v-stack-definition of the VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories decomposition (accepted review, 2026-09-16; the same node is in its packet): its second proof step records these criteria and its third hypothesis the variant with a chart that is only v-surjective.

items.name: Surjectivity of smooth charts on geometric points
items.statement: Since cohomologically smooth morphisms are open, to prove that a separated, representable in locally spatial diamonds, cohomologically smooth morphism U → X is surjective, it suffices to verify it on geometric points.
items.note: Used in Theorem IV.1.19 to see that the Beauville–Laszlo map is a v-cover. Planned as the third proof step of node VS0/artin-v-stack-definition of the VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories decomposition (accepted review, 2026-09-16; the same node is in its packet).

items.name: Relative Artin v-stacks agree with absolute ones
items.statement: Let g : X → S be a map of small v-stacks such that ∆_S is representable in locally spatial diamonds (e.g. S an Artin v-stack). Then ∆_{X/S} : X → X ×_S X is representable in locally spatial diamonds if and only if ∆_X is; hence X is an "Artin v-stack over S" if and only if it is an Artin v-stack.
items.note: Formal consequence of X ×_S X → X × X being a base change of ∆_S. Planned in node VS0/artin-v-stack-definition of the VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories decomposition (accepted review, 2026-09-16; the same node is in its packet) (statement and fourth hypothesis).

items.name: Locally spatial diamonds are Artin v-stacks
items.statement: Any locally spatial diamond is an Artin v-stack.
items.note: VS0 plans: "Define Artin v-stacks by representable diagonals and the cohomologically smooth atlas condition of FS IV.1; prove atlas independence and stability under fibre products." Immediate example.

items.name: Fibre products of Artin v-stacks
items.statement: Any fibre product of Artin v-stacks is an Artin v-stack.
items.note: VS0 plans: "Define Artin v-stacks by representable diagonals and the cohomologically smooth atlas condition of FS IV.1; prove atlas independence and stability under fibre products." (PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E20).

items.name: Artin property can be tested after product with a smooth cover of the point
items.statement: Let S → ∗ be a pro-étale surjective, representable in locally spatial diamonds, separated and cohomologically smooth morphism of v-sheaves. The v-stack X is an Artin v-stack if and only if X × S is an Artin v-stack.
items.note: Used with S = Spd E or Spa F_q((t^{1/p^∞})) (Example IV.1.9 (i)). Planned in node VS0/stability-under-fibre-products-and-representable-maps of the VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories decomposition (accepted review, 2026-09-16; the same node is in its packet), statement (ii).

items.name: Stacks representable over an Artin v-stack
items.statement: If X is an Artin v-stack and f : Y → X is representable in locally spatial diamonds, then Y is an Artin v-stack.
items.note: Proof uses [Sch17a, Proposition 11.10] (0-truncated injective maps are representable in diamonds) and Remark IV.1.4. Planned in node VS0/stability-under-fibre-products-and-representable-maps of the VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories decomposition (accepted review, 2026-09-16; the same node is in its packet), statement (iii).

items.name: First examples of Artin v-stacks
items.statement: (i) X is an Artin v-stack if and only if X × Spd E, resp. X × Spa(F_q((t^{1/p^∞}))), is an Artin v-stack. (ii) Any small v-sheaf X such that X → ∗ is representable in locally spatial diamonds is an Artin v-stack; e.g. X = ∗. (iii) Any locally closed substack of an Artin v-stack is an Artin v-stack.
items.note: (iii) uses Proposition IV.1.8 (iii) and [Sch17a, Proposition 11.20]. Used for the Harder–Narasimhan strata Bun_G^b. Planned in node VS0/stability-under-fibre-products-and-representable-maps of the VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories decomposition (accepted review, 2026-09-16; the same node is in its packet): its second hypothesis is (i) and its first acceptance item is (iii); (ii) is immediate from Definition IV.1.1.

items.name: [∗/G] is an Artin v-stack
items.statement: Let G be a locally profinite group that admits a closed embedding into GL_n(E) for some n. Then the classifying stack [∗/G] is an Artin v-stack.
items.note: Proof: [Spd E/G] = Spd E × [∗/G]; with H = GL_{n,E}^♢, H/G → [Spd E/G] is separated cohomologically smooth, and H/G is a locally spatial diamond, cohomologically smooth over Spd E by [Sch17a, Propositions 13.4 (iv), 23.15, 24.2]. Used (as ℓ-dimension 0) in Theorem IV.1.19, where it is cited as 'Example IV.1.9 (4)'. Planned in node VS0/stability-under-fibre-products-and-representable-maps of the VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories decomposition (accepted review, 2026-09-16; the same node is in its packet) through its acceptance item 'Check (ii) by verifying the Artin property of [*/G] via [Spd E/G]'; the BunGAndNewtonStrata packet node BG2:smooth-Artin/bun-g-is-smooth-artin consumes it.

items.name: ∗ → [∗/G] is not cohomologically smooth
items.statement: In the situation of Example IV.1.9 (iv), the map f : ∗ → [∗/G] is not cohomologically smooth unless G is finite, since for its pullback f̃ : G → ∗ the sheaf f̃^!Λ is the sheaf of distributions on G with values in Λ.
items.note: Contrast with algebraic groups. Related to DiamondSixOperations S5's warning on Rq^! for quotients, but that stage concerns [Sch17a, 24.2–24.3].

items.name: Cohomologically smooth map of Artin v-stacks
items.statement: Let f : Y → X be a map of Artin v-stacks. Assume that there is some separated, representable in locally spatial diamonds, and cohomologically smooth surjection g : V → Y from a locally spatial diamond V such that f ∘ g : V → X is separated. Then f is cohomologically smooth if for any (equivalently, one) such g, the map f ∘ g : V → X (which is separated by assumption, and automatically representable in locally spatial diamonds) is cohomologically smooth. (Convention IV.1.12: saying f is cohomologically smooth includes the existence of such a g.)
items.locator: Chapter IV, §IV.1.1.2, Definition IV.1.11 and Convention IV.1.12, pp. 110–111
items.note: Independence of g from [Sch17a, Proposition 23.13] (cohomological smoothness is cohomologically smooth local on the source). Convention IV.1.12 notes that the separatedness condition is automatic when the charts are perfectoid spaces and ∆_X is representable in perfectoid spaces. Planned in node VS0/shriek-pullback-for-smooth-stacky-maps of the VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories decomposition (accepted review, 2026-09-16; the same node is in its packet) (first sentence of its statement; Convention IV.1.12 is its third hypothesis).

items.name: Dualizing complex of a smooth map of Artin v-stacks
items.statement: Let f : Y → X be a cohomologically smooth map of Artin v-stacks. The dualizing complex Rf^!Λ ∈ D_ét(Y, Λ) is the invertible object equipped with isomorphisms Rg^!(Rf^!Λ) ≅ R(f∘g)^!Λ for all separated, representable in locally spatial diamonds, and cohomologically smooth maps g : V → Y from a locally spatial diamond V, such that for all cohomologically smooth maps h : V′ → V between such g′ : V′ → Y and g : V → Y, the composite isomorphism R(g′)^!(Rf^!Λ) ≅ R(f∘g′)^!Λ ≅ R(f∘g∘h)^!Λ ≅ Rh^!(R(f∘g)^!Λ) ≅ Rh^!(Rg^!(Rf^!Λ)) ≅ R(g′)^!(Rf^!Λ) is the identity. It exists and is unique up to unique isomorphism, being given by the rule (V →g Y) ↦ RHom_Λ(Rg^!Λ, R(f∘g)^!Λ) in 2-lim_{(V→Y)∈C} {invertible objects in D_ét(V,Λ)} ≅ {invertible objects in D_ét(Y,Λ)}.
items.locator: Chapter IV, §IV.1.1.2, Definition IV.1.13 and following paragraph, p. 111
items.note: VS0 plans: "Prove pullback, exceptional pullback and their normalization for smooth atlases". Λ is killed by some n prime to p, or an adic ring as in [Sch17a, Section 26]. Remark IV.1.14 warns that Rg^!(Rf^!Λ) ≅ R(f∘g)^!Λ is only known for g separated cohomologically smooth from a locally spatial diamond.

items.name: Rf^! for smooth maps of Artin v-stacks
items.statement: Let f : Y → X be a cohomologically smooth map of Artin v-stacks. The functor Rf^! : D_ét(X, Λ) → D_ét(Y, Λ) is given by Rf^! = Rf^!Λ ⊗^L_Λ f^*. Checking after a cohomologically smooth cover, Rf^! preserves all limits (and colimits) and hence admits a left adjoint Rf_! (Remark IV.1.16).
items.locator: Chapter IV, §IV.1.1.2, Definition IV.1.15 and Remark IV.1.16, p. 111
items.note: VS0 plans: "Prove pullback, exceptional pullback and their normalization for smooth atlases". The left adjoint Rf_! (Remark IV.1.16) is the 'pi-sharp' functor VS0 warns is not an unqualified ECD Rpi!.

items.name: Pure ℓ-dimension; decomposition by dimension
items.statement: Let f : Y → X be a cohomologically smooth map of Artin v-stacks and let ℓ ≠ p be a prime. Then f is pure of ℓ-dimension d ∈ ½ℤ if Rf^!F_ℓ sits in homological degree 2d. As Rf^!F_ℓ is invertible, it is v-locally (and a posteriori étale locally) isomorphic to F_ℓ[n] for some n ∈ ℤ, so any cohomologically smooth map f : Y → X of Artin v-stacks decomposes uniquely into a disjoint union of f_d : Y_d → X that are pure of ℓ-dimension d.
items.locator: Chapter IV, §IV.1.1.2, Definition IV.1.17 and following paragraph, pp. 111–112
items.note: The local form F_ℓ[n] is deduced from Proposition IV.2.6 (ii). The decomposition may a priori depend on ℓ and involve half-integers. Used for dim Bun_G = 0 and dim Bun_G^b = −⟨2ρ,ν_b⟩. Planned in node VS0/shriek-pullback-for-smooth-stacky-maps of the VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories decomposition (accepted review, 2026-09-16; the same node is in its packet) (last sentence of its statement, last proof step, last hypothesis).

items.name: Open Schubert cells are cohomologically smooth
items.statement: For any µ ∈ X_*(T)^+, the open Schubert cell Gr_{G,µ}/Spd E′ is cohomologically smooth of ℓ-dimension ⟨2ρ, µ⟩. (Here E′|E is a finite Galois extension splitting G, and for µ̄ ∈ X_*(T)^+/Γ, Gr_{G,µ̄} ⊂ Gr_G is the subsheaf with Gr_{G,µ̄} ×_{Spd E} Spd E′ = ⨆_{µ′≡µ} Gr_{G,µ′}.)
items.locator: Chapter IV, §IV.1.2.1, Proposition IV.1.18, p. 112 (proof deferred to Proposition VI.2.4)
items.note: GS0:Schubert-smoothness plans: "Prove FS VI.2.4/IV.1.18: over a splitting field the open cell Gr_(G,μ) is ℓ-cohomologically smooth of ℓ-dimension <2rho,μ>, ℓ≠p; descend the Galois-orbit cells." Input to Theorem IV.1.19.

items.name: Bun_G is a cohomologically smooth Artin v-stack of dimension 0
items.statement: The stack Bun_G is a cohomologically smooth Artin v-stack of ℓ-dimension 0. The Beauville–Laszlo map defines a separated cohomologically smooth cover ⨆_{µ̄∈X_*(T)^+/Γ} [G(E)\Gr_{G,µ̄}] → Bun_G.
items.note: BG2:smooth-Artin plans: "Prove FS IV.1.19: Bun_G is an ℓ-cohomologically smooth Artin v-stack of ℓ-dimension zero, for ℓ≠p, with the separated cohomologically smooth Beauville–Laszlo covering by the disjoint union of `[G(E)\Gr_(G,μ̄)]`." Proof: diagonal via Tannakian reduction (Chevalley: G = stabilizer of a line D ⊂ W in GL_n) to Lemma IV.1.20; π: ⨆[G(E)\Gr_{G,µ̄}] → Bun_G ×_k Spd Ĕ has fibres open in modifications of locally constant type (v-locally ⨆ Gr_{G,µ̄,E} ×_{Spd E} S), smooth by IV.1.18, of ℓ-dimension ⟨2ρ,µ⟩; [G(E)\Gr_{G,µ̄}] → [Spd E/G(E)] has ℓ-dimension ⟨2ρ,µ⟩ and [∗/G(E)] has dimension 0 (Example IV.1.9 (iv)). Surjectivity on geometric points uses Beauville–Laszlo uniformization (Chapter III).

items.name: Isom and surjection sheaves of vector bundles on X_S
items.statement: For E_1, E_2 vector bundles on X_S, the sheaf T/S ↦ {surjections E_1|_{X_T} ↠ E_2|_{X_T}}, resp. T/S ↦ Isom(E_1|_{X_T}, E_2|_{X_T}), is representable by an open subdiamond of BC(E_1^∨ ⊗ E_2). In particular, those are locally spatial diamonds.
items.note: BG2:smooth-Artin plans: "Construct the locally spatial diagonal via Isom sheaves (IV.1.20)". Proof: u is an isomorphism iff u and u^∨ are surjective; the support of the cokernel is closed in |X_S| with closed image in |S| (properness of X_S → S). Needs BC(E) locally spatial (Chapter II).

items.name: HN strata are smooth of dimension −⟨2ρ,ν_b⟩
items.statement: For every b ∈ B(G), the stratum Bun_G^b is a cohomologically smooth Artin v-stack of ℓ-dimension −⟨2ρ, ν_b⟩.
items.note: BG3 plans: "Use the positive Banach–Colmez filtration to identify the kernel and prove its ell-cohomological smoothness and dimension pairing <2rho,nu_b>", and BG2:smooth-Artin: "BG3 also records IV.1.22's stratum ℓ-dimension `−<2rho,nu_b>` using the full automorphism group." Proof: Bun_G^b ≅ [∗/G̃_b] → [∗/G_b(E)], target smooth of dimension 0, fibre admits a smooth surjection from ∗ of ℓ-dimension ⟨2ρ,ν_b⟩ (positive Banach–Colmez spaces are cohomologically smooth).

items.name: Connected components of Bun_G
items.statement: The Kottwitz map induces a bijection κ : π_0(Bun_G) → π_1(G)_Γ.
items.note: Proof: κ is well defined (locally constant) and surjective; basic elements of B(G) biject to π_1(G)_Γ; |Bun_G| maps continuously to the T0 space (X_*(T)^+_ℚ)^Γ × π_1(G)_Γ, an increasing union of finite open subspaces, so a nonempty open U ⊂ Bun_G contains an open point (Lemma IV.1.24), i.e. some Bun_G^b ⊂ U open; then IV.1.19 and IV.1.22 force −⟨2ρ,ν_b⟩ = 0, so b is basic. A weak form of Conjecture III.2.15. Planned in the BunGAndNewtonStrata packet node BG2:smooth-Artin/connected-components ('The Kottwitz map induces a BIJECTION kappa : pi_0(Bun_G) -> pi_1(G)_Gamma'), with this proof in its proof steps. Review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21): a node of the draft BunGAndNewtonStrata packet states this (layer BunGAndNewtonStrata:BG2:smooth-Artin), but that packet has not been reviewed or promoted, and the stage description alone does not name the statement. Packets count as planning only once promoted (PROTOCOL §6), so the item stays missing and is routed as a source to that layer.

items.name: Finite T0 spaces have an open point
items.statement: If X is a nonempty finite spectral space, that is to say a finite (T0) topological space, there exists an open point x ∈ X.
items.note: Read mathlib Mathlib/Topology/Separation/Basic.lean:213: theorem exists_open_singleton_of_finite [T0Space X] [Finite X] [Nonempty X] : ∃ x : X, IsOpen ({x} : Set X) — exactly the statement (the 'finite spectral' phrasing is equivalent to finite T0). Used in Corollary IV.1.23.

items.name: f-locally acyclic and f-universally locally acyclic complexes
items.statement: Let f : X → S be a compactifiable map of locally spatial diamonds with locally dim.trg f < ∞ and let A ∈ D_ét(X, Λ) for some Λ with nΛ = 0 with n prime to p. (i) A is f-locally acyclic if (a) for all geometric points x of X with image s in S and a generization t of s, the map RΓ(X_x, A) → RΓ(X_x ×_{S_s} S_t, A) is an isomorphism, where X_x = Spa(C(x), C(x)^+) is the strict localization; and (b) for all separated étale maps j : U → X such that f ∘ j is quasicompact, the complex R(f∘j)_!(A|_U) ∈ D_ét(S, Λ) is perfect-constructible. (ii) A is f-universally locally acyclic if for any map S′ → S of locally spatial diamonds with base change f′ : X′ = X ×_S S′ → S′ and A′ ∈ D_ét(X′, Λ) the pullback of A, the sheaf of complexes A′ is f′-locally acyclic.
items.note: VS1 plans: "Define relative local acyclicity and universal local acyclicity with the overconvergence, geometric-fibre and constructibility conditions of FS IV.2. Prove base change, composition, descent, tensor and relative-dual properties with all compactness hypotheses." Condition (b) replaces finiteness that is automatic for schemes; condition (a) is the analogue of [Ill06, Corollary 3.5]'s formulation.

items.name: Reformulations of condition (a) (relative overconvergence)
items.statement: In the setup of condition (a), X_x = Spa(C, C^+) is strictly local and RΓ(X_x, A) = A_x; X_x ×_{S_s} S_t ⊂ X_x is quasicompact pro-constructible generalizing and strictly local with closed point y the minimal generization of x mapping to t, and RΓ(X_x ×_{S_s} S_t, A) = A_y. Equivalently: (i) for a geometric point s̄ of S, a generization t̄, j : X ×_S S_t̄ ↪ X ×_S S_s̄ and B = A|_{X×_S S_s̄}, one has B = Rj_*j^*B; (ii) for any Spa(C, C^+) → S, with B = A|_{X×_S Spa(C,C^+)} and j : X ×_S Spa(C, O_C) ↪ X ×_S Spa(C, C^+), one has B = Rj_*j^*B; (iii) if x̄ ↦ s̄ and f_x̄ : X_x̄ → S_s̄, then Rf_{x̄*}A|_{X_x̄} is overconvergent, i.e. constant.
items.locator: Chapter IV, §IV.2.1, Remarks IV.2.2 and IV.2.3, p. 115
items.note: Used in Proposition IV.2.11, Proposition IV.2.19 and Theorem IV.2.23 ((iii)⇒(i)). Uses quasicompact base change. Planned in node VS1/ula-definition-with-constructibility of the VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories decomposition (accepted review, 2026-09-16; the same node is in its packet): its second hypothesis records Remark IV.2.2 (strict localization, generization subspace, overconvergence along horizontal lifts) and its second proof step Remark IV.2.3.

items.name: Universal condition (a) is overconvergence
items.statement: Let f : X → S be a compactifiable map of locally spatial diamonds with locally dim.trg f < ∞ and let A ∈ D_ét(X, Λ) for some Λ with nΛ = 0 with n prime to p. The condition (a) of Definition IV.2.1 holds after any base change S′ → S if and only if A is overconvergent, i.e. for any specialization y ⇝ x of geometric points of X, the map A_x → A_y is an isomorphism.
items.note: VS1 plans: "Define relative local acyclicity and universal local acyclicity with the overconvergence, geometric-fibre and constructibility conditions of FS IV.2. Prove base change, composition, descent, tensor and relative-dual properties with all compactness hypotheses." Necessity: base change along X_x → S and use the section x′ : X_x → X ×_S X_x.

items.name: Local acyclicity descends along v-covers of the target
items.statement: In the setup of Definition IV.2.1, if S′ → S is a v-cover and A′ is f′-locally acyclic, then A is f-locally acyclic.
items.note: VS1 plans: "Define relative local acyclicity and universal local acyclicity with the overconvergence, geometric-fibre and constructibility conditions of FS IV.2. Prove base change, composition, descent, tensor and relative-dual properties with all compactness hypotheses." Condition (b) descends by [Sch17a, Proposition 20.13].

items.name: Overconvergent constructible sheaves are locally constant
