items.statement: Let Y be a spatial diamond. (i) If F is a constructible étale sheaf of Λ-modules on Y, then F is locally constant if and only if F is overconvergent. (ii) If A ∈ D_ét,pc(Y, Λ), then A is overconvergent if and only if it is locally a constant perfect complex of Λ-modules.
items.note: Proof via 2-lim_{y→U} Cons(U,Λ) = Cons(Y_y,Λ) [Sch17a, Proposition 20.7] and [Sch17a, Proposition 20.15]. Remark IV.2.7: a constructible F is locally constant near every maximal point (e.g. near classical Tate points of a rigid space); Example IV.2.8: for j : B^1_K∖{0} ↪ B^1_K, j_!Λ is not constructible but j_!Λ = colim_{R→0} j_{R!}Λ with j_{R!}Λ constructible; D_ét-sheaves on a spatial diamond are Ind-constructible [Sch17a, Proposition 20.6]. Planned as the fourth proof step of node VS1/ula-definition-with-constructibility of the VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories decomposition (accepted review, 2026-09-16; the same node is in its packet); its third acceptance item is Remark IV.2.7 and its first is Example IV.2.8.

items.name: Local acyclicity for the identity
items.statement: Assume that f : S → S is the identity. Then A ∈ D_ét(S, Λ) is f-locally acyclic if and only if it is locally constant with perfect fibres.
items.note: Follows from Proposition IV.2.6. Planned as the fifth proof step of node VS1/ula-definition-with-constructibility of the VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories decomposition (accepted review, 2026-09-16; the same node is in its packet).

items.name: Local systems are ULA for smooth maps
items.statement: Assume that f : X → S is a separated map of locally spatial diamonds that is ℓ-cohomologically smooth for all divisors ℓ of n, where nΛ = 0. If A ∈ D_ét(X, Λ) is locally constant with perfect fibres, then A is f-universally locally acyclic.
items.note: Uses [Sch17a, Proposition 23.12 (ii)] (quasicompact separated cohomologically smooth Rf_! preserves constructibility).

items.name: Proper pushforward preserves (universal) local acyclicity
items.statement: Let g : Y → X, f : X → S be maps of locally spatial diamonds where g is proper and f is compactifiable and locally dim.trg g, dim.trg f < ∞. Assume that A ∈ D_ét(Y, Λ) is f∘g-locally acyclic (resp. f∘g-universally locally acyclic). Then Rg_*A ∈ D_ét(X, Λ) is f-locally acyclic (resp. f-universally locally acyclic).
items.note: VS1 plans: "Define relative local acyclicity and universal local acyclicity with the overconvergence, geometric-fibre and constructibility conditions of FS IV.2. Prove base change, composition, descent, tensor and relative-dual properties with all compactness hypotheses." (listed under 'composition'). Uses proper base change and Rg_* = Rg_!.

items.name: Proper and ULA gives locally constant cohomology
items.statement: Let f : X → S be a proper map of locally spatial diamonds with dim.trg f < ∞ and A ∈ D_ét(X, Λ) that is f-locally acyclic. Then Rf_*A is locally a constant perfect complex of Λ-modules.
items.note: Proposition IV.2.11 with Proposition IV.2.9. Generalizes the proper smooth case. Planned in the statement of node VS1/ula-descent-and-smooth-locality of the VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories decomposition (accepted review, 2026-09-16; the same node is in its packet); its second acceptance item checks it on a proper family of Schubert varieties.

items.name: Smooth pullback preserves local acyclicity
items.statement: Let f : X → S be a compactifiable map of locally spatial diamonds with locally dim.trg f < ∞ (for the locally acyclic case assume S spatial and the cohomological dimension of U_ét for all quasicompact separated étale U → S is ≤ N for some fixed N). Let A ∈ D_ét(X, Λ) where nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p and let g : Y → X be a separated map of locally spatial diamonds that is ℓ-cohomologically smooth for all ℓ dividing n. If A is f-locally acyclic (resp. f-universally locally acyclic), then g^*A is f∘g-locally acyclic (resp. f∘g-universally locally acyclic).
items.note: VS1 plans: "Define relative local acyclicity and universal local acyclicity with the overconvergence, geometric-fibre and constructibility conditions of FS IV.2. Prove base change, composition, descent, tensor and relative-dual properties with all compactness hypotheses." Uses the projection formula, [Sch17a, Proposition 23.12 (ii)] and Lemma IV.2.14.

items.name: Local acyclicity descends along smooth surjections of the source
items.statement: In the setting of Proposition IV.2.13 (same hypotheses on f, S, A, g): if g^*A is f∘g-locally acyclic (resp. f∘g-universally locally acyclic) and g is surjective, then A is f-locally acyclic (resp. f-universally locally acyclic).
items.note: VS1 plans: "Define relative local acyclicity and universal local acyclicity with the overconvergence, geometric-fibre and constructibility conditions of FS IV.2. Prove base change, composition, descent, tensor and relative-dual properties with all compactness hypotheses." ('descent'). Proof shows {Rg_!C : C perfect-constructible on Y} compactly generate D_ét(X,Λ), using [Sch17a, Proposition 20.17]. Essential for Definition IV.2.31.

items.name: Tensoring with perfect-constructible complexes preserves condition (b)
items.statement: Let f : X → S be a compactifiable map of locally spatial diamonds with locally dim.trg f < ∞. Suppose there exists an integer N such that the cohomological dimension of U_ét is bounded by N for all U → X separated étale. Let A ∈ D_ét(X, Λ) be f-locally acyclic and B ∈ D_ét(X, Λ) be perfect-constructible. Then A ⊗^L_Λ B satisfies condition (b) of Definition IV.2.1: for any j : U → X separated étale such that f ∘ j is quasicompact, R(f∘j)_!j^*(A ⊗^L_Λ B) is perfect-constructible.
items.note: VS1 plans: "Define relative local acyclicity and universal local acyclicity with the overconvergence, geometric-fibre and constructibility conditions of FS IV.2. Prove base change, composition, descent, tensor and relative-dual properties with all compactness hypotheses." ('tensor'). (PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E21).

items.name: Relative Verdier dual of a ULA complex commutes with base change
items.statement: Let f : X → S be a compactifiable map of locally spatial diamonds with locally dim.trg f < ∞ and let A ∈ D_ét(X, Λ) be f-universally locally acyclic. Let g : S′ → S be a map of locally spatial diamonds with pullback f′ : X′ = X ×_S S′ → S′, g̃ : X′ → X. Then the composite g̃^*D_{X/S}(A) → D_{X′/S′}(g̃^*A) of the natural maps g̃^*RHom_Λ(A, Rf^!Λ) → RHom_Λ(g̃^*A, g̃^*Rf^!Λ) → RHom_Λ(g̃^*A, Rf′^!Λ) is an isomorphism, where D_{X/S}(A) := RHom_Λ(A, Rf^!Λ). More generally, for any B ∈ D_ét(S, Λ), the map g̃^*RHom_Λ(A, Rf^!B) → RHom_Λ(g̃^*A, Rf′^!g^*B) is an isomorphism.
items.note: VS1 plans: "Define relative local acyclicity and universal local acyclicity with the overconvergence, geometric-fibre and constructibility conditions of FS IV.2. Prove base change, composition, descent, tensor and relative-dual properties with all compactness hypotheses." ('base change ... relative-dual'). Proof reduces to S′ strictly totally disconnected, approximates by finite-dimensional balls (Lemma IV.2.16, [Sch17a, Proposition 11.23]) and uses [Sch17a, Proposition 17.6, Theorems 1.8 (iv), 1.9 (ii)] and Lemma IV.2.17.

items.name: Affinoid perfectoids over S as limits of opens in balls
items.statement: Let S be a spatial diamond and X → S be a morphism from an affinoid perfectoid space to S. Then one can write X = lim_i U_i where U_i is a quasicompact open subset inside a finite dimensional ball over S, and the projective limit is cofiltered.
items.note: Proof: X ↪ B^I_S (I = O(X)^+), B^I_S representing T/S ↦ (O(T)^+)^I, B^I_S = lim_{J⊂I finite} B^J_S; the image in B^J_S is pro-constructible generalizing, hence an intersection of quasicompact opens.

items.name: RHom out of a perfect-constructible complex commutes with base change
items.statement: Let X be a spatial diamond and A ∈ D_ét(X, Λ) perfect-constructible, and let B ∈ D_ét(X, Λ) be arbitrary. Then the formation of RHom_Λ(A, B) commutes with any base change.
items.note: Reduction to A = j_!L via [Sch17a, Proposition 20.16 (iii)], then quasicompact base change [Sch17a, Proposition 17.6].

items.name: Naive dual of a perfect-constructible complex is overconvergent
items.statement: For X a spatial diamond and A ∈ D_ét(X, Λ) perfect constructible, RHom_Λ(A, Λ) is overconvergent.
items.note: Hence never constructible unless locally constant.

items.name: Rf^! against a ULA complex is Verdier dual tensor f^*
items.statement: Let f : X → S be a compactifiable map of locally spatial diamonds with locally dim.trg f < ∞ and let A ∈ D_ét(X, Λ) be f-universally locally acyclic. Then for all B ∈ D_ét(S, Λ), the natural map D_{X/S}(A) ⊗^L_Λ f^*B → RHom_Λ(A, Rf^!B), given as the composite RHom_Λ(A, Rf^!Λ) ⊗^L_Λ f^*B → RHom_Λ(A, Rf^!Λ ⊗^L_Λ f^*B) → RHom_Λ(A, Rf^!B), is an isomorphism.
items.note: VS1 plans: "Define relative local acyclicity and universal local acyclicity with the overconvergence, geometric-fibre and constructibility conditions of FS IV.2. Prove base change, composition, descent, tensor and relative-dual properties with all compactness hypotheses." ('relative-dual'). Proof: reduce to S = Spa(C,C^+) strictly local, use Lemma IV.2.20 to reduce to B = j_!Λ, and the canonical compactification over S to compute stalks.

items.name: Right adjoints of compact-preserving functors preserve sums
items.statement: Let C and D be triangulated categories such that C is compactly generated. Let F : C → D and G : D → C be such that G is right adjoint to F. If F sends compact objects to compact objects then G commutes with arbitrary direct sums.
items.note: Classical, cited from [Nee96, Theorem 5.1]. No compactly generated triangulated category API found in the pinned mathlib/Tau Ceti index (searched declarations.tsv for compact objects in triangulated categories). Owner: EnhancedDerivedSheaves (E3, E5:presentability). The same criterion is PAPER-SCHOLZE-17 item 603 ("[Nee96] (Neeman): compact objects and coproduct-preserving right adjoints"), which that paper's accepted route 4 sends there ("Neeman's compact-objects criterion (603) belong[s] there"). E3 lies upstream of VS1 (E3 -> DiamondSixOperations:S3 -> S4 -> VS1).

items.name: Condition (b) is characterized by the twisted inverse image property
items.statement: (i) Assume that locally on X there exists an integer N such that for any U → X quasicompact separated étale the cohomological dimension of U_ét is ≤ N. If D_{X/S}(A) ⊗^L_Λ f^*B → RHom_Λ(A, Rf^!B) is an isomorphism for all B, then A satisfies condition (b) of Definition IV.2.1 (since R Hom_Λ(R(f∘j)_!A, B) = RΓ(U, RHom_Λ(A, Rf^!B)) for j : U → X separated étale with f∘j quasicompact). (ii) The property of Proposition IV.2.19 holding universally on S, together with the overconvergence condition (a), characterizes universally locally acyclic objects.
items.note: (ii) uses [Sch17a, Proposition 20.13] to reduce to strictly totally disconnected base.

items.name: ULA over a small v-stack base
items.statement: Let f : X → S be a map of small v-stacks that is compactifiable and representable in locally spatial diamonds with locally dim.trg f < ∞. Let A ∈ D_ét(X, Λ). Then A is f-universally locally acyclic if for any map S′ → S from a locally spatial diamond S′ with pullback f′ : X′ = X ×_S S′ → S′, the complex A|_{X′} ∈ D_ét(X′, Λ) is f′-locally acyclic.
items.note: VS1 plans: "Define relative local acyclicity and universal local acyclicity with the overconvergence, geometric-fibre and constructibility conditions of FS IV.2. Prove base change, composition, descent, tensor and relative-dual properties with all compactness hypotheses." All previous results extend to this setting.

items.name: The 2-category C_S of cohomological correspondences
items.statement: Fix a small v-stack S and Λ killed by some integer prime to p. The objects of C_S are maps f : X → S of small v-stacks that are compactifiable, representable in locally spatial diamonds, with locally dim.trg f < ∞. For X, Y ∈ C_S, Fun_{C_S}(X, Y) = D_ét(X ×_S Y, Λ), with A acting as the kernel functor D_ét(X,Λ) → D_ét(Y,Λ) : B ↦ Rπ_{2!}(A ⊗^L_Λ π_1^*B). Composition Fun_{C_S}(X,Y) × Fun_{C_S}(Y,Z) → Fun_{C_S}(X,Z) is (A, B) ↦ A ⋆ B = Rπ_{13!}(π_{12}^*A ⊗^L_Λ π_{23}^*B), well defined by the projection formula; the identity is R∆_!Λ = R∆_*Λ for the closed immersion ∆ : X ↪ X ×_S X. C_S is naturally equivalent to C_S^op. Any functor of 2-categories preserves adjunctions; this applies to pullback C_S → C_{S′} and to the functor X ↦ D_ét(X,Λ).
items.locator: Chapter IV, §IV.2.3.3, construction before Theorem IV.2.23, p. 124
items.note: Planned in node VS1/ula-dualizability-criterion of the VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories decomposition (accepted review, 2026-09-16; the same node is in its packet), whose statement defines C_S (objects, Fun_{C_S}(X,Y) = D_ét(X ×_S Y, Λ), composition ⋆, identity R∆_!Λ) and whose second acceptance item checks that ⋆ makes C_S a 2-category. Lu–Zheng [LZ22] give a different monoidal characterization. Coherences are asserted without an ∞-categorical model; see EnhancedDerivedSheaves for enhancements. HeckeStacksAndLocalShtukas HS1 consumes a 'dualizable/ULA category'. In the proofs of Theorem IV.2.23 and Proposition IV.2.24 ⋆ is used in functional order (PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E23).

items.name: ULA ⇔ dualizability in C_S
items.statement: Let S be a small v-stack, X ∈ C_S (with structure map f), and A ∈ D_ét(X, Λ). The following conditions are equivalent. (i) The complex A is f-universally locally acyclic. (ii) The natural map p_1^*D_{X/S}(A) ⊗^L_Λ p_2^*A → RHom_Λ(p_1^*A, Rp_2^!A) is an isomorphism, where p_1, p_2 : X ×_S X → X are the two projections. (iii) The object A ∈ Fun_{C_S}(X, S) is a left adjoint in C_S. In that case, its right adjoint is given by D_{X/S}(A) ∈ D_ét(X, Λ) = Fun_{C_S}(S, X).
items.note: Analogue of Lu–Zheng [LZ22]. (i)⇒(ii) from IV.2.15, IV.2.19; (ii)⇒(iii) via [Sch17a, Theorem 1.8 (v)] and a diagram chase; (iii)⇒(i) over strictly totally disconnected S. Central to geometric Satake (dualizability). Planned in node VS1/ula-dualizability-criterion of the VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories decomposition (accepted review, 2026-09-16; the same node is in its packet), whose statement is this theorem. Misprints in its proof: PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E22, E23.

items.name: Relative ULA kernels are left adjoints when Y/S is proper
items.statement: Let S be a small v-stack and X, Y ∈ C_S. If Y/S is proper and A ∈ Fun_{C_S}(X, Y) = D_ét(X ×_S Y, Λ) is p_2-universally locally acyclic, then it is a left adjoint and the right adjoint is given by D_{X×_S Y/Y}(A) ∈ D_ét(X ×_S Y, Λ) ≅ D_ét(Y ×_S X, Λ) = Fun_{C_S}(Y, X).
items.note: Properness is important: for X = S, A = Λ, being a left adjoint would force Rf_* ≅ Rf_!(B ⊗ −) for some B.

items.name: Verdier dual of ULA is ULA; biduality
items.statement: Let f : X → S be a compactifiable map of locally spatial diamonds with locally dim.trg f < ∞ and let A ∈ D_ét(X, Λ) be f-universally locally acyclic. Then D_{X/S}(A) is again f-universally locally acyclic, and the biduality map A → D_{X/S}(D_{X/S}(A)) is an isomorphism.
items.locator: Chapter IV, §IV.2.3.3, Corollary IV.2.25 (first part), p. 126
items.note: VS1 plans: "Define relative local acyclicity and universal local acyclicity with the overconvergence, geometric-fibre and constructibility conditions of FS IV.2. Prove base change, composition, descent, tensor and relative-dual properties with all compactness hypotheses." ('relative-dual'). Proof via Theorem IV.2.23 and C_S ≅ C_S^op.

items.name: External products of ULA complexes
items.statement: If f_i : X_i → S for i = 1, 2 are compactifiable maps of small v-stacks that are representable in locally spatial diamonds with locally dim.trg f_i < ∞ and A_i ∈ D_ét(X_i, Λ) are f_i-universally locally acyclic, then A_1 ⊠ A_2 ∈ D_ét(X_1 ×_S X_2, Λ) is f_1 ×_S f_2-universally locally acyclic, and the natural map D_{X_1/S}(A_1) ⊠ D_{X_2/S}(A_2) → D_{X_1×_S X_2/S}(A_1 ⊠ A_2) is an isomorphism.
items.locator: Chapter IV, §IV.2.3.3, Corollary IV.2.25 (second part), p. 126
items.note: VS1 plans: "Define relative local acyclicity and universal local acyclicity with the overconvergence, geometric-fibre and constructibility conditions of FS IV.2. Prove base change, composition, descent, tensor and relative-dual properties with all compactness hypotheses." ('tensor').

items.name: Composition of ULA complexes
items.statement: Let g : Y → X and f : X → S be compactifiable maps of small v-stacks representable in locally spatial diamonds with locally dim.trg f, dim.trg g < ∞, and let A ∈ D_ét(X, Λ) be f-universally (locally) acyclic and B ∈ D_ét(Y, Λ) be g-universally locally acyclic. Then g^*A ⊗^L_Λ B is f∘g-universally locally acyclic, and there is a natural isomorphism D_{Y/S}(g^*A ⊗^L_Λ B) ≅ g^*D_{X/S}(A) ⊗^L_Λ D_{Y/X}(B).
items.note: VS1 plans: "Define relative local acyclicity and universal local acyclicity with the overconvergence, geometric-fibre and constructibility conditions of FS IV.2. Prove base change, composition, descent, tensor and relative-dual properties with all compactness hypotheses." ('composition'). Printed hypothesis says 'f-universally acyclic', meaning f-universally locally acyclic.

items.name: ULA-ness of Λ passes to retracts
items.statement: Let f : X → S and g : Y → S be maps of small v-stacks that are compactifiable and representable in locally spatial diamonds with locally dim.trg f, dim.trg g < ∞. Assume that f is a retract of g over S, i.e. there are maps i : X → Y, r : Y → X over S such that ri = id_X. If Λ is g-universally locally acyclic, then Λ is f-universally locally acyclic.
items.note: Used with the formal smoothness/retract picture in the Jacobian criterion (IV.4).

items.name: Converse to proper pushforward for proper quasi-pro-étale maps
items.statement: Let g : Y → X, f : X → S be maps of locally spatial diamonds where g is proper and quasi-pro-étale and f is compactifiable and locally dim.trg f < ∞. Then A ∈ D_ét(Y, Λ) is f∘g-universally locally acyclic if and only if Rg_*A ∈ D_ét(X, Λ) is f-universally locally acyclic.
items.note: Uses Theorem IV.2.23 (ii) and conservativity of R(g×_S g)_* (RΓ(T,−) conservative on D(T,Λ) for T profinite).

items.name: ULA base change
items.statement: Consider a cartesian diagram of small v-stacks X′ = X ×_S S′ with g̃ : X′ → X, f′ : X′ → S′, g : S′ → S, and f : X → S representable in locally spatial diamonds, compactifiable, locally dim.trg f < ∞. Assume that Λ is f-universally locally acyclic. Then for A ∈ D_ét(S′, Λ) the base change map f^*Rg_*A → Rg̃_*f′^*A is an isomorphism. More generally, if B ∈ D_ét(X, Λ) is f-universally locally acyclic and A ∈ D_ét(S′, Λ), then (f^*Rg_*A) ⊗^L_Λ B → Rg̃_*(f′^*A ⊗^L_Λ g̃^*B) is an isomorphism.
items.note: VS1 plans: "Define relative local acyclicity and universal local acyclicity with the overconvergence, geometric-fibre and constructibility conditions of FS IV.2. Prove base change, composition, descent, tensor and relative-dual properties with all compactness hypotheses." ('base change'). False without hypotheses on f (stalks vs countable products). Proof via IV.2.19, IV.2.25, IV.2.15 and [Sch17a, Theorem 1.9 (iii)]. General version suggested by D. Hansen.

items.name: ULA is compatible with analytification
items.statement: Let K be a complete non-archimedean field with residue characteristic p, f : X → S a separated morphism of K-schemes locally of finite type, and A ∈ D^b_c(X, Λ). Then A is f-universally (locally) acyclic if and only if its analytification A^ad is f^{ad,♢}-universally locally acyclic, where f^{ad,♢} : X^{ad,♢} → S^{ad,♢}.
items.note: Via Theorem IV.2.23 (ii) and the algebraic criterion [LZ22]; compatibility of the six operations with analytification, the key case Rj_* for open immersions being [Hub96, Theorem 3.8.1] (footnote 2). E.g. for S = Spec K every A^ad is ULA.

items.name: ULA for maps of Artin v-stacks
items.statement: Let f : X → S be a map of Artin v-stacks and assume that there is some separated, representable in locally spatial diamonds, and cohomologically smooth surjection g : U → X from a locally spatial diamond U such that f ∘ g : U → S is compactifiable with locally dim.trg(f∘g) < ∞. Then A ∈ D_ét(X, Λ) is f-universally locally acyclic if g^*A is f∘g-universally locally acyclic.
items.note: Well defined by Proposition IV.2.13 and descent. All previous results extend where the relevant operations are defined. Planned in node VS1/ula-for-artin-v-stacks of the VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories decomposition (accepted review, 2026-09-16; the same node is in its packet), whose statement opens with this definition. The sentence before it cites the wrong descent result (PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E24).

items.name: ULA criterion over a smooth map of Artin v-stacks
items.statement: Let f : X → S be a cohomologically smooth map of Artin v-stacks, and let A ∈ D_ét(X, Λ). Consider X ×_S X with its two projections p_1, p_2 : X ×_S X → X. Then A is f-universally locally acyclic if and only if the natural map p_1^*RHom_Λ(A, Λ) ⊗^L_Λ p_2^*A → RHom_Λ(p_1^*A, p_2^*A) is an isomorphism.
items.note: Reduction to Theorem IV.2.23 via charts, replacing Rp_2^! by p_2^* using cohomological smoothness. Used in Theorem V.7.1. Planned in node VS1/ula-for-artin-v-stacks of the VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories decomposition (accepted review, 2026-09-16; the same node is in its packet) (second sentence of its statement and second proof step).

items.name: ℓ-cohomological smoothness via ULA
items.statement: Let f : X → S be a compactifiable map of v-stacks that is representable in locally spatial diamonds with locally dim.trg f < ∞. Then f is ℓ-cohomologically smooth if and only if F_ℓ is f-universally locally acyclic and its Verdier dual Rf^!F_ℓ is invertible. Equivalently, f is ℓ-cohomologically smooth if and only if Rf^!F_ℓ is invertible and its formation commutes with any base change (F_ℓ being f-ULA iff p_1^*Rf^!F_ℓ → Rp_2^!F_ℓ is an isomorphism).
items.note: Checks [Sch17a, Definition 23.8] via Proposition IV.2.19. Key input for the Jacobian criterion and Corollary IV.2.34. Planned in node VS1/ula-dualizability-criterion of the VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories decomposition (accepted review, 2026-09-16; the same node is in its packet) through its first acceptance item and its second source excerpt, which quotes this proposition and the remark after it as 'used repeatedly downstream'.

items.name: Spd O_E → Spd F_q is ℓ-cohomologically smooth
items.statement: The map f : Spd O_E → Spd F_q is ℓ-cohomologically smooth for all ℓ ≠ p.
items.note: Resolves a question of [Sch17a]. DiamondSixOperations:S5 says 'Question 24.7 about regular integral bases is not promoted to a theorem' — this corollary answers that circle of questions for Spd O_E, so it is an unplanned downstream theorem. Proof: F_ℓ is f-ULA via f′ : Spd O_Ẽ ≅ Spd F_q[[t^{1/p^∞}]] for a totally ramified ℤ_p-extension Ẽ/E and the argument of [Sch17a, Proposition 24.3]; then Ri^!Rf^!F_ℓ = F_ℓ, j^*Rf^!F_ℓ ≅ F_ℓ(1)[2] [Sch17a, Proposition 24.5] and the triangle i_*F_ℓ → Rf^!F_ℓ → Rj_*F_ℓ(1)[2] give Rf^!F_ℓ ≅ F_ℓ(1)[2].

items.name: Formally smooth map of v-stacks
items.statement: Let f : Y → X be a map of v-stacks. Then f is formally smooth if for any affinoid perfectoid space S of characteristic p with a Zariski closed subspace S_0 ⊂ S, and any commutative diagram g_0 : S_0 → Y, h : S → X with f ∘ g_0 = h|_{S_0}, there is some étale map S′ → S containing S_0 in its image and a map g : S′ → Y such that f ∘ g = h|_{S′} and g|_{S′×_S S_0} = g_0 ∘ (S′ ×_S S_0 → S_0).
items.note: VS1 plans: "Construct formal smoothness and the Jacobian criterion of IV.3–IV.4". Key step in the Jacobian criterion Theorem IV.4.2.

items.name: Formally smooth affinoids are étale-neighbourhood retracts in balls
items.statement: Suppose Y → X is formally smooth with Y and X affinoid perfectoid. Choose a Zariski closed embedding Y ↪ B^I_X for some set I. Then there exists an étale neighborhood U → B^I_X of Y such that the closed embedding i : Y ×_{B^I_X} U ↪ U admits a retraction r : U → Y ×_{B^I_X} U, r ∘ i = Id. Thus Y/X is a retract of an (étale) neighborhood inside a ball/X.
items.locator: Chapter IV, §IV.3.1, paragraph after Definition IV.3.1, p. 130
items.note: VS1 plans: "Construct formal smoothness and the Jacobian criterion of IV.3–IV.4". Analogy with absolute neighborhood retracts [Bor67], [Dol80]; combines with Corollary IV.2.27 in IV.4.

items.name: Basic permanence properties of formal smoothness
items.statement: (i) The composite of two formally smooth morphisms is formally smooth. (ii) If Y → X is formally smooth and X′ → X is any map then Y ×_X X′ → X′ is formally smooth. (iii) Étale maps are formally smooth. (iv) For morphisms of locally spatial diamonds, formal smoothness is étale local on the source and the target.
items.locator: Chapter IV, §IV.3.2, list (i)–(iv) before Proposition IV.3.2, p. 131
items.note: VS1 plans: "Construct formal smoothness and the Jacobian criterion of IV.3–IV.4". Stated without proof.

items.name: Formally smooth maps are universally open
items.statement: Formally smooth maps are universally open.
items.note: VS1 plans: "Construct formal smoothness and the Jacobian criterion of IV.3–IV.4". Proof via the retract picture, approximation of U → B^I_X by V → B^J_X ([Sch17a, Proposition 6.4]) and openness of cohomologically smooth maps.

items.name: B, A^1 and Spd O_E are formally smooth
items.statement: The morphisms B → ∗, A^1 → ∗ and Spd O_E → ∗ are formally smooth, where B → ∗ is the v-sheaf O^+ on Perf_k and A^1 → ∗ is the v-sheaf O.
items.note: VS1 plans: "Construct formal smoothness and the Jacobian criterion of IV.3–IV.4". Uses surjectivity of R → R_0 and R^{∘∘} → R_0^{∘∘} for Zariski closed immersions (discussion after [Sch17a, Definition 5.7]), lifting untilts ξ = π + Σ π^i[r_i].

items.name: Smooth maps of analytic adic spaces give formally smooth diamonds
items.statement: If f : Y → X is a smooth morphism of analytic adic spaces over ℤ_p then f^♢ : Y^♢ → X^♢ is formally smooth.
items.note: VS1 plans: "Construct formal smoothness and the Jacobian criterion of IV.3–IV.4". Any smooth morphism is locally étale over a finite-dimensional ball.

items.name: Formally smooth surjections split étale locally
items.statement: If f : Y → X is a formally smooth and surjective map of v-stacks, then f is surjective as a map of étale stacks. Equivalently, in case X is a perfectoid space, the map f splits over an étale cover of X.
items.note: VS1 plans: "Construct formal smoothness and the Jacobian criterion of IV.3–IV.4". Uses [Sch17a, Lemma 9.5] at geometric points.

items.name: Formal smoothness is formally-smooth local on the source
items.statement: Let f : Y → X be a morphism of v-stacks. Suppose there exists a v-surjective formally smooth morphism of v-stacks g : Y′ → Y such that f ∘ g is formally smooth. Then f is formally smooth.
items.note: VS1 plans: "Construct formal smoothness and the Jacobian criterion of IV.3–IV.4". Analogue of [Sch17a, Proposition 23.13]; uses Proposition IV.3.5 and [Sch17a, Proposition 6.4].

items.name: Bun_G is formally smooth
items.statement: The stack Bun_G → ∗ is formally smooth.
items.note: VS1 plans: "Construct formal smoothness and the Jacobian criterion of IV.3–IV.4". (covers §IV.3 as a whole; not separately named in any BunG stage). Proof: pullback of E_0 to Y_{C,[1,q]} is trivial (Theorem III.2.2); [GR03, Proposition 5.4.21] (henselian-pair lifting) twice, first to trivialize on Y_{S_0,[1,q]} étale locally, then to lift the descent matrix A ∈ G(B_{R_0,[1,1]}).

items.name: Banach–Colmez spaces of positive/negative complexes are formally smooth
items.statement: Let S be a perfectoid space and let [E_1 → E_0] be a map of vector bundles on X_S such that E_0 is everywhere of positive Harder–Narasimhan slopes, and E_1 is everywhere of negative Harder–Narasimhan slopes. Then BC([E_1 → E_0]) → S is formally smooth.
items.note: VS1 plans: "Construct formal smoothness and the Jacobian criterion of IV.3–IV.4". Analogue of Proposition II.3.5 (iii); uses Corollary II.3.3, Propositions II.2.5 (iv), II.3.4 (iii), Theorem II.2.6 and Corollary IV.3.6. This result lies on p. 133, just past the nominal page range, but belongs to §IV.3.

items.name: Moduli of sections M_Z
items.statement: Let S be a perfectoid space and Z → X_S a smooth map of sous-perfectoid adic spaces. M_Z is the v-sheaf of sections of Z → X_S, sending any perfectoid space S′ → S to the set of maps X_{S′} → Z lifting X_{S′} → X_S.
items.note: VS1 description: "Construct formal smoothness and the Jacobian criterion of IV.3–IV.4 for the specified relative section functors on Fargues–Fontaine curves. Prove the tangent/cohomology calculation, the positive-slope condition and the resulting cohomological smoothness." ("relative section functors on Fargues–Fontaine curves"). No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched). Z is called quasiprojective when it is a Zariski closed subspace of an open subset of the adic space P^n_{X_S}; only then is M_Z shown to be a locally spatial diamond. Heuristic: tangent space H^0(X_{S′}, s^*T_{Z/X_S}), obstruction space H^1(X_{S′}, s^*T_{Z/X_S}).

items.name: Smooth locus M^sm_Z (Def. IV.4.1)
items.statement: Let M^sm_Z ⊂ M_Z be the open subfunctor of all sections s : X_{S′} → Z such that s^*T_{Z/X_S} has everywhere positive Harder–Narasimhan slopes.
items.note: VS1 description: "Construct formal smoothness and the Jacobian criterion of IV.3–IV.4 for the specified relative section functors on Fargues–Fontaine curves. Prove the tangent/cohomology calculation, the positive-slope condition and the resulting cohomological smoothness." ("the positive-slope condition"). T_{Z/X_S} is the tangent bundle (dual of Ω^1_{Z/X_S}, Def. IV.4.11). Openness is asserted ("open subfunctor"), relying on openness of the positive-slope locus (HN semicontinuity, Chapter II). Motivation: positive slopes give H^1 = 0 locally (Prop. II.3.4(iii)).

items.name: Jacobian criterion (Thm. IV.4.2): M_Z locally spatial and compactifiable
items.statement: Let S be a perfectoid space and let Z → X_S be a smooth map of sous-perfectoid spaces such that Z admits a Zariski closed immersion into an open subset of (the adic space) P^n_{X_S} for some n ≥ 0. Then M_Z is a locally spatial diamond, and the map M_Z → S is compactifiable.
items.note: VS1 description: "Construct formal smoothness and the Jacobian criterion of IV.3–IV.4 for the specified relative section functors on Fargues–Fontaine curves. Prove the tangent/cohomology calculation, the positive-slope condition and the resulting cohomological smoothness." Proved in Prop. IV.4.22 (locally closed in M_{P^n_{X_S}}, which is described by Prop. IV.4.21). Main application: charts on Bun_G in §V.3 (BunGAndNewtonStrata:BG4 consumes "the FS IV Jacobian theorem from VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories VS1").

items.name: Jacobian criterion (Thm. IV.4.2): M^sm_Z → S cohomologically smooth
items.statement: Let S be a perfectoid space and let Z → X_S be a smooth map of sous-perfectoid spaces such that Z admits a Zariski closed immersion into an open subset of (the adic space) P^n_{X_S} for some n ≥ 0. Then M^sm_Z → S is cohomologically smooth.
items.note: VS1 description: "Construct formal smoothness and the Jacobian criterion of IV.3–IV.4 for the specified relative section functors on Fargues–Fontaine curves. Prove the tangent/cohomology calculation, the positive-slope condition and the resulting cohomological smoothness." Described by the authors as the most profound result in the theory of diamonds so far. Proof: ULA of F_ℓ (Prop. IV.4.27) + Prop. IV.2.33 reduce to invertibility of Rf^!F_ℓ in the right degree, obtained by deformation to the normal cone (Prop. IV.4.29), using Rf^! base change (Prop. IV.2.15). Formal smoothness is Prop. IV.4.24.

items.name: Jacobian criterion (Thm. IV.4.2): dimension formula
items.statement: In the situation of Theorem IV.4.2, for a geometric point x : Spa C → M^sm_Z given by a map Spa C → S and a section s : X_C → Z, the map M^sm_Z → S is at x of ℓ-dimension equal to the degree of s^*T_{Z/X_S}.
items.note: VS1 description: "Construct formal smoothness and the Jacobian criterion of IV.3–IV.4 for the specified relative section functors on Fargues–Fontaine curves. Prove the tangent/cohomology calculation, the positive-slope condition and the resulting cohomological smoothness." ("the tangent/cohomology calculation"). Follows from Prop. IV.4.29 (t^*Rf^!F_ℓ ≅ F_ℓ[2d] étale locally, d = deg s^*T_{Z/X_S}). Remark IV.4.3: M^sm_Z → S is only locally of finite dimension (connected components of increasing dimension).

items.name: Projective-bundle hypothesis is equivalent (Rem. IV.4.6)
items.statement: One could make the a priori weaker assumption that Z admits a Zariski closed immersion inside an open subset of P(E) where E is a vector bundle on X_S. Since the result is local on S and one can suppose S affinoid perfectoid, and since when S is affinoid perfectoid O_{X_S}(1) "is ample", i.e. there is a surjection O_{X_S}(−N)^n ↠ E for N, n ≫ 0, this assumption is equivalent to the one made in Theorem IV.4.2, i.e. one can suppose E is free.
items.note: VS1 description: "Construct formal smoothness and the Jacobian criterion of IV.3–IV.4 for the specified relative section functors on Fargues–Fontaine curves. Prove the tangent/cohomology calculation, the positive-slope condition and the resulting cohomological smoothness." Ampleness input from Chapter II (Theorem II.2.6-type surjections). Remark IV.4.4 records the classical analogue (smoothness of M^sm_Z for a proper smooth curve X/k and quasi-projective smooth Z → X); Remark IV.4.5 notes the "Gromov–Witten" case Z = W ×_E X_S.

items.name: Quot diamond Quot_E (Ex. IV.4.7)
items.statement: Let E be a vector bundle on X_S. Quot_E → S denotes the moduli space over S of locally free quotients of E. Quot^sm_E ⊂ Quot_E is the open subset parametrizing quotients u : E → F such that fiberwise, the greatest slope of ker u is strictly less than the smallest slope of F. For an integer n ≥ 1, N ∈ Z and r ∈ N_{≥1}, Quot^{n,sm,◦}_{O(N)^r} is the open subset of Quot^sm_{O(N)^r} where the quotient has rank n and its slopes are greater than N.
items.note: No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched). The paper states it will not be used later (charts on Bun_G are built in §V.3 instead). Planned in node VS1/jacobian-criterion of the VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories decomposition (accepted review, 2026-09-16; the same node is in its packet) through its first acceptance item, 'Verify the Quot example IV.4.7: Quot_E^sm, the locus where the greatest slope of ker u is strictly less than the smallest slope of the quotient, is cohomologically smooth'.

items.name: Quot_E representable and compactifiable (Ex. IV.4.7)
items.statement: Fixing the rank of such a quotient, Quot_E is a finite disjoint union of spaces M_Z with Z → X_S a Grassmannian of quotients of E. Thus Quot_E → S is representable in locally spatial diamonds, compactifiable, of locally finite dim. trg.
items.note: Consequence of Theorem IV.4.2 (with Remark IV.4.6 for the Grassmannian of a non-free E). No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched). Planned in node VS1/jacobian-criterion of the VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories decomposition (accepted review, 2026-09-16; the same node is in its packet) through its first acceptance item, 'Verify the Quot example IV.4.7: Quot_E^sm, the locus where the greatest slope of ker u is strictly less than the smallest slope of the quotient, is cohomologically smooth'.

items.name: Quot^sm_E cohomologically smooth (Ex. IV.4.7)
items.statement: Quot^sm_E → S is cohomologically smooth.
items.note: Stated as a consequence of Theorem IV.4.2: the slope condition on ker u vs F is the positivity of s^*T = Hom(ker u, F). No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched). Planned in node VS1/jacobian-criterion of the VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories decomposition (accepted review, 2026-09-16; the same node is in its packet) through its first acceptance item, 'Verify the Quot example IV.4.7: Quot_E^sm, the locus where the greatest slope of ker u is strictly less than the smallest slope of the quotient, is cohomologically smooth'.

items.name: Quot charts on Bun_{GL_n} (Ex. IV.4.7)
items.statement: The morphism Quot^{n,sm,◦}_{O(N)^r} → Bun_{GL_n} given by the quotient of O(N)^r is separated cohomologically smooth. When pulled back by a morphism S → Bun_{GL_n} with S perfectoid, this is an open subset of a positive Banach–Colmez space. As N and r vary one constructs, as in the "classical case", cohomologically smooth charts on Bun_{GL_n} using Quot^{n,sm,◦}_{O(N)^r}.
items.note: Asserted without proof in an example; not used later in the paper. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: Sous-perfectoid adic space (recalled)
items.statement: An adic space X is sous-perfectoid if it is analytic and admits an open cover by U = Spa(R, R^+) where each R is a sous-perfectoid Tate algebra, meaning that there is some perfectoid R-algebra R̃ such that R → R̃ is a split injection in the category of topological R-modules.
items.note: Recalled from Hansen–Kedlaya, cf. [SW20, Section 6.3]. Planned in AdicSpacesPartII:R5 ("Construct the sousperfectoid class and its usable local affinoid descriptions"), nodes AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-ring (a complete Tate Z_p-algebra is sousperfectoid if it admits a perfectoid frame (R̃, ι, σ) with σ ∘ ι = id, i.e. R → R̃ is split in topological R-modules) and AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-adic-space (an adic space covered by Spa(R, R^+) with R sousperfectoid; such spaces are analytic). The accepted restructuring RS-05 records that "R5 owns the early sousperfectoid ambient class used by A3, BG0 and RF0". The same definition from [SW20] is planned there by the accepted extraction PAPER-SCHOLZE-WEINSTEIN-20/43. AdicEtaleGeometry:A3 and VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories:VS1 only use the class. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (declarations.tsv searched).

items.name: Stability of sous-perfectoid rings (recalled)
items.statement: The class of sous-perfectoid rings R is stable under passage to rational localizations, finite étale maps, and R⟨T_1, …, T_n⟩.
items.note: Cited input ([HK20], [SW20, §6.3]); used for Prop. IV.4.10(iii). Planned node by node in AdicSpacesPartII:R5: AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-rational-localisation (Berkeley 6.3.3(1)), AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-finite-etale (6.3.3(2)) and AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-rings (R⟨T_1, …, T_n⟩ is sousperfectoid, 6.3.3(3)). Also planned there by the accepted extraction PAPER-SCHOLZE-WEINSTEIN-20/43. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (declarations.tsv searched).

items.name: Étale maps of sous-perfectoid spaces (recalled)
items.statement: A map f : Y → X of sous-perfectoid adic spaces is étale if locally on the source and target it can be written as an open immersion followed by a finite étale map.
items.note: Recalled definition. Planned by node AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphism: "A morphism f: Y → X of analytic adic spaces is étale in A1's sense if every y ∈ Y has an open neighbourhood U ⊆ Y such that f|_U factors as U → W → V → X with j an open immersion, g finite étale and i an open immersion" (Kedlaya–Liu Definition 8.2.16), which is FS's definition for analytic (in particular sous-perfectoid) spaces. That étale spaces over a sous-perfectoid space are again sous-perfectoid is AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-etale-stability. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (declarations.tsv searched).

items.name: Smooth maps of sous-perfectoid spaces (Def. IV.4.8)
items.statement: Let f : Y → X be a map of sous-perfectoid adic spaces. Then f is smooth if one can cover Y by open subsets V ⊂ Y such that there are étale maps V → B^d_X for some integer d ≥ 0.
items.note: Planned by node AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/smooth-morphism-ball-charts ("f is locally étale over a relative ball if every y' ∈ Y' has an open neighbourhood U, an integer n ≥ 0 and a morphism g : U → B^n_Y that is étale in the local-description sense of AdicEtaleGeometry A1, with f|_U = π ∘ g. This is the notion 'smooth' of ECD Proposition 24.4 for analytic adic spaces over Spa ℤ_p, including non-noetherian ones such as spaces étale over a perfectoid or sousperfectoid base"), with the relative ball B^n_X from AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/relative-closed-polydisc. Its hypothesis (base covered by complete stably sheafy affinoids) holds for sous-perfectoid spaces (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-sheafy). No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (declarations.tsv searched).

items.name: Analytification of smooth schemes is smooth (Prop. IV.4.9)
items.statement: Let X = Spa(A, A^+) be an affinoid sous-perfectoid adic space, and let f_0 : Y_0 → Spec A be a smooth map of schemes. Let f : Y → X be the analytification of f_0 : Y_0 → Spec A, representing the functor taking Spa(B, B^+) → Spa(A, A^+) to the Spec B-valued points of Y_0 → Spec A. Then f : Y → X is smooth.
items.note: VS1 description: "Construct formal smoothness and the Jacobian criterion of IV.3–IV.4 for the specified relative section functors on Fargues–Fontaine curves. Prove the tangent/cohomology calculation, the positive-slope condition and the resulting cohomological smoothness." Proof: locally étale over affine space, whose analytification is a union of balls. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: Smooth maps: local on Y (Prop. IV.4.10 (i))
items.statement: Let f : Y → X and g : Z → Y be maps of sous-perfectoid adic spaces. The property of f being smooth is local on Y.
items.note: Planned in the API of AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/smooth-morphism-ball-charts: "AdicSpace.IsLocallyEtaleOverPolydisc.of_isOpenImmersion_comp — Local on the source: if Y' = ⋃ U_i and each f|_{U_i} satisfies it, so does f." By Prop. IV.4.18 smoothness is even étale local on Y (and smooth local on X and Y using (v)). No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (declarations.tsv searched).

items.name: Smooth maps: composition (Prop. IV.4.10 (ii))
items.statement: Let f : Y → X and g : Z → Y be maps of sous-perfectoid adic spaces. If f and g are smooth, then so is f ∘ g : Z → X.
items.note: Planned in the API of AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/smooth-morphism-ball-charts: "AdicSpace.IsLocallyEtaleOverPolydisc.comp — Stable under composition (with B^{m+n}_Y ≅ B^m_Y ×_Y B^n_Y)", with the same proof as FS (swap the middle étale map and ball projection). No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (declarations.tsv searched).

items.name: Smooth maps: base change (Prop. IV.4.10 (iii))
items.statement: Let f : Y → X and g : Z → Y be maps of sous-perfectoid adic spaces. If h : X′ → X is any map of sous-perfectoid adic spaces and f is smooth, then the fibre product Y′ = Y ×_X X′ in adic spaces exists, is sous-perfectoid, and f′ : Y′ → X′ is smooth.
items.note: Base change of the class is the API entry AdicSpace.IsLocallyEtaleOverPolydisc.baseChange of AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/smooth-morphism-ball-charts ("Stable under base change along morphisms Y₁ → Y of the same kind"; fibre products exist by AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-products-existence). That the fibre product is again sous-perfectoid is AdicSpacesPartII:R5 (R5/sousperfectoid-rings for relative balls, R5/sousperfectoid-etale-stability for étale maps). No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (declarations.tsv searched).

items.name: Smooth maps: universally open (Prop. IV.4.10 (iv))
items.statement: Let f : Y → X and g : Z → Y be maps of sous-perfectoid adic spaces. If f is smooth, then f is universally open.
items.note: VS1 description: "Construct formal smoothness and the Jacobian criterion of IV.3–IV.4 for the specified relative section functors on Fargues–Fontaine curves. Prove the tangent/cohomology calculation, the positive-slope condition and the resulting cohomological smoothness." No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: Smooth maps: étale-local sections (Prop. IV.4.10 (v))
items.statement: Let f : Y → X and g : Z → Y be maps of sous-perfectoid adic spaces. If f is smooth and surjective, then there is some étale cover X′ → X with a lift X′ → Y.
items.note: VS1 description: "Construct formal smoothness and the Jacobian criterion of IV.3–IV.4 for the specified relative section functors on Fargues–Fontaine curves. Prove the tangent/cohomology calculation, the positive-slope condition and the resulting cohomological smoothness." Proof of (v) uses [Sch17a, Lemma 9.5] and approximation of geometric points by affinoid étale neighbourhoods. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: Vector bundles on sous-perfectoid spaces (recalled)
items.statement: If Y is sous-perfectoid, then one can define a stack (for the étale topology) of vector bundles on Y, such that for Y = Spa(R, R^+) affinoid with R sous-perfectoid, the category of vector bundles is equivalent to the category of finite projective R-modules. By definition, a vector bundle on Y is an O_Y-module that is locally free of finite rank.
items.note: Cited input: [KL15], [SW20, Theorem 5.2.8, Proposition 6.3.4]. Planned by AdicSpacesPartII:R3/locally-free-sheaf (vector bundles as locally free O_X-modules of finite rank), AdicSpacesPartII:R3/sheafy-tate-acyclicity-and-kiehl-gluing (finite projective modules = vector bundles on sheafy affinoids, analytic topology), and for the étale topology AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-stably-adic with AdicSpacesPartII:R5/stable-basis-etale-vector-bundles ("finite projective R-modules are equivalent to finite locally free O_{X_ét}-modules" for R sousperfectoid, holding on every sousperfectoid affinoid open). The accepted extractions PAPER-SCHOLZE-WEINSTEIN-20/33 and PAPER-KEDLAYA-LIU-15/265 plan the cited inputs at the same layers. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (declarations.tsv searched).

items.name: Kähler differentials Ω^1_{Y/X} (Def. IV.4.11)
items.statement: Let f : Y → X be a smooth map of sous-perfectoid adic spaces, with diagonal Δ_f : Y → Y ×_X Y. Let I_{Y/X} ⊂ O_{Y×_X Y} be the ideal sheaf. Then Ω^1_{Y/X} := I_{Y/X}/I^2_{Y/X}, considered as O_{Y×_X Y}/I_{Y/X} = O_Y-module. There is a canonical O_X-linear derivation d : O_Y → Ω^1_{Y/X}, given by g ↦ g ⊗ 1 − 1 ⊗ g.
items.note: VS1 description: "Construct formal smoothness and the Jacobian criterion of IV.3–IV.4 for the specified relative section functors on Fargues–Fontaine curves. Prove the tangent/cohomology calculation, the positive-slope condition and the resulting cohomological smoothness." Mathlib has algebraic KaehlerDifferential, but not this adic (completed, diagonal-ideal) version on sous-perfectoid spaces; AdicEtaleGeometry:A2 plans "continuous Kähler differentials in the finite-presentation setting" only. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: Ω^1 is a vector bundle; dimension decomposition (Prop. IV.4.12)
items.statement: Let f : Y → X be a smooth map of sous-perfectoid adic spaces. Then Ω^1_{Y/X} is a vector bundle on Y. There is a unique open and closed decomposition Y = Y_0 ⊔ Y_1 ⊔ … ⊔ Y_n such that Ω^1_{Y/X}|_{Y_d} is of rank d for all d = 0, …, n. In that case, for any nonempty open subset V ⊂ Y_d with an étale map V → B^{d′}_X, necessarily d′ = d.
items.note: VS1 description: "Construct formal smoothness and the Jacobian criterion of IV.3–IV.4 for the specified relative section functors on Fargues–Fontaine curves. Prove the tangent/cohomology calculation, the positive-slope condition and the resulting cohomological smoothness." Proof reduces to Y étale over B^d_X, where the diagonal ideal is generated by the regular sequence (T_i^{(1)} − T_i^{(2)}) (Lemma IV.4.13). No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: Smooth of dimension d
items.statement: f is smooth of dimension d if Ω^1_{Y/X} is of rank d. By Proposition IV.4.12, this is equivalent to asking that Y can be covered by open subsets V that admit étale maps V → B^d_X. In particular, f is smooth of dimension 0 if and only if it is étale.
items.locator: Chapter IV, §IV.4.1, after Proposition IV.4.12, p. 137
items.note: VS1 description: "Construct formal smoothness and the Jacobian criterion of IV.3–IV.4 for the specified relative section functors on Fargues–Fontaine curves. Prove the tangent/cohomology calculation, the positive-slope condition and the resulting cohomological smoothness." No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: Coordinates form a regular sequence (Lem. IV.4.13)
items.statement: Let X = Spa(R⟨T_1, …, T_n⟩, R^+⟨T_1, …, T_n⟩) where R is a sous-perfectoid Tate ring, let Y = Spa(S, S^+) where S is a sous-perfectoid Tate ring, and let f : Y → X be a smooth map. Then T_1, …, T_n define a regular sequence on S and (T_1, …, T_n)S ⊂ S is a closed ideal.
items.note: AdicEtaleGeometry:A3 plans only a special case: "Prove the characteristic-p specialization of the local assertions used from FS IV.4.13, IV.4.15, IV.4.17 and IV.4.19 by analytic algebra and pseudocoherent gluing". Proof: reduce to n = 1 and f étale; spreading out of étale maps over X′ = Spa(R⟨T′⟩, R^+⟨T′⟩), T′ = ϖ^nT. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: Smooth spaces are balls near a section (Lem. IV.4.14)
items.statement: Let f : Y → X be a smooth map of sous-perfectoid spaces with a section s : Spa(K, K^+) → Y for some point Spa(K, K^+) → X. Then there are open neighborhoods U ⊂ X of Spa(K, K^+) and V ⊂ Y of s(Spa(K, K^+)) such that V ≅ B^d_U.
items.note: VS1 description: "Construct formal smoothness and the Jacobian criterion of IV.3–IV.4 for the specified relative section functors on Fargues–Fontaine curves. Prove the tangent/cohomology calculation, the positive-slope condition and the resulting cohomological smoothness." Uses [Sch17a, Lemma 15.6, Lemma 12.17] for the étale case. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: Relative cotangent sequence (Prop. IV.4.15 (i))
items.statement: Let f_i : Y_i → X, i = 1, 2, be smooth maps of sous-perfectoid adic spaces, and let g : Y_1 → Y_2 be a map over X. If g is smooth, then the sequence 0 → g^*Ω^1_{Y_2/X} → Ω^1_{Y_1/X} → Ω^1_{Y_1/Y_2} → 0 is exact.
items.note: AdicEtaleGeometry:A3 plans only a special case: "Prove the characteristic-p specialization of the local assertions used from FS IV.4.13, IV.4.15, IV.4.17 and IV.4.19 by analytic algebra and pseudocoherent gluing". No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: Differential criterion for smoothness (Prop. IV.4.15 (ii))
items.statement: Let f_i : Y_i → X, i = 1, 2, be smooth maps of sous-perfectoid adic spaces, and let g : Y_1 → Y_2 be a map over X. If g^*Ω^1_{Y_2/X} → Ω^1_{Y_1/X} is a locally split injection, then g is smooth. In particular, if g^*Ω^1_{Y_2/X} → Ω^1_{Y_1/X} is an isomorphism, then g is étale.
items.note: AdicEtaleGeometry:A3 plans only a special case: "Prove the characteristic-p specialization of the local assertions used from FS IV.4.13, IV.4.15, IV.4.17 and IV.4.19 by analytic algebra and pseudocoherent gluing". Proof uses [Hub96, Proposition 1.6.9 (iii)] on fibres, [Sch17a, Lemma 12.17] to spread out, Lemma IV.4.14 and Lemma IV.4.16. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: Spreading out isomorphisms from a fibre (Lem. IV.4.16)
items.statement: Let X = Spa(A, A^+) be a sous-perfectoid affinoid adic space with a point X′ = Spa(K, K^+) → X. Let f_1, …, f_n ∈ A^+⟨T_1, …, T_n⟩ be functions such that K → K⟨T_1, …, T_n⟩/(f_1, …, f_n) is an isomorphism. Then, after replacing X by an open neighborhood of X′, the map A → A⟨T_1, …, T_n⟩/(f_1, …, f_n) is an isomorphism.
items.note: VS1 description: "Construct formal smoothness and the Jacobian criterion of IV.3–IV.4 for the specified relative section functors on Fargues–Fontaine curves. Prove the tangent/cohomology calculation, the positive-slope condition and the resulting cohomological smoothness." Proof shows the stronger claim that A → Kos(A⟨T_1, …, T_n⟩, (f_i)_{i=1}^n) is a quasi-isomorphism after shrinking, by descent to strictly totally disconnected X and reduction mod ϖ. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: Jacobian criterion for sous-perfectoid spaces (Prop. IV.4.17)
items.statement: Let f : Y → X be a smooth map of sous-perfectoid adic spaces, and let f_1, …, f_r ∈ O_Y(Y) be global functions such that df_1, …, df_r ∈ Ω^1_{Y/X}(Y) can locally be extended to a basis of Ω^1_{Y/X}. Then Z = V(f_1, …, f_r) ⊂ Y is a sous-perfectoid space smooth over X.

Prove the tangent/cohomology calculation, the positive-slope condition and the resulting cohomological smoothness." items.name: Smoothness is étale local on the source (Prop. IV.4.18)
items.statement: Let f : Y → X be a map of sous-perfectoid adic spaces. Assume that there is some étale cover j : V → Y such that f ∘ j is smooth. Then f is smooth.
items.note: VS1 description: "Construct formal smoothness and the Jacobian criterion of IV.3–IV.4 for the specified relative section functors on Fargues–Fontaine curves. Prove the tangent/cohomology calculation, the positive-slope condition and the resulting cohomological smoothness." Proof uses étale descent of vector bundles, [Hub96, 1.6.2] on fibres, Prop. IV.4.15, and [Sch17a, Lemma 15.6, Proposition 11.30]. items.name: Zariski closed immersions between smooth spaces (Prop. IV.4.19)
items.statement: Let f : Y → X, f′ : Y′ → X be smooth maps of sous-perfectoid adic spaces, and let g : Y → Y′ be a map over X. The following conditions are equivalent. (i) There is a cover of Y′ by open affinoid V′ = Spa(S′, S′^+) such that V = Y ×_{Y′} V′ = Spa(S, S^+) is affinoid and S′ → S is surjective, with S^+ ⊂ S the integral closure of the image of S′^+. (ii) For any open affinoid V′ = Spa(S′, S′^+) ⊂ Y′, the preimage V = Y ×_{Y′} V′ = Spa(S, S^+) is affinoid and S′ → S is surjective, with S^+ ⊂ S the integral closure of the image of S′^+.
items.note: AdicEtaleGeometry:A3 plans only a special case: "Prove the characteristic-p specialization of the local assertions used from FS IV.4.13, IV.4.15, IV.4.17 and IV.4.19 by analytic algebra and pseudocoherent gluing". A3 also notes that ECD Prop. 6.4(iv) cites FS IV.4.19. Proof uses gluing of pseudocoherent modules [KL16]. items.name: Ideal of a Zariski closed immersion (Prop. IV.4.19, moreover)
items.statement: In the situation of Proposition IV.4.19, when the equivalent conditions hold, the ideal sheaf I_{Y⊂Y′} ⊂ O_{Y′} is pseudocoherent in the sense of [KL16], and locally generated by sections f_1, …, f_r ∈ O_{Y′} such that df_1, …, df_r ∈ Ω^1_{Y′/X} can locally be extended to a basis.

(A3 task 2: "locally finite generation by as many equations as ball variables, with invertible Jacobian"; task 3: "Prove that this ideal sheaf is the sheaf of a pseudocoherent module"). items.name: Zariski closed immersion (Def. IV.4.20)
items.statement: In the setup of Proposition IV.4.19, the map g is a Zariski closed immersion if the equivalent conditions are satisfied.

items.name: Maps X_S → P^n: representability (Prop. IV.4.21)
items.statement: Let n ≥ 0 and consider the small v-sheaf M_{P^n} taking any perfectoid space S to the set of maps X_S → P^n_E. Then M_{P^n} → ∗ is partially proper and representable in locally spatial diamonds.

Prove the tangent/cohomology calculation, the positive-slope condition and the resulting cohomological smoothness." items.name: Maps X_S → P^n: degree decomposition (Prop. IV.4.21)
items.statement: M_{P^n} admits a decomposition into open and closed subspaces M_{P^n} = ⊔_{m≥0} M^m_{P^n} such that each M^m_{P^n} → ∗ has finite dim. trg, and the degree of the pullback of O_{P^n}(1) to X_{M^m_{P^n}} is m.
items.note: VS1 description: "Construct formal smoothness and the Jacobian criterion of IV.3–IV.4 for the specified relative section functors on Fargues–Fontaine curves. Prove the tangent/cohomology calculation, the positive-slope condition and the resulting cohomological smoothness." The proof decomposes by all m ∈ Z; negative m contribute nothing since n+1 sections without common zeroes are needed. Uses closedness of |X_S| → |S| (proof of Lemma IV.1.20). No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: Maps X_S → P^n: open immersion into projectivized BC (Prop. IV.4.21)
items.statement: There is a canonical open immersion M^m_{P^n} ↪ (BC(O(m)^{n+1}) \ {0})/E^×, where E^× is the locally profinite group (underlined E^× in the text).
items.note: VS1 description: "Construct formal smoothness and the Jacobian criterion of IV.3–IV.4 for the specified relative section functors on Fargues–Fontaine curves. Prove the tangent/cohomology calculation, the positive-slope condition and the resulting cohomological smoothness." Trivialising L ≅ O_{X_S}(m) is an E^×-torsor; then one parametrizes n+1 sections without common zeroes, an open condition. Uses Banach–Colmez spaces of Chapter II. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: M_Z → M_{P^n_{X_S}} locally closed (Prop. IV.4.22)
items.statement: Let S be a perfectoid space and let Z → X_S be a smooth map of sous-perfectoid adic spaces such that Z admits a Zariski closed embedding into an open subspace of P^n_{X_S}. Then the induced functor M_Z → M_{P^n_{X_S}} is locally closed. More precisely, for any perfectoid space T → M_{P^n_{X_S}}, the preimage of M_Z is representable by some perfectoid space T_Z ⊂ T that is étale locally Zariski closed in T, i.e. there is some étale cover of T by affinoid perfectoid T′ = Spa(R, R^+) → T such that T_Z ×_T T′ = Spa(R_Z, R_Z^+) is affinoid perfectoid, with R → R_Z surjective and R_Z^+ ⊂ R_Z the integral closure of the image of R^+.
items.note: VS1 description: "Construct formal smoothness and the Jacobian criterion of IV.3–IV.4 for the specified relative section functors on Fargues–Fontaine curves. Prove the tangent/cohomology calculation, the positive-slope condition and the resulting cohomological smoothness." Proof: open locus where the section lands in W, local trivialisation of O(1) on Y_{S,[1,q]} (Cor. II.1.12, B_{C,[1,q]} a PID), embedding Z_{[1,q]} ↪ B^{n+1}_{Y_{S,[1,q]}}, then Lemma IV.4.23. items.name: M_Z → S representable and compactifiable (Prop. IV.4.22)
items.statement: In the situation of Proposition IV.4.22, the map M_Z → S is representable in locally spatial diamonds and compactifiable, of locally finite dim. trg.

items.name: Vanishing locus of functions on Y_{S,I} (Lem. IV.4.23)
items.statement: Let S = Spa(R, R^+) ∈ Perf_{F_q} be affinoid perfectoid with a fixed pseudouniformizer ϖ, I ⊂ (0, ∞) a compact interval with rational ends, and Z ⊂ |Y_{S,I}| a closed subset defined by the vanishing locus of an ideal J ⊂ O(Y_{S,I}). Then, via the open projection υ : |Y_{S,I}| → |S|, the closed subset |S| \ υ(|Y_{S,I}| \ Z) is Zariski closed. The corresponding Zariski closed perfectoid subspace of S is universal for perfectoid spaces T → S such that J ↦ 0 via O(Y_{S,I}) → O(Y_{T,I}).
items.note: VS1 description: "Construct formal smoothness and the Jacobian criterion of IV.3–IV.4 for the specified relative section functors on Fargues–Fontaine curves. Prove the tangent/cohomology calculation, the positive-slope condition and the resulting cohomological smoothness." Proof: υ open since Y^♢_{S,I} → S is cohomologically smooth; intersect Zariski closed loci (Prop. II.0.2) over untilts; a function vanishing at infinitely many untilts in a fibre vanishes (Cor. II.1.12); uniformity of sous-perfectoid rings. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: M^sm_Z → S formally smooth (Prop. IV.4.24)
items.statement: Let S = Spa(R, R^+) be an affinoid perfectoid space over F_q and let Z → X_S be a smooth map of sous-perfectoid adic spaces that is Zariski closed in an open subspace of P^n_{X_S}. Then M^sm_Z → S is formally smooth.
items.note: VS1 description: "Construct formal smoothness and the Jacobian criterion of IV.3–IV.4 for the specified relative section functors on Fargues–Fontaine curves. Prove the tangent/cohomology calculation, the positive-slope condition and the resulting cohomological smoothness." ("Construct formal smoothness ... of IV.3–IV.4"). Formal smoothness in the sense of Definition IV.3.1 (extension of sections across Zariski closed S_0 ⊂ S up to étale localization). Proof: local coordinates Z_{[1,q]} ⊃ (π^N B)^r, gluing power series α_i normalised to a standard isocrystal of negative slopes, then an iterative correction T_i ↦ T_i + ε_i converging by the quantitative Lemma IV.4.25. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: Quantitative H^1-vanishing for positive slopes (Lem. IV.4.25)
items.statement: Fix a standard Dieudonné module of negative slopes, given explicitly on a basis e_1, …, e_r by fixing cycles 1, …, r_1; r_1 + 1, …, r_2; …; r_{a−1} + 1, …, r_a = r and positive integers d_1, …, d_a > 0, via φ(e_i) = e_{i+1} for i ≠ r_j, φ(e_{r_j}) = π^{−d_j} e_{r_{j−1}+1} (so that the associated vector bundle on X_S has positive slopes). Then there is an integer c ≥ 0 with the following property. Let S = Spa(R, R^+) be an affinoid perfectoid space over F_q with Zariski closed subspace S_0 = Spa(R_0, R_0^+), and a pseudouniformizer ϖ ∈ R. Let I^+_{[1,q]} = ker(B^+_{(R,R^+),[1,q]} → B^+_{(R_0,R_0^+),[1,q]}), I^+_{[1,1]} = ker(B^+_{(R,R^+),[1,1]} → B^+_{(R_0,R_0^+),[1,1]}). Then for all f_1, …, f_r ∈ I^+_{[1,1]} one can find g_1, …, g_r ∈ π^{−c} I^+_{[1,q]} such that f_i = φ(g_i) − g_{i+1} for i ≠ r_j, and f_{r_j} = φ(g_{r_j}) − π^{d_j} g_{r_{j−1}+1}.
items.note: VS1 description: "Construct formal smoothness and the Jacobian criterion of IV.3–IV.4 for the specified relative section functors on Fargues–Fontaine curves. Prove the tangent/cohomology calculation, the positive-slope condition and the resulting cohomological smoothness." The printed equation reads f_{r_j} = φ(g_{r_j}) − π^{−d_j} g_{r_{j−1}+1}; with FS's convention H^0(X_S, O(1)) = H^0(Y_S, O)^{φ=π} that is the H^1 equation of a bundle of negative slopes, and the printed statement fails (see the sign finding on Lemmas IV.4.25–IV.4.26 in this review); the statement above uses the corrected sign π^{d_j}, i.e. the H^1 of the positive-slope bundle attached to the Dieudonné module. The constant c depends only on the Dieudonné module, uniformly in (S, S_0, ϖ). Proof: reduce to a = 1, then r = 1 (unramified extension of degree r), then a product-of-counterexamples argument with R^+ = ∏ R_i^+ reducing to the qualitative Lemma IV.4.26. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (declarations.tsv searched).

items.name: Surjectivity of φ − π^{d} on kernels (Lem. IV.4.26)
items.statement: Let d be a positive integer, let S_0 = Spa(R_0, R_0^+) ⊂ S = Spa(R, R^+) be a Zariski closed immersion of affinoid perfectoid spaces over F_q, and let ϖ ∈ R be a pseudouniformizer. Let I_{[1,q]} = ker(B_{R,[1,q]} → B_{R_0,[1,q]}), I_{[1,1]} = ker(B_{R,[1,1]} → B_{R_0,[1,1]}). Then the map φ − π^{d} : I_{[1,q]} → I_{[1,1]} is surjective.
items.note: VS1 description: "Construct formal smoothness and the Jacobian criterion of IV.3–IV.4 for the specified relative section functors on Fargues–Fontaine curves. Prove the tangent/cohomology calculation, the positive-slope condition and the resulting cohomological smoothness." The paper prints φ − π^{−d}, which is false (its kernel and cokernel on B are H^0 and H^1 of O(−d)); the statement above is the corrected one that the printed proof proves (see the sign finding in this review). Proof: by the snake lemma and H^1(X_S, O_{X_S}(d)) = 0 (Prop. II.2.5(iii)) it is equivalent to surjectivity of H^0(X_S, O_{X_S}(d)) → H^0(X_{S_0}, O_{X_{S_0}}(d)); for d ≤ [E : Q_p] via Prop. II.2.5(iv) and R^{◦◦} ↠ R_0^{◦◦}, in general by induction using 0 → O(d−2) → O(d−1)^2 → O(d) → 0 (E ≠ Q_p) and a finite extension trick for E = Q_p. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (declarations.tsv searched).

items.name: F_ℓ is ULA for M^sm_Z → S (Prop. IV.4.27)
items.statement: Let S be a perfectoid space and let Z → X_S be a smooth map of sous-perfectoid spaces such that Z is Zariski closed inside an open subset of P^n_{X_S} for some n ≥ 0. Then, for any ℓ ≠ p, the sheaf F_ℓ is universally locally acyclic for the map M^sm_Z → S.
items.note: VS1 description: "Construct formal smoothness and the Jacobian criterion of IV.3–IV.4 for the specified relative section functors on Fargues–Fontaine curves. Prove the tangent/cohomology calculation, the positive-slope condition and the resulting cohomological smoothness." Proof: cover M_Z by T_0 → M_Z (from Lemma IV.4.28) that are Zariski closed in spaces étale over a perfectoid ball B̃^n_S; formal smoothness (Prop. IV.4.24) makes T_0 a retract of a space étale over a perfectoid ball; conclude by Corollary IV.2.27. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: Perfectoid covers of projectivized Banach–Colmez spaces (Lem. IV.4.28)
items.statement: Let S be a perfectoid space over F_q and let E be a vector bundle on X_S that is everywhere of nonnegative Harder–Narasimhan slopes. There is a perfectoid space T → S that is locally Zariski closed in a perfectoid ball B̃^n_S over S and that admits a surjective map T → (BC(E) \ {0})/E^× over S that is separated, representable in locally spatial diamonds, cohomologically smooth, and formally smooth.
items.note: VS1 description: "Construct formal smoothness and the Jacobian criterion of IV.3–IV.4 for the specified relative section functors on Fargues–Fontaine curves. Prove the tangent/cohomology calculation, the positive-slope condition and the resulting cohomological smoothness." E^× is underlined (locally profinite). Proof: add an injection L ↪ O_{X_S}(1) (Prop. II.3.5, Prop. IV.3.8), sections of E(1) vanishing at the untilt S^♯ (Zariski closed by [BS22, Theorem 7.4, Remark 7.5]), reduction to BC(E(1)) × Spd E, and [∗/O_E^×] via BC(O(1)) and 0 → O → O(1/2) → O(1) → 0 (Prop. II.3.4). No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: Dualizing complex along a section (Prop. IV.4.29)
items.statement: Let S be a perfectoid space and let Z → X_S be a smooth map of sous-perfectoid spaces such that Z admits a Zariski closed immersion into an open subset of (the adic space) P^n_{X_S} for some n ≥ 0. Let f : M_Z → S be the moduli space of sections of Z → X_S. Moreover, let s : X_S → Z be a section such that s^*T_{Z/X_S} is everywhere of positive Harder–Narasimhan slopes, and of degree d. Let t : S → M_Z be the section of f corresponding to s. Then t^*Rf^!F_ℓ is étale locally on S isomorphic to F_ℓ[2d].
items.note: VS1 description: "Construct formal smoothness and the Jacobian criterion of IV.3–IV.4 for the specified relative section functors on Fargues–Fontaine curves. Prove the tangent/cohomology calculation, the positive-slope condition and the resulting cohomological smoothness." Proof by deformation to the normal cone: family Z′ → X_{S′} over S′ = S × (N_{≥N} ∪ {∞}) with generic fibres Z^{(n)} and special fibre an open of BC(s^*T_{Z/X_S}); ULA (Prop. IV.4.27), constructibility and [Sch17a, Prop. 20.7], Verdier duality (Cor. IV.2.25), [Sch17a, Prop. 14.9]. Completes the proof of Theorem IV.4.2. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: Deformation to the normal cone family Z′ → X_{S′}
items.statement: With S strictly totally disconnected and local coordinates π^N B^r_{Y_{S,[1,q]}} ⊂ Z_{[1,q]} ⊂ B^r_{Y_{S,[1,q]}} with gluing power series α_i as in the proof of Proposition IV.4.24 (constant coefficients zero), defining a map φ : π^d B^r_{Y_{S,[1,1]}} → B^r_{Y_{S,[q,q]}} preserving the origin (d the maximum of the d_j), for n ≥ N, d set Z^{(n)}_{[1,q]} = π^n B^r_{Y_{S,[1,q]}} ∪ φ(π^n B^r_{Y_{S,[1,1]}}) ⊂ Z_{[1,q]}, descending to an open Z^{(n)} ⊂ Z, with rescaled gluing α_i^{(n)} = π^{−n} α_i(π^n T_1, …, π^n T_r) in the coordinates T_i^{(n)} = π^{−n} T_i; the limit α_i^{(∞)} = lim_{n→∞} α_i^{(n)} ∈ B_{R,[1,1]}⟨T_1, …, T_r⟩ exists and is linear in the T_i. Let S′ = S × (N_{≥N} ∪ {∞}) and let Z′ → X_{S′} be the smooth map of sous-perfectoid spaces obtained by descending Z′_{[1,q]} = B^r_{Y_{S′,[1,q]}} ∪ φ′(B^r_{Y_{S′,[1,1]}}) along the isomorphism φ′ given by α′_i = (α_i^{(N)}, α_i^{(N+1)}, …, α_i^{(∞)}) ∈ B_{R′,[1,1]}⟨T_1, …, T_r⟩. Then the fibre of Z′ → X_{S′} over S × {n} is Z^{(n)}, its fibre Z^{(∞)} over S × {∞} is an open subset of the total space over X_S of the vector bundle s^*T_{Z/X_S} (the gluing α^{(∞)} being linear), so that M_{Z^{(∞)}} is an open subset of the Banach–Colmez space BC(s^*T_{Z/X_S}), and the shift S × {n+1} ≅ S × {n} gives an isomorphism γ : S′^{(>N)} → S′ lifting to an open immersion γ : Z′^{(>N)} = Z′ ×_{X_{S′}} X_{S′^{(>N)}} ↪ Z′.

items.name: Partially compactly supported cohomology of the punctured disc (Lem. IV.5.1)
items.statement: Let C be a complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean field with pseudouniformizer ϖ ∈ C. Let Spa Z((t)) ×_Z Spa C = D^∗_C be the punctured open unit disc over C, and consider the subsets j : U = {|t| ≤ |ϖ|} ↪ D^∗_C, j′ : U′ = {|t| ≥ |ϖ|} ↪ D^∗_C. Then the partially compactly supported cohomology groups RΓ(D^∗_C, j_!Λ) = 0 = RΓ(D^∗_C, j′_!Λ) vanish. Here Λ is any coefficient ring killed by an integer n prime to p.

Lambda) = 0 = RGamma(D^*_C, j'_! Lambda) on the punctured open unit disc"; acceptance: "Verify Lemma IV.5.1 directly for the annulus and the algebraic P^1 comparison"; source locator "Lemma IV.5.1 and proof, printed p. 152"). Proof: triangle (kj)_!Λ → Rk_∗j_!Λ → i_∗A with A = lim RΓ(U_n, Λ) (H^0 = Λ, H^1 = Λ(−1); the paper prints Λ(1)), comparison with P^1_C \ {0, ∞} and algebraic comparison theorems.
