items.name: Opens U_{a,b}, U_a, U_b ⊂ X × S
items.statement: Fix an algebraically closed field k|F_q and work on Perf_k. Let X be a spatial diamond such that f : X → ∗ = Spd k is partially proper with dim. trg f < ∞, and S a spatial diamond. Pick quasi-pro-étale and universally open surjections X̃ → X and S̃ → S from affinoid perfectoid spaces, and maps X̃ → Spa k((t)), S̃ → Spa k((u)) (choices of pseudouniformizers). Let Ũ_{a,b} ⊂ X̃ × S̃ be the preimage of the affinoid {|u|^b ≤ |t| ≤ |u|^a} ⊂ Spa k((t)) × Spa k((u)) (for rational 0 < a ≤ b < ∞) and U_{a,b} ⊂ X × S its image, a qcqs open subset. The doubly indexed ind-system {U_{a,b}}_{0<a≤b<∞} is independent of all choices made. Let U_a = ⋃_{b<∞} U_{a,b} (so that U_a is the image of {|t| ≤ |u|^a}), U_b = ⋃_{a>0} U_{a,b}, with open immersions j_{a,b} : U_{a,b} → X × S, j_a : U_a → X × S, j_b : U_b → X × S.
items.note: VS0 description: "Construct partial compact-support functors of FS IV.5 for stacks whose structural map is not in the original representable ECD class. Prove independence of presentation, adjunctions and base-change formulas in their actual scope." Scope differs: VS0 targets stacks, FS IV.5 treats X × S for a partially proper spatial X over Spd k. The printed inequality {|t|^b ≤ |u| ≤ |t|^a} is inconsistent with p. 152 and p. 155 (PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E30); the convention used in the proof is U_a = {|t| ≤ |u|^a}. Uses [Sch17a, Proposition 11.24]. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: Partially compactly supported pushforwards Rβ_{!+}, Rβ_{!−} (Def. IV.5.2)
items.statement: The functors Rβ_{!+}, Rβ_{!−} : D_ét(X × S, Λ) → D_ét(S, Λ) are defined by Rβ_{!+}C := lim_{→a} Rβ_∗(j_{a!}C|_{U_a}), Rβ_{!−}C := lim_{→b} Rβ_∗(j_{b!}C|_{U_b}) for C ∈ D_ét(X × S, Λ), where β : X × S → S is the projection, Λ is a coefficient ring killed by some integer n prime to p, and the transition maps are given by (Rβ_∗ applied to) the counits of the adjunction between j_{a,a′!} and j^∗_{a,a′}, where j_{a,a′} : U_a ⊂ U_{a′} is the open immersion. As the ind-systems of U_a and U_b are independent of all choices, these functors are canonical.
items.note: VS0 description: "Construct partial compact-support functors of FS IV.5 for stacks whose structural map is not in the original representable ECD class. Prove independence of presentation, adjunctions and base-change formulas in their actual scope." (scope: FS applies it to X × S, not general stacks). Used in Chapter IX (Hecke operators / partial support; HeckeStacksAndLocalShtukas:HS1 mentions "the partial-support or relative-homology operation specified by FS IX.2"). No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: Vanishing of partially compactly supported cohomology (Thm. IV.5.3)
items.statement: Fix an algebraically closed field k|F_q and work on Perf_k; let Λ be a coefficient ring killed by an integer n prime to p. Let X be a spatial diamond with f : X → Spd k partially proper and dim. trg f < ∞, let S be a spatial diamond, and let α : X × S → X and β : X × S → S be the two projections, with Rβ_{!+}, Rβ_{!−} as in Definition IV.5.2. Assume that C = α^∗A ⊗^L_Λ β^∗B for A ∈ D_ét(X, Λ) and B ∈ D_ét(S, Λ). Then Rβ_{!+}C = 0 = Rβ_{!−}C.
items.note: Planned by packet node VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories:VS0/partial-compactly-supported-vanishing (title "FS IV.5: partially compactly supported cohomology towards one end vanishes"; statement "If C = alpha^* A tensor^L_Lambda beta^* B ... then Rbeta_{!+} C = 0 = Rbeta_{!-} C"; source "Theorem IV.5.3, printed p. 153"). Remark IV.5.4: the essential case is B = Λ. Proof: hypercover by partially proper affinoid perfectoid X_i (Huber compactifications) and [Sch17a, Theorem 19.2, Proposition 17.3, 17.6, 22.11], reduce to X = Spa K (K the completed algebraic closure of k((t))), then to S a rank-1 geometric point and B = Λ, then to Lemma IV.5.1. Input to Proposition IV.6.6 (hyperbolic localization). The introduction's version (Theorem I.5.2) is planned at the same node. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (declarations.tsv searched).

items.name: G_m-action and fixed points (§IV.6 setup)
items.statement: Let S be a small v-stack, and let f : X → S be proper and representable in spatial diamonds with dim. trg f < ∞, and assume that there is a G_m-action on X/S, where G_m is the v-sheaf sending Spa(R, R^+) to R^×. The fixed point space X^0 := X^{G_m} ⊂ X defines a closed subfunctor. (A^1)^+ (resp. (A^1)^−) denotes the affine line Spa(R, R^+) ↦ R with the natural G_m-action (resp. its inverse).
items.note: VS1 description: "Construct attractor/repeller correspondences, hyperbolic localization and the comparison map of FS IV.6, including equivariance and boundedness hypotheses. Prove its compatibility with base change and duality." Closedness of X^0 is asserted without proof. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: Hypothesis IV.6.1 (attractor/repeller decomposition)
items.statement: There is a decomposition of X^0 into open and closed subsets X^0_1, …, X^0_n such that for each i = 1, …, n, there are locally closed G_m-stable subfunctors X^+_i, X^−_i ⊂ X with X^0 ∩ X^+_i = X^0_i (resp. X^0 ∩ X^−_i = X^0_i) such that the G_m-action on X^+_i (resp. X^−_i) extends to a G_m-equivariant map (A^1)^+ × X^+_i → X^+_i (resp. (A^1)^− × X^−_i → X^−_i), and such that X = ⋃_{i=1}^n X^+_i = ⋃_{i=1}^n X^−_i.
items.note: VS1 description: "Construct attractor/repeller correspondences, hyperbolic localization and the comparison map of FS IV.6, including equivariance and boundedness hypotheses. Prove its compatibility with base change and duality." No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: Attractor/repeller X^± and maps q^±, i^±, p^±
items.statement: Let X^+ = ⊔_{i=1}^n X^+_i, X^− = ⊔_{i=1}^n X^−_i, with natural maps q^+ : X^+ → X, q^− : X^− → X, closed immersions i^+ : X^0 → X^+, i^− : X^0 → X^−, and projections p^+ : X^+ → X^0, p^− : X^− → X^0; here p^+ is given by the restriction of (A^1)^+ × X^+_i → X^+_i to {0} × X^+_i, and p^− is defined analogously.
items.note: VS1 description: "Construct attractor/repeller correspondences, hyperbolic localization and the comparison map of FS IV.6, including equivariance and boundedness hypotheses. Prove its compatibility with base change and duality." ("attractor/repeller correspondences"). No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: Functorial description of X^± (Prop. IV.6.2)
items.statement: Consider the functor (X^+)′ sending any perfectoid space T over S to the set of G_m-equivariant maps from (A^1)^+ to X. There is a natural map X^+ → (X^+)′, as there is a natural G_m-equivariant map (A^1)^+ × X^+ → X^+ → X. The map X^+ → (X^+)′ is an isomorphism. Analogously, X^− classifies the set of G_m-equivariant maps from (A^1)^− to X.
items.note: VS1 description: "Construct attractor/repeller correspondences, hyperbolic localization and the comparison map of FS IV.6, including equivariance and boundedness hypotheses. Prove its compatibility with base change and duality." Consequence: X^± are independent of the choice of decomposition in Hypothesis IV.6.1. Proof uses properness (separatedness) of X/S and convergence of γ^n(x) to the fixed locus. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: X^0 = X^+ ×_X X^− locally (Lem. IV.6.3)
items.statement: The map j : X^0 → X^+ ×_X X^− is an open and closed immersion. More precisely, for any i = 1, …, n, the map j_i : X^0_i → X^+_i ×_X X^−_i is an isomorphism.
items.note: VS1 description: "Construct attractor/repeller correspondences, hyperbolic localization and the comparison map of FS IV.6, including equivariance and boundedness hypotheses. Prove its compatibility with base change and duality." Proof: closed immersion, check on geometric rank 1 points by extending to a G_m-equivariant map P^1_C → X. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: Functors L^±_{X/S} and the comparison map (Def. IV.6.4)
items.statement: In the setting of Hypothesis IV.6.1, define the functors L^+_{X/S} = R(p^+)_!(q^+)^∗ : D_ét(X, Λ) → D_ét(X^0, Λ), L^−_{X/S} = R(p^−)_∗R(q^−)^! : D_ét(X, Λ) → D_ét(X^0, Λ), and a natural transformation L^−_{X/S} → L^+_{X/S} as the composite L^−_{X/S} = R(p^−)_∗R(q^−)^! → (i^−)^∗R(q^−)^! → R(i^+)^!(q^+)^∗ → R(p^+)_!(q^+)^∗ = L^+_{X/S}, using the natural transformations R(i^+)^! = R(p^+)_!R(i^+)_!R(i^+)^! → R(p^+)_! and R(p^−)_∗ = (i^−)^∗(p^−)^∗R(p^−)_∗ → (i^−)^∗. The middle map is defined via the cartesian square with q̃^+ : X^+ ×_X X^− → X^− (the base change of q^+), q̃^− : X^+ ×_X X^− → X^+ (the base change of q^−) and the open and closed immersion j : X^0 ↪ X^+ ×_X X^− (Lemma IV.6.3), for which q̃^+ ∘ j = i^− and q̃^− ∘ j = i^+: it is the composite (i^−)^∗R(q^−)^! → (i^−)^∗R(q^−)^!R(q^+)_∗(q^+)^∗ = (i^−)^∗R(q̃^+)_∗R(q̃^−)^!(q^+)^∗ → (i^−)^∗R(q̃^+)_∗j_∗j^∗R(q̃^−)^!(q^+)^∗ = (i^−)^∗(i^−)_∗Rj^!R(q̃^−)^!(q^+)^∗ = R(i^+)^!(q^+)^∗. Equivalently, on each X^0_i it is the composite (i^−_i)^∗R(q^−_i)^! → (i^−_i)^∗R(q^−_i)^!R(q^+_i)_∗(q^+_i)^∗ = (i^−_i)^∗(i^−_i)_∗R(i^+_i)^!(q^+_i)^∗ = R(i^+_i)^!(q^+_i)^∗, using that X^0_i = X^+_i ×_X X^−_i.
items.note: VS1 description: "Construct attractor/repeller correspondences, hyperbolic localization and the comparison map of FS IV.6, including equivariance and boundedness hypotheses. Prove its compatibility with base change and duality." ("hyperbolic localization and the comparison map of FS IV.6"). No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: Braden's theorem for diamonds (Thm. IV.6.5)
items.statement: In the setting of Hypothesis IV.6.1, for any A ∈ D_ét(X/G_m, Λ) whose restriction to X we continue to denote by A, the map L^−_{X/S}A → L^+_{X/S}A is an isomorphism; in fact L^−_{X/S}A = R(p^−)_∗R(q^−)^!A ≅ (i^−)^∗R(q^−)^!A ≅ R(i^+)^!(q^+)^∗A ≅ R(p^+)_!(q^+)^∗A = L^+_{X/S}A is a series of isomorphisms.
items.note: VS1 description: "Construct attractor/repeller correspondences, hyperbolic localization and the comparison map of FS IV.6, including equivariance and boundedness hypotheses. Prove its compatibility with base change and duality." Version of [Bra03], cf. [Ric19, Theorem B]. Proof: reduce to A bounded below and S strictly totally disconnected; parts (b),(c) via Prop. IV.6.6 + Lemma IV.6.8; middle isomorphism via Prop. IV.6.9 on a G_m-orbit of a neighbourhood of X^0_i. Used throughout geometric Satake from §VI.3 (GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS1 "hyperbolic-localization comparisons"). No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: Contraction isomorphism R(i^+)^! ≅ R(p^+)_! (Thm. IV.6.5)
items.statement: In the setting of Hypothesis IV.6.1, for any A^+ ∈ D_ét(X^+/G_m, Λ), the map R(i^+)^!A^+ → R(p^+)_!A^+ is an isomorphism.
items.note: VS1 description: "Construct attractor/repeller correspondences, hyperbolic localization and the comparison map of FS IV.6, including equivariance and boundedness hypotheses. Prove its compatibility with base change and duality." No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: Contraction isomorphism R(p^−)_∗ ≅ (i^−)^∗ (Thm. IV.6.5)
items.statement: In the setting of Hypothesis IV.6.1, for any A^− ∈ D_ét(X^−/G_m, Λ), the map R(p^−)_∗A^− → (i^−)^∗A^− is an isomorphism.
items.note: VS1 description: "Construct attractor/repeller correspondences, hyperbolic localization and the comparison map of FS IV.6, including equivariance and boundedness hypotheses. Prove its compatibility with base change and duality." Analogue of the classical contraction lemma (Springer/Braden). No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: Relative cohomology with partial supports (Prop. IV.6.6)
items.statement: Let S = Spa(R, R^+) be an affinoid perfectoid space, ϖ ∈ R a pseudouniformizer, let f : Y → S be a partially proper map of locally spatial diamonds, and assume that Y is equipped with a G_m-action over S. Assume that the quotient v-stack Y/G_m is qcqs. In that case, one can find a quasicompact open subset V ⊂ Y such that G_m × V → Y is surjective and quasicompact. Write G_{m,S} = lim_{→n≥0} U_n, U_n = {x ∈ G_{m,S} | |x| ≤ |ϖ|^{−n}}, and let j_n : V_n ⊂ Y be the open image of the cohomologically smooth map U_n ×_S V ⊂ G_{m,S} ×_S Y → Y. For any A ∈ D_ét(Y, Λ) the relative cohomology with partial supports is lim_{→n} Rf_∗(j_{n!}A|_{V_n}) ∈ D_ét(S, Λ); this functor is canonically independent of the choices made in its definition.
items.note: VS1 description: "Construct attractor/repeller correspondences, hyperbolic localization and the comparison map of FS IV.6, including equivariance and boundedness hypotheses. Prove its compatibility with base change and duality." Remark IV.6.7: for S = Spa C a geometric rank 1 point this is RΓ_{c+}(Y, A) = lim_{→n} RΓ(Y, j_{n!}A_{V_n}), cohomology compactly supported towards one of the two ends ⋃_{n<0}γ^n(V), ⋃_{n>0}γ^n(V). No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: Vanishing of partial-support cohomology for equivariant sheaves (Prop. IV.6.6)
items.statement: In the situation of Proposition IV.6.6, for any A ∈ D^+_ét(Y/G_m, Λ) (resp. any A ∈ D_ét(Y/G_m, Λ) if dim. trg f < ∞), lim_{→n} Rf_∗(j_{n!}A|_{V_n}) = 0.
items.note: VS1 description: "Construct attractor/repeller correspondences, hyperbolic localization and the comparison map of FS IV.6, including equivariance and boundedness hypotheses. Prove its compatibility with base change and duality." Proof: Postnikov reduction; v-hypercover of Y by G_m × X_i with X_i proper spatial over S; reduce to Y = G_{m,S}, then to Theorem IV.5.3 by writing G_m as an increasing union of punctured discs. The proof is only sketched. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: (X^± \ X^0)/G_m is qcqs (Lem. IV.6.8)
items.statement: The G_m-action on X^+ \ X^0 (resp. X^− \ X^0) has the property that the quotient v-stack (X^+ \ X^0)/G_m (resp. (X^− \ X^0)/G_m) is qcqs over S (thus, over X^0).
items.note: VS1 description: "Construct attractor/repeller correspondences, hyperbolic localization and the comparison map of FS IV.6, including equivariance and boundedness hypotheses. Prove its compatibility with base change and duality." Proof: G_{m,S}/ϖ^Z is qcqs (a Tate elliptic curve), reduce to (X^+ \ X^0)/γ^Z and apply the criterion of Lemma II.2.17 on |X^+_i|, with divergence for n → −∞ from Lemma IV.6.3. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: Local hyperbolic situation: geometry (Prop. IV.6.9)
items.statement: Let S = Spa(R, R^+) be a strictly totally disconnected perfectoid space, let f : Y → S be a compactifiable map of locally spatial diamonds, and assume that Y/S is equipped with a G_m-action, with fixed points Y^0 ⊂ Y, and the following properties. (i) There are G_m-invariant closed subspaces q^+ : Y^+ ⊂ Y, q^− : Y^− ⊂ Y, containing Y^0 (via i^+ : Y^0 → Y^+, i^− : Y^0 → Y^−) such that the action maps extend to maps (A^1)^+ × Y^+ → Y^+ resp. (A^1)^− × Y^− → Y^−. (ii) The quotient v-stack Y/G_m is quasicompact. In particular, picking a pseudouniformizer ϖ ∈ R with induced action γ on Y, we can find some quasicompact open V ⊂ Y such that Y = γ^Z · V. (iii) With V as in (ii), let W^− be the closure of γ^N · V and W^+ the closure of γ^{−N} · V. Then ⋂_{n≥0} γ^n(W^−) = Y^− and ⋂_{n≥0} γ^{−n}(W^+) = Y^+. Then Y^0 is a spatial diamond, the square Y^0 → Y^+, Y^0 → Y^−, Y^+ → Y, Y^− → Y is cartesian, and the quotient v-stacks (Y \ Y^+)/G_m and (Y \ Y^−)/G_m are qcqs.
items.note: VS1 description: "Construct attractor/repeller correspondences, hyperbolic localization and the comparison map of FS IV.6, including equivariance and boundedness hypotheses. Prove its compatibility with base change and duality." No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: Local hyperbolic situation: comparison isomorphism (Prop. IV.6.9)
items.statement: In the situation of Proposition IV.6.9, for all A ∈ D^+_ét(Y/G_m, Λ) (resp. all A ∈ D_ét(Y/G_m, Λ) if dim. trg f < ∞) whose pullback to Y we continue to denote by A, the map (i^−)^∗R(q^−)^!A → (i^−)^∗R(q^−)^!(q^+)_∗(q^+)^∗A = (i^−)^∗(i^−)_∗R(i^+)^!(q^+)^∗A = R(i^+)^!(q^+)^∗A in D_ét(Y^0, Λ) is an isomorphism.
items.note: VS1 description: "Construct attractor/repeller correspondences, hyperbolic localization and the comparison map of FS IV.6, including equivariance and boundedness hypotheses. Prove its compatibility with base change and duality." Proof: reduce to global sections by lifting quasicompact separated étale Y_0′ → Y_0 G_m-equivariantly ([Sch17a, Prop. 11.23]), reduce to Y partially proper via the canonical compactification ([Sch17a, Prop. 17.6, 23.16(i)]), and compare both sides with the auxiliary functor F(A) = lim_{→n} Rf_∗(j_{n!}A|_{V_n}) via Lemma IV.6.10. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: Auxiliary partial-support functor vanishes on boundary sheaves (Lem. IV.6.10)
items.statement: In the proof of Proposition IV.6.9 (Y partially proper), let j_n : V_n = ⋃_{m≥−n} γ^m(V) ↪ Y and F(A) = lim_{→n} Rf_∗(j_{n!}A|_{V_n}) : D_ét(Y, Λ) → D_ét(S, Λ). Let j^− : Y \ Y^− → Y, j^+ : Y \ Y^+ → Y denote the open immersions. (i) If A = Rj^−_∗A^− for A^− ∈ D^+_ét((Y \ Y^−)/G_m, Λ), then F(A) = 0. (ii) If A = j^+_!A^+ for A^+ ∈ D^+_ét((Y \ Y^+)/G_m, Λ), then F(A) = 0.
items.note: VS1 description: "Construct attractor/repeller correspondences, hyperbolic localization and the comparison map of FS IV.6, including equivariance and boundedness hypotheses. Prove its compatibility with base change and duality." Proof: Proposition IV.6.6 and condition (iii). No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: Hyperbolic localization functor L_{X/S} (Def. IV.6.11)
items.statement: Let f : X → S with G_m-action be as above, satisfying Hypothesis IV.6.1. Let D_ét(X, Λ)^{G_m-mon} ⊂ D_ét(X, Λ) be the full subcategory generated under finite colimits and retracts by the image of D_ét(X/G_m, Λ) → D_ét(X, Λ). The hyperbolic localization functor is the functor L_{X/S} : D_ét(X, Λ)^{G_m-mon} → D_ét(X^0, Λ) given by L^−_{X/S} ≅ L^+_{X/S}.
items.note: VS1 description: "Construct attractor/repeller correspondences, hyperbolic localization and the comparison map of FS IV.6, including equivariance and boundedness hypotheses. Prove its compatibility with base change and duality." Well-defined by Theorem IV.6.5 (the isomorphism L^− → L^+ extends from the image of D_ét(X/G_m) to finite colimits and retracts). No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: Hyperbolic localization commutes with pullback (Prop. IV.6.12)
items.statement: In the situation of Definition IV.6.11, let g : S′ → S be a map of small v-stacks, with pullback f′ : X′ = X ×_S S′ → S′, g_X : X′ → X, g^0 : X^{0′} → X^0. Then there is a natural equivalence g^{0∗}L_{X/S} ≅ L_{X′/S′}g_X^∗.
items.note: VS1 description: "Construct attractor/repeller correspondences, hyperbolic localization and the comparison map of FS IV.6, including equivariance and boundedness hypotheses. Prove its compatibility with base change and duality." Proof: clear for L^+_{X/S} (proper base change / composition of shrieks). No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: Hyperbolic localization commutes with pushforward (Prop. IV.6.12)
items.statement: In the situation of Definition IV.6.11, let g : S′ → S be a map of small v-stacks, with pullback f′ : X′ = X ×_S S′ → S′, g_X : X′ → X, g^0 : X^{0′} → X^0. Then there is a natural equivalence L_{X/S}Rg_{X∗} ≅ Rg^0_∗L_{X′/S′}.
items.note: VS1 description: "Construct attractor/repeller correspondences, hyperbolic localization and the comparison map of FS IV.6, including equivariance and boundedness hypotheses. Prove its compatibility with base change and duality." Proof: clear for L^−_{X/S}. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: Hyperbolic localization commutes with shriek pushforward (Prop. IV.6.12)
items.statement: In the situation of Definition IV.6.11, let g : S′ → S be a map of small v-stacks, with pullback f′ : X′ = X ×_S S′ → S′, g_X : X′ → X, g^0 : X^{0′} → X^0. Then there is a natural equivalence L_{X/S}Rg_{X!} ≅ Rg_{0!}L_{X′/S′} (this equivalence in case g is compactifiable and representable in locally spatial diamonds with dim. trg g < ∞, so that the relevant functors are defined).

Prove its compatibility with base change and duality." Proof: clear for L^+_{X/S} (proper base change / composition of shrieks). No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: Hyperbolic localization commutes with shriek pullback (Prop. IV.6.12)
items.statement: In the situation of Definition IV.6.11, let g : S′ → S be a map of small v-stacks, with pullback f′ : X′ = X ×_S S′ → S′, g_X : X′ → X, g^0 : X^{0′} → X^0. Then there is a natural equivalence Rg^{0!}L_{X/S} ≅ L_{X′/S′}Rg^!_X (this equivalence in case g is compactifiable and representable in locally spatial diamonds with dim. trg g < ∞, so that the relevant functors are defined).
items.note: VS1 description: "Construct attractor/repeller correspondences, hyperbolic localization and the comparison map of FS IV.6, including equivariance and boundedness hypotheses. Prove its compatibility with base change and duality." Proof: clear for L^−_{X/S}. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: Hyperbolic localization and Verdier duality (Prop. IV.6.13)
items.statement: In the situation of Definition IV.6.11, let A ∈ D_ét(X, Λ)^{G_m-mon} and B ∈ D_ét(S, Λ). Let L′_{X/S} denote the hyperbolic localization functor for the inverse G_m-action. Then there is a natural isomorphism RHom(L_{X/S}(A), Rf^{0!}B) ≅ L′_{X/S}RHom(A, Rf^!B). In particular, taking B = Λ, hyperbolic localization commutes with Verdier duality, up to changing the G_m-action.
items.note: VS1 description: "Construct attractor/repeller correspondences, hyperbolic localization and the comparison map of FS IV.6, including equivariance and boundedness hypotheses. Prove its compatibility with base change and duality." ("compatibility with ... duality"). More generally RHom(L^+_{X/S}(A), Rf^{0!}B) ≅ L′^−_{X/S}RHom(A, Rf^!B) for all A. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: Hyperbolic localization preserves ULA (Prop. IV.6.14)
items.statement: In the situation of Definition IV.6.11, assume that A ∈ D_ét(X, Λ)^{G_m-mon} is f-universally locally acyclic. Then L_{X/S}(A) ∈ D_ét(X^0, Λ) is universally locally acyclic with respect to f^0 : X^0 ⊂ X → S.
items.note: VS1 plans hyperbolic localization with "compatibility with base change and duality" and, separately, ULA theory, but no stage names preservation of ULA under hyperbolic localization. Proof: base change (Prop. IV.6.12) for condition (a); for (b), RHom_Λ(L_{X/S}(A), Rf^{0!}−) ≅ L′_{X/S}(D_{X/S}(A) ⊗^L_Λ f^∗−) commutes with direct sums (Prop. IV.6.13, Prop. IV.2.19). Used for constant-term functors in geometric Satake. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: Div^1 = Spd Ĕ/φ^Z
items.statement: Work on Perf_k where k = F̄_q. The moduli space of degree 1 Cartier divisors on the Fargues–Fontaine curve can be written as Div^1 = Spd Ĕ/φ^Z, where φ acts on Spd Ĕ = Spd k ×_{Spd F_q} Spd E via the second factor.
items.note: RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2:untilts: "Define Div^1 using the unramified coefficient base Spd(E-breve)/phi^Z over Perf_Fq. Keep this moduli object distinct from the diamond of one fixed curve." Identification with degree 1 Cartier divisors is from Chapter II. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: Map ψ : Div^1 → [∗/W_E]
items.statement: If C = Ê is a completed algebraic closure of E, there is an action of W_E on Spd C, with the inertia subgroup I_E ⊂ W_E acting via its usual action, while Frobenius elements act via the composite of the usual action and the Frobenius of Spd C; more precisely, τ ∈ W_E acts as τ ∘ Frob^{−deg τ} where deg : W_E → Z is the projection (a map over Spd k). The natural map [Spd C/W_E] → [Spd Ĕ/φ^Z] is an isomorphism, yielding the natural map ψ : [Spd Ĕ/φ^Z] ≅ [Spd C/W_E] → [∗/W_E]. Equivalently W_E × Spd C ≅ Spd C ×_{Div^1} Spd C for the natural map Spd C → Div^1. For any small v-stack X, this gives ψ_X : X × Div^1 → X × [∗/W_E].
items.note: VS1 description: "Establish Drinfeld's lemma IV.7 for the divisor/Weil-action applications, separating partial Frobenius descent from an arbitrary fundamental-group product claim." ("divisor/Weil-action applications"). The isomorphism [Spd C/W_E] ≅ [Spd Ĕ/φ^Z] is asserted without proof. LanglandsParameterStacks:LP0 owns Weil groups. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: ψ_X^∗ fully faithful (Prop. IV.7.1)
items.statement: Let X be a small v-stack and Λ a ring killed by some integer n prime to p. The functor ψ_X^∗ : D_ét(X × [∗/W_E], Λ) → D_ét(X × Div^1, Λ) is fully faithful.
items.note: VS1 description: "Establish Drinfeld's lemma IV.7 for the divisor/Weil-action applications, separating partial Frobenius descent from an arbitrary fundamental-group product claim." Proof: descent along ∗ → [∗/W_E]; [Sch17a, Theorem 1.13] gives full faithfulness of D_ét(X × W_E^•, Λ) → D_ét(X × Spd C × W_E^•, Λ). No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: ψ_X^∗ an equivalence under a Spd C-invariance hypothesis (Prop. IV.7.1)
items.statement: If the natural pullback functor D_ét(X, Λ) → D_ét(X × Spd C, Λ) is an equivalence, then ψ_X^∗ : D_ét(X × [∗/W_E], Λ) → D_ét(X × Div^1, Λ) is also an equivalence.
items.note: VS1 description: "Establish Drinfeld's lemma IV.7 for the divisor/Weil-action applications, separating partial Frobenius descent from an arbitrary fundamental-group product claim." Essential surjectivity on cartesian objects reduces to degree 0 of the simplicial resolution. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: Fully faithfulness for (Div^1)^I (Cor. IV.7.2)
items.statement: For any finite set I, pullback along X × (Div^1)^I → X × [∗/W_E^I] induces a fully faithful functor D_ét(X × [∗/W_E^I], Λ) → D_ét(X × (Div^1)^I, Λ).
items.note: VS1 description: "Establish Drinfeld's lemma IV.7 for the divisor/Weil-action applications, separating partial Frobenius descent from an arbitrary fundamental-group product claim." Inductively from Prop. IV.7.1. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: D_lc(Y, Λ): v-locally constant with perfect fibres
items.statement: For any small v-stack Y, let D_lc(Y, Λ) ⊂ D_ét(Y, Λ) be the full subcategory of all objects that are v-locally constant with perfect fibres. Being v-locally constant with perfect fibres is equivalent to dualizability, and on spatial diamonds such objects are actually étale locally constant, as follows from Proposition IV.2.6.
items.locator: Chapter IV, §IV.7, before Proposition IV.7.3, p. 165
items.note: No stage names this subcategory explicitly (VS1 plans Drinfeld's lemma; lisse categories of VS2–VS3 are a different, solid construction). The equivalence with dualizability is asserted without proof. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: Drinfeld's lemma (Prop. IV.7.3)
items.statement: For any finite set I and any small v-stack X, the functor D_lc(X × [∗/W_E^I], Λ) → D_lc(X × (Div^1)^I, Λ) is an equivalence of categories.
items.note: VS1 description: "Establish Drinfeld's lemma IV.7 for the divisor/Weil-action applications, separating partial Frobenius descent from an arbitrary fundamental-group product claim." Refined in Prop. VI.9.2; mostly used for X a point; fails without local constancy (partial diagonals). Proof: full faithfulness from Cor. IV.7.2; reduce to |I| = 1, X a geometric rank 1 point, Λ = F_{ℓ^r}[[T_1, …, T_d]] (discrete) via [Sch17a, Prop. 20.15]; use a point Spa K → Y_C with Gal(K̄|K) ↠ I_E (Lemma II.1.14), [SW20, Lemma 16.3.2] (finite étale covers of Spa C × Div^1 come from Div^1), so the monodromy W_E → Aut_Λ(M̂) is trivial on an open subgroup of I_E and descends to Spa C × Spd E′. Consumed by HeckeStacksAndLocalShtukas:HS1 ("Construct the continuous W_E^I action through Drinfeld's lemma"). No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart (no sous-perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves or étale sheaf theory on diamonds in the pinned libraries; declarations.tsv and sources searched).

items.name: Theorem V.0.1(o): local charts π_b
items.statement: Standing conventions of Chapter V: k|F_q algebraically closed, work on Perf_k; Λ a ring with nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. For any b ∈ B(G), there is a map π_b : M_b → Bun_G that is representable in locally spatial diamonds, partially proper and cohomologically smooth, where M_b parametrizes G-bundles E together with an increasing Q-filtration whose associated graded is, at all geometric points, isomorphic to E_b with its slope grading. The v-stack M_b is representable in locally spatial diamonds, partially proper and cohomologically smooth over [∗/G_b(E)].
items.locator: Chapter V, introduction, Theorem V.0.1(o), p. 167
items.note: BG4 plans: "Construct the filtered-bundle chart M_b with associated graded geometrically E_b. Prove representability, partial properness and cohomological smoothness over [*/J_b(E)] and for M_b → Bun_G in FS V.3's precise sense. Establish surjectivity/covering of the neighborhoods it is intended to cover, compatibility with HN strata and dimension.". Summary statement; proved as Theorem V.3.7 and Proposition V.3.5/V.3.6.

items.name: Theorem V.0.1(i): semiorthogonal decomposition of D_ét(Bun_G,Λ)
items.statement: Standing conventions of Chapter V: k|F_q algebraically closed, work on Perf_k; Λ a ring with nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. Via excision triangles, there is an infinite semiorthogonal decomposition of D_ét(Bun_G, Λ) into the various D_ét(Bun_G^b, Λ) for b ∈ B(G).
items.locator: Chapter V, introduction, Theorem V.0.1(i), p. 167
items.note: VS4 plans: "Prove localization triangles and the infinite semiorthogonal decomposition along the HN strata using justified exhaustions. Characterize compact objects by compact restrictions with finite stratum support, and by the thick closure of compact induction from pro-p open subgroups.". Stated in the introduction; no separate numbered proof in the chapter — follows from the stratification of Bun_G by the locally closed Bun_G^b (Chapter III) and excision triangles j_!j^* → id → i_*i^*.

items.name: Theorem V.0.1(ii): sheaves on a stratum are smooth representations
items.statement: Standing conventions of Chapter V: k|F_q algebraically closed, work on Perf_k; Λ a ring with nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. For each b ∈ B(G), pullback along Bun_G^b ≅ [∗/G̃_b] → [∗/G_b(E)] gives an equivalence D_ét([∗/G_b(E)], Λ) ≅ D_ét(Bun_G^b, Λ), and D_ét([∗/G_b(E)], Λ) ≅ D(G_b(E), Λ) is equivalent to the derived category of the category of smooth representations of G_b(E) on Λ-modules.
items.locator: Chapter V, introduction, Theorem V.0.1(ii), p. 167
items.note: VS4 plans: "Identify D_et([*/H],Lambda) with the enhanced derived category of smooth H-representations for H locally pro-p and prime-to-p torsion Lambda"; VS4 plans: "Apply this to J_b(E), and prove the connected-kernel invariance giving the category for nonbasic Bun_G^b.". Proved as Proposition V.2.2 and Theorem V.1.1.

items.name: Theorem V.0.1(iii): compact generation
items.statement: Standing conventions of Chapter V: k|F_q algebraically closed, work on Perf_k; Λ a ring with nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. The category D_ét(Bun_G, Λ) is compactly generated, and a complex A ∈ D_ét(Bun_G, Λ) is compact if and only if for all b ∈ B(G), the restriction i^{b∗}A ∈ D_ét(Bun_G^b, Λ) ≅ D(G_b(E), Λ) is compact, and zero for almost all b. Here, compactness in D(G_b(E), Λ) is equivalent to lying in the thick triangulated subcategory generated by c-Ind_K^{G_b(E)} Λ as K runs over open pro-p-subgroups of G_b(E).
items.locator: Chapter V, introduction, Theorem V.0.1(iii), p. 167
items.note: VS4 plans: "Prove localization triangles and the infinite semiorthogonal decomposition along the HN strata using justified exhaustions. Characterize compact objects by compact restrictions with finite stratum support, and by the thick closure of compact induction from pro-p open subgroups.". Case U = Bun_G of Theorem V.4.1.

items.name: Theorem V.0.1(iv): Bernstein–Zelevinsky duality on compact objects
items.statement: Standing conventions of Chapter V: k|F_q algebraically closed, work on Perf_k; Λ a ring with nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. On the subcategory D_ét(Bun_G, Λ)^ω ⊂ D_ét(Bun_G, Λ) of compact objects, there is a Bernstein–Zelevinsky duality functor D_BZ : (D_ét(Bun_G, Λ)^ω)^op → D_ét(Bun_G, Λ)^ω with a functorial identification R Hom(A, B) ≅ π_♮(D_BZ(A) ⊗^L_Λ B) for B ∈ D_ét(Bun_G, Λ), where π : Bun_G → ∗ is the projection. The functor D_BZ is an equivalence, and D_BZ² is naturally equivalent to the identity. It is compatible with usual Bernstein–Zelevinsky duality on D(G_b(E), Λ) for basic b ∈ B(G).
items.locator: Chapter V, introduction, Theorem V.0.1(iv), p. 168
items.note: VS5 plans: "Construct Bernstein–Zelevinsky duality on compact Bun_G objects using the partial-support functor; prove biduality and its basic-stratum comparison.". Proved as Theorem V.5.1 (there written R Hom(D_BZ(A), B) ≅ π_♮(A ⊗ B); equivalent via D_BZ² ≅ id).

items.name: Theorem V.0.1(v): ULA objects are the admissible ones; Verdier duality
items.statement: Standing conventions of Chapter V: k|F_q algebraically closed, work on Perf_k; Λ a ring with nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. An object A ∈ D_ét(Bun_G, Λ) is universally locally acyclic (with respect to Bun_G → ∗) if and only if for all b ∈ B(G), the restriction i^{b∗}A ∈ D_ét(Bun_G^b, Λ) ≅ D(G_b(E), Λ) is admissible, i.e. for all pro-p open subgroups K ⊂ G_b(E), the complex (i^{b∗}A)^K is perfect. Universally locally acyclic complexes are preserved by Verdier duality, and satisfy Verdier biduality.
items.locator: Chapter V, introduction, Theorem V.0.1(v), p. 168
items.note: VS5 plans: "Separately construct Verdier duality on ULA objects and prove that ULA is equivalent to perfection of K-invariants on every stratum for every appropriate pro-p open K.". First sentence is Theorem V.7.1; the Verdier-duality clause is not reproved in Chapter V — it is the general ULA formalism of §IV.2 (ULA objects are preserved by relative Verdier duality and are reflexive), cf. also Theorem V.6.2.

items.name: D_ét(∗,Λ) = D(Λ)
items.statement: D_ét(∗, Λ) = D(Λ). More precisely, for any complete algebraically closed field C one has D_ét(Spa C, Λ) = D(Λ) and there is a sequence D(Λ) → D_ét(∗, Λ) → D_ét(Spa C, Λ) = D(Λ), the second functor fully faithful, whose composite is the identity; hence D(Λ) → D_ét(∗, Λ) is an equivalence.
items.locator: Chapter V, §V.1, unnumbered (after Theorem V.1.1), p. 168
items.note: Deduced from [Sch17a, Theorem 1.13(ii)] applied to X = ∗ (∗ = Spd k over Perf_k) together with D_ét(Spa C, Λ) = D(Λ). It is also the case G = {1} of Theorem V.1.1, which VS4 plans for every locally pro-p H, and the VS4 packet node VS4/classifying-stack-equivalence quotes it inside V.1.1 ('D_et([*/G],Lambda) -> D_et(*,Lambda) = D(Lambda)'), but no node states or proves it. Its input, [Sch17a, Thm 1.13(ii)] = ECD Theorem 19.5, is planned by DiamondEtaleCohomology:C6. Used throughout as the target of π_♮ and of stalk functors.

items.name: Theorem V.1.1: D_ét([∗/G],Λ) ≃ D(G,Λ)
items.statement: Fix Λ with nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p, and let G be a locally pro-p-group. Let D(G, Λ) be the derived category of the category of smooth representations of G on Λ-modules. There is a natural symmetric monoidal equivalence D(G, Λ) ≃ D_ét([∗/G], Λ) under which the functor D(G, Λ) → D(Λ) forgetting the G-action gets identified with the pullback functor D_ét([∗/G], Λ) → D_ét(∗, Λ) = D(Λ) under the projection ∗ → [∗/G].
items.note: VS4 plans: "Identify D_et([*/H],Lambda) with the enhanced derived category of smooth H-representations for H locally pro-p and prime-to-p torsion Lambda"; "identify pullback with forgetting the action". The derived smooth category itself is SR.0:derived-extension. Proof: construct V ↦ F_V, reduce to [Spa C/G], compare étale site with G-Set (Lemmas V.1.2–V.1.3), reduce to G pro-p and use left-completeness [Sch17a, Prop. 14.11].

items.name: Theorem V.1.1 (second part): invariance under base change to Spa C
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem V.1.1, the same result holds true for the base change [Spa C/G] = [∗/G] × Spa C for any complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean field C/k; more precisely, the base change functor D_ét([∗/G], Λ) → D_ét([Spa C/G], Λ) is an equivalence.
items.note: VS4 plans: "Identify D_et([*/H],Lambda) with the enhanced derived category of smooth H-representations for H locally pro-p and prime-to-p torsion Lambda". Fully faithfulness is [Sch17a, Thm 1.13(ii)]; the proof shows D([Spa C/G]_ét,Λ) → D_ét([Spa C/G],Λ) is an equivalence.

items.name: The v-sheaf F_V attached to a smooth representation
items.statement: For a smooth G-representation V on a Λ-module, F_V is the v-sheaf on [∗/G] taking a perfectoid space X with a G-torsor X̃ → X to the set of all continuous G-equivariant maps |X̃| → V. Its pullback along ∗ → [∗/G] is the v-sheaf corresponding to V (a disjoint union of points), so F_V ∈ D_ét([∗/G], Λ); V ↦ F_V is exact and extends to complexes, giving D(G, Λ) → D_ét([∗/G], Λ) compatible with forgetful functors and derived tensor products.
items.locator: Chapter V, §V.1, proof of Theorem V.1.1, p. 169
items.note: VS4: "Construct both functors using continuous torsor descent". Uses [Sch17a, Prop. 12.9] (v-covers induce quotient maps), [Sch17a, Def. 14.13, Prop. 14.16].

items.name: |S × A| = |S| × A
items.statement: For any perfectoid space S and any locally profinite set A, |S × A| = |S| × A. Consequently, for a G-torsor X̃ → X, the space |X̃| has a continuous G-action.
items.locator: Chapter V, §V.1, proof of Theorem V.1.1, p. 169
items.note: Stated as 'one checks'; used to make sense of F_V. The VS4 packet node VS4/classifying-stack-equivalence records it among its hypotheses ('The construction of the functor uses that |S x A| = |S| x A for a perfectoid space S and a locally profinite set A') but does not prove it. For profinite A it follows from PerfectoidSpaces:P5/limit-underlying-space-homeomorphism (|lim X_i| = lim |X_i|) applied to S × A = lim S × A_i; DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/compact-hausdorff-diamonds proves only the case S = Spa(K, O_K).

items.name: Lemma V.1.2: étale site of [Spa C/G] is G-Set
items.statement: Let G be locally pro-p, C a complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean field over k, X = [Spa C/G], and X_ét ⊂ X_v the full subcategory of all Y ∈ X_v which are étale (and locally separated) over X. The étale site X_ét is equivalent to the category G-Set of discrete G-sets, via sending a discrete set S with continuous G-action to [S × Spa C/G].
items.note: Step of VS4 plans: "Identify D_et([*/H],Lambda) with the enhanced derived category of smooth H-representations for H locally pro-p and prime-to-p torsion Lambda".

items.name: Lemma V.1.3: D(G,Λ) ≃ D(G-Set,Λ)
items.statement: There is a natural equivalence D(G, Λ) ≃ D(G-Set, Λ), such that the diagram with top row D(G, Λ) ≅ D(G-Set, Λ) ≅ D([Spa C/G]_ét, Λ), bottom row D_ét([∗/G], Λ) → D_ét([Spa C/G], Λ), and vertical functors the functor of Theorem V.1.1 and the natural functor D([Spa C/G]_ét, Λ) → D_ét([Spa C/G], Λ), commutes. On abelian level: V ↦ (S ↦ continuous G-equivariant maps S → V), with inverse F ↦ lim_{→H⊂G open} F(G/H).
items.note: Step of VS4 plans: "Identify D_et([*/H],Lambda) with the enhanced derived category of smooth H-representations for H locally pro-p and prime-to-p torsion Lambda". Classical (smooth reps = sheaves on the classifying site of G).

items.name: v-cohomology of [Spa C/G] for G pro-p
items.statement: Let G be pro-p and nΛ = 0 with n prime to p. For any smooth G-representation V on Λ-modules, RΓ([Spa C/G]_v, V) = V^G, i.e. H^0 is V^G and there are no higher H^i. Consequently D([Spa C/G]_ét, Λ) → D_ét([Spa C/G], Λ) is an equivalence (for G pro-p, and then for G locally pro-p by localization).
items.locator: Chapter V, §V.1, proof of Theorem V.1.1, p. 170
items.note: Key step of VS4 plans: "Identify D_et([*/H],Lambda) with the enhanced derived category of smooth H-representations for H locally pro-p and prime-to-p torsion Lambda". Computed via the Čech nerve of Spa C → [Spa C/G] (continuous cochains) and vanishing of continuous cohomology of pro-p groups on prime-to-p torsion; left-completeness from [Sta, Tag 0719] and [Sch17a, Prop. 14.11].

items.name: Smooth dual (V^∗)^sm
items.statement: For a locally pro-p group G and a smooth G-representation V on Λ-modules, (V^∗)^sm = {f : V → Λ | ∃H ⊂ G open ∀h ∈ H, v ∈ V : f(hv) = f(v)}; V ↦ (V^∗)^sm is left exact and its derived functor is A ↦ (A^∗)^sm : D(G, Λ)^op → D(G, Λ).
items.note: Contragredient over Λ; adjunction Hom(B,(A^∗)^sm) = Hom(B ⊗^L_Λ A, Λ). On the abelian level (V^∗)^sm is the smooth vectors of the algebraic dual Hom_Λ(V, Λ), and SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.0 plans 'smooth vectors in an arbitrary representation and the relevant adjunction'. SR.3 plans smooth contragredient duality only for complex representations, and SR.2 only 'compatibility with duals for admissible representations'. No stage plans the Λ-coefficient smooth dual as a functor or its right derived functor on D(G, Λ) (SR.0:derived-extension builds the derived category only).

items.name: Corollary V.1.4: RHom(−,Λ) is derived smooth duality
items.statement: Under the equivalence of Theorem V.1.1, the operation RHom_Λ(−, Λ) : D_ét([∗/G], Λ)^op → D_ét([∗/G], Λ) corresponds to the derived smooth duality functor A ↦ (A^∗)^sm : D(G, Λ)^op → D(G, Λ) induced on derived categories by the left-exact smooth duality functor V ↦ (V^∗)^sm.
items.note: Proved from the adjunction Hom_{D(G,Λ)}(B, (A^∗)^sm) = Hom_{D(G,Λ)}(B ⊗^L_Λ A, Λ) and symmetric monoidality. Not named in VS4/VS5 text (VS5 does 'Verdier duality on ULA objects'). Used in §V.6 (reflexivity on strata).

items.name: Proposition V.2.1: Banach–Colmez torsors have fully faithful pullback
items.statement: Let f : S′ → S be a map of small v-stacks that is a torsor under BC(E) resp. BC(E[1]), where E is a vector bundle on X_S that is everywhere of positive (resp. negative) slopes. Then the pullback functor f^∗ : D_ét(S, Λ) → D_ét(S′, Λ) is fully faithful.
items.note: VS4 plans: "Apply this to J_b(E), and prove the connected-kernel invariance giving the category for nonbasic Bun_G^b." (the connected kernel of G̃_b → G_b(E) is a successive extension of positive Banach–Colmez spaces; BG3 says "Agreement of étale coefficient categories after removing this kernel is a separate theorem owned by VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories"). Proof: v-descent, Cor. II.3.3(iv) reduces to E = O(1/n), BC(E) a perfectoid open unit ball (Prop. II.2.5(iv)); cohomology of the open disc; negative case via 0 → E → O(d)^m → G → 0.

items.name: Proposition V.2.2: D_ét(Bun_G^b,Λ) ≅ D(G_b(E),Λ)
items.statement: Standing conventions of Chapter V: k|F_q algebraically closed, work on Perf_k; Λ a ring with nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. For any b ∈ B(G), the map Bun_G^b = [∗/G̃_b] → [∗/G_b(E)] induces via pullback an equivalence D(G_b(E), Λ) ≅ D_ét([∗/G_b(E)], Λ) ≅ D_ét([∗/G̃_b], Λ).
items.note: VS4 plans: "Apply this to J_b(E), and prove the connected-kernel invariance giving the category for nonbasic Bun_G^b.". Proof: Sch17a Thm 1.13 + Theorem V.1.1 reduce to [Spa C/G_b(E)] → [Spa C/G̃_b]; fully faithful pullback along the section by Prop. III.5.1 and Prop. V.2.1. (Display misprinted: (PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E33).)

items.name: Proposition V.2.2 (second part): base change for strata
items.statement: Standing conventions of Chapter V: k|F_q algebraically closed, work on Perf_k; Λ a ring with nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. For any b ∈ B(G) and any complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean field C/k, the map D_ét([∗/G̃_b], Λ) → D_ét([Spa C/G̃_b], Λ) is an equivalence.
items.note: VS4 plans: "Apply this to J_b(E), and prove the connected-kernel invariance giving the category for nonbasic Bun_G^b.".

items.name: Corollary V.2.3: the base field plays no role
items.statement: Standing conventions of Chapter V: k|F_q algebraically closed, work on Perf_k; Λ a ring with nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. For any complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean field C and any locally closed substack U ⊂ Bun_G, the functor D_ét(U, Λ) → D_ét(U × Spa C, Λ) is an equivalence of categories.
items.note: Fully faithful by [Sch17a, Thm 1.13(ii)]; essential surjectivity via the finite stratification of a quasicompact U, Proposition V.2.2 and compatibility of !-extension with base change to Spa C. The paper says it plays a key role for Hecke operators (Chapter IX). Planned by the VS4 packet node VS4/strata-are-classifying-stacks ('FS V.2.2-V.2.3: the connected-kernel invariance on strata and independence of the base field'), whose statement includes this corollary ('Consequently, for any complete algebraically closed C and any locally closed substack U of Bun_G, D_et(U,Lambda) -> D_et(U x Spa C, Lambda) is an equivalence') and whose last proof step is its proof.

items.name: Example V.3.1: the chart for GL_2 and O(1) ⊕ O
items.statement: Let G = GL_2 and b correspond to O(1) ⊕ O. M_b is the moduli space of extensions 0 → L → E → L′ → 0 with L of degree 0 and L′ of degree 1, mapping to Bun_G by (extension) ↦ E. The natural E^× × E^×-torsor M̃_b → M_b parametrizing isomorphisms L ≅ O and L′ ≅ O(1) has M̃_b = BC(O(−1)[1]), a negative absolute Banach–Colmez space. Any E parametrized by M_b is isomorphic to O ⊕ O(1) or O(1/2); the fibres of π_b over a rank 2 bundle E are open subsets of (BC(E) \ {0})/E^×, interpolating between (BC(O(1/2)) \ {0})/E^× (cohomologically smooth by Prop. II.3.7) and an open subset of (BC(O ⊕ O(1)) \ {0})/E^× = (E × Spd k[[t^{1/p^∞}]] \ {(0,0)})/E^×, which is still cohomologically smooth.
items.note: BG4 plans: "Construct the filtered-bundle chart M_b with associated graded geometrically E_b. Prove representability, partial properness and cohomological smoothness over [*/J_b(E)] and for M_b → Bun_G in FS V.3's precise sense. Establish surjectivity/covering of the neighborhoods it is intended to cover, compatibility with HN strata and dimension.". Motivating example; for GL_n smoothness of π_b can be checked by hand.

items.name: Definition V.3.2: the stack M of Q-filtered G-bundles
items.statement: The v-stack M is the moduli stack taking S ∈ Perf_k to the groupoid of G-bundles E on X_S together with an increasing separated and exhaustive Q-filtration (ρ_∗E)^{≤λ} ⊂ ρ_∗E (ranging over algebraic representations ρ : G → GL_n, and compatible with exact sequences and tensor products) on the corresponding fibre functor such that (letting (ρ_∗E)^{<λ} = ⋃_{λ′<λ}(ρ_∗E)^{≤λ′}) the quotient (ρ_∗E)^λ = (ρ_∗E)^{≤λ}/(ρ_∗E)^{<λ} is a semistable vector bundle of slope λ, for all λ ∈ Q and representations ρ : G → GL_n.
items.note: BG4 plans: "Construct the filtered-bundle chart M_b with associated graded geometrically E_b. Prove representability, partial properness and cohomological smoothness over [*/J_b(E)] and for M_b → Bun_G in FS V.3's precise sense. Establish surjectivity/covering of the neighborhoods it is intended to cover, compatibility with HN strata and dimension.".

items.name: Decomposition M = ⊔ M_b and maps q_b
items.statement: Passing to the associated graded, M maps to the moduli stack of G-bundles in Q-graded vector bundles on X_S with weight-λ piece semistable of slope λ, which by Proposition III.4.7 is ⊔_{b∈B(G)} [∗/G_b(E)]. Hence M = ⊔_{b∈B(G)} M_b, with natural maps q_b : M_b → [∗/G_b(E)]; π_b : M_b → Bun_G forgets the filtration. M̃_b → M_b denotes the pullback of the v-cover ∗ → [∗/G_b(E)] (a G_b(E)-torsor).
items.locator: Chapter V, §V.3, after Definition V.3.2, pp. 173–174
items.note: BG4 plans: "Construct the filtered-bundle chart M_b with associated graded geometrically E_b. Prove representability, partial properness and cohomological smoothness over [*/J_b(E)] and for M_b → Bun_G in FS V.3's precise sense. Establish surjectivity/covering of the neighborhoods it is intended to cover, compatibility with HN strata and dimension.".

items.name: Example V.3.3: M for GL_n
items.statement: When G = GL_n, M sends S to the groupoid of filtered vector bundles 0 = Fil_0 E ⊊ Fil_1 E ⊊ ⋯ ⊊ Fil_r E = E for some r, such that Fil_{i+1}E/Fil_iE is semistable and the slopes (μ(Fil_{i+1}E/Fil_iE))_{0≤i<r} form an increasing sequence (the opposite condition to the one defining the Harder–Narasimhan filtration). The maps q_b send such a vector bundle to the graded vector bundle ⊕_{i=0}^{r−1} Fil_{i+1}E/Fil_iE.
items.note: BG4 plans: "Construct the filtered-bundle chart M_b with associated graded geometrically E_b. Prove representability, partial properness and cohomological smoothness over [*/J_b(E)] and for M_b → Bun_G in FS V.3's precise sense. Establish surjectivity/covering of the neighborhoods it is intended to cover, compatibility with HN strata and dimension.".

items.name: Example V.3.4: M_b via parabolic reduction (G quasisplit)
items.statement: Suppose G is quasisplit. Let M_b be the centralizer of the slope morphism (a Levi subgroup) and P_b the parabolic subgroup with Levi M_b such that the weights of ν_b on Lie P_b are positive. With Bun_{P_b} → Bun_G and Bun_{P_b} → Bun_{M_b} induced by P_b ⊂ G and P_b → M_b, there is a cartesian diagram 𝓜_b = Bun_{P_b} ×_{Bun_{M_b}} Bun_{M_b}^b.
items.note: Asserted without proof and not used later in the paper (Chapter IX's parabolic argument uses the different identification Bun_G^{b_N} ≅ Bun_P^{b_N} from the Harder–Narasimhan reduction). Not planned: BG4's description ('Construct the filtered-bundle chart M_b … compatibility with HN strata and dimension') and its four packet nodes (filtered-bundle-chart, chart-over-classifying-stack, section-and-spatial-complement, chart-to-bun-g) never mention Bun_{P_b}, Bun_{M_b} or this fibre product, and no stage description in the atlas constructs Bun_P for a parabolic P (only the ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction ES7:parabolic packet uses it). Here the chart is written 𝓜_b (calligraphic) and the Levi M_b (roman). Belongs with the charts in BunGAndNewtonStrata:BG4.

items.name: Proposition V.3.5: q_b is a successive negative Banach–Colmez torsor
items.statement: Standing conventions of Chapter V: k|F_q algebraically closed, work on Perf_k; Λ a ring with nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. For any b ∈ B(G), the map q_b : M_b → [∗/G_b(E)] is partially proper, representable in locally spatial diamonds, and cohomologically smooth, of dimension ⟨2ρ, ν_b⟩. In fact, after pullback along ∗ → [∗/G_b(E)], it is a successive torsor under negative Banach–Colmez spaces. In particular, M_b is a cohomologically smooth Artin v-stack, of dimension ⟨2ρ, ν_b⟩.
items.note: BG4 plans: "Construct the filtered-bundle chart M_b with associated graded geometrically E_b. Prove representability, partial properness and cohomological smoothness over [*/J_b(E)] and for M_b → Bun_G in FS V.3's precise sense. Establish surjectivity/covering of the neighborhoods it is intended to cover, compatibility with HN strata and dimension.". Proof: M̃_b(S) = H^{<0}-torsors on X_S where H is the automorphism group of E_b (Prop. III.5.2) with filtration (H^{≤λ})_{λ≤0} (opposite to the one in Prop. III.5.1); graded pieces are negative-slope bundles.

items.name: Proposition V.3.6(a): closed section [∗/G_b(E)] → M_b
items.statement: Standing conventions of Chapter V: k|F_q algebraically closed, work on Perf_k; Λ a ring with nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. The map M_b → [∗/G_b(E)] has a section [∗/G_b(E)] → M_b given by the closed substack where E is (at every geometric point) isomorphic to E_b, in which case (ρ_∗E)^{≤λ} ⊂ ρ_∗E is a splitting of the Harder–Narasimhan filtration of ρ_∗E for all representations ρ : G → GL_n.
items.note: BG4 plans: "Construct the filtered-bundle chart M_b with associated graded geometrically E_b. Prove representability, partial properness and cohomological smoothness over [*/J_b(E)] and for M_b → Bun_G in FS V.3's precise sense. Establish surjectivity/covering of the neighborhoods it is intended to cover, compatibility with HN strata and dimension.". Closedness by semicontinuity: Newton point of E bounded by b on M_b (reduced to GL_n by [RR96, Lemma 2.2(iv)]).

items.name: Proposition V.3.6(b): M̃_b° is a spatial diamond
items.statement: Standing conventions of Chapter V: k|F_q algebraically closed, work on Perf_k; Λ a ring with nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. Let M_b° = M_b \ [∗/G_b(E)] be the open complement of the section, with preimage M̃_b° = M̃_b \ {∗}. Then M̃_b° is a spatial diamond.
items.note: BG4 plans: "Construct the filtered-bundle chart M_b with associated graded geometrically E_b. Prove representability, partial properness and cohomological smoothness over [*/J_b(E)] and for M_b → Bun_G in FS V.3's precise sense. Establish surjectivity/covering of the neighborhoods it is intended to cover, compatibility with HN strata and dimension.". Proof uses a decent representative b [RZ96, Def. 1.8], Lemma II.2.17, Lemma II.3.8, [Sch17a, Thm 12.18] and Prop. II.3.7 (punctured absolute Banach–Colmez spaces are diamonds). The paper stresses M̃_b itself is not a diamond but is representable in locally spatial diamonds over ∗.

items.name: Proposition V.3.6(c): M̃_b°/U_π^Z → ∗ is proper
items.statement: Standing conventions of Chapter V: k|F_q algebraically closed, work on Perf_k; Λ a ring with nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. If U_π := ν_b^N(π) ∈ G_b(E) for any large enough N (so that ν_b^N : G_m → G_b is a well-defined cocharacter), then M̃_b°/U_π^Z → ∗ is proper.
items.note: BG4 plans: "Construct the filtered-bundle chart M_b with associated graded geometrically E_b. Prove representability, partial properness and cohomological smoothness over [*/J_b(E)] and for M_b → Bun_G in FS V.3's precise sense. Establish surjectivity/covering of the neighborhoods it is intended to cover, compatibility with HN strata and dimension.". Proof: U_π acting on |M̃_b ×_k Spa k((t))| satisfies Lemma II.2.17 (contracting to the origin for positive powers, divergent for negative ones), shown for GL_n via Q-filtered descent data on Y_{C,[1,q]}; partial properness of M̃_b° → ∗ plus quasicompactness.

items.name: Theorem V.3.7(a): π_b is a cohomologically smooth chart
items.statement: Standing conventions of Chapter V: k|F_q algebraically closed, work on Perf_k; Λ a ring with nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. The map π_b : M_b → Bun_G forgetting the filtration is partially proper, representable in locally spatial diamonds, and cohomologically smooth of ℓ-dimension ⟨2ρ, ν_b⟩. (In the proof: M = ⊔_b M_b → Bun_G is partially proper, representable in locally spatial diamonds and cohomologically smooth.)
items.note: BG4 plans: "Construct the filtered-bundle chart M_b with associated graded geometrically E_b. Prove representability, partial properness and cohomological smoothness over [*/J_b(E)] and for M_b → Bun_G in FS V.3's precise sense. Establish surjectivity/covering of the neighborhoods it is intended to cover, compatibility with HN strata and dimension." Proof via the Jacobian criterion Theorem IV.4.2 applied to Z = E ×^G Fl → X_S^alg (Fl a disjoint union of projective flag schemes classifying Q-filtrations of the fibre functor), tangent bundle Q_{>0}-filtered with semistable positive-slope graded pieces. BG4: "The proof uses the FS IV Jacobian theorem from VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories VS1".

items.name: Theorem V.3.7(b): image of π_b
items.statement: Standing conventions of Chapter V: k|F_q algebraically closed, work on Perf_k; Λ a ring with nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. The image of π_b : M_b → Bun_G is open, and consists exactly of the set of points of |Bun_G| specializing to b.
items.note: BG4 plans: "Construct the filtered-bundle chart M_b with associated graded geometrically E_b. Prove representability, partial properness and cohomological smoothness over [*/J_b(E)] and for M_b → Bun_G in FS V.3's precise sense. Establish surjectivity/covering of the neighborhoods it is intended to cover, compatibility with HN strata and dimension." ("Establish surjectivity/covering of the neighborhoods it is intended to cover"). Openness from cohomological smoothness; converse via the explicit degeneration in the proof of Prop. V.3.6. For GL_n: Hansen [Han17]; [BFH+22] determines the image of π_b for GL_n.

items.name: Theorem V.4.1(a): D_ét(U,Λ) compactly generated
items.statement: Standing conventions of Chapter V: k|F_q algebraically closed, work on Perf_k; Λ a ring with nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. For any locally closed substack U ⊂ Bun_G, the triangulated category D_ét(U, Λ) is compactly generated.
items.note: VS4 plans: "Prove localization triangles and the infinite semiorthogonal decomposition along the HN strata using justified exhaustions. Characterize compact objects by compact restrictions with finite stratum support, and by the thick closure of compact induction from pro-p open subgroups." Generators: A^b_K = Rf_{K!}Rf_K^!Λ for b ∈ |U| and K ⊂ G_b(E) open pro-p.

items.name: Theorem V.4.1(b): characterization of compact objects
items.statement: Standing conventions of Chapter V: k|F_q algebraically closed, work on Perf_k; Λ a ring with nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. For any locally closed substack U ⊂ Bun_G, an object A ∈ D_ét(U, Λ) is compact if and only if for all b ∈ B(G) contained in U, the restriction i^{b∗}A ∈ D_ét(Bun_G^b, Λ) ≅ D(G_b(E), Λ) along i^b : Bun_G^b ⊂ Bun_G is compact, and zero for almost all b. Here, compactness in D(G_b(E), Λ) is equivalent to lying in the thick triangulated subcategory generated by c-Ind_K^{G_b(E)} Λ as K runs over open pro-p-subgroups of G_b(E).
items.note: VS4 plans: "Prove localization triangles and the infinite semiorthogonal decomposition along the HN strata using justified exhaustions. Characterize compact objects by compact restrictions with finite stratum support, and by the thick closure of compact induction from pro-p open subgroups." Proof by induction on |U| finite, showing j^∗ and !-extension from strata preserve compacts; uses that M̃_b° is a spatial diamond of finite dim.trg (Props. V.3.5, V.3.6). Compact induction itself: SR.2.

items.name: Proposition V.4.2: RΓ(M̃_b, A) = stalk at the closed point
items.statement: Standing conventions of Chapter V: k|F_q algebraically closed, work on Perf_k; Λ a ring with nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. Let b ∈ B(G). For any A ∈ D_ét(M̃_b, Λ) with stalk A_0 = i^∗A ∈ D_ét(∗, Λ) ≅ D(Λ) at the closed point i : ∗ ⊂ M̃_b, the map RΓ(M̃_b, A) → A_0 is an isomorphism. In particular, RΓ(M̃_b, −) commutes with all direct sums.
items.note: Step of VS4 plans: "Prove localization triangles and the infinite semiorthogonal decomposition along the HN strata using justified exhaustions. Characterize compact objects by compact restrictions with finite stratum support, and by the thick closure of compact induction from pro-p open subgroups." (not named explicitly). Proof: reduce to A = j_!A′ and show RΓ(M̃_b, j_!A′) = 0 by Theorem IV.5.3 with X = M̃_b°, S = Spa k((t)), the partial compactification M̃_b° ⊂ M̃_b compactifying towards one end (Frobenius/U_π dynamics of Prop. V.3.6).

items.name: Remark V.4.3: cohomology of Spd of adic rings
items.statement: (i) For X = Spd(k[[x_1,…,x_d]]) and U = X \ V(x_1,…,x_d), for any A ∈ D_ét(X, Λ) one has RΓ(X, A) ≅ i^∗A where i : Spd(k) ↪ X is V(x_1,…,x_d). (ii) More generally, for a W(k)-affine formal scheme Spf(R) with R an I-adic ring for a finitely generated ideal I, for any A ∈ D_ét(Spd(R), Λ) one has RΓ(Spd(R), A) = RΓ(Spd(R/I), i^∗A) with i : Spd(R/I) ↪ Spd(R); in particular, for A ∈ D_ét(Spd(R) \ V(I), Λ) one has RΓ(Spd(R) \ V(I), A) ≅ RΓ(Spd(R/I), i^∗Rj_∗A).
items.note: Asserted in a remark without proof (by analogy with Prop. V.4.2); interprets V.4.2 as 'nearby cycles on the strict henselization of Bun_G at b'. Not used later in the chapter. No stage plans it.

items.name: Corollary V.4.4: RΓ(M̃_b/K, A) = V^K
items.statement: Standing conventions of Chapter V: k|F_q algebraically closed, work on Perf_k; Λ a ring with nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. Let b ∈ B(G) and let K ⊂ G_b(E) be an open pro-p-subgroup. Then for any A ∈ D_ét(M̃_b/K, Λ) with pullback A_0 = i^∗A ∈ D_ét([∗/K], Λ) ≅ D(K, Λ) corresponding to a complex V of smooth K-representations, the map RΓ(M̃_b/K, A) → RΓ([∗/K], A_0) ≅ V^K is an isomorphism. In particular, RΓ(M̃_b/K, −) commutes with all direct sums.
items.note: Step of VS4 plans: "Prove localization triangles and the infinite semiorthogonal decomposition along the HN strata using justified exhaustions. Characterize compact objects by compact restrictions with finite stratum support, and by the thick closure of compact induction from pro-p open subgroups.". Formal from V.4.2 by descent along ψ : M̃_b → M̃_b/K (A a direct summand of ψ_∗ψ^∗A).

items.name: Remark V.4.5: i^∗Rj_∗ via M̃_b°
items.statement: Standing conventions of Chapter V: k|F_q algebraically closed, work on Perf_k; Λ a ring with nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. For i : [∗/G_b(E)] ↪ M_b ↩ M_b° : j, regarding i^∗Rj_∗A ∈ D_ét([∗/G_b(E)], Λ) ≅ D(G_b(E), Λ) as a complex of G_b(E)-representations, it is given by RΓ(M̃_b°, A); as M̃_b° is qcqs of finite cohomological dimension this commutes with all direct sums in A. For GL_2 and E_b = O(1) ⊕ O, M̃_b° = BC(O(−1)[1]) \ {0} = Spa k((t^{1/p^∞}))/SL_1(D), so i^∗Rj_∗A = RΓ(Spa k((t^{1/p^∞}))/SL_1(D), A).
items.note: Deduced from Cor. V.4.4; uses Example II.3.12. Remarks that the gluing of strata is encoded in M̃_b° and that quasicompactness of the absolute M̃_b° is critical (its base change to Spa C is not qc). No stage names it.

items.name: Compact generators A^b_K and Hom formula
items.statement: Standing conventions of Chapter V: k|F_q algebraically closed, work on Perf_k; Λ a ring with nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. For b ∈ B(G) and K ⊂ G_b(E) open pro-p, let f_K : M̃_b/K → Bun_G and A^b_K := Rf_{K!}Rf_K^!Λ ∈ D_ét(Bun_G, Λ). Then A^b_K is compact and R Hom(A^b_K, B) ≅ RΓ(M̃_b/K, f_K^∗B) ≅ (i^{b∗}B)^K for all B. The restriction of A^b_K to Bun_G^b corresponds to c-Ind_K^{G_b(E)} Λ, and for j : U \ {b} ⊂ U, j^∗A^b_K = Rf°_{K!}f°_K^!Λ for f°_K : M̃_b°/K → U \ {b} ⊂ Bun_G.
items.locator: Chapter V, §V.4, proof of Theorem V.4.1, pp. 179–180
items.note: VS4 plans: "Prove localization triangles and the infinite semiorthogonal decomposition along the HN strata using justified exhaustions. Characterize compact objects by compact restrictions with finite stratum support, and by the thick closure of compact induction from pro-p open subgroups." Key ingredient reused in §§V.5–V.7 (R Hom(A^b_K, B) = (i^{b∗}B)^K).

items.name: π_♮ : left adjoint of π^∗
items.statement: Standing conventions of Chapter V: k|F_q algebraically closed, work on Perf_k; Λ a ring with nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. For π : Bun_G → ∗ the (cohomologically smooth) projection, π_♮ : D_ét(Bun_G, Λ) → D(∗, Λ) = D(Λ), A ↦ Rπ_!(A ⊗^L_Λ Rπ^!Λ), is the left adjoint of π^∗.
items.note: VS0: "Construct partial compact-support functors of FS IV.5 for stacks whose structural map is not in the original representable ECD class... notation pi-sharp for an Artin stack is not an unqualified ordinary ECD Rpi!." VS5 uses 'the partial-support functor'.

items.name: Footnote 3: Rπ^!Λ ≅ Λ[0]
items.statement: Standing conventions of Chapter V: k|F_q algebraically closed, work on Perf_k; Λ a ring with nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. For π : Bun_G → ∗, the dualizing sheaf Rπ^!Λ is isomorphic to Λ[0], by fixing a Haar measure on G_b(E) for each basic b ∈ B(G); hence π_♮ ≅ Rπ_!. (Uses that local systems concentrated in degree 0 on Bun_G embed fully faithfully into local systems on the semistable locus, from purity and smoothness of all Harder–Narasimhan strata.)
items.locator: Chapter V, §V.5, footnote 3, p. 180; used in proof of Theorem V.5.1, p. 181
items.note: Sketched in footnote 3 only; the proof of Theorem V.5.1 (p. 181) fixes Haar measures on G_b(E) for all basic b to get Rπ^!Λ ≅ Λ 'at generic points, but then by spreading out everywhere, noting that both are invertible'. Planned by the VS5 packet node VS5/bernstein-zelevinsky-duality, whose first proof step is exactly this ('Fix Haar measures on G_b(E) for all basic b to get Rpi^! Lambda = Lambda (at generic points, then by spreading out everywhere, noting both are invertible), and hence pi_sharp = Rpi_!') and whose hypotheses record the footnote's purity argument. The dualizing complex itself is VS0's construction (node VS0/shriek-pullback-for-smooth-stacky-maps). §V.6 also recalls that D_{Bun_G} is locally isomorphic to Λ[0].

items.name: Theorem V.5.1(a): existence of Bernstein–Zelevinsky dual
items.statement: Standing conventions of Chapter V: k|F_q algebraically closed, work on Perf_k; Λ a ring with nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. For any compact object A ∈ D_ét(Bun_G, Λ), there is a unique compact object D_BZ(A) ∈ D_ét(Bun_G, Λ) with a functorial identification R Hom(D_BZ(A), B) ≅ π_♮(A ⊗^L_Λ B) for B ∈ D_ét(Bun_G, Λ).
items.note: VS5 plans: "Construct Bernstein–Zelevinsky duality on compact Bun_G objects using the partial-support functor; prove biduality and its basic-stratum comparison." Proof: for A = Rg_{K!}Λ with g_K : [∗/K] → Bun_G, D_BZ(A) = A^b_K by Cor. V.4.4.

items.name: Theorem V.5.1(b): D_BZ is an involutive anti-autoequivalence
items.statement: Standing conventions of Chapter V: k|F_q algebraically closed, work on Perf_k; Λ a ring with nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. The functor D_BZ is a contravariant autoequivalence of D_ét(Bun_G, Λ)^ω, and D_BZ² is naturally isomorphic to the identity.
items.note: VS5 plans: "Construct Bernstein–Zelevinsky duality on compact Bun_G objects using the partial-support functor; prove biduality and its basic-stratum comparison." Proof checks D_BZ²(A) → A on generators, reducing to RΓ_c(M̃_b/K, Rj_{K∗}A′) = 0 via Theorem IV.5.3.

items.name: Theorem V.5.1(c): D_BZ preserves support on open substacks
items.statement: Standing conventions of Chapter V: k|F_q algebraically closed, work on Perf_k; Λ a ring with nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. If U ⊂ Bun_G is an open substack and the compact object A is concentrated on U, then so is D_BZ(A). In particular, D_BZ restricts to an autoequivalence of the compact objects in D_ét(Bun_G^b, Λ) ≅ D(G_b(E), Λ) for b ∈ B(G) basic.
items.note: VS5 plans: "Construct Bernstein–Zelevinsky duality on compact Bun_G objects using the partial-support functor; prove biduality and its basic-stratum comparison."

items.name: Theorem V.5.1(d): comparison with classical Bernstein–Zelevinsky involution
items.statement: Standing conventions of Chapter V: k|F_q algebraically closed, work on Perf_k; Λ a ring with nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. For b ∈ B(G) basic, the restriction of D_BZ to compact objects of D(G_b(E), Λ) is the usual Bernstein–Zelevinsky involution, i.e. R Hom into the regular representation of G_b(E) (with its residual G_b(E)-action from the second commuting action).
items.note: VS5 plans: "Construct Bernstein–Zelevinsky duality on compact Bun_G objects using the partial-support functor; prove biduality and its basic-stratum comparison." ('basic-stratum comparison'). Classical: Zelevinsky [Zel80], Aubert [Aub95], Bernstein, Schneider–Stuhler [SS97]; categorical form [Far06]. Also shows D_BZ(i^b_! c-Ind_K^{G_b(E)}Λ) ↔ A^b_K. Used in Chapter IX (ES6 per ExcursionOperators roadmap).

items.name: Theorem V.6.1: j_! commutes with Λ-duality
items.statement: Standing conventions of Chapter V: k|F_q algebraically closed, work on Perf_k; Λ a ring with nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. Let j : V ↪ U be an open immersion of open substacks of Bun_G. For any A ∈ D_ét(V, Λ), the natural map j_! RHom_Λ(A, Λ) → RHom_Λ(Rj_∗A, Λ) is an isomorphism in D_ét(U, Λ).
items.note: VS5 plans: "Separately construct Verdier duality on ULA objects and prove that ULA is equivalent to perfection of K-invariants on every stratum for every appropriate pro-p open K." (the Verdier-duality part; V.6.1 itself not named). Proof tests against A^b_K using R Hom(A^b_K, −) = (i^{b∗}−)^K and π_♮/Theorem V.5.1.

items.name: Consequence of V.6.1: j_! preserves reflexivity
items.statement: Standing conventions of Chapter V: k|F_q algebraically closed, work on Perf_k; Λ a ring with nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. For j : V ↪ U an open immersion of open substacks of Bun_G, one always has Rj_∗RHom_Λ(A, Λ) = RHom_Λ(j_!A, Λ); by Theorem V.6.1, if A ∈ D_ét(V, Λ) is reflexive then j_!A ∈ D_ét(U, Λ) is reflexive.
items.locator: Chapter V, §V.6, after Theorem V.6.1, p. 182
items.note: VS5 plans: "Separately construct Verdier duality on ULA objects and prove that ULA is equivalent to perfection of K-invariants on every stratum for every appropriate pro-p open K."

items.name: Theorem V.6.2: reflexivity is checked on strata
items.statement: Standing conventions of Chapter V: k|F_q algebraically closed, work on Perf_k; Λ a ring with nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. Let D_{Bun_G} ∈ D_ét(Bun_G, Λ) be the dualizing complex (locally isomorphic to Λ[0]). For any open substack U ⊂ Bun_G, an object A ∈ D_ét(U, Λ) is reflexive, i.e. the natural map A → RHom_Λ(RHom_Λ(A, D_U), D_U) is an equivalence, if and only if for all b ∈ B(G) lying in U with corresponding locally closed stratum i^b : Bun_G^b → U, the restriction i^{b∗}A ∈ D_ét(Bun_G^b, Λ) = D_ét([∗/G̃_b], Λ) ≅ D_ét([∗/G_b(E)], Λ) = D(G_b(E), Λ) is reflexive as a complex of admissible G_b(E)-representations; this means that the complex of K-invariants is reflexive in D(Λ) for all open pro-p-subgroups K ⊂ G_b(E).
items.note: VS5 plans: "Separately construct Verdier duality on ULA objects and prove that ULA is equivalent to perfection of K-invariants on every stratum for every appropriate pro-p open K." In the definition D_U may be replaced by Λ. Follows immediately from Lemma V.6.3.

items.name: Lemma V.6.3: biduality commutes with restriction to strata
items.statement: Standing conventions of Chapter V: k|F_q algebraically closed, work on Perf_k; Λ a ring with nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. Let U ⊂ Bun_G be an open substack and A ∈ D_ét(U, Λ). For any b ∈ B(G) lying in U, there is a natural isomorphism i^{b∗}RHom_Λ(RHom_Λ(A, Λ), Λ) ≅ RHom_Λ(RHom_Λ(i^{b∗}A, Λ), Λ).
items.note: VS5 plans: "Separately construct Verdier duality on ULA objects and prove that ULA is equivalent to perfection of K-invariants on every stratum for every appropriate pro-p open K." Proof: excision triangle j_!B → A → i^b_∗i^{b∗}A, invertibility of i^{b!}Λ, and Theorem V.6.1.

items.name: Theorem V.7.1: ULA sheaves on Bun_G are the admissible ones
items.statement: Standing conventions of Chapter V: k|F_q algebraically closed, work on Perf_k; Λ a ring with nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. Let A ∈ D_ét(Bun_G, Λ). Then A is universally locally acyclic with respect to Bun_G → ∗ if and only if for all b ∈ B(G), the pullback i^{b∗}A to i^b : Bun_G^b ↪ Bun_G corresponds under D_ét(Bun_G^b, Λ) ≅ D(G_b(E), Λ) to a complex M_b of smooth G_b(E)-representations for which M_b^K is a perfect complex of Λ-modules for all open pro-p subgroups K ⊂ G_b(E).
items.note: VS5 plans: "Separately construct Verdier duality on ULA objects and prove that ULA is equivalent to perfection of K-invariants on every stratum for every appropriate pro-p open K." Proof uses Proposition IV.2.32 (ULA ⇔ p_1^∗RHom(A,Λ) ⊗ p_2^∗A → RHom(p_1^∗A, p_2^∗A) iso) and Proposition V.7.2.

items.name: ULA ⇔ π_♮(A_1 ⊗ A) perfect
items.statement: Standing conventions of Chapter V: k|F_q algebraically closed, work on Perf_k; Λ a ring with nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. An object A ∈ D_ét(Bun_G, Λ) is universally locally acyclic with respect to Bun_G → ∗ if and only if π_♮(A_1 ⊗^L_Λ A) ∈ D(Λ) is perfect for all compact A_1 ∈ D_ét(Bun_G, Λ).
items.locator: Chapter V, §V.7, proof of Theorem V.7.1, p. 184
items.note: VS5 plans: "Separately construct Verdier duality on ULA objects and prove that ULA is equivalent to perfection of K-invariants on every stratum for every appropriate pro-p open K." Converse direction uses A_2 = D_BZ(A_1) and dualizable = perfect in D(Λ).

items.name: Proposition V.7.2: Künneth for Bun_{G_1 × G_2}
items.statement: Standing conventions of Chapter V: k|F_q algebraically closed, work on Perf_k; Λ a ring with nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. Let G_1 and G_2 be two reductive groups over E, and let G = G_1 × G_2. Then Bun_G ≅ Bun_{G_1} × Bun_{G_2}, giving rise to an exterior tensor product − ⊠ − : D_ét(Bun_{G_1}, Λ) × D_ét(Bun_{G_2}, Λ) → D_ét(Bun_G, Λ). For all compact objects A_i ∈ D_ét(Bun_{G_i}, Λ), i = 1, 2, the exterior tensor product A_1 ⊠ A_2 ∈ D_ét(Bun_G, Λ) is compact, these objects form a class of compact generators, and for all further objects B_i ∈ D_ét(Bun_{G_i}, Λ), i = 1, 2, the natural map R Hom(A_1, B_1) ⊗^L_Λ R Hom(A_2, B_2) → R Hom(A_1 ⊠ A_2, B_1 ⊠ B_2) is an isomorphism.
items.note: Proof: M_b ≅ M_{b_1} × M_{b_2}, the Künneth formula, A^{b_1}_{K_1} ⊠ A^{b_2}_{K_2} ≅ A^b_K, B(G) = B(G_1) × B(G_2) and cofinality of K_1 × K_2. The VS5 packet node VS5/ula-equals-admissibility states it in full among its hypotheses and uses it in two proof steps of V.7.1, but no node proves it.

items.name: Remark V.7.3: D_ét(Bun_{G_1}) ⊗ D_ét(Bun_{G_2}) ≃ D_ét(Bun_G)
items.statement: Standing conventions of Chapter V: k|F_q algebraically closed, work on Perf_k; Λ a ring with nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. As Λ-linear presentable stable ∞-categories, the exterior tensor product functor D_ét(Bun_{G_1}, Λ) ⊗_{D(Λ)} D_ét(Bun_{G_2}, Λ) → D_ét(Bun_{G_1×G_2}, Λ) is an equivalence (Lurie's tensor product [Lur16, §4.8]).
items.note: Reformulation of Prop. V.7.2 at ∞-categorical level; requires EnhancedDerivedSheaves' enhancement and Lurie tensor product of presentable categories; no stage names it.

items.name: Local Hecke stack and Beilinson–Drinfeld Grassmannian (overview)
items.statement: For d ≥ 0 and affinoid S with a degree d Cartier divisor D ⊂ 𝒴_S, let B⁺ be the completion along D and B = B⁺ localized by inverting D; L⁺G = L⁺_{Div^d_𝒴}G and LG = L_{Div^d_𝒴}G have values G(B⁺) resp. G(B). The local Hecke stack is 𝓗ck_{G,Div^d_𝒴} = [L⁺G\LG/L⁺G] → Div^d_𝒴, the Beilinson–Drinfeld Grassmannian is Gr_{G,Div^d_𝒴} = LG/L⁺G → Div^d_𝒴, so that 𝓗ck_{G,Div^d_𝒴} = L⁺G\Gr_{G,Div^d_𝒴}. Gr_{G,Div^d_𝒴} → Div^d_𝒴 is a small v-sheaf that is an increasing union of closed subsheaves proper and representable in spatial diamonds (bounding relative position); L⁺G is an inverse limit of truncated positive loop groups, representable in locally spatial diamonds and cohomologically smooth, and on each bounded subset acts through such a finite-dimensional quotient.
items.note: Overview of VI.1–VI.2; GS0:loop-geometry plans 'Construct `L+G`, `LG`, the étale quotient `LG/L+G` and double quotient local Hecke stack'. Printed 'completion B⁺ of O_{X_S} along D' with D ⊂ 𝒴_S (PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E35). Precise versions: Definitions VI.1.5–VI.1.8, Propositions VI.1.7, VI.1.9, VI.2.3, VI.2.7, VI.2.8.

items.name: Bounded Hecke category and convolution product
items.statement: For a small v-stack S → Div^d_𝒴 put 𝓗ck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴} = 𝓗ck_{G,Div^d_𝒴} ×_{Div^d_𝒴} S and let D_ét(𝓗ck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴},Λ)^bd ⊂ D_ét(𝓗ck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴},Λ) be the full subcategory of objects with quasicompact support over Div^d_𝒴. It is monoidal under convolution A ⋆ B = Rm_*(p_1^*A ⊗^L_Λ p_2^*B), using the diagram 𝓗ck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴} ×_S 𝓗ck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴} ←(p_1,p_2)− L⁺G\LG ×^{L⁺G} LG/L⁺G −m→ 𝓗ck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴}.
items.note: GS2:correspondences: 'Construct convolution diagrams, the convolution map and operation in the ambient bounded-support derived category via actual proper-support pushforward.' The monoidal structure is established in §VI.8.
