items.name: Convolution is left t-exact for relative perverse t-structure (announced)
items.statement: On D_ét(𝓗ck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴},Λ)^bd there is a relative perverse t-structure (an object is perverse iff it is perverse over every geometric fibre of S), compatible with any base change in S; convolution ⋆ is left t-exact for it (t-exactness only fails for issues related to non-flatness over Λ). Universal local acyclicity over S is preserved under convolution. For d = 1, or when S maps to (Div^d_𝒴)_≠, universally locally acyclic objects are characterized by local constancy with perfect fibres of the restriction to every Schubert cell.
items.note: Forward announcement (proved in §§VI.6–VI.8). GS1: 'Construct the relative perverse t-structure on bounded constructible complexes'; GS2:Satake-closure: 'prove perversity, flatness and ULA preservation'. The ULA characterization is Propositions VI.6.5/VI.6.8 in this range.

items.name: Satake category (Definition VI.0.1)
items.statement: The Satake category Sat(𝓗ck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴},Λ) ⊂ D_ét(𝓗ck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴},Λ)^bd is the category of all A ∈ D_ét(𝓗ck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴},Λ)^bd that are perverse, flat over Λ (i.e., for all Λ-modules M, also A ⊗^L_Λ M is perverse), and universally locally acyclic over S.
items.locator: Chapter VI, introduction, Definition VI.0.1, p. 188
items.note: GS2:correspondences: 'Define Satake objects by the equivariance, relative perversity, ULA and coefficient flatness conditions of FS VI.6–VI.8.' The printed 'universally locally acyclic over (Div^1)^I' is corrected to 'over S' (PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E36): it was copied from Chapter I's definition of Sat^I_G, whose base is (Div^1)^I. Definition VI.7.8 (p. 219) later repeats the definition for any small v-stack S → Div^d_𝒴.

items.name: Satake category is monoidal and embeds fully faithfully into sheaves on Gr
items.statement: Sat(𝓗ck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴},Λ) is a monoidal category under convolution, and the forgetful functor Sat(𝓗ck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴},Λ) → D_ét(Gr_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴},Λ) is fully faithful. For d = 1 the categories for S = Spd O_C and S = Spd C (C = completed algebraic closure of E) are naturally equivalent, via base change, to the category for S = Spd F̄_q, which compares to the Witt-vector affine Grassmannian category of Zhu and Yu.
items.note: Announced here; proved later in Chapter VI (§§VI.7–VI.8, outside this range); the base-change equivalence rests on Corollary VI.6.7. GS1: 'Construct the one-leg special/generic-fibre comparison on the ULA, flat-perverse categories over Spd(O_C), Spd(C) and Spd(k̄)'.

items.name: Fusion product and symmetric monoidal structure on Sat^I_G
items.statement: Put 𝓗ck^I_G = 𝓗ck_{G,(Div^1_X)^I} and Sat^I_G(Λ) = Sat(𝓗ck^I_G,Λ). For I = I_1 ⊔ … ⊔ I_k, over the open (Div^1)^{I;I_1,…,I_k} ⊂ (Div^1)^I where x_i ≠ x_{i'} whenever i, i' lie in different I_j, one has 𝓗ck^I_G ×_{(Div^1)^I} (Div^1)^{I;I_1,…,I_k} ≅ ∏_{j=1}^k 𝓗ck^{I_j}_G ×_{(Div^1)^I} (Div^1)^{I;I_1,…,I_k}; the restriction functor Sat^I_G(Λ) → Sat^{I;I_1,…,I_k}_G(Λ) is fully faithful and the exterior product ⊠ lands in its essential image, giving ∗_{j=1}^k : ∏_j Sat^{I_j}_G(Λ) → Sat^I_G(Λ), independent of ordering; with functoriality in I this defines a symmetric monoidal structure ∗ on Sat^I_G(Λ) commuting with ⋆ (hence agreeing with ⋆), after modifying the commutativity constraint by signs depending on the parity of supports.
items.note: GS3:fusion: 'Over disjoint-leg loci prove factorization into products of single-leg Grassmannians. Construct fusion ... obtain the commutativity constraint. Verify the Koszul/sign ... normalization'. Proved in §VI.9. Also uses the Eckmann–Hilton-type fact that a commuting monoidal structure agrees with a symmetric monoidal one.

items.name: Fibre functor F^I to W_E^I-representations
items.statement: Restricting A ∈ Sat^I_G(Λ) to Gr^I_G and pushing forward to (Div^1)^I, all cohomology sheaves are local systems of Λ-modules on (Div^1)^I, which by a version of Drinfeld's lemma are equivalent to representations of W_E^I; this defines a symmetric monoidal fibre functor F^I : Sat^I_G(Λ) → Rep_{W_E^I}(Λ), where Rep_{W_E^I}(Λ) is the category of continuous representations of W_E^I on finite projective Λ-modules. By Tannaka duality Sat^I_G(Λ) is the category of representations of a Hopf algebra in Ind(Rep_{W_E^I}(Λ)), the I-fold tensor power of the one for I = {∗}, given by an affine group scheme Ǧ over Λ with W_E-action.
items.note: GS4:integral-dual-group: 'Construct the total cohomology fibre functor, prove exactness, faithfulness, tensor compatibility and duals ... and reconstruct its affine group scheme'; VS1: 'Establish Drinfeld's lemma IV.7'. Proved in §VI.10.

items.name: Geometric Satake equivalence (Theorem VI.0.2 = VI.11.1)
items.statement: There is a canonical isomorphism Ǧ ≅ Ĝ with the Langlands dual group, under which the action of W_E on Ǧ agrees with the usual action of W_E on Ĝ up to an explicit cyclotomic twist. If √q ∈ Λ, the cyclotomic twist can be trivialized, and Sat^I_G(Λ) is naturally equivalent to the category of (Ĝ ⋊ W_E)^I-representations on finite projective Λ-modules.
items.locator: Chapter VI, introduction, Theorem VI.0.2 (= Theorem VI.11.1), p. 190
items.note: Main result of Chapter VI; stated here, proved in §VI.11 (outside this range). GS4:integral-dual-group: 'identify the group with the pinned dual ... distinguish the geometric Weil action from the standard pinned action, with the normalization isomorphism involving rho and the chosen sqrt(q)'. Proof sketch (p. 190): reduce to Λ = Z/ℓ^n, pass to Z_ℓ; generic fibre reductive via semisimplicity (decomposition theorem on Witt Grassmannian, GS4:rational-reductivity); tori, rank 1 via PGL_2 minuscule cell; Levi functors Sat_G → Sat_M via hyperbolic localization; integrality via Ĝ(Z_ℓ) maximal compact generated by rank 1 Levis (Bruhat–Tits).

items.name: Switch involution is the twisted Chevalley involution (Proposition VI.0.3 = VI.12.1)
items.statement: The local Hecke stack 𝓗ck^I_G has the involution sw reversing the roles of the two G-torsors (induced by inversion on LG); sw^* induces an involution of Sat^I_G(Λ) upgrading to a symmetric monoidal functor commuting with the fibre functor, hence a W_E-equivariant automorphism of Ǧ ≅ Ĝ. Proposition: the action of sw^* on Sat^I_G induces the automorphism of Ĝ that is the Chevalley involution of the split group Ĝ, conjugated by ρ̂(−1).
items.locator: Chapter VI, introduction, Proposition VI.0.3 (= Proposition VI.12.1), p. 190
items.note: GS4:integral-dual-group: 'Construct the Chevalley involution and prove its compatibility with Verdier duality, inversion of modifications and representation duals.' Proved in §VI.12 (outside range). Used for duality in Chapters IX–X.

items.name: Div^d_𝒴, Div^d_Y, Div^d_X (Definition VI.1.1)
items.statement: For any d ≥ 0, consider the small v-sheaves on Perf_{F_q} given by Div^d_𝒴 = (Spd O_E)^d/Σ_d, Div^d_Y = (Spd E)^d/Σ_d, Div^d_X = Div^d = (Spd E/φ^ℤ)^d/Σ_d, where Σ_d is the symmetric group (quotients taken in v-sheaves; they are still small).
items.note: RF2:integral-divisors: 'Construct `Div^d_𝒴=(Spd O_E)^d/Σ_d`, with the quotient understood as a v-sheaf ... Construct Div^d_X by Frobenius descent'. Library audit: no Spd/v-sheaf in either library.

items.name: Div^d maps injectively to closed Cartier divisors (Proposition VI.1.2)
items.statement: For any d ≥ 0, there is a functorial injection (i) from Div^d_𝒴(S) into the set of closed Cartier divisors on 𝒴_S, (ii) from Div^d_Y(S) into the set of closed Cartier divisors on Y_S, (iii) from Div^d_X(S) into the set of closed Cartier divisors on X_S. Moreover, in case (i) and (ii), if S = Spa(R,R⁺) is affinoid perfectoid, then for any closed Cartier divisor D ⊂ 𝒴_S resp. D ⊂ Y_S in the image of this embedding, the adic space D = Spa(Q,Q⁺) is affinoid. In case (iii), the same happens locally in the analytic topology on S.
items.note: RF2:integral-divisors: 'prove FS VI.1.1–VI.1.4: its map into relative degree-d closed Cartier divisors on 𝒴_S ... affineness of the divisor for affinoid S'. Proof: product ξ = ∏ξ_i of primitive elements, Proposition II.1.4, v-descent of line bundles [SW20, Prop. 19.5.3].

items.name: Div^d(S) = relative Cartier divisors of degree d (Remark VI.1.3)
items.statement: As in [Far20b], Div^d_𝒴(S) is the set of 'relative Cartier divisors' of degree d, i.e. Cartier divisors that give degree d Cartier divisors when pulled back via any geometric point Spa(C,C⁺) → S. The same holds for Div^d_Y and Div^d_X.
items.note: RF2:integral-divisors: 'the geometric degree criterion'. Stated without proof (reference to Fargues [Far20b]).

items.name: Vector bundles on D_S form a v-stack (Proposition VI.1.4)
items.statement: For a perfectoid space S with a map f : S → Div^d_𝒴 (resp. Div^d_Y, Div^d_X) and corresponding closed Cartier divisor D_S ⊂ 𝒴_S (resp. Y_S, X_S), sending S to the category of vector bundles on D_S defines a v-stack.
items.note: RF2:integral-divisors: 'v-descent for bundles on that divisor and its infinitesimal thickenings'. Proof: geometric points via [SW20, Lemma 17.1.8]; étale case via de Jong–van der Put / [KL15, Prop. 8.2.20]; general v-case by approximation using almost vanishing of H^1_v(S, O(𝒴_{[0,n]})⁺).

items.name: Completed rings B⁺_{Div^d} and B_{Div^d}
items.statement: Assuming D_S affinoid (locally on S), B⁺_{Div^d_𝒴}(S) (resp. B⁺_{Div^d_Y}(S), B⁺_{Div^d_X}(S)) is the global sections of the completion of O_{𝒴_S} along I_S (resp. O_{Y_S}, O_{X_S}), and B_{Div^d_{(−)}}(S) = B⁺_{Div^d_{(−)}}(S)[1/I_S]. This defines v-sheaves B⁺_{Div^d_{(−)}} ⊂ B_{Div^d_{(−)}} over Div^d_{(−)}; for d = 1 these are B⁺_dR resp. B_dR.
items.note: RF2:integral-divisors: 'Construct the completed sheaf B_D^+ and B_D=B_D^+[1/I_D], independently of equation and ordering.' Mathlib has only the classical period ring B_dR^+ of C_p-type (library audit), not this relative sheaf.

items.name: Positive loop space and loop space (Definition VI.1.5)
items.statement: Let Z be an affine scheme over O_E. The positive loop space L⁺_{Div^d_𝒴}Z (resp. loop space L_{Div^d_𝒴}Z) of Z is the v-sheaf over Div^d_𝒴 given by S ↦ L⁺_{Div^d_𝒴}Z(S) = Z(B⁺_{Div^d_𝒴}(S)) (resp. S ↦ L_{Div^d_𝒴}Z(S) = Z(B_{Div^d_𝒴}(S))). Similarly, if Z is an affine scheme over E, one defines L⁺_{Div^d_Y}Z and L⁺_{Div^d_X}Z (resp. L_{Div^d_Y}Z and L_{Div^d_X}Z).
items.note: GS0:loop-geometry: 'Construct `L+G`, `LG`' and 'FS VI.1.5–VI.1.10 supplies the exact local construction'. Affineness of Z is used to get v-sheaves.

items.name: Local Hecke stack (Definition VI.1.6)
items.statement: Let G be a reductive group over O_E (resp. over E, resp. over E). The local Hecke stack 𝓗ck_{G,Div^d_𝒴} (resp. 𝓗ck_{G,Div^d_Y}, resp. 𝓗ck_{G,Div^d_X}) is the functor sending an affinoid perfectoid S → Div^d_𝒴 (resp. S → Div^d_Y, resp. S → Div^d_X, assuming that D_S is affinoid) to the groupoid of pairs of G-bundles 𝓔_1, 𝓔_2 over B⁺_{Div^d_𝒴}(S) (resp. B⁺_{Div^d_Y}(S), resp. B⁺_{Div^d_X}(S)) together with an isomorphism 𝓔_1 ≅ 𝓔_2 over B_{Div^d_𝒴}(S) (resp. B_{Div^d_Y}(S), resp. B_{Div^d_X}(S)).
items.note: GS0:loop-geometry: 'double quotient local Hecke stack; prove the torsor interpretation'. G-bundles are algebraic, on the spectrum of the rings; Tannakian viewpoint as in Chapter III.

items.name: Local Hecke stack is a small v-stack, double-coset presentation (Proposition VI.1.7)
items.statement: The local Hecke stack 𝓗ck_{G,Div^d_𝒴} (resp. 𝓗ck_{G,Div^d_Y}, resp. 𝓗ck_{G,Div^d_X}) is a small v-stack. There is a natural isomorphism of étale stacks over Div^d_𝒴 (resp. Div^d_Y, resp. Div^d_X) 𝓗ck_{G,Div^d_𝒴} ≅ (L⁺_{Div^d_𝒴}G)\(L_{Div^d_𝒴}G)/(L⁺_{Div^d_𝒴}G) (resp. with Div^d_Y, resp. Div^d_X).
items.note: GS0:loop-geometry: 'prove the torsor interpretation and descent of finite projective modules on the completed divisor rings'. Proof: v-descent of vector bundles over B⁺ modulo powers of I_S (Prop. VI.1.4), Tannakian formalism, smallness as in Prop. III.1.3; G-bundles over B⁺ are étale-locally trivial via [GR03, Prop. 5.4.21].

items.name: G-bundles over B⁺_{Div^d} are étale-locally trivial
items.statement: Any G-bundle over B⁺_{Div^d_𝒴}(S) is étale locally on S trivial. (If S is a geometric point, B⁺_{Div^d_𝒴}(S) is a product of complete discrete valuation rings with algebraically closed residue field; in general triviality is implied by triviality modulo I_S.)
items.locator: Chapter VI, §VI.1, proof of Proposition VI.1.7, p. 193
items.note: Key unnumbered fact used for the presentations in VI.1.7/VI.1.9. GS0:loop-geometry: 'changes of trivialization'. Uses [GR03, Proposition 5.4.21] (Gabber–Ramero henselian pair lifting).

items.name: Beilinson–Drinfeld Grassmannian (Definition VI.1.8)
items.statement: Let G be a reductive group over O_E (resp. over E, resp. over E). The Beilinson–Drinfeld Grassmannian Gr_{G,Div^d_𝒴} (resp. Gr_{G,Div^d_Y}, resp. Gr_{G,Div^d_X}) is the functor sending an affinoid perfectoid S → Div^d_𝒴 (resp. S → Div^d_Y, resp. S → Div^d_X, assuming again that D_S is affinoid) to the groupoid of G-bundles 𝓔 over B⁺_{Div^d_𝒴}(S) (resp. B⁺_{Div^d_Y}(S), resp. B⁺_{Div^d_X}(S)) together with a trivialization of 𝓔 over B_{Div^d_𝒴}(S) (resp. B_{Div^d_Y}(S), resp. B_{Div^d_X}(S)).
items.note: GS0:loop-geometry: 'the relative Grassmannian of a G-bundle with trivialization off those divisors'. Library audit: Mathlib Module.Grassmannian is the finite-dimensional Grassmannian only; no affine Grassmannian.

items.name: Gr is a small v-sheaf, Gr = LG/L⁺G (Proposition VI.1.9)
items.statement: The Beilinson–Drinfeld Grassmannian Gr_{G,Div^d_𝒴} (resp. Gr_{G,Div^d_Y}, resp. Gr_{G,Div^d_X}) is a small v-sheaf. There is a natural isomorphism of étale sheaves over Div^d_𝒴 (resp. Div^d_Y, resp. Div^d_X) Gr_{G,Div^d_𝒴} ≅ (L_{Div^d_𝒴}G)/(L⁺_{Div^d_𝒴}G) (resp. with Div^d_Y, resp. Div^d_X).
items.note: GS0:loop-geometry: 'Construct ... the étale quotient `LG/L+G` ... Establish v-sheaf representability'. Proof identical to VI.1.7.

items.name: Principal congruence subgroups (L⁺G)^{≥m}
items.statement: For m ≥ 1, (L⁺_{Div^d_𝒴}G)^{≥m} ⊂ L⁺_{Div^d_𝒴}G is the closed subgroup defined as the kernel of G(B⁺_{Div^d_𝒴}) → G(B⁺_{Div^d_𝒴}/I_S^m); similarly over Div^d_Y and Div^d_X.
items.note: GS0:Schubert-smoothness: 'Construct truncated positive loop groups and their congruence filtration by vector-group quotients'.

items.name: Graded pieces of the congruence filtration, d = 1 (Proposition VI.1.10)
items.statement: There are natural isomorphisms L⁺_{Div^1_𝒴}G/(L⁺_{Div^1_𝒴}G)^{≥1} ≅ G^♢ and (L⁺_{Div^1_𝒴}G)^{≥m}/(L⁺_{Div^1_𝒴}G)^{≥m+1} ≅ (Lie G)^♢{m}, where {m} signifies a 'Breuil–Kisin twist' by I_S^m/I_S^{m+1}. (Also for Div^1_Y, Div^1_X.) Here G^♢ sends S = Spa(R,R⁺) to an untilt R^♯ of R and an element of G(R^♯).
items.note: GS0:Schubert-smoothness: 'congruence filtration by vector-group quotients'; GS0:loop-geometry cites 'FS VI.1.5–VI.1.10'. Proof via the exponential.

items.name: Congruence graded pieces for general d (Proposition VI.1.11)
items.statement: For any d and m ≥ 1, the quotient (L⁺_{Div^d_𝒴}G)^{≥m}/(L⁺_{Div^d_𝒴}G)^{≥m+1} sends a perfectoid space S → Div^d_𝒴 with corresponding Cartier divisor D_S ⊂ 𝒴_S with ideal sheaf I_S to (Lie G ⊗_{O_E} I_S^m/I_S^{m+1})(S), where I_S^m/I_S^{m+1} is a line bundle on D_S. This is representable in locally spatial diamonds, partially proper, and cohomologically smooth of ℓ-dimension equal to d times the dimension of G. Moreover, one can filter (L⁺_{Div^d_𝒴}G)^{≥m}/(L⁺_{Div^d_𝒴}G)^{≥m+1} ×_{Div^d_𝒴} (Div^1_𝒴)^d with subquotients given by twists of (Lie G)^♢ ×_{Div^1_𝒴,π_i} (Div^1_𝒴)^d, where π_i : (Div^1_𝒴)^d → Div^1_𝒴 is the projection to the i-th factor.
items.note: GS0:Schubert-smoothness: 'prove cohomological smoothness'. Filtration of O_{D_S} by O/I_1, I_1/I_1I_2, …; uses smoothness of the perfectoid affine line (DiamondSixOperations S5).

items.name: Mapping spaces T_Z are cohomologically smooth (Proposition VI.1.12)
items.statement: For any d, the quotient L⁺_{Div^d_𝒴}G/(L⁺_{Div^d_𝒴}G)^{≥1} → Div^d_𝒴 parametrizes over a perfectoid space S → Div^d_𝒴 maps D_S → G. For any quasiprojective smooth scheme Z over O_E, the sheaf T_Z → Div^d_𝒴 taking a perfectoid S over Div^d_𝒴 to maps D_S → Z (of locally ringed spaces) is representable in locally spatial diamonds, partially proper, and cohomologically smooth over Div^d_𝒴 of ℓ-dimension equal to d times the dimension of Z; in particular, this applies to this quotient group.
items.note: GS0:Schubert-smoothness: 'Construct truncated positive loop groups ... prove cohomological smoothness'. Proof: affine space case from VI.1.11 via tower T_{A^n} = W_1 → … → W_{d+1} = (Div^1_𝒴)^d with fibres A^{n,♢}_{S_i^♯}; separated étale Z′ → Z gives separated étale T_{Z′} → T_Z (Lemma VI.1.13); local étale maps to A^d.

items.name: Separated étale maps over D_S come from S (Lemma VI.1.13)
items.statement: Let S be a perfectoid space with a map S → Div^d_𝒴 giving rise to the Cartier divisor D_S ⊂ 𝒴_S. Let D′ → D_S be a separated étale map. Then there is a separated étale map S′ → S such that for T → S, maps T → S′ over S are equivalent to lifts D_T → D′ over D_S.
items.note: Auxiliary to Proposition VI.1.12. The GS0 packet node GS0:loop-geometry/congruence-filtration-and-graded-pieces cites it ('separated etale Z' -> Z gives separated etale T_{Z'} -> T_Z by Lemma VI.1.13') but does not state or prove it. Proof: descent of separated étale maps [Sch17a, Prop. 9.7], reduce to strictly totally disconnected S and quasicompact D′, spread out via [Sch17a, Prop. 11.23, Lemma 15.6], reduce to open immersions, and use that |D_S| → |S| is closed.

items.name: Cartan decomposition: geometric points of Hck_{Div^1} = X_*(T)^+
items.statement: Let G be split over O_E with split torus and Borel T ⊂ B ⊂ G. For a geometric point S = Spa(C,C⁺) → Div^1_𝒴 = Spd O_E given by an untilt S^♯ = Spa(C^♯,C^♯⁺), one has B⁺_{Div^1_𝒴} = B⁺_dR(C^♯) and B_{Div^1_𝒴} = B_dR(C^♯); B⁺_dR(C^♯) is a complete discrete valuation ring with residue field C^♯, fraction field B_dR(C^♯) and uniformizer ξ, so by the Cartan decomposition G(B_dR(C^♯)) = ⊔_{μ ∈ X_*(T)^+} G(B⁺_dR(C^♯)) μ(ξ) G(B⁺_dR(C^♯)); as a set 𝓗ck_{G,Div^1_𝒴}(S)/≅ = X_*(T)^+. (When the divisor is π = 0, C^♯ = C and B⁺_dR(C^♯) = W_{O_E}(C) (Remark VI.2.1).) X_*(T)^+ carries the dominance order µ ≥ µ′ iff µ − µ′ is a ℤ_{≥0}-sum of positive coroots.
items.note: Planned by the GS0 packet node GS0:loop-geometry/schubert-bounds-and-properness, whose statement opens with 'By the Cartan decomposition over a geometric point, Hck_{G,Div^1_Y-curly}(S)/iso = X_*(T)^+' and whose hypotheses include Remark VI.2.1 (the divisor π = 0, B⁺_dR(C^♯) = W_{O_E}(C)). The input, the Cartan decomposition for split G over the complete discrete valuation field B_dR(C^♯) with algebraically closed residue field C^♯, is requested by the GS0 packet from ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.3, but ReductiveGroupsPartII works over nonarchimedean local fields with finite residue field, so RG2.4 ('Cartan and Iwahori–Bruhat decompositions') does not plan this case.

items.name: Schubert varieties Hck_{≤µ}, Gr_{≤µ} for d = 1 (Definition VI.2.2)
items.statement: For any μ ∈ X_*(T)^+, let 𝓗ck_{G,Div^1_𝒴,≤μ} ⊂ 𝓗ck_{G,Div^1_𝒴} be the subfunctor of all those maps S → 𝓗ck_{G,Div^1_𝒴} such that at all geometric points S′ = Spa(C,C⁺) → S, the corresponding S′-valued point is given by some μ′ ∈ X_*(T)^+ with μ′ ≤ μ. Moreover, Gr_{G,Div^1_𝒴,≤μ} ⊂ Gr_{G,Div^1_𝒴} is the preimage of 𝓗ck_{G,Div^1_𝒴,≤μ} ⊂ 𝓗ck_{G,Div^1_𝒴}.
items.note: GS0:loop-geometry: 'construct Schubert cells/closures'. Library audit: 'grep -c -i Schubert in declarations.tsv is 0'.

items.name: Schubert varieties are closed, exhaust, and are proper (Proposition VI.2.3)
items.statement: The inclusion 𝓗ck_{G,Div^1_𝒴,≤μ} ⊂ 𝓗ck_{G,Div^1_𝒴} is a closed subfunctor and 𝓗ck_{G,Div^1_𝒴} = lim→_μ 𝓗ck_{G,Div^1_𝒴,≤μ}; thus similar properties hold for Gr_{G,Div^1_𝒴}. Here the index category is the partially ordered set of μ's under the dominance order, which is a disjoint union (over π_1(G)) of filtered partially ordered sets. The map Gr_{G,Div^1_𝒴,≤μ} → Div^1_𝒴 is proper and representable in spatial diamonds.
items.locator: Chapter VI, §VI.2, Proposition VI.2.3 ([SW20, Proposition 20.3.6]), p. 197
items.note: GS0:loop-geometry: 'Prove properness of bounded Schubert diamonds ... closure relations'; GS0:Witt-geometry: 'Prove the integral family and bounded properness using Berkeley §§19.2–19.3, §§20.3–20.5'. Cited from Scholze–Weinstein Berkeley lectures [SW20, Prop. 20.3.6]; FS add the colimit statement (bounded poles on quasicompact S).

items.name: Open Schubert cell Hck_µ and section [µ]
items.statement: 𝓗ck_{G,Div^1_𝒴,μ} = 𝓗ck_{G,Div^1_𝒴,≤μ} \ ⋃_{μ′<μ} 𝓗ck_{G,Div^1_𝒴,≤μ′} is an open subfunctor of 𝓗ck_{G,Div^1_𝒴,≤μ}, similarly its preimage Gr_{G,Div^1_𝒴,μ} ⊂ Gr_{G,Div^1_𝒴,≤μ}. By the Cartan decomposition 𝓗ck_{G,Div^1_𝒴,μ} has one point in every geometric fibre over Div^1_𝒴, defined by a global section [μ] : Div^1_𝒴 → Gr_{G,Div^1_𝒴,μ} given by μ(ξ) ∈ (L_{Div^1_𝒴}G)(S) whenever ξ is a local generator of I_S; up to the action of L⁺_{Div^1_𝒴}G this is independent of the choice of ξ.
items.note: GS0:loop-geometry: 'construct Schubert cells/closures'.

items.name: Structure and smoothness of open Schubert cells (Proposition VI.2.4)
items.statement: The map [μ] : Div^1_𝒴 → 𝓗ck_{G,Div^1_𝒴,μ} given by μ is a v-cover. This gives an isomorphism 𝓗ck_{G,Div^1_𝒴,μ} ≅ [Div^1_𝒴/(L⁺_{Div^1_𝒴}G)_μ], where (L⁺_{Div^1_𝒴}G)_μ ⊂ L⁺_{Div^1_𝒴}G is the closed subgroup stabilizing the section [μ] of Gr_{G,Div^1_𝒴}/Div^1_𝒴. With (L⁺_{Div^1_𝒴}G)^{≥m}_μ = (L⁺_{Div^1_𝒴}G)_μ ∩ (L⁺_{Div^1_𝒴}G)^{≥m}, one has (L⁺_{Div^1_𝒴}G)_μ/(L⁺_{Div^1_𝒴}G)^{≥1}_μ ≅ (P_μ^−)^♢ ⊂ L⁺_{Div^1_𝒴}G/(L⁺_{Div^1_𝒴}G)^{≥1} ≅ G^♢ and (L⁺_{Div^1_𝒴}G)^{≥m}_μ/(L⁺_{Div^1_𝒴}G)^{≥m+1}_μ ≅ (Lie G)^♢_{μ≤m}{m} ⊂ (L⁺_{Div^1_𝒴}G)^{≥m}/(L⁺_{Div^1_𝒴}G)^{≥m+1} ≅ (Lie G)^♢{m}, where P_μ^− ⊂ G is the parabolic with Lie algebra (Lie G)_{μ≤0}, and (Lie G)_{μ≤m} ⊂ Lie G is the subspace on which μ acts via weights ≤ m via the adjoint action. In particular, Gr_{G,Div^1_𝒴,μ} ≅ L⁺_{Div^1_𝒴}G/(L⁺_{Div^1_𝒴}G)_μ is cohomologically smooth of ℓ-dimension ⟨2ρ,μ⟩ over Div^1_𝒴.
items.note: GS0:Schubert-smoothness: 'Prove FS VI.2.4/IV.1.18: over a splitting field the open cell Gr_(G,μ) is ℓ-cohomologically smooth of ℓ-dimension <2rho,μ>'. Used for smoothness of charts of Bun_G (IV.1.18) and throughout. Proof: GL_n lattice computation via [SW20, Prop. 19.4.2], then closed embedding G ↪ GL_n and [SW20, Prop. 20.3.7], [Sch17a, Lemma 12.5].

items.name: Bialynicki-Birula map on Schubert cells (Remark VI.2.5)
items.statement: The map Gr_{G,Div^1_𝒴,μ} = L⁺_{Div^1_𝒴}G/(L⁺_{Div^1_𝒴}G)_μ → L⁺_{Div^1_𝒴}G/((L⁺_{Div^1_𝒴}G)_μ·(L⁺_{Div^1_𝒴}G)^{≥1}) ≅ G^♢/(P_μ^−)^♢ = (G/P_{−μ})^♢, induced by reduction modulo ξ, is the Bialynicki-Birula map, see [CS17]. (P_{−μ} = P_μ^− is the parabolic with Lie algebra (Lie G)_{μ≤0}.)
items.note: GS0:Schubert-smoothness: 'Identify a Schubert cell by its parabolic flag base and positive-loop unipotent fibres'. The printed target L⁺G/(L⁺G)^{≥1}_μ is corrected (PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E37): (L⁺G)^{≥1}_μ ⊂ (L⁺G)_μ, so the printed arrow points the wrong way; the intended target is G^♢ modulo the image (P_μ^−)^♢ of (L⁺G)_μ (Proposition VI.2.4). Convention P_λ has Lie algebra (Lie G)_{λ≥0} (§VI.3, p. 201). Comparison with Caraiani–Scholze.

items.name: Geometric fibres of Hck_{Div^d} factor over distinct untilts
items.statement: If f : Spa(C,C⁺) → Div^d_𝒴 is a geometric point, given by an unordered tuple Spa(C_i^♯,C_i^♯⁺), i ∈ I, |I| = d, of untilts over O_E, partition I into I_1,…,I_r of equal untilts, giving f_1,…,f_r : Spa(C,C⁺) → Div^1_𝒴. Then 𝓗ck_{G,Div^d_𝒴} ×_{Div^d_𝒴,f} Spa(C,C⁺) ≅ ∏_{i=1}^r 𝓗ck_{G,Div^1_𝒴} ×_{Div^1_𝒴,f_i} Spa(C,C⁺), and similarly for L⁺_{Div^d_𝒴}G, L_{Div^d_𝒴}G and Gr_{G,Div^d_𝒴}.
items.note: Follows from the decomposition of B⁺_{Div^d_𝒴} after pullback. Used in §VI.2 itself, to define the multi-leg Schubert varieties (Definition VI.2.6) and to reduce Proposition VI.2.8 to d = 1. Planned in GS0: GS0:loop-geometry plans loop groups and the Grassmannian 'with base change in legs', and the packet node GS0:Schubert-smoothness/truncation-of-the-loop-action uses it ('At a geometric point decompose into products to reduce to d = 1'). This is a pointwise statement that allows coincident legs, not GS3's factorization over the disjoint-leg locus.

items.name: Multi-leg Schubert varieties Hck_{≤µ•} (Definition VI.2.6)
items.statement: For any unordered collection μ_• = (μ_j)_{j∈J} of elements μ_j ∈ X_*(T)^+ with |J| = d, let 𝓗ck_{G,Div^d_𝒴,≤μ_•} ⊂ 𝓗ck_{G,Div^d_𝒴} be the subfunctor of all those S → 𝓗ck_{G,Div^d_𝒴} such that at all geometric points Spa(C,C⁺) → S, then equipped with an (unordered) tuple of d untilts Spa(C_i^♯,C_i^♯⁺), i ∈ I with |I| = d, there is some bijection ψ : J ≅ I such that the relative position of 𝓔_1 and 𝓔_2 at Spa(C_i^♯,C_i^♯⁺) is bounded by Σ_{j∈J, C^♯_{ψ(j)} ≅ C^♯_i} μ_j. Let Gr_{G,Div^d_𝒴,≤μ_•} ⊂ Gr_{G,Div^d_𝒴} be the preimage of 𝓗ck_{G,Div^d_𝒴,≤μ_•}.
items.note: GS0:loop-geometry: 'construct Schubert cells/closures'. The printed 'bijection between ψ : I ≅ J' is corrected to ψ : J ≅ I (PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E38), since ψ is applied to j ∈ J.

items.name: Multi-leg Schubert varieties closed and proper (Proposition VI.2.7)
items.statement: The inclusion 𝓗ck_{G,Div^d_𝒴,≤μ_•} ⊂ 𝓗ck_{G,Div^d_𝒴} is a closed subfunctor. The map Gr_{G,Div^d_𝒴,≤μ_•} → Div^d_𝒴 is proper, representable in spatial diamonds, and of finite dim.trg.
items.note: GS0:loop-geometry: 'Prove properness of bounded Schubert diamonds'. Proof: pull back to (Div^1_𝒴)^d and cite [SW20, Proposition 20.5.4].

items.name: Truncated positive loop group (L⁺G)^{<m}
items.statement: (L⁺_{Div^d_𝒴}G)^{<m} = L⁺_{Div^d_𝒴}G/(L⁺_{Div^d_𝒴}G)^{≥m}, the quotient by the principal congruence subgroup.
items.note: GS0:Schubert-smoothness: 'Construct truncated positive loop groups'. Cohomologically smooth by VI.1.11–VI.1.12.

items.name: L⁺G-action on bounded Gr factors through a finite truncation (Proposition VI.2.8)
items.statement: For any μ_• = (μ_j)_{j∈J} as above, the action of L⁺_{Div^d_𝒴}G on Gr_{G,Div^d_𝒴,≤μ_•} factors over (L⁺_{Div^d_𝒴}G)^{<m} where m is chosen so that for μ = Σ_{j∈J} μ_j, all weights of μ on Lie G are ≤ m.
items.note: GS0:Schubert-smoothness: 'Also prove VI.2.8's explicit congruence bound from weights of μ on Lie G' and 'the action on each bounded locus factors through a finite truncation'. Reduces bounded Hecke stacks to Artin stacks.

items.name: G_m-action on Gr via λ and Gr_{P_λ}
items.statement: Let G be split. Fix a cocharacter λ : G_m → T ⊂ G, with Levi M_λ (Lie algebra (Lie G)_{λ=0}), parabolic P_λ = P_λ^+ (Lie algebra (Lie G)_{λ≥0}) and unipotent radical U_λ (Lie algebra (Lie G)_{λ>0}). The v-sheaf G_m (S = Spa(R,R⁺) ↦ R^×) acts on Gr_{G,Div^d_𝒴} via the Teichmüller map [·] : G_m → L⁺_{Div^d_𝒴}G_m, L⁺_{Div^d_𝒴}λ : L⁺_{Div^d_𝒴}G_m → L⁺_{Div^d_𝒴}G and the action of L⁺_{Div^d_𝒴}G. There are maps Gr_{P_λ,Div^d_𝒴} → Gr_{M_λ,Div^d_𝒴} → Gr_{M̄_λ,Div^d_𝒴}, M̄_λ the cocenter of M_λ; the sum μ := Σ_{i=1}^d μ_i defines a well-defined locally constant function (VI.3.1) Gr_{M̄_λ,Div^d_𝒴} → X_*(M̄_λ) (weighting each distinct untilt by its multiplicity), and for ν ∈ X_*(M̄_λ), Gr^ν_{P_λ,Div^d_𝒴} ⊂ Gr_{P_λ,Div^d_𝒴} is the open and closed preimage.
items.note: GS1: 'Construct positive-loop equivariance, orbit stratifications, semi-infinite orbits'. Setup to apply Braden's theorem / hyperbolic localization (Hypothesis IV.6.1).

items.name: Semi-infinite orbits stratify Gr (Proposition VI.3.1)
items.statement: The map ⊔_ν Gr^ν_{P_λ,Div^d_𝒴} = Gr_{P_λ,Div^d_𝒴} → Gr_{G,Div^d_𝒴} is bijective on geometric points, and it is a locally closed immersion on each Gr^ν_{P_λ,Div^d_𝒴}. The union ⋃_{ν′≤ν} Gr^{ν′}_{P_λ,Div^d_𝒴} has closed image in Gr_{G,Div^d_𝒴}. The action of G_m via L⁺_{Div^d_𝒴}G_m on Gr_{P_λ,Div^d_𝒴} extends to an action of the monoid A^1, and the G_m-fixed points agree with Gr_{M_λ,Div^d_𝒴}.
items.note: GS1: 'semi-infinite orbits and their intersections with Schubert strata'; VS1 owns hyperbolic localization (IV.6). Applied also to the inverse G_m-action and pulled back to relative Schubert varieties, verifies Hypothesis IV.6.1. Proof reduces to GL_n and the mirabolic via Lemma VI.3.2; bijectivity on points via the Iwasawa decomposition (printed 'Iwahori', (PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E39)).

items.name: Semicontinuity of relative position of rank-1 lattices (Lemma VI.3.2)
items.statement: Let S = Spa(R,R⁺) be an affinoid perfectoid space over F_q with untilts S_i^♯ = Spa(R_i^♯,R_i^♯⁺) over O_E for i = 1,…,n. Let ξ_i ∈ W_{O_E}(R⁺) generate the kernel of θ_i : W_{O_E}(R⁺) → R_i^♯⁺ and let ξ = ξ_1⋯ξ_n. Let B⁺ be the ξ-adic completion of W_{O_E}(R⁺)[1/[ϖ]] where ϖ ∈ R is a pseudouniformizer, and let B = B⁺[1/ξ]. Finally, let L ⊂ B be a finitely generated B⁺-module that is open and bounded, i.e. there is some integer N such that ξ^N B⁺ ⊂ L ⊂ ξ^{−N}B⁺ ⊂ B. For any m ∈ ℤ, let S_m ⊂ S be the subset of those points at which the relative position of L to B⁺ ⊂ B is given by m. Then ⋃_{m′≥m} S_{m′} is closed, and if S_m = S then the B⁺-module L is a line bundle.
items.note: Key input to VI.3.1 (GS1), but not named in any stage. 'Relative position' is via Gr_{G_m,Div^d_𝒴} → X_*(G_m) = ℤ.

items.name: Semicontinuity of length of B⁺_s/f (Lemma VI.3.3)
items.statement: In the situation of Lemma VI.3.2, let f ∈ B⁺ be any element, and consider the map |S| → ℤ_{≥0} ∪ {∞} sending any point s of S to the length of B_s⁺/f as B_s⁺-module. This map is semicontinuous in the sense that for any m ≥ 0, the locus where it is ≤ m is open.
items.note: Input to Lemma VI.3.2. Proof by induction dividing by ξ_i on the closed loci S_i where f vanishes in R_i^♯.

items.name: Stratification by semi-infinite orbits for λ regular (Example VI.3.4)
items.statement: Suppose λ ∈ X_*(T) is regular dominant. Then P_λ = B, and one obtains the stratification by semi-infinite orbits S_ν = Gr^ν_{B,Div^d_𝒴} for ν ∈ X_*(T). One has S_ν ↪ Gr_{G,Div^d_𝒴}, a locally closed immersion, and Gr_{G,Div^d_𝒴} = ⋃_{ν∈X_*(T)} Gr^ν_{B,Div^d_𝒴} (disjoint union) at the level of points.
items.note: GS1: 'semi-infinite orbits'. Special case of VI.3.1.

items.name: Bounded sheaves on Gr_{G,S/Div^d}
items.statement: For a small v-stack S → Div^d_𝒴, Gr_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴} = Gr_{G,Div^d_𝒴} ×_{Div^d_𝒴} S and 𝓗ck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴} = 𝓗ck_{G,Div^d_𝒴} ×_{Div^d_𝒴} S. A ∈ D_ét(Gr_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴},Λ) is bounded if it arises via pushforward from some finite union Gr_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴,≤μ_•} ⊂ Gr_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴}; D_ét(Gr_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴},Λ)^bd ⊂ D_ét(Gr_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴},Λ) is the corresponding full subcategory.
items.note: GS1: 'relative perverse t-structure on bounded constructible complexes'.

items.name: Hyperbolic localization / constant term functor CT_{P_λ} (Corollary VI.3.5)
items.statement: Let S → Div^d_𝒴 be any small v-stack. Consider the diagram Gr_{G,Div^d_𝒴} ←q^+− Gr_{P_λ,Div^d_𝒴} −p^+→ Gr_{M_λ,Div^d_𝒴}, Gr_{G,Div^d_𝒴} ←q^−− Gr_{P_λ^−,Div^d_𝒴} −p^−→ Gr_{M_λ,Div^d_𝒴}, and denote by q_S^+ etc. the base change along S → Div^d_𝒴. Consider the full subcategory D_ét(Gr_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴},Λ)^{G_m-mon,bd} ⊂ D_ét(Gr_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴},Λ)^bd of all A that are bounded and G_m-monodromic in the sense of Definition IV.6.11. On D_ét(Gr_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴},Λ)^{G_m-mon,bd}, the natural map R(p_S^−)_*R(q_S^−)^! → R(p_S^+)_!(q_S^+)^* is an equivalence, inducing a 'constant term' functor CT_{P_λ} : D_ét(Gr_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴},Λ)^{G_m-mon,bd} → D_ét(Gr_{M_λ,S/Div^d_𝒴},Λ)^bd. This functor commutes with any base change in S and preserves the condition of being universally locally acyclic over S (which is well-defined for bounded A).
items.note: GS1: 'finiteness needed for compact-support cohomology and hyperbolic-localization comparisons'; VS1: 'Construct attractor/repeller correspondences, hyperbolic localization and the comparison map of FS IV.6 ... compatibility with base change'. Proof: VI.3.1 + Theorem IV.6.5, Propositions IV.6.12, IV.6.14.

items.name: CT_B for d = 1 as sum over semi-infinite orbits (Example VI.3.6)
items.statement: In the context of Example VI.3.4 with d = 1, Gr_{T,S/Div^1_𝒴} = X_*(T) × S, the semi-infinite orbits are S_ν ⊂ Gr_{G,Div^1_𝒴} for ν ∈ X_*(T), and CT_B(A) = ⊕_{ν∈X_*(T)} R(p_ν)_!(A|_{S_ν}) with p_ν : S_ν ×_{Div^1_𝒴} S → S ⊂ Gr_{T,S/Div^1_𝒴} the embedding indexed by ν.
items.note: GS1: 'hyperbolic-localization comparisons'. Used in VI.4.2 and for weight functors in §VI.10–11.

items.name: Semi-infinite orbit ∩ Witt Schubert variety is affine (Proposition VI.3.7)
items.statement: Let Gr^Witt_G be the Witt vector affine Grassmannian (so that (Gr^Witt_G)^♢ ≅ Gr_{G,Spd F_q/Div^1_𝒴}), an increasing union of perfections of projective varieties over F_q by [BS17]; for λ ∈ X_*(T) let S_λ = LU·[λ] ⊂ Gr^Witt_G. For any μ ∈ X_*(T)^+, the intersection S_λ ∩ Gr^Witt_{G,≤μ} is representable by an affine scheme.
items.note: GS0:Witt-geometry: 'This stage owns the projectivity/ample-line inputs to FS VI.3.7'; GS1: 'semi-infinite orbits and their intersections with Schubert strata'. Proof: reduce to GL_n, trivialize the Bhatt–Scholze ample determinant line bundle on Gr^Witt_B and show the section extends to the closure vanishing exactly off S_λ (v-descent of [BS17], [SW20, Lemma 14.2.3]).

items.name: Closed unions of semi-infinite orbits and their extremes
items.statement: The union ⋃_{λ,⟨2ρ,λ⟩≤d} S_λ ⊂ Gr^Witt_G is closed, thus so is ⋃_{λ,⟨2ρ,λ⟩≤d} S_λ ∩ Gr^Witt_{G,≤μ} ⊂ Gr^Witt_{G,≤μ}. For d = ⟨2ρ,μ⟩ this is all of Gr^Witt_{G,≤μ}, while for d = −⟨2ρ,μ⟩ it contains only a point, corresponding to [λ] for λ the antidominant representative of the Weyl orbit of μ; only d of the same parity as ⟨2ρ,μ⟩ are relevant. The successive complements ⊔_{λ,⟨2ρ,λ⟩=d} S_λ ∩ Gr^Witt_{G,≤μ} are affine.
items.note: Unnumbered facts leading to Corollary VI.3.8; GS1: 'Prove dimension estimates'. The reviewed decomposition states VI.3.7–VI.3.8 in node GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS0:Witt-geometry/semi-infinite-intersections-and-MV-cycles ('it is equidimensional of dimension <rho, mu + lambda>', with the dimension-drop count along the closed unions as a proof step).

items.name: Mirković–Vilonen dimension formula (Corollary VI.3.8)
items.statement: The scheme S_λ ∩ Gr^Witt_{G,≤μ} is equidimensional of dimension ⟨ρ, μ + λ⟩.
items.note: GS1: 'semi-infinite orbits and their intersections with Schubert strata. Prove dimension estimates'. Cf. [MV07, Thm 3.2], [GHKR10], [Zhu17, Cor. 2.8]. Proof: affine successive complements force dimension drops ≤ 1 per step, and ⟨2ρ,μ⟩ drops occur in ⟨2ρ,μ⟩ steps. Key for t-exactness of CT and weight functors. The reviewed decomposition states VI.3.7–VI.3.8 in node GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS0:Witt-geometry/semi-infinite-intersections-and-MV-cycles ('it is equidimensional of dimension <rho, mu + lambda>', with the dimension-drop count along the closed unions as a proof step).

items.name: Invariance under pro-unipotent part of the group (Proposition VI.4.1)
items.statement: Let H be a group small v-sheaf over a small v-sheaf S that admits a filtration H^{≥m} ⊂ H by closed subgroups such that, v-locally on S, for each m ≥ 1 each quotient H^{≥m}/H^{≥m+1} admits a further finite filtration with graded pieces given by (A^1_{S^♯})^♢ for some untilt S^♯ of S (that may depend on the graded piece). Let X be some small v-sheaf over S with an action of H that factors over H^{<m} = H/H^{≥m} for some m > 0. Then the pullback functor D_ét(H^{<m}\X,Λ) → D_ét(H\X,Λ) is an equivalence.
items.note: GS1: 'Construct positive-loop equivariance ... Stabilizer and unipotent quotient invariance must carry their exact prime-to-p coefficient hypotheses.' Applied with H = L⁺G (VI.1.10–11, VI.2.8) so that D_ét of bounded Hecke stacks is D_ét of Artin stacks. Proof: descent, Postnikov towers, [Sch17a, Prop. 14.9], contractibility of balls.

items.name: Conservativity of constant term (Proposition VI.4.2)
items.statement: Assume that B ⊂ G is a Borel. Let S → Div^d_𝒴 be any small v-sheaf. Let A ∈ D_ét(𝓗ck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴},Λ) with support quasicompact over S. Assume that the hyperbolic localization CT_B(A) = 0 of the pullback of A to Gr_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴} vanishes. Then A = 0. The similar assertion holds with Div^d_Y and Div^d_X in place of Div^d_𝒴.
items.note: Planned in node GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS1/semi-infinite-orbits-and-hyperbolic-localization ('FS VI.3.1, VI.3.5 and VI.4.2 ... and conservativity'; statement: 'If B is a Borel and A is a bounded complex on Hck_{G,S/Div^d} with support quasicompact over S and CT_B(A) = 0, then A = 0'), with the proof steps of p. 208. Used for VI.6.4 (ULA via CT), VI.7.4 and VI.7.10. Printed 'μ_1, …, μ_n' for μ_1, …, μ_d in the proof (PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E40).

items.name: Iwahori and parahoric group schemes over A = W_{O_E}(O_{C♭})
items.statement: Let G be split reductive over O_E with Borel B ⊂ G over O_E, C = completed algebraic closure of E, A = W_{O_E}(O_{C♭}) with Fontaine's θ : A → O_C, G_A the base change. The 'Iwahori' group scheme 𝓘 → G_A, flat over A, has points in a ker θ-torsionfree A-algebra R given by g ∈ G(R) with θ(g) ∈ B(R ⊗_A O_C); for a parabolic P ⊃ B the 'parahoric' 𝓟 → G_A has points g ∈ G(R) with θ(g) ∈ P(R ⊗_A O_C); in particular 𝓟_i for the parabolics P_i of the simple reflections s_i, and for any affine simple reflection s_i a parahoric 𝓟_i → G_A flat over A through which 𝓘 → G_A factors. (Reduced to W_{O_E}(k)[[u]] ↪ A and [BT84, §3.9.4].)
items.note: GS0:loop-geometry: 'Provide the affine flag and Demazure-resolution ingredients needed in the proof, with parahoric models supplied by ReductiveGroupsPartII'. ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.3 constructs parahoric group schemes over O_E for a facet of the building of a group over E; it does not plan these group schemes over the two-dimensional base A = W_{O_E}(O_{C♭}) (or W_{O_E}(k)[[u]]), defined as dilatations of G_A along B or P over ker θ. The GS0 stage therefore owns them; its deferral to ReductiveGroupsPartII names a supplier whose layer does not cover this base. Printed 'one can define a parabolic 𝒫_i → G_A' for the affine simple reflections (new misprint reported by this review). Setting restricted to d = 1 and S over Spd O_C.

items.name: Affine flag variety Fℓ_{G,S} (Definition VI.5.1)
items.statement: In the situation above, including a small v-stack S over Spd O_C, mapping to Div^1_𝒴, let Fℓ_{G,S} → S be the étale quotient LG/L⁺𝓘, where L⁺𝓘(R,R⁺) = 𝓘(B⁺_dR(R^♯)).
items.note: GS0:loop-geometry: 'Provide the affine flag and Demazure-resolution ingredients'. B⁺_dR(R^♯) is an A-algebra since S lives over Spd O_C.

items.name: Fℓ → Gr is a (G/B)^♢-bundle (Proposition VI.5.2)
items.statement: There is a natural projection map Fℓ_{G,S} → Gr_{G,S/Div^1_𝒴} that is v-locally isomorphic to a product with (G/B)^♢. In particular, it is proper, representable in spatial diamonds, and cohomologically smooth.
items.note: GS0:loop-geometry (affine flag ingredients). Proof: L⁺G/L⁺𝓘 ≅ (G/B)^♢.

items.name: Iwahori–Weyl group W̃ and its exact sequences
items.statement: W̃ = N(T)(B_dR(C′))/T(B⁺_dR(C′)) for any complete algebraically closed C′ over O_E with a map C♭ → C′♭ (independent of C′); as T(B_dR(C′))/T(B⁺_dR(C′)) ≅ X_*(T), there is a short exact sequence 0 → X_*(T) → W̃ → W → 0 with W the Weyl group of G. Fixing the alcove 𝔞 of 𝓘, the affine simple reflections s_i (reflections along faces of 𝔞) generate a normal subgroup W_aff ⊂ W̃; with Ω ⊂ W̃ the stabilizer of the alcove there is a split short exact sequence 1 → W_aff → W̃ → Ω → 1.
items.note: RG2.4: 'Prove the Cartan and Iwahori–Bruhat decompositions ... with the correct relative cocharacter lattice' (the affine Weyl group is the index set of the Iwahori–Bruhat decomposition). Printed 'N(T) ⊂ T be the normalizer of T' (PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E42).

items.name: Iwahori orbits on the affine flag variety (Proposition VI.5.3)
items.statement: The decomposition of Fℓ_{G,S}(C′) into L⁺𝓘(C′)-orbits is given by Fℓ_{G,S}(C′) = ⊔_{w∈W̃} L⁺𝓘(C′)·w.
items.note: RG2.4 'Iwahori–Bruhat decompositions'; GS0:loop-geometry affine flag ingredients. Proof: over E via B_dR(C′) ≅ C′((ξ)) and the classical result; over F_q via the Witt vector affine flag variety [Zhu17]. Printed orbit group 'L⁺𝓘(C)' (PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E43).

items.name: Bruhat order on W̃
items.statement: If w_i = w_{i,0}ω_i ∈ W̃ = W_aff ⋊ Ω for i = 1,2, then w_1 ≤ w_2 if ω_1 = ω_2 and in one (hence every) presentation of w_2 as a product of affine simple reflections, w_1 is obtained by removing some factors.
items.note: Tau Ceti has the Bruhat order on a Coxeter group, tauceti:CoxeterSystem.BruhatLE (TauCeti/GroupTheory/Coxeter/Bruhat.lean:156, defined via Bruhat-graph chains) with subword results (CoxeterSystem.BruhatLE.exists_sublist_wordProd_eq, line 266), applicable to W_aff once presented as a Coxeter system; the extension to W̃ = W_aff ⋊ Ω and the affine Weyl group of G are absent. Independence of the reduced word is deduced geometrically at the end of the proof of VI.5.5. The extension to W-tilde = W_aff ⋊ Omega is planned in ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.4 by accepted routes: PAPER-HE-21 item 5 ("Wtilde=Wa⋊Ω with Ω the alcove stabilizer and length zero. Extend length and Bruhat order cosetwise to Wtilde", planned in RG2.4, route 4 accepted) and PAPER-HE-18 item A2 (same, planned in RG2.4). FS use it for the affine flag variety of §VI.5, so GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS0:loop-geometry needs a link from RG2.4 (none exists; adding it creates no cycle).

items.name: Affine Schubert cells and varieties in Fℓ (Definition VI.5.4)
items.statement: For w ∈ W̃, the affine Schubert cell is the subfunctor Fℓ_{G,w,S} ⊂ Fℓ_{G,S} of all maps Spa(R,R⁺) → Fℓ_{G,S} that on all geometric points lie in the L⁺𝓘-orbit of w. The affine Schubert variety is the subfunctor Fℓ_{G,≤w,S} of all maps Spa(R,R⁺) → Fℓ_{G,S} that on all geometric points lie in the L⁺𝓘-orbit of w′ for some w′ ≤ w.
items.note: GS0:loop-geometry: 'Provide the affine flag and Demazure-resolution ingredients'.

items.name: Affine Schubert varieties closed, proper, cell open dense (Theorem VI.5.5)
items.statement: For each w ∈ W̃, the subfunctor Fℓ_{G,≤w,S} ⊂ Fℓ_{G,S} is closed, and Fℓ_{G,≤w,S} → S is proper and representable in spatial diamonds, of finite dim.trg. The subfunctor Fℓ_{G,w,S} ⊂ Fℓ_{G,≤w,S} is open and dense. (Printed with 'Fℓ_{G,≤w,S} → Spd O_C'; see PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E44.)
items.note: GS0:loop-geometry (affine flag + Demazure ingredients). Proof via Demazure resolution, [SW20, Thm 19.2.4]; the proof establishes properness over S (PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E44). Also yields independence of the Bruhat order from the reduced word.

items.name: Demazure variety (Definition VI.5.6)
items.statement: Write w = w_0ω ∈ W̃ = W_aff ⋊ Ω and fix a reduced decomposition w_0 = ∏_{j=1}^l s_{i_j} (l(w) = l(w_0) = l), denoted ẇ; for each affine simple reflection s_i the parahoric 𝓟_i has L⁺𝓟_i/L⁺𝓘 ≅ (P^1)^♢. The Demazure variety corresponding to ẇ is the étale sheaf Dem_{ẇ,S} = L⁺𝓟_{s_{i_1}} ×^{L⁺𝓘} L⁺𝓟_{s_{i_2}} ×^{L⁺𝓘} … ×^{L⁺𝓘} L⁺𝓟_{s_{i_l}}/L⁺𝓘 → S, equipped with the left L⁺𝓘-action and the L⁺𝓘-equivariant map Dem_{ẇ,S} → Fℓ_{G,S} given by (p_1,…,p_l) ↦ p_1⋯p_l·ω. It is a successive (P^1)^♢-fibration over S, a spatial diamond proper over S of finite dim.trg, surjects onto Fℓ_{G,≤w,S}, and is an isomorphism over Fℓ_{G,w,S}, whose preimage is (L⁺𝓟_{s_{i_1}} \ L⁺𝓘) ×^{L⁺𝓘} … ×^{L⁺𝓘} (L⁺𝓟_{s_{i_l}} \ L⁺𝓘)/L⁺𝓘.
items.locator: Chapter VI, §VI.5, Definition VI.5.6 and proof of Theorem VI.5.5, pp. 210–211
items.note: GS0:loop-geometry: 'Provide the affine flag and Demazure-resolution ingredients needed in the proof'. Library audit: no Demazure resolution in either library.

items.name: Standard sheaves j_{w!}Λ on Fℓ are ULA (Proposition VI.5.7)
items.statement: For any w ∈ W̃, let j_w : Fℓ_{G,w,S} ↪ Fℓ_{G,≤w,S} be the open embedding. Then j_{w!}Λ ∈ D_ét(Fℓ_{G,≤w,S},Λ) is universally locally acyclic over S.
items.note: GS1: 'Prove full faithfulness and essential surjectivity using the stratified local-constancy criterion and Demazure resolutions in FS VI.5–VI.7'. Proof: Prop. IV.2.11, resolve j̃_{w!}Λ on Dem_{ẇ,S} by pushforwards from sub-Demazure varieties (normal crossings boundary), each cohomologically smooth over S.

items.name: ULA sheaves on the local Hecke stack (Definition VI.6.1)
items.statement: Let S → Div^d_𝒴 be any small v-stack. An object A ∈ D_ét(𝓗ck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴},Λ) is universally locally acyclic over S if it is bounded, and its pullback to Gr_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴} is universally locally acyclic over S. Let D^ULA_ét(𝓗ck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴},Λ) ⊂ D_ét(𝓗ck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴},Λ) be the corresponding full subcategory.
items.note: GS2:correspondences: 'Define Satake objects by the equivariance, relative perversity, ULA and coefficient flatness conditions of FS VI.6–VI.8.' ULA for diamonds is Chapter IV.2 (VS1). Library audit: universal local acyclicity absent.

items.name: ULA is symmetric under switching the two bundles (Proposition VI.6.2)
items.statement: Consider the automorphism sw : 𝓗ck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴} ≅ 𝓗ck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴} switching 𝓔_1 and 𝓔_2. Then A ∈ D_ét(𝓗ck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴},Λ) is universally locally acyclic over S if and only if sw^*A is universally locally acyclic over S.
items.note: Planned in node GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS1/ULA-sheaves-on-the-hecke-stack ('FS VI.6.1-VI.6.6: ULA sheaves on Hck, switching invariance, ...'; statement: 'This condition is invariant under the switching involution sw'), whose hypotheses record the proof: the pro-systems (LG)_U/(L⁺G)^{≥m} and (L⁺G)^{≥m}\(LG)_U are pro-isomorphic with cohomologically smooth transition maps (Lemma VI.6.3, via VI.1.11–VI.1.12). Used for VI.8.2 (dualizability).

items.name: Two-out-of-six criterion for ULA / smoothness (Lemma VI.6.3)
items.statement: Call a map f universally locally acyclic if Λ is f-universally locally acyclic. Let X_4 −f_3→ X_3 −f_2→ X_2 −f_1→ X_1 −f_0→ X_0 be surjective maps of locally spatial diamonds that are compactifiable and of locally finite dim.trg. Assume that f_0∘f_1 and f_1∘f_2 are cohomologically smooth. Then f_0 is universally locally acyclic. If f_1 is universally locally acyclic and f_0∘f_1 is cohomologically smooth, then f_1 is cohomologically smooth. Thus, if f_0∘f_1, f_1∘f_2 and f_2∘f_3 are cohomologically smooth, then f_0 and f_1 are cohomologically smooth.
items.note: Planned at proof-step level in node GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS1/ULA-sheaves-on-the-hecke-stack (hypothesis: 'sw-invariance (VI.6.2) is proved by comparing the two pro-systems ... with cohomologically smooth transition maps (Lemma VI.6.3)'; proof step: 'Lemma VI.6.3's two-out-of-six argument'); the decomposition's GS1 coverage lists 'Propositions VI.6.1-VI.6.3 ... located but not decomposed' as remaining. A general statement about locally spatial diamonds; the node should state it with its hypotheses when GS1 is refined. Authors expect f_3 unnecessary. Proof: two-out-of-six on base-change maps f̃_0^*Rg_0^! → Rg_1^!f_0^*, then Theorem IV.2.23; R(f_0∘f_1)^!Λ ≅ f_1^*Rf_0^!Λ ⊗^L_Λ Rf_1^!Λ invertible.

items.name: ULA detected by constant term (Proposition VI.6.4)
items.statement: Let B ⊂ G be a Borel with torus quotient T. Let S be a small v-stack with a map S → Div^d_𝒴, and let A ∈ D_ét(𝓗ck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴},Λ)^bd. Then A is universally locally acyclic over S if and only if the hyperbolic localization CT_B(A) ∈ D_ét(Gr_{T,S/Div^d_𝒴},Λ)^bd is universally locally acyclic over S. This, in turn, is equivalent to the property that Rπ_{T,S,*}CT_B(A) ∈ D_ét(S,Λ) is locally constant with perfect fibres, where π_{T,S} : Gr_{T,S/Div^d_𝒴} → S is the projection.
items.note: Planned in node GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS1/ULA-sheaves-on-the-hecke-stack (statement: 'For a Borel B with torus quotient T, a bounded A is ULA over S if and only if CT_B(A) is ULA over S, equivalently if and only if R pi_{T,S,*} CT_B(A) is locally constant with perfect fibres'), with the proof steps of p. 213: Cor. VI.3.5 and Cor. IV.2.12 forward; Theorem IV.2.23, Prop. VI.4.2 for G × G with CT_{B⁻×B}, Prop. IV.6.13 and Prop. IV.2.28 for the converse.

items.name: ULA characterization with one leg (Proposition VI.6.5)
items.statement: Assume that G is split. Let S → Div^1_𝒴 be any small v-stack. Consider A ∈ D_ét(𝓗ck_{G,S/Div^1_𝒴},Λ)^bd. Then A is universally locally acyclic over S if and only if for all μ ∈ X_*(T)^+, the restriction of A to the section [μ] : S → 𝓗ck_{G,S/Div^1_𝒴} is locally constant with perfect fibres in D_ét(S,Λ). (For nonsplit G a similar characterization holds étale locally; also for Div^1_Y and Div^1_X.)
items.note: GS1: 'using the stratified local-constancy criterion and Demazure resolutions in FS VI.5–VI.7'. Proof: reduce to j_{μ!}Λ over Spd O_C, pass to Fℓ via VI.5.2 and Prop. IV.2.13, apply VI.5.7; converse by induction on support using that strata are classifying stacks of pro-smooth groups.

items.name: Stability of D^ULA under six operations, one leg (Corollary VI.6.6)
items.statement: Let S → Div^1_𝒴 be any small v-stack (G not necessarily split). Then D^ULA_ét(𝓗ck_{G,S/Div^1_𝒴},Λ) is stable under Verdier duality and − ⊗^L_Λ −, RHom_Λ(−,−) as well as j_!j^*, Rj_*j^*, j_!Rj^!, Rj_*Rj^! where j is the locally closed immersion of a Schubert cell. Moreover, all of these operations commute with all pullbacks in S.
items.note: Planned in node GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS1/ULA-sheaves-on-the-hecke-stack (statement: 'The ULA subcategory is stable under Verdier duality, tensor, internal Hom and the four functors j_! j^*, Rj_* j^*, j_! Rj^!, Rj_* Rj^! for a Schubert-cell immersion j, all commuting with pullback in S'; hypothesis: 'The stability statements of VI.6.6 are for d = 1'). Proof: Cor. IV.2.25 for Verdier duality and base change; the rest from VI.6.5 locally on S.

items.name: ULA categories over O_C, C, k agree (Corollary VI.6.7)
items.statement: For a complete algebraically closed extension C of E with residue field k, taking S = Spd O_C, S = Spd C and S = Spd k, the functors D^ULA_ét(𝓗ck_{G,Spd C/Div^1_𝒴},Λ) ← D^ULA_ét(𝓗ck_{G,Spd O_C/Div^1_𝒴},Λ) → D^ULA_ét(𝓗ck_{G,Spd k/Div^1_𝒴},Λ) are equivalences.
items.note: GS1: 'Construct the one-leg special/generic-fibre comparison on the ULA, flat-perverse categories over Spd(O_C), Spd(C) and Spd(k̄) ... Prove full faithfulness and essential surjectivity'. Proof: RHom commutes with base change; locally constant sheaves with perfect fibres on these S are perfect Λ-modules. This is the degeneration from B_dR⁺ to Witt-vector Grassmannian used for the decomposition theorem.

items.name: ULA characterization and stability for distinct legs (Proposition VI.6.8)
items.statement: Assume that G is split. Let S → (Div^1_𝒴)^d_≠ → Div^d_𝒴 be a small v-stack. Consider A ∈ D_ét(𝓗ck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴},Λ)^bd. Then A is universally locally acyclic over S if and only if for all μ_1,…,μ_d ∈ X_*(T)^+, the restriction of A to the section [μ_•] : S → 𝓗ck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴} is locally constant with perfect fibres in D_ét(S,Λ). The category D^ULA_ét(𝓗ck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴},Λ) is stable under Verdier duality and − ⊗^L_Λ −, RHom_Λ(−,−) as well as j_!j^*, Rj_*j^*, j_!Rj^!, Rj_*Rj^! where j is the locally closed immersion of a Schubert cell. Moreover, all of these operations commute with all pullbacks in S.
items.note: The reviewed decomposition's coverage for GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS3:fusion lists 'Proposition VI.6.8 (the multi-leg ULA statement over the disjoint-leg locus) was located but not read' as a remaining obligation of that stage, whose description begins 'Over disjoint-leg loci prove factorization into products of single-leg Grassmannians'. Uses 𝓗ck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴} ≅ ∏_i 𝓗ck_{G,S/π_i Div^1_𝒴} over S and Cor. IV.2.25 (exterior products preserve ULA).

items.name: Relative perverse t-structure on the local Hecke stack
items.statement: Let S → Div^d_𝒴 be a small v-stack. There is a unique t-structure (ᵖD^{≤0}, ᵖD^{≥0}) on D_ét(Hck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴}, Λ)^{bd} such that A ∈ ᵖD^{≤0}_ét(Hck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴}, Λ)^{bd} if and only if for all geometric points Spa(C, C⁺) → S and open Schubert cells of Hck_{G,Spa(C,C⁺)/Div^d_𝒴}, parametrized by some μ_1, …, μ_r ∈ X_*(T)^+ (where r is the number of distinct untilts at Spa(C, C⁺) → Div^d_𝒴), the pullback of A to this open Schubert cell sits in cohomological degrees ≤ −Σ_{i=1}^r ⟨2ρ, μ_i⟩.
items.note: GS1: "Construct the relative perverse t-structure on bounded constructible complexes, with the stalk/costalk dimension inequalities and gluing across finite Schubert stratifications." Proof: on bounded closed Z the class is stable under colimits and extensions and generated by a set, so [Lur16, Proposition 1.4.4.11] gives the t-structure; the inclusions for growing Z are t-exact and the t-structures glue in the direct limit. Underlies all of §§VI.7–VI.12.

items.name: Relative perverse sheaves Perv(Hck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴}, Λ)
items.statement: Perv(Hck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴}, Λ) ⊂ D_ét(Hck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴}, Λ)^{bd} is the heart of the perverse t-structure of Definition/Proposition VI.7.1.
items.note: GS1: "Construct the relative perverse t-structure on bounded constructible complexes, with the stalk/costalk dimension inequalities and gluing across finite Schubert stratifications." The heart of the t-structure.

items.name: Pullback of relative perverse sheaves to the affine Grassmannian is fully faithful
items.statement: The pullback functor Perv(Hck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴}, Λ) → D_ét(Gr_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴}, Λ)^{bd} is fully faithful.
items.note: GS1: "Prove its compatibility with change of legs, ULA and equivariant descent. In integral coefficients distinguish flat perverse objects from arbitrary perverse objects". Proof: by the second part of VI.7.2 and descent, reduce to showing maps between pullbacks are automatically L⁺_{Div^d_𝒴}G-invariant, which follows from Lemma VI.7.3 applied to a finite-dimensional approximation of Gr ×_{Div^d_𝒴} L⁺G → Gr. Used to view Satake objects on Gr (VI.7.10, VI.7.12).

items.name: RHom from ᵖD^{≤0} to ᵖD^{≥0} is coconnective
items.statement: If A ∈ ᵖD^{≤0}_ét(Hck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴}, Λ)^{bd} and B ∈ ᵖD^{≥0}_ét(Hck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴}, Λ)^{bd}, then RHom_Λ(A, B) ∈ D^{≥0}_ét(Hck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴}, Λ)^{bd} (standard t-structure).
items.locator: Chapter VI, §VI.7, Proposition VI.7.2 (second part), p. 216
items.note: GS1: "Construct the relative perverse t-structure on bounded constructible complexes, with the stalk/costalk dimension inequalities and gluing across finite Schubert stratifications." Proof: for C ∈ D^{≤−1}, maps C → RHom(A,B) correspond to C ⊗^L_Λ A → B and C ⊗^L_Λ A ∈ ᵖD^{≤−1}. Input to the first part of VI.7.2.

items.name: H⁰ of pullback-pushforward along a map with connected fibres and a section
items.statement: Let f : Y → X be a compactifiable cohomologically smooth map of locally spatial diamonds with a section s : X → Y. Assume that all geometric fibres of f are connected. Then for all A ∈ D^{≥0}_ét(X, Λ), the map of cohomology sheaves 𝓗⁰(Rf_* f^* A) → 𝓗⁰(A) given by evaluation at the section s is an isomorphism.
items.note: Planned at proof-step level in node GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS1/relative-perverse-t-structure (hypothesis: 'Full faithfulness of Perv -> D_et(Gr)^{bd} rests on Lemma VI.7.3 about connected group actions, applied to a finite-dimensional approximation of Gr x_{Div^d} L^+G -> Gr'; proof step: '... automatically L^+G-equivariant, which is Lemma VI.7.3'); GS1's coverage lists VI.7.2–VI.7.3 as located but not decomposed. A general lemma on locally spatial diamonds. Proof: Rf_*f^*A ≅ RHom(Rf_!Rf^!Λ, A) and Rf_!Rf^!Λ ≅ Λ ⊕ B with B in degrees ≤ −1, checked on geometric stalks with Λ = F_ℓ via connectedness of fibres. Used in VI.7.2 and VI.7.4 (full faithfulness of [μ_•]^* on complexes in one degree).

items.name: Base change in S is perverse t-exact
items.statement: For any S′ → S → Div^d_𝒴, pullback along Hck_{G,S′/Div^d_𝒴} → Hck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴} is t-exact for the perverse t-structure.
items.locator: Chapter VI, §VI.7, Proposition VI.7.4 (first part), p. 217
items.note: GS1: "Prove its compatibility with change of legs, ULA and equivariant descent. In integral coefficients distinguish flat perverse objects from arbitrary perverse objects". Proof: v-locally reduce to G split and use the characterization via CT_B[deg] (second part of VI.7.4), which commutes with pullback (Corollary VI.3.5).

items.name: CT_B[deg] is t-exact and detects the perverse t-structure (G split)
items.statement: Assume G is split. There is the natural locally constant map Gr_{T,Div^d_𝒴} → X_*(T) measuring the sum of relative positions, and pairing with 2ρ gives a locally constant map deg : Gr_{T,Div^d_𝒴} → ℤ. Then CT_B[deg] : D_ét(Hck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴}, Λ)^{bd} → D_ét(Gr_{T,S/Div^d_𝒴}, Λ) is t-exact for the perverse t-structure on the source and the standard t-structure on the target. As CT_B[deg] is conservative, A ∈ ᵖD^{≤0} (resp. ᵖD^{≥0}) if and only if CT_B(A)[deg] ∈ D^{≤0}_ét(Gr_{T,S/Div^d_𝒴}, Λ) (resp. D^{≥0}).
items.locator: Chapter VI, §VI.7, Proposition VI.7.4 (second part), pp. 217–219
items.note: GS1: "Construct positive-loop equivariance, orbit stratifications, semi-infinite orbits and their intersections with Schubert strata. Prove dimension estimates, finiteness needed for compact-support cohomology and hyperbolic-localization comparisons." Proof: stratify by partial diagonals, reduce via excision and Künneth to A = j_{μ!}F_ℓ[⟨2ρ,μ⟩] on the special fibre (Gr^Witt_G)^◇, and bound RΓ_c((S_λ ∩ Gr^Witt_{G,μ})_{F̄_q}, F_ℓ) using dim(S_λ ∩ Gr^Witt_{G,μ}) ≤ ⟨ρ, λ+μ⟩ (Corollary VI.3.8); the ᵖD^{≥0} case follows by Proposition IV.6.13. Central tool for VI.7.5–VI.7.7, VI.8.1, VI.9.3.

items.name: Perverse sheaves over Spd k identify with L⁺G-equivariant perverse sheaves on the Witt vector affine Grassmannian
items.statement: If d = 1, G is split, and S = Spd k → Div^1_𝒴 for k = F̄_q, then under the full inclusion Perv(Hck_{G,Spd k/Div^1_𝒴}, Λ) ⊂ D_ét(Gr_{G,Spd k/Div^1_𝒴}, Λ)^{bd}, the identification Gr_{G,Spd k/Div^1_𝒴} ≅ (Gr^Witt_{G,k})^◇ and the full embedding D_ét(Gr^Witt_{G,k}, Λ)^{bd} ↪ D_ét(Gr_{G,Spd k/Div^1_𝒴}, Λ)^{bd} of [Sch17a, Proposition 27.2], the category Perv(Hck_{G,Spd k/Div^1_𝒴}, Λ) identifies with the full subcategory Perv_{L⁺G}(Gr^Witt_{G,k}, Λ) ⊂ D_ét(Gr^Witt_{G,k}, Λ)^{bd} of L⁺G-equivariant perverse sheaves on Gr^Witt_{G,k}.
items.locator: Chapter VI, §VI.7, unnumbered paragraph before Proposition VI.7.5, p. 219
items.note: GS1: "Construct the one-leg special/generic-fibre comparison on the ULA, flat-perverse categories over Spd(O_C), Spd(C) and Spd(k̄) ... using the stratified local-constancy criterion and Demazure resolutions in FS VI.5–VI.7." Compares with Zhu [Zhu17] and Yu [Yu22]; used for VI.7.5.

items.name: Standard and costandard objects are ULA with locally free weight functors
items.statement: Assume that G is split, so that for any μ ∈ X_*(T)^+ we have the inclusion j_μ : Hck_{G,Div^1_𝒴,μ} ↪ Hck_{G,Div^1_𝒴} of the open Schubert cell, of dimension d_μ = ⟨2ρ, μ⟩. Then ᵖj_{μ!}Λ[d_μ] = ᵖH⁰(j_{μ!}Λ[d_μ]) and ᵖRj_{μ*}Λ[d_μ] = ᵖH⁰(Rj_{μ*}Λ[d_μ]) are universally locally acyclic, and their image under CT_B[deg] is locally finite free over Λ. Their formation commutes with any base change in Λ.
items.note: GS1: "Prove its compatibility with change of legs, ULA and equivariant descent. In integral coefficients distinguish flat perverse objects from arbitrary perverse objects". Proof via top compactly supported cohomology of Mirković–Vilonen cycles S_λ ∩ Gr^Witt_{G,μ}. Used in VI.7.9, VI.10.1 and VI.11.

items.name: Costandard is the Verdier dual of standard
items.statement: In the situation of Proposition VI.7.5, the natural map ᵖRj_{μ*}Λ[d_μ](d_μ) → D(ᵖj_{μ!}Λ[d_μ]) is an isomorphism.
items.note: GS1: "Prove its compatibility with change of legs, ULA and equivariant descent. In integral coefficients distinguish flat perverse objects from arbitrary perverse objects". Proof: CT_B(D(A))[deg] ≅ D(w_0^* CT_B(A)[deg]) by Proposition IV.6.13, and degree-0 parts are finite free and exchanged by duality.

items.name: Kernel and cokernel of ᵖH⁰(j_!) → ᵖH⁰(Rj_*) are bounded ℓ-power torsion
items.statement: In the situation of Proposition VI.7.5, if Λ is a ℤ_ℓ-algebra, then there is some integer a = a(μ) (independent of Λ) such that the kernel and cokernel of the map ᵖH⁰(j_{μ!}Λ[d_μ]) → ᵖH⁰(Rj_{μ*}Λ[d_μ]) are killed by ℓ^a.
items.locator: Chapter VI, §VI.7, Proposition VI.7.5 (final part), p. 219
items.note: GS4:rational-reductivity: "Prove geometric semisimplicity of the rational Satake category using the decomposition theorem and the orbit/IC calculation, hence reductivity of the generic fibre of the Tannakian group." The paper remarks this uses the decomposition theorem via the Witt vector affine Grassmannian. Reduces to the rational statement (next item). Used in the proof of VI.10.1(iii) to show K = 0.

items.name: ᵖj_! ≅ ᵖRj_* with ℚ_ℓ-coefficients on Witt Schubert varieties (parity of IC stalks)
items.statement: On the perfectly projective scheme Gr^Witt_{G,k,≤μ}, the map ᵖj_{μ!}ℚ_ℓ[d_μ] → ᵖRj_{μ*}ℚ_ℓ[d_μ] is an isomorphism. Equivalently, for i : Gr^Witt_{G,k,<μ} ↪ Gr^Witt_{G,k,≤μ}, i^* j_{μ!*}ℚ_ℓ[d_μ] ∈ ᵖD^{≤−2}; this follows since all geometric fibres of the intersection complex j_{μ!*}ℚ_ℓ[d_μ] are concentrated in degrees of the same parity as d_μ.
items.locator: Chapter VI, §VI.7, proof of Proposition VI.7.5, p. 220
items.note: GS4:rational-reductivity: "Prove geometric semisimplicity of the rational Satake category using the decomposition theorem and the orbit/IC calculation, hence reductivity of the generic fibre of the Tannakian group." Cites [Zhu17, Lemma 2.1], [Gai01, Proposition 1], [Lus83]. Proof: smooth pullback to the Witt affine flag variety Fℓ^Witt_{G,k,≤w}, Demazure–Bott–Samuelson resolution with fibres paved by affine spaces [Zhu17, §1.4.2], and the decomposition theorem.

items.name: Relative perversity can be checked on geometric fibres
items.statement: Let S → Div^d_𝒴 be any small v-stack and let A ∈ D_ét(Hck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴}, Λ)^{bd}. Then A ∈ ᵖD^{≥0}_ét if and only if this holds true after pullback to all strictly local Spa(C, C⁺) → S. In particular, A ∈ Perv(Hck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴}, Λ) if and only if for all strictly local Spa(C, C⁺) → S, the pullback of A to Hck_{G,Spa(C,C⁺)/Div^d_𝒴} is perverse.
items.note: GS1: "Prove its compatibility with change of legs, ULA and equivariant descent. In integral coefficients distinguish flat perverse objects from arbitrary perverse objects". Proof: pullback is t-exact; reduce to G split and use the CT_B[deg] characterization.

items.name: ULA flat perverse iff RπT∗CT_B[deg] is finite projective in degree 0
items.statement: Let S be any small v-stack over Div^d_𝒴 and assume that G is split. Then A ∈ D^{ULA}_ét(Hck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴}, Λ) has the property that A is a flat perverse sheaf (in the sense that A ⊗^L_Λ M is perverse for all Λ-modules M) if and only if Rπ_{T*}CT_B(A)[deg] ∈ D_ét(S, Λ) is étale locally on S isomorphic to a finite projective Λ-module in degree 0.
items.note: GS1: "Prove its compatibility with change of legs, ULA and equivariant descent. In integral coefficients distinguish flat perverse objects from arbitrary perverse objects". Used throughout to verify membership in the Satake category (VI.7.9, VI.7.10, VI.7.13, VI.8.1, VI.9.4).

items.name: The Satake category Sat(Hck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴}, Λ)
items.statement: For S → Div^d_𝒴 any small v-stack and G general, Sat(Hck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴}, Λ) ⊂ D_ét(Hck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴}, Λ) is the full subcategory of all objects that are universally locally acyclic and flat perverse.
items.note: GS2:correspondences: "Define Satake objects by the equivariance, relative perversity, ULA and coefficient flatness conditions of FS VI.6–VI.8. Construct convolution diagrams, the convolution map and operation in the ambient bounded-support derived category via actual proper-support pushforward. Prove ambient associativity and unit with coherent maps." The paper notes the definition is invariant under sw^*.

items.name: Standard and costandard perverse sheaves lie in the Satake category
items.statement: Assume d = 1 and G split. For μ ∈ X_*(T)^+ with open Schubert cell j_μ : Hck_{G,Div^1_𝒴,μ} ↪ Hck_{G,Div^1_𝒴} of dimension d_μ = ⟨2ρ, μ⟩, the perverse sheaves ᵖj_{μ!}Λ[d_μ] = ᵖH⁰(j_{μ!}Λ[d_μ]) and ᵖRj_{μ*}Λ[d_μ] = ᵖH⁰(Rj_{μ*}Λ[d_μ]) lie in the Satake category Sat(Hck_{G,Div^1_𝒴}, Λ).
items.note: GS2:correspondences: "Define Satake objects by the equivariance, relative perversity, ULA and coefficient flatness conditions of FS VI.6–VI.8. Construct convolution diagrams, the convolution map and operation in the ambient bounded-support derived category via actual proper-support pushforward. Prove ambient associativity and unit with coherent maps." Follows from VI.7.7 and VI.7.5; analogue of highest weight modules. Used in VI.10.1(iii) and VI.11.

items.name: Cohomology of Satake objects is a local system and each Hⁱ is exact
items.statement: The functor Rπ_{G,S*} : Sat(Hck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴}, Λ) → D_ét(S, Λ) of pullback to Gr_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴} and pushforward along π_{G,S} : Gr_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴} → S takes values in complexes C ∈ D_ét(S, Λ) such that all Hⁱ(C) are local systems of finite projective Λ-modules, and each functor Hⁱ(Rπ_{G,S*}) : Sat(Hck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴}, Λ) → LocSys(S, Λ) is exact.
items.note: GS4:integral-dual-group: "Construct the total cohomology fibre functor, prove exactness, faithfulness, tensor compatibility and duals in the precise integral category, and reconstruct its affine group scheme." Proof: filtration by semi-infinite strata S_ν with graded pieces Rp_{ν!}(A|_{S_ν}) in degrees of one parity per connected component, so the spectral sequence degenerates; then VI.7.7 and VI.4.2. The reviewed decomposition (data/decompositions/GeometricSatakeAndFusion.json) states VI.7.8–VI.7.12 in node GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS2:correspondences/satake-category-and-fibre-functor ('F_{G,S} ... is exact, faithful and conservative; it detects kernels and cokernels whose F-image kernel is a direct summand. The image of Sat in D_et(Gr) is stable under Verdier duality, and D is an equivalence with D^2 = id').

items.name: The fibre functor F_{G,S} is exact, faithful and conservative
items.statement: Let F_{G,S} = ⊕_{i∈ℤ} Hⁱ(Rπ_{G,S*}) : Sat(Hck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴}, Λ) → LocSys(S, Λ). The functor F_{G,S} is exact, faithful, and conservative.
items.note: GS4:integral-dual-group: "Construct the total cohomology fibre functor, prove exactness, faithfulness, tensor compatibility and duals in the precise integral category, and reconstruct its affine group scheme." Faithfulness reduces to conservativity plus the Barr–Beck type assertion (next item). The reviewed decomposition (data/decompositions/GeometricSatakeAndFusion.json) states VI.7.8–VI.7.12 in node GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS2:correspondences/satake-category-and-fibre-functor ('F_{G,S} ... is exact, faithful and conservative; it detects kernels and cokernels whose F-image kernel is a direct summand. The image of Sat in D_et(Gr) is stable under Verdier duality, and D is an equivalence with D^2 = id').

items.name: Kernels and cokernels of F-split maps exist in the Satake category
items.statement: If f : A → B is a map in Sat(Hck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴}, Λ) such that ker F_{G,S}(f) is a direct summand of F_{G,S}(A), then f admits a kernel in Sat(Hck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴}, Λ); similarly for cokernels.
items.note: GS4:integral-dual-group: "Construct the total cohomology fibre functor, prove exactness, faithfulness, tensor compatibility and duals in the precise integral category, and reconstruct its affine group scheme." Supplies "existence of coequalizers of F_{G,S}-split parallel pairs" for the Barr–Beck theorem in VI.10.2. Proof: take the kernel in all perverse sheaves and check ULA/flatness after hyperbolic localization, deg-shift and pushforward to S. The reviewed decomposition (data/decompositions/GeometricSatakeAndFusion.json) states VI.7.8–VI.7.12 in node GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS2:correspondences/satake-category-and-fibre-functor ('F_{G,S} ... is exact, faithful and conservative; it detects kernels and cokernels whose F-image kernel is a direct summand. The image of Sat in D_et(Gr) is stable under Verdier duality, and D is an equivalence with D^2 = id').

items.name: Verdier duality on the Satake category, compatible with duals of local systems
items.statement: The image of the fully faithful functor Sat(Hck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴}, Λ) → D_ét(Gr_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴}, Λ) is stable under Verdier duality D_{Gr_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴}/S}. The induced functor D : Sat(Hck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴}, Λ)^{op} → Sat(Hck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴}, Λ) is an equivalence, with D² = id. Moreover, it makes the diagram with F_{G,S} on both sides and V ↦ V^* : LocSys(S, Λ)^{op} → LocSys(S, Λ) on the bottom commute naturally, i.e. F_{G,S} ∘ D ≅ (F_{G,S}(−))^*.
items.note: GS4:integral-dual-group: "Construct the total cohomology fibre functor, prove exactness, faithfulness, tensor compatibility and duals in the precise integral category, and reconstruct its affine group scheme." ("and duals"). Proof: define D already on Hck via Verdier duality along bounded subsets of Hck_G → [∗/L⁺G]; it commutes with F_{G,S}; biduality from Corollary IV.2.25. Remark VI.7.11 notes that isomorphisms F_{G,S}(sw^*A) ≅ F_{G,S}(A) are not clear at this stage. The reviewed decomposition (data/decompositions/GeometricSatakeAndFusion.json) states VI.7.8–VI.7.12 in node GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS2:correspondences/satake-category-and-fibre-functor ('F_{G,S} ... is exact, faithful and conservative; it detects kernels and cokernels whose F-image kernel is a direct summand. The image of Sat in D_et(Gr) is stable under Verdier duality, and D is an equivalence with D^2 = id').

items.name: The degree function deg_P on Gr_{M,Div^d_𝒴}
items.statement: For a parabolic P ⊂ G with Levi M, deg_P : Gr_{M,Div^d_𝒴} → ℤ is the locally constant function obtained as the composite of the projection Gr_{M,Div^d_𝒴} → X_*(M̄) (sum of relative positions, as in (VI.3.1)), where M̄ is the maximal torus quotient (cocenter) of M, and the map X_*(M̄) → ℤ given by pairing with 2ρ_G − 2ρ_M (a character of M trivial on its derived group, hence of M̄).
items.note: GS4:integral-dual-group: "Prove naturality for Levi restriction/constant term, products, maps inducing isomorphisms on adjoint groups and Weil restriction".

items.name: Constant term functors preserve the Satake category
items.statement: Let P ⊂ G be a parabolic with Levi M. Let S → Div^d_𝒴 be any small v-stack. Consider the diagram Gr_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴} ←(q_S)− Gr_{P,S/Div^d_𝒴} −(p_S)→ Gr_{M,S/Div^d_𝒴}. Then the functor Rp_{S!}q_S^*[deg_P] defines a functor CT_{P,S}[deg_P] : Sat(Hck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴}, Λ) → Sat(Hck_{M,S/Div^d_𝒴}, Λ).
items.note: GS4:integral-dual-group: "Prove naturality for Levi restriction/constant term, products, maps inducing isomorphisms on adjoint groups and Weil restriction". Proof: refine to Hck via division by L⁺M using a cocharacter λ with P = P_λ; ULA by Proposition IV.6.14; flat perversity by VI.7.7 and composition with the Borel.

items.name: Transitivity of constant term functors
items.statement: If P′ ⊂ P is a further parabolic with image Q ⊂ M and Levi M′, then there is a natural equivalence CT_{P′,S}[deg_{P′}] ≅ CT_{Q,S}[deg_Q] ∘ CT_{P,S}[deg_P] : Sat(Hck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴}, Λ) → Sat(Hck_{M′,S/Div^d_𝒴}, Λ) (and for triple compositions, the obvious diagram commutes).
items.note: GS4:integral-dual-group: "Prove naturality for Levi restriction/constant term, products, maps inducing isomorphisms on adjoint groups and Weil restriction".

items.name: Convolution product on D_ét(Hck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴}, Λ)^{bd}
items.statement: With all loop groups over Div^d_𝒴, consider Hck_{G,Div^d_𝒴} ×_{Div^d_𝒴} Hck_{G,Div^d_𝒴} ←a− L⁺G\LG ×^{L⁺G} LG/L⁺G −b→ L⁺G\LG/L⁺G = Hck_{G,Div^d_𝒴}, where a is an L⁺G-torsor and b is ind-proper (its fibres are those of Gr_{G,Div^d_𝒴} → Div^d_𝒴). With a_S, b_S the pullbacks along S → Div^d_𝒴, the convolution product is A_1 ⋆ A_2 = Rb_{S*}a_S^*(A_1 ⊠ A_2) for A_1, A_2 ∈ D_ét(Hck_{S/Div^d_𝒴}, Λ)^{bd}; it is associative, making D_ét(Hck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴}, Λ)^{bd} a monoidal category.
items.note: GS2:correspondences: "Define Satake objects by the equivariance, relative perversity, ULA and coefficient flatness conditions of FS VI.6–VI.8. Construct convolution diagrams, the convolution map and operation in the ambient bounded-support derived category via actual proper-support pushforward. Prove ambient associativity and unit with coherent maps." The paper also identifies this monoidal category with endomorphisms of [Div^d_𝒴/L⁺G] ×_{Div^d_𝒴} S in the 2-category C_T of §IV.2.3.3, modulo ind-representability.

items.name: Convolution preserves ULA objects
items.statement: Let A_1, A_2 ∈ D_ét(Hck_{S/Div^d_𝒴}, Λ)^{bd}. If A_1 and A_2 are universally locally acyclic, then A_1 ⋆ A_2 is universally locally acyclic.
items.note: GS2:Satake-closure: "Using GS3:fusion and the semi-infinite/hyperbolic-localization estimates, prove perversity, flatness and ULA preservation, thereby restricting the operation to Satake objects." Proof: Propositions IV.2.11 and IV.2.26. The reviewed decomposition states (i) and (ii) in node GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS2:correspondences/convolution-diagram ('Convolution preserves universal local acyclicity, and preserves ^p D^{<=0}'), so GS2:correspondences is the planning stage; GS2:Satake-closure plans only (iii).

items.name: Convolution preserves ᵖD^{≤0}
items.statement: Let A_1, A_2 ∈ D_ét(Hck_{S/Div^d_𝒴}, Λ)^{bd}. If A_1 and A_2 lie in ᵖD^{≤0}, then A_1 ⋆ A_2 ∈ ᵖD^{≤0}.
items.note: GS2:Satake-closure: "Using GS3:fusion and the semi-infinite/hyperbolic-localization estimates, prove perversity, flatness and ULA preservation, thereby restricting the operation to Satake objects." Proof: reduce to d = 1, S = Div^1_𝒴 and !-extensions of constant sheaves on Schubert cells; form the two-leg convolution Grassmannian Hck~_{G,(Div^1_𝒴)²} and B = Rm_*(p_1^*A_1 ⊗ p_2^*A_2), ULA over (Div^1_𝒴)²; the degree bound on CT_B(B)[deg] off the diagonal extends by density, and restriction to the diagonal is A_1 ⋆ A_2 (a fusion-type argument; goes back to Lusztig [Lus83]). The reviewed decomposition states (i) and (ii) in node GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS2:correspondences/convolution-diagram ('Convolution preserves universal local acyclicity, and preserves ^p D^{<=0}'), so GS2:correspondences is the planning stage; GS2:Satake-closure plans only (iii).

items.name: Convolution preserves the Satake category
items.statement: If A_1, A_2 ∈ Sat(Hck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴}, Λ), then also A_1 ⋆ A_2 ∈ Sat(Hck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴}, Λ).
items.note: GS2:Satake-closure: "Using GS3:fusion and the semi-infinite/hyperbolic-localization estimates, prove perversity, flatness and ULA preservation, thereby restricting the operation to Satake objects." From (i), (ii) and commutation of convolution with Verdier duality.

items.name: All Satake objects are dualizable, with dual sw^*D(A)
items.statement: All objects of the monoidal category Sat(Hck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴}, Λ) are (left and right) dualizable. The right dual of A ∈ Sat(Hck_{G,S/Div^d_𝒴}, Λ) is given by sw^*D(A) where sw : Hck_{G,Div^d_𝒴} ≅ Hck_{G,Div^d_𝒴} is the switching isomorphism (induced by inversion on L_{Div^d_𝒴}G).
items.note: GS4:integral-dual-group: "Construct the total cohomology fibre functor, prove exactness, faithfulness, tensor compatibility and duals in the precise integral category, and reconstruct its affine group scheme." ("and duals"). Proof: Proposition IV.2.24 (adapted to ind-representable maps), invariance of ULA under sw^* (Proposition VI.6.2) and VI.7.12. Remark VI.8.3: asserted without proof in [MV07, end of §11]. Needed for rigidity in VI.10.2 and for VI.9.5. The reviewed decomposition states VI.8.2 in node GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS2:Satake-closure/convolution-preserves-satake-and-dualizability ('every object of the monoidal category Sat(Hck_{G,S/Div^d},Lambda) is left and right dualizable, with right dual sw^* D(A)'); the earlier listing of GS2:correspondences was not the planning stage.

items.name: Results of §§VI.7–VI.8 hold for G reductive over E over Div^d_Y and Div^d_X
items.statement: All results of §§VI.7–VI.8 also hold if G is reductive over E and Div^d_𝒴 is replaced with Div^d_Y or Div^d_X: the case of Div^d_Y follows from that of Div^d_𝒴 as it is an open subset, at least if G admits a reductive model over O_E, which happens étale locally; the case of Div^d_X follows as any map S → Div^d_X locally lifts to S → Div^d_Y with isomorphic pullbacks of the local Hecke stacks.
items.note: GS0:loop-geometry: "Treat arbitrary G/E by descent on the generic Y/X side; do not assert that a ramified group has a reductive integral model over O_E." Assertive remark used to pass to §VI.9 onwards (base Div^1_X). Decorations 𝒴 vs Y lost in the text layer; read from context.

items.name: Hecke stacks and Grassmannians with legs indexed by a finite set I
items.statement: Let G be reductive over E, k = F̄_q, working on Perf_k. For a finite set I with d = |I|, Hck^I_G = Hck_{G,Div^d_X} ×_{Div^d_X} (Div^1_X)^I and Gr^I_G = Gr_{G,Div^d_X} ×_{Div^d_X} (Div^1_X)^I.
items.note: GS3:fusion: "Export coCartesian finite-set functoriality: permutations, maps I → J, disjoint unions, diagonal pullback and unit insertion with all composition laws."

items.name: Sat^I_G(Λ) and the fibre functor F^I
items.statement: For any finite set I, the Satake category Sat^I_G(Λ) is the category Sat(Hck^I_G, Λ) of all A ∈ D_ét(Hck^I_G, Λ) that are universally locally acyclic and flat perverse over (Div^1_X)^I. By Proposition VI.7.10 there is a (not yet monoidal) fibre functor F^I : Sat^I_G(Λ) → LocSys((Div^1_X)^I, Λ).
items.note: GS2:correspondences: "Define Satake objects by the equivariance, relative perversity, ULA and coefficient flatness conditions of FS VI.6–VI.8. Construct convolution diagrams, the convolution map and operation in the ambient bounded-support derived category via actual proper-support pushforward. Prove ambient associativity and unit with coherent maps." GS3:fusion: "Export coCartesian finite-set functoriality: permutations, maps I → J, disjoint unions, diagonal pullback and unit insertion with all composition laws."

items.name: Local systems on (Div^1_X)^I are W_E^I-representations
items.statement: The category LocSys((Div^1_X)^I, Λ) is naturally equivalent to the category Rep_{W_E^I}(Λ) of continuous representations of W_E^I on finite projective Λ-modules.
items.note: VS1: "Establish Drinfeld's lemma IV.7 for the divisor/Weil-action applications". Consequence of Proposition IV.7.3 (Drinfeld's lemma). Also stated in decomposition node GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS3:fusion/finite-set-functoriality-and-constant-terms ('LocSys((Div^1_X)^I,Lambda) is naturally equivalent to Rep_{W_E^I}(Lambda)'), with the proof step 'VI.9.2 from Drinfeld's lemma (IV.7.3)'.

items.name: Functor Sat^I_G(Λ) → Sat^J_G(Λ) for a map of finite sets I → J
items.statement: For any map f : I → J of finite sets there is a natural monoidal functor Sat^I_G(Λ) → Sat^J_G(Λ), defined by pull-push along Gr^I_G ← Gr^I_G ×_{(Div^1_X)^I} (Div^1_X)^J → Gr^J_G (the latter a closed immersion), compatible with composition of maps of finite sets and making the square with F^I, F^J and pullback Rep_{W_E^I}(Λ) → Rep_{W_E^J}(Λ) along W_E^J → W_E^I commute naturally.
items.note: GS3:fusion: "Export coCartesian finite-set functoriality: permutations, maps I → J, disjoint unions, diagonal pullback and unit insertion with all composition laws." Footnote 1 (thanks to T. Feng): on Hecke stacks the corresponding map is not a closed immersion, hence the construction on Gr.

items.name: Restriction to the disjoint-legs locus is fully faithful on Satake categories
items.statement: For I = I_1 ⊔ … ⊔ I_k let j : (Div^1_X)^{I;I_1,…,I_k} ⊂ (Div^1_X)^I be the open subset where x_i ≠ x_{i′} whenever i, i′ lie in different I_j's, and Sat^{I;I_1,…,I_k}_G(Λ) ⊂ D^{ULA}_ét(Hck^I_G ×_{(Div^1_X)^I} (Div^1_X)^{I;I_1,…,I_k}, Λ) defined similarly as Sat^I_G(Λ). The restriction functor j^* : Sat^I_G(Λ) → Sat^{I;I_1,…,I_k}_G(Λ) is fully faithful.
