items.note: GS3:fusion: "Over disjoint-leg loci prove factorization into products of single-leg Grassmannians. Construct fusion by the source's ULA extension along collision diagonals, prove uniqueness and compatibility with repeated collisions, and obtain the commutativity constraint. Verify the Koszul/sign and half-Tate normalization so that the cohomology fibre functor is symmetric monoidal" Proof: A ≅ ᵖH⁰(Rj_*j^*A), since i_*i^!A ∈ ᵖD^{≥2} for the complementary closed i : Z ↪ (Div^1_X)^I, checked after the t-exact RπT∗CT_B[deg] using that Z is stratified by smooth partial diagonals of ℓ-codimension ≥ 1.

items.name: Restriction of local systems to the disjoint-legs locus is fully faithful
items.statement: j^* : LocSys((Div^1_X)^I, Λ) → LocSys((Div^1_X)^{I;I_1,…,I_k}, Λ) is fully faithful.
items.note: GS3:fusion: "Over disjoint-leg loci prove factorization into products of single-leg Grassmannians. Construct fusion by the source's ULA extension along collision diagonals, prove uniqueness and compatibility with repeated collisions, and obtain the commutativity constraint. Verify the Koszul/sign and half-Tate normalization so that the cohomology fibre functor is symmetric monoidal" Same argument (i_*i^!Λ ∈ D^{≥2}).

items.name: Exterior product over the disjoint-legs locus, with modified sign rule
items.statement: Over (Div^1_X)^{I;I_1,…,I_k} one has Hck^I_G ×_{(Div^1_X)^I} (Div^1_X)^{I;I_1,…,I_k} ≅ ∏_{j=1}^k Hck^{I_j}_G ×_{∏_j (Div^1_X)^{I_j}} (Div^1_X)^{I;I_1,…,I_k}, giving a monoidal functor Sat^{I_1}_G(Λ) × … × Sat^{I_k}_G(Λ) → Sat^{I;I_1,…,I_k}_G(Λ) by exterior product. Each Hck^I_G = (Hck^I_G)^{even} ⊔ (Hck^I_G)^{odd} according to the parity of d_{μ•} = Σ_i ⟨2ρ, μ_i⟩ (open and closed, as the dominance order only compares elements of the same parity), F^I of sheaves on the even (resp. odd) part is concentrated in even (resp. odd) degrees, and a minus sign is introduced whenever two sheaves concentrated on odd parts are commuted; equivalently, the square with (F^{I_1}, …, F^{I_k}), F^{I;I_1,…,I_k} and ⊠ on local systems commutes functorially in I_1, …, I_k and under permutations.
items.note: GS3:fusion: "Over disjoint-leg loci prove factorization into products of single-leg Grassmannians. Construct fusion by the source's ULA extension along collision diagonals, prove uniqueness and compatibility with repeated collisions, and obtain the commutativity constraint. Verify the Koszul/sign and half-Tate normalization so that the cohomology fibre functor is symmetric monoidal" The sign choice is pinned down by faithfulness of the fibre functors.

items.name: Convolution local Hecke stacks for collision and fusion (Hck~_{G,(Div^1_𝒴)^2} and Hck^{I;I_1,…,I_k}_G)
items.statement: Over (Div^1_𝒴)^2, Hck~_{G,(Div^1_𝒴)^2} is the moduli space of G-bundles 𝓔_0, 𝓔_1, 𝓔_2 over B⁺_{(Div^1_𝒴)^2} with isomorphisms 𝓔_0 ≅ 𝓔_1 over B⁺_{(Div^1_𝒴)^2}[1/𝓘_1] and 𝓔_1 ≅ 𝓔_2 over B⁺_{(Div^1_𝒴)^2}[1/𝓘_2], where 𝓘_1, 𝓘_2 ⊂ 𝒪_{𝒴_S} are the ideal sheaves of the two Cartier divisors. It has projections p_1, p_2 : Hck~_{G,(Div^1_𝒴)^2} → Hck_{G,Div^1_𝒴} (remembering (𝓔_0, 𝓔_1) resp. (𝓔_1, 𝓔_2)) and m : Hck~_{G,(Div^1_𝒴)^2} → Hck_{G,(Div^1_𝒴)^2/Div^2_𝒴} (remembering (𝓔_0, 𝓔_2)). Away from the diagonal m is an isomorphism onto Hck_{G,(Div^1_𝒴)^2_≠/Div^2_𝒴}; over the diagonal Hck~ is L⁺G\LG ×^{L⁺G} LG/L⁺G, so restricting Rm_*(p_1^*A_1 ⊗^L_Λ p_2^*A_2) to the diagonal gives A_1 ⋆ A_2. More generally, for a finite set I = I_1 ⊔ … ⊔ I_k, Hck^{I;I_1,…,I_k}_G → (Div^1_X)^I parametrizes G-bundles 𝓔_0, …, 𝓔_k over B⁺_{(Div^1_X)^I} with isomorphisms 𝓔_{j−1} ≅ 𝓔_j after inverting 𝓘_i for all i ∈ I_j (j = 1, …, k), with projections p_j : Hck^{I;I_1,…,I_k}_G → Hck^{I_j}_G and m : Hck^{I;I_1,…,I_k}_G → Hck^I_G (remembering 𝓔_0 and 𝓔_k); over (Div^1_X)^{I;I_1,…,I_k} the map m is an isomorphism, and B = Rm_*(p_1^*A_1 ⊗^L_Λ … ⊗^L_Λ p_k^*A_k) is the fusion product of A_j ∈ Sat^{I_j}_G(Λ).
items.locator: Chapter VI, §VI.8, proof of Proposition VI.8.1(ii), p. 225; §VI.9, proof of Definition/Proposition VI.9.4, p. 229
items.note: The geometric object behind both the t-exactness of convolution (VI.8.1(ii), 'a fusion-type argument') and the fusion product (VI.9.4); items c6b-convolution-right-t-exact-VI.8.1ii and c6b-fusion-product-VI.9.4 describe it only in their notes. GS2:correspondences: 'Construct convolution diagrams, the convolution map …'; its decomposition node GS2:correspondences/convolution-diagram records 'one then passes to the universal situation over (Div^1_Y-curly)^2 and uses density of the complement of the diagonal'. GS3:fusion: 'Construct fusion by the source's ULA extension along collision diagonals'. Added in review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21).

items.name: Fusion product lands in Sat^I_G(Λ)
items.statement: The image of Sat^{I_1}_G(Λ) × … × Sat^{I_k}_G(Λ) → Sat^{I;I_1,…,I_k}_G(Λ) lands in Sat^I_G(Λ) ⊂ Sat^{I;I_1,…,I_k}_G(Λ) (via the fully faithful j^* of VI.9.3), defining the fusion product ∗ : Sat^{I_1}_G(Λ) × … × Sat^{I_k}_G(Λ) → Sat^I_G(Λ), a functor of monoidal categories, functorial in I_1, …, I_k. It makes the diagram with (F^{I_1}, …, F^{I_k}), F^I and ⊠ : LocSys((Div^1_X)^{I_1}, Λ) × … × LocSys((Div^1_X)^{I_k}, Λ) → LocSys((Div^1_X)^I, Λ) commute functorially in I_1, …, I_k and permutations of I_1, …, I_k.
items.note: GS3:fusion: "Over disjoint-leg loci prove factorization into products of single-leg Grassmannians. Construct fusion by the source's ULA extension along collision diagonals, prove uniqueness and compatibility with repeated collisions, and obtain the commutativity constraint. Verify the Koszul/sign and half-Tate normalization so that the cohomology fibre functor is symmetric monoidal" Proof: convolution Hecke stack Hck^{I;I_1,…,I_k}_G with projections p_j, m; B = Rm_*(p_1^*A_1 ⊗ … ⊗ p_k^*A_k) is ULA (Propositions IV.2.11, IV.2.26), equals the exterior product on the disjoint locus, and RπT∗CT_B(B)[deg] is a finite projective local system.

items.name: Symmetric monoidal structure on Sat^I_G(Λ) via fusion; F^I symmetric monoidal
items.statement: Using Sat^I_G(Λ) × … × Sat^I_G(Λ) → Sat^{I⊔…⊔I}_G(Λ) → Sat^I_G(Λ) (the latter for I ⊔ … ⊔ I → I), Sat^I_G(Λ) becomes an E_∞-monoid object in monoidal categories, functorially in I; equivalently a symmetric monoidal structure refining the convolution product. The functor F^I : Sat^I_G(Λ) → LocSys((Div^1_X)^I, Λ) ≅ Rep_{W_E^I}(Λ) is symmetric monoidal, functorially in I.
items.note: GS3:fusion: "Over disjoint-leg loci prove factorization into products of single-leg Grassmannians. Construct fusion by the source's ULA extension along collision diagonals, prove uniqueness and compatibility with repeated collisions, and obtain the commutativity constraint. Verify the Koszul/sign and half-Tate normalization so that the cohomology fibre functor is symmetric monoidal"

items.name: F^I(sw^*A) ≅ F^I(A) and D commutes with sw^*
items.statement: For A ∈ Sat^I_G(Λ), there are natural isomorphisms F^I(sw^*A) ≅ F^I(A) and D(sw^*A) ≅ sw^*D(A).
items.note: GS4:integral-dual-group: "Construct the Chevalley involution and prove its compatibility with Verdier duality, inversion of modifications and representation duals." Proof: in a symmetric monoidal category the dual sw^*D(A) (VI.8.2) satisfies sw^*Dsw^*D(A) ≅ A; with F^I symmetric monoidal and VI.7.12. Resolves Remark VI.7.11.

items.name: Verdier duality is symmetric monoidal and D∘F^I ≅ (F^I)^*
items.statement: D is naturally a symmetric monoidal functor, and D ∘ F^I ≅ (F^I)^* as symmetric monoidal functors.
items.note: GS4:integral-dual-group: "Construct the Chevalley involution and prove its compatibility with Verdier duality, inversion of modifications and representation duals."

items.name: Constant term functors commute with fusion
items.statement: Given a parabolic P ⊂ G with Levi M and the constant term functors CT^I_P[deg_P] : Sat^I_G(Λ) → Sat^I_M(Λ), for any finite set I = I_1 ⊔ … ⊔ I_k the diagram with fusion ∗ : ∏_j Sat^{I_j}_G(Λ) → Sat^I_G(Λ), ∗ : ∏_j Sat^{I_j}_M(Λ) → Sat^I_M(Λ), (CT^{I_1}_P[deg_P], …, CT^{I_k}_P[deg_P]) and CT^I_P[deg_P] commutes functorially in I and permutations of I_1, …, I_k. In particular CT^I_P[deg_P] is naturally symmetric monoidal for the fusion product, compatibly with composition for P′ ⊂ P.
items.note: GS4:integral-dual-group: "Prove naturality for Levi restriction/constant term, products, maps inducing isomorphisms on adjoint groups and Weil restriction". Proof: Künneth over the disjoint locus plus VI.9.3.

items.name: Bounded Satake subcategories Sat^I_{G,(W_i)_i}(Λ)
items.statement: Given finite Galois-stable subsets W_i ⊂ X_*(T)^+, i ∈ I, closed under the dominance order, Hck^I_{G,(W_i)_i} ⊂ Hck^I_G is the corresponding quasicompact closed substack and Sat^I_{G,(W_i)_i}(Λ) ⊂ Sat^I_G(Λ) the full subcategory of objects supported on it.
items.note: GS4:integral-dual-group: "Construct the total cohomology fibre functor, prove exactness, faithfulness, tensor compatibility and duals in the precise integral category, and reconstruct its affine group scheme."

items.name: The fibre functor on bounded Satake categories has a left adjoint
items.statement: The functor F^I : Sat^I_{G,(W_i)_i}(Λ) → Rep_{W_E^I}(Λ) admits a left adjoint L^I_{(W_i)_i}.
items.note: GS4:integral-dual-group: "Construct the total cohomology fibre functor, prove exactness, faithfulness, tensor compatibility and duals in the precise integral category, and reconstruct its affine group scheme." Gives the representing objects X_i for Proposition VI.10.2.

items.name: L^I(V) ≅ L^I(1) ⊗ V
items.statement: There is a natural isomorphism L^I_{(W_i)_i}(V) ≅ L^I_{(W_i)_i}(1) ⊗ V, V ∈ Rep_{W_E^I}(Λ), where 1 ∈ Rep_{W_E^I}(Λ) is the tensor unit, and we use that Sat^I_G(Λ) is tensored over Rep_{W_E^I}(Λ).
items.note: GS4:integral-dual-group: "Construct the total cohomology fibre functor, prove exactness, faithfulness, tensor compatibility and duals in the precise integral category, and reconstruct its affine group scheme."

items.name: L^I(1) is the fusion of the one-leg L^{{i}}(1)
items.statement: There is a natural isomorphism L^I_{(W_i)_i}(1) ≅ ∗_{i∈I} L^{{i}}_{W_i}(1) as the fusion of L^{{i}}_{W_i}(1) ∈ Sat^{{i}}_{G,W_i}(Λ).
items.note: GS4:integral-dual-group: "Construct the total cohomology fibre functor, prove exactness, faithfulness, tensor compatibility and duals in the precise integral category, and reconstruct its affine group scheme." Proof: generic Künneth for the left adjoint to hyperbolic localization, then full faithfulness of j^* (B = ᵖH⁰(Rj_*j^*B)).

items.name: One-leg left adjoint is the restriction of the perverse left adjoint; its value on 1 is flat ULA
items.statement: If I = {i} has one element and W = W_i, then the left adjoint is the restriction of the left adjoint to F′ = ⊕_m H^m(Rπ_{G*}) : Perv(Hck^{{i}}_{G,W}, Λ) → Mod_{W_E}(Λ).
items.note: GS4:integral-dual-group: "Construct the total cohomology fibre functor, prove exactness, faithfulness, tensor compatibility and duals in the precise integral category, and reconstruct its affine group scheme." Proof: adjoint functor theorem gives L′_W; P_W = L′_W(1) is shown ULA and flat perverse over Λ = ℤ/ℓ^cℤ by induction on W, using VI.7.9 and the ℓ^a-bound of VI.7.5 to kill K in 0 → K → ᵖj_{μ!}j_μ^*P_W → P_W → P_{W̄} → 0.

items.name: Relative Tannakian reconstruction over a rigid symmetric monoidal base
items.statement: Let 𝒜 be a rigid symmetric monoidal category, and let 𝒞 be a symmetric monoidal category with a tensor action of 𝒜. Let F : 𝒞 → 𝒜 be a symmetric monoidal 𝒜-linear conservative functor, such that 𝒞 admits and F reflects coequalizers of F-split parallel pairs. Assume that 𝒞 can be written as a filtered union of full subcategories 𝒞_i, stable under coequalizers of F-split parallel pairs and the 𝒜-action, such that F|_{𝒞_i} is representable by some X_i ∈ 𝒞. Then ℋ = lim→_i F(X_i)^∨ ∈ Ind(𝒜) admits a natural structure as a bialgebra (with commutative multiplication and associative comultiplication), and 𝒞 is naturally equivalent to the symmetric monoidal category of representations of ℋ in 𝒜 (comodules over ℋ as a coalgebra, with the symmetric monoidal structure from the commutative multiplication).
items.note: GS4:integral-dual-group: "Construct the total cohomology fibre functor, prove exactness, faithfulness, tensor compatibility and duals in the precise integral category, and reconstruct its affine group scheme." Axiomatization of [MV07, Proposition 11.1]. Proof uses the Barr–Beck monadicity theorem (Mathlib has Beck's monadicity theorem in CategoryTheory.Monad.Monadicity, a general input only). Tau Ceti's TauCeti.Tannaka namespace (TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/*) treats reconstruction of a Hopf algebra from its comodule category over a commutative ring, not this relative recognition statement.

items.name: Relative Tannakian reconstruction: ℋ is Hopf when 𝒞 is rigid
items.statement: In the situation of Proposition VI.10.2, if 𝒞 is rigid, then ℋ admits an inverse, i.e. is a Hopf algebra.
items.locator: Chapter VI, §VI.10, Proposition VI.10.2 (final sentence), pp. 233–234
items.note: GS4:integral-dual-group: "Construct the total cohomology fibre functor, prove exactness, faithfulness, tensor compatibility and duals in the precise integral category, and reconstruct its affine group scheme." Antipode from F(X_i)^∨ ≅ ℋom(X_i ⊗ X_i, 1) and the swap. (PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E46).

items.name: Hopf algebras ℋ^I_G(Λ) ∈ Ind(Rep_{W_E^I}(Λ))
items.statement: Applying Proposition VI.10.2 to Sat^I_G(Λ) (with fibre functor F^I, the filtration by Sat^I_{G,(W_i)_i}(Λ) and the representing objects of VI.10.1) gives Hopf algebras ℋ^I_G(Λ) ∈ Ind(Rep_{W_E^I}(Λ)).
items.note: GS4:integral-dual-group: "Construct the total cohomology fibre functor, prove exactness, faithfulness, tensor compatibility and duals in the precise integral category, and reconstruct its affine group scheme."

items.name: ℋ^I_G(Λ) is the tensor product of one-leg Hopf algebras
items.statement: The exterior tensor product ⊠_{i∈I} : ∏_{i∈I} Sat^{{i}}_G(Λ) → Sat^I_G(Λ) induces an isomorphism ⊗_{i∈I} ℋ^{{i}}_G(Λ) ≅ ℋ^I_G(Λ).
items.note: GS4:integral-dual-group: "Construct the total cohomology fibre functor, prove exactness, faithfulness, tensor compatibility and duals in the precise integral category, and reconstruct its affine group scheme." Proof: VI.10.1(ii) and F^I(∗_{i∈I} A_i) ≅ ⊗_{i∈I} F(A_i).

items.name: The Tannaka group Ǧ over ℤ̂^p
items.statement: ℋ_G(Λ) = ℋ^{{∗}}_G(Λ) ∈ Ind(Rep_{W_E}(Λ)) is compatible with base change in Λ; taking Sat_G(ℤ̂^p) = lim←_n Sat_G(ℤ/nℤ) (n prime to p) with fibre functor into Rep^cont_{W_E}(ℤ̂^p) = lim←_n Rep_{W_E}(ℤ/nℤ) yields a Hopf algebra ℋ_G ∈ Ind(Rep^cont_{W_E}(ℤ̂^p)), equivalently an affine group scheme Ǧ over ℤ̂^p with a (suitably continuous) action of W_E. Here lim←_n Rep_{W_E}(ℤ/nℤ) is the category of compatible systems of continuous W_E-representations on finite projective ℤ/nℤ-modules, equivalently of continuous W_E-representations on ℤ̂^p-modules M = ∏_{ℓ≠p} M_ℓ with each M_ℓ finite free over ℤ_ℓ (i.e. ∏_{ℓ≠p} Rep^cont_{W_E}(ℤ_ℓ)); the paper's gloss 'on finite free ℤ̂^p-modules' is inaccurate.
items.note: GS4:integral-dual-group: "Construct the total cohomology fibre functor, prove exactness, faithfulness, tensor compatibility and duals in the precise integral category, and reconstruct its affine group scheme." GS4:integral-dual-group: "Implement FS VI.9–VI.11's passage from Z/ℓ^n to Z_ℓ, then its integral recovery from torus/rank-one Levi maps and the maximal-compact-generation argument (RG2.2–RG2.4)."

items.name: The pinned dual group Ĝ over ℤ̂^p with Tate-twisted W_E-action
items.statement: From the universal Cartan of G: X_* with its Gal-action, coroots Φ^∨ ⊂ X_* with positive coroots Φ^∨_+, characters X^* with dominant chamber (X^*)^+ and roots Φ ⊃ Φ_+. Let Ĝ be the pinned Chevalley group scheme over ℤ̂^p for the dual root datum (X^*, Φ, X_*, Φ^∨), with T̂ ⊂ B̂ ⊂ Ĝ, X^*(T̂) ≅ X_* such that Φ^∨_+ are the weights of T̂ on Lie B̂/Lie T̂ = ⊕_{a∈Φ^∨_+} Lie Û_a. Write the pinnings of simple root groups with a Tate twist as ψ_a : Lie Û_a ≅ ℤ̂^p(1); then W_E acts naturally on the root datum and the pinning, and thereby on Ĝ.
items.note: RG2.5: "Construct a pinned split dual group over ℤ from the dual root datum and the continuous finite-image action on its pinning induced by the E-form of G." and GS4:integral-dual-group: "Identify the maximal torus and root datum via weight functors, rank-one calculations and simple reflections, then identify the group with the pinned dual. Prove descent for nonsplit G and distinguish the geometric Weil action from the standard pinned action". Caveat: RG2.5 describes a finite-image action, while FS's Tate-twisted action on the pinning goes through the cyclotomic character; GS4:integral-dual-group's "distinguish the geometric Weil action from the standard pinned action" covers this.

items.name: Identification of the Tannaka group with the Langlands dual group
items.statement: There is a canonical W_E-equivariant isomorphism Ǧ ≅ Ĝ.
items.note: GS4:integral-dual-group: "Identify the maximal torus and root datum via weight functors, rank-one calculations and simple reflections, then identify the group with the pinned dual. Prove descent for nonsplit G and distinguish the geometric Weil action from the standard pinned action". More precise than [MV07] (canonical isomorphism, non-split G). Proof: reduce to ℤ_ℓ (CRT), split pinned case via torus, PGL_2, rank one, Levi M_a maps and integral closure (PY06), then independence of pinning and Galois descent. Combined with VI.10.2 this is the geometric Satake equivalence Sat_G ≅ Rep(Ĝ) used by Hecke operators (Chapter IX) and excursion operators.

items.name: Satake for tori: Ť ≅ T̂
items.statement: If G = T is a split torus (the split case of the proof of Theorem VI.11.1), then Gr_{T,Div^1_X} ≅ X_*(T) × Div^1_X, Sat_T is the category of X_*(T)-graded objects in Rep^cont_{W_E}(ℤ_ℓ), and Ť ≅ T̂ is the dual torus with X^*(T̂) = X_*(T).
items.locator: Chapter VI, §VI.11, proof of Theorem VI.11.1, p. 236
items.note: GS4:integral-dual-group: "Identify the maximal torus and root datum via weight functors, rank-one calculations and simple reflections, then identify the group with the pinned dual. Prove descent for nonsplit G and distinguish the geometric Weil action from the standard pinned action"

items.name: The map T̂ = Ť → Ǧ induced by CT_B[deg] is a W_E-equivariant closed immersion
items.statement: The symmetric monoidal constant term functor CT_B[deg] : Sat_G → Sat_T commutes with the fibre functors by ⊕_i Hⁱ(Rπ_{G*}) ≅ H⁰(Rπ_{T*}CT_B[deg]), giving a W_E-equivariant map T̂ = Ť → Ǧ; using A_μ = ᵖj_{μ!}ℤ_ℓ[d_μ], whose μ-weight space is 1-dimensional, this map is a closed immersion.
items.locator: Chapter VI, §VI.11, proof of Theorem VI.11.1, p. 236
items.note: GS4:integral-dual-group: "Identify the maximal torus and root datum via weight functors, rank-one calculations and simple reflections, then identify the group with the pinned dual. Prove descent for nonsplit G and distinguish the geometric Weil action from the standard pinned action"

items.name: Ǧ_{ℚ_ℓ} is a connected reductive group with maximal torus Ť_{ℚ_ℓ} and Borel B̌_{ℚ_ℓ}
items.statement: Sat_G(ℚ_ℓ) = Sat_G(ℤ_ℓ)[1/ℓ] (Sat_G(ℤ_ℓ) = lim←_m Sat_G(ℤ/ℓ^mℤ)) satisfies Sat_G(ℚ_ℓ) ≅ ⊕_μ Rep^cont_{W_E}(ℚ_ℓ) ⊗ A_μ, so Rep(Ǧ_{ℚ_ℓ}) ≅ ⊕_μ Vect(ℚ_ℓ) ⊗ A_μ is semisimple. Hence Ǧ_{ℚ_ℓ} is of finite type [DM82, Prop. 2.20], connected [DM82, Cor. 2.22] and reductive [DM82, Prop. 2.23]. The weights of A_μ on T̂_{ℚ_ℓ} lie in {λ ∈ X_* = X^*(T̂) : dominant representative of λ ≤ μ} and include μ with multiplicity 1, so Ť_{ℚ_ℓ} → Ǧ_{ℚ_ℓ} is a maximal torus. The stabilizer B̌ ⊂ Ǧ of the filtration ⊕_{m≤i} R^mπ_{G*} on F = ⊕_m R^mπ_{G*} satisfies that B̌_{ℚ_ℓ} ⊂ Ǧ_{ℚ_ℓ} is a Borel.
items.locator: Chapter VI, §VI.11, proof of Theorem VI.11.1, p. 236
items.note: GS4:rational-reductivity: "Prove geometric semisimplicity of the rational Satake category using the decomposition theorem and the orbit/IC calculation, hence reductivity of the generic fibre of the Tannakian group." Follows [MV07, §7]; the Deligne–Milne Tannakian criteria are external inputs.

items.name: For G = PGL_2, Ǧ ≅ SL(ℤ_ℓ ⊕ ℤ_ℓ(−1))
items.statement: For G = PGL_2 with minuscule μ and Gr_{G,Div^1_X,μ} ≅ ℙ^1_{Div^1_X}, F(A_μ) = H⁰(ℙ^1) ⊕ H²(ℙ^1) = ℤ_ℓ ⊕ ℤ_ℓ(−1) as W_E-representation, and the induced map Ǧ → GL(ℤ_ℓ ⊕ ℤ_ℓ(−1)) is a closed immersion with image SL(ℤ_ℓ ⊕ ℤ_ℓ(−1)); B̌ is the Borel stabilizing the line ℤ_ℓ ⊂ ℤ_ℓ ⊕ ℤ_ℓ(−1), with unipotent radical Hom(ℤ_ℓ(−1), ℤ_ℓ) ≅ ℤ_ℓ(1).
items.locator: Chapter VI, §VI.11, proof of Theorem VI.11.1, pp. 236–237
items.note: GS4:integral-dual-group: "Identify the maximal torus and root datum via weight functors, rank-one calculations and simple reflections, then identify the group with the pinned dual. Prove descent for nonsplit G and distinguish the geometric Weil action from the standard pinned action" ("rank-one calculations"). Proof: generic fibre by rank-1 reductivity; special fibre surjective by Lemma VI.11.2 (irreducibles B_μ = j_{μ!*}F_ℓ); then Lemma VI.11.3 on Hopf algebras.

items.name: Simple objects of the mod-ℓ Satake category are the intersection complexes B_μ, with highest weight μ
items.statement: Let G be split (in the application G = PGL_2) and Λ = F_ℓ. The irreducible representations of Ǧ_{F_ℓ} are in bijection with X_*(T)^+: they correspond to the simple objects B_μ = j_{μ!*}F_ℓ (the intersection complex of the Schubert variety Gr_{G,≤μ}, normalized to be perverse) on Gr_{G,Spd C}, and each B_μ has a highest weight vector of weight μ for Ť ⊂ Ǧ (weights read through CT_B[deg]). Consequently the image H ⊂ SL(F_ℓ ⊕ F_ℓ(−1)) of Ǧ_{F_ℓ} satisfies the hypothesis of Lemma VI.11.2.
items.locator: Chapter VI, §VI.11, proof of Theorem VI.11.1 (case G = PGL_2), p. 237
items.note: Asserted in one sentence ('the irreducible representations of Ǧ_{F_ℓ} are in bijection with dominant cocharacters, corresponding to the simple objects B_μ = j_{μ!*}F_ℓ on Gr_{G,Spd C}; each B_μ has a highest weight vector given by weight μ'). It rests on the classification of simple L⁺G-equivariant perverse F_ℓ-sheaves on the affine Grassmannian over a geometric point (connected stabilizers, so IC sheaves of constant rank-one local systems), and it supplies the hypothesis of Lemma VI.11.2 in the rank-one step. GS4:integral-dual-group: 'Identify the maximal torus and root datum via weight functors, rank-one calculations'; the decomposition node GS4:integral-dual-group/dual-group-identification has acceptance item 'Check the rank-one calculation for PGL_2'. Added in review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21).

items.name: A closed subgroup of SL_2/F_ℓ with irreducibles classified by highest weights is SL_2
items.statement: Let H be a closed subgroup of SL_2/F_ℓ containing the diagonal torus such that its set of irreducible representations injects into ℤ_{≥0} via consideration of highest weight vectors. Then H = SL_2.
items.note: Planned at proof-step level in node GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS4:integral-dual-group/dual-group-identification (proof step: 'recover the integral group scheme from the torus and rank-one Levi maps ... with the auxiliary Lemmas VI.11.2 (subgroups of SL_2/F_l containing the diagonal torus), VI.11.3 (...) and VI.11.4 ([PY06, Corollary 5.2])'); GS4:integral-dual-group's coverage lists Lemmas VI.11.2–VI.11.4 as located but not read. Not in Mathlib or Tau Ceti. Proof: reduce to H reduced (Frobenius power), connected by [DM82, Cor. 2.22], and exclude torus and Borel (too many irreducibles). Used for surjectivity Ǧ_{F_ℓ} → SL_2 in the PGL_2 case.

items.name: Iso criterion for maps of flat ℤ_ℓ-modules
items.statement: Let f : M → N be a map of flat ℤ_ℓ-modules such that M/ℓ → N/ℓ is injective and M[1/ℓ] → N[1/ℓ] is an isomorphism. Then f is an isomorphism.
items.note: Planned at proof-step level in node GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS4:integral-dual-group/dual-group-identification ('VI.11.3 (flat Z_l-modules with injective reduction)'). Elementary commutative algebra; no Mathlib or Tau Ceti declaration of this exact statement found. Applied to the Hopf algebras to conclude Ǧ ≅ SL_2 and Ǧ ≅ Ĝ integrally. Printed 'ℓ^k n = f(m)' for ℓ^k x = f(m) in the proof (PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E48).

items.name: For G split of semisimple rank 1, Ǧ ≅ (Ǧ_ad)~ ×^{μ_2} Ž
items.statement: If G is split, pinned and of semisimple rank 1 (printed 'of rank 1'), with G → G_ad ≅ PGL_2 (isomorphism determined by the pinning), Gr_{G,Div^1_X} ≅ π_1(G) ×_{π_1(G_ad)} Gr_{G_ad,Div^1_X} with π_1(G_ad) ≅ ℤ/2ℤ, so Sat_G is the category of A ∈ Sat_{G_ad} with a refinement of the ℤ/2ℤ-grading to a π_1(G)-grading; hence Ǧ = (G_ad)̌ ×^{μ_2} Ž where Ž is the split torus with character group π_1(G), and Ǧ ≅ Ĝ including the isomorphism ψ_a on the root group.
items.locator: Chapter VI, §VI.11, proof of Theorem VI.11.1, p. 237
items.note: GS4:integral-dual-group: "Identify the maximal torus and root datum via weight functors, rank-one calculations and simple reflections, then identify the group with the pinned dual. Prove descent for nonsplit G and distinguish the geometric Weil action from the standard pinned action"

items.name: Levi maps identify roots, Weyl group and root datum of Ǧ_{ℚ_ℓ} with the dual datum
items.statement: For G split and a a simple coroot with minimal Levi M_a ⊃ T and parabolic P_a ⊃ B, CT_{P_a}[deg_{P_a}] : Sat_G → Sat_{M_a} induces M̌_a → Ǧ compatible with Ť, so a ∈ X_* = X^*(Ť) is a root and a^∨ ∈ X^* = X_*(Ť) a coroot of Ǧ, s_a ∈ W̌; thus W ⊂ W̌, Φ^∨ ⊂ Φ(Ǧ_{ℚ_ℓ}), Φ ⊂ Φ^∨(Ǧ_{ℚ_ℓ}), and these inclusions are equalities (weights of A_μ lie in the convex hull of Wμ). With the isomorphisms on simple root groups one gets a unique isomorphism Ǧ_{ℚ_ℓ} ≅ Ĝ_{ℚ_ℓ}, compatible with M̂_a ≅ M̌_a → Ǧ.
items.locator: Chapter VI, §VI.11, proof of Theorem VI.11.1, pp. 237–238
items.note: GS4:integral-dual-group: "Identify the maximal torus and root datum via weight functors, rank-one calculations and simple reflections, then identify the group with the pinned dual. Prove descent for nonsplit G and distinguish the geometric Weil action from the standard pinned action"

items.name: Integral isomorphism Ǧ ≅ Ĝ in the split pinned case
items.statement: Ĝ(ℤ̆_ℓ) is generated by the M̂_a(ℤ̆_ℓ), so Ĝ(ℤ̆_ℓ) ⊂ Ǧ(ℤ̆_ℓ) inside Ǧ(ℚ̆_ℓ) ≅ Ĝ(ℚ̆_ℓ); for a representation Ǧ → GL_N closed immersion over ℚ_ℓ, the map Ĝ_{ℚ_ℓ} → GL_N extends to Ĝ → GL_N, a closed immersion by Lemma VI.11.4 (after reducing to Ĝ simply connected via G_ad), so Ǧ → GL_N factors through Ĝ ↪ GL_N; the resulting Ǧ → Ĝ is an isomorphism on generic fibres and surjective on special fibres, hence an isomorphism by Lemma VI.11.3.
items.locator: Chapter VI, §VI.11, proof of Theorem VI.11.1, p. 238
items.note: GS4:integral-dual-group: "Implement FS VI.9–VI.11's passage from Z/ℓ^n to Z_ℓ, then its integral recovery from torus/rank-one Levi maps and the maximal-compact-generation argument (RG2.2–RG2.4)."

items.name: Prasad–Yu: homomorphisms from reductive ℤ_ℓ-groups that are generically closed immersions
items.statement: Let H be a reductive group over ℤ_ℓ, H′ some affine group scheme of finite type over ℤ_ℓ, and let ρ : H → H′ be a homomorphism that is a closed immersion in the generic fibre. Assume that ℓ ≠ 2, or that no almost simple factor of the derived group of H_{ℚ̄_ℓ} is isomorphic to SO_{2n+1} (e.g., the derived group of H is simply connected). Then ρ is a closed immersion.
items.locator: Chapter VI, §VI.11, Lemma VI.11.4 ([PY06, Corollary 5.2]), p. 238
items.note: Cited external result [PY06, Corollary 5.2] (G. Prasad, J.-K. Yu, On quasi-reductive group schemes, J. Algebraic Geom. 15 (2006)). Planned at proof-step level in node GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS4:integral-dual-group/dual-group-identification ('VI.11.4 ([PY06, Corollary 5.2])'), but PY06 is not among the node's prerequisites and no atlas layer or library proves it; the paper's prerequisites list should add PY06. Not in Mathlib or Tau Ceti.

items.name: The isomorphism Ǧ ≅ Ĝ is independent of the pinning; Galois descent
items.statement: For G split, the cohomological grading on F alone determines Ť ⊂ Ǧ as its stabilizer and B̌ ⊂ Ǧ as the stabilizer of the associated filtration, and the isomorphisms ψ_a : Lie Û_a ≅ ℤ_ℓ(1) are independent of choices: over the Gm-torsor Fℓ~_a → Fℓ of pinnings of M_a and S = Fℓ~_a^◇/φ^ℤ → Div^1_X, constant term for P_a is symmetric monoidal and independent of the Borel, reducing to PGL_2 where Û_a ≅ Hom(H²(Fℓ), H⁰(Fℓ)) ≅ ℤ_ℓ(1) canonically for Fℓ ≅ ℙ^1. Hence for split G the isomorphism Ǧ ≅ Ĝ is canonical, and the general case follows by Galois descent from a finite Galois extension E′|E splitting G.
items.locator: Chapter VI, §VI.11, proof of Theorem VI.11.1, pp. 238–239
items.note: GS4:integral-dual-group: "Identify the maximal torus and root datum via weight functors, rank-one calculations and simple reflections, then identify the group with the pinned dual. Prove descent for nonsplit G and distinguish the geometric Weil action from the standard pinned action"

items.name: Inner automorphisms of G act trivially on Ǧ
items.statement: By transport of structure, an automorphism of G induces a symmetric monoidal autoequivalence of Sat_G commuting with the fibre functor, hence an automorphism of Ǧ. For an inner automorphism of G the induced automorphism of Ǧ is the identity; in particular Ǧ depends on G only up to inner automorphisms.
items.locator: Chapter VI, §VI.11, remark after Theorem VI.11.1, p. 235; used in §VI.12, proof of Proposition VI.12.1, p. 240
items.note: p. 235: 'Note that in particular, Ǧ only depends on G up to inner automorphisms; this is not clear [a priori]'. p. 240: 'We know, by the proof of Theorem VI.11.1, that any inner automorphism of G induces the identity on Ǧ'; this lets the proof of VI.12.1 replace the Chevalley involution θ by θ′ = θ ∘ Ad(w_0). It follows from the canonicity of Ǧ ≅ Ĝ (item c6b-canonicity-independent-of-pinning) and the fact that inner automorphisms act trivially on the based root datum. GS4:integral-dual-group: 'Prove naturality for … maps inducing isomorphisms on adjoint groups …'. Added in review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21).

items.name: sw^* as a symmetric monoidal autoequivalence and the induced automorphism of Ǧ
items.statement: sw^* : Sat^I_G(Λ) → Sat^I_G(Λ) upgrades to a symmetric monoidal functor, written as the composition of Verdier duality D and the duality functor sw^*D in Sat^I_G(Λ); this symmetric monoidal functor commutes with the fibre functor F^I (as symmetric monoidal functors), cf. Corollary VI.9.5. Thus sw^* induces an automorphism of the Tannaka group Ǧ commuting with the W_E-action.
items.note: GS4:integral-dual-group: "Construct the Chevalley involution and prove its compatibility with Verdier duality, inversion of modifications and representation duals."

items.name: sw^* is the Chevalley involution up to conjugation by ρ̂(−1)
items.statement: Under the isomorphism Ǧ ≅ Ĝ with the dual group, the isomorphism sw^* is given by the Chevalley involution (induced by the map on root data which on X_* is μ ↦ −w_0(μ)), up to conjugation by ρ̂(−1) ∈ Ĝ_ad(ℤ_ℓ).
items.note: GS4:integral-dual-group: "Construct the Chevalley involution and prove its compatibility with Verdier duality, inversion of modifications and representation duals." Proof: reduce to G split adjoint; θ^*sw^* preserves the grading, hence Ť and B̌, and is conjugation by s ∈ Ť_ad; compatibility with CT_P via θ′ = θ∘w_0 and Proposition IV.6.13 reduces to PGL_2, where A = i_{μ*}ℤ_ℓ[1](1/2) (√q ∈ Λ) and the determinant pairing on the standard SL_2-representation is alternating, giving (u, −u). Remark VI.12.2: Ginzburg [Gin90] overlooked the sign ρ̂(−1); Zhu [Zhu17] and Lusztig–Yun [LY13] control it.

items.name: Smooth Q_ℓ-representations embed into solid sheaves on [∗/G(E)]
items.statement: If V is a (discrete) Q_ℓ-vector space, it gives rise to the solid condensed sheaf V ⊗_{Q_ℓ^disc} Q_ℓ whose value on a profinite set S is lim_{→, W⊂V finite dim.} Cont(S, W). The category of smooth representations of G(E) with values in discrete Q_ℓ-vector spaces injects into the category of solid Q_ℓ-pro-étale sheaves on [∗/G(E)]; since ℓ ≠ p and G(E) is locally pro-p, representations of the condensed group G(E) on the condensed Q_ℓ-vector space V ⊗_{Q_ℓ^disc} Q_ℓ are the same as smooth representations of G(E) on V.
items.note: Unnumbered motivating fact, stated without proof in the introduction; made precise by Proposition VII.7.1 (D_lis([∗/G_b(E)],Λ) ≅ D(G_b(E),Λ)). VS4 plans "Extend to D_lis in the precise coefficient range of VII.7" and "Prove localization triangles and the infinite semiorthogonal decomposition along the HN strata ... Characterize compact objects by compact restrictions with finite stratum support, and by the thick closure of compact induction from pro-p open subgroups"; the discrete-vs-condensed comparison is VS3 ("Compare ordinary, adic, solid and lisse coefficients"). No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: j♮Ẑ and the free solid sheaf Ẑ[U]^■ for quasi-pro-étale U
items.statement: Ẑ denotes the pro-étale sheaf lim_n Z/nZ over nonzero integers n, and Ẑ^p = lim_{(n,p)=1} Z/nZ. Let X be a spatial diamond; on qcqs objects there is a fully faithful functor Pro(X_ét^qcqs) → X_qproét^qcqs whose image is a basis of the quasi-pro-étale topology ([Sch17a, Prop. 11.23(ii), 11.24]). For quasi-pro-étale j : U → X written as a cofiltered inverse limit of qcqs étale j_i : U_i → X, set j♮Ẑ = lim_{←i} j_{i!}Ẑ (well defined as the pro-system is unique). There is a tautological section of j♮Ẑ over U, equivalently a natural map Ẑ[U] → lim_{←i} Ẑ[U_i] = j♮Ẑ from the free pro-étale Ẑ-module on U. When X = Spa(C), j♮Ẑ is the sheaf denoted Ẑ[U]^■ in [CS], and this notation is used in general.
items.note: VS2 plans "the generators/exactness needed for FS VII.1" and "Construct the missing solidification universal property, derived solid tensor/Hom"; the decomposition node VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories:VS2/solid-sheaves-on-v-stacks records this construction. Generators of the solid category. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Solid Ẑ-sheaf on a spatial diamond (Definition VII.1.1)
items.statement: Let X be a spatial diamond and F a pro-étale sheaf of Ẑ-modules on X. Then F is solid if for all quasi-pro-étale j : U → X that can be written as a cofiltered inverse limit of qcqs étale maps, the map Hom(j♮Ẑ, F) → F(U) is an isomorphism.
items.note: VS2 plans "the generators/exactness needed for FS VII.1" and "Construct the missing solidification universal property, derived solid tensor/Hom". Sheaf-level analogue of Clausen–Scholze solidity; over Spa C it recovers solid Ẑ-modules (Remark VII.1.18). No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Étale torsion sheaves are solid (Proposition VII.1.2)
items.statement: Let X be a spatial diamond and ν : X_qproét → X_ét the projection. For any étale sheaf F of Z/nZ-modules on X_ét, ν^∗F is solid.
items.note: VS2 plans "the generators/exactness needed for FS VII.1" and "Construct the missing solidification universal property, derived solid tensor/Hom". Proof: consequence of [Sch17a, Proposition 14.9]. Base case for all of VII.1. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Solid Ẑ-sheaves form an abelian subcategory with solidification (Theorem VII.1.3, first part)
items.statement: Let X be a spatial diamond. The category of solid Ẑ-sheaves on X is an abelian subcategory of all pro-étale Ẑ-sheaves on X, stable under all limits, colimits, and extensions. It is generated by the finitely presented objects j♮Ẑ for quasi-pro-étale j : U → X as above, and the inclusion admits a left adjoint F ↦ F^■ that commutes with all colimits.
items.note: VS2 plans "the generators/exactness needed for FS VII.1" and "Construct the missing solidification universal property, derived solid tensor/Hom". Proof (pp. 247–248) via Proposition VII.1.6, Lemma VII.1.5, Proposition VII.1.12 and Ind(Pro(constructible)); Ẑ[U]^■ = j♮Ẑ. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Characterization of finitely presented solid sheaves (Theorem VII.1.3, second part)
items.statement: Let X be a spatial diamond and F a pro-étale Ẑ-sheaf on X. The following are equivalent: (1) F is finitely presented in the category of all pro-étale Ẑ-sheaves, and is solid; (2) F is solid, and finitely presented in the category of solid Ẑ-sheaves; (3) F can be written as a cofiltered inverse limit of torsion constructible étale sheaves. For any such F, the underlying pro-étale sheaf is representable by a spatial diamond. The category of F satisfying (1)–(3) is stable under kernels, cokernels, and extensions, in particular an abelian category, and is equivalent to the Pro-category of torsion constructible étale sheaves.
items.note: VS2 plans "the generators/exactness needed for FS VII.1" and "Construct the missing solidification universal property, derived solid tensor/Hom". Used constantly to reduce solid statements to étale ones by writing finitely presented solid sheaves as cofiltered limits of constructible sheaves. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Solid sheaves = Ind(Pro(torsion constructible)) (Theorem VII.1.3, third part)
items.statement: Let X be a spatial diamond. The category of all solid Ẑ-sheaves on X is equivalent to the Ind-category of the Pro-category of torsion constructible étale sheaves.
items.note: VS2 plans "the generators/exactness needed for FS VII.1" and "Construct the missing solidification universal property, derived solid tensor/Hom". Question VII.1.4 (open) asks whether qcqs-representability alone implies solidity. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Torsion constructible sheaves are spatial diamonds (Lemma VII.1.5)
items.statement: Any torsion constructible étale sheaf on the spatial diamond X is represented by a spatial diamond.
items.note: VS2 plans "the generators/exactness needed for FS VII.1" and "Construct the missing solidification universal property, derived solid tensor/Hom" (input to Theorem VII.1.3). Proof: surjection ⊕_i j_{i!}Z/n_iZ → F from a finite sum with j_i qc separated étale; that is qc separated étale, hence universally open, so F is a spatial diamond. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Higher inverse limits of constructible sheaves vanish (Proposition VII.1.6)
items.statement: Let X be a spatial diamond and let F_i, i ∈ I, be a cofiltered system of torsion constructible étale sheaves. Then for all j > 0 the higher inverse limit R^j lim_{←i} F_i = 0, taken in the category of pro-étale sheaves on X, vanishes.
items.note: VS2 plans "the generators/exactness needed for FS VII.1" and "Construct the missing solidification universal property, derived solid tensor/Hom" (this is the exactness of Pro(constructible) → pro-étale sheaves). Proof uses w-contractible Y (strictly totally disconnected, closed points closed, π_0Y extremally disconnected; [BS15, §2.4]), duality with S^1 = R/Z and Lemma VII.1.7. items.name: R/Z is injective on an extremally disconnected set (Lemma VII.1.7)
items.statement: Let S be an extremally disconnected profinite set. Then the abelian sheaf R/Z (continuous maps to the circle) on S is injective.

items.name: Pullback preserves solidity and commutes with solidification (Proposition VII.1.8, first part)
items.statement: Let f : Y → X be a map of spatial diamonds. Then pullbacks of solid Ẑ-sheaves are solid, and the functor f^∗ commutes with solidification.
items.note: VS2 plans "the generators/exactness needed for FS VII.1" and "Construct the missing solidification universal property, derived solid tensor/Hom". Proof: f^∗ commutes with all limits [Sch17a, Lemma 14.4], so f^∗(Ẑ[U]^■) = Ẑ[f^∗U]^■. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Solidity descends along surjections (Proposition VII.1.8, second part)
items.statement: Let f : Y → X be a surjective map of spatial diamonds and F a pro-étale Ẑ-sheaf on X such that f^∗F is solid. Then F is solid.
items.note: VS2 plans "the generators/exactness needed for FS VII.1" and "Construct the missing solidification universal property, derived solid tensor/Hom". items.name: Solid v-sheaf on a small v-stack (Definition VII.1.9)
items.statement: Let Y be a small v-stack and let F be a v-sheaf of Ẑ-modules on Y. Then F is solid if for all maps f : X → Y from a spatial diamond X, the pullback f^∗F comes via pullback from a solid Ẑ-sheaf on X_qproét.

items.name: The solid derived category D■(X, Ẑ) (Definition VII.1.10)
items.statement: Let X be a small v-stack. Let D■(X, Ẑ) ⊂ D(X_v, Ẑ) be the full subcategory of all A such that each cohomology sheaf H^i(A) is solid. (As being solid is stable under kernels, cokernels and extensions, this is a triangulated subcategory.)

items.name: Quasi-pro-étale and v-site definitions of D■ agree for diamonds
items.statement: If X is a diamond, the full subcategory of D(X_qproét, Ẑ) of complexes with solid cohomology sheaves maps, via pullback from the quasi-pro-étale site to the v-site, equivalently onto D■(X, Ẑ).

items.name: Solid sheaves satisfy v-descent from the quasi-pro-étale site (Proposition VII.1.11)
items.statement: Let X be a diamond and let F be a sheaf of Ẑ-modules on X_qproét that is solid. Let λ : X_v → X_qproét be the map of sites. Then F → Rλ_∗λ^∗F is an isomorphism.

items.name: Breen's functorial resolution of abelian sheaves (input to Propositions VII.1.12 and VII.4.1)
items.statement: (Breen [Bre78, §3], sheafified.) Every sheaf G of Ẑ-modules on the quasi-pro-étale (or v-) site of a spatial diamond X has a resolution ⋯ → P_1(G) → P_0(G) → G → 0, functorial in G, in which every term P_k(G) is a finite direct sum of free sheaves Ẑ[G^i × Ẑ^j] (i, j ≥ 0). FS use it to compute RHom(G, −) through the functors RHom(Ẑ[G^i × Ẑ^j], −) = RΓ(G^i × Ẑ^j, −). When G is representable by a spatial diamond (for example G = j♮Ẑ), these commute with filtered colimits. When G = j♮Ẑ = lim_i j_{i!}Ẑ, they turn the cofiltered limit into a filtered colimit, RHom(j♮Ẑ, F) = colim_i Rj_{i∗}F|_{U_i} for étale F.
items.locator: Chapter VII, §VII.1, proof of Proposition VII.1.12, p. 250 ('by a resolution of Breen [Bre78, Section 3] (appropriately sheafified)'); used again in the proof of Proposition VII.4.1, p. 263 ('it follows from Breen's resolution that the Pro-structure on A^∨ dualizes to a filtered colimit')
items.note: External input, not proved in FS. Proposition VII.1.12 rests on it, and so does everything built on VII.1.12: the extension-closure in Theorem VII.1.3, and Propositions VII.1.13–VII.1.14. So does the biduality of Proposition VII.4.1 and, through it, VII.4.2, VII.5.2 and VII.5.3. No atlas stage, packet node or decomposition plans a Breen or Breen–Deligne resolution: searching stage texts, packets and decompositions for 'Breen' finds only the unrelated Berthelot–Breen–Messing and Breen–Bökstedt mentions. Neither Mathlib nor Tau Ceti has it (declarations index). Breen, 'Extensions du groupe additif', Publ. Math. IHÉS 48 (1978), 39–125, is also a candidate for prerequisites. Added in review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21).

items.name: Derived internal solidity (Proposition VII.1.12)
items.statement: Let X be a spatial diamond. For all A ∈ D■(X, Ẑ), the map RHom(j♮Ẑ, A) → Rj_∗A|_U is an isomorphism for all quasi-pro-étale j : U → X.
items.note: VS2 plans "the generators/exactness needed for FS VII.1" and "Construct the missing solidification universal property, derived solid tensor/Hom". Proof uses Breen's resolution [Bre78, §3] and [Sch17a, Proposition 14.9]; key for VII.1.13–VII.1.14. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Derived solidification on a spatial diamond (Proposition VII.1.13)
items.statement: Let X be a spatial diamond. The inclusion D■(X, Ẑ) ⊂ D(X_qproét, Ẑ) admits a left adjoint A ↦ A^■ : D(X_qproét, Ẑ) → D■(X, Ẑ). Moreover, D■(X, Ẑ) identifies with the derived category of solid Ẑ-sheaves on X, and A ↦ A^■ with the left derived functor of F ↦ F^■. The formation of A ↦ A^■, for A ∈ D(X_qproét, Ẑ), commutes with any base change X′ → X of spatial diamonds.
items.note: VS2 plans "the generators/exactness needed for FS VII.1" and "Construct the missing solidification universal property, derived solid tensor/Hom" No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Solid tensor product on a spatial diamond (Proposition VII.1.14)
items.statement: Let X be a spatial diamond. The kernel of A ↦ A^■ is a tensor ideal. In particular, there is a unique symmetric monoidal structure −⊗^{■L}− on D■(X, Ẑ) making A ↦ A^■ symmetric monoidal. It is the left derived functor of the induced symmetric monoidal structure on solid Ẑ-sheaves. This symmetric monoidal structure commutes with all colimits (in each variable) and any pullback.
items.note: VS2 plans "the generators/exactness needed for FS VII.1" and "Construct the missing solidification universal property, derived solid tensor/Hom". On generators j♮Ẑ ⊗^{■L} j′♮Ẑ = (j ×_X j′)♮Ẑ. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Solidification from all v-sheaves on a diamond (Proposition VII.1.15)
items.statement: For any diamond X, the fully faithful embedding D■(X, Ẑ) ⊂ D(X_v, Ẑ) admits a left adjoint A ↦ A^■. The formation of A^■ commutes with quasi-pro-étale base change X′ → X.
items.note: VS2 plans "the generators/exactness needed for FS VII.1" and "Construct the missing solidification universal property, derived solid tensor/Hom". Proof via [Sch17a, Lemma 14.5] (Y → Y′ bijective on connected components); improved to arbitrary base change in Proposition VII.2.2. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Solid coefficient rings Λ
items.statement: Coefficients Λ are constant, i.e. come via pullback from the pro-étale site of a point: Λ is a condensed ring that is solid over Ẑ (any solid Ẑ-algebra Λ). Via pullback this gives a v-sheaf of Ẑ-algebras on any small v-stack X, and one considers D(X_v, Λ). From §VII.2 on, Λ is a solid Ẑ^p-algebra.
items.note: VS2 plans "the generators/exactness needed for FS VII.1" and "Construct the missing solidification universal property, derived solid tensor/Hom" ("then extend to general coefficient rings"). No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Z̄_ℓ as a solid condensed ring (Example VII.1.16)
items.statement: One may consider Λ = Z̄_ℓ as the solid condensed ring lim_{→ L|Q_ℓ finite} O_L.

items.name: D■(X, Λ) (Definition VII.1.17)
items.statement: Let D■(X, Λ) ⊂ D(X_v, Λ) be the full subcategory of all A ∈ D(X_v, Λ) such that the image of A in D(X_v, Ẑ) is solid. On the level of ∞-categorical enrichments, D■(X, Λ) is the category of Λ-modules in D■(X, Ẑ), and the inclusion D■(X, Λ) ⊂ D(X_v, Λ) admits a symmetric monoidal left adjoint A ↦ A^■, compatible with forgetting the Λ-structure.

items.name: Comparison with Clausen–Scholze over a point (Remark VII.1.18)
items.statement: Over a geometric point X = Spa C, D■(X, Ẑ) is the derived category of solid Ẑ-modules in the sense of [CS]. For general Λ, D■(X, Λ) consists of Λ-modules in D■(X, Ẑ); this is in general different from the theory of Λ_■-modules and corresponds to the analytic ring structure on Λ induced from Ẑ_■. (For a general analytic ring A, defining a category D(X, A) of A-complete pro-étale sheaves on a spatial diamond does not seem possible formally; already for A = Z_■ there is no abelian category.)

items.name: Pushforward preserves solidity (Proposition VII.2.1)
items.statement: Let Λ be a solid Ẑ^p-algebra and f : Y → X a map of small v-stacks, and let A ∈ D■(Y, Λ) ⊂ D(Y_v, Λ). Then Rf_{v∗}A ∈ D(X_v, Λ) lies in D■(X, Λ). In particular, Rf_{v∗} : D(Y_v, Λ) → D(X_v, Λ) restricts to a functor Rf_∗ : D■(Y, Λ) → D■(X, Λ) that is right adjoint to f^∗.

Prove the solid projection/base-change identities". Proof reduces to constructible étale sheaves and [Sch17a, Proposition 17.6]. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Solidification on small v-stacks commutes with base change (Proposition VII.2.2, first part)
items.statement: Let Λ be a solid Ẑ^p-algebra. For any small v-stack X, the inclusion D■(X, Λ) ⊂ D(X_v, Λ) admits a left adjoint A ↦ A^■ : D(X_v, Λ) → D■(X, Λ). The functor A ↦ A^■ commutes with any base change.
items.note: VS2 plans "Construct D_solid(X,Lambda) over the appropriate cutoffs on a small v-stack, four operations and relative homology f-sharp in the FS VII.2–VII.3 range. Prove the solid projection/base-change identities". Uses that Y ↦ D■(Y, Ẑ^p) is a v-sheaf of ∞-categories and [Lur16, Prop. 4.7.4.19]; commuting with base change is adjoint to VII.2.1. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Solid tensor product on small v-stacks (Proposition VII.2.2, second part)
items.statement: The kernel of A ↦ A^■ is a tensor ideal. In particular, there is a unique symmetric monoidal structure −⊗^{■L}_Λ− on D■(X, Λ) making A ↦ A^■ a symmetric monoidal functor. The functor −⊗^{■L}_Λ− commutes with all colimits (in each variable) and with all pullbacks f : Y → X. These agree with the earlier definitions where they overlap.

items.name: Solid tensor is almost exact (Proposition VII.2.3, first part)
items.statement: Let X be a small v-stack and A, B ∈ D■(X, Ẑ^p) be concentrated in degree 0. Then A ⊗^{■L} B sits in cohomological degrees −1 and 0.

items.name: Solid tensor of finitely presented solid sheaves (Proposition VII.2.3, second part)
items.statement: If X is a spatial diamond and F = lim_{←i} F_i and G = lim_{←j} G_j are finitely presented solid Ẑ^p-sheaves written as cofiltered limits of constructible étale sheaves killed by some integer prime to p, then the natural map F ⊗^{■L} G → R lim_{←i,j} F_i ⊗^L G_j is an isomorphism.

items.name: Solid internal Hom
items.statement: There is a functor RHom_Λ(−,−) : D■(X, Λ)^op × D■(X, Λ) → D■(X, Λ), a partial right adjoint to −⊗^{■L}_Λ−, obtained by restricting the corresponding functor on D(X_v, Λ): for all A ∈ D(X_v, Λ) and B ∈ D■(X, Λ), one has RHom_Λ(A, B) ∈ D■(X, Λ).

items.name: RHom commutes with pullback (Proposition VII.2.4, second part)
items.statement: For any map f : Y → X of small v-stacks and all A, B ∈ D■(X, Λ), the map f^∗RHom(A, B) → RHom(f^∗A, f^∗B) in D■(Y, Λ) is an isomorphism.

items.name: Failure of the projection formula for proper Rf_∗ (Warning VII.2.5)
items.statement: If f : Y → X is a proper map of small v-stacks that is representable in spatial diamonds with dim.trg f < ∞, the map A ⊗^{■L} Rf_∗B → Rf_∗(f^∗A ⊗^{■L} B) may fail to be an isomorphism for A ∈ D■(X, Ẑ^p) and B ∈ D■(Y, Ẑ^p). Already if X = B_C is a perfectoid ball and f = j : Y = Spa C → X is the inclusion of a point (which is quasi-pro-étale), this fails for A = j♮Ẑ^p and B = Ẑ^p: the map becomes j♮Ẑ^p → Rj_∗Ẑ^p, and on global sections the left side is Ẑ^p[−2] while the right side is Ẑ^p.

items.name: Solid Drinfeld lemma, one leg (Corollary VII.2.7)
items.statement: Fix an algebraically closed field k|F_q and work on Perf_k. For any small v-stack X, the functor ψ_X^∗ : D■(X × [∗/W_E], Λ) → D■(X × Div^1, Λ) is fully faithful. If the natural pullback functor D■(X, Λ) → D■(X × Spd C, Λ) is an equivalence, where C = \hat{\bar E} is a completed algebraic closure of E (printed 'Spd \widehat{\overline{E}}'), then ψ_X^∗ is also an equivalence.
items.note: VS2 plans "Construct D_solid(X,Lambda) over the appropriate cutoffs on a small v-stack, four operations and relative homology f-sharp in the FS VII.2–VII.3 range. Prove the solid projection/base-change identities". Solid version of Proposition IV.7.1; proof by descent along X → X × [∗/W_E] and Proposition VII.2.6. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Solid Drinfeld lemma, I legs (Corollary VII.2.8)
items.statement: For any small v-stack X and finite set I, pullback along X × (Div^1)^I → X × [∗/W_E^I] induces a fully faithful functor D■(X × [∗/W_E^I], Λ) → D■(X × (Div^1)^I, Λ).
items.note: VS2 plans "Construct D_solid(X,Lambda) over the appropriate cutoffs on a small v-stack, four operations and relative homology f-sharp in the FS VII.2–VII.3 range. Prove the solid projection/base-change identities". Solid version of Corollary IV.7.2; inductively from VII.2.7. Needed for W_E^I-actions on solid Hecke operators. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Solid partial compact support functors Rβ_{!+}, Rβ_{!−} (Definition VII.2.9)
items.statement: Work over Perf_k; let X be a spatial diamond such that X → ∗ is proper, of finite dim.trg, and S any spatial diamond, with the doubly-indexed ind-system {U_{a,b}}_{(a,b)} ⊂ X × S of §IV.5, U_a = ⋃_{b<∞} U_{a,b}, U_b = ⋃_{a>0} U_{a,b}. The functors Rβ_{!+}, Rβ_{!−} : D■(X × S, Λ) → D■(S, Λ) are defined by Rβ_{!+}C := lim_{→a} Rβ_∗(j_{a!}C|_{U_a}), Rβ_{!−}C := lim_{→b} Rβ_∗(j_{b!}C|_{U_b}) for C ∈ D■(X × S, Λ), where j_{a!}, j_{b!} denote the left adjoints to j_a^∗, j_b^∗.
items.note: VS2 plans "Construct D_solid(X,Lambda) over the appropriate cutoffs on a small v-stack, four operations and relative homology f-sharp in the FS VII.2–VII.3 range. Prove the solid projection/base-change identities"; the étale version is VS0 ("Construct partial compact-support functors of FS IV.5"). No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Solid partial-support vanishing (Theorem VII.2.10)
items.statement: In the setting of Definition VII.2.9, let α : X × S → X be the projection. Assume that C = α^∗A for A ∈ D■(X, Λ), and assume that either A ∈ D■^+(X, Λ), or that X → ∗ is cohomologically smooth. Then Rβ_{!+}C = 0 = Rβ_{!−}C.
items.note: VS2 plans "Construct D_solid(X,Lambda) over the appropriate cutoffs on a small v-stack, four operations and relative homology f-sharp in the FS VII.2–VII.3 range. Prove the solid projection/base-change identities". Restricted solid analogue of Theorem IV.5.3; used in VII.7.2 and VII.7.6. Proof uses [Sch17a, Theorem 25.1] finiteness. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Relative homology f♮ with projection formula (Proposition VII.3.1(i))
items.statement: Let Λ be a solid Ẑ^p-algebra and f : Y → X any map of small v-stacks. The functor f^∗ : D■(X, Λ) → D■(Y, Λ) admits a left adjoint f♮ : D■(Y, Λ) → D■(X, Λ). The natural map f♮(A ⊗^{■L}_Λ f^∗B) → f♮A ⊗^{■L}_Λ B is an isomorphism for all A ∈ D■(Y, Λ) and B ∈ D■(X, Λ). Similarly, the map RHom(f♮A, B) → Rf_∗RHom(A, f^∗B) is an isomorphism.
items.note: VS2 plans "Construct D_solid(X,Lambda) over the appropriate cutoffs on a small v-stack, four operations and relative homology f-sharp in the FS VII.2–VII.3 range. Prove the solid projection/base-change identities". f♮ is the solidification of the slice left adjoint f_{v♮}. The distinctive feature of the solid 5-functor formalism; used throughout (D_lis is generated by f♮Λ). No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: f♮ commutes with restriction of coefficients (Proposition VII.3.1(ii))
items.statement: For any map f : Y → X of small v-stacks, the formation of f♮ commutes with restriction of coefficients along a map Λ′ → Λ of solid Ẑ^p-algebras.
items.note: VS2 plans "Construct D_solid(X,Lambda) over the appropriate cutoffs on a small v-stack, four operations and relative homology f-sharp in the FS VII.2–VII.3 range. Prove the solid projection/base-change identities" No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: f♮ commutes with any base change (Proposition VII.3.1(iii))
items.statement: For any cartesian diagram of small v-stacks with f : Y → X, g : X′ → X, f′ : Y′ → X′, g′ : Y′ → Y, the natural map f′♮g′^∗A → g^∗f♮A is an isomorphism for all A ∈ D■(Y, Λ).
items.note: VS2 plans "Construct D_solid(X,Lambda) over the appropriate cutoffs on a small v-stack, four operations and relative homology f-sharp in the FS VII.2–VII.3 range. Prove the solid projection/base-change identities". Left adjoint of VII.2.4. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Proper smooth pushforward has bounded cohomological dimension (Proposition VII.3.2)
items.statement: Let f : Y → X be a proper map of small v-stacks that is representable in spatial diamonds with dim.trg f < ∞, and cohomologically smooth (ℓ-cohomologically smooth for all ℓ ≠ p, or all ℓ relevant for Λ). Then Rf_∗ : D■(Y, Λ) → D■(X, Λ) has bounded cohomological dimension and commutes with arbitrary direct sums. If X is a spatial diamond (thus Y is) and F is a finitely presented solid Ẑ^p-sheaf on Y, then Rf_∗F is a bounded complex all of whose cohomology sheaves are finitely presented solid Ẑ^p-sheaves on X.
items.note: VS2 plans "Construct D_solid(X,Lambda) over the appropriate cutoffs on a small v-stack, four operations and relative homology f-sharp in the FS VII.2–VII.3 range. Prove the solid projection/base-change identities". Proof via [Sch17a, Proposition 23.12(ii)]. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Projection formula for proper smooth Rf_∗ (Proposition VII.3.3)
items.statement: Let f : Y → X be a proper map of small v-stacks that is representable in spatial diamonds with dim.trg f < ∞, and cohomologically smooth. Then for all A ∈ D■(Y, Λ) and B ∈ D■(X, Λ), the projection map Rf_∗A ⊗^{■L} B → Rf_∗(A ⊗^{■L} f^∗B) is an isomorphism.
items.note: VS2 plans "Construct D_solid(X,Lambda) over the appropriate cutoffs on a small v-stack, four operations and relative homology f-sharp in the FS VII.2–VII.3 range. Prove the solid projection/base-change identities". Contrast with Warning VII.2.5 (fails without smoothness). Proof reduces to [Sch17a, Proposition 22.11]. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: g♮ commutes with proper smooth Rf_∗ (Proposition VII.3.4)
items.statement: Let Y′ → Y (g′), f′ : Y′ → X′, f : Y → X, g : X′ → X be a cartesian diagram of small v-stacks, where f : Y → X is proper, representable in spatial diamonds, with dim.trg f < ∞ and cohomologically smooth. Then the natural transformation g♮Rf′_∗A → Rf_∗g′♮A is an isomorphism for all A ∈ D■(Y′, Λ).
items.note: VS2 plans "Construct D_solid(X,Lambda) over the appropriate cutoffs on a small v-stack, four operations and relative homology f-sharp in the FS VII.2–VII.3 range. Prove the solid projection/base-change identities". Proof tests against constructible étale B via Rf^! and [Sch17a, Proposition 23.12(iii)]. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Rf_∗ expressed through f♮
items.statement: Let f : Y → X be a proper map of small v-stacks that is representable in spatial diamonds with dim.trg f < ∞ and cohomologically smooth; let Δ_f : Y → Y ×_X Y be the diagonal and π_1, π_2 : Y ×_X Y → Y the projections. Then Rf_∗A ≅ Rf_∗π_{2♮}Δ_{f♮}A ≅ f♮Rπ_{1∗}Δ_{f♮}A ≅ f♮Rπ_{1∗}Δ_{f♮}Δ_f^∗π_1^∗A ≅ f♮Rπ_{1∗}(Δ_{f♮}Λ ⊗^{■L}_Λ π_1^∗A) ≅ f♮(Rπ_{1∗}Δ_{f♮}Λ ⊗^{■L}_Λ A).
items.locator: Chapter VII, §VII.3, display before Proposition VII.3.5, p. 260
items.note: VS2 plans "Construct D_solid(X,Lambda) over the appropriate cutoffs on a small v-stack, four operations and relative homology f-sharp in the FS VII.2–VII.3 range. Prove the solid projection/base-change identities". Unnumbered; uses VII.3.4 and the projection formulas. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Rπ_{1∗}Δ_{f♮}Λ is invertible with inverse Rf^!Λ (Proposition VII.3.5, first part)
items.statement: Let f : Y → X be a proper map of small v-stacks that is representable in spatial diamonds with dim.trg f < ∞ and cohomologically smooth. Then Rπ_{1∗}Δ_{f♮}Λ ∈ D■(Y, Λ) is invertible, and its inverse is canonically isomorphic to Rf^!Λ := lim_{←n} Rf^!Z/nZ ⊗^L_{Ẑ^p} Λ.
items.note: VS2 plans "Construct D_solid(X,Lambda) over the appropriate cutoffs on a small v-stack, four operations and relative homology f-sharp in the FS VII.2–VII.3 range. Prove the solid projection/base-change identities". The proof also shows Rf^!A ≅ RHom(Rπ_{1∗}Δ_{f♮}Ẑ^p, f^∗A) for A ∈ D_ét(X, Z/nZ), n prime to p, i.e. the right adjoint of solid Rf_∗ extends étale Rf^!. FS remark the fibres of Rπ_{1∗}Δ_{f♮}Ẑ^p are the limit of RΓ_c(U, Ẑ^p) over étale neighbourhoods U of the geometric point. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Solid Poincaré duality f♮ ≅ Rf_∗(− ⊗ Rf^!Λ) (Proposition VII.3.5, second part)
items.statement: Let f : Y → X be a proper map of small v-stacks that is representable in spatial diamonds with dim.trg f < ∞ and cohomologically smooth. There is a canonical isomorphism f♮A ≅ Rf_∗(A ⊗^{■L}_Λ Rf^!Λ) of functors D■(Y, Λ) → D■(X, Λ).
items.note: VS2 plans "Construct D_solid(X,Lambda) over the appropriate cutoffs on a small v-stack, four operations and relative homology f-sharp in the FS VII.2–VII.3 range. Prove the solid projection/base-change identities". "Somewhat unusual formula for the dualizing complex"; Remark VII.3.6 notes important instances of Rf^! can be described via g♮ functors. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Naive embedding D_ét ↪ D■ and its right adjoint (§VII.4.1)
items.statement: Let Λ be discrete (so nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p). For any small v-stack X, there is a fully faithful embedding D_ét(X, Λ) ↪ D■(X, Λ) as full subcategories of D(X_v, Λ); it admits a right adjoint R_{Xét} : D■(X, Λ) → D_ét(X, Λ). The inclusion is symmetric monoidal and compatible with pullback, and by [Sch17a, Proposition 17.6] commutes with Rf_∗ if f : Y → X is qcqs and one restricts to D^+, or in general if f is qcqs of finite cohomological dimension. Moreover one always has R_{Xét}Rf_∗ ≅ Rf_∗R_{Yét}.
items.note: VS2 plans "comparison with torsion D_et, and dualizability theorem of VII.4–VII.5" No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Internal Hom and the naive embedding (§VII.4.1)
items.statement: With Λ discrete as in §VII.4: R_{Xét}RHom_{D■(X,Λ)}(A, B) ≅ RHom_{D_ét(X,Λ)}(A, R_{Xét}B) if A ∈ D_ét(X, Λ) and B ∈ D■(X, Λ). If A is perfect-constructible, then for all B ∈ D_ét(X, Λ), RHom_{D_ét(X,Λ)}(A, B) ≅ RHom_{D■(X,Λ)}(A, B).
items.note: VS2 plans "comparison with torsion D_et, and dualizability theorem of VII.4–VII.5". Second claim reduces to A = j_!Λ, j qc separated étale. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Overconvergent étale complexes D_ét^†(X, Λ) (§VII.4.2)
items.statement: For a small v-stack X, let D_ét^†(X, Λ) ⊂ D_ét(X, Λ) be the full subcategory of overconvergent objects: A ∈ D_ét(X, Λ) is overconvergent if for any strictly local Spa(C, C^+) → X, the map RΓ(Spa(C, C^+), A) → RΓ(Spa(C, O_C), A) is an isomorphism.
items.note: VS2 plans "comparison with torsion D_et, and dualizability theorem of VII.4–VII.5". Recalled definition ("Recall that"); the overconvergence condition also appears in the ULA theory of VS1. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Dual embedding of overconvergent sheaves (Proposition VII.4.1, first part)
items.statement: Assume that Λ = Z/nZ with n prime to p. For any overconvergent A ∈ D_ét^†(X, Λ), let A^∨ = RHom_{D■(X,Λ)}(A, Λ) ∈ D■(X, Λ). Then the functor D_ét^†(X, Λ)^op → D■(X, Λ) : A ↦ A^∨ is fully faithful, t-exact (for the standard t-structure), and compatible with pullback.
items.note: VS2 plans "comparison with torsion D_et, and dualizability theorem of VII.4–VII.5". Proof: v-descent to strictly totally disconnected X, where D_ét^† ≅ D(π_0X, Λ) and dualization exchanges Ind- and Pro-constructible complexes (Λ self-injective). No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Biduality for overconvergent sheaves (Proposition VII.4.1, second part)
items.statement: Assume that Λ = Z/nZ with n prime to p. For any A ∈ D_ét^†(X, Λ), the map A → RHom_{D■(X,Λ)}(A^∨, Λ) is an isomorphism.
items.note: VS2 plans "comparison with torsion D_et, and dualizability theorem of VII.4–VII.5". Proof via Breen's resolution. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Lax symmetric monoidality of A ↦ A^∨
items.statement: The functor A ↦ A^∨ is lax symmetric monoidal: there is a natural functorial map A^∨ ⊗^{■L}_Λ B^∨ → (A ⊗^L_Λ B)^∨.
items.note: VS2 plans "comparison with torsion D_et, and dualizability theorem of VII.4–VII.5" No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Dual embedding is monoidal on finite Tor-amplitude objects (Proposition VII.4.2)
items.statement: Let Λ = Z/nZ, n prime to p. Assume that A ∈ D_ét^†(X, Λ) has finite Tor-amplitude over Λ, i.e. for all quotients Λ → F_ℓ, the complex A ⊗^L_Λ F_ℓ ∈ D_ét^†(X, F_ℓ) is bounded. Then for all B ∈ D_ét^†(X, Λ), the maps A^∨ ⊗^{■L}_Λ B^∨ → (A ⊗^L_Λ B)^∨ and A ⊗^L_Λ B → RHom_{D■(X,Λ)}(A^∨, B) are isomorphisms.
items.note: VS2 plans "comparison with torsion D_et, and dualizability theorem of VII.4–VII.5". Used for the kernel 2-category comparison and VII.5.3. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Duality exchanges proper pushforward and f♮ (Proposition VII.4.3)
items.statement: Let Λ = Z/nZ, n prime to p. Let f : Y → X be a proper map of small v-stacks that is representable in spatial diamonds with dim.trg f < ∞. Let A ∈ D_ét^†(Y, Λ) with dual A^∨ ∈ D■(Y, Λ). Then Rf_∗A is again overconvergent (by proper base change) and there is a natural isomorphism (Rf_∗A)^∨ ≅ f♮A^∨.
items.note: VS2 plans "comparison with torsion D_et, and dualizability theorem of VII.4–VII.5". No smoothness hypothesis. Proof reduces to canonical compactifications of w-contractible spaces and Ind/Pro duality on profinite sets. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Universally locally acyclic complexes with Ẑ^p-type coefficients D^ULA(X/S, Λ)
items.statement: Assume Λ is a quotient of Ẑ^p of the form lim_{←n} Z/nZ where n runs over some integers prime to p. For f : X → S a compactifiable map of small v-stacks, representable in locally spatial diamonds with locally dim.trg f < ∞, D^ULA(X/S, Λ) is the limit (on ∞-categorical enhancements) of the full subcategories D^ULA(X/S, Z/nZ) ⊂ D_ét(X, Z/nZ) of f-universally locally acyclic objects; equivalently, the category of all A ∈ D■(X, Λ) such that A_n = A ⊗^L_Λ Z/nZ lies in D_ét(X, Z/nZ) for all such n, is f-universally locally acyclic, and A is the derived limit of the A_n.
items.note: VS2 plans "comparison with torsion D_et, and dualizability theorem of VII.4–VII.5" No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Fully faithful embeddings of ULA complexes into D■
items.statement: For A ∈ D^ULA(X/S, Λ), all A_n are overconvergent, and A ↦ A^∨ = RHom_{D■(X,Λ)}(A, Λ) = R lim_{←n} A_n^∨ ∈ D■(X, Λ) defines a fully faithful contravariant embedding D^ULA(X/S, Λ)^op ↪ D■(X, Λ). Precomposing with Verdier duality D_{X/S} gives a covariant fully faithful embedding D^ULA(X/S, Λ) ↪ D■(X, Λ) : A ↦ D_{X/S}(A)^∨.
items.note: VS2 plans "comparison with torsion D_et, and dualizability theorem of VII.4–VII.5". Unnumbered; follows from VII.4.1. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Algebraic constructible sheaves embed into D■ (Example VII.5.1, first part)
items.statement: Assume that S = Spa C is a geometric point, and X is the analytification of an algebraic variety X^alg/Spec C. Then any constructible complex on X^alg is universally locally acyclic over S, yielding a fully faithful embedding D_c^b(X^alg, Z_ℓ) ↪ D^ULA(X/S, Z_ℓ) ↪ D■(X, Z_ℓ). The image lands in bounded complexes with finitely presented solid cohomology sheaves, in fact in compact objects, so this extends to a fully faithful embedding Ind D_c^b(X^alg, Z_ℓ) ↪ D■(X, Z_ℓ), taking i_∗Z_ℓ for a point i : Spec C → X^alg to i♮Z_ℓ.
items.note: VS2 plans "comparison with torsion D_et, and dualizability theorem of VII.4–VII.5" — covered only by the section-range phrase; no stage names the algebraic comparison (which additionally needs analytification of varieties to diamonds and algebraic ULA). No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Ind-constructible sheaves on algebraic stacks embed into D■ (Example VII.5.1, second part)
items.statement: If Y is a stack on the category of schemes over Spec C, let D(Y, Z_ℓ) := lim_{← X^alg → Y} Ind D_c^b(X^alg, Z_ℓ), X^alg of finite type over Spec C, with transition functors Rf^!. This embeds naturally into D■(Y^♢, Z_ℓ) via the previous embedding, which intertwines Rf^! with the usual pullback f^∗ on solid sheaves: D_{X′/S}(Rf^!A)^∨ ≅ (f^∗D_{X/S}(A))^∨ ≅ f^∗D_{X/S}(A)^∨ for a map f : X′^alg → X^alg of algebraic varieties over Spec C.
items.note: Not planned: no stage mentions the comparison with the geometric-Langlands category lim Ind D_c^b along Rf^!. Stated without detailed proof (limit-compatibility of the embedding is asserted). No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: The A-twisted homology functor f♮(D_{X/S}(A)^∨ ⊗ −)
items.statement: For A ∈ D^ULA(X/S, Λ), the functor f♮(D_{X/S}(A)^∨ ⊗^{■L}_Λ −) : D■(X, Λ) → D■(S, Λ) commutes with all colimits, its formation commutes with any base change, it satisfies the projection formula, and it extends the functor Rf_!(A ⊗^L_Λ −).
items.note: VS2 plans "comparison with torsion D_et, and dualizability theorem of VII.4–VII.5". Unnumbered; the extension claim is Proposition VII.5.2. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Twisted homology recovers Rf_! (Proposition VII.5.2)
items.statement: Let Λ be as in §VII.5 and f : X → S compactifiable, representable in locally spatial diamonds with locally dim.trg f < ∞. Assume that A ∈ D^ULA(X/S, Λ) has bounded Tor-amplitude. Let Z/nZ be a discrete quotient of Λ. For B ∈ D_ét(X, Z/nZ), there is a natural equivalence f♮(D_{X/S}(A)^∨ ⊗^{■L}_Λ B) ≅ Rf_!(A_n ⊗^L_{Z/nZ} B) ∈ D_ét(S, Z/nZ).
items.note: VS2 plans "comparison with torsion D_et, and dualizability theorem of VII.4–VII.5". Uses VII.4.1 and IV.2.19. Key consequence used in VII.6.5–VII.6.6: for f separated ℓ-cohomologically smooth, f♮Z/ℓ^mZ ≅ Rf_!Rf^!Z/ℓ^mZ (take A = Rf^!Λ, so that D_{X/S}(A) = Λ and D_{X/S}(A)^∨ = Λ, and B = Λ); decomposition gap note in data/decompositions/VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories.json flags that VII.6 depends on it.
