items.name: A-twisted Poincaré duality (Proposition VII.5.3)
items.statement: Assume that f : X → S is a proper map of small v-stacks that is representable in spatial diamonds with dim.trg f < ∞. Let A ∈ D^ULA(X/S, Λ) with bounded Tor-amplitude. Then there is a natural equivalence f♮(D_{X/S}(A)^∨ ⊗^{■L}_Λ −) ≅ Rf_∗RHom_{D■(X,Λ)}(A^∨, −) of functors D■(X, Λ) → D■(S, Λ).
items.note: VS2 plans "comparison with torsion D_et, and dualizability theorem of VII.4–VII.5". Generalizes VII.3.5 from smooth f to ULA A. Proof constructs the map via Δ♮Λ ≅ (Δ_∗Λ)^∨ (VII.4.3), VII.4.2, and the ULA identity π_2^∗D_{X/S}(A) ⊗ π_1^∗A ≅ RHom(π_2^∗A, Rπ_1^!A). No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: The 2-category C_{S,■} of solid kernels
items.statement: For a small v-stack S, C_{S,■} is the 2-category whose objects are relatively 0-truncated small v-stacks X over S, with Fun_{C_{S,■}}(X, Y) = D■(X ×_S Y, Λ). To A ∈ D■(X ×_S Y, Λ) is associated the functor p_{2♮}(A ⊗^{■L}_Λ p_1^∗) : D■(X, Λ) → D■(Y, Λ), and composition is the convolution D■(X ×_S Y, Λ) × D■(Y ×_S Z, Λ) → D■(X ×_S Z, Λ) : (A, B) ↦ A ⋆ B = p_{13♮}(p_{12}^∗A ⊗^{■L}_Λ p_{23}^∗B).
items.note: VS2 plans "comparison with torsion D_et, and dualizability theorem of VII.4–VII.5"; the dualizability theorem (Corollary VII.5.4) is formulated in this 2-category, so VS2 owns it. HeckeStacksAndLocalShtukas:HS1 only consumes it: the stage takes "VS2–VS3's dualizable solid/lisse kernels" as inputs, and its node HeckeStacksAndLocalShtukas:HS1/satake-kernel-and-solid-monoidal-functor uses "the convolution of FS VII.5" with VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories:VS2 as a prerequisite. Solid variant of the 2-category C_S of §IV.2.3.3. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Fully faithful embedding C_S^† ↪ C_{S,■}^co
items.statement: Let C_S^† ⊂ C_S be the sub-2-category whose objects are the proper X/S representable in spatial diamonds of finite dim.trg, with Fun_{C_S^†}(X, Y) = D_{ét,ftor}^†(X ×_S Y, Λ) (finite Tor-dimension over Λ). Then A ↦ A^∨ defines fully faithful embeddings Fun_{C_S^†}(X, Y) ↪ D■(X ×_S Y, Λ)^op = Fun_{C_{S,■}^co}(X, Y) compatible with composition, giving a fully faithful embedding C_S^† ↪ C_{S,■}^co (co = reversing 2-morphisms). The naive embedding D_ét ↪ D■ is not compatible with convolution (Rπ_{13!} vs π_{13♮}).
items.note: VS2 plans "comparison with torsion D_et, and dualizability theorem of VII.4–VII.5". Compatibility with composition by VII.4.2 and VII.4.3. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Adjunction of ULA kernels in C_{S,■} (Corollary VII.5.4)
items.statement: Let f : X → S be a proper map of small v-stacks that is representable in spatial diamonds with dim.trg f < ∞. Let A ∈ D_ét(X, Λ) be f-universally locally acyclic and of finite Tor-dimension over Λ. Then A^∨ ∈ D■(X, Λ) = Fun_{C_{S,■}}(X, S) is right adjoint to D_{X/S}(A)^∨ ∈ D■(X, Λ) = Fun_{C_{S,■}}(S, X). In particular, the functor f♮(A^∨ ⊗^{■L}_Λ −) : D■(X, Λ) → D■(S, Λ) is right adjoint to D_{X/S}(A)^∨ ⊗^{■L}_Λ f^∗− : D■(S, Λ) → D■(X, Λ), so f♮(A^∨ ⊗^{■L}_Λ −) ≅ Rf_∗RHom_Λ(D_{X/S}(A)^∨, −) : D■(X, Λ) → D■(S, Λ).
items.note: VS2 plans "comparison with torsion D_et, and dualizability theorem of VII.4–VII.5". Another proof of VII.5.3 (with A replaced by D_{X/S}(A)). No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Satake category embeds into solid sheaves on the Hecke stack
items.statement: Applied to the Satake category, A ↦ A^∨ gives a fully faithful embedding (Sat_G^I)^op ↪ D■(Hck_G^I, Ẑ^p), compatible with the monoidal structure and functorial in I, where the right side is Fun_{C_{S,■}}([(Div^1)_X^I/L^+_{(Div^1_X)^I}G], [(Div^1)_X^I/L^+_{(Div^1_X)^I}G]) for S = [(Div^1_X)^I/L_{(Div^1_X)^I}G]. Precomposing with Verdier duality gives a covariant fully faithful embedding Sat_G^I ↪ D■(Hck_G^I, Ẑ^p) : A ↦ D_{X/S}(A)^∨. By Proposition VII.5.2, using Satake objects as kernels, this extends Hecke operators from D_ét to D■.
items.note: VS2 plans "comparison with torsion D_et, and dualizability theorem of VII.4–VII.5"; HS1 plans "Show that the kernel lies in the required dualizable/ULA category" and "Prove preservation of D_lis". Unnumbered, stated without separate proof; depends on Chapter VI (Sat_G^I, Hck_G^I). items.statement: From §VII.6 on, fix ℓ ≠ p and a discrete Z_ℓ-algebra Λ, or rather the corresponding condensed ring Λ := Z_ℓ ⊗_{Z_ℓ,disc} Λ_disc.

items.name: Lisse-étale category D_lis(X, Λ) (Definition VII.6.1)
items.statement: Let X be an Artin v-stack. The full subcategory D_lis(X, Λ) ⊂ D■(X, Λ) is the smallest triangulated subcategory stable under all direct sums that contains f♮Λ for all maps f : Y → X that are separated, representable in locally spatial diamonds, and ℓ-cohomologically smooth.
items.note: VS3 plans "Define D_lis of an Artin v-stack as the stable subcategory closed under sums generated by f-sharp Lambda for separated maps f representable in locally spatial diamonds and ell-cohomologically smooth" and "Prove the inclusion's right adjoint, tensor closure, pullback and lisse internal Hom/pushforward constructions. Compare ordinary, adic, solid and lisse coefficients through the actual fully faithful functors of VII.6". "lis" refers to lisse-étale sheaves on Artin stacks [LMB00], not local systems. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: D_lis is stable under tensor and pullback (Proposition VII.6.2)
items.statement: Let X be an Artin v-stack. The full subcategory D_lis(X, Λ) ⊂ D■(X, Λ) is stable under −⊗^{■L}_Λ−. Moreover, if f : Y → X is a map of Artin v-stacks, then f^∗ maps D_lis(X, Λ) ⊂ D■(X, Λ) into D_lis(Y, Λ) ⊂ D■(Y, Λ).
items.note: VS3 plans "Define D_lis of an Artin v-stack as the stable subcategory closed under sums generated by f-sharp Lambda for separated maps f representable in locally spatial diamonds and ell-cohomologically smooth" and "Prove the inclusion's right adjoint, tensor closure, pullback and lisse internal Hom/pushforward constructions. Compare ordinary, adic, solid and lisse coefficients through the actual fully faithful functors of VII.6" No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Right adjoint A ↦ A^lis (Proposition VII.6.3)
items.statement: Let X be an Artin v-stack. The inclusion D_lis(X, Λ) ⊂ D■(X, Λ) admits a right adjoint A ↦ A^lis : D■(X, Λ) → D_lis(X, Λ). The kernel of A ↦ A^lis is the class of all A ∈ D■(X, Λ) such that A(Y) = 0 for all f : Y → X that are separated, representable in locally spatial diamonds, and ℓ-cohomologically smooth.
items.note: VS3 plans "Define D_lis of an Artin v-stack as the stable subcategory closed under sums generated by f-sharp Lambda for separated maps f representable in locally spatial diamonds and ell-cohomologically smooth" and "Prove the inclusion's right adjoint, tensor closure, pullback and lisse internal Hom/pushforward constructions. Compare ordinary, adic, solid and lisse coefficients through the actual fully faithful functors of VII.6". Proof notes D■(X, Λ) is not presentable but a large filtered colimit of presentable D■(X_κ, Λ) over uncountable strong limit cardinals κ, and D_lis ⊂ D■(X_κ, Λ) for some κ ([Sch17a, Remark 17.4]); VS2 correspondingly plans "construct compatible adjoints at adequate cutoffs". No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: RHom_lis and Rf_{lis∗}
items.statement: Using Proposition VII.6.3, define RHom_lis(A, B) := RHom(A, B)^lis ∈ D_lis(X, Λ) for A, B ∈ D_lis(X, Λ), and Rf_{lis∗} : D_lis(Y, Λ) → D_lis(X, Λ) for a map f : Y → X of Artin v-stacks, satisfying the usual adjunctions to the tensor product and pullback.

items.name: Discrete modules embed into condensed modules (Proposition VII.6.4)
items.statement: For any condensed ring A with underlying ring A(∗), the functor M ↦ M ⊗_{A(∗)} A induces a fully faithful functor D(A(∗)) ↪ D(A) from the derived category of usual A(∗)-modules to the derived category of condensed modules over the condensed ring A.
items.note: VS3 plans "Define D_lis of an Artin v-stack as the stable subcategory closed under sums generated by f-sharp Lambda for separated maps f representable in locally spatial diamonds and ell-cohomologically smooth" and "Prove the inclusion's right adjoint, tensor closure, pullback and lisse internal Hom/pushforward constructions. Compare ordinary, adic, solid and lisse coefficients through the actual fully faithful functors of VII.6". Pure condensed-mathematics statement. Mathlib has the underived special case for a discrete ring: the discrete ⊣ underlying adjunction (Condensed.discreteUnderlyingAdj, Mathlib/Condensed/Discrete/Basic.lean:58) and the full faithfulness of Mod_R → CondensedMod R, M ↦ locally constant maps to M (CondensedMod.LocallyConstant.fullyFaithfulFunctor, Mathlib/Condensed/Discrete/Module.lean:145). It does not have the derived statement over a condensed ring A, so this is not claimed as library. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: D_lis of a geometric point is D(Λ) (Proposition VII.6.5)
items.statement: Let X = Spa C for some complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean field C. Then D_lis(X, Λ) ≅ D(Λ), the derived category of (relatively) discrete Λ-modules.
items.note: VS3 plans "Define D_lis of an Artin v-stack as the stable subcategory closed under sums generated by f-sharp Lambda for separated maps f representable in locally spatial diamonds and ell-cohomologically smooth" and "Prove the inclusion's right adjoint, tensor closure, pullback and lisse internal Hom/pushforward constructions. Compare ordinary, adic, solid and lisse coefficients through the actual fully faithful functors of VII.6". Proof: for separated ℓ-cohomologically smooth f : Y → X of spatial diamonds, f♮Z_ℓ = lim_m f♮Z/ℓ^mZ with f♮Z/ℓ^mZ ≅ Rf_!Rf^!Z/ℓ^mZ perfect (VII.5.2). No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Torsion D_lis lies in D_ét (Proposition VII.6.6, first part)
items.statement: Let X be an Artin v-stack, and assume that Λ is killed by a power of ℓ. Then D_lis(X, Λ) ⊂ D■(X, Λ) is contained in the image of the naive embedding D_ét(X, Λ) ↪ D■(X, Λ).
items.note: VS3 plans "Define D_lis of an Artin v-stack as the stable subcategory closed under sums generated by f-sharp Lambda for separated maps f representable in locally spatial diamonds and ell-cohomologically smooth" and "Prove the inclusion's right adjoint, tensor closure, pullback and lisse internal Hom/pushforward constructions. Compare ordinary, adic, solid and lisse coefficients through the actual fully faithful functors of VII.6". Uses f♮Λ = Rf_!Rf^!Λ. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Torsion D_lis equals D_ét under bounded cd (Proposition VII.6.6, second part)
items.statement: Let X be an Artin v-stack and Λ killed by a power of ℓ. If there is a separated ℓ-cohomologically smooth surjection U → X from a locally spatial diamond U such that U_ét has a basis with bounded ℓ-cohomological dimension, then the naive embedding induces an equivalence D_lis(X, Λ) ≅ D_ét(X, Λ).

Compare ordinary, adic, solid and lisse coefficients through the actual fully faithful functors of VII.6". Uses [Sch17a, Proposition 20.17] (only a basis of bounded cd needed). items.name: Semi-orthogonal decomposition at a closed point (Proposition VII.6.7)
items.statement: Let X be a locally spatial diamond with a closed point x ∈ X, giving a corresponding closed subdiamond i : Z ⊂ X with complement j : U ⊂ X. Assume that Z = Spa C is representable, with C an algebraically closed nonarchimedean field. Moreover, assume that Z can be written as a cofiltered intersection of qcqs open neighborhoods V ⊂ X such that RΓ(V, F_ℓ) ≅ F_ℓ. Then one has a semi-orthogonal decomposition of D_lis(X, Λ) into D_lis(U, Λ) and D_lis(Z, Λ) ≅ D(Λ).

Characterize compact objects by compact restrictions with finite stratum support, and by the thick closure of compact induction from pro-p open subgroups". items.name: D_lis of a Newton stratum is smooth representations (Proposition VII.7.1)
items.statement: Let E be a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q, G a reductive group over E; work over Perf_k, k = F̄_q, with C/k complete algebraically closed. Let b ∈ B(G). The pullback functors D_lis(Bun_G^b, Λ) → D_lis([∗/G_b(E)], Λ) → D_lis([Spa C/G_b(E)], Λ) and D_lis(Bun_G^b, Λ) → D_lis(Bun_G^b × Spa C, Λ) → D_lis([Spa C/G_b(E)], Λ) are equivalences, and all categories are naturally equivalent (as symmetric monoidal categories) to the derived category D(G_b(E), Λ) of smooth representations of G_b(E) on discrete Λ-modules.

Characterize compact objects by compact restrictions with finite stratum support, and by the thick closure of compact induction from pro-p open subgroups" and "Identify D_et([*/H],Lambda) with the enhanced derived category of smooth H-representations". Proof: s : [∗/G_b(E)] → Bun_G^b cohomologically smooth with positive Banach–Colmez fibres gives s♮Λ ≅ Λ; smoothness of condensed actions via local pro-p-ness. Includes Λ = Q̄_ℓ. items.name: The distinguished point of M̃_{b,C} has acyclic neighbourhoods
items.statement: For b ∈ B(G), with chart π_b : M_b → Bun_G, projection q_b : M_b → [∗/G_b(E)] and G_b(E)-torsor M̃_b → M_b, the base change M̃_{b,C} = M̃_b ×_{Spd k} Spa C is representable by a locally spatial diamond with a distinguished point i : Spa C ↪ M̃_{b,C}, and this closed subset can be written as a cofiltered intersection of quasicompact open subsets V with RΓ(V, F_ℓ) ≅ F_ℓ.

items.name: Left adjoint to restriction to a stratum (Proposition VII.7.2)
items.statement: For any b ∈ B(G) with locally closed immersion i^b : Bun_G^b → Bun_G, the functor i^{b∗} : D_lis(Bun_G, Λ) → D_lis(Bun_G^b, Λ) ≅ D_lis([∗/G_b(E)], Λ) admits a left adjoint, given by π_{b♮}q_b^∗ : D_lis([∗/G_b(E)], Λ) → D_lis(Bun_G, Λ). The unit of the adjunction is given by the equivalence id ≅ i^{b∗}π_{b♮}q_b^∗ arising from base change and the identification of the pullback of i^b along π_b with [∗/G_b(E)] ⊂ M_b.

items.name: Compact generation and compact objects of D_lis(Bun_G) (Proposition VII.7.4, first part)
items.statement: The category D_lis(Bun_G, Λ) is compactly generated. An object A ∈ D_lis(Bun_G, Λ) is compact if and only if it has finite support and i^{b∗}A ∈ D_lis(Bun_G^b, Λ) ≅ D(G_b(E), Λ) is compact for all b ∈ B(G), i.e. lies in the thick triangulated subcategory generated by c-Ind_K^{G_b(E)}Λ for open pro-p subgroups K ⊂ G_b(E).

items.name: Finite cohomological dimension on the punctured chart (Lemma VII.7.5)
items.statement: For K ⊂ G_b(E) an open pro-p subgroup, the functor RΓ(M°_{b,K}, −) : D■(M°_{b,K}, Λ) → D(Λ) has finite cohomological dimension and commutes with all direct sums.
items.note: VS4 plans "Extend to D_lis in the precise coefficient range of VII.7" and "Prove localization triangles and the infinite semiorthogonal decomposition along the HN strata ... Characterize compact objects by compact restrictions with finite stratum support, and by the thick closure of compact induction from pro-p open subgroups" (proof step for the compact-object characterization). M°_{b,K} = M̃°_b/K with M̃°_b a spatial diamond, open in a successive extension of negative Banach–Colmez spaces; proof via Theorem IV.5.3 and finiteness of H^j. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: The pairing (A, B) ↦ π♮(A ⊗ B) on D_lis(Bun_G)
items.statement: Denoting π : Bun_G → ∗ the projection, π^∗ has a left adjoint π♮ : D_lis(Bun_G, Λ) → D_lis(∗, Λ) ≅ D(Λ), inducing a pairing D_lis(Bun_G, Λ) × D_lis(Bun_G, Λ) → D(Λ) : (A, B) ↦ π♮(A ⊗^{■L}_Λ B).
items.note: VS5 plans "Construct Bernstein–Zelevinsky duality on compact Bun_G objects using the partial-support functor; prove biduality and its basic-stratum comparison. Separately construct Verdier duality on ULA objects and prove that ULA is equivalent to perfection of K-invariants on every stratum for every appropriate pro-p open K" No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Bernstein–Zelevinsky duality on D_lis(Bun_G) (Proposition VII.7.6, first part)
items.statement: For any compact object A ∈ D_lis(Bun_G, Λ), there is a unique compact object D_BZ(A) ∈ D_lis(Bun_G, Λ) with a functorial identification RHom(D_BZ(A), B) ≅ π♮(A ⊗^{■L}_Λ B) for B ∈ D_lis(Bun_G, Λ). Moreover, D_BZ is a contravariant autoequivalence of D_lis(Bun_G, Λ)^ω, and D_BZ^2 is naturally isomorphic to the identity.
items.note: VS5 plans "Construct Bernstein–Zelevinsky duality on compact Bun_G objects using the partial-support functor; prove biduality and its basic-stratum comparison. Separately construct Verdier duality on ULA objects and prove that ULA is equivalent to perfection of K-invariants on every stratum for every appropriate pro-p open K". Proof as Theorem V.5.1 using VII.7.2 and Theorem VII.2.10. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: D_BZ preserves open support and is the classical involution on basic strata (Proposition VII.7.6, second part)
items.statement: If U ⊂ Bun_G is an open substack and A is concentrated on U, then so is D_BZ(A). In particular, D_BZ restricts to an autoequivalence of the compact objects in D_lis(Bun_G^b, Λ) ≅ D(G_b(E), Λ) for b ∈ B(G) basic, and in that setting it is the usual Bernstein–Zelevinsky involution.
items.note: VS5 plans "Construct Bernstein–Zelevinsky duality on compact Bun_G objects using the partial-support functor; prove biduality and its basic-stratum comparison. Separately construct Verdier duality on ULA objects and prove that ULA is equivalent to perfection of K-invariants on every stratum for every appropriate pro-p open K". ES6:duality consumes VS5 for IX.5.3. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Verdier duality and open immersions in D_lis (Proposition VII.7.7)
items.statement: Let j : V ↪ U be an open immersion of open substacks of Bun_G. For any A ∈ D_lis(V, Λ), the natural map j♮RHom_lis(A, Λ) → RHom_lis(Rj_{lis∗}A, Λ) is an isomorphism in D_lis(U, Λ).
items.note: VS5 plans "Construct Bernstein–Zelevinsky duality on compact Bun_G objects using the partial-support functor; prove biduality and its basic-stratum comparison. Separately construct Verdier duality on ULA objects and prove that ULA is equivalent to perfection of K-invariants on every stratum for every appropriate pro-p open K" — the stage's Verdier-duality clause; FS: proof identical to Theorem V.6.1. The reflexive-object characterization (analogue of V.6.2) is omitted in the paper. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Universally locally acyclic objects of D_lis(Bun_G) (Definition VII.7.8)
items.statement: A complex A ∈ D_lis(Bun_G, Λ) is universally locally acyclic (with respect to Bun_G → ∗) if the natural map p_1^∗RHom_lis(A, Λ) ⊗^{■L}_Λ p_2^∗A → RHom_lis(p_1^∗A, p_2^∗A) is an isomorphism, where p_1, p_2 : Bun_G × Bun_G → Bun_G are the two projections.
items.note: VS5 plans "Construct Bernstein–Zelevinsky duality on compact Bun_G objects using the partial-support functor; prove biduality and its basic-stratum comparison. Separately construct Verdier duality on ULA objects and prove that ULA is equivalent to perfection of K-invariants on every stratum for every appropriate pro-p open K". Imported from the characterization Proposition IV.2.32 (no general lisse ULA notion is defined). No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: ULA lisse sheaves on Bun_G = stratumwise admissible (Proposition VII.7.9)
items.statement: Let A ∈ D_lis(Bun_G, Λ). Then A is universally locally acyclic if and only if for all b ∈ B(G), the pullback i^{b∗}A to i^b : Bun_G^b ↪ Bun_G corresponds under D_lis(Bun_G^b, Λ) ≅ D(G_b(E), Λ) to a complex M_b of smooth G_b(E)-representations for which M_b^K is a perfect complex of Λ-modules for all open pro-p subgroups K ⊂ G_b(E).
items.note: VS5 plans "Construct Bernstein–Zelevinsky duality on compact Bun_G objects using the partial-support functor; prove biduality and its basic-stratum comparison. Separately construct Verdier duality on ULA objects and prove that ULA is equivalent to perfection of K-invariants on every stratum for every appropriate pro-p open K". Proof identical to Theorem V.7.1, via VII.7.10. The statement uses the corrected M_b^K (printed 'M^K'; see the new source issue on Proposition VII.7.9). No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Exterior products of compact objects on Bun_{G1×G2} (Proposition VII.7.10)
items.statement: Let G_1 and G_2 be two reductive groups over E, and let G = G_1 × G_2. Consider the exterior tensor product − ⊠ − : D_lis(Bun_{G_1}, Λ) × D_lis(Bun_{G_2}, Λ) → D_lis(Bun_G, Λ). For all compact objects A_i ∈ D_lis(Bun_{G_i}, Λ), i = 1, 2, the exterior tensor product A_1 ⊠ A_2 ∈ D_lis(Bun_G, Λ) [printed: D_ét(Bun_G, Λ)] is compact, these objects form a class of compact generators, and for all further objects B_i ∈ D_lis(Bun_{G_i}, Λ), i = 1, 2, the natural map RHom(A_1, B_1) ⊗^L_Λ RHom(A_2, B_2) → RHom(A_1 ⊠ A_2, B_1 ⊠ B_2) is an isomorphism.
items.note: No stage names this Künneth statement for D_lis(Bun_{G1×G2}); VS5 plans only its consequence ("prove that ULA is equivalent to perfection of K-invariants"), for which this is the proof input. Proof identical to Proposition V.7.2. (PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E56). No Mathlib/Tau Ceti counterpart: neither library has diamonds, pro-étale/v-sites of diamonds or solid sheaves on them (Mathlib/Condensed/Solid.lean has only the provisional CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules over a point).

items.name: Theorem VIII.0.1 (= Theorem VIII.1.3): representability of the space of L-parameters
items.statement: There is a scheme Z¹(W_E, Ĝ) over ℤ_ℓ whose Λ-valued points, for a ℤ_ℓ-algebra Λ, are the condensed 1-cocycles φ : W_E → Ĝ(Λ). The scheme Z¹(W_E, Ĝ) is a union of open and closed affine subschemes Z¹(W_E/P, Ĝ) as P runs through open subgroups of the wild inertia subgroup of W_E, and each Z¹(W_E/P, Ĝ) is a flat local complete intersection over ℤ_ℓ of dimension dim G. (Standing hypotheses: E nonarchimedean local field with residue field 𝔽_q of characteristic p, G reductive over E, ℓ ≠ p, Ĝ/ℤ_ℓ with its algebraic W_E-action factoring through a finite quotient Q; Λ = Λ_disc ⊗_{ℤ_ℓ,disc} ℤ_ℓ regarded as a relatively discrete condensed ℤ_ℓ-module.)
items.locator: Chapter VIII, introduction, Theorem VIII.0.1, p. 277
items.note: Introduction restatement of Theorem VIII.1.3 (see c8-thm-VIII.1.3). LP1 plans "Construct the affine scheme Z^1(W_E/P,dual G) over Z_ell ... glue the open-and-closed pieces over P to Z^1(W_E,dual G). Prove flatness and local complete-intersection structure, including the dimension dim G for each finite wild piece".

items.name: Theorem VIII.0.2 (= Theorem VIII.5.1): invariants, excursion presentation and generation of Perf
items.statement: Assume that ℓ does not divide the order of π₁(Ĝ)_tor. Then Hⁱ(Ĝ, O(Z¹(W_E/P, Ĝ))) = 0 for i > 0 and the formation of the invariants O(Z¹(W_E/P, Ĝ))^Ĝ commutes with any base change. The algebra O(Z¹(W_E/P, Ĝ))^Ĝ admits an explicit presentation in terms of excursion operators, O(Z¹(W_E/P, Ĝ))^Ĝ = colim_{(n, F_n→W)} O(Z¹(F_n, Ĝ))^Ĝ, where the colimit runs over all maps from a free group F_n to W ⊂ W_E/P, and Z¹(F_n, Ĝ) ≅ Ĝⁿ with the simultaneous twisted Ĝ-conjugation. Moreover, the ∞-category Perf(Z¹(W_E/P, Ĝ)/Ĝ) is generated under cones, shifts and retracts by the image of Rep(Ĝ) → Perf(Z¹(W_E/P, Ĝ)/Ĝ), and Ind Perf(Z¹(W_E/P, Ĝ)/Ĝ) (printed without the quotient by Ĝ, PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E3) is equivalent to the ∞-category of modules over O(Z¹(W_E/P, Ĝ)) in Ind Perf(BĜ). All of these results also hold with ℚ_ℓ-coefficients, without the assumption on ℓ.
items.locator: Chapter VIII, introduction, Theorem VIII.0.2, pp. 277–278
items.note: Introduction restatement of Theorem VIII.3.6/VIII.5.1; the vanishing of higher cohomology and base change of invariants are deduced from Theorem VIII.5.1 (isomorphism in Ind Perf(∗/Ĝ)). LP4 plans "Construct Perf on the finite-wild quotient and its action of Rep(dual G). Prove generation by representation bundles under cones, shifts and retracts, and the comparison of Ind-Perf with module objects over the cocycle algebra in Ind-Perf(B dual G). Establish the finite-free-group colimit theorem". LP3 also plans "vanishing of higher group cohomology of the cocycle coordinate algebra and base change of invariants". The printed Ind Perf(Z¹(W_E/P, Ĝ)) omits the quotient by Ĝ (PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E57, same slip as the second clause of PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E3); the statement above uses the corrected form. The accepted decomposition node LanglandsParameterStacks:LP4/generation-and-module-comparison still quotes the uncorrected form.

items.name: Theorem VIII.0.3 (Section VIII.5.3): fixed points of prime-to-ℓ group actions on reductive groups
items.statement: Let G be a reductive group over an algebraically closed field L of characteristic ℓ. Let P be a finite group of order prime to ℓ acting on G. Then H = G^P is a smooth linear algebraic group whose connected component H° is reductive, and with π₀H of order prime to ℓ. If P is solvable, the image of Perf(∗/G) → Perf(∗/H) generates the whole category under cones and retracts. Moreover, still under the assumption that P is solvable, H° ⊂ G is a Donkin subgroup, i.e. for any representation V of G that admits a good G-filtration, also V|_{H°} has a good H°-filtration.
items.locator: Chapter VIII, introduction, Theorem VIII.0.3, p. 278
items.note: Summary of Proposition VIII.5.14, Theorem VIII.5.15 and Proposition VIII.5.17(vi). Generalizes Brundan [Bru98] and van der Kallen [vdK01] (P = ℤ/2ℤ). LP3 plans "For a finite group P of order prime to ell acting on a reductive group in characteristic ell, construct the fixed-point subgroup, prove smoothness/reductivity of its identity component and the prime-to-ell component-group order. Under the source's solvability hypothesis prove the Donkin subgroup property and generation of perfect complexes by restriction."

items.name: Definition VIII.1.1: L-parameter with coefficients in Λ
items.statement: Let Λ be any ℤ_ℓ-algebra, regarded as the condensed ℤ_ℓ-algebra Λ_disc ⊗_{ℤ_ℓ,disc} ℤ_ℓ (its value on a profinite set S is the ring of maps S → Λ that take values in a sub-ℤ_ℓ-module of finite type and are continuous). An L-parameter for G, with coefficients in Λ, is a section φ : W_E → Ĝ(Λ) ⋊ W_E of the natural map of condensed groups Ĝ(Λ) ⋊ W_E → W_E. Equivalently, an L-parameter for G with coefficients in Λ is a (condensed) 1-cocycle φ : W_E → Ĝ(Λ) for the given W_E-action on Ĝ. Concretely: a 1-cocycle φ : W_E → Ĝ(Λ) such that if Ĝ ↪ GL_N, the associated map W_E → GL_N(Λ) is continuous, i.e. the matrix coefficients of its restriction to I_E are maps I_E → Λ that take values in finite type ℤ_ℓ-modules and are continuous.
items.note: LP0 plans "Construct nonabelian continuous/condensed 1-cocycles, twisted conjugation, restriction, scalar extension and sections of the L-group projection. Establish equivalence of these descriptions." The pinned dual group with W_E-action and the L-group are RG2.5 ("Construct a pinned split dual group over ℤ ... Supply the semidirect L-group with its projection and action law"). Uses the standard (pinning-compatible) W_E-action, not the cyclotomically twisted one; the two agree after base change to ℤ_ℓ[√q].

items.name: Remark VIII.1.2: parameters as maps to Ĝ(Λ) ⋊ Q
items.statement: The standard action of W_E on Ĝ factors over a finite quotient Q. Hence L-parameters are also equivalent to maps W_E → Ĝ(Λ) ⋊ Q lifting W_E → Q.
items.note: LP0 plans "Construct nonabelian continuous/condensed 1-cocycles, twisted conjugation, restriction, scalar extension and sections of the L-group projection. Establish equivalence of these descriptions." The Q-form is used throughout VIII.3–VIII.4 (excursion data live on (Ĝ ⋊ Q)^I).

items.name: Theorem VIII.1.3: the scheme of L-parameters
items.statement: There is a scheme Z¹(W_E, Ĝ) over ℤ_ℓ parametrizing L-parameters for G, which is a disjoint union of affine schemes of finite type over ℤ_ℓ. It is flat and a relative complete intersection of dimension dim G = dim Ĝ.
items.note: LP1 plans "Construct the affine scheme Z^1(W_E/P,dual G) over Z_ell ... glue the open-and-closed pieces over P to Z^1(W_E,dual G). Prove flatness and local complete-intersection structure, including the dimension dim G for each finite wild piece". Proof: decomposition by the kernel on P_E, discretization W, extension W → W'_E, deformation theory of [X/Ĝ] (obstructions H², tangent H¹, automorphisms H⁰ of W with prime-to-p cohomological dimension 2 and Euler characteristic 0), reduction to fibre dimension over 𝔽̄_ℓ, the centralizer of the prime-to-ℓ inertia (reductive identity component by [PY02, Theorem 2.1]) and Lemma VIII.1.4. Cited results with prior references: [DHKM20], [Zhu20].

items.name: Clopen decomposition by the kernel on wild inertia (proof of Theorem VIII.1.3)
items.statement: Any condensed 1-cocycle φ : W_E → Ĝ(Λ) is trivial on an open subgroup of the wild inertia subgroup P_E; P_E acts on Ĝ through a finite quotient. For any γ ∈ P_E acting trivially on Ĝ, the locus where φ(γ) = 1 is open and closed (via a closed embedding Ĝ ↪ GL_N, since A = 1 is a connected component of the locus of all A ∈ GL_N with A^{p^r} = 1, its tangent space at A = 1 being trivial). Hence the moduli space of L-parameters decomposes as a disjoint union of open and closed subspaces according to the kernel of φ on P_E.
items.locator: Chapter VIII, §VIII.1.1, proof of Theorem VIII.1.3, p. 279
items.note: LP1 plans "glue the open-and-closed pieces over P to Z^1(W_E,dual G)"; LP0 adds "Finite wild ramification means triviality on an open subgroup P of wild inertia".

items.name: Discretization W ⊂ W'_E of the Weil group (proof of Theorem VIII.1.3)
items.statement: Fix a quotient W_E → W'_E by an open subgroup of P_E such that the action of W_E on Ĝ factors over W'_E. Inside W'_E let W be the discrete dense subgroup generated by the image of P_E, a choice of generator τ of tame inertia and a choice of Frobenius σ. Then W sits in an exact sequence 0 → I → W → σ^ℤ → 0, where I sits in an exact sequence 0 → P → I → τ^{ℤ[1/p]} → 0 with P a finite p-group; in W/P the elements τ and σ satisfy σ⁻¹τσ = τ^q.
items.locator: Chapter VIII, §VIII.1.1, proof of Theorem VIII.1.3, p. 279
items.note: LP0 plans "For each such P stable under the relevant action, choose and construct the dense discretization W in W_E/P using tame inertia and Frobenius ... Pin the relation sigma^(-1) tau sigma = tau^q". W is finitely generated, so Z¹(W, Ĝ) is visibly an affine scheme of finite type over ℤ_ℓ (indeed defined over ℤ[1/p]).

items.name: Unique extension of cocycles from the discretization (proof of Theorem VIII.1.3)
items.statement: Any condensed 1-cocycle W'_E → Ĝ(Λ) is determined by its restriction to the discrete dense subgroup W (as Ĝ(Λ) is quasiseparated), and conversely any 1-cocycle W → Ĝ(Λ) extends uniquely to a condensed 1-cocycle W'_E → Ĝ(Λ); so restriction gives Z¹(W_E/P, Ĝ) ≅ Z¹(W, Ĝ). Key step: for any A ∈ GL_N(Λ) such that A is conjugate to A^q, the map ℤ → GL_N(Λ), n ↦ Aⁿ, extends uniquely to ℤ̂^p; after replacing A by a prime-to-p power one may assume A unipotent, and then n ↦ Aⁿ = Σ_{i≥0} (n choose i)(A − 1)^i defines ℤ_ℓ → GL_N(Λ).
items.locator: Chapter VIII, §VIII.1.1, proof of Theorem VIII.1.3, pp. 279–280
items.note: LP0 plans "Prove the source's unique extension theorem from W to condensed W_E/P, including the topological unipotent binomial-series argument and its coefficients." Eigenvalues of A at geometric points are roots of unity of order prime to p. Mathlib has binomial coefficients but no such continuity statement.

items.name: Fibre-dimension bound over 𝔽̄_ℓ via the prime-to-ℓ inertia (proof of Theorem VIII.1.3)
items.statement: Over 𝔽̄_ℓ, the stack [Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)_{𝔽̄_ℓ}/Ĝ] maps to the stack of 1-cocycles φ^{I^ℓ} : I^ℓ → Ĝ_{𝔽̄_ℓ} of the prime-to-ℓ inertia subgroup I^ℓ up to conjugation. By deformation theory that stack is smooth, and each connected component is the quotient of Spec 𝔽̄_ℓ by the centralizer C_{φ^{I^ℓ}} ⊂ Ĝ_{𝔽̄_ℓ}, a smooth group whose identity component is reductive [PY02, Theorem 2.1]. Fix φ^{I^ℓ} and let X_{φ^{I^ℓ}} ⊂ Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)_{𝔽̄_ℓ} be the closed subscheme of cocycles restricting to φ^{I^ℓ}. With C̃ the normalizer of φ^{I^ℓ}(I^ℓ) in Ĝ_{𝔽̄_ℓ} ⋊ Q, X_{φ^{I^ℓ}} maps with finite fibres to the space of homomorphisms W_E/I^ℓ ≅ ℤ_ℓ ⋊ σ^ℤ → C̃/φ^{I^ℓ}(I^ℓ), and the universal such homomorphism factors over some ℤ/ℓ^mℤ ⋊ σ^ℤ. Lemma VIII.1.4 then gives dim X_{φ^{I^ℓ}} ≤ dim C_{φ^{I^ℓ}}, i.e. every fibre of [Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)/Ĝ] over 𝔽̄_ℓ has dimension ≤ 0.
items.locator: Chapter VIII, §VIII.1.1, proof of Theorem VIII.1.3, p. 280
items.note: LP1 plans 'Show how obstructions and centralizers appear' and the dimension statement; the accepted decomposition's LP1 coverage records [PY02, Theorem 2.1] as the unread input of this step. The same Prasad–Yu input appears in Proposition VIII.5.14 (LP3). Without this step Lemma VIII.1.4 (c8-lem-VIII.1.4-dimension-bound) has no stated use. Added in review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21).

items.name: Deformation theory of [Z¹(W, Ĝ)/Ĝ] and reduction of Theorem VIII.1.3 to a fibre-dimension bound (proof of Theorem VIII.1.3)
items.statement: Let W be a discretization of W_E/P as in the proof of Theorem VIII.1.3 and X = Z¹(W, Ĝ), an affine scheme of finite type over ℤ_ℓ (indeed defined over ℤ[1/p], with W independent of ℓ). For a field Λ and a point φ ∈ X(Λ), the Artin stack [X/Ĝ] has obstruction group H²(W, (ĝ ⊗_{ℤ_ℓ} Λ)_φ), tangent space H¹(W, (ĝ ⊗_{ℤ_ℓ} Λ)_φ) and infinitesimal automorphisms H⁰(W, (ĝ ⊗_{ℤ_ℓ} Λ)_φ), with W acting through φ twisted by the given action. The prime-to-p cohomological dimension of W is 2 and the Euler characteristic of every such representation is 0. Hence [X/Ĝ] is flat and a relative complete intersection of dimension 0 over ℤ_ℓ (equivalently X is flat, lci, of relative dimension dim Ĝ) as soon as every fibre of [X/Ĝ] → Spec ℤ_ℓ has dimension ≤ 0. By constructibility of fibre dimension over Spec ℤ[1/p], it suffices to prove this over 𝔽̄_ℓ for every ℓ ≠ p.
items.locator: Chapter VIII, §VIII.1.1, proof of Theorem VIII.1.3, p. 280
items.note: LP1 plans 'Show how obstructions and centralizers appear' and 'Prove flatness and local complete-intersection structure, including the dimension dim G for each finite wild piece'. The accepted decomposition node LanglandsParameterStacks:LP1/representability-flatness-and-lci carries this proof: its review lists 'the tangent-space computation, the Euler-characteristic and dimension estimates in its proof (pp. 279-280)' as checked. It is the step that makes the space lci and the input reused by Propositions VIII.2.1 and VIII.3.5, and it is only mentioned in the note of c8-thm-VIII.1.3-representability. Added in review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21).

items.name: Lemma VIII.1.4: dimension of Hom(ℤ/ℓ^mℤ ⋊ σ^ℤ, H)
items.statement: Let H be a smooth group scheme over 𝔽̄_ℓ whose identity component is reductive. Then the affine scheme parametrizing maps of groups ℤ/ℓ^mℤ ⋊ σ^ℤ → H, where σ acts on ℤ/ℓ^mℤ via multiplication by q, is of dimension at most dim H.
items.note: Proof ingredient of the dimension bound in Theorem VIII.1.3 (LP1: "Prove flatness and local complete-intersection structure, including the dimension dim G"). Uses finiteness of unipotent conjugacy classes ([Lus76], [FG12, Corollary 2.6]); stratify by the class of τ, and σ ranges over a coset of the centralizer.

items.name: Proposition VIII.2.1: tangent complex of the stack of L-parameters
items.statement: For any parameter φ : W_E → Ĝ(Λ) ⋊ Q corresponding to x : Spec(Λ) → [Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)/Ĝ], x*𝕃^∨_{Z¹(W_E,Ĝ)/Ĝ} = RΓ(W_E, (ĝ ⊗_{ℤ_ℓ} Λ)_φ)[1], where (ĝ ⊗_{ℤ_ℓ} Λ)_φ is ĝ ⊗_{ℤ_ℓ} Λ equipped with the twisted action of W_E deduced from φ.
items.note: LP1 plans "Construct the derived mapping stack over the finite pinned-action quotient, its tangent complex by cocycle cohomology, and the comparison with the classical cocycle scheme where the source proves it underived." Proof: the derived moduli problem is a derived lci of expected dimension 0 and the classical stack is already lci of dimension 0, so they agree on animated rings. Cotangent complexes from DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.0 / EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:cotangent-export.

items.name: Proposition VIII.2.2: perfectness and duality for W_E-cohomology
items.statement: Let M be a free Λ-module of finite rank equipped with a condensed action of W_E. Then RΓ(W_E, M) is a perfect complex of Λ-modules and there is a canonical isomorphism RΓ(W_E, M)* ≅ RΓ(W_E, M*(1))[2].
items.note: Proof: Poincaré duality for Div¹ → ∗ via Proposition VII.3.5 (Chapter VII), or by hand via the discretization W. Planned at node level: LanglandsParameterStacks:LP1/cotangent-complex-and-deformation-theory ("for M a free Lambda-module of finite rank with a condensed W_E-action, RGamma(W_E,M) is a PERFECT complex of Lambda-modules and there is a canonical isomorphism RGamma(W_E,M)^dual = RGamma(W_E, M^dual(1))[2]") (packet research/blueprint/packets/LanglandsParameterStacks.json; the packet was committed 24 September 2026 and its review REV-LanglandsParameterStacks is still queued). items.name: Unipotent monodromy morphism 𝓜 (§VIII.2.1)
items.statement: Fix an isomorphism I_E/P_E ≅ ℤ̂^p and lift ℤ_ℓ ↪ ℤ̂^p ≅ I_E/P_E to a morphism ℤ_ℓ → I_E. There is a Ĝ_{ℚ_ℓ}-equivariant morphism 𝓜 : Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)_{ℚ_ℓ} → 𝒩_{Ĝ_{ℚ_ℓ}}, the nilpotent cone inside ĝ ⊗ ℚ_ℓ: if φ : W_E → Ĝ(Λ), Λ a ℚ_ℓ-algebra, then for n ≫ 0, φ|_{ℓⁿℤ_ℓ} is a morphism of condensed groups with φ(σ^m) φ|_{ℓⁿℤ_ℓ} φ(σ^m)⁻¹ = φ^{q^m}|_{ℓⁿℤ_ℓ} for m ≫ 0, and there is a unique N ∈ 𝒩_Ĝ(Λ) such that φ(x) = exp(xN) for n ≫ 0 and x ∈ ℓⁿℤ_ℓ.

items.name: Definition VIII.2.4: Weil–Deligne L-parameters Par^WD_Ĝ
items.statement: For Λ a ℚ_ℓ-algebra one defines Par^WD_Ĝ(Λ) to be the set of pairs (φ₀, N) where (i) φ₀ : W_E → Ĝ(Λ) is a 1-cocycle that is continuous for the discrete topology on Ĝ(Λ) (i.e., trivial on an open subgroup of I_E), (ii) N ∈ 𝒩_Ĝ ⊗ Λ satisfies Ad(φ₀(σ)).σN = q^{|σ|}N for all σ ∈ W_E.

items.name: Hochschild cohomology acting on Ext (§VIII.2.2.1)
items.statement: Let A → B be a flat map of commutative rings, HH^•(B/A) = Ext^•_{B⊗_A B}(B, B). For any N ∈ D(B) there is a natural map of graded algebras HH^•(B/A) → Ext^•_B(N, N) (via M ↦ (N ↦ M ⊗^L_B N), with M = B inducing the identity). There is a natural map H¹(L^∨_{B/A}) = Ext¹_B(L_{B/A}, B) = Exalcomm_A(B, B) ([Gro64, Chap. 0, 18.4]) → HH²(B/A) (a commutative square-zero extension is in particular an associative one, and HH² classifies the associative ones, [ML95, Theorem X.3.1]); the paper states this map as an identification HH²(B/A) = Ext¹_B(L_{B/A}, B), which is false in general (see the new issue on p. 282). Composing gives H¹(L^∨_{B/A}) → HH²(B/A) → Ext²_B(N, N).
items.note: Following [AG15]. The printed identification HH²(B/A) = Ext¹_B(L_{B/A}, B) fails already for B = k[x, y] over a field k (HH² ≅ B by Hochschild–Kostant–Rosenberg, Ext¹(L_{B/k}, B) = 0); only the map is used later. Hochschild cochains and HH² of (DG) algebras over a commutative base are planned in the Tau Ceti roadmap DGAInfinity (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/DGAInfinity#layer-8-hochschild-cochains-deformations-massey-products-and-formality, which also recovers HH² as infinitesimal deformations); no stage plans the map HH^•(B/A) → Ext^•_B(N, N), its comparison with Exalcomm, or singular support. Mathlib has Kähler differentials and the naive cotangent complex (Algebra.Extension.cotangentComplex) but no HH^•. items.name: Definition VIII.2.6: the scheme Sing_{X/S}
items.statement: Suppose A → B is syntomic (flat and a local complete intersection), X = Spec B → S = Spec A. The scheme Sing_{X/S} → X represents the functor T/X ↦ H^{−1}(L_{X/S} ⊗^L_{O_X} O_T). Locally, if L_{X/S} ≅ [E^{−1} → E⁰] with vector bundles, Sing_{X/S} = ker(V(E^{−1}) → V(E⁰)); explicitly O(Sing_{X/S}) = Sym^•_B H¹(L^∨_{B/A}). It is an X-group scheme with a 𝔾_m-action, and the image of Sing_{X/S} ∖ {0} → X is the closed complement of the smooth locus of X → S.

items.name: Theorem VIII.2.9 ([AG15, Theorem 4.2.6]): perfectness via singular support
items.statement: (S regular, A → B syntomic, N ∈ D^b_coh(X).) The following are equivalent: (i) N is a perfect complex, (ii) SingSupp(N) is contained in the zero section of Sing_{X/S}.
items.note: Proof given: reduce to Ext^i_B(N,N) = 0 for i ≫ 0 ⇒ N perfect, using Gorensteinness of B and Jorgensen's theorem [Jor08] (a finitely generated B-module with Ext^i_B(N,N) = 0 for i > n has pd_B N ≤ n). Mathlib has projective dimension (CategoryTheory.HasProjectiveDimensionLE) but no Gorenstein rings or Jorgensen's theorem. items.name: Proposition VIII.2.11: singular support lies in the nilpotent cone
items.statement: For a ℤ_ℓ-field L and a point x : Spec(L) → [Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)/Ĝ] we have x*Sing_{[Z¹(W_E,Ĝ)/Ĝ]/ℤ_ℓ} ⊂ 𝒩*_Ĝ ⊗_{ℤ_ℓ} L in the following two cases: (i) L|ℚ_ℓ, (ii) if n = f_{E′/E} with W_{E′} = ker(W_E → Out(Ĝ)), then q^{en} − 1 is not divisible by ℓ for any degree e of a basic invariant of Ĝ (the paper says 'exponent', meaning these degrees; PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E58).
items.note: Proof: x*Sing = H⁰(W_E, ĝ* ⊗ L(1)) twisted by φ; v is conjugate to qⁿv, and the Chevalley map ĝ → ĝ//Ĝ = t̂//W ≅ 𝔸^m (valid since (ii) makes ℓ very good, and ĝ* ≅ ĝ) forces v nilpotent. 'Exponents' here means the degrees of the basic invariants (PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E58). The paper notes (ii) holds e.g. if ℓ > q^{hn} − 1, h the Coxeter number; finer results in [DHKM20, §5.3]. items.name: Geometric points of the coarse moduli space (§VIII.3.1)
items.statement: Let Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)//Ĝ be the quotient in the category of schemes (componentwise Spec A^Ĝ for Spec A ⊂ Z¹(W_E, Ĝ) connected). For any algebraically closed field L over ℤ_ℓ, the L-valued points of Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)_L//Ĝ are in bijection with the closed Ĝ-orbits in Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)_L.
items.note: LP2:integral-invariants plans "Construct the invariant algebra and the affine coarse quotient on each finite-wild piece, its universal property for invariant maps, change of coefficients and the relation to closed semisimple geometric orbits." Standard GIT (geometric reductivity).

items.name: Definition VIII.3.1: semisimple L-parameter
items.statement: Let L be an algebraically closed field over ℤ_ℓ. Parabolic subgroups of Ĝ ⋊ W_E are those of Ĝ_L ⋊ W_E surjecting onto W_E; up to Ĝ(L)-conjugation they are P̂_L ⋊ W_E for P ⊂ G* a standard parabolic of the quasisplit inner form G* of G, with Levi M̂_L ⋊ W_E. An L-parameter φ : W_E → Ĝ(L) ⋊ W_E is semisimple if whenever the image of φ is contained in a parabolic subgroup of Ĝ ⋊ W_E then it is contained in a Levi subgroup of this parabolic subgroup. Equivalently: if some Ĝ(L)-conjugate φ′ of φ factorizes through P̂(L) ⋊ W_E, then there exists g ∈ P̂(L) with gφ′g⁻¹ = i_{L M} pr_{L M} ∘ φ′.
items.note: LP2:semisimple-characters plans "excursion characters ... determine a unique conjugacy class of continuous semisimple L-parameters ... prove simultaneous conjugacy/complete reducibility". Standard parabolics correspond to finite W_E-stable subsets of Δ̂ ([Bor79]).

items.name: Proposition VIII.3.2 ([DHKM20, Proposition 4.13]): closed orbits are semisimple parameters
items.statement: Let L be an algebraically closed field over ℤ_ℓ and φ : W_E → Ĝ(L) ⋊ W_E a parameter. The following are equivalent: (i) The Ĝ-orbit of φ in Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)_L is closed. (ii) For any conjugate φ′ of φ such that φ′ : W_E → P̂(L) ⋊ W_E factors over a standard parabolic subgroup, φ is Ĝ(L)-conjugate to i_{L M} pr_{L M} ∘ φ′. (iii) φ is semi-simple.
items.note: LP2:integral-invariants: "the relation to closed semisimple geometric orbits"; LP2:semisimple-characters: "prove simultaneous conjugacy/complete reducibility". Proof uses Hilbert–Mumford–Kempf [Kem78, Corollary 3.5], Lemma VIII.3.3, and [BMR05] (strong reductivity, complete reducibility, non-connected version §6) with [Ric88]. Tau Ceti has the untwisted dynamic parabolic and limit (tauceti:TauCeti.Cocharacter.limit, TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Dynamic/Parabolic.lean:332, read) but no Hilbert–Mumford criterion. The paper also notes semisimplicity equals complete reducibility (in [BMR05, §6] sense) of the Zariski closure of the image in Ĝ(L) ⋊ Q.

items.name: Lemma VIII.3.3: existence of twisted limits
items.statement: Let L be an algebraically closed field over ℤ_ℓ and T̂ ⊂ Ĝ the maximal torus of the pinning. For λ ∈ X_*(T̂)^+ (printed X_*(T)^+) and g ⋊ τ ∈ Ĝ(L) ⋊ W_E, the limit lim_{t→0} λ(t)gλ(t)^{−τ} exists if and only if g ∈ Q_λ(L), the parabolic subgroup attached to λ, and λ^τ = λ.
items.note: Proof ingredient of Proposition VIII.3.2 (LP2:integral-invariants: "the relation to closed semisimple geometric orbits"). Tau Ceti has the untwisted case: the dynamic parabolic P(λ) is defined as the set of points whose conjugate extends over the origin, with the limit homomorphism (tauceti:TauCeti.Cocharacter.limit, TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Dynamic/Parabolic.lean:332, read); the τ-twisted statement and λ^τ = λ are absent. Proof via Bruhat decomposition g = g′ẇg″. The printed X_*(T)^+ means X_*(T̂)^+ (the proof ends 'Since λ^τ ∈ X_*(T̂)^+'); see the new issue. The lemma is the key step of Proposition VIII.3.2, which the accepted decomposition node LanglandsParameterStacks:LP2:semisimple-characters/semisimple-parameters-and-closed-orbits plans.

items.name: Presentation of O(Z¹(W, Ĝ)) by free groups; universal homeomorphism on invariants (§VIII.3.2)
items.statement: Let P be an open subgroup of wild inertia with the W_E-action on Ĝ factoring over W_E/P, and W ⊂ W_E/P a discretization, so Z¹(W_E/P, Ĝ) = Z¹(W, Ĝ). For each n ≥ 0 and F_n → W there is a Ĝ-equivariant map O(Z¹(F_n, Ĝ)) → O(Z¹(W, Ĝ)), with O(Z¹(F_n, Ĝ)) ≅ O(Ĝⁿ) with twisted diagonal Ĝ-conjugation. The index category {(n, F_n → W)} is sifted, and colim_{(n,F_n→W)} O(Z¹(F_n, Ĝ)) → O(Z¹(W, Ĝ)) is an isomorphism of algebras with Ĝ-action. By Haboush's theorem [Hab75], the induced map colim_{(n,F_n→W)} O(Z¹(F_n, Ĝ))^Ĝ → O(Z¹(W, Ĝ))^Ĝ is a universal homeomorphism of finite type ℤ_ℓ-algebras, and an isomorphism after inverting ℓ.
items.note: LP2:excursion-presentation: "Its canonical map to the invariant-coordinate algebra is a universal homeomorphism in the general coefficient case, not always an isomorphism." LP2:integral-invariants: "Prove the presentation of the invariant algebra by all finite free-group cocycle spaces mapping to W". Haboush geometric reductivity is not in the library (grep); Tau Ceti has linear reductivity/complete reducibility of comodules only.

items.name: Definition VIII.3.4: the algebra of excursion operators
items.statement: The algebra of excursion operators (for Z¹(W, Ĝ)) is Exc(W, Ĝ) = colim_{(n,F_n→W)} O(Z¹(F_n, Ĝ))^Ĝ. In particular the geometric points of Exc(W, Ĝ) and Z¹(W, Ĝ)//Ĝ agree.
items.note: LP2:excursion-presentation plans "Construct Exc(W,dual G) from finite free-group cocycle invariants". The paper prints 'the geometric points of Exc(W, Ĝ) and Z¹(W, Ĝ) agree'; Z¹(W, Ĝ)//Ĝ is meant (new issue), and the statement above uses the corrected form, as does the accepted decomposition node LanglandsParameterStacks:LP2:excursion-presentation/excursion-algebra-and-universal-homeomorphism.

items.name: Proposition VIII.3.5: the free-group colimit is underived
items.statement: Working in the derived ∞-category D(ℤ_ℓ), the map colim_{(n,F_n→W)} O(Z¹(F_n, Ĝ)) → O(Z¹(W, Ĝ)) is an isomorphism in D(ℤ_ℓ). (Both sides are animated ℤ_ℓ-algebras — the left side is the universal animated ℤ_ℓ-algebra A with a 1-cocycle W → Ĝ(A) — and the map is an isomorphism of animated ℤ_ℓ-algebras.)
items.note: LP1 plans "the comparison with the classical cocycle scheme where the source proves it underived". Proof: A is a derived complete intersection by the deformation theory of Theorem VIII.1.3 and π₀A has the correct dimension, so A = π₀A.

items.name: Theorem VIII.3.6: excursion algebra = invariant algebra
items.statement: Assume that ℓ does not divide the order of π₁(Ĝ)_tor. Then the map colim_{(n,F_n→W)} O(Z¹(F_n, Ĝ)) → O(Z¹(W, Ĝ)) is an isomorphism in the presentable stable ∞-category Ind Perf(∗/Ĝ). In particular, the map Exc(W, Ĝ) = colim_{(n,F_n→W)} O(Z¹(F_n, Ĝ))^Ĝ → O(Z¹(W, Ĝ))^Ĝ is an isomorphism. (Footnote: the map is also a map, hence isomorphism, of E_∞-algebras in Ind Perf(∗/Ĝ).)
items.note: Proved in §VIII.5 (Theorem VIII.5.1). LP2:integral-invariants: "For integral coefficients impose ell not dividing the torsion order of pi_1(dual G) for the base-change/vanishing/generation theorems"; LP4: "Establish the finite-free-group colimit theorem".

items.name: Proposition VIII.3.7: universal property of Exc(W, Ĝ)
items.statement: Fix a finite quotient Q of W_E over which the W_E-action on Ĝ factors; let (Ĝ ⋊ Q)ⁿ//Ĝ be the quotient of (Ĝ ⋊ Q)ⁿ under simultaneous Ĝ-conjugation. The algebra Exc(W, Ĝ) is the universal ℤ_ℓ-algebra A equipped with maps of ℤ_ℓ-algebras Θ_n (printed 'maps'; the proof needs ring maps) : O((Ĝ ⋊ Q)ⁿ//Ĝ) → Map(Wⁿ, A) for n ≥ 1, linear over O(Qⁿ) → Map(Wⁿ, A), such that for any map g : {1,…,m} → {1,…,n}: (a) the square O((Ĝ⋊Q)^m//Ĝ) → Map(W^m, A), O((Ĝ⋊Q)ⁿ//Ĝ) → Map(Wⁿ, A) with vertical natural pullback maps commutes; (b) with the maps (Ĝ⋊Q)^m → (Ĝ⋊Q)ⁿ multiplying in every fibre over i the terms in g⁻¹(i) (in their order in {1,…,m}), and similarly W^m → Wⁿ, the induced square O((Ĝ⋊Q)ⁿ//Ĝ) → Map(Wⁿ, A), O((Ĝ⋊Q)^m//Ĝ) → Map(W^m, A) commutes.
items.note: LP2:excursion-presentation plans "prove FS VIII.4's universal property"; LP2:integral-invariants: "with the reindexing and multiplication relations of FS VIII.3–VIII.4". The inversion relation is left as an exercise (hint via Θ_{n+1} at (γ₁,…,γ_n,γ_n⁻¹)). The printed statement says only 'maps' Θ_n; the proof's first sentence ('The datum of the Θ_n is equivalent the datum of a map of algebras O(Z¹(F_n, Ĝ))^Ĝ → A for each map F_n → W') and Proposition VIII.3.8(iii) require maps of ℤ_ℓ-algebras (new issue). Planned by the accepted decomposition node LanglandsParameterStacks:LP2:excursion-presentation/universal-property-of-the-excursion-algebra.

items.name: Proposition VIII.3.7, second part: the ℓ-torsion-free quotient
items.statement: The ℓ-torsion free quotient of Exc(W, Ĝ) is also the universal flat ℤ_ℓ-algebra A′ equipped with maps of ℤ_ℓ-algebras Θ′_n : O((Ĝ ⋊ Q)ⁿ//Ĝ) → Map((W_E/P)ⁿ, A′) for n ≥ 1, linear over O(Qⁿ) → Map((W_E/P)ⁿ, A′), satisfying the same relations, where Map((W_E/P)ⁿ, A′) denotes maps of condensed sets (A′ relatively discrete over ℤ_ℓ). In particular, the ℓ-torsion free quotient of Exc(W, Ĝ) is independent of the discretization W of W_E/P. Moreover the ℓ-torsion in Exc(W, Ĝ) is always nilpotent (so passing to this quotient is a universal homeomorphism), and if ℓ ∤ |π₁(Ĝ)_tor| then Exc(W, Ĝ) ≅ O(Z¹(W_E/P, Ĝ))^Ĝ is flat over ℤ_ℓ.
items.locator: Chapter VIII, §VIII.3.3, Proposition VIII.3.7 (second paragraph) and the remark after it, p. 289
items.note: LP2:semisimple-characters: "prove independence of the finite-wild/discretization choices"; LP2:integral-invariants: "continuity of evaluations on W_E". The authors do not know whether passing to the ℓ-torsion-free quotient is necessary for independence of W.

items.name: Proposition VIII.3.8: semisimple parameters, coarse points and excursion characters
items.statement: Let L be an algebraically closed field over ℤ_ℓ. Then the following are in canonical bijection. (i) Semisimple L-parameters φ : W_E → Ĝ(L) ⋊ W_E, up to Ĝ(L)-conjugation. (ii) L-valued points of Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)//Ĝ. (iii) Collections of maps of ℤ_ℓ-algebras Θ_n : O((Ĝ ⋊ Q)ⁿ//Ĝ) → Map(W_Eⁿ, L) for n ≥ 1, linear over O(Qⁿ) → Map(W_Eⁿ, L), such that for any map g : {1,…,m} → {1,…,n}, the diagrams induced by pullback and by multiplication commute.
items.note: LP2:semisimple-characters plans "Prove FS VIII.3.8: excursion characters over an algebraically closed field L ... determine a unique conjugacy class of continuous semisimple L-parameters". Continuity from the proof of [Laf18, Proposition 11.7] and [Laf18, Lemma 11.10]. Map(W_Eⁿ, L) are maps of condensed sets.

items.name: Theorem VIII.4.1 (after V. Lafforgue): excursion algebra acts on the Bernstein center
items.statement: Let W be any discrete group (e.g. W ⊂ W_E/P), Λ a discrete ℤ_ℓ-algebra and 𝒞 a Λ-linear category (printed 'ℤ_ℓ-linear'; the proof uses the structure map Λ → End(id_𝒞)). Assume that functorially in finite sets I, we are given a monoidal Rep_{ℤ_ℓ}(Q^I)-linear functor Rep_{ℤ_ℓ}((Ĝ ⋊ Q)^I) → End(𝒞)^{BW^I} : V ↦ T_V, where End(𝒞)^{BW^I} is the category of F ∈ End(𝒞) equipped with a map of groups W^I → Aut(F). Then there is a natural map of algebras Exc(W, Ĝ) = colim_{(n,F_n→W)} O(Z¹(F_n, Ĝ))^Ĝ → End(id_𝒞) to the Bernstein center of 𝒞 (the algebra of endomorphisms of the identity of 𝒞).
items.note: ES0 plans "Construct excursion operators from a finite leg set, a matrix coefficient/invariant function, creation by a coevaluation map, the prescribed tuple of Weil elements and annihilation by evaluation ... Establish linearity, multiplication, reindexing, unit insertion and composition relations"; LP2:excursion-presentation: "prove FS VIII.4's universal property". The printed superscript on p. 291 is BW_E^I, while the definition uses maps W^I → Aut(F); W is meant (new issue). The printed '𝒞 a ℤ_ℓ-linear category' should be Λ-linear (new issue). The same theorem is also planned by the accepted decomposition node LanglandsParameterStacks:LP2:excursion-presentation/map-to-a-bernstein-center, so two roadmaps plan it.

items.name: Definition VIII.4.2: excursion datum and excursion operator S_𝒟
items.statement: An excursion datum is a tuple 𝒟 = (I, V, α, β, (γ_i)_{i∈I}) consisting of a finite set I, an object V ∈ Rep_{ℤ_ℓ}((Ĝ ⋊ Q)^I) with maps α : 1 → V|_{Rep_{ℤ_ℓ}(Ĝ)}, β : V|_{Rep_{ℤ_ℓ}(Ĝ)} → 1 and elements γ_i ∈ W, i ∈ I (restriction to the diagonal Ĝ ⊂ Ĝ^I ⊂ (Ĝ ⋊ Q)^I). It gives the endomorphism S_𝒟 : id = T_1 --T_α--> T_V --(γ_i)_{i∈I}--> T_V --T_β--> T_1 = id of the identity functor of 𝒞; varying the γ_i gives a map W^I → End(id_𝒞).
items.note: ES0 plans "Construct excursion operators from a finite leg set, a matrix coefficient/invariant function, creation by a coevaluation map, the prescribed tuple of Weil elements and annihilation by evaluation."

items.name: The maps Θ^I and their properties (proof of Theorem VIII.4.1)
items.statement: (a) If g : V → V′ takes α to α′ and β′ to β, then S_𝒟 = S_𝒟′. (b) (V, α, β) gives f(V, α, β) ∈ O(Ĝ\(Ĝ ⋊ Q)^I/Ĝ) (by g ↦ β∘(g_i)∘α); conversely f generates V_f ⊂ O((Ĝ ⋊ Q)^I/Ĝ) with α_f, β_f (evaluation at 1), so S_𝒟 depends only on f, giving Θ^I : O(Ĝ\(Ĝ ⋊ Q)^I/Ĝ) → Map(W^I, End(id_𝒞)), restricting on O(Q^I) to O(Q^I) → Map(W^I, Λ). (c) Θ^I is compatible with pullback along any g : I → J. (d) Θ^{I⊔I}(f₁ ⊠ f₂)((γ_i, γ′_i)_{i∈I}) = Θ^I(f₁)((γ_i))Θ^I(f₂)((γ′_i)), hence Θ^I(f₁f₂) = Θ^I(f₁)Θ^I(f₂). (e) Via O(Ĝ\(Ĝ ⋊ Q)^{{0,…,n}}/Ĝ) ⊗_{O(Q^{{0,…,n}})} O(Q^{{1,…,n}}) ≅ O((Ĝ ⋊ Q)ⁿ//Ĝ) (pullback along (g₁,…,g_n) ↦ (1, g₁,…,g_n)) one gets algebra maps Θ_n : O((Ĝ ⋊ Q)ⁿ//Ĝ) → Map(Wⁿ, End(id_𝒞)) compatible with pullback and (as in [Laf18, Lemma 10.1, (10.5), Proposition 10.8(iii), Definition-Proposition 11.3(d)]) with multiplication.
items.note: ES0 plans "Prove independence of the representation realizing the function using the parameter algebra's presentation. Establish linearity, multiplication, reindexing, unit insertion and composition relations". The printed text calls the pullback square in (c) "cartesian"; it should be "commutative" (PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E59).

items.name: Corollary VIII.4.3: semisimple parameter attached to a Schur object
items.statement: (In the setting of Theorem VIII.4.1.) Assume that Λ = L is an algebraically closed field and X ∈ 𝒞 is an object with End(X) = L. Then there is, up to Ĝ(L)-conjugation, a unique semisimple L-parameter φ_X : W → Ĝ(L) ⋊ W such that for all excursion data 𝒟 = (I, V, α, β, (γ_i)_{i∈I}), the endomorphism S_𝒟(X) ∈ End(X) = L, X = T_1(X) --α--> T_V(X) --(γ_i)_{i∈I}--> T_V(X) --β--> T_1(X) = X, is given by the composite L --α--> V --(φ_X(γ_i))_{i∈I}--> V --β--> L.
items.note: Uses the description of geometric points (Proposition VIII.3.8). LP2:semisimple-characters plans the character-to-parameter step; ES5 plans the application to D_lis(Bun_G) ("construct FS Definition/Proposition IX.4.1's continuous semisimple parameter ... Prove the defining identity for every excursion datum"). The general categorical corollary is not stated as a separate stage. The target is written Ĝ(L) ⋊ W (for a discrete W, with Q-form implicit).

items.name: Theorem VIII.5.1: integral colimit isomorphism and generation
items.statement: Assume that ℓ does not divide the order of π₁(Ĝ)_tor. Then the map colim_{(n,F_n→W)} O(Z¹(F_n, Ĝ)) → O(Z¹(W, Ĝ)) is an isomorphism in the presentable stable ∞-category Ind Perf(∗/Ĝ). Moreover, the ∞-category Perf(Z¹(W, Ĝ)/Ĝ) is generated under cones and retracts by Perf(∗/Ĝ), and Ind Perf(Z¹(W, Ĝ)/Ĝ) identifies with the ∞-category of modules over O(Z¹(W, Ĝ)) in Ind Perf(∗/Ĝ).
items.note: LP4 plans "Construct Perf on the finite-wild quotient and its action of Rep(dual G). Prove generation by representation bundles under cones, shifts and retracts, and the comparison of Ind-Perf with module objects over the cocycle algebra in Ind-Perf(B dual G). Establish the finite-free-group colimit theorem". Refines Theorem VIII.3.6; used for the spectral action (Chapter X).

items.name: Theorem VIII.5.2: the characteristic-ℓ version
items.statement: Assume that ℓ does not divide the order of π₁(Ĝ)_tor, and let L = 𝔽̄_ℓ. Then the map colim_{(n,F_n→W)} O(Z¹(F_n, Ĝ)_L) → O(Z¹(W, Ĝ)_L) is an isomorphism in the presentable stable ∞-category Ind Perf(∗/Ĝ). Moreover, the ∞-category Perf(Z¹(W, Ĝ)_L/Ĝ) is generated under cones and retracts by Perf(∗/Ĝ).
items.note: LP4 plans "Construct Perf on the finite-wild quotient and its action of Rep(dual G). Prove generation by representation bundles under cones, shifts and retracts, and the comparison of Ind-Perf with module objects over the cocycle algebra in Ind-Perf(B dual G). Establish the finite-free-group colimit theorem". Proved in §VIII.5.4 via the tame case and Proposition VIII.5.21.

items.name: Theorem VIII.5.2 implies Theorem VIII.5.1
items.statement: Theorem VIII.5.2 implies Theorem VIII.5.1: the colimit claim reduces (after inverting ℓ by semisimplicity, and on underlying complexes by Proposition VIII.3.5) to the statement mod ℓ; generation plus Barr–Beck–Lurie [Lur16, Theorem 4.7.4.5] identifies Ind Perf(Z¹(W, Ĝ)/Ĝ) with O(Z¹(W, Ĝ))-modules in Ind Perf(BĜ), and a Ĝ-equivariant vector bundle is a retract of an induced one up to a power of ℓ, reducing generation to V/ℓ.
items.locator: Chapter VIII, §VIII.5, proof that Theorem VIII.5.2 implies Theorem VIII.5.1, pp. 293–294
items.note: LP4 plans "Construct Perf on the finite-wild quotient and its action of Rep(dual G). Prove generation by representation bundles under cones, shifts and retracts, and the comparison of Ind-Perf with module objects over the cocycle algebra in Ind-Perf(B dual G). Establish the finite-free-group colimit theorem".

items.name: Good filtrations and the induced modules ∇_λ (§VIII.5.1)
items.statement: Let G be a (connected) reductive group over an algebraically closed field L of characteristic ℓ, T ⊂ B ⊂ G a torus and Borel. For a dominant weight λ of T, ∇_λ = H⁰(G/B, O(λ)). A representation V of G has a good filtration if it admits an exhaustive filtration 0 = V_{−1} ⊂ V₀ ⊂ V₁ ⊂ … ⊂ V such that each V_i/V_{i−1} is isomorphic to a direct sum of ∇_λ's. (With a total ordering λ₀ = 0, λ₁, … compatible with dominance and V_i the maximal subrepresentation with weights λ_j, j ≤ i, V has a good filtration iff all maps V_i → W_i ⊗ ∇_{λ_i} are surjective.)
items.note: LP3 plans "Construct highest-weight modules, Weyl and dual-Weyl modules, good filtrations, the good-filtration t-structure and the relevant Ext-vanishing criteria ... Prove stability under tensor, induction and restriction under the FS VIII.5 hypotheses." In §VIII.5 G denotes the dual group Ĝ_L; the paper writes "dominant cocharacter" for the dominant weights (PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E65). Not in the library: Tau Ceti has comodules and complete reducibility over linearly reductive groups, no induced modules H⁰(G/B, λ).

items.name: Donkin–Mathieu tensor product theorem and Kempf vanishing (§VIII.5.1)
items.statement: If V and W admit good G-filtrations, then so does V ⊗ W ([Don85], [Mat90]). If V admits a good filtration, then Hⁱ(G, V) = 0 for i > 0 (reducing to V = ∇_λ, Kempf's vanishing theorem [Kem76]).
items.note: LP3 plans "Construct highest-weight modules, Weyl and dual-Weyl modules, good filtrations, the good-filtration t-structure and the relevant Ext-vanishing criteria ... Prove stability under tensor, induction and restriction under the FS VIII.5 hypotheses." Cited inputs, not proved in the paper.

items.name: Proposition VIII.5.3 ([Don81]): cohomological criterion for good filtrations
items.statement: A G-representation V admits a good filtration if and only if for all λ, one has Hⁱ(G, V ⊗ ∇_λ) = 0 for i > 0.
items.note: LP3 plans "Construct highest-weight modules, Weyl and dual-Weyl modules, good filtrations, the good-filtration t-structure and the relevant Ext-vanishing criteria ... Prove stability under tensor, induction and restriction under the FS VIII.5 hypotheses." Cited. Also defines good filtration dimension: minimal i with H^j(G, V ⊗ ∇_λ) = 0 for all λ, j > i; every finite-dimensional representation has finite good filtration dimension.

items.name: Definition VIII.5.4: the good filtration t-structure
items.statement: Consider the stable ∞-category Ind Perf(∗/G) compactly generated by bounded complexes of G-representations. The good filtration t-structure is defined as follows. (i) M ∈ Ind Perf(∗/G) is connective if for all λ one has Hⁱ(G, M ⊗ ∇_λ) = 0 for i > 0; equivalently, M has good filtration dimension ≤ 0. (ii) M is coconnective if for all λ one has Hⁱ(G, M ⊗ Δ_λ) = 0 for i < 0. Equivalently, the connective part is generated under colimits by the ∇_λ; existence follows from [Lur16, Proposition 1.4.4.11]. Perf(∗/G) ⊂ Ind Perf(∗/G) is not stable under truncations.
items.note: LP3 plans "Construct highest-weight modules, Weyl and dual-Weyl modules, good filtrations, the good-filtration t-structure and the relevant Ext-vanishing criteria ... Prove stability under tensor, induction and restriction under the FS VIII.5 hypotheses."

items.name: Proposition VIII.5.5: the good filtration t-structure is separated
items.statement: The good filtration t-structure on Ind Perf(∗/G) is separated.
items.note: LP3 plans "Construct highest-weight modules, Weyl and dual-Weyl modules, good filtrations, the good-filtration t-structure and the relevant Ext-vanishing criteria ... Prove stability under tensor, induction and restriction under the FS VIII.5 hypotheses." In contrast the standard t-structure on Ind Perf(∗/G) is far from separated (infinite cohomological dimension).

items.name: Theorem VIII.5.6 ([Kop84], [Don88]): O(G) has a good filtration
items.statement: The G × G-representation O(G) (via left and right multiplication) admits a good filtration.
items.note: Cited. LP3 plans "Prove the good-filtration and invariant cohomology results used in VIII.5.1".

items.name: Corollary VIII.5.7: O(Z¹(F_n, G)) has a good filtration
items.statement: For any n ≥ 0 and any map F_n → Aut(G), the G-representation O(Z¹(F_n, G)) admits a good filtration.
items.note: LP3 plans "vanishing of higher group cohomology of the cocycle coordinate algebra". Proof: Z¹(F_n, G) = Gⁿ with simultaneous twisted conjugation; restrict the G^{2n}-good filtration of O(Gⁿ).

items.name: Perf^ind(X/G) (§VIII.5.2)
items.statement: Let X = Spec(A) be an affine scheme of finite type over L with an action of a linear algebraic group G. Perf(X/G) is the stable ∞-category of G-equivariant perfect complexes on X (the dualizable objects of D(X/G)); Perf^ind(X/G) ⊂ Perf(X/G) is the full subcategory generated under cones and retracts by the image of Perf(∗/G).
items.note: LP4 plans "Construct Perf on the finite-wild quotient and its action of Rep(dual G). Prove generation by representation bundles under cones, shifts and retracts, and the comparison of Ind-Perf with module objects over the cocycle algebra in Ind-Perf(B dual G). Establish the finite-free-group colimit theorem". In characteristic ℓ these objects are usually not compact in D(X/G).

items.name: Proposition VIII.5.8: bar-construction criterion for Perf^ind
items.statement: Let X = Spec(A) be an affine scheme of finite type over the algebraically closed field L with an action of a linear algebraic group G. Let M ∈ Perf(X/G), with dual M* and internal endomorphisms M ⊗_A M* ∈ Perf(X/G). Then M ∈ Perf^ind(X/G) if and only if the natural map colim[… → M ⊗_L A ⊗_L M* → M ⊗_L M*] → M ⊗_A M* (a bar construction; tensor products over the base field L) in Ind Perf(∗/G) is an isomorphism.
items.note: LP4 plans "Construct Perf on the finite-wild quotient and its action of Rep(dual G). Prove generation by representation bundles under cones, shifts and retracts, and the comparison of Ind-Perf with module objects over the cocycle algebra in Ind-Perf(B dual G). Establish the finite-free-group colimit theorem". Proof via dualizability in Mod_A(Ind Perf(∗/G)) with compact unit.

items.name: Corollary VIII.5.9: reduction to a Borel
items.statement: Assume that G° is reductive with π₀G of order prime to ℓ, and let B ⊂ G° be a Borel subgroup of G°. Let M ∈ Perf(X/G) and assume that the corresponding object M|_B ∈ Perf(X/B) lies in the subcategory generated under cones and retracts by Perf(∗/B). Then M ∈ Perf^ind(X/G).
items.note: LP4 plans "Construct Perf on the finite-wild quotient and its action of Rep(dual G). Prove generation by representation bundles under cones, shifts and retracts, and the comparison of Ind-Perf with module objects over the cocycle algebra in Ind-Perf(B dual G). Establish the finite-free-group colimit theorem". Uses conservativity of Ind Perf(∗/G) → Ind Perf(∗/G°) and full faithfulness of Perf(∗/G°) → Perf(∗/B) (Kempf vanishing).

items.name: Proposition VIII.5.10: Perf^ind via good filtration dimension
items.statement: Assume that G° is reductive and π₀G of order prime to ℓ, and G acts on X = Spec(A) such that A admits a good G°-filtration. Let M ∈ Perf(X/G) and assume that M, without its A-action, has good G°-filtration dimension ≤ 0. Then M ∈ Perf^ind(X/G) if and only if for all N ∈ Perf(X/G) that have good G°-filtration dimension ≤ 0, also M ⊗_A N has good G°-filtration dimension ≤ 0.
items.note: LP4 plans "Construct Perf on the finite-wild quotient and its action of Rep(dual G). Prove generation by representation bundles under cones, shifts and retracts, and the comparison of Ind-Perf with module objects over the cocycle algebra in Ind-Perf(B dual G). Establish the finite-free-group colimit theorem". Uses [TvdK10, Corollary 1.5] (finite good filtration dimension). Only the easy direction is used, to show necessity of the π₁ hypothesis.

items.name: Proposition VIII.5.11: Perf(G/G) and the fundamental group
items.statement: Assume that G° is reductive and π₀G is of order prime to ℓ. Let G act on itself via conjugation. Let i : ∗ → G be the inclusion of the unit element. The following are equivalent. (i) The order of π₁(G°)_tor is not divisible by ℓ. (ii) The object i_*L ∈ Perf(G/G) lies in Perf^ind(G/G). (iii) The inclusion Perf^ind(G/G) ⊂ Perf(G/G) is an equality.
items.note: LP4 plans "Construct Perf on the finite-wild quotient and its action of Rep(dual G). Prove generation by representation bundles under cones, shifts and retracts, and the comparison of Ind-Perf with module objects over the cocycle algebra in Ind-Perf(B dual G). Establish the finite-free-group colimit theorem". Proof: (ii)⇒(i) via a central extension and the unipotence of the ℓ-primary centre; (i)⇒(ii) via a B-equivariant flag of Cartier divisors X₀ = {1} ⊂ … ⊂ X_{dim G} = G; (ii)⇒(iii) via the diagonal as pullback of i_*L along (g₁,g₂) ↦ g₁g₂⁻¹.

items.name: Proposition VIII.5.12: generation for twisted simultaneous conjugation
items.statement: Assume that G° is reductive and the orders of π₀G and π₁(G°)_tor are not divisible by ℓ. Let Θ₁, …, Θ_n be automorphisms of G, and let G act on Gⁿ via g·(g₁, …, g_n) = (gg₁Θ₁(g)⁻¹, …, gg_nΘ_n(g)⁻¹). Then the inclusion Perf^ind(Gⁿ/_Θ G) ⊂ Perf(Gⁿ/_Θ G) is an equality.
items.note: LP4 plans "Construct Perf on the finite-wild quotient and its action of Rep(dual G). Prove generation by representation bundles under cones, shifts and retracts, and the comparison of Ind-Perf with module objects over the cocycle algebra in Ind-Perf(B dual G). Establish the finite-free-group colimit theorem".

items.name: Proposition VIII.5.13: derived fibres over the unit
items.statement: Consider a derived fibre product X = ∗ ×_G X̃ of affine schemes of finite type over L with G-action, where G carries the adjoint action, i₀ : ∗ → G is the unit and X̃ = Spec(Ã) → G is G-equivariant; X = Spec(A). Assume that G° is reductive, and π₀G and π₁(G°)_tor are of order prime to ℓ. (i) The map L ⊗_{O(G)} Ã → A is an isomorphism in Ind Perf(∗/G), where the tensor product on the left is formed in Ind Perf(∗/G). (ii) Assume in addition that Perf(X̃/G) = Perf^ind(X̃/G) and that Ã lies in the connective part of the good filtration t-structure. Then also A lies in the connective part of the good filtration t-structure, and Perf(X/G) = Perf^ind(X/G).
items.note: LP4 plans "Construct Perf on the finite-wild quotient and its action of Rep(dual G). Prove generation by representation bundles under cones, shifts and retracts, and the comparison of Ind-Perf with module objects over the cocycle algebra in Ind-Perf(B dual G). Establish the finite-free-group colimit theorem". Proof of (ii) uses a separated quotient of Ind Coh(∗ ×_G ∗/G) and generation via the flag of Proposition VIII.5.11.

items.name: Application: L-parameters of a compact Riemann surface and tame parameters
items.statement: For X the fibre product of G^{2g} → G (commutator map) with ∗ → G (the space of L-parameters of a compact Riemann surface of genus g), the preceding propositions show Perf(X/G) = Perf^ind(X/G) and identify A with the excursion algebra; the same argument applies to tame L-parameters of local fields.

items.name: Proposition VIII.5.14: structure of fixed-point subgroups
items.statement: Let L be an algebraically closed field of characteristic ℓ > 0, and let G be a linear algebraic group over L such that G° is reductive and π₀G is of order prime to ℓ. Assume that P is a finite group of order prime to ℓ acting on G and let H = G^P be the fixed points. Then H is a smooth linear algebraic group, H° is reductive, and π₀H is of order prime to ℓ.
items.note: LP3 plans "For a finite group P of order prime to ell acting on a reductive group in characteristic ell, construct the fixed-point subgroup, prove smoothness/reductivity of its identity component and the prime-to-ell component-group order. Under the source's solvability hypothesis prove the Donkin subgroup property and generation of perfect complexes by restriction." Reductivity of H° by [PY02, Theorem 2.1]; π₀H prime to ℓ via [TvdK10, Corollary 1.5] applied to ∏_{P∖{1}} G (for solvable P, Steinberg [Ste68, Theorem 8.1] suffices).

items.name: Theorem VIII.5.15: H° is a Donkin subgroup
items.statement: (Setting of Proposition VIII.5.14, with P solvable.) The subgroup H° ⊂ G° is a Donkin subgroup. In other words, for any representation V of G° that admits a good G°-filtration, also V|_{H°} admits a good H°-filtration. Equivalently, for any representation W of H° that admits a good H°-filtration, also Ind^{G°}_{H°} W admits a good G°-filtration.
items.note: LP3 plans "For a finite group P of order prime to ell acting on a reductive group in characteristic ell, construct the fixed-point subgroup, prove smoothness/reductivity of its identity component and the prime-to-ell component-group order. Under the source's solvability hypothesis prove the Donkin subgroup property and generation of perfect complexes by restriction." Generalizes Levi subgroups and Brundan's conjecture for involutions ([Bru98], [vdK01]); exceptional cases in [HM13]. Proof: reduce to P = ℤ/p, G simple simply connected; O(G/H) has a good filtration via Lemma VIII.5.16; inner case by highest-weight induction; outer case p ∈ {2,3} by the same argument or [Bru98], [vdK01].

items.name: Consequence: centralizers of semisimple elements are Donkin subgroups
items.statement: Levi subgroups are Donkin subgroups, and more generally centralizers of (the paper says: regular) semisimple elements g (of order prime to ℓ in G_ad) define Donkin subgroups; the proof of Theorem VIII.5.15 gives in particular a new proof that Levi subgroups are Donkin subgroups.
items.locator: Chapter VIII, §VIII.5.3, remark after Theorem VIII.5.15, p. 302
items.note: Special case P = ℤ/p acting by an inner automorphism. The word 'regular' is misleading (PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E60): the argument concerns fixed points of an inner automorphism of order p, i.e. centralizers of semisimple elements.

items.name: Lemma VIII.5.16: fixed points via a cosimplicial resolution
items.statement: Let G be a linear algebraic group over an algebraically closed field L of characteristic ℓ such that G° is reductive and π₀G is of order prime to ℓ. Let Θ be an automorphism of G of prime order p ≠ ℓ. Let X = {(g₀, …, g_{p−1}) ∈ G^p | g₀Θ(g₁)⋯Θ^{p−1}(g_{p−1}) = 1} equipped with the G-action of simultaneous Θ-conjugation, and the P = ℤ/pℤ-action of cyclic permutation. Consider the corresponding augmented cosimplicial G-space X^P → X ⇉ ∏_P X …. Then the map colim_{[n]∈Δ^op} O(∏_{P^n} X) → O(X^P) is an isomorphism in Ind Perf(∗/G).
items.note: LP3 plans "For a finite group P of order prime to ell acting on a reductive group in characteristic ell, construct the fixed-point subgroup, prove smoothness/reductivity of its identity component and the prime-to-ell component-group order. Under the source's solvability hypothesis prove the Donkin subgroup property and generation of perfect complexes by restriction." Proof ingredient (not a separately named stage deliverable): formal completion along X^P in IndProPerf(∗/G) (Pro(Rep(G))), idempotence of the completed O(G) at 1, and a (G,P)-equivariant retraction h₀ = (g_{0,0}Θ(g_{1,1})⋯Θ^{p−1}(g_{p−1,p−1}))^{−1/p} g_{0,0} using p-th roots in the formal group Ĝ. Also used for the wild part of Theorem VIII.5.2 (X^P = Z¹(P, G)).

items.name: Proposition VIII.5.17 (i),(ii): converse of the Donkin property
items.statement: In the situation of Theorem VIII.5.15: (i) Let W be a representation of H°. Then W admits a good H°-filtration if and only if Ind^{G°}_{H°} W admits a good G°-filtration. (ii) Let W be a representation of H. Then W admits a good H°-filtration if and only if Ind^G_H W admits a good G°-filtration.
items.note: LP3 plans "For a finite group P of order prime to ell acting on a reductive group in characteristic ell, construct the fixed-point subgroup, prove smoothness/reductivity of its identity component and the prime-to-ell component-group order. Under the source's solvability hypothesis prove the Donkin subgroup property and generation of perfect complexes by restriction."

items.name: Proposition VIII.5.17 (iii),(iv): kernels of the counit
items.statement: In the situation of Theorem VIII.5.15: (iii) Let W be a representation of H° that admits a good H°-filtration. Then the kernel of (Ind^{G°}_{H°} W)|_{H°} → W admits a good H°-filtration. (iv) Let W be a representation of H that admits a good H°-filtration. Then the kernel of (Ind^G_H W)|_H → W admits a good H°-filtration.
items.note: LP3 plans "For a finite group P of order prime to ell acting on a reductive group in characteristic ell, construct the fixed-point subgroup, prove smoothness/reductivity of its identity component and the prime-to-ell component-group order. Under the source's solvability hypothesis prove the Donkin subgroup property and generation of perfect complexes by restriction."

items.name: Proposition VIII.5.17 (v),(vi): generation of Perf(∗/H) by restriction
items.statement: In the situation of Theorem VIII.5.15: (v) The image of the restriction Perf(∗/G°) → Perf(∗/H°) generates under cones and retracts. (vi) The image of the restriction Perf(∗/G) → Perf(∗/H) generates under cones and retracts.
items.note: LP3 plans "For a finite group P of order prime to ell acting on a reductive group in characteristic ell, construct the fixed-point subgroup, prove smoothness/reductivity of its identity component and the prime-to-ell component-group order. Under the source's solvability hypothesis prove the Donkin subgroup property and generation of perfect complexes by restriction."
