Proof: (i),(iii),(v) equivalent, (ii),(iv),(vi) equivalent, (vi)⇒(v), and all six equivalent for connected G; then induction on P, highest weights for simply connected G, dévissage through the simply connected cover and G/G′. An earlier version proved (vi) by case analysis.

items.name: Remark VIII.5.18: necessity of |P| prime to ℓ and dependence on the centre
items.statement: If G = (SL₂ × SL₂)/μ₂ with the automorphism switching the two factors, then H = PGL₂ × (μ₂ × μ₂)/μ₂. If ℓ = 2, then for all objects A ∈ Perf(∗/H) in the image of Perf(∗/G), the summand A₁ of A with nontrivial central character has perfect homotopy invariants under ℤ/2ℤ ⊂ PGL₂; hence the nontrivial character of H is not generated by Perf(∗/G) under cones and retracts. So the hypothesis that P is of order prime to ℓ cannot be weakened to quasi-semisimple or pinning-preserving automorphisms, and the precise form of the centre matters.
items.note: Planned by the accepted decomposition node LanglandsParameterStacks:LP3/donkin-subgroup-and-generation (data/decompositions/LanglandsParameterStacks.json, parentStageId LanglandsParameterStacks:LP3, review accepted 2026-09-16), whose statement includes 'Remark VIII.5.18 shows the prime-to-l hypothesis on |P| cannot be weakened ... for G = (SL_2 x SL_2)/mu_2 with the switching automorphism, H = PGL_2 x (mu_2 x mu_2)/mu_2, and if l = 2 the nontrivial character of H is NOT generated by Perf(*/G)' and whose acceptance list has 'Reproduce the characteristic-two example'. Footnote 3 sketches the argument via Steinberg's tensor product description of irreducible SL₂-representations in characteristic 2.

items.name: Proposition VIII.5.19: π₁ of fixed points
items.statement: Assume that G° is reductive and that P is a finite solvable group of order prime to ℓ acting on G with fixed points H = G^P. If π₁(G°)_tor is of order prime to ℓ, then also π₁(H°)_tor is of order prime to ℓ.
items.note: Planned by the accepted decomposition node LanglandsParameterStacks:LP3/fixed-points-of-prime-to-l-group-actions (data/decompositions/LanglandsParameterStacks.json, parentStageId LanglandsParameterStacks:LP3, review accepted 2026-09-16), titled 'FS VIII.5.14 and VIII.5.19' and stating 'Moreover (VIII.5.19), if P is in addition SOLVABLE and pi_1(G^circ)_tors has order prime to l, then also pi_1(H^circ)_tors has order prime to l', with the case-by-case proof as a proof step; the decomposition review corrected its locator to p. 310. Proof is a case check over simple types (Levi subgroups, classical fixed groups, triality, exceptional cases via [vdK01], [Spr87], [HM13, Theorem 4.3.3]); 'inner involutions ... of prime order p > 2' on p. 311 is PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E64.

items.name: The functor S ↦ Ind Perf(Map^Σ_{∗/W}(S, 𝒢)) (§VIII.5.4)
items.statement: Let W be a discrete group and 𝒢 → ∗/W a stack whose pullback along ∗ → ∗/W is a finite disjoint union of classifying stacks of linear algebraic groups G over L with G° reductive and π₀G of order prime to ℓ (e.g. a gerbe given by an extension 1 → G → ℰ_𝒢 → W → 1). For anima S over ∗/W consider the derived fpqc stack Map_{∗/W}(S, 𝒢) and Ind Perf(Map_{∗/W}(S, 𝒢)). Restricted to finite sets with a W-torsor (compact projective generators) this commutes with finite coproducts, since Ind Perf(∗/G) ⊗_{D(L)} Ind Perf(∗/H) ≅ Ind Perf(∗/G × H) (by highest weight theory); its left Kan extension is S ↦ Ind Perf(Map^Σ_{∗/W}(S, 𝒢)), with a comparison map Ind Perf(Map^Σ_{∗/W}(S, 𝒢)) → Ind Perf(Map_{∗/W}(S, 𝒢)).
items.note: LP4 plans "Construct Perf on the finite-wild quotient and its action of Rep(dual G). Prove generation by representation bundles under cones, shifts and retracts, and the comparison of Ind-Perf with module objects over the cocycle algebra in Ind-Perf(B dual G). Establish the finite-free-group colimit theorem". LP4 also: "and its universal property for exact monoidal functors". The Künneth-type equivalence is asserted with a one-line proof sketch.

items.name: Proposition VIII.5.20: the case of free groups
items.statement: In this situation (S = ∗/F_n → ∗/W for a finite free group F_n with a map F_n → W, 𝒢 connected, so Map_{∗/W}(∗/F_n, 𝒢) = ∏_{i=1}^n π⁻¹(γ_i)/G with simultaneous conjugation), the functor Ind Perf(Map^Σ_{∗/W}(∗/F_n, 𝒢)) → Ind Perf(Map_{∗/W}(∗/F_n, 𝒢)) is fully faithful and the essential image is the full subcategory generated under colimits by Ind Perf(∗/G), which is equivalent to the category of O(∏_{i=1}^n π⁻¹(γ_i))-modules in Ind Perf(∗/G). If π₁(G°)_tor is of order prime to ℓ, the displayed functor is an equivalence. (An obvious variant holds if 𝒢 ×_{∗/W} ∗ is a finite disjoint union of such gerbes.)
items.note: LP4 plans "Construct Perf on the finite-wild quotient and its action of Rep(dual G). Prove generation by representation bundles under cones, shifts and retracts, and the comparison of Ind-Perf with module objects over the cocycle algebra in Ind-Perf(B dual G). Establish the finite-free-group colimit theorem". Uses Barr–Beck and Proposition VIII.5.12.

items.name: Theorem VIII.5.2 in the tame case (§VIII.5.4)
items.statement: For W = ℤ[1/p] ⋊ ℤ (a discretization of the tame quotient) and 𝒢 over ∗/W with 𝒢 ×_{∗/W} ∗ a finite disjoint union of classifying stacks of groups G with G° reductive and π₀G, π₁(G°)_tor of order prime to ℓ, the functor Ind Perf(Map^Σ_{∗/W}(∗/W, 𝒢)) → Ind Perf(Map_{∗/W}(∗/W, 𝒢)) is an equivalence. Equivalently (writing ∗/W as the pushout of ∗ ← ∗/ℤ → ∗/F₂ along σ⁻¹τστ^{−q}), Ind Perf(∗/G) ⊗_{Ind Perf(G/_{ad}G)} Ind Perf((G × G)/_{(σ,τ)}G) → Ind Perf(Z¹(W, G)/G) is an equivalence, Z¹(W, G) being the fibre of (g, h) ↦ g⁻¹hgh^{−q} over 1.
items.note: LP4 plans "Construct Perf on the finite-wild quotient and its action of Rep(dual G). Prove generation by representation bundles under cones, shifts and retracts, and the comparison of Ind-Perf with module objects over the cocycle algebra in Ind-Perf(B dual G). Establish the finite-free-group colimit theorem". Follows from Propositions VIII.5.11–VIII.5.13. Full faithfulness is the colimit isomorphism; essential surjectivity is generation of Perf(Z¹(W, G)/G) by Perf(∗/G).

items.name: Proposition VIII.5.21: pushing forward along the wild quotient
items.statement: Let P be a finite solvable group of order prime to ℓ with a map P → W. Assume that 𝒢 is a stack over ∗/W such that 𝒢 ×_{∗/W} ∗ is a finite disjoint union of classifying stacks of linear-algebraic groups G with G° reductive and π₀G of order prime to ℓ. Then the pushforward 𝒢^t of 𝒢 along ∗/W → ∗/W^t, where W^t = W/P, has pullback along ∗ → ∗/W^t given by Map_{∗/W}(∗/P, 𝒢), and this is again a finite disjoint union of classifying stacks of linear-algebraic groups H with H° reductive and π₀H of order prime to ℓ. Moreover, the functor Ind Perf(Map^Σ_{∗/W}(∗/P, 𝒢)) → Ind Perf(Map_{∗/W}(∗/P, 𝒢)) is an equivalence. If all G appearing in 𝒢 ×_{∗/W} ∗ have π₁(G°)_tor of order prime to ℓ, then the same holds true for the groups H appearing in 𝒢^t ×_{∗/W^t} ∗.
items.note: LP4 plans "Construct Perf on the finite-wild quotient and its action of Rep(dual G). Prove generation by representation bundles under cones, shifts and retracts, and the comparison of Ind-Perf with module objects over the cocycle algebra in Ind-Perf(B dual G). Establish the finite-free-group colimit theorem". For P = ℤ/p uses Lemma VIII.5.16 (X^P = Z¹(P, G)), Proposition VIII.5.17 (essential surjectivity) and Proposition VIII.5.19 (π₁); general solvable P by induction on a normal series. Haboush is used for the empty (non-split) case. Wild inertia P is a p-group, hence solvable and of order prime to ℓ.

items.name: End of proof of Theorem VIII.5.2: reduction to the tame case
items.statement: If W is a discretization of W_E and P ⊂ W its wild part (a finite p-group, normal in W), let 𝒢^t be the pushforward of 𝒢 along ∗/W → ∗/W^t, W^t = W/P; its pullback along ∗ → ∗/W^t is Map_{∗/W}(∗/P, 𝒢). Replacing (W, 𝒢) by (W^t, 𝒢^t) reduces Theorem VIII.5.2 to the tame case.
items.note: LP4 plans "Construct Perf on the finite-wild quotient and its action of Rep(dual G). Prove generation by representation bundles under cones, shifts and retracts, and the comparison of Ind-Perf with module objects over the cocycle algebra in Ind-Perf(B dual G). Establish the finite-free-group colimit theorem".

items.name: Hecke operator T_V for torsion coefficients
items.statement: Let E be a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q of characteristic p, G reductive over E, Λ a Z_ℓ[√q]-algebra killed by a power of ℓ, Q a finite quotient of W_E over which the action on Ĝ factors. For a finite set I and V ∈ Rep_Λ(Ĝ ⋊ Q)^I let S_V be the perverse (Satake) sheaf on the local Hecke stack Hck^{loc,I}_G, and write S_V also for its pullback to the global Hecke stack Hck^{glob,I}_G. Using the correspondence Bun_G ←p₁— Hck^{glob,I}_G —p₂→ Bun_G × (Div¹)^I, define T_V : D_ét(Bun_G, Λ) → D_ét(Bun_G × (Div¹)^I, Λ), A ↦ Rp₂*(p₁*A ⊗^L_Λ S_V). By Corollary IV.7.2 the target contains D_ét(Bun_G × [∗/W_E^I], Λ) ≅ D_ét(Bun_G, Λ)^{BW_E^I} (W_E^I-equivariant objects of the condensed ∞-category D_ét(Bun_G, Λ)) as a full subcategory, and T_V factors over it.
items.note: HS1 plans this: 'Pull the Satake sheaf attached to a finite projective representation V of the appropriate dual L-group to the Hecke stack and define T_V by the actual pull-tensor-push construction.' Uses geometric Satake (Ch. VI) and Drinfeld's lemma (Cor. IV.7.2). The general (non-torsion) version is IX.2.

items.name: Theorem IX.0.1(i): Hecke operators preserve limits, colimits, compact and ULA objects; duality
items.statement: For any Z_ℓ[√q]-algebra Λ, finite set I and V ∈ Rep_Λ(Ĝ ⋊ Q)^I there is a natural Hecke operator T_V : D_lis(Bun_G, Λ) → D_lis(Bun_G, Λ)^{BW_E^I}. Forgetting the W_E^I-action, i.e. as an endofunctor of D_lis(Bun_G, Λ), T_V commutes with all limits and colimits and preserves compact objects and universally locally acyclic objects. With sw* : Rep_Λ Ĝ^I → Rep_Λ Ĝ^I the involution of Proposition VI.12.1, there are natural isomorphisms 𝔻_BZ(T_V(A)) ≅ T_{sw*V^∨}(𝔻_BZ(A)) and R𝓗om_lis(T_V(A), Λ) ≅ T_{sw*V^∨} R𝓗om_lis(A, Λ).
items.locator: Chapter IX, Theorem IX.0.1(i), pp. 317–318 (proved as Theorem IX.2.2, Corollary IX.2.4)
items.note: Summary statement; the proofs are Theorem IX.2.2 and Corollary IX.2.3/IX.2.4 (items c9-...-IX.2.2-*). HS1: 'Prove preservation of D_lis, compact objects and ULA objects in the source's range'. Duality part uses VS5 (Bernstein–Zelevinsky duality).

items.name: Theorem IX.0.1(ii): monoidal Hecke action with finite wild ramification per compact object
items.statement: As a functor of V, the Hecke operators induce an exact Rep_Λ(Q^I)-linear monoidal functor Rep_Λ(Ĝ ⋊ Q)^I → End_Λ(D_lis(Bun_G, Λ)^ω)^{BW_E^I}, where the target denotes W_E^I-equivariant objects inside the condensed ∞-category End_Λ(D_lis(Bun_G, Λ)^ω) (with trivial W_E^I-action). Moreover, for any compact X ∈ D_lis(Bun_G, Λ)^ω there is an open subgroup P of the wild inertia subgroup of W_E such that for all I and V the P^I-action on T_V(X) is trivial. In particular D_lis(Bun_G, Λ)^ω is an increasing union of full stable ∞-subcategories D^P_lis(Bun_G, Λ)^ω such that the Hecke action defines functors Rep_Λ(Ĝ ⋊ Q)^I → End_Λ(D^P_lis(Bun_G, Λ)^ω)^{B(W_E/P)^I}.
items.locator: Chapter IX, Theorem IX.0.1(ii), p. 318 (proved as Corollary IX.2.4 and Proposition IX.5.1)
items.note: HS1 constructs the W_E^I-equivariant family; the finite-wild part is ES1:finite-ramification: 'prove IX.5.1's single wild subgroup P for all representations V and finite leg sets on each compact A'. Input to Theorem VIII.4.1 (excursion operators).

items.name: Theorem IX.0.1(iii): functoriality in I
items.statement: Varying I, the functors Rep_Λ(Ĝ ⋊ Q)^I → End_Λ(D_lis(Bun_G, Λ)^ω)^{BW_E^I} of (ii) are functorial in I: treating the objects as coCartesian fibrations over the category of finite sets, the functors lift to the total spaces of these coCartesian fibrations.
items.note: HS1: 'tensor/convolution composition and fusion across arbitrary finite sets'; HS4: 'fusion along every finite-set map'. The coCartesian-fibration formulation is what Theorem VIII.4.1 and Theorem X.0.1 consume.

items.name: Definition IX.0.2(i): Bernstein center of G(E)
items.statement: The Bernstein center of G(E) is Z(G(E), Λ) = π₀End(id_{D(G(E),Λ)}) = lim_{←, K⊂G(E)} Z(Λ[K\G(E)/K]), where K runs over open pro-p subgroups of G(E), and Λ[K\G(E)/K] = End_{G(E)}(c-Ind_K^{G(E)} Λ) is the Hecke algebra of level K.
items.note: ES0: 'Define the algebra of natural endomorphisms of the identity ... Compare the degree-zero center with the ordinary smooth-representation Bernstein center'; SR.1 owns Hecke algebras over rings; SR.3 constructs the classical (complex) Bernstein center. Target of Ψ_G.

items.name: Definition IX.0.2(ii): geometric Bernstein center and its Hecke-commuting subring
items.statement: The geometric Bernstein center of G is Z^geom(G, Λ) = π₀End(id_{D_lis(Bun_G,Λ)}). Inside it, Z^geom_Hecke(G, Λ) is the subring of all endomorphisms f : id → id commuting with Hecke operators, in the sense that for all V ∈ Rep(Ĝ^I) and A ∈ D_lis(Bun_G, Λ) one has T_V(f(A)) = f(T_V(A)) ∈ End(T_V(A)).
items.note: ES0: 'Define the algebra of natural endomorphisms of the identity, its centrality and scalar structure on the chosen enhanced category.' ES1:spectral-center: 'Prove compatibility with Hecke functors'.

items.name: Definition IX.0.2(iii): spectral Bernstein center
items.statement: The spectral Bernstein center of G is Z^spec(G, Λ) = 𝒪(Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)_Λ)^Ĝ, the ring of global functions on Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)_Λ ⫽ Ĝ.
items.note: LP2:integral-invariants: 'Construct the invariant algebr[a]'; ES1:spectral-center: 'use LP2:integral-invariants to construct the map from functions on the parameter stack to the categorical center'. Z¹(W_E, Ĝ) is from Chapter VIII.

items.name: Map Z^geom(G,Λ) → Z(G(E),Λ)
items.statement: The fully faithful inclusion D(G(E), Λ) ↪ D_lis(Bun_G, Λ) (extension by zero from the open stratum Bun_G^1 ≅ [∗/G(E)]) induces a map of algebras Z^geom(G, Λ) → Z(G(E), Λ) to the usual Bernstein center of smooth G(E)-representations on Λ-modules.
items.locator: Chapter IX, p. 318 (after Definition IX.0.2) and p. 329
items.note: ES0 'Compare the degree-zero center with the ordinary smooth-representation Bernstein center'; ES7:parabolic 'Construct Ψ_G and Ψ_G^b from ES1:spectral-center and VS4's stratum embeddings'. Uses Chapter V/VII identification D_lis(Bun_G^1) ≅ D(G(E), Λ).

items.name: Corollary IX.0.3: map Ψ_G from the spectral to the Bernstein center
items.statement: Assume that the order of π₀Z(G) is invertible in Λ. There is a canonical map Z^spec(G, Λ) → Z^geom_Hecke(G, Λ) ⊂ Z^geom(G, Λ), and in particular a map Ψ_G : Z^spec(G, Λ) → Z(G(E), Λ).
items.locator: Chapter IX, Corollary IX.0.3, p. 319 (proved as Theorem IX.5.2 and Definition IX.7.1)
items.note: ES1:spectral-center: 'When |π₀Z(G)| is invertible in Λ, use LP2:integral-invariants to construct the map from functions on the parameter stack to the categorical center, then to the relevant Bernstein center'. Uses Theorem VIII.3.6 (Exc ⊗ Λ ≅ invariants) and Theorem VIII.4.1.

items.name: Theorem IX.0.5(i): tori
items.statement: If G = T is a torus, then π ↦ φ_π is the usual Langlands correspondence.
items.locator: Chapter IX, Theorem IX.0.5(i), p. 319; proved in Proposition IX.6.5 (§IX.6.4)
items.note: ES6:functoriality: 'Prove the spectral-to-geometric torus center map is diagonal and φ_χ equals local class field theory with the fixed geometric-Frobenius normalization.' Summary statement of the introduction to Chapter IX.

items.name: Theorem IX.0.5(ii): twisting
items.statement: The correspondence π ↦ φ_π is compatible with twisting.
items.locator: Chapter IX, Theorem IX.0.5(ii), p. 319; proved in §IX.6.4, final paragraph (Theorem IX.6.1 applied to G → G × D, D = G/G_der)
items.note: ES6:functoriality: 'Derive twisting through G→G×(G/G_der)'. Summary statement of the introduction to Chapter IX.

items.name: Theorem IX.0.5(iii): central characters
items.statement: The correspondence π ↦ φ_π is compatible with central characters (cf. [Bor79, 10.1]).
items.locator: Chapter IX, Theorem IX.0.5(iii), p. 319; proved in §IX.6.4, final paragraph (Theorem IX.6.1 for Z × G → G; z-extensions [Kal18, §5])
items.note: ES6:functoriality: 'central-character compatibility through Z×G→G; for disconnected center construct and compare z-embeddings'. Summary statement of the introduction to Chapter IX.

items.name: Theorem IX.0.5(iv): contragredients
items.statement: The correspondence π ↦ φ_π is compatible with passage to contragredients (printed 'congradients') (cf. [AV16]).
items.locator: Chapter IX, Theorem IX.0.5(iv), p. 319; proved in Proposition IX.5.3
items.note: ES6:duality: 'prove IX.5.3 for the Bernstein–Zelevinsky dual and hence parameters of supercuspidal smooth duals'. The dual parameter involves the Chevalley involution; [AV16] fixes the expected formula. Summary statement of the introduction to Chapter IX.

items.name: Theorem IX.0.5(v): isogenies
items.statement: If G′ → G is a map of reductive groups inducing an isomorphism of adjoint groups, π is an irreducible smooth representation of G(E) and π′ is an irreducible constituent of π|_{G′(E)}, then φ_{π′} is the image of φ_π under the induced map Ĝ → Ĝ′.
items.locator: Chapter IX, Theorem IX.0.5(v), p. 319; proved in Theorem IX.6.1
items.note: ES6:functoriality: 'For G'→G inducing an adjoint-group isomorphism, parameters of Schur-irreducible constituents of pullback are composed with dual G→dual G''. Summary statement of the introduction to Chapter IX.

items.name: Theorem IX.0.5(vi): products
items.statement: If G = G₁ × G₂ is a product of two groups and π is an irreducible smooth representation of G(E), then π = π₁ ⊠ π₂ for irreducible smooth representations π_i of G_i(E), and φ_π = φ_{π₁} × φ_{π₂} under Ĝ = Ĝ₁ × Ĝ₂.
items.locator: Chapter IX, Theorem IX.0.5(vi), p. 319; proved in Proposition IX.6.2
items.note: ES6:functoriality: 'Product groups give product parameters'. The decomposition π = π₁ ⊠ π₂ is a classical representation-theoretic input. Summary statement of the introduction to Chapter IX.

items.name: Theorem IX.0.5(vii): weil restriction
items.statement: If G = Res_{E′|E} G′ is the Weil restriction of scalars of a reductive group G′ over some finite separable extension E′|E, so that G(E) = G′(E′), then L-parameters for G|E agree with L-parameters for G′|E′.
items.locator: Chapter IX, Theorem IX.0.5(vii), p. 319; proved in Proposition IX.6.3
items.note: ES6:functoriality: 'For finite separable E'/E and G=Res_(E'/E)G', construct nonabelian Shapiro equivalence...' Summary statement of the introduction to Chapter IX.

items.name: Theorem IX.0.5(viii): parabolic induction
items.statement: The correspondence π ↦ φ_π is compatible with parabolic induction.
items.locator: Chapter IX, Theorem IX.0.5(viii), p. 319; proved in Corollary IX.7.3
items.note: ES7:parabolic: 'Deduce IX.7.3 for unnormalized parabolic induction and every irreducible subquotient.' The precise form involves the cyclotomic twist of the Levi embedding (IX.7.1). Summary statement of the introduction to Chapter IX.

items.name: Theorem IX.0.5(ix): GLn
items.statement: For G = GL_n and supercuspidal π, the correspondence π ↦ φ_π agrees with the usual local Langlands correspondence [LRS93], [HT01], [Hen00].
items.locator: Chapter IX, Theorem IX.0.5(ix), p. 319; proved in Theorem IX.7.4
items.note: ES7:GLn-comparison / ES7:equal-characteristic. Theorem IX.7.4 proves more: all irreducible smooth Q̄_ℓ-representations, semisimplified parameter. Summary statement of the introduction to Chapter IX.

items.name: Condensed ∞-category structure on D■(Bun_G,Λ) and D_lis(Bun_G,Λ)
items.statement: To an extremally disconnected profinite set S associate the ∞-category D■(Bun_G × S, Λ); this defines a condensed ∞-category D■(Bun_G, Λ) (a hypersheaf in S, by v-hyperdescent of D■(X, Λ), deduced from the case of D(X_v, Λ)), and S ↦ D_lis(Bun_G × S, Λ) is a full condensed ∞-subcategory. By descent D■(Bun_G × [∗/W_E^I], Λ) ≅ D■(Bun_G, Λ)^{BW_E^I}, the evaluation of the condensed ∞-category on the condensed anima BW_E^I; concretely, objects A ∈ D■(Bun_G, Λ) with a map of condensed animated groups W_E^I → Aut(A). Only the structure of an ∞-category enriched in condensed anima is needed; it induces the same structure on D_lis(Bun_G, Λ).
items.note: HS1: 'Construct the continuous W_E^I action through Drinfeld's lemma and the condensed enriched functor category; a discrete abstract action without continuity is insufficient'. Uses D■ from Ch. VII (VS2) and Clausen–Scholze condensed mathematics [CS]. Mathlib has condensed sets/modules (Condensed, CondensedMod) but no condensed ∞-categories.

items.name: Proposition IX.1.1: W_E^I-equivariant lisse sheaves embed into D■(Bun_G×(Div¹)^I)
items.statement: Pullback under Bun_G × (Div¹)^I → Bun_G × [∗/W_E^I] induces a fully faithful functor D_lis(Bun_G, Λ)^{BW_E^I} ↪ D■(Bun_G, Λ)^{BW_E^I} ≅ D■(Bun_G × [∗/W_E^I], Λ) ↪ D■(Bun_G × (Div¹)^I, Λ). The essential image of the first functor consists of all objects A ∈ D■(Bun_G × [∗/W_E^I], Λ) whose pullback to Bun_G lies in D_lis(Bun_G, Λ).
items.note: Stated as following directly from the discussion (Corollary IV.7.2-type Drinfeld lemma). Used in Corollary IX.2.3. HS1 plans the condensed W_E^I-action.

items.name: Proposition IX.1.2: condensed Hom out of compact objects is relatively discrete
items.statement: For A ∈ D_lis(Bun_G, Λ)^ω and B ∈ D_lis(Bun_G, Λ), the condensed animated Λ-module Hom_{D_lis(Bun_G,Λ)}(A, B) is relatively discrete over Z_ℓ. Consequently the condensed structure on D_lis(Bun_G, Λ) is the relatively discrete one on compact objects, and in general induced from it.
items.note: Proof: reduce to A = f_{K♮} Z_ℓ for the charts f_K : M̃_b/K → Bun_G (K ⊂ G_b(E) open pro-p); RΓ(M̃_b/K, B′) → RΓ([∗/K], B′) is an isomorphism with condensed structure (proof of Prop. VII.7.2 plus Thm VII.2.10), and RΓ([∗/K], B′) is a summand of a stalk. Enables Corollary IX.2.4. Falls under HS1's 'condensed enriched functor category'; VS4 supplies the charts.

items.name: Solid Satake kernels V ↦ S′_V on the Hecke stack
items.statement: Geometric Satake gives exact Rep_{Z_ℓ[√q]}(Q^I)-linear monoidal functors Rep_{Z_ℓ[√q]}(Ĝ ⋊ Q)^I → Sat(Hck_G^I, Z_ℓ[√q]), V ↦ S_V (inverse limit over n of the Z/ℓ^n[√q] categories), functorial in I. Composing with A ↦ D(A)^∨ (Verdier duality relative to Hck_G^I → [(Div¹)^I/L⁺G]) gives exact monoidal functors Rep_{Z_ℓ[√q]}(Ĝ ⋊ Q)^I → D■(Hck_G^I, Z_ℓ[√q]) (convolution of §VII.5 on the target; monoidal as an ∞-functor since the D■ convolution uses only pullback, tensor product and ♮-pushforward). This extends by linearity uniquely to an exact Rep_Λ(Q^I)-linear monoidal functor Rep_Λ(Ĝ ⋊ Q)^I → D■(Hck_G^I, Λ), V ↦ S′_V, using highest weight theory: Perf(B(Ĝ ⋊ Q)^I_{Z_ℓ[√q]}) ⊗_{Perf(BQ^I_{Z_ℓ[√q]})} Perf(∗/Q^I_Λ) ≅ Perf(∗/(Ĝ ⋊ Q)^I_Λ), and Perf(∗/(Ĝ ⋊ Q)^I_Λ) is the free stable ∞-category with an exact functor from Rep_Λ(Ĝ ⋊ Q)^I; then pull back to the global Hecke stack.
items.note: HS1: 'Show that the kernel lies in the required dualizable/ULA category'; 'use the partial-support or relative-homology operation specified by FS IX.2 when the naive ECD lower shriek is unavailable'. Inputs: Section VI.7 (Satake category), Section VII.5 (solid convolution), Proposition VII.5.2.

items.name: Hecke operator T_V for general Z_ℓ[√q]-algebras Λ
items.statement: There is a natural exact Rep_Λ(Q^I)-linear monoidal functor D■(Hck_G^I, Λ) → End_{D■((Div¹)^I,Λ)}(D■(Bun_G × (Div¹)^I, Λ)) (D■((Div¹)^I, Λ)-linear endofunctors). Any V ∈ Rep_Λ(Ĝ ⋊ Q)^I gives T_V : D_lis(Bun_G, Λ) → D■(Bun_G × (Div¹)^I, Λ), T_V(A) = p_{2♮}(p₁*A ⊗■^L_Λ S′_V) for Bun_G ←p₁— Hck_G^I —p₂→ Bun_G × (Div¹)^I. After pullback to the diagonal geometric point Spd C → (Div¹)^I (C = Ê̄), the functor depends only on the composite Rep_Λ(Ĝ ⋊ Q)^I → D■(Hck_G^I ×_{(Div¹)^I} Spd C, Λ), which factors naturally over Rep_Λ(Ĝ^I).
items.note: HS1: 'define T_V by the actual pull-tensor-push construction'. Extends the torsion-coefficient Hecke operators via Proposition VII.5.2.

items.name: Proposition IX.2.1: Hecke operators preserve D_lis
items.statement: For any V ∈ Rep_Λ(Ĝ^I), the functor T_V : D■(Bun_G × Spd C, Λ) → D■(Bun_G × Spd C, Λ) restricts to a functor T_V : D_lis(Bun_G, Λ) → D_lis(Bun_G, Λ).
items.note: Proof: reduce by highest weight theory and monoidality to I = {∗}; the ULA objects B on Hck_{G,Spd C}/Div¹_X are generated under colimits by Rf_{ẇ∗}Z_ℓ for Demazure resolutions f_ẇ : L⁺I\Dem_ẇ → Hck; by Proposition VII.4.3 reduce to the proper, cohomologically smooth Demazure correspondence on Bun_{G,C}. HS1: 'Prove preservation of D_lis'.

items.name: Theorem IX.2.2 (first part): T_V preserves limits, colimits, compact and ULA objects
items.statement: For any V ∈ Rep_Λ(Ĝ^I), the action of T_V on D_lis(Bun_G, Λ) preserves all limits and colimits, and the full subcategories of compact objects and of universally locally acyclic objects.
items.note: Proof: V is dualizable in the Satake category with dual V^∨, so T_V has left and right adjoint T_{V^∨}; ULA preservation by adjointness since A is ULA iff RHom_Λ(B, A) is perfect for all compact B (Proposition VII.7.9). HS1: 'Prove preservation of D_lis, compact objects and ULA objects in the source's range'. Key input for IX.3 finiteness.

items.name: Theorem IX.2.2 (second part): Hecke operators and duality
items.statement: For the automorphism sw* of Rep_Λ(Ĝ^I) given by Proposition VI.12.1, there are natural isomorphisms 𝔻_BZ(T_V(A)) ≅ T_{sw*V^∨}(𝔻_BZ(A)) and R𝓗om_lis(T_V(A), Λ) ≅ T_{sw*V^∨} R𝓗om_lis(A, Λ).
items.note: Proof from π_♮(T_V(A) ⊗■^L_Λ B) ≅ π_♮(A ⊗■^L_Λ T_{sw*V}(B)) for π : Bun_G → ∗ (both are homology of Hck_G^I ×_{(Div¹)^I} Spd C with coefficients h₁*A ⊗ h₂*B ⊗ S′_V) and Proposition VI.12.1, plus adjunctions. VS5 (BZ duality) with HS1; the Chevalley/sw comparison is GS4 per ES6:duality.

items.name: Corollary IX.2.3: T_V lands in W_E^I-equivariant lisse sheaves
items.statement: For any V ∈ Rep_Λ(Ĝ ⋊ Q)^I, the functor T_V : D_lis(Bun_G, Λ) → D■(Bun_G × (Div¹_X)^I, Λ) takes image in the full subcategory D■(Bun_G × [∗/W_E^I], Λ); moreover all objects in the image have pullback to D■(Bun_G, Λ) lying in D_lis(Bun_G, Λ), so by Proposition IX.1.1 T_V induces a functor D_lis(Bun_G, Λ) → D_lis(Bun_G, Λ)^{BW_E^I}.
items.note: Proof: reduce to exterior tensor products (possibly infinite resolutions involving finitely many weights) and I = {∗}; use Corollary VII.2.7, Proposition IX.2.1 and Proposition VII.7.3 (D_lis(Bun_G) → D_lis(Bun_G × Spd C) equivalence). HS1 (Drinfeld lemma / W_E^I action).

items.name: Corollary IX.2.4: the Hecke action
items.statement: Endowing the stable Z_ℓ-linear ∞-category D_lis(Bun_G, Λ)^ω with the relatively discrete condensed structure, the Hecke action defines exact Rep_Λ(Q^I)-linear monoidal functors Rep_Λ(Ĝ ⋊ Q)^I → End_Λ(D_lis(Bun_G, Λ)^ω)^{BW_E^I}, functorially in I.
items.note: Combines IX.1.2, IX.2.2, IX.2.3. This is the input datum to Theorem VIII.4.1 (excursion operators) and Theorem X.0.1 (spectral action). HS1/HS4.

items.name: Compactly supported cohomology of local Shimura varieties (after Huber)
items.statement: Specialise the base field to Q_p, the standard setting of local Shimura varieties; from here on the letter E denotes the reflex field (the paper's 'small sin' of reusing the letter). A local Shimura datum is a reductive group G over Q_p, a conjugacy class μ of minuscule cocharacters G_m → G_{Q̄_p} with field of definition E|Q_p, and b ∈ B(G, μ) ⊂ B(G). By [SW20, Lecture 24] there is a tower (M_{(G,b,μ),K})_{K⊂G(Q_p)} of partially proper smooth rigid-analytic spaces over Ĕ with a Weil descent datum, each with a G_b(Q_p)-action and the tower with a G(Q_p)-action. Following Huber, define RΓ_c(M_{(G,b,μ),K,C}, Z_ℓ) = lim_{→,U} RΓ_c(U, Z_ℓ) over quasicompact open U ⊂ M_{(G,b,μ),K,C}, where RΓ_c(U, Z_ℓ) = lim_{←,m} RΓ_c(U, Z/ℓ^m Z); it carries actions of G_b(Q_p) and of W_E.
items.note: HS3: 'Define compactly supported complexes with Satake coefficients at finite level and the colimit over levels, with commuting J_b(E), J_b'(E) and Weil actions.' HS2 owns the moduli; [SW20] Lectures 23–24 and [Hub98] are cited inputs.

items.name: Theorem IX.3.1: finiteness of cohomology of local Shimura varieties
items.statement: The complex RΓ_c(M_{(G,b,μ),K,C}, Z_ℓ) is naturally a complex of smooth G_b(Q_p)-representations, and, if K is pro-p, a compact object in D(G_b(Q_p), Z_ℓ). Moreover, the action of W_E is continuous. In particular each H^i_c(M_{(G,b,μ),K,C}, Z_ℓ) is a finitely generated smooth G_b(Q_p)-representation; by descent this holds for all K (not necessarily pro-p).
items.locator: Chapter IX, §IX.3, Theorem IX.3.1, p. 324 (and the sentence following it)
items.note: Unconditional proof/refinement of [RV14, §6]. Proof: up to shift RΓ_c ≅ H(f_{K♮}Z_ℓ) (Proposition VII.5.2); identify with i^{b*}T_μ(j_! c-Ind_K^{G(Q_p)} Z_ℓ) via [SW20, Lectures 23–24]; compactness from Theorem IX.2.2 and Proposition VII.7.4; continuity from descent to Spd E/φ^Z. HS3: 'Source IX.3.1's integral pro-p-level compactness'.

items.name: R Hom from local Shimura cohomology into admissible representations
items.statement: For each admissible representation ρ of G_b(Q_p) on a Z_ℓ-algebra Λ, R Hom_{G_b(Q_p)}(RΓ_c(M_{(G,b,μ),K,C}, Z_ℓ), ρ) is a perfect complex of Λ-modules. Passing to the colimit over K, colim_K R Hom_{G_b(Q_p)}(RΓ_c(M_{(G,b,μ),K,C}, Z_ℓ), ρ) is (up to shift) i^{1*}T_{μ^∨}(Ri^b_*[ρ]) ∈ D_lis(Bun_G^1, Λ) ≅ D(G(Q_p), Λ), a natural complex of admissible G(Q_p)-representations; here [ρ] ∈ D(G_b(Q_p), Λ) ≅ D_lis(Bun_G^b, Λ) may be any complex of smooth representations.
items.locator: Chapter IX, §IX.3, p. 325 (unnumbered, after Theorem IX.3.1)
items.note: Uses T_μ left adjoint to T_{μ^∨}. HS3: 'Prove the source's finiteness, compactness and admissibility statements'.

items.name: Positive answer to [RV14, Remark 6.2(iii)]: finite length
items.statement: If Λ = Q̄_ℓ and ρ is an admissible representation of G_b(Q_p) of finite length, then each cohomology group of colim_K R Hom_{G_b(Q_p)}(RΓ_c(M_{(G,b,μ),K,C}, Z_ℓ), ρ) has finite length as a G(Q_p)-representation. (Via Verdier duality i^{1*}T_{μ^∨}(Ri^b_*[ρ]) ≅ 𝔻(i^{1*}T_{sw*μ}(i^b_![ρ^∨])) and preservation of compact objects by T_{sw*μ}.)
items.note: Finite global dimension of smooth Q̄_ℓ-representations: compact ⇔ cohomology finitely generated; finitely generated + admissible ⇒ finite length by Howe's theorem [Ren10, VI.6.3]. HS3 (admissibility statements); Howe's theorem is SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups territory (SR.3 plans 'finite length of parabolic induction of finite-length admissibles', not Howe's theorem itself).

items.name: Satake sheaf S_W on the twisted Beilinson–Drinfeld Grassmannian of local shtukas
items.statement: For general E, conjugacy classes {μ_i}_{i∈I} of cocharacters with fields of definition E_i/E and b ∈ B(G), there is a tower f_K : (Sht_{(G,b,μ•),K})_{K⊂G(E)} → ∏_{i∈I} Spd Ĕ_i of moduli spaces of local shtukas with compatible étale period maps π_K : Sht_{(G,b,μ•),K} → Gr^tw_{G,∏ Spd Ĕ_i,≤μ•} to a twisted form of the convolution affine Grassmannian ([SW20, §23.5]). With W = ⊠_{i∈I} V_{μ_i}, S_W is defined on the locus away from Frobenius-twisted partial diagonals (where Gr^tw is isomorphic to the Beilinson–Drinfeld Grassmannian) and extends uniquely across them to universally locally acyclic, necessarily perverse, sheaves (as for the fusion product); S_W also denotes its pullback to Sht_{(G,b,μ•),K}, and S′_W = D(S_W)^∨. With torsion coefficients f_{K♮}S′_W agrees with Rf_{K!}S_W (Proposition VII.5.2), but f_{K♮}S′_W is defined in general.
items.note: HS2 (local shtuka moduli, 'Include minuscule and nonminuscule bounds') and HS3 ('compactly supported complexes with Satake coefficients'). Uses GS3 fusion.

items.name: Proposition IX.3.2(a): partial Frobenii and compactness for local shtuka cohomology
items.statement: The sheaf f_{K♮}S′_W ∈ D■([∗/G_b(E)] × ∏_{i∈I} Spd Ĕ_i, Λ) is equipped with partial Frobenii, thus descends to an object of D■([∗/G_b(E)] × ∏_{i∈I} Spd Ĕ_i/φ_i^Z, Λ). This object lives in the full ∞-subcategory D(G_b(E), Λ)^{B∏_{i∈I} W_{E_i}} ⊂ D■([∗/G_b(E)] × ∏_{i∈I} Spd Ĕ_i/φ_i^Z, Λ), and its restriction to D(G_b(E), Λ) is compact.
items.note: Proof: f_{K♮}S′_W ≅ T_W(j_![c-Ind_K^{G(E)} Λ])|_{Bun_G^b}; the modification space M maps to Sht_{(G,b,μ•),K} isomorphically away from Frobenius-twisted partial diagonals; fusion compatibility of S_W gives partial Frobenii. HS3.

items.name: Proposition IX.3.2(b): admissible Weil-equivariant cohomology of local shtukas
items.statement: For any admissible representation ρ of G_b(E), R Hom_{G_b(E)}(f_{K♮}S′_W, ρ) ∈ D(Λ)^{B∏_{i∈I}W_{E_i}} is a representation of ∏_{i∈I} W_{E_i} on a perfect complex of Λ-modules. Taking the colimit over K gives a complex of admissible G(E)-representations lim_{→,K} R Hom_{G_b(E)}(f_{K♮}S′_W, ρ) equipped with a ∏_{i∈I} W_{E_i}-action. If ρ is compact, then so is lim_{→,K} R Hom_{G_b(E)}(f_{K♮}S′_W, ρ) as a complex of G(E)-representations.
items.note: This is Corollary I.7.3 of the introduction. HS3: 'Prove the source's finiteness, compactness and admissibility statements using compact Hecke kernels'.

items.name: Definition/Proposition IX.4.1: existence and uniqueness of φ_A
items.statement: Let L be an algebraically closed field over Z_ℓ[√q], and let A ∈ D_lis(Bun_G, L) be a Schur-irreducible object, i.e. End(A) = L as condensed algebras. Then there is a semisimple L-parameter φ_A : W_E → Ĝ(L) ⋊ Q, unique up to Ĝ(L)-conjugation (printed 'a unique semisimple L-parameter'), such that for all excursion data (I, V, α, β, (γ_i)_{i∈I}) consisting of a finite set I, V ∈ Rep((Ĝ ⋊ Q)^I), α : 1 → V|_Ĝ, β : V|_Ĝ → 1 and γ_i ∈ W_E for i ∈ I, the endomorphism A = T_1(A) —α→ T_V(A) —(γ_i)_{i∈I}→ T_V(A) —β→ T_1(A) = A is given by the scalar L —α→ V —(φ_A(γ_i))_{i∈I}→ V —β→ L.
items.locator: Chapter IX, §IX.4, Definition/Proposition IX.4.1, p. 327 (restated as Definition IX.0.4, p. 319)
items.note: Proof: build excursion data as in §VIII.4 and apply Proposition VIII.3.8. Uniqueness is only up to Ĝ(L)-conjugation, as Corollary VIII.4.3 ('there is, up to Ĝ(L)-conjugation, a unique semisimple L-parameter') and Proposition VIII.3.8(i) say. Definition IX.0.4, this Definition/Proposition and Proposition I.9.1 print plain 'unique' (a new source issue raised by the review). Works in every characteristic ≠ p, with no condition on π₀Z(G). ES5: 'construct FS Definition/Proposition IX.4.1's continuous semisimple parameter φ_A'.

items.name: L-parameter φ_π of an irreducible smooth representation
items.statement: For an irreducible smooth representation π of G(E) (resp. of G_b(E)) over an algebraically closed field L over Z_ℓ[√q], φ_π := φ_A for the Schur-irreducible object A ∈ D_lis(Bun_G, L) given by π on the stratum Bun_G^1 (resp. Bun_G^b) via the fully faithful embedding D(G_b(E), L) ↪ D_lis(Bun_G, L).
items.locator: Chapter IX, p. 319 ('We can apply this in particular in the case of irreducible smooth representations π of G(E)') and §IX.7
items.note: ES5: 'For every irreducible smooth L-representation π of G_b(E), use VS4's fully faithful stratum embedding ... to obtain a Schur object and define φ_(G,b,π)'. The Schur property (End = L as condensed algebra) needs the smooth-representation Schur lemma.

items.name: Proposition IX.5.1: uniform finite wild ramification of Hecke operators on a compact object
items.statement: Let A ∈ D_lis(Bun_G, Λ)^ω be any compact object. Then there is an open subgroup P ⊂ W_E of the wild inertia subgroup such that for all finite sets I and all V ∈ Rep((Ĝ ⋊ Q)^I), the object T_V(A) ∈ D_lis(Bun_G, Λ)^{BW_E^I} lies in the full ∞-subcategory D_lis(Bun_G, Λ)^{B(W_E/P)^I} ⊂ D_lis(Bun_G, Λ)^{BW_E^I}.
items.note: Proof: if P^I acts trivially on T_V(A) and T_W(A) then on T_{V⊗W}(A); reduce to I = {∗} and a ⊗-generator V; then use the fact that every map Z_ℓ[W_E] → R to a relatively discrete condensed animated Z_ℓ-algebra factors over Z_ℓ[W_E/P]. ES1:finite-ramification: 'prove IX.5.1's single wild subgroup P for all representations V and finite leg sets on each compact A'.

items.name: Full faithfulness of D_lis^{B(W_E/P)^I} → D_lis^{BW_E^I}
items.statement: For P an open subgroup of wild inertia, the functor D_lis(Bun_G, Λ)^{B(W_E/P)^I} → D_lis(Bun_G, Λ)^{BW_E^I} is fully faithful; this follows from full faithfulness of f* : D■(Bun_G × [∗/(W_E/P)^I], Λ) → D■(Bun_G × [∗/W_E^I], Λ), which follows from f_♮Λ ≅ Λ (and the projection formula for f_♮), reducing via base change / a v-cover Spa C → [∗/(W_E/P)^I] to vanishing of the Λ-homology of the pro-p group P^I.
items.locator: Chapter IX, §IX.5, proof of Proposition IX.5.1, pp. 327–328
items.note: Lemma inside the proof of IX.5.1; ES1:finite-ramification.

items.name: Maps Z_ℓ[W_E] → relatively discrete condensed algebras factor through a finite wild quotient
items.statement: (D_lis(Bun_G, Λ)^ω)^{BW_E} = ⋃_P (D_lis(Bun_G, Λ)^ω)^{B(W_E/P)}, because for any relatively discrete condensed animated Z_ℓ-algebra R with a map Z_ℓ[W_E] → R, the map factors over Z_ℓ[W_E/P] for some open P of wild inertia: restricting to Z_ℓ[I_E], compactness of I_E puts the image in a finitely generated Z_ℓ-submodule R₀ ⊂ R, so one may assume R finite over Z_ℓ; then Aut_{Z_ℓ}(R) is profinite and locally pro-ℓ, so I_E → R^× factors over I_E/P.
items.locator: Chapter IX, §IX.5, proof of Proposition IX.5.1, p. 328
items.note: ES1:finite-ramification: 'use compactness in the condensed endomorphism algebra'.

items.name: D^P_lis(Bun_G,Λ)^ω and its excursion algebra map
items.statement: Fix an open subgroup P of wild inertia of W_E; D^P_lis(Bun_G, Λ)^ω ⊂ D_lis(Bun_G, Λ)^ω is the full ∞-subcategory of all A such that P^I acts trivially on T_V(A) for all V ∈ Rep((Ĝ ⋊ Q)^I). Picking a discrete dense subgroup W ⊂ W_E/P (discretizing tame inertia), Theorem VIII.4.1 gives a canonical map of algebras Exc(W, Ĝ) → Z(D^P_lis(Bun_G, Λ)^ω) = π₀End(id_{D^P_lis(Bun_G,Λ)^ω}).
items.note: ES0: 'Construct excursion operators from a finite leg set ...'; LP2:excursion-presentation constructs Exc(W, Ĝ).

items.name: Decomposition of D_lis(Bun_G,Λ) along connected components of Z¹(W_E,Ĝ)_Λ
items.statement: As Exc(W, Ĝ) ⊗ Λ → 𝒪(Z¹(W_E/P, Ĝ)_Λ)^Ĝ is a universal homeomorphism, there are idempotents for the connected components of Z¹(W_E/P, Ĝ)_Λ, giving D^P_lis(Bun_G, Λ)^ω = ⊕_{c∈π₀Z¹(W_E/P,Ĝ)_Λ} D^c_lis(Bun_G, Λ)^ω. Taking the union over P, D_lis(Bun_G, Λ)^ω = ⊕_{c∈π₀Z¹(W_E,Ĝ)_Λ} D^c_lis(Bun_G, Λ)^ω, and on Ind-categories D_lis(Bun_G, Λ) = ∏_{c∈π₀Z¹(W_E,Ĝ)_Λ} D^c_lis(Bun_G, Λ). Any Schur-irreducible A ∈ D_lis(Bun_G, Λ) lies in one factor c, and its L-parameter φ_A lies in the connected component c.
items.note: ES1:finite-ramification: 'Construct the component decomposition of compact D_lis as a direct sum and of its Ind-category as a product'. Universal homeomorphism from Chapter VIII (Theorem VIII.3.6 / §VIII.4).

items.name: Theorem IX.5.2: spectral action of Z^spec on D_lis(Bun_G,Λ) commuting with Hecke operators
items.statement: Assume that the order of π₀Z(G) is invertible in Λ. There is a natural map Z^spec(G, Λ) → Z^geom(G, Λ) compatible with the decomposition into connected components. Moreover, for all finite sets I, all V ∈ Rep_Λ(Ĝ^I) and all A ∈ D_lis(Bun_G, Λ), the diagram Z^spec(G, Λ) → End(A) → End(T_V(A)) and Z^spec(G, Λ) → End(T_V(A)) commutes, so the map factors over Z^geom_Hecke(G, Λ) ⊂ Z^geom(G, Λ).
items.note: Generalizes Helm–Moss [HM18]. Proof: component decomposition, the map Exc(W, Ĝ)_Λ → Z(D^P_lis(Bun_G, Λ)^ω), and Theorem VIII.3.6. ES1:spectral-center (cites 'FS IX.5.2').

items.name: Involutions 𝔻^geom and 𝔻^spec of the centers
items.statement: The Bernstein–Zelevinsky duality functor 𝔻_BZ on D_lis(Bun_G, Λ) induces an involution 𝔻^geom of Z^geom(G, Λ). The Chevalley involution of Ĝ induces an involution of Z¹(W_E, Ĝ); after passing to the quotient by Ĝ-conjugation one can forget the inner automorphism appearing in Proposition VI.12.1; 𝔻^spec is the induced involution of Z^spec(G, Λ).
items.note: ES6:duality: 'Use VS5 and GS4's Chevalley/sw comparison ... Preserve the Chevalley involution in the dual parameter.'

items.name: Proposition IX.5.3 (diagram): Z^spec → Z^geom intertwines 𝔻^spec and 𝔻^geom
items.statement: The diagram with horizontal maps Z^spec(G, Λ) → Z^geom(G, Λ) and vertical maps 𝔻^spec, 𝔻^geom commutes.
items.note: Proof from the construction of excursion operators and Proposition VI.12.1. ES6:duality: 'prove IX.5.3 for the Bernstein–Zelevinsky dual'.

items.name: Proposition IX.5.3 (parameters): compatibility with Bernstein–Zelevinsky and smooth duals
items.statement: The formation of L-parameters for irreducible smooth representations of G(E) is compatible with passage to Bernstein–Zelevinsky duals, and to smooth duals (the parameter of the dual is obtained via the Chevalley involution).
items.note: For supercuspidals the BZ dual agrees with the smooth dual; the general smooth-dual case uses compatibility with parabolic induction (Corollary IX.7.3), proved later — a forward reference, not circular. ES6:duality: 'The general smooth-dual compatibility additionally imports ES7:parabolic'.

items.name: Theorem IX.6.1: compatibility with maps inducing isomorphisms of adjoint groups
items.statement: Let G′ → G be a map of reductive groups inducing an isomorphism of adjoint groups, inducing a dual map Ĝ → Ĝ′, and π : Bun_{G′} → Bun_G. Then for any A ∈ D_lis(Bun_G, Λ) the square with top row Z^spec(G′, Λ) → End(π*A), bottom row Z^spec(G, Λ) → End(A), left vertical map Z^spec(G′, Λ) → Z^spec(G, Λ) (induced by Ĝ → Ĝ′) and right vertical map End(A) → End(π*A) commutes (printed with Z^spec(Ĝ′, Λ) and Z^spec(Ĝ, Λ)). In particular, if Λ = L is an algebraically closed field, A is Schur-irreducible and A′ is a Schur-irreducible constituent of π*A, then φ_{A′} is the composite of φ_A with Ĝ → Ĝ′.
items.note: Standing assumption of §IX.6: |π₀Z(G)| invertible in Λ (excursion-algebra variant otherwise). Proof: π_♮T_{V′}(π*A) ≅ T_V(A ⊗ π_♮Λ) using π_{H♮}S′_{V′} ≅ h₁*π_♮Λ ⊗ S′_V (geometric Satake compatibility, proof of Theorem VI.11.1). ES6:functoriality.

items.name: Proposition IX.6.2: compatibility with products
items.statement: If G = G₁ × G₂ is a product of two groups, then the diagram Z^spec(G₁, Λ) ⊗_Λ Z^spec(G₂, Λ) → Z^geom(G₁, Λ) ⊗_Λ Z^geom(G₂, Λ), Z^spec(G₁, Λ) ⊗_Λ Z^spec(G₂, Λ) ≅ Z^spec(G, Λ) → Z^geom(G, Λ) commutes. In particular, if Λ = L is an algebraically closed field and A₁ ∈ D_lis(Bun_{G₁}, L), A₂ ∈ D_lis(Bun_{G₂}, L) are Schur-irreducible, and A is a Schur-irreducible constituent of A₁ ⊠ A₂, then φ_A = (φ_{A₁}, φ_{A₂}) : W_E → Ĝ(L) ≅ Ĝ₁(L) × Ĝ₂(L).
items.note: Printed with Z^geom(G₁, Λ) twice and A₁, A₂ ∈ D_lis(Bun_G, L); corrected here (PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E66, PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E67). Proof by a diagram chase with excursion operators. ES6:functoriality: 'Product groups give product parameters'.

items.name: Proposition IX.6.3 (identifications): Bun, parameter stacks and excursion algebras under Weil restriction
items.statement: Let G = Res_{E′|E} G′ for a reductive group G′ over a finite separable extension E′ of E. Choose P an open subgroup of the wild inertia of W_{E′} ⊂ W_E, and let W′ ⊂ W_{E′}/P be the preimage of W ⊂ W_E/P. Then there are canonical identifications Bun_{G′} ≅ Bun_G, Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)/Ĝ ≅ Z¹(W_{E′}, Ĝ′)/Ĝ′ and Exc(W, Ĝ) ≅ Exc(W′, Ĝ′).
items.note: Excursion identification: use Exc(W, Ĝ) = colim_{(n,F_n→W)} 𝒪(Z¹(F_n, Ĝ))^Ĝ and the Shapiro isomorphism Z¹(F_n, Ĝ)⫽Ĝ ≅ Z¹(F_n ×_W W′, Ĝ′)⫽Ĝ′ (F_n ×_W W′ ⊂ F_n has finite index, so it is free of finite rank). The comparison with Exc(W′, Ĝ′) = colim_{(m,F_m→W′)} 𝒪(Z¹(F_m, Ĝ′))^{Ĝ′} then needs the functor (F_n → W) ↦ (F_n ×_W W′ → W′) to be cofinal. The paper's printed chain instead restricts to maps F_n → W that land in W′, and asserts isomorphisms that fail, for example for G = Res_{E′/E} G_m (newIssues entry 2). The identification itself is not in doubt. ES6:functoriality: 'construct nonabelian Shapiro equivalence, the corresponding Bun identification and the excursion-algebra comparison using finite-index subgroups of finite free groups'.

items.name: Proposition IX.6.3 (compatibility): L-parameters compatible with Weil restriction
items.statement: In the situation of IX.6.3, the diagram Z^spec(G′, Λ) → Z^geom(G′, Λ), Z^spec(G, Λ) → Z^geom(G, Λ), with the vertical isomorphisms induced by the identifications, commutes. In particular, L-parameters are compatible with Weil restriction.
items.note: Proof: inflate V′ from (Ĝ′ ⋊ W_{E′})^I to (Ĝ ⋊ W_{E′})^I and induce to (Ĝ ⋊ W_E)^I; geometrically ψ_* along Hck^I_{G′} → Hck^I_G ×_{(Div¹)^I} (Div′¹)^I, a closed immersion. ES6:functoriality.

items.name: Sheaves on Bun_T and the geometric Bernstein center of a torus
items.statement: If G = T is a torus, then D_lis(Bun_T, Λ) ≅ ∏_{b∈B(T)=π₁(T)_Γ} D(T(E), Λ); in particular Z^geom(T, Λ) = ∏_{b∈B(T)} Z(T(E), Λ), where Z(T(E), Λ) = lim_{←, K⊂T(E)} Λ[T(E)/K] (K running over open subgroups of T(E)) is the Bernstein center of T(E).
items.note: Uses the structure of Bun_T (Chapter III: B(T) = π₁(T)_Γ, all strata basic). ES6:functoriality torus bullet.

items.name: Proposition IX.6.4: spectral Bernstein center of a torus
items.statement: There is a natural isomorphism Z^spec(T, Λ) ≅ lim_{←, K⊂T(E)} Λ[T(E)/K].
items.note: Proof: resolve T by products of induced tori, reduce by Weil restriction to T = G_m, where Z¹(W_E, G_m) = Hom(E^×, G_m) by local class field theory. Local class field theory is not in Mathlib/Tau Ceti (the ClassFieldTheory Tau Ceti roadmap is the natural owner). ES6:functoriality: 'For a torus, resolve by induced tori and reduce to G_m'.

items.name: Proposition IX.6.5: the torus center map is diagonal
items.statement: Under the identifications Z^spec(T, Λ) = lim_{←,K⊂T(E)} Λ[T(E)/K] and Z^geom(T, Λ) = ∏_{b∈B(T)} lim_{←,K⊂T(E)} Λ[T(E)/K], the map Z^spec(T, Λ) → Z^geom(T, Λ) is the diagonal embedding.
items.note: Proof: reduce to G_m via Theorem IX.6.1, Propositions IX.6.2, IX.6.3; compute the excursion operator for I = {1,2}, V = std ⊠ std^∨ with tautological α, β, using §II.2.1. Shows the L-parameters for tori are the usual ones. ES6:functoriality: 'Prove the spectral-to-geometric torus center map is diagonal'.

items.name: Compatibility of L-parameters with twisting and central characters
items.statement: The L-parameters constructed for tori are the usual L-parameters (local class field theory). Applying Theorem IX.6.1 to Z × G → G and to G → G × D (Z ⊂ G the center, G → D the quotient by the derived group) together with Proposition IX.6.2, L-parameters are compatible with central characters (for connected center) and with twisting by characters of G(E) factoring through D(E). Compatibility with central characters in general follows by reducing to connected center via z-extensions [Kal18, Section 5].
items.note: ES6:functoriality: 'Derive twisting through G→G×(G/G_der) and central-character compatibility through Z×G→G; for disconnected center construct and compare z-embeddings as in IX.6's final paragraph and Kaletha §5.'

items.name: Definition IX.7.1: the maps Ψ_G and Ψ_G^b
items.statement: The map Ψ_G : Z^spec(G, Λ) → Z(G(E), Λ) is the composite Z^spec(G, Λ) → Z^geom(G, Λ) → Z(G(E), Λ) induced by the fully faithful functor j_! : D(G(E), Λ) ≅ D_lis(Bun_G^1, Λ) → D_lis(Bun_G, Λ). More generally, for b ∈ B(G), Ψ_G^b : Z^spec(G, Λ) → Z(G_b(E), Λ) is defined using the fully faithful embedding D(G_b(E), Λ) ≅ D_lis(Bun_G^b, Λ) → D_lis(Bun_G, Λ) given e.g. by the left adjoint to i^{b*} (i^b : Bun_G^b ↪ Bun_G the locally closed embedding, Proposition VII.7.2); all such embeddings induce the same map to the Bernstein center.
items.note: ES7:parabolic: 'Construct Ψ_G and Ψ_G^b from ES1:spectral-center and VS4's stratum embeddings (IX.7.1)'.

items.name: Twisted map Z¹(W_E, Ĝ_b) → Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)
items.statement: Ĝ_b is naturally a Levi subgroup of Ĝ, as G_{b,Ĕ} ⊂ G_Ĕ is the centralizer of the slope morphism ν_b : 𝔻 → G_Ĕ; this extends to Ĝ_b ⋊ Q → Ĝ ⋊ Q. Geometric Satake instead gives the natural inclusion Ǧ_b ⋊ W_E → Ǧ ⋊ W_E, where the W_E-actions include the cyclotomic twist. The latter induces Z¹(W_E, Ĝ_b) → Z¹(W_E, Ĝ) which, in terms of the usual W_E-action, sends a 1-cocycle φ : W_E → Ĝ_b(A) to W_E → Ĝ(A) : w ↦ (2ρ_Ĝ − 2ρ_{Ĝ_b})(√q)^{|w|} φ(w), where |·| : W_E → W_E/I_E ≅ Z sends a geometric Frobenius to 1. The induced map Z^spec(G, Λ) → Z^spec(G_b, Λ) is the one used in Theorem IX.7.2.
items.note: ES7:parabolic: 'the Ψ_G^b map factors through Ψ_(G_b) with the twisted Levi cocycle inclusion φ(w) ↦ (2ρ_(dual G)−2ρ_(dual G_b))(sqrt(q))^deg(w) · φ(w) … Prove this is a cocycle for the fixed pinned actions.' Read 2ρ_Ĝ as the sum of the positive coroots of Ĝ, i.e. the positive roots of G, an element of X^*(T) = X_*(T̂); this is the paper's ρ̂ of Proposition VI.12.1. Then 2ρ_Ĝ − 2ρ_{Ĝ_b} pairs to zero with every root of Ĝ_b, so it is a cocharacter of Z(Ĝ_b) and the formula defines a cocycle. With the usual meaning (the sum of the positive roots of Ĝ, a character of T̂), (2ρ_Ĝ − 2ρ_{Ĝ_b})(√q) is not an element of Ĝ(A) (newIssues entry 5).

items.name: Theorem IX.7.2: Ψ_G^b factors through Ψ_{G_b}
items.statement: For all G and b ∈ B(G), the diagram Z^spec(G, Λ) —Ψ_G^b→ Z(D(G_b(E), Λ)), Z^spec(G, Λ) → Z^spec(G_b, Λ) —Ψ_{G_b}→ Z(D(G_b(E), Λ)) commutes (the left map induced by the twisted embedding Z¹(W_E, Ĝ_b) → Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)).
items.note: If ℓ divides |π₀Z(G)| the left side is replaced by an excursion algebra. Proof: reduce to Λ killed by a power of ℓ (Z(D(G_b(E), Λ)) = lim_K Z(Λ[G_b(E)⫽K]) is ℓ-adically separated); basic b via Bun_G ≅ Bun_{G_b} (Corollary III.4.3); reduce to quasisplit G by a z-embedding G ↪ G′ [Kal18, §5]; for quasisplit G use b_N = bμ(π^N), Harder–Narasimhan reduction to P, Hck^I_{M,P} and the constant term CT_P(S_V) ≅ S_V|_{(M̌⋊Q)^I}[deg_P]. ES7:parabolic: 'prove IX.7.2'.

items.name: z-embeddings: B(G) → B(G′) injective
items.statement: Let G ↪ G′ be a z-embedding as in [Kal18, Section 5] with quotient a torus D, so that Z(G′) is connected. Then Bun_G = Bun_{G′} ×_{Bun_D} {∗} and the map B(G) → B(G′) is injective: for all b ∈ B(G) with image b′ ∈ B(G′), G_b → G′_{b′} is a z-embedding with quotient D, and Z′(E) → D(E) is surjective by [Kal18, Fact 5.5] with Z′ = Z(G′) ⊂ G′_{b′}, so G′_{b′}(E) → D(E) is surjective. An element of the Bernstein center of G_b(E) is determined by its action on π′|_{G_b(E)} for representations π′ of G′_{b′}(E).
items.locator: Chapter IX, §IX.7.1, proof of Theorem IX.7.2, p. 335
items.note: ES6:functoriality: 'These z-embedding and rational-point-surjectivity lemmas are obligations here on BG0's reductive carriers'. Also uses: when Z(G) is connected there is a basic b₀ with G_{b₀} quasisplit.

items.name: Ψ_G^b = Ψ_G^{b_N} along the increasingly unstable sequence b_N
items.statement: Let G be quasisplit with Borel B, b ∈ B(G) with canonical parabolic P = P_b ⊃ B, μ : G_m → G a cocharacter with dynamical parabolic P, and b_N = bμ(π^N) (N ≥ 0); then G_b = G_{b_N} and Ψ_G^b = Ψ_G^{b_N} as maps Z^spec(G, Λ) → Z(G_b(E), Λ). Indeed, for a representation σ of G_b(E) and A_N ∈ D_ét(Bun_G, Λ) concentrated on Bun_G^{b_N} given by σ, with V ∈ Rep Ĝ of highest weight μ^N, T_V(A_N)|_{Bun_G^b} is given by σ: there is exactly one modification of E_b of type bounded by μ^N isomorphic to E_{b_N} (pushout of O → O(1) along μ^N), of type exactly μ^N. For N large, every modification of E_{b_N} to itself of type bounded by V is compatible with the Harder–Narasimhan reduction to P.
items.locator: Chapter IX, §IX.7.1, proof of Theorem IX.7.2, pp. 335–336
items.note: ES7:parabolic: 'Construct the increasingly unstable sequence b_N, prove bounded self-modifications eventually preserve its canonical parabolic, and identify the constant-term Hecke diagram.'

items.name: Corollary IX.7.3 (center form): compatibility with parabolic induction
items.statement: Let G be a reductive group with a parabolic P ⊂ G and Levi P → M. Then for all representations σ of M(E) with (unnormalized) parabolic induction Ind_{P(E)}^{G(E)} σ, the diagram Z^spec(G, Λ) → End(Ind_{P(E)}^{G(E)} σ), Z^spec(G, Λ) → Z^spec(M, Λ) → End(σ) → End(Ind_{P(E)}^{G(E)} σ) commutes (Z^spec(G,Λ) → Z^spec(M,Λ) induced by the twisted embedding of §IX.7.1).
items.note: Proof: reduce to σ = c-Ind_K^{M(E)} Λ, K pro-p, Λ = Z_ℓ[√q], then torsion coefficients; for μ with dynamical parabolic P and b = μ(π^{-1}), G_b = M and T_{μ^{-1}}(A)|_{Bun_G^1} = Ind_{P(E)}^{G(E)} σ(−d/2)[−d], d = ⟨2ρ, μ⟩ (moduli of modifications = G(E)/P(E), all of type exactly μ; cf. [GI16, Theorem 4.26]); then Theorem IX.7.2. ES7:parabolic: 'Deduce IX.7.3 for unnormalized parabolic induction'.

items.name: Corollary IX.7.3 (parameters): L-parameters of subquotients of parabolic inductions
items.statement: If Λ = L is an algebraically closed field, σ is an irreducible representation of M(E) and σ̃ is an irreducible subquotient of Ind_{P(E)}^{G(E)} σ, then φ_σ̃ is conjugate to the composite W_E —φ_σ→ M̂(L) ⋊ W_E → Ĝ(L) ⋊ W_E, where M̂ ⋊ W_E → Ĝ ⋊ W_E is the map of §IX.7.1 involving the cyclotomic twist.
items.note: ES7:parabolic: 'every irreducible subquotient. Then prove the dictionary with the local-group owner's normalized induction (SR.1–SR.2)'.

items.name: Theorem IX.7.4: agreement with the classical local Langlands correspondence for GL_n
items.statement: Let π be any irreducible smooth Q̄_ℓ-representation of GL_n(E). Then the L-parameter φ_π agrees with the usual (semisimplified) L-parameter.
items.note: Only place relying on previous work on LLC ([LRS93], [HT01], [Hen00]) and the cohomology of Lubin–Tate and Drinfeld towers ([Boy99], [Har97], [HT01], [Hau05], [Dat07], [SW13]). Proof: reduce to supercuspidal π by IX.7.3; evaluate the excursion operator for I = {1,2}, V = std ⊠ std^∨ on the sheaf B on Bun^b_{GL_n} (b ↔ O(−1/n)) given by σ = JL(π): T_V(B)|_{Bun^b} = σ ⊗ ρ_π ⊗ ρ_π^* (Lubin–Tate then Drinfeld tower); π is a summand of T_std(B). ES7:GLn-comparison (E/Q_p) and ES7:equal-characteristic (E = F_q((t))).

items.name: Integral spectral-to-Bernstein-center map for GL_n agrees with the usual one (Helm–Moss)
items.statement: The map Z^spec(GL_n, Q̄_ℓ) → Z(GL_n(E), Q̄_ℓ) agrees with the usual map; it refines to a map Z^spec(GL_n, Z_ℓ[√q]) → Z(GL_n(E), Z_ℓ[√q]) to the integral Bernstein center, recovering a result of Helm–Moss [HM18].
items.note: Consequence of Theorem IX.7.4 and Corollary IX.0.3 (π₀Z(GL_n) trivial). ES1:spectral-center + ES7:GLn-comparison; SR.5 owns Helm's integral GL_n families.

items.name: Compactly supported action of Perf(Z¹(W_E,Ĝ)/Ĝ)
items.statement: Z¹(W_E, Ĝ) is not quasicompact; it is the increasing union of the open and closed quasicompact subschemes Z¹(W_E/P, Ĝ). An action of Perf(Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)/Ĝ) on a stable ∞-category C is compactly supported if for all X ∈ C the functor Perf(Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)/Ĝ) → C (induced by acting on X) factors over some Perf(Z¹(W_E/P, Ĝ)/Ĝ).
items.note: LP4: 'The infinite union is non-quasicompact, so define the required compact-support factorization through one finite-wild piece for each object of a consumer category.' ES2: 'Establish compact support object by object over the non-quasicompact parameter union.'

items.name: Universal functor Rep_Λ(Ĝ⋊Q)^I → Perf(Z¹(W_E,Ĝ)_Λ/Ĝ)^{BW_E^I}
items.statement: The exact Rep_Λ(Q^I)-linear symmetric monoidal functor Rep_Λ(Ĝ ⋊ Q)^I → Perf(Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)_Λ/Ĝ)^{BW_E^I} is induced by tensor products from the exact Rep_Λ(Q)-linear symmetric monoidal functor Rep_Λ(Ĝ ⋊ Q) → Perf(Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)_Λ/Ĝ)^{BW_E} corresponding to the universal Ĝ ⋊ Q-torsor, with the universal W_E-equivariance as parametrized by Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)/Ĝ. Given a Λ-linear action of Perf(Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)_Λ/Ĝ) on C, composing gives an exact Rep_Λ(Q^I)-linear monoidal functor Rep_Λ(Ĝ ⋊ Q)^I → End_Λ(C)^{BW_E^I}, functorially in I.
items.note: LP4: 'Construct Perf on the finite-wild quotient and its action of Rep(dual G)'; ES2: 'recover the Hecke family from the universal parameter'.

items.name: Theorem X.0.1 (integral coefficients): Hecke data ⇔ compactly supported spectral action
items.statement: Let Λ be the ring of integers in a finite extension of Q_ℓ(√q) and assume that ℓ does not divide the order of π₁(Ĝ)_tor. Let C be a small idempotent-complete Λ-linear stable ∞-category. Then giving, functorially in the finite set I (i.e. as a map on total spaces over Fin of the corresponding coCartesian fibrations), an exact Rep_Λ(Q^I)-linear monoidal functor Rep_Λ(Ĝ ⋊ Q)^I → End_Λ(C)^{BW_E^I} is equivalent to giving a compactly supported Λ-linear action of Perf(Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)_Λ/Ĝ); the functor from actions to Hecke data is composition with Rep_Λ(Ĝ ⋊ Q)^I → Perf(Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)_Λ/Ĝ)^{BW_E^I}.
items.note: First versions: Nadler–Yun [NY19] (Betti), Gaitsgory–Kazhdan–Rozenblyum–Varshavsky [GKRV22] (split G, char 0, discrete group). Reduced to Theorem X.0.2 via the proof of IX.5.1. Proof completed at end of §X.3 by Propositions X.3.1–X.3.4 and Theorem VIII.5.1. ES3: 'Construct the integral Perf action and its equivalence with coherent Hecke data in FS X.0.1–X.0.2/X.3'; the hypothesis 'ell not dividing |pi_1(dual G)_tors|' is carried there.

items.name: Theorem X.0.1 (field coefficients)
items.statement: The statement of Theorem X.0.1 holds true if Λ is a field over Q_ℓ(√q), for any prime ℓ (no condition on π₁(Ĝ)_tor).
items.locator: Chapter X, Theorem X.0.1 (last sentence), p. 339
items.note: Characteristic-zero case; follows from Theorem X.1.1 as in Corollary X.1.3. ES2: 'For characteristic-zero coefficients prove the universal theorem of FS X.1'.

items.name: Theorem X.0.2: discretized version
items.statement: Assume that ℓ does not divide the order of π₁(Ĝ)_tor. Let C be a small idempotent-complete Λ-linear stable ∞-category, P an open subgroup of wild inertia and W ⊂ W_E/P a discretization. Then giving, functorially in the finite set I, an exact Rep_Λ(Q^I)-linear monoidal functor Rep_Λ(Ĝ ⋊ Q)^I → End_Λ(C)^{BW^I} is equivalent to giving a Λ-linear action of Perf(Z¹(W, Ĝ)_Λ/Ĝ), with the same compatibility as in Theorem X.0.1. The same holds if Λ is a field over Q_ℓ, for any prime ℓ.
items.note: Proved at the end of §X.3 ('Combining this with Theorem VIII.5.1, we have finished the proof of Theorem X.0.2'). ES3 (integral) and ES2 (rational).

items.name: Derived mapping stack Map_{∗/Q}(S, ∗/(H⋊Q))
items.statement: Let H be a reductive group over a field L of characteristic 0 with an action of a finite group Q, and S an anima over ∗/Q. The derived stack Map_{∗/Q}(S, ∗/(H ⋊ Q)) over L has as values on an animated L-algebra A the maps of anima S → ∗/(H ⋊ Q)(A) over ∗/Q. For S = ∗/W (W ⊂ W_E/P a discretization) and H = Ĝ it recovers [Z¹(W, Ĝ)_{Q̄_ℓ}/Ĝ] (Proposition VIII.3.5).
items.note: LP1: 'Construct the derived mapping stack over the finite pinned-action quotient'.

items.name: Map_{∗/Q}(S, ∗/(H⋊Q)) is an fpqc quotient of an affine derived scheme by a power of H
items.statement: Map_{∗/Q}(S, ∗/(H ⋊ Q)) is the fpqc quotient of an affine derived scheme by a power of H: choosing a surjection S′ → S ×_{∗/Q} ∗ from a set S′, the map Map_{∗/Q}(S, ∗/(H ⋊ Q)) → ∗/H^{S′} has fibre an affine derived scheme (representable by an animated L-algebra). Indeed Map_{∗/Q}(S, ∗/(H ⋊ Q)) → Map(S ×_{∗/Q} ∗, ∗/H) is relatively representable (Q-fixed points), and for connected T, Map(T, ∗/H) ×_{∗/H} ∗ parametrizes pointed maps T → ∗/H, equivalently maps of E₁-groups Ω(T) → H ([Lur09, Lemma 7.2.2.11(1)]); writing Ω(T) as a sifted colimit of finite free groups F_n reduces to maps F_n → H, represented by H^n.
items.note: LP1 ('Build derived affine schemes, fpqc quotient stacks ... Construct the derived mapping stack'). Uses Lurie's HTT.

items.name: Theorem X.1.1: rational spectral action for general mapping stacks
items.statement: Let C be an idempotent-complete small stable L-linear ∞-category (L of characteristic 0, H, Q, S as above). Giving, functorially in finite sets I, an exact Rep_L(Q^I)-linear monoidal functor Rep_L((H ⋊ Q)^I) → End_L(C)^{S^I} is equivalent to giving an L-linear action of Perf(Map_{∗/Q}(S, ∗/(H ⋊ Q))) on C. Here, from such an action one gets the functors by precomposing Perf(Map_{∗/Q}(S, ∗/(H ⋊ Q))) → End_L(C) with the natural exact Rep_L(Q^I)-linear symmetric monoidal functor Rep_L((H ⋊ Q)^I) → Perf(Map_{∗/Q}(S, ∗/(H ⋊ Q)))^{S^I}, the I-fold tensor product of Rep_L(H ⋊ Q) → Perf(Map_{∗/Q}(S, ∗/(H ⋊ Q)))^S assigning to s ∈ S pullback along evaluation at s, Map_{∗/Q}(S, ∗/(H ⋊ Q)) → ∗/(H ⋊ Q).
items.note: Follows [GKRV22]. Proof: exact functors from Rep_L((H⋊Q)^I) = exact functors from Perf(∗/(H⋊Q)^I); both sides (anima F₁(S), F₂(S)) take sifted colimits in S to limits (Lemma X.1.2), reducing to S a finite set, where Map = ∗/H^S; then Perf(∗/(H⋊Q)^I) ⊗_{Perf(∗/Q^I)} Perf(L) ≅ Perf(∗/H^I) (highest weight theory) and the Yoneda lemma. ES2: 'prove the universal theorem of FS X.1 ... prove the two constructions are inverse as spaces of coherent data'.

items.name: Lemma X.1.2: S ↦ Perf(Map_{∗/Q}(S, ∗/(H⋊Q))) commutes with colimits (characteristic 0)
items.statement: The functor taking an anima S over ∗/Q to Perf(Map_{∗/Q}(S, ∗/(H ⋊ Q))), regarded as an idempotent-complete stable ∞-category, commutes with sifted colimits. More precisely, as a functor into L-linear symmetric monoidal idempotent-complete stable ∞-categories, it commutes with all colimits.
items.note: Uses [Lur16, Corollary 3.2.3.2] (sifted colimits agree with or without symmetric monoidal structure) and Barr–Beck–Lurie [Lur16, Theorem 4.7.4.5]. Fails integrally (§X.3). LP4: 'Establish the finite-free-group colimit theorem and its universal property for exact monoidal functors ... rational proofs use the separate reductive invariant theory'.

items.name: Filtered colimits: lim Perf(X_i/G_i) ≅ Perf(X/G) for pro-reductive G
items.statement: Let X_i be affine derived L-schemes with actions of pro-reductive groups G_i (i in a filtered diagram; in the application G_i = H^{S′_i} for sets S′_i), X = lim X_i, G = lim G_i (pro-reductive). Then lim_{→,i} Perf(X_i/G_i) → Perf(X/G) is an isomorphism of idempotent-complete stable ∞-categories. In the course of the proof: Rep(G) = lim_{→} Rep(G_i) is semisimple, and Perf(X/G) is generated by Rep(G) as an idempotent-complete stable ∞-category.
items.locator: Chapter X, §X.1, proof of Lemma X.1.2, p. 342
items.note: Generation argument: kill top cohomology with V ⊗ O_{X/G} → H⁰(A) lifted by semisimplicity, reduce projective amplitude, split vector-bundle extensions by vanishing of H¹. Pushout case: Perf(X₁/G) ⊗_{Perf(X₀/G)} Perf(X₂/G) → Perf(X₁ ×_{X₀} X₂/G) is an equivalence (printed '×_X', (PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E68)). LP4 (rational generation).

items.name: Pushouts: Perf(X₁/G) ⊗_{Perf(X₀/G)} Perf(X₂/G) ≅ Perf(X₁ ×_{X₀} X₂/G) for pro-reductive G (characteristic 0)
items.statement: Let L be a field of characteristic 0, G a pro-reductive group over L (so Rep(G) is semisimple), and X₁ → X₀ ← X₂ affine derived L-schemes with compatible G-actions, X = X₁ ×_{X₀} X₂. (a) For each i, Ind Perf(X_i/G) is equivalent to the ∞-category of 𝒪(X_i)-modules in Ind Perf(∗/G): by Barr–Beck–Lurie [Lur16, Theorem 4.7.4.5], since Perf(∗/G) generates Perf(X_i/G), so the forgetful functor Ind Perf(X_i/G) → Ind Perf(∗/G) is conservative. (b) The functor Perf(X₁/G) ⊗_{Perf(X₀/G)} Perf(X₂/G) → Perf(X/G) is an equivalence (printed with target Perf(X₁ ×_X X₂/G), PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21/E68). Indeed the tensor product is the category of 𝒪(X₁) ⊗_{𝒪(X₀)} 𝒪(X₂)-modules in Ind Perf(∗/G), and 𝒪(X₁) ⊗_{𝒪(X₀)} 𝒪(X₂) → 𝒪(X) is an isomorphism in Ind Perf(∗/G), which can be checked after the conservative forgetful functor to D(L). Together with the filtered-colimit case and disjoint unions, this gives the 'all colimits' clause of Lemma X.1.2.
items.locator: Chapter X, §X.1, proof of Lemma X.1.2, p. 343
items.note: The second half of the proof of Lemma X.1.2; item c10-perf-quotient-filtered-limit covers only the first (filtered) half and mentions this one only in its note. Planned by the ES packet node ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction:ES2/mapping-stack-commutes-with-sifted-colimits (proof step 'Pushouts: identify the tensor product of the Ind-categories with modules over O(X_1) tensor_{O(X_0)} O(X_2) in IndPerf(BG) …'). LP4 plans 'the comparison of Ind-Perf with module objects over the cocycle algebra in Ind-Perf(B dual G)' for the parameter stack. Added in review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21). Review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21): the ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction packets are not yet reviewed or promoted, so this is missing and routed to route 7.

items.name: Corollary X.1.3: the spectral action with field coefficients in characteristic 0
items.statement: Let L be a field over Q_ℓ(√q). There is a natural compactly supported L-linear action of Perf(Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)_L/Ĝ) on D_lis(Bun_G, L)^ω, uniquely characterized by the requirement that by restricting along the Rep_L(Q^I)-linear maps Rep_L((Ĝ ⋊ Q)^I) → Perf(Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)_L/Ĝ)^{BW_E^I} it induces the Hecke action, which gives, functorially in the finite set I, exact Rep_L(Q^I)-linear functors Rep_L((Ĝ ⋊ Q)^I) → End_L(D_lis(Bun_G, L)^ω)^{BW_E^I}.
items.note: Proof: reduce to D^P_lis for P acting trivially on Ĝ, restrict the Hecke action to W ⊂ W_E/P, apply Theorem X.1.1 and Z¹(W, Ĝ) = Z¹(W_E/P, Ĝ) (Chapter VIII). ES2: 'Establish compact support object by object'.

items.name: Whittaker data and the Whittaker sheaf W_ψ
items.statement: For a quasisplit reductive group G over E, Whittaker data consist of a Borel B ⊂ G with unipotent radical U ⊂ B together with a generic character ψ : U(E) → Q̄_ℓ^×; fix √q ∈ Q̄_ℓ. The Whittaker sheaf W_ψ ∈ D_lis(Bun_G, Q̄_ℓ) is the sheaf concentrated on Bun_G^1 ⊂ Bun_G corresponding to the representation c-Ind_{U(E)}^{G(E)} ψ of G(E). (Integral version, Conjecture X.3.5: ψ : U(E) → O_L^×, Λ = O_L[1/n], W_ψ ∈ D_lis(Bun_G, Λ).)
items.note: No atlas stage defines generic characters or the Whittaker sheaf for general quasisplit G (SR.5 treats Whittaker functionals only for GL_n). Needed only for the conjectures X.1.4, X.2.2, X.3.5. Whittaker data (a Borel B = TU and a generic character ψ of U(E)) are routed to SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.3 by the accepted route 3 of PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23 (item rev-whittaker-generic-representations-uniqueness-of); ES4 should import them and own only the sheaf W_ψ. W_ψ is consumed by Conjectures X.1.4 and X.3.5 and Example X.1.6, which the extraction places in ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions:ML.5, so ML.5 needs a link from ES4 (none exists; adding it creates no cycle).

items.name: Conjecture X.1.4: categorical local Langlands on the Fargues–Fontaine curve (Q̄_ℓ)
items.statement: CONJECTURE. Let G be quasisplit with Whittaker datum. Consider the functor D_qcoh(Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)_{Q̄_ℓ}/Ĝ) = Ind Perf^qc(Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)_{Q̄_ℓ}/Ĝ) → D_lis(Bun_G, Q̄_ℓ) : M ↦ Act_M(W_ψ), the colimit-preserving extension of the spectral action Act on the Whittaker sheaf. The corresponding right adjoint functor is fully faithful when restricted to compact objects, and induces an equivalence of (Perf(Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)_{Q̄_ℓ}/Ĝ)-linear small stable) ∞-categories D_lis(Bun_G, Q̄_ℓ)^ω ≅ D^{b,qc}_coh(Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)_{Q̄_ℓ}/Ĝ), where D^{b,qc}_coh denotes bounded complexes with coherent cohomology and quasicompact support (living on finitely many connected components).
items.note: Conjecture (not proved). No layer plans it (see reason). Equivalently, M ↦ M ∗ W_ψ, Perf^qc → D_lis(Bun_G, Q̄_ℓ), is fully faithful and extends to D^{b,qc}_coh ≅ D_lis(Bun_G, Q̄_ℓ)^ω. Route 7 (ES2), recorded as a statement and not a target, like c1-conj-I.10.2.

items.name: Remark X.1.5: matching orthogonal decompositions (expected)
items.statement: There is an orthogonal decomposition D_lis(Bun_G, Q̄_ℓ)^ω = ⊕_{α∈π₁(G)_Γ} D_lis(Bun_G^{c₁=α}, Q̄_ℓ)^ω given by the connected components of Bun_G. There is a morphism Z(Ĝ)^Γ → Aut(Id_{Z¹(W_E,Ĝ)_{Q̄_ℓ}/Ĝ}), as Z(Ĝ)^Γ ⊂ Ĝ acts trivially on Z¹(W_E, Ĝ), with an associated eigenspace decomposition D^{b,qc}_coh(Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)_{Q̄_ℓ}/Ĝ) = ⊕_{χ∈X*(Z(Ĝ)^Γ)} D^{b,qc}_coh(Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)_{Q̄_ℓ}/Ĝ)_χ. Compatibility with the spectral action implies that via π₁(G)_Γ = X*(Z(Ĝ)^Γ) these decompositions should match.
items.note: Remark X.1.5 is attached to Conjecture X.1.4 ("Compatibility with the spectral action implies that ... those two decompositions should match"; TeX, the remark after Conjecture X.1.4), which the extraction marks planned in ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions:ML.5 (conditional implications of the categorical conjecture). The two decompositions themselves are proved elsewhere: components of Bun_G (BunGAndNewtonStrata:BG2:smooth-Artin) and the Z(G-hat)^Gamma-eigenspace decomposition. Review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21): kept missing. ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions:ML.5 names categorical Langlands only as an area, has no Bun_G or spectral-action inputs, and its packet says 'Not started'; the body forms of these conjectures (X.1.4, X.3.5) are missing too, and all go to route 7.

items.name: Example X.1.6: conjectural endomorphisms of the Whittaker representation
items.statement: Fully faithfulness in Conjecture X.1.4, applied to the structure sheaf, implies Z^spec(G, Q̄_ℓ) ≅ End(c-Ind_{U(E)}^{G(E)} ψ).
items.note: Conditional on Conjecture X.1.4. Not planned: the ES packet says Examples X.1.6 and X.1.7 are 'deliberately not planned', and ML.5 names only the general area. Route 7 (ES2), as a statement.

items.name: Example X.1.7: kernel of functoriality (conditional)
items.statement: Let f : ^LH → ^LG be an L-morphism between L-groups of quasisplit reductive groups H, G over E, inducing Z¹(W_E, Ĥ)_{Q̄_ℓ}/Ĥ → Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)_{Q̄_ℓ}/Ĝ and pushforward Ind D^{b,qc}_coh(Z¹(W_E, Ĥ)_{Q̄_ℓ}/Ĥ) → Ind D^{b,qc}_coh(Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)_{Q̄_ℓ}/Ĝ) (e.g. via D^{≥0}_qcoh = Ind D^{b,qc,≥0}_coh and shifts). Conjecture X.1.4 then yields a canonical functor D_lis(Bun_H, Q̄_ℓ) → D_lis(Bun_G, Q̄_ℓ), which (by Bernstein–Zelevinsky self-duality of D_lis and Proposition VII.7.10) is given by a kernel A_f ∈ D_lis(Bun_H × Bun_G, Q̄_ℓ), expected (up to minor twists) to correspond to the structure sheaf of the graph of Z¹(W_E, Ĥ)/Ĥ → Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)/Ĝ; restricting to the direct factors D(H(E), Q̄_ℓ), D(G(E), Q̄_ℓ) should give classical functoriality D(H(E), Q̄_ℓ) → D(G(E), Q̄_ℓ).
items.note: Conditional on Conjecture X.1.4. Remark X.1.8 notes that quasisplitness is needed: the Jacquet–Langlands correspondence cannot be completely canonical, because of fields of moduli for D^×. Not planned: the ES packet says it is 'deliberately not planned', and ML.5 names only the general area. Route 7 (ES2), as a statement.

items.name: Fargues's conjecture in this context: E_φ and the Hecke eigensheaf Aut_φ
items.statement: For an L-parameter φ : W_E → Ĝ(Q̄_ℓ) with i : Spec Q̄_ℓ → Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)_{Q̄_ℓ}/Ĝ, let E_φ = i_*Q̄_ℓ ∈ D_qcoh(Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)_{Q̄_ℓ}/Ĝ) = Ind Perf^qc(Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)_{Q̄_ℓ}/Ĝ); factoring i via [Spec Q̄_ℓ/S_φ], E_φ carries an S_φ-action, and tensoring with V ∈ Rep(Ĝ ⋊ Q) takes E_φ to E_φ ⊗ (V ∘ φ) (projection formula). The S_φ-equivariant automorphic complex Aut_φ = E_φ ∗ W_ψ ∈ D_lis(Bun_G, Q̄_ℓ) is a Hecke eigensheaf with eigenvalue φ. (Whether Aut_φ ≠ 0 is not known; the fully faithfulness in Conjecture X.1.4 would imply it and some properties of [Far16].)
items.note: The construction of E_φ and Aut_φ = E_φ ∗ W_ψ, and the Hecke-eigensheaf property, are proved consequences of Corollary X.1.3 and the Whittaker sheaf; only Aut_φ ≠ 0 is conjectural. No layer plans them: the ES packet's ES2 coverage says they 'belong with the elliptic material of ES4 and with the conjectural part, and no node claims them', and ML.5 names only the general area. Route 7 (ES2/ES4).

items.name: Definition X.2.1: elliptic L-parameter
items.statement: An L-parameter φ : W_E → Ĝ(Q̄_ℓ) is elliptic if it is semisimple and the centralizer S_φ ⊂ Ĝ_{Q̄_ℓ} has the property that S_φ/Z(Ĝ)^Γ_{Q̄_ℓ} is finite.
items.note: Planned by the packet node ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction:ES4/elliptic-parameters-and-components ('FS X.2.1: elliptic L-parameters and the connected component they span'), which quotes Definition X.2.1 with both conditions, together with the component C_φ and its summand. The packet is research/blueprint/packets/ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction--ES0.json, a draft still awaiting REV-ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction--ES0. Used in §X.2 and Conjecture X.2.2. Review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21): a node of the draft ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction packet states this (layer ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction:ES4), but that packet has not been reviewed or promoted, and the stage description alone does not name the statement. Packets count as planning only once promoted (PROTOCOL §6), so the item stays missing and is routed as a source to that layer.

items.name: Elliptic component C_φ and the decomposition of D^{C_φ}_lis(Bun_G, Q̄_ℓ)^ω
items.statement: For elliptic φ, the unramified twists of φ define a connected component C_φ ↪ [Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)_{Q̄_ℓ}/Ĝ] (deformation theory: H²(W_E, ad φ) = 0 by Tate duality and H⁰ is Lie Z(Ĝ)^Γ). The excursion operators give a direct summand D^{C_φ}_lis(Bun_G, Q̄_ℓ)^ω ⊂ D_lis(Bun_G, Q̄_ℓ)^ω, and by compatibility with parabolic induction i^{b*}A = 0 for non-basic b, so D^{C_φ}_lis(Bun_G, Q̄_ℓ)^ω ≅ ⊕_{b∈B(G)_basic} D^{C_φ}(G_b(E), Q̄_ℓ)^ω, all objects lying in supercuspidal Bernstein components. If Z(Ĝ)^Γ is finite (equivalently, the connected split center of G is trivial), then C_φ = [∗/S_φ] and D^{C_φ}_lis(Bun_G, Q̄_ℓ)^ω ≅ ⊕_{b∈B(G)_basic} ⊕_π Perf(Q̄_ℓ) ⊗ π, π running over supercuspidal Q̄_ℓ-representations of G_b(E) with φ_π = φ; Perf(C_φ) acts as a direct summand of Perf([Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)_{Q̄_ℓ}/Ĝ]), giving an action of Rep(S_φ).
items.note: Argued in the text (not numbered) from Theorem IX.5.2, Corollary IX.7.3 and Corollary X.1.3. ES4: 'Construct support of an object ... and the associated localization/decomposition operations in the cases justified by the parameter-stack geometry'. The deformation-theory claim (footnote 3) needs local Tate duality for ad φ.

items.name: Act_W(π_b) is concentrated on b + b_χ
items.statement: Assume Z(Ĝ)^Γ finite. If π_b is a supercuspidal representation of some G_b(E) with φ_{π_b} = φ elliptic, and W ∈ Rep(S_φ) with W|_{Z(Ĝ)^Γ} isotypic of character χ : Z(Ĝ)^Γ → Q̄_ℓ^×, let b_χ ∈ π₁(G)_Γ = B(G)_basic be the corresponding element (Z(Ĝ)^Γ is diagonalizable with characters π₁(G)_Γ). Then Act_W(π_b) is concentrated on b′ = b + b_χ, and Act_W(π_b) ≅ ⊕_{π_{b′}} V_{π_{b′}} ⊗ π_{b′} for multiplicity spaces V_{π_{b′}} ∈ Perf(Q̄_ℓ), π_{b′} running over supercuspidal representations of G_{b′}(E) with φ_{π_{b′}} = φ.
items.note: Unnumbered consequence of the spectral action and its compatibility with the Z(Ĝ)^Γ-grading (compare Remark X.1.5). Not planned: ES4's text (support, localization/decomposition, duality, excursion operators on local-shtuka cohomology) does not name it, and the ES4 packet coverage lists only the duality square, Definition X.2.1 and the decomposition over basic b. Route 7 (ES4).

items.name: Conjecture X.2.2: elliptic L-packets via the spectral action
items.statement: CONJECTURE. Assume that G is quasisplit, with a fixed Whittaker datum, and that the connected split center of G is trivial; let φ be an elliptic L-parameter. Then there is a unique generic supercuspidal representation π of G(E) with L-parameter φ_π = φ, and the functor Perf([Spec Q̄_ℓ/S_φ]) → D^{C_φ}_lis(Bun_G, Q̄_ℓ)^ω : W ↦ Act_W(π) is an equivalence. In particular, the set of irreducible supercuspidal representations of some G_b(E) with L-parameter φ is in bijection with the set of irreducible representations of S_φ. Moreover, the equivalence is t-exact for the standard t-structures on source and target.
items.note: Conjecture; up to t-exactness it is the specialisation of Conjecture X.1.4 to elliptic parameters, motivated by [Kal14]. Not planned: ES4 excludes 'Identifying a particular classical packet', its packet says X.2.2 'is conjectural … and no node claims it', and ML.5 names only the general area. Route 7 (ES4), as a statement.

items.name: Hecke operators on elliptic components via Rep(S_φ) (Kottwitz conjecture shape)
items.statement: For V ∈ Rep(Ĝ ⋊ Q), restriction to S_φ with the commuting W_E-action given by φ defines Rep(Ĝ ⋊ Q) → Rep(S_φ)^{BW_E}, and the diagram of monoidal functors Rep(Ĝ ⋊ Q) → End_{Q̄_ℓ}(D^{C_φ}_lis(Bun_G, Q̄_ℓ))^{BW_E}, Rep(Ĝ ⋊ Q) → Rep(S_φ)^{BW_E} → End_{Q̄_ℓ}(D^{C_φ}_lis(Bun_G, Q̄_ℓ))^{BW_E} commutes. Concretely, if the image of V in Rep(S_φ)^{BW_E} is ⊕_{i∈I} W_i ⊗ σ_i (W_i irreducible, σ_i continuous finite-dimensional W_E-representations), then T_V(π) ≅ ⊕_{i∈I} Act_{W_i}(π) ⊗ σ_i. Assuming Conjecture X.2.2 (and matching parametrizations), this yields the Kottwitz conjecture [RV14, Conjecture 7.3].
items.note: The commutativity follows from the compatibility of the spectral action with the Hecke action (Corollary X.1.3); the deduction of the Kottwitz conjecture is conditional. Compare PAPER-HANSEN-KALETHA-WEINSTEIN-22 (Kottwitz conjecture). Not planned: ES4's text does not name the factorisation through Rep(S_φ)^{BW_E}, since its local-shtuka clause is about excursion operators on shtuka cohomology, and the ES4 packet lists 'the Hecke formula T_V(pi) = sum of Act_{W_i}(pi) tensor sigma_i' among what was read but writes no node for it. Route 7 (ES4).

items.name: Sifted-colimit approximation Perf(Map^Σ_{∗/Q}(S, ∗/(H⋊Q)))
items.statement: Let H be a split reductive group over a discrete valuation ring R with an action of a finite group Q, S an anima over ∗/Q, and Map_{∗/Q}(S, ∗/(H ⋊ Q)) the derived stack over R as before; S ↦ Perf(Map_{∗/Q}(S, ∗/(H ⋊ Q))) does not in general commute with sifted colimits. Anima over ∗/Q form the animation of sets with a Q-torsor, freely generated under sifted colimits by finite sets with a Q-torsor; Perf(Map^Σ_{∗/Q}(S, ∗/(H ⋊ Q))) is the animation (left Kan extension along sifted colimits) of the restriction of S ↦ Perf(Map_{∗/Q}(S, ∗/(H ⋊ Q))) to finite sets with Q-torsors. It is an R-linear idempotent-complete small stable ∞-category mapping to Perf(Map_{∗/Q}(S, ∗/(H ⋊ Q))).
items.note: Σ refers to [Lur09, §5.5.8]. ES3: 'Prove the finite-free-group descent and generation statement using LP3–LP4's integral good-filtration and Donkin-subgroup results'.

items.name: Proposition X.3.1: Hecke data ⇔ action of Perf(Map^Σ)
items.statement: Let C be an R-linear idempotent-complete small stable ∞-category. Giving, functorially in finite sets I, an exact Rep_R(Q^I)-linear monoidal functor Rep_R((H ⋊ Q)^I) → End_R(C)^{S^I} is equivalent to giving an R-linear action of Perf(Map^Σ_{∗/Q}(S, ∗/(H ⋊ Q))) on C; given such an action, one gets the functors by composing Perf(Map^Σ_{∗/Q}(S, ∗/(H ⋊ Q))) → End_R(C) with the natural exact Rep_R(Q^I)-linear symmetric monoidal functor Rep_R((H ⋊ Q)^I) → Perf(Map^Σ_{∗/Q}(S, ∗/(H ⋊ Q)))^{S^I}, the I-fold tensor product of Rep_R(H ⋊ Q) → Perf(Map^Σ_{∗/Q}(S, ∗/(H ⋊ Q)))^S (pullback along evaluation at s ∈ S when S is a finite set, in general by animation).
items.note: Proof: as for Theorem X.1.1. ES3.

items.name: Proposition X.3.2: Perf(Map^Σ) commutes with all colimits
items.statement: The functor S ↦ Perf(Map^Σ_{∗/Q}(S, ∗/(H ⋊ Q))) from anima over ∗/Q to symmetric monoidal idempotent-complete stable R-linear ∞-categories commutes with all colimits.
items.note: Proof: sifted colimits by definition; for finite sets S₁, S₂ one needs Perf(∗/H^{S₁}) ⊗_{Perf(R)} Perf(∗/H^{S₂}) ≅ Perf(∗/H^{S₁⊔S₂}), by highest weight theory for split reductive H over R (filtration of Perf(∗/H) by copies of Perf(R) indexed by highest weights). LP3 (integral highest-weight theory) / ES3.

items.name: Proposition X.3.3: free groups — full faithfulness and essential image
