items.statement: Assume that S = ∗/F_n is the classifying space of a free group. Then the functor Perf(Map^Σ_{∗/Q}(S, ∗/(H ⋊ Q))) → Perf(Map_{∗/Q}(S, ∗/(H ⋊ Q))) is fully faithful, and the essential image is the idempotent-complete stable ∞-subcategory generated by the image of Rep_R(H).
items.note: Map_{∗/Q}(∗/F_n, ∗/(H⋊Q)) = [H^n/H] with (σ₁,…,σ_n)-twisted diagonal conjugation; Perf(Map^Σ) = compact objects in O(H^n)-modules in Ind Perf(∗/H) (Barr–Beck–Lurie [Lur16, Theorem 4.7.4.5]); reduce to n = 1, the circle as pushout of ∗ ⊔ ∗ ⇉ ∗. LP4: 'Establish the finite-free-group colimit theorem'; ES3.

items.name: Proposition X.3.4: Perf(Map^Σ) for S = ∗/Γ
items.statement: Let S = ∗/Γ with Γ any discrete group, and lift S → ∗/Q to Γ → Q. One can write ∗/Γ = colim_{(n,F_n→Γ)} ∗/F_n as a sifted colimit (in anima). Then Perf(Map^Σ_{∗/Q}(S, ∗/(H ⋊ Q))) is the ∞-category of compact objects in the ∞-category of modules over colim_{(n,F_n→Γ)} 𝒪(H^n) in Ind Perf(∗/H), where 𝒪(H^n) is equipped with the twisted (via F_n → Γ → Q) diagonal conjugation of H.
items.note: Proof: E₁-groups in anima = animated groups, with compact projective generators F_n; then Proposition X.3.3 and commutation with sifted colimits. Combined with Theorem VIII.5.1 (the colimit of 𝒪(H^n) is 𝒪(Z¹(W, Ĝ)) with generation by Rep(Ĝ) under the ℓ ∤ |π₁(Ĝ)_tor| hypothesis) this finishes Theorem X.0.2, giving the spectral action on D_lis(Bun_G). LP4 / ES3.

items.name: The integral spectral action on D_lis(Bun_G, Λ)
items.statement: Let Λ be the ring of integers in a finite extension of Q_ℓ(√q), and assume that ℓ does not divide the order of π₁(Ĝ)_tor. Propositions X.3.1–X.3.4, combined with Theorem VIII.5.1, prove Theorem X.0.2 and hence Theorem X.0.1. Applied to C = D_lis(Bun_G, Λ)^ω with the Hecke action of Corollary IX.2.4, this gives a compactly supported Λ-linear action of Perf(Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)_Λ/Ĝ) on D_lis(Bun_G, Λ)^ω. Restricted along Rep_Λ((Ĝ ⋊ Q)^I) → Perf(Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)_Λ/Ĝ)^{BW_E^I}, it induces the Hecke action, and it is determined by this.
items.locator: Chapter X, §X.3, end of section (before Conjecture X.3.5), p. 350
items.note: The paper says: 'Combining this with Theorem VIII.5.1, we have finished the proof of Theorem X.0.2. In particular, this gives the spectral action on D_lis(Bun_G).' It is the integral analogue of Corollary X.1.3 (item c10-rational-spectral-action-X.1.3) and the action Act that Conjecture X.3.5 uses. Uniqueness is the equivalence of Theorem X.0.1. Planned by the ES packet node ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction:ES3/integral-spectral-action ('Applied to C = D_lis(Bun_G,Lambda)^omega with its Hecke action, this gives the spectral action on D_lis(Bun_G)'). Added in review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21). Review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21): the ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction packets are not yet reviewed or promoted, so this is missing and routed to route 7.

items.name: Conjecture X.3.5: categorical local Langlands with integral coefficients
items.statement: CONJECTURE. Assume that G is quasisplit and choose Whittaker data consisting of a Borel B ⊂ G and a generic character ψ : U(E) → O_L^× of the unipotent radical U ⊂ B, where L/Q_ℓ is some algebraic extension; also fix √q ∈ O_L. Let n be the order of π₀Z(G) and Λ = O_L[1/n]. Let W_ψ ∈ D_lis(Bun_G, Λ) be the Whittaker sheaf (concentrated on Bun_G^1, corresponding to c-Ind_{U(E)}^{G(E)} ψ), and let Ind Perf^qc(Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)_Λ/Ĝ) → D_lis(Bun_G, Λ) : M ↦ Act_M(W_ψ) be the colimit-preserving extension of the spectral action on W_ψ. Then the corresponding right adjoint functor is fully faithful when restricted to compact objects, and induces an equivalence of (Perf(Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)_Λ/Ĝ)-linear small stable) ∞-categories D_lis(Bun_G, Λ)^ω ≅ D^{b,qc}_{coh,Nilp}(Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)_Λ/Ĝ).
items.note: Conjecture. The printed left side is 'D(Bun_G, Λ)^ω'; D_lis is intended, since the introduction identifies D(Bun_G, Λ) = D_lis(Bun_G, Λ) on p. 25 (newIssues entry 4). Nilp means nilpotent singular support (§VIII.2.2), and the formulation may need adapting at bad primes. Not planned (see reason). It is the same statement as c1-conj-I.10.2-categorical-LLC, which is missing. Route 7 (ES3), as a statement.

routes.reason: RF0–RF2 plan the relative curves Y_S, X_S and the degree-one divisors Div¹ from §II.1. The missing items are §II.1's analysis of the absolute curve. First, classical points of 𝒴_C, 𝔻_C and X_C (II.1.6–II.1.9, II.1.22) and the tilting map, the Gauss-point and inertia lemmas (II.1.10, II.1.14), and maximal ideals with the local-PID structure (II.1.11–II.1.12, and Theorem II.0.1 / I.3.1 / I.2.3 of the introduction). Second, the topology of |X_S| → |S|. Third, Fargues' Cartier-divisor description of Div¹ (Remark II.1.20) and its properness and smoothness (Proposition II.1.21, whose smoothness input DiamondSixOperations S5 plans). The paper is the source for all of these. Review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21): corrected in place. The classical-point statements (I.2.3, I.3.1, II.0.1(a), II.1.11, II.1.12, II.1.22 and its footnote) are planned by the accepted VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals decomposition node VB2:classification/classical-points-and-principal-ideal-domains, and Div¹'s properness and smoothness (II.1.21) and |X_S| → |S| by RF2:untilts and RF1 nodes, so they leave the route. The route now carries the definition of classical points of 𝒴_C and their comparison with untilts (II.0.1(b), II.1.6–II.1.10), the tilting map, Lemma II.1.14 (consumed downstream by Drinfeld's lemma in VS1), Fargues's relative Cartier divisors (Remark II.1.20) and the openness and closedness of |X_S| → |S|. The Artin-reciprocity remark moves to route 2 to avoid a cycle. RF0:integral-Y and RF2:integral-divisors (RS-20) are named. Recommendation to the blueprint jobs: widen VB2:classification/classical-points-and-principal-ideal-domains from Y_C to 𝒴_C, as FS state II.1.11–II.1.12.

VB2–VB3 plan vector bundles on the curve, the classification, and Banach–Colmez spaces. The missing items are steps of FS §§II.2–II.3 that those stages do not name. From §II.2: the Harder–Narasimhan filtration under change of C and E (II.2.13), semistable bundles of fixed slope as an abelian category, the HN polygon, the contracting-action lemma (II.2.17), (BC(𝒪(1)) ∖ {0})/E^× ≅ Div¹ (II.2.4) and independence of 𝒪(1) (II.2.8). From §II.3: the presentations and H⁰/H¹ vanishing in families (II.3.1–II.3.4), Banach–Colmez spaces of two-term complexes, punctured and projectivized absolute BC spaces (II.3.5–II.3.8, II.3.10–II.3.11), and the examples BC(𝒪(−1)[1]) via the quaternion algebra and BC(𝒪(−2)[1]) = U/SL₂(E) (II.3.12–II.3.13). Review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21): corrected in place. Seventeen of the routed items are planned by nodes of the accepted VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals decomposition (VB1 degree-rank-slope, VB2:classification HN base change, VB2:ampleness GAGA, VB3:positive-basic-examples fundamental exact sequence, VB3:general-BC positive-slope resolution and Banach–Colmez spatiality, VB4 semicontinuity) and leave the route; Remark II.2.18(ii) is ECD Proposition 18.10 and is planned in DiamondEtaleCohomology:C4. The route keeps the vanishing results of Proposition II.3.4, the spatiality criteria of Lemma II.3.8, the punctured absolute Banach–Colmez remarks and Examples II.3.12–II.3.13, and gains the E^×-torsor over Div¹ and its comparison with local class field theory (from route 1).

BG0–BG3 plan Bun_G, B(G), |Bun_G| ≅ B(G), Beauville–Laszlo uniformization and the strata. The missing items are Chapter III's supporting results. They are the G-isocrystal stack and its stratification (I.2.1), pro-étale torsor triviality (III.2.5–III.2.6) and Rapoport–Richartz local constancy of κ (III.2.8), Borovoi's second proof via B_ab(G) = π₁(G)_Γ and étale cohomology of the curve (III.2.11–III.2.14), and Viehmann's homeomorphism (Conjecture III.2.15). They also include the affine Grassmannian lemmas (III.3.2–III.3.6, the non-split decomposition), inner twisting and Bun_G ≃ Bun_{G_b} for basic b (III.4.2–III.4.3) with the Morita and torus examples, split HN moduli (III.4.7), the filtered automorphism group and G̃_b (III.5.2–III.5.4), and π₀(Bun_G) ≅ π₁(G)_Γ. BG2:uniformization's v-surjectivity lemma rests on III.3.4–III.3.5, so that stage should take them. Review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21): corrected in place. The draft BunGAndNewtonStrata packet (not yet reviewed or promoted) states much of Chapter III node by node. Its nodes are recorded in the items' notes, but they do not yet count as planning, so those items stay here as missing and this route is their source route to the layers the draft nodes name (BG0 pure inner twisting; BG1 abelianization and τ; BG2:uniformization Beauville–Laszlo surjectivity and Rapoport–Richartz semicontinuity; BG2:smooth-Artin π₀(Bun_G); BG3 automorphism groups and strata; BG4 charts). The route also carries the stack of G-isocrystals and its stratification (cited from [RR96], [CS17], [HK22], [Iva23]), the homeomorphism |Bun_G| ≅ B(G) as Viehmann's theorem (recorded as a cited statement; see prerequisites), the non-split decomposition of Gr_G, the Morita and torus examples, the quasi-split description of G̃_b, the comparison morphism from W_E-cohomology to étale cohomology of X_S (added in review) and Example V.3.4 (M_b as Bun_{P_b} ×_{Bun_{M_b}} Bun_{M_b}^b), which BG4's text does not yet plan. Remark III.2.5 is planned in DiamondsAndVStacks:D3, whose stage text names it.

VS0–VS5 plan the sheaf theory of Chapters IV, V and VII: Artin v-stacks, ULA sheaves, D_■, D_lis and D_ét(Bun_G). Many foundational statements there are named only by their headline, and the missing items supply them. From §IV.1: Artin v-stacks and their examples and criteria (IV.1.2–IV.1.17). From §IV.2: universal local acyclicity, including ULA ⇔ dualizability in the 2-category C_S (IV.2.23), its consequences (IV.2.24–IV.2.33), Neeman's lemma (IV.2.20) and smoothness of Spd O_E → Spd F_q (IV.2.34, which DiamondSixOperations S5 leaves open). From §§IV.4–IV.6: the Quot example, the vanishing of partially compactly supported cohomology (IV.5.1/IV.5.3, Theorem I.5.2) and ULA-preservation under hyperbolic localization (IV.6.14). From Chapter V: the base-field invariance V.2.3, the derived smooth dual, Rπ^!Λ ≅ Λ and the Künneth statements V.7.2–V.7.3. From Chapter VII: VII.5.1 and VII.7.10. Review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21): corrected in place. Twenty-five items are planned by nodes of the accepted VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories decomposition (VS0 Artin v-stacks, representability and shriek pullback, partial compactly supported vanishing; VS1 ULA definition, dualizability, descent and the Jacobian criterion; VS4 strata as classifying stacks; VS5 Bernstein–Zelevinsky duality) and leave the route. π₀(Bun_G) (IV.1.23) moves to route 3, Neeman's lemma IV.2.20 to route 8 (EnhancedDerivedSheaves, following PAPER-SCHOLZE-17's accepted route), and the smooth dual to route 10 (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups). The route gains Breen's functorial resolution (input to VII.1.12 and VII.4.1, added in review) at VS2.

GS0–GS4 plan geometric Satake over the Fargues–Fontaine curve from FS Chapter VI. The missing items are proof ingredients no stage names. From §§VI.1–VI.6: the étale-over-divisor lemma VI.1.13, semicontinuity lemmas VI.3.2–VI.3.3, conservativity of the constant term VI.4.2, the Bruhat order on W̃, and the ULA calculus VI.6.2–VI.6.8. From §VI.7: Lemma VI.7.3. From §VI.11, the identification of the dual group: the SL₂ subgroup classification VI.11.2, the flat-ℤ_ℓ-module criterion VI.11.3 and Prasad–Yu VI.11.4. Review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21): corrected in place. Most routed items are planned by nodes of the accepted GeometricSatakeAndFusion decomposition (GS1 semi-infinite orbits and hyperbolic localization, ULA sheaves on the Hecke stack, relative perverse t-structure; GS4:integral-dual-group dual-group identification) and leave the route; the Bruhat order on W̃ is planned in ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.4 through accepted routes of HE-18 and HE-21. The route keeps Lemma VI.1.13 and Lemmas VI.3.2–VI.3.3, the auxiliary lemmas the GS nodes cite without stating.

LP0–LP4 plan the stack of L-parameters and its invariant theory from FS Chapter VIII, but almost all of §VIII.2 is unplanned. That covers local Tate duality for W_E-cohomology and the cotangent complex (VIII.2.2–VIII.2.3), the unipotent monodromy morphism, Weil–Deligne parameters and Zhu's comparison (VIII.2.4–VIII.2.5), and Hochschild cohomology with singular support and Gulliksen's and Arinkin–Gaitsgory's theorems (VIII.2.6–VIII.2.10). It also covers nilpotence of singular support (VIII.2.11). Also missing are Remark VIII.5.18 and Proposition VIII.5.19 (π₁ of fixed points), the Riemann-surface remark and Problem I.11.1. These refine the stack LP1 constructs; they are in its direction and belong in LP1/LP3/LP4, with no separate Part II. Review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21): corrected in place. The route's premise that 'almost all of §VIII.2 is unplanned' is not right: the draft LanglandsParameterStacks packet (review still queued) states VIII.2.1–VIII.2.3, VIII.2.6–VIII.2.9 and VIII.2.11 in LP1 and the monodromy map in LP2:integral-invariants, and the accepted decomposition plans Remark VIII.5.18 and Proposition VIII.5.19 in LP3 (now planned). The draft packet does not yet count as planning, so the §VIII.2 items stay here as missing with the draft nodes recorded in their notes, and this route names LP1 and LP2:integral-invariants. Problem I.11.1 moves to route 9 (DiamondEtaleCohomology:C8). The Weil–Deligne items (Definition VIII.2.4, Proposition VIII.2.5) overlap PAPER-GAN-HARRIS-SAWIN-ETAL-24 items whose LP0 route was rejected; whichever review settles them first fixes the owner for both papers. Inputs with existing owners are imported, not re-planned: quasi-unipotence (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2), Hochschild cochains (Tau Ceti DGAInfinity layer 8), Iwanaga–Gorenstein rings and complete intersections (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.3).

ES0–ES7 plan the Hecke and spectral actions of Chapters IX–X, and deliberately exclude the categorical equivalence (ES2–ES4). The missing items are the Whittaker sheaf for quasi-split G, elliptic L-parameters (Definition X.2.1) and Remark X.1.5, which the spectral action's elliptic and Whittaker-normalised statements use. They also include the paper's conjectures, recorded as statements not targets: independence of ℓ (I.9.5), Haines' conjecture on the stable center, and the categorical local Langlands conjecture (I.10.2). Review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21): corrected in place. ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions:ML.5 names categorical Langlands only as an area and its packet says 'Not started', so the Chapter X conjectures and statements it was credited with (X.1.4, X.1.6, X.1.7, X.2.2, X.3.5, the eigensheaf Aut_φ, the elliptic action shift and the Hecke/Rep(S_φ) compatibility, together with their introduction forms I.10.2 and X.1.5) are missing and recorded here as statements, not targets. The ES packets are not yet reviewed, so the elliptic parameter (X.2.1), the pushout half of Lemma X.1.2 and the integral spectral action on D_lis(Bun_G) (added in review) are routed here too, to ES2–ES4. ES1:spectral-center records the ℓ-independence conjecture I.9.5. Haines' stable-center conjecture moves to route 11, the accepted StableCenter Part II of PAPER-HANSEN-26. Whittaker data are imported from SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups (accepted route 3 of PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23); only the Whittaker sheaf is constructed here.

Added in review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21). Neeman's criterion ([Nee96, Theorem 5.1]: for a compactly generated C, a right adjoint preserves direct sums when the left adjoint preserves compact objects) is PAPER-SCHOLZE-17 item 603, whose accepted route 4 makes EnhancedDerivedSheaves the single supplier of such ∞-categorical foundations. FS use it in §IV.2.3.2 (VS1), which lies downstream (E3 → DiamondSixOperations S3 → S4 → VS1).

Added in review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21). Problem I.11.1 asks whether Krull dimension, dim.trg and the cohomological dimension of [Sch17a] agree on Zariski closed subsets of perfectoid balls; it is not about parameter stacks. C8 implements dim.trg and the cohomological bounds of [Sch17a, §21] and already records ECD's open Question 21.4 as a question; the problem is recorded there the same way, citing PerfectoidSpaces:P4 for Zariski closed subsets.

Added in review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21). The smooth dual (V^∗)^sm and its derived functor on D(G,Λ) are a general smooth-representation construction, used in Chapter V and by SR.2 for duals of admissible representations; SR.0 owns smooth vectors and the derived category of smooth representations.

routes.title: Excursion operators and the spectral action, Part II: stability of the Fargues–Scholze Bernstein center
routes.brief: Joins the accepted Part II proposed by PAPER-HANSEN-26 (route 1), whose brief governs; it adds no new endpoint. Final statement contributed by this paper, as FS state it in §I.9 (p. 35, after Conjecture I.9.5), citing Haines [Hai14] (see also [BKV15], [SS13, §6]): for G quasisplit, the Fargues–Scholze map Ψ_G : Z^spec(G,Λ) → Z(G(E),Λ) from the spectral Bernstein center to the Bernstein center of G(E) is injective, and its image is the set of elements of the Bernstein center of G(E) whose corresponding distribution is invariant under stable conjugation. The Part II should record this conjecture, state which cases Hansen proves, and import the spectral center and Ψ_G from ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction ES1:spectral-center and the Bernstein center from SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups; it plans none of these again.
routes.reason: Added in review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21). Haines' conjecture on the stable Bernstein center (FS §I.9) is the subject of the accepted StableCenter Part II of PAPER-HANSEN-26; routing it there, with the same id, title, parent and area, keeps one owner.

routes.title: Finite flat group schemes and integral p-adic Hodge theory, Part II: Lubin–Tate formal modules and quasi-canonical lifts
routes.brief: Joins the accepted Part II proposed by PAPER-BURUNGALE-KOBAYASHI-OTA-21 (route 2) and PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18 (route 8), whose briefs govern. Final statements this paper needs, as FS state them in §II.2.1 (p. 58, with the height-one condition the printed text omits): up to isomorphism there is a unique one-dimensional formal group G over O_Ĕ with an action of O_E such that the two induced actions on Lie G coincide and [π]_G is an isogeny of O_E-height one (the Lubin–Tate formal group), with its logarithm and universal cover, which FS use to identify BC(O(1)) with the universal cover of G. The Part II must state these in both mixed and equal characteristic, and import formal groups from Tau Ceti and O_E-module structures from its parent FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory; VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB3:positive-basic-examples consumes them.
routes.reason: Added in review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21). The Lubin–Tate formal group and its logarithm sequence are owned by the accepted Part II LubinTateFormalModulesAndQuasiCanonicalLifts; VB3:positive-basic-examples consumes them for BC(O(1)). Routing them there keeps one owner; the Part II must include equal characteristic.

sourceIssues.locator: Chapter I, §I.10, Theorem I.10.1, p. 37, first sentence (arXiv v4)
sourceIssues.printed: The assertion requires the order of π_0 Z(G) to be indivisible by ℓ, and takes a small stable ∞-category C that is Λ-linear. It equates two data: an exact monoidal functor Rep(Ĝ ⋊ Q)^I → End_Λ(C)^{BW_E^I}, linear over Rep_Λ(Q^I) and functorial in the finite set I; and an action of Perf(Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)_Λ/Ĝ) that is Λ-linear and compactly supported.
sourceIssues.correction: Let C be a small idempotent-complete Λ-linear stable ∞-category (as in Theorem X.0.1).
sourceIssues.reason: Theorem X.0.1 (p. 339), its discretized form Theorem X.0.2 (p. 340) and the rational Theorem X.1.1 (p. 341) all assume C idempotent-complete. The proof of X.1.1 begins 'for any L-linear idempotent-complete small stable ∞-category C, giving an exact L-linear functor Rep_L((H ⋊ Q)^I) → C is equivalent to giving an exact L-linear functor … Perf((H ⋊ Q)^I) → C'. The integral case uses that Perf(Z¹/Ĝ) is generated by Rep(Ĝ) only under cones and retracts (Theorem VIII.5.1). Without the hypothesis the printed equivalence is false. Example: G = 𝔾_m, q ≥ 3, and Λ containing μ_{q−1} with ℓ ∤ q − 1. Then Z¹(W_E/P, Ĝ) = Hom(E^×/(1 + 𝔪_E), 𝔾_m) ≅ 𝔾_m × μ_{q−1} is a disjoint union of q − 1 copies of 𝔾_{m,Λ}, with trivial Ĝ-action. Let D = Perf(Z¹(W_E/P, Ĝ)/Ĝ) with its tautological action. Let C ⊂ D be the full subcategory of objects whose K_0-class lies in the image H of K_0(Rep Ĝ). By Thomason's theorem C is a dense stable subcategory. H is a subring containing every class [V ⊗ 𝒪], so the exact monoidal functors Rep(Ĝ ⋊ Q)^I → End_Λ(D)^{BW_E^I} given by the tautological action preserve C and restrict to such functors for C. Suppose a compactly supported action of Perf(Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)/Ĝ) on C induced these restricted functors. It would extend to the idempotent completion D, and by the uniqueness in Theorem X.0.1 it would be the tautological action. Then 𝒪_{Z_0} = 𝒪_{Z_0} ⊗ 𝒪, for a connected component Z_0, would lie in C. It does not, because every class in H has the same rank on all q − 1 components while [𝒪_{Z_0}] does not. So these functors on C come from no action, contrary to the printed equivalence. Every application in the paper is to D_lis(Bun_G, Λ)^ω, which is idempotent-complete, so nothing downstream is affected.

sourceIssues.locator: Chapter IV, §IV.1.1.1, proof of Proposition IV.1.8(i), p. 109 (arXiv v4)
sourceIssues.printed: For point (i), the proof takes X = X_2 ×_{X_1} X_3 and maps f_i : U_i → X_i. It claims local spatiality for the diamond U = (U_1 ×_{X_2} U_2) ×_{U_2} (U_2 ×_{X_2} U_3), citing representability of ∆_{X_2} by locally spatial diamonds.
sourceIssues.correction: Keep X = X_2 ×_{X_1} X_3, as in the diagonal argument that follows, and interchange the indices 1 and 2 in the first sentence: U = (U_2 ×_{X_1} U_1) ×_{U_1} (U_1 ×_{X_1} U_3) is a locally spatial diamond using that ∆_{X_1} is representable in locally spatial diamonds. (Reading X = X_1 ×_{X_2} X_3 in the first sentence alone also makes it correct, but then it no longer matches the diagonal argument.)
sourceIssues.reason: With X = X_2 ×_{X_1} X_3 the maps are X_2 → X_1 ← X_3, so there is no map U_1 → X_2 and U_1 ×_{X_2} U_2 is undefined. The diagonal part of the same proof uses u : X_2 ×_{X_1} X_3 → X_2 × X_3 and the representability of ∆_{X_1}, so in the first sentence the indices 1 and 2 are interchanged. After the swap, U = U_2 ×_{X_1} U_1 ×_{X_1} U_3 → X_2 ×_{X_1} X_3 is the base change of f_1 along U_2 ×_{X_1} U_3 → X_1, followed by the base change of f_2 × f_3. It is therefore a separated, representable, cohomologically smooth surjection, as claimed.

sourceIssues.locator: Chapter IV, §IV.2.3.3, proof of Theorem IV.2.23, p. 125, with the definition of ⋆ on p. 124 (arXiv v4)
sourceIssues.printed: The source assigns A ⋆ D_{X/S}(A) = Rf_!(D_{X/S}(A) ⊗^L_Λ A) ∈ D_ét(S, Λ) = Fun_{C_S}(S, S). It also assigns D_{X/S}(A) ⋆ A = p_1^*A ⊗^L_Λ p_2^*D_{X/S}(A) ∈ D_ét(X ×_S X, Λ) = Fun_{C_S}(X, X).
sourceIssues.correction: With the p. 124 convention (Fun(X,Y) × Fun(Y,Z) → Fun(X,Z), (A,B) ↦ A ⋆ B), swap the two labels: D_{X/S}(A) ⋆ A = Rf_!(…) ∈ Fun(S,S) and A ⋆ D_{X/S}(A) = p_1^*A ⊗ p_2^*D_{X/S}(A) ∈ Fun(X,X), and likewise in the definitions of α and β. Alternatively, read ⋆ here as composition in functional order, g ⋆ f = g∘f.
sourceIssues.reason: On p. 124, A ⋆ B is defined for A ∈ Fun(X,Y), B ∈ Fun(Y,Z) (diagrammatic order). For A ∈ Fun(X,S) and D ∈ Fun(S,X) that gives A ⋆ D ∈ Fun(X,X), yet the proof places A ⋆ D in Fun(S,S). The proof follows the functional-order convention of the adjunction definition (α : id_X → gf, β : fg → id_Y). The maps α and β are correct once the order is read that way. This is a notational inconsistency only.

sourceIssues.locator: Chapter VIII, §VIII.2.2.2, Proposition VIII.2.11(ii) (p. 284), its proof and the following paragraph (p. 285) (arXiv v4)
sourceIssues.printed: Item (ii) asserts that, for n = f_{E′/E} and W_{E′} = ker(W_E → Out(Ĝ)), ℓ does not divide q^{en} − 1 for any exponent e of Ĝ. The proof describes m homogeneous polynomials whose degrees are root-system exponents, identifies the largest exponent of Ĝ with the Coxeter number h of G, and gives ℓ > q^{hn} − 1 as a sufficient condition.
sourceIssues.correction: Replace 'exponent' by 'degree' (degree of a basic invariant polynomial, d_i = m_i + 1) throughout: (ii) should read 'q^{dn} − 1 is not divisible by ℓ for any degree d of a fundamental invariant of Ĝ'. The largest degree is h, which is consistent with the rest of the paragraph.
sourceIssues.reason: The proof needs, for each basic invariant P_i of degree d_i, that P_i(v) = P_i(q^n v) = q^{n d_i} P_i(v) forces P_i(v) = 0, i.e. that q^{n d_i} − 1 is a unit in L. The proof itself says the invariants have 'degrees the exponents'. The claim 'supremum of the exponents = Coxeter number h' also holds only for degrees, since standard exponents m_i = d_i − 1 have maximum h − 1. So the paper consistently uses 'exponent' to mean 'degree', which is not the standard meaning. Read with standard exponents, (ii) does not imply what the proof needs, and the two conditions are incomparable. Example: Ĝ = G₂ (split, so n = 1), q = 5, ℓ = 3. The exponents are 1 and 5; 5 − 1 = 4 and 5⁵ − 1 = 3124 are prime to 3, so the printed (ii) holds. But 3 is a bad prime for G₂, contradicting the first step of the proof ('ℓ is very good'), and for the degree-6 invariant 5⁶ − 1 = 15624 = 3·5208, so the key step fails. With degrees (2, 6), 3 divides 5² − 1 = 24, so ℓ = 3 is correctly excluded. Conversely, for G₂ with q = 3 and ℓ = 11 the degree condition holds (3² − 1 = 8, 3⁶ − 1 = 728) while the exponent condition fails (11 divides 3⁵ − 1 = 242). The degree condition excludes bad primes and torsion primes: ℓ − 1 divides some degree whenever ℓ is not very good, and q^{ℓ−1} ≡ 1 mod ℓ. So the result is correct under the paper's own usage but misstated in standard terminology.

Then g^p is central, so g is semisimple (the unipotent part has p-power order and ℓ-power order, so it is trivial), and H = G^Θ = Z_G(g). Such a g need not be regular: Levi subgroups and the non-Levi fixed groups on p. 311 (A₂ ⊂ G₂, A₄ × A₄ ⊂ E₈) arise this way. The proof only uses that a maximal torus through g lies in H, which holds for every semisimple g. Kind 'error' with affects 'nothing' stands. 'Misprint' would also be defensible, since deleting 'regular' is clearly intended. Item c8-cor-VIII.5.15-centralizers-Donkin already uses the corrected form.

The two bounds become q^{−M/q} and q^{(N′−M)/q}, both larger than q^{−M−1}; the printed exponents are those of the reciprocal convention |π| = |[ϖ]|^ρ. The claimed estimate (II.2.1) is itself false as stated, so the proof does not establish global generation as written; the theorem is [KL15, Proposition 6.2.4] and stands, but the quantitative step must be redone (for example following [KL15]). For A = π^N·Id the choice v_i = Σ_j π^{Nj}[ϖ^{Mq^{−j}}]e_i works when (N/r + 1)/(q − 1) ≤ M ≤ (N − q)/(q − 1), i.e. with N made large by twisting and M chosen in a window, not with M large.

Writing h = Σ h_iπ^i, φ(h) = π^N h gives h_i^q = h_{i−N}; if |h_M| = 1 then |h_{M−kN}| = 1 for all k ≥ 0 and h cannot converge on Y_{C,[1,q]}, so |h_M| ≠ 1 and the π^M-coefficient of v has absolute value ≥ 1. Hence ||v||_{B_{C,[r,q]}} ≥ sup|π|^M = q^{−M/q} > q^{−M−1} for every M ≥ 1 and 1 < r ≤ q. The same computation on φ^{−1}(w₁) = [ϖ]^{(N−1)/q}π^{M−N+1} gives q^{−M/q}, not the printed q^{−(N−1)/q−r(M−N+1)}.

sourceIssues.printed: Lemma IV.4.26 asserts surjectivity of φ − π^{−d} : I_{[1,q]} → I_{[1,1]}. For i ≠ r_j, Lemma IV.4.25 gives f_i = φ(g_i) − g_{i+1}; it also gives f_{r_j} = φ(g_{r_j}) − π^{−d_j} g_{r_{j−1}+1}. In B_{C,[1,1]}[T_1, …, T_r]/(T_1, …, T_r)^2, the Proposition IV.4.24 proof uses α_{r_j} ≡ π^{−d_j} T_{r_{j−1}+1}.
sourceIssues.correction: Replace π^{−d} by π^{d} throughout: Lemma IV.4.26 should read "the map φ − π^{d} : I_{[1,q]} → I_{[1,1]} is surjective"; in Lemma IV.4.25, f_{r_j} = φ(g_{r_j}) − π^{d_j} g_{r_{j−1}+1} (and f = φ^r(g) − π^{d} g in its proof); in the proofs of Propositions IV.4.24 and IV.4.29 the linear terms are α_{r_j} ≡ π^{d_j} T_{r_{j−1}+1}, with α′_{r_j}(0, …, 0) ≡ α_{r_j}(0, …, 0) + π^{d_j} ε_{r_{j−1}+1} − φ(ε_{r_j}) and α_{r_j}(0, …, 0) = φ(ε_{r_j}) − π^{d_j} ε_{r_{j−1}+1}. The Dieudonné module φ(e_{r_j}) = π^{−d_j} e_{r_{j−1}+1} of Lemma IV.4.25 is right; the error is in translating it into the H^1 equation and the coordinate gluing.
sourceIssues.reason: FS's convention is H^0(X_S, O_{X_S}(1)) = H^0(Y_S, O_{Y_S})^{φ=π} (p. 60), and in the proof of Proposition II.2.5(iii), p. 62, H^1(X_S, O(n)) = 0 for n > 0 is shown by proving "φ − π^n : B_{R,[1,q]} → B_{R,[1,1]} is surjective". So on B the kernel and cokernel of φ − π^{−d} are H^0 and H^1 of O(−d), not O(d), while the proof of Lemma IV.4.26 ("By the snake lemma and the vanishing H^1(X_S, O_{X_S}(d)) = 0 ... equivalent to the surjectivity of H^0(X_S, O(d)) → H^0(X_{S_0}, O(d))") and the lead-in to Lemma IV.4.25 ("vanishing of H^1(X_S, E) for E of positive slopes") are about O(d). The printed Lemma IV.4.26 is false: take E = F_q((π)), d = 1, C the completed algebraic closure of F_q((ϖ)), S = Spa C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and S_0 = V(T) ≅ Spa C (Zariski closed), f = ϖ^{−1}T ∈ I_{[1,1]}. Writing g = Σ g_i π^i with g_i ∈ R, (φ − π^{−1})(g) has coefficients g_i^q − g_{i+1}. Convergence as i → −∞ forces g_i = 0 for i ≤ 0, and then g_1 = −ϖ^{−1}T and g_{k+1} = g_k^q, so |g_{k+1}| = |ϖ|^{−q^k}, and Σ g_i π^i diverges on Y_{S,[1,q]}. The same f with a factor π (f = ϖ^{−1}Tπ ∈ I^+_{[1,1]}) contradicts the printed Lemma IV.4.25 for r = 1. Geometrically, with the printed linear term a section t of Z near s satisfies t_{i+1} = φ(t_i), φ(t_{r_j}) = π^{−d_j} t_{r_{j−1}+1}, i.e. is a section of a bundle of negative slopes, contradicting the positivity of s^*T_{Z/X_S}. With π^{d_j} every step goes through: H^1 of the positive bundle vanishes, and the snake-lemma argument of the printed proof proves the corrected Lemma IV.4.26.

sourceIssues.locator: Chapter VI, §VI.2, proof of Proposition VI.2.4, first paragraph, pp. 198–199 (arXiv v4)
sourceIssues.printed: The source gives Fil^i_Ξ(R^♯)^n = (ξ^iΞ ∩ B^+_dR(R^♯)^n)/(ξ^iΞ ∩ ξB^+_dR(R^♯)^n) as finite projective R^♯-modules, with rank counting occurrences of −i in k_1, …, k_n. It then lifts e_{n_{i−1}+1}, …, e_{n_i} to f_{n_{i−1}+1}, …, f_{n_i} ∈ ξ^iΞ ∩ B^+_dR(R^♯)^n.

The filtration is decreasing (Fil^{i+1} ⊂ Fil^i), and its graded piece Fil^i/Fil^{i+1} has rank the number of occurrences of −i. Accordingly, the basis vectors lifted at step i are e_{n_{i+1}+1}, …, e_{n_i}: those in Fil^i but not in Fil^{i+1}, for which k_j = −i.
sourceIssues.reason: Take Ξ = ⊕_j ξ^{k_j}B⁺_dR, the lattice [μ] itself. Then ξ^iΞ ∩ B⁺_dR^n = ⊕_j ξ^{max(k_j+i,0)}B⁺_dR, whose image modulo ξ is spanned by the e_j with k_j ≤ −i. sourceIssues.locator: Chapter VI, §VI.10, last paragraph, p. 234 (arXiv v4)
sourceIssues.printed: The source defines Rep^cont_{W_E}(ℤ̂^p) = lim←_n Rep_{W_E}(ℤ/nℤ) as continuous W_E-representations on finite free modules over ℤ̂^p = lim←_n ℤ/nℤ.
sourceIssues.correction: Rep^cont_{W_E}(ℤ̂^p) = lim←_n Rep_{W_E}(ℤ/nℤ), the category of compatible systems of continuous representations of W_E on finite projective ℤ/nℤ-modules; equivalently, of continuous representations of W_E on ℤ̂^p-modules M = ∏_{ℓ≠p} M_ℓ with each M_ℓ finite free over ℤ_ℓ (i.e. ∏_{ℓ≠p} Rep^cont_{W_E}(ℤ_ℓ)).

The system (ℤ/nℤ ⊗_{ℤ̂^p} ℤ_ℓ)_n with trivial action is compatible, and each term ℤ/ℓ^{v_ℓ(n)}ℤ is a direct factor of ℤ/nℤ, hence finite projective. Its limit ℤ_ℓ is projective but not free over ℤ̂^p = ∏_{ℓ′≠p} ℤ_{ℓ′}. Systems with ℓ-ranks r_ℓ unbounded in ℓ have limit ∏_ℓ ℤ_ℓ^{r_ℓ}, which is not even finitely generated. So the inverse limit is strictly larger than the representations on finite free ℤ̂^p-modules. The construction of ℋ_G and Ǧ over ℤ̂^p and the proof of Theorem VI.11.1 (which reduces to ℤ_ℓ by the Chinese remainder theorem) are unaffected.

sourceIssues.locator: Chapter VII, §VII.2, proof of Proposition VII.2.3, p. 254 (arXiv v4)
sourceIssues.printed: The source places F_i ⊗^L G_j in degrees −1 and 0, citing global dimension 1 for Ẑ^p.
sourceIssues.correction: 'as Ẑ^p has weak (Tor-)dimension 1', or 'as F_i and G_j are killed by some n prime to p, so that the derived tensor product is computed over the direct factor ∏_{ℓ | n} Z_ℓ of Ẑ^p, a finite product of discrete valuation rings'.
sourceIssues.reason: Ẑ^p = ∏_{ℓ≠p} Z_ℓ does not have global dimension 1. The element x = (ℓ)_ℓ is a non-zero-divisor and a non-unit, and Ẑ^p/x = ∏_{ℓ≠p} F_ℓ. In this von Neumann regular ring the ideal I = ⊕_ℓ F_ℓ is projective (a sum of idempotent-generated ideals) but not a direct summand (it is not finitely generated), so the module M = (∏F_ℓ)/I has projective dimension exactly 1 over Ẑ^p/x. Kaplansky's change-of-rings theorem gives pd_{Ẑ^p} M = 2. What the proof needs is still true. Ẑ^p is a Bézout ring whose principal ideals (x) ≅ e·Ẑ^p are projective, so it is semihereditary and has weak dimension 1. In any case constructible sheaves killed by n prime to p are modules over the hereditary direct factor ∏_{ℓ|n} Z_ℓ. So the conclusion that F_i ⊗^L G_j lies in degrees [−1, 0] holds; only the stated reason is false.

sourceIssues.locator: Chapter VIII, §VIII.2.2.1, paragraph before Definition VIII.2.6, p. 282, and its reuse before Theorem VIII.2.7, p. 283 (arXiv v4)
sourceIssues.printed: The source cites [ML95, Theorem X.3.1] for HH^2(B/A) = Ext^1_B(L_{B/A}, B), identifies this with Exalcom_A(B, B) via [Gro64, Chap.0, Sec. 18.4], and concludes HH^2(B/A) = H^1(L^∨_{B/A}). On p. 283 it uses H^1(L^∨_{B/A}) = HH^2(B/A) → Ext^2_B(N, N) to claim a natural graded O(Sing_{X/S})-algebra structure.
sourceIssues.correction: There is a natural (injective) map Ext^1_B(L_{B/A}, B) = Exalcom_A(B, B) → HH^2(B/A), sending a commutative square-zero extension of B by B to the same extension viewed as an associative one; it is not an isomorphism in general. On p. 283 read 'Using the map H^1(L^∨_{B/A}) → HH^2(B/A) → Ext^2_B(N, N)'.
sourceIssues.reason: Counterexample: A = k a field, B = k[x, y]. B is smooth over k, so L_{B/k} ≅ Ω_{B/k} is free of rank 2 and Ext^1_B(L_{B/k}, B) = 0; but the Koszul resolution of B over B ⊗_k B gives HH^2(B/k) ≅ Hom_B(Λ^2 Ω_{B/k}, B) ≅ B ≠ 0 (Hochschild–Kostant–Rosenberg), e.g. B[ε] with xy − yx = ε is a nonsplit first-order associative deformation. [ML95, Theorem X.3.1] identifies HH^2 with all singular (associative) extensions, while [Gro64, 0_IV 18.4] concerns commutative ones, so the two cited identifications do not compose. The later text only uses a map H^1(L^∨_{B/A}) → Ext^2_B(N, N): its image lies in the image of HH^•(B/A), which graded-commutes with Ext^•_B(N, N), so Sym^•_B H^1(L^∨_{B/A}) = O(Sing_{X/S}) still acts, and μEnd(N), Definition VIII.2.8, Theorems VIII.2.7 and VIII.2.9 and Corollary VIII.2.10 are unaffected.

sourceIssues.locator: Chapter VIII, §VIII.5.3, proof of Theorem VIII.5.15 (inner case), p. 303 (arXiv v4)
sourceIssues.printed: The source defines W_i ⊂ W by the condition that wλ_i be H-dominant for w ∈ W. Inducting on i, it claims a surjection ∇_{λ_i}|_H → ⊕_{w∈W_i} ∇^H_{wλ_i} with a kernel admitting a good H-filtration.
sourceIssues.correction: … a surjective map ∇_{λ_i}|_H → ⊕_{μ ∈ W_iλ_i} ∇^H_μ, the sum running over the distinct H-dominant weights μ = wλ_i (w ∈ W_i), whose kernel has a good H-filtration (and likewise ⊕_{w′∈W_j} ∇^H_{w′λ_j} later on the page).
sourceIssues.reason: If λ_i has a nontrivial stabiliser in W, the sum over w ∈ W_i repeats summands. For i = 0 the enumeration has λ_0 = 0 and W_0 = W, so the claim would be a surjection L = ∇_0|_H → (∇^H_0)^{⊕|W|} = L^{|W|}, which is impossible. The text's own justification ('∇_{λ_i}|_H has a wλ_i-weight space of dimension 1 for all w ∈ W_i') produces one map per distinct weight.

sourceIssues.locator: Chapter VIII, §VIII.5.3, proof of Theorem VIII.5.15 (inner case), p. 303 (arXiv v4)
sourceIssues.printed: The proof reduces connectivity in the good filtration t-structure to connectivity of RΓ(H, X ⊗ ∇^H_{w′λ_j}) for w′ ∈ W_j and j < i. It asserts RΓ(H, ∇^H_{wλ_i} ⊗ ∇^H_{w′λ_j}) = 0 and, using the definition of X, restates the requirement for m > 0 as H^m(H, ∇_{λ_i}|_H ⊗ ∇^H_{w′λ_j}) = 0.
sourceIssues.correction: Test against the duals of these weights: it suffices that RΓ(H, X ⊗ ∇^H_μ) is connective for the H-dominant μ = −w_0^H(w′λ_j), j < i, w′ ∈ W_j (equivalently, Ext^m_H(Δ^H_{w′λ_j}, X) = 0 for m > 0). For these, RΓ(H, ∇^H_{wλ_i} ⊗ ∇^H_μ) = RHom_H(Δ^H_{w′λ_j}, ∇^H_{wλ_i}) = 0 does hold (different W-orbits), and the argument continues with λ_j replaced by −w_0λ_j, ending with H^m(G, Ind_H^G 1 ⊗ ∇_{λ_i} ⊗ ∇_{−w_0λ_j}) = 0. The induction then needs −w_0λ_j to come before λ_i, so the enumeration should be stable under λ ↦ −w_0λ in this sense, e.g. by increasing ⟨λ + ρ, λ + ρ⟩, which also satisfies the printed condition on the weights of ∇_{λ_i}.
sourceIssues.reason: RΓ(H, ∇^H_μ ⊗ ∇^H_ν) = RHom_H(Δ^H_{−w_0^H μ}, ∇^H_ν) is L in degree 0 when ν = −w_0^H μ, so the asserted vanishing fails whenever −w_0λ_i = λ_j with j < i. Example in the proof's own setting: G = SL_3, p ≥ 3 a prime ≠ ℓ, Θ = Int(diag(1, ζ, ζ^2)) with ζ a primitive p-th root of unity, so H = G^Θ is the diagonal torus T (the centralizer of a regular semisimple element, as the proof says). The enumeration 0, ω_1, ω_2, … satisfies the printed condition. For i = 2, j = 1, take wω_2 = −ε_1 and w′ω_1 = ε_1: RΓ(T, ∇^T_{−ε_1} ⊗ ∇^T_{ε_1}) = RΓ(T, L) = L ≠ 0. The reduction to these test objects is also not what the weight argument gives. H^m(H, X ⊗ ∇^H_μ) = Ext^m_H(Δ^H_{−w_0^H μ}, X) can be nonzero only if −w_0^H μ lies below a weight of X, i.e. μ ∈ W·{−w_0λ_0, …, −w_0λ_{i−1}}. That set differs from W·{λ_0, …, λ_{i−1}} when −1 ∉ W (types A_n with n ≥ 2, D_n with n odd, E_6). The repaired argument proves the same theorem. Proposition VIII.5.17's proof reuses 'the arguments with highest weights in the proof of Theorem VIII.5.15' (p. 309) and needs the same repair.

sourceIssues.locator: Chapter IX, Definition IX.0.4, p. 319, and §IX.4, Definition/Proposition IX.4.1, p. 327; same wording in Proposition I.9.1, p. 34 (arXiv v4)
sourceIssues.printed: The source asserts a unique φ_A : W_E → Ĝ(L) ⋊ Q that is a semisimple L-parameter. For every excursion datum (I, V, α, β, (γ_i)_{i∈I}), it requires A = T_1(A) → T_V(A) → T_V(A) → T_1(A) = A to act by the scalar represented by L → V → V → L.
sourceIssues.correction: Then there is a semisimple L-parameter φ_A : W_E → Ĝ(L) ⋊ Q, unique up to Ĝ(L)-conjugation, such that … (as in Corollary VIII.4.3: 'there is, up to Ĝ(L)-conjugation, a unique semisimple L-parameter').
sourceIssues.reason: For g ∈ Ĝ(L), the conjugate parameter gφ_Ag^{-1} gives the scalars β∘(gφ_A(γ_i)g^{-1})_i∘α = β∘diag(g)∘(φ_A(γ_i))_i∘diag(g)^{-1}∘α = β∘(φ_A(γ_i))_i∘α. This holds because α : 1 → V|_Ĝ and β : V|_Ĝ → 1 are equivariant for the diagonal Ĝ. So every conjugate satisfies the defining identities, and literal uniqueness fails as soon as the Ĝ(L)-orbit of φ_A has more than one point (e.g. G = GL₂ and φ_A = χ₁ ⊕ χ₂ with χ₁ ≠ χ₂). The proof invokes Proposition VIII.3.8, whose (i) is 'Semisimple L-parameters … up to Ĝ(L)-conjugation', and Corollary VIII.4.3 (pp. 292–293) states the conjugacy qualifier. The intended meaning is clear, so this is a misprint.

sourceIssues.locator: Chapter IX, §IX.6.3, proof of Proposition IX.6.3, p. 332 (arXiv v4)
sourceIssues.printed: The source claims that restricting F_n → W to maps through W′ leaves the colimit unchanged, giving Exc(W, Ĝ) = colim_{(n,F_n→W)} 𝒪(Z¹(F_n, Ĝ))^Ĝ ←∼ colim_{(n,F_n→W′)} 𝒪(Z¹(F_n, Ĝ))^Ĝ ≅ colim_{(n,F_n→W′)} 𝒪(Z¹(F_n, Ĝ′))^{Ĝ′} = Exc(W′, Ĝ′).
sourceIssues.correction: Apply the Shapiro isomorphism termwise over the W-indexed diagram: Exc(W, Ĝ) = colim_{(n,F_n→W)} 𝒪(Z¹(F_n, Ĝ))^Ĝ ≅ colim_{(n,F_n→W)} 𝒪(Z¹(F_n ×_W W′, Ĝ′))^{Ĝ′} → colim_{(m,F_m→W′)} 𝒪(Z¹(F_m, Ĝ′))^{Ĝ′} = Exc(W′, Ĝ′). The last map is induced by the functor (F_n → W) ↦ (F_n ×_W W′ → W′), and one must show that this functor is cofinal. For example, every F_m → W′ factors through F_n ×_W W′ for F_n = F_m ∗ F_k, with the generators of F_k sent to coset representatives of W/W′. Restricting the index category to maps F_n → W with image in W′, as printed, does not compute Exc(W, Ĝ).
sourceIssues.reason: Counterexample to both printed isomorphisms. Take E′/E unramified quadratic, G′ = G_m and G = Res_{E′/E} G_m, so that Ĝ = G_m × G_m, with W acting through W/W′ ≅ Z/2 by swapping the factors and W′ acting trivially. For F_n → W′ one has Z¹(F_n, Ĝ)⫽Ĝ = Hom(F_n, G_m²) = G_m^{2n}, while Z¹(F_n, Ĝ′)⫽Ĝ′ = G_m^n. So the middle colimit is, up to universal homeomorphism, the ring of functions on Hom(W′, G_m²) and the right one that on Hom(W′, G_m): the printed '≅' fails. The printed '←∼' is induced by restricting cocycles, Z¹(W, Ĝ)⫽Ĝ ≅ Hom(W′, G_m) → Hom(W′, G_m²), χ ↦ (χ, χ∘Int(σ)) for σ ∈ W ∖ W′ (Shapiro). This is a closed immersion that is not an isomorphism, so the ring map is surjective but not injective. The identification Exc(W, Ĝ) ≅ Exc(W′, Ĝ′) in the statement is not affected: it follows from the Shapiro isomorphism and the cofinality argument above, which the proof does not give.

sourceIssues.locator: Chapter II, §II.3.1, proof of Proposition II.3.1, p. 76, paragraph beginning 'First, we handle the case that S = Spa(K, K⁺)' (arXiv v4)
sourceIssues.printed: The proof reduces to ensuring that the extension pulled back to ℰ^{≥λ} does not split. It claims that splitting lifts ℰ^{≥λ} → 𝒪_{S_1^♯} to ℰ^{≥λ} → 𝒪_{X_S}, which slopes force to vanish. It defines W′_1 ⊂ W_1 by taking the fibre at S_1^♯ of ℰ^{≥λ} ⊂ ℰ, and concludes that a quotient W_1 → K_1^♯ nonzero on W′_1 suffices.
sourceIssues.correction: The extension pulled back is 0 → 𝒪_{X_S} → 𝒪_{X_S}(1) → 𝒪_{S_1^♯} → 0. So the pullback to ℰ^{≥λ} splits exactly when ℰ^{≥λ} → 𝒪_{S_1^♯} lifts to a map ℰ^{≥λ} → 𝒪_{X_S}(1), not to 𝒪_{X_S}. By slopes such a lift vanishes only when λ > 1. For 1/r < λ ≤ 1 the quotient W_1 → K_1^♯ must be chosen so that the induced map ℰ^{≥λ} → 𝒪_{S_1^♯} does not lift to 𝒪_{X_S}(1); a nonzero restriction to W′_1 is not enough. Over a complete algebraically closed field such a choice exists. For ℱ = (ℰ^{≥λ})^∨ ⊗ 𝒪(1), of slope 1 − λ ≥ 0, H¹(ℱ) = 0, so the evaluation map H⁰(ℱ) → ℱ|_{S_1^♯} has cokernel H¹((ℰ^{≥λ})^∨) ≠ 0 (slope −λ < 0). The proof must add this choice, and an argument that it can be made over the non-algebraically-closed perfectoid fields it also treats.
sourceIssues.reason: Counterexample to the printed sufficiency claim: r = 2, S = Spa(C, C⁺), ℰ = 𝒪(1), so n = d = m = 1 and ℰ^{≥λ} = ℰ with λ = 1 > 1/2. Here W_1 = 𝒪(1)|_{S_1^♯}, and the cokernel term of 0 → 𝒪 → 𝒪(1) → 𝒪_{S_1^♯} → 0 is canonically 𝒪(1)|_{S_1^♯}. Take the quotient W_1 → K_1^♯ to be this identification; it is nonzero on W′_1 = W_1. Then ℰ → 𝒪_{S_1^♯} is the quotient map of the sequence itself, the pulled-back extension splits, and ℰ_1 ≅ 𝒪 ⊕ 𝒪(1) has a slope 0 < 1/2. Rescaling the quotient by c ∈ C^♯ ∖ E, i.e. outside the image of End(𝒪(1)) = E, gives a nonsplit extension of 𝒪(1) by 𝒪 of rank 2 and degree 1. That is 𝒪(1/2), as the proposition predicts, so the gap is in the argument, not the statement. The passage is a leftover from v1–v3, which pulled back 0 → 𝒪(−1) → 𝒪 → 𝒪_{S♯} → 0 for slopes ≥ 0. There the lift goes to 𝒪_{X_S} and vanishes by slopes because λ > 0.

sourceIssues.locator: Chapter IV, §IV.2.3.3, proof of Theorem IV.2.23, p. 125 (arXiv v4)
sourceIssues.printed: The proof seeks a map R∆_!Λ → p_1^*A ⊗^L_Λ p_2^*D_{X/S}(A), and invokes (ii) to identify its target naturally with RHom_Λ(p_1^*A, Rp_2^!A).
sourceIssues.correction: … naturally isomorphic to RHom_Λ(p_2^*A, Rp_1^!A) (condition (ii) with the two factors of X ×_S X interchanged).
sourceIssues.reason: Condition (ii) identifies p_1^*D_{X/S}(A) ⊗ p_2^*A with RHom_Λ(p_1^*A, Rp_2^!A): the dual sits on the same factor as the A in the source of RHom. The target of α is p_1^*A ⊗ p_2^*D_{X/S}(A), which is right for the kernel of the composite X → S → X. There the dual is on the second factor, so (ii) applied after the swap of X ×_S X gives RHom_Λ(p_2^*A, Rp_1^!A). The next step, R∆^! of this RHom ≅ RHom_Λ(A, A), is symmetric in the factors, so the argument is unaffected.
